review:
A beautiful and huge lake surrounded with green hills and a temple in the centre. Many options of boating are available ranging from as low as 100npr, sharing, to options of private boat for a day for a group. 
We took a private boat for 700npr for 1 hour with visit to temple included, which we felt was enough. 
Overall a good spot to visit and enjoy. 

You also have to mandatory rent a life jacket for 10npr, which were actually not very clean, and check the size beforehand to avoid hassles later, as it can be very inconvenient during the trip.
Nice view and a very local place. Monkeys aplenty, watch that apple in the hand. On descend, we walked around the temple’s circumference enjoying the surrounding view.

We stayed at Bodhi Boutique Hotel where is a stone throw from Thamel district. It is a tourists centre with many cafes/ restaurants, convenient stores, hotels, travel/ hiking companies/ agents, drug stores, souvenirs shops and many other shops. Overall, it is one of the cool place in Kathmandu and highly recommend any tourists to stay around this area for convenient location where almost everything can be found here easily.

Definitely the tourist heart of Khatmandu. Lots of great shopping, many great (and some not so great) restaurants. If you forget any trekking gear, you can get it here, maybe not genuine, but functional and cheap.

Make sure your hotel is within walking distance of here, otherwise you will be catching a taxi here every day.

So, great base and great shopping, but make sure you see other parts of Nepal, as this is in no way indicative of Nepal

Our fourth trip to Nepal and once again stayed in Thamel. It's a hodge-podge of shops, restaurants and bars and is full on. Easy to spend your money on all sorts of bargains. It's fast paced at night and we felt safe every time we visited.
Hotel is best and maintained..very good staff behaviour..Sabina nabina binita alsihwa sanma  was very good . Beautiful location breakfast was good

The place is nice and cosy, albeit the rooms are small with no mini bar in our deluxe room and small washroom.

Food is average at best, menu is overpriced according to that.

Property is nice and pleasant to the eyes, but no pool and gym make it less appealing.

Located in the heart of Thamel and close to airport and nearby hangout places and casino.

Overall an average experience.

Stayed here for a night during my stay in Thamel. On first impressions, the place is dated and is in need of a revamp. It was dark inside the building and was quite off putting. The rooms are decent with air-conditioning and a television. But the bathroom was subpar and the water coming out of the shower smelt like rust.

The location is very good, and is opposite the fantastic pilgrims book shop, and next to the roadhouse cafe.

It was passable, but for that money I ended up spending the rest of my trip staying somewhere else, and was glad I did.
As a tourist, Thamel area is the hub and the best place you can be at. Lot's of hotels around. Place comes alive post sunset.

Fewa lake itself is just average and you can find many more interesting lakes in Nepal (Begnas lake, for example, not so far away). anyway, it's worth to have a stroll along the bank or  chill out in one of plenty small restaurants in the east side of the lake (much cheaper than along the main lakeside street). hilly way to Peace Temple on the opposite side of Pokhara will provide you view on the lake and the city.

Friendly helpful service. Manager’s welcome evening very pleasant. Spa massages wonderful. Granitas in the ground floor bar were terrific. Food and drink great. Room nice. Location good. Markets nearby. We had a pleasant and enjoyable stay.

so it's the tourist hub, crack on, you know the prices can be beaten down. you will be offered hash 10 times a day, but then hey it's got people floating around, shops with stuff you need. check out Nepal cooking school for a half day you will really enjoy. the Kathmandu kitchen has decent cheap eats.
This is an excellent museum but you need a whole day to do it justices the temperature inside was very cold and the restaurant too out of the way!

For the center of the nation's capitol the sanitary conditions of the streets leave much more to be desired. Traffic during rush hour is horrendous. Absence of traffic lights makes it nearly impossible to cross the street. Air quality is atrocious due to traffic.
Not good as I thought. I never got time to be here before but now going there is not that much good I found. Good but not that much

We are saty here two nights  staff are so nice and hotel manager Saroj pudasaini very helpful . WiFi is workingAll the services and rooms were very comfortable , Network speed was exellent,rooms are so clean ,they have a rooftop garden .

They stuffed up my accommodation booking on the first night and in the morning made me go through a hour and a half ordeal with some accountant who didn't speak English to prove that I had already booked the preceding nights accommodation. The then put me in a gross room with a mouldy ceiling and a bathroom with a broken light. Expensive as all hell for Nepal and the manager was patronising. The waiters keep bothering me in the garden in the same way the guy/girls on the street selling weed and tiger balms did. Breakfast was expensive and poor. There was a cleaner who was nice for a chat. Go to the holy Himalayas, same price less poor. They completely rely on the name and past prestigious guests. Also was loud at night on the side with the cheaper rooms, deluxe room didn't have this issue they were quite nice tbh but for $100 Aussie u can find better. They are generous with water. Wifi was poor and cut out every 20 minutes in the cheaper rooms.

Stayed here for a few days early March and again later in month. Booked by an agent but we moved out during our second stay and found a much cheaper alternative (Kathmandu Resort Hotel). The hotel (Kantipur) is situated in a quiet part of Kathmandu and that 's probably the best thing about it, although we were warned by a local not to walk the streets in the immediate area after dark.
The hotel has a certain charm but the price of the accommodation is far too high. When we complained, they did reduce their charges but it was still far higher (4 times the price) than similar hotels.
The accommodation was ok but the ensuite bathroom was awful. The smell of sewage meant you had to keep the door closed between the bathroom and the room. The fixtures and fittings were grubby - in fact we both had stomach problems when we were there and they miraculously improved when we left the hotel.  We put some clothes into wash and they were returned grubbier than they had gone in. The roof terrace was a welcome surprise but it probably won't be for much longer as there was frantic building work going on all around it when we were there.The food was below average.Buffet breakfast was left uncovered so it wasn't only the guests who had something to eat. The serving hatch to the kitchen was blackened with continuous grubby use. The electricity problems of Kathmandu (2 hours a day, and it could be 2 hours in the middle of the night) are exasperated  at this hotel because of it's decor. Designed in a traditional style, it has few windows and a dark interior, guaranteed to make even a simple excursion to the restaurant an event. A few doors away there's a small cafe 'Spicy Affair' run by a charming woman who serves much better food for a fraction of the price of the hotel.On one occasion, we had to use the phone in our room to make an urgent call to London (had to use the phone in our room because our stomachs wouldn't permit us to travel far from the loo). We were charged 2400 rupees to make this call.We definitely wouldn't return to this hotel.
amazing treasurable city , lots to do and see , the shopping is nice but the places and the vibes are even better

My son and I stayed here during July and August 2024 for seven nights over three periods - on arrival in Kathmandu, between a trek and then a tour, and prior to leaving Nepal. For each stay check-in and check-out were smooth and efficient.

It is located in busy Thamel but it is on a lane which has relatively little traffic so is quiet and peaceful. The shops, bars and cafes of Thamel are reached in one minute.

The building is in a traditional Newari style; the brick and carved wood contribute to the ambience very well (unlike ‘concrete box’ buildings). It is built around two courtyards with chairs and tables overlooking them in the corridors outside the rooms.

The rooms we stayed in (two different ones) had a view over a courtyard or to the font of the hotel. Both were large with a seating area, the beds were very comfortable and the bathrooms functioned well and were kept very clean by housekeeping staff. 

The buffet-style breakfast was excellent. Fresh fruit and freshly-juiced fruit (definitely not commercial, processed and sugary muck), pastries, muffins and toast. Eggs and pancakes are cooked to order and the good coffee and tea are unlimited.

The staff were wonderful and really enhanced our stay. They balanced a professional and efficient service with friendliness. Unlike some other places in this price bracket, they avoided the starchy, polished hotel-school stiffness and smarmy, false over-friendliness. They provided helpful information and were genuinely interested in our trip, giving suggestions and checking our day went well. My son particularly enjoyed chatting with them and learning about their lives in Nepal.

The hotel is more expensive than the ones I usually stay at in Kathmandu. I chose it partly because I had passed it on previous visits and it looked very nice, partly so my son could have a comfortable start to his first trip to Nepal. I intended to stay in cheaper places after the first couple of nights but we liked it so much and returned. The off-season discount price helped with this decision too.

The hotel is very clean but a little dusty which is not uncommon because Kathmandu is a very dusty (and polluted) city even in the monsoon (after a downpour the sun dries the streets very quickly). I have yet to stay in a hotel in Kathmandu that does not have this minor issue. The ambience is lovely but corridors are perhaps a little dark. However, I am partially-sighted and would not want the hotel to change this and lose the traditional feel of the place. .

Overall, the experience was wonderful and we enjoyed our three stays there equally and we will return - selecting the hotel to stay in Kathmandu is now an easy one for me. The staff make this hotel what it is - excellent.
The surroundings are cleaner and small vendors seem to be more aware about keeping  their workplace clean.

A beautiful lake surrounded by mountains, a peaceful walkway around the lake, lots & lots of places to eat or sip a cup of amazing Nepali tea, wellness centers, games & boating - well, what more can you ask for??
Amazing, beautiful, peaceful, calm and serene.
Amazing resort. Have been coming here for years and they’ve never disappointed me. The service is excellent and the property is like non other in Pokhara. They’ve been our second home in Pokhara.
The rooms super good the service super good locations excellent the ambience is superb everything was superbe.......

The trekking and shopping centre of Kathmandu.

Touts on every corner, the need to negotiate pedestrian, motor bike, rickshaw and four wheeled vehicle traffic is constant.

There are back streets and squares away from the rush - which are probably more representative of how Kathmandu once was...but the busy streets of Thamel are predominantly full of tourists, travelers and those trying to sell them something.
Too noisy, too many people, too bland taste... it's more a fastfood restaurant than a cosy one these days. Not our cup of tea!

Booked to stay in Thamel as it is in the centre of Katmandu and easy access to sites, accommodation is available at all price ranges and restaurants are numerous . I stayed here a week which is perhaps a little long for Katmandu but I enjoyed exploring the area and finding good places to eat.

Thamel is a district located in the old city of Kathmandu.  It is a tourist place, a bit noisy but not far from Dream garden and some temples.  My stay at the Norbulinka Boutique hotel allowed me to easily discover Thamel

One of the three great temples which I visit on all my trekking visits to Nepal and Kathmandu.

Monkeys everywhere and several groups of pilgrims chanting from the scriptures.

When i checked in the room it was dirty. Then the electricity to the AC and the TV kept shutting off. We had to have technitions come turn the power back on three times before deciding to leave after the power would switch back off after being turned on. Whenn we decided to leave they offered us a different room which we accepted and it was really nice but we had already spent four or five hours of our one night anniversary stay dealing with no electricity no AC and no TV and continual visits from hotel staff to try and fix these issues

Thamel is The Hub for tourists visiting Kathmandu Nepal and is full of activities and shoppers till late in the night as compared to any other place in Kathmandu.

This is best place to get traditional Nepal handicrafts and souvenir also the gear for trekking and mountaineering.

Also lots of eating joints and bars which are otherwise a rarity in Nepal.

This place is nice. But there are many people around who want to sell you things, and some of them tend to follow you around a bit. A good set of market places, but again some pushy salespeople. It is nice to visit though, so if you don’t mind people trying to see you things, I would recommend going.
Kathmandu Durbar Square is located in front of the old royal palace of the former Kathmandu Kingdom. This place is really beautiful.
Beautiful is the word. Worth waiting to see the sunrise and the beauty is to see the rays on Annapurna range.

We stayed overnight in order to catch the views of the Annapurna ranges. Unfortunately the low lying clouds meant we could barely see the neighbouring hills. Without the views, there's not much else to do in Sarangkot (other than paragliding). Plus, meals and drinks are more expensive than Pokhara - likely because everything needs to be driven up.
Nice best place  for enjoy too,all, quit rain,some time,and some-time-aftrnoon,hot,morning good eaving good time,to,walk

We went up at 4.30am to see the dawn and it was cloudy so there wasn’t much to see - we could just make out the outline of the mountains through the clouds - so this isn’t a bad review as such, just to help manage your expectations - I’d so hoped for a beautiful view of the mountains, and instead there were lots and lots of people and not much to see. I think it’s just the luck of the draw!

The Radison Kathmandu experience has been delightful. The hotel is very clean and efficient. Anu in the restaurant is extremely gracious. Usha kept the room impeccable. And at the front guest services, Ganga Maya is professional and personable. Total class. 
The hotel is so accommodating to all your needs.
A wonderful place to stay.

Great stay, excellent staff and perfect location. Food was good and the rooms were maintained to a high standard. Overall very satisfied with the Radisson Kathmandu and will stay again on next visit. Thank you
Great place to visit and see how hard the earlier mountaineers did it.Some amazing stories,pictures and relics of years gone by.

I have to go to Pokhara many times as I am a travel and trek guide in Nepal and most of the times my company books Best Camp Resort for my stay with my clients. I have been to the hotel many times and stayed there for many times. I have some good experiences with them and some bad as well......
The Resort has numbers of good things like the comfortable rooms in reasonable price, good greeny garden, nice managements etc. The hotel has various room structures which suit from medium budget travelers to deluxe looking people. And, also the hotel has a wide space inside the hotel. There are single buildings with less rooms, not a big single building with large numbers of room.
Some rooms are not good though. On the last time I went there I got a room where the lock was broken. I needed to change the room once I kept all my things inside the room, that was a bit boring for me because I was tired to do so!
Overall, the hotel is nice to stay, make sure your door lock is working before you enter the room! And the Breakfast was nice!

Just go!!!!!!! 
It's a must visit if you are in Kathmandu 
The monkeys are not anywhere near as bad as you will be led to believe

I will start by saying that I am a Hyatt member; I've been to Hyatts all over the world; I have stayed at this particular Hyatt 4 times. The Rox restaurant has some of the best Italian I have eaten in Nepal and I would genuinely recommend its food to any visitor. I would also like to highlight the lovely decor--it's a wide open restaurant with glass walls. Unfortunately, I had an extremely negative experience here, mostly due to a nasty and very privileged client of the hotel but also due to the way this situation was handled by hotel staff, which means I will not be coming back again. I live in a rural part of Nepal where there is not reliable wifi/cell service/beds/showers. I come to the Hyatt from time to time to have a taste of comfort after a work day in Kathmandu. Mind you, the Rox restaurant is a hotel restaurant. There are visitors from all walks of life, different dresses, different cultures, different time zones. I am from America where the time zones are opposite to Nepal--night calls here are morning calls there, so the only way to make a work call work is during the hours between 6pm-9pm Kathmandu time. The Hyatt Regency is an older hotel; it's one of the most beautiful hotels in Nepal, however, it struggles with some of the same problems an old hotel in Nepal would: yellowish bath water, poor in-room wifi. So, it is common for the wifi not to be strong enough in room for a work call. In this case, I went to the Rox restaurant to have dinner over a work call scheduled at 6:45pm. I confirmed with hotel staff that there is no dress code or rule about phone calls in the restaurants, and 2 of the 4 restaurants at the Regency actually have work tables where you can use your devices, as this is quite common. I sat at the Rox in the furthest corner that I could find, but it is an open space that can be a bit echoing because of the glass walls. About 20 minutes into my work call, a family sat down at the table next to me. There is no assigned or reserved seating, so they could have sat anywhere in the restaurant that they chose. However, because I was on the phone at the restaurant, the older European gentleman was very upset with me. For the first 20 minutes of his dinner he tried to intimidate me by turning his seat around and staring at me with a very ugly face. The restaurant staff saw this going on, but I tried to ignore it as I still had food on the table and had told the waitress that I planned to get another course for dessert. The man did not like that I ignored his intimidation tactics. So, he called the waitress over and turned to me and started raising his voice trying to shame me publicly at the restaurant, saying how inappropriate and rude I was for using a phone at the restaurant and how I wasn't dressed accordingly and I should get out. To be clear, I was on a work call that had been scheduled 5 weeks ahead of time due to my lack of wifi and service at site, the nature of the call was very professional and not boisterous or inappropriate. I lowered my voice to a whisper on the phone at that point but he was still not happy with me even sharing the same space as him with a phone, so he called the manager to have me removed. He said that this was a public space and I should go somewhere private with my call. Which seemed odd to me, because not only was traditional Nepali music playing in the lobby area where I could hold a call, but also if it is a public space then everyone has the right to use it accordingly. I understand he is not familiar with Nepali culture, but it is also extremely common in Nepal for people to use the phone in restaurants. I also am visiting Kathmandu solo, so it's not as if I have someone to talk to at dinner anyway. Regardless of this man creating a scene at the restaurant and trying to put me down and embarrass me, the waitress asked me to leave the restaurant while I was on my professional call. It was humiliating. I began to cry and had to ask for the bill 3 times before I could leave. The incident was so distressing even the daughter of the father came over to apologize on her father's behalf, though I was still forced to leave. Not only that, but I still had to pay for my unfinished meal despite the traumatic experience. Clearly this was a monster customer, but the staff did not reinforce the rules of the restaurant, ask the other family who got there later to move, or ask the man to stop staring at me or raising his voice, and then I was still asked to pay and leave at the end. Really saddening experience considering I had hoped to have a few days that I could relax and feel like I belonged somewhere, only to be reminded that I don't.

The resort and staff were very nice! A quiet reprieve from the busy of the city. The food was very good, rooms comfortable, and pool area just perfect! The grounds were very beautiful. Again all the staff were very kind and helpful. It was very close to the lake drive for shops and restaurants. The hotel arranged out airport transfer in a comfortable SUV. Thanks!

It gives a glimpse of various aspects of Nepal, the people, their culture, the household items, the dresses and most importantly about the Himalayan Ranges, for which this place is best known for. A lot of information in the form of pictures, facts and figures are presented in the museum. Apart from this, they run a short about the Himalayas every 2 hours for the audiences better understanding.
A good place to grab knowledge about the mountains.

The temple was very interesting to view and explore.  There were many locals there that were praying and site seeing.  The monkeys were all over the temples, but many of them looked very sick with noses and ears missing, and it was sad to watch them digging through the pile of trash behind the temples.  The shops had many different paintings and art work that I had not seen in other areas of Nepal. The cost to get into the site was only approx $1.50 US dollars, and the view was great, but not on my top things to do in Kathmandu.

Very excellent dormety and staff behavior is very helpful. Mr saroj tracker home manager is Very Good Service and help him guys rooms are so clean 🙂 when will coming in hotel reception .then reception boy give good semail . I wil back this place.
Phewa lake is paradise of Pokhara lake is so  beautiful and really cool place to walk  a bank of lake is awesome place

I went as a day guest to the spa to have a leg wax. The staff is extremely formal and concludes every sentence with "Mam". I would prefer friendliness.

On my way to the spa I got a glimpse of the pool area. It was closed for renovation. No information on homepage. Glad I didn't book a room at the hotel.

The treatment room for my wax was a massage room. The light was dim and the therapist brought in an old, dilapidated work lamp that looked like it was bought at a flea market. The light bulb didn't give more than maybe 30 or 40 Watt so she wasn't able to see much while she was doing her work. The towel that covered the massage bed was so washed-out there were holes in it.

I've had wax treatments in many different European countries and many places in the US. Normally, a full leg wax treatment would take 30-45 minutes with a well-trained and experienced therapist. I also had wax treatments done by trainees. They took 60-90 minutes for full leg.

My full leg wax treatment at Temple Tree spa took 90 minutes.

Communication problems:

After the treatment I was asked to sit down and wait for 5 minutes to have my bill. I was very hungry (because I hadn't expect the treatment to drag on for so long!) so I asked if I could go to the restaurant and pay the bill later. 

"NO! Sit down, MAM!!!"

Eh, ok. I asked why, they couldn't answer. "MAM, just sit down, MAM", I was told. They called the receptionist and then she came and told me I could go to the restaurant and pay the bill later. I never understood why they had to call her to come and tell me that but it seemed that she was higher in the hiearchy and the spa staff couldn't make even the smallest deciscion on their own.

Reception lady asked if I was satisfied with the service. I said the wax took a very long time. She didn't answer.

If you don't care about the customer's feedback, then why do you ask for it??? Her question was an empty formality just like all the "MAM"s. I think it's okay not to ask for the customer's feedback if you know you're doing your best and just can't do it any better in the circumstances you are. But what really annoys me is when staff say stuff and asks questions like trained parrots but really don't care. And that's exactly the feeling I had at the Temple Tree.

At the restaurant the service was again equally ridiculously formal compared to the quality of the services delivered. I got a meal which contained factory-made french fries, factory-made ketchup, dry factory-made bread, flavourless factory-made pickles. It was basically a pot pourri of processed food on my plate - but it did come with a "MAM"!

I want to add that the kitchen staff had done nothing wrong. The chicken steak in my burger was cooked to perfection - the meal was a disappointment only because of the quality of the ingredients. And that's not their fault.

The wait staff asked me how the food was, which again seemed ridiculous.

I generally had the feeling that everyone of the normal staff was trying their very best but that the management had created an atmosphere of fear of commiting mistakes and had trained the staff in saying "MAM" and asking questions without explaining WHY you ask questions and how to respond in a sensible manner.

Seriously, if you love monkeys you will love your visit. We had an amazing time. In fact, I put this right up there with my 2 days spent at the Everest View Hotel.  I mean, what’s better than hanging out with more than 100 monkeys?

Zig zag steps lead up 2500 ft (ascent) for view of Annapurna region. It was a hazy day so we couldn’t see much. The trail is hard to find and not easily marked. Snacks and shops at the top. Not truly a nature experience, houses line the trail.

You cannot visit Kathmandu without spending a good amount of time in Durbar Square. It has been a part of the city's culture since the Third Century.  Religiously important to Hindus and Buddhists and many others who are looking for a spiritual experience. It is the heart of Nepal and the Nepalese monarchy and history.

The main tourist area but it is very noisy with a constant flow of traffic running through it.Plenty of guest houses,hotels and restaurants but you are better off staying in adjacent areas just outside thamel

OR2K is a perfect place where to untie your shoes and relax for a while. The atmosphere in this restaurant is very pleasant and relaxing, lying down on the ground (with pillows, don't worry) and getting served many different foods by friendly staff. However, I think that the extended menu, offering a variety of different kitchens, doesn't allow the restaurant to serve excellent food. Trying to offer many plates doesn't give them the possibility to specialize in anything, making their plates average and nothing special. Furthermore if you are used to Nepalese prices, you will find OR2K not too cheap considering the quality of food offered.

The experience of Pokhara starts within your Temple Tree hotel itself, polite staff, very good food and 24/7 room service. SPA and Tourist activity center. Everything was done smoothy. The location is perfect, your within city place - so access to city life. 

Best moment was - Briyani served @ 5AM  😆

Thamel is a crappy tourist area. The neighborhood has some of the best variety of international food in town, but it is filled with tourist shops, bad dance bars and random men offering to sell you drugs on the streets.
It was nice once we got in. People could be friendlier but was educational. Take your own snacks & drinks, Don't recall any for purchase.
This is a beautiful place and to really enjoy you should spend at least one night here there are some great walks and the sunrise and sunset are amazing.

Took a pedal boat ride to the temple organised by the tour company we travelled with.
Beautiful lake and the scenery is fantastic, although we were unlucky with the weather, as it was overcast and no real view of the Annapurna range.

The temple is very nice but commercialised.....and it was very busy that morning. Lots of pigeons here, which dive bomb from all directions. Would happily just take the boat ride next time.

Kathmandu has a power cut everyday lasting up to 12hours.  But this hotel even when charging you through the nose will never turn their generator even in the dark.  You are left to stumble in the dark and on asking them why they do not turn the generator on they will sing the song of "Staying Green".  They will trap you by showing you the well appointed room and the nice architecuture but it is all a set up.  Basic ameneties like electricity, shampoo, TV (if that matters), AC, heat is missing from the rooms.  Is that too much to ask for at $140.00 per night.  Breakfast is a joke with one only choice of 1 juice, 2 cereals and eggs to order.  Stay away from this place if you want to maintain you sanity.

This museum has a wealth of  treasures to share. The information and history of the Nepali people groups is very informative. The history of mountaineering in the Himalayas is very well covered and time flies as you read all the posters and look at all the displays. The current conservation effort in Nepal are also shown. 
Very good place to bring children of any age although as some of the items are in the open keep a tight hold on those with grabby hands 😋

Stayed in Thamel more then twice while in Kathmandu, Nepal. Been to trekkers bar for drinks it was nice spot you most try if you are looking for chill place to have drinks with lots of care like family member.

Under renovation yet it is a very nice historical land mark of Nepal.museum was close when we went.
Entrance ticket to south Asian regional counties are Rs.200 per guest.

This is the area where most tourists visiting Kathmandu stay. There are many hotels to choose from, ranging in various nightly rates. Also present in this neighborhood are restaurants, shops seeling all types of goods, and of course, the Durbar Square.

Thamel has lot of shops on either side of the road and along small allys. It is one of the main tourist attractions as lot of tourists come here to buy souvenirs and other tracking gear. Make sure you wear a mask as their is lot of dust in the area.

Yes there are lots of monkeys, but the temple is a disgusting and filthy waste of time.  the only good thing about the temple is the view over the city.

The place is filthy and a cultural DISASTER. I gave this rating for the following reasons:
1. Monkey faeces everywhere
2. Dogs and Monkeys everywhere
3. The stairs are covered in human saliva, its really disgusting
4. The handrails must carry all sorts of disease and bacteria.
5. The site at the top is covered in beggars, tourist crap outlets, and every the historic buildings have been turned into cheap and nasty tourist shops and restaurant.
6. Rubbish - why visitors and the Nepalese drop so much rubbish and don't pick it up is beyond me.
7. Cheap crap everywhere

Save your time and money and go to one of the Buddhist temples that are better looked after and respected.

The property as is good. But the staff in the hotel are very arrogant and unprofessional. So be really to be treated not well! Best of Luck! Not worth for the money you pay. It was a very bad experience with the Staff, very arrogant and not accommodating. Non of the request are fulfilled, it is take or leave it. A perfect example of the over professionalism, but zero professionalism. Highly not recommended, unless you want to waste your money.

Thamel is the district that you have to visit, when in Kathmandu.  The hotels are better.  Everything is close.  The shopping options and food options are better.  Just find a hotel in Thamel, and you will be in the right area.

This place is amazing collection of the entire mountaineering experience. It depicts a small film showing the trek to mountains and the place called namchi bazar from where climb to Everest begins. In museum the ethnicity and culture of different tribes of Nepal are depicted. Also various mountaineering photos and equipments are depicted. Also housed are different soil topography and sea fossils found on mountains. Very informative place.

I was expecting very good facilities according to the conversation with the staff, as I paid Rs10000 for a night. 
Room- Very poor condition (based on price) 
Food- Thakali Set was not good as explained by the staff. He said you will have the best Thakali Food comparing outside restaurants as it's a STAR RESORT. One of the worst Thakali Food I had here, but the breakfast was good. 
Staff- Very Friendly. 
Communication- The landline phone was not working.

Hotel based in central Kathmandu so perfect for everything.  Just walk out into the city to eat, shop, sightsee. Lovely spacious rooms but ours wasnt quite ready when we arrived early evening, and neither were some of the rooms for others in our party of 17 (towels missing, kettles missing, some beds not made up into doubles etc) Only one person at a time on main desk so sometimes we had to wait a while before getting our key/information etc. Felt like management needed to sharpen up. nice coffee bar in grounds, lovely grounds, nicely maintained. Good breakfast.

While the lake might be beautiful when blue...it is brown due to rain. It is still nice however there is zero effort of locals or govt to provide bins  a nice walkway lighting or even cleanliness... everywhere is dirty , pavement is broken or sometimes just sand with potholes.... piles of rubbish and water weeds everywhere. Disappointing. The boat rentals are a complete sham. Spiritual, Scenic, and Full of History — A Must-Visit in Kathmandu

We visited Swayambhunath Stupa, also known as the Monkey Temple, and it was one of the highlights of our Kathmandu trip. The place is rich in history, culture, and spirituality, with a beautiful white stupa, golden spire, and the iconic eyes of Buddha watching over the city.

To reach the top, you can either climb a series of steep steps or drive closer and walk a shorter distance. The climb is a bit tiring but worth it for the panoramic view of Kathmandu city from the top.

Apart from the main stupa, you’ll also find Shree Harati (Sherla) Temple, an important shrine where many locals come to offer prayers. It adds to the spiritual atmosphere of the place, and it’s interesting to see both Buddhist and Hindu traditions blending here.

There are many prayer wheels, small shrines, monasteries, and playful monkeys along the way. It’s a lively yet peaceful place where you can experience both local faith and stunning scenery.

Overall, a must-visit site in Kathmandu — perfect for those who love culture, history, and a bit of a hike with rewarding view

Kathmandu Durbar Square, which capability Royal Squares in English, is the standard name used to describe plazas and areas opposite the historical royal palaces in Nepal. It consists of temples, idols, open courts, water fountains and more. Before the Unification of Nepal, Nepal consisted of small kingdoms, and Durbar Squares are most prominent remnants of those historical kingdoms in Nepal. In particular, three Durbar Squares in the Kathmandu Valley, belonging to the three Newar kingdoms situated there earlier than unification, are most famous: Kathmandu Durbar Square, Patan Durbar Square, and Bhaktapur Durbar Square. All three are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.These web sites have received good sized harm due to the devastating earthquake of 2015 however most constructions still remain.

Kantipur temple house is a true gem. This was my second time staying at this beautiful property with my family. We were there for a little over 2 weeks. The hotel is located in the Thamel area and close to the airport and many of the happening places (Durbar Marg, Narayanhiti Royal Palace) and would be a good base for your stay. The architecture at this hotel is marvelous featuring pagoda style architecture (resembling a temple). The rooms are spacious, beautiful, and simple. We were in and out of the hotel, as we were visiting other cities and every time we came back it felt like we were coming home. This hotel had the most comfortable mattress compared to any other hotel I stayed at in nepal. I appreciated the fact that this hotel did not have television. Who needs television when traveling? I was able to unwind and connect with my family each day and just soak in my time in nepal. They offer yoga every morning as well. They were all kind, humble, and helpful with all requests. We lost our bags and received them late, they helped call around and track down our bags and received them at the hotel as well. Staff were all dressed in Nepalese traditional wear and it was so beautiful to see Nepalese culture and customs being kept alive. Although they don’t advertise it, they have a box where you can leave a tip for staff so that it gets distributed evenly among all staff. I think this is a great idea as there may be many staff behind the scenes that may have made things happen for you that you don’t necessarily see. The food at the restaurant was delicious and the local organic coffee was to die for. I cannot have acidic coffee due to health issues and the coffee they serve here was perfect for me (not acidic at all). They use and serve organic products at their restaurant. You can definitely taste the quality. They have a sister restaurant called bhojan griha. I would highly recommend visiting bhojan griha for an exceptional experience into nepali culture and food. You cannot leave nepal until you visit bhojan griha and stay at this hotel.  THANK YOU to everyone at this hotel for making our stay so pleasant and memorable. We enjoyed our time here and would highly recommend staying at this beautiful property without any hesitation. If you’re browsing through reviews and wondering whether you should stay here, just go ahead and book this hotel, you won’t regret it.

The Kathmandu Guest House is one of the oldest in the Thamel area, with several additions having been added to the first original building.  I first stayed at the KGH quite a few years ago, before it was upgraded, with new buildings, a lovely large garden area, a museum, and several shops including an art house; significantly higher prices reflected the upgrade. It is now part of  the KGH Group of hotels.
It is centrally located in Thamel and offers the usual desk services, such as tour booking. Free airport pickup on arrival is available for international flights, with 48 hr pre-notification.
There are 4 basic room prices (in addition to suites and a family room), for the different annexes - Standard, Garden Facing, Deluxe and Superior, with and without breakfast option. The very good breakfast is $15 if ordered separately, and about half that if included in the room price. On this trip, I stayed at different times in the Standard and the Garden Facing rooms. My friend had stayed in the Deluxe room. The beds and pillows are very comfortable in all the rooms. A hot water pot, with coffee/tea, is in each room.
The best value is the Garden Facing room. The Deluxe is almost double the price, and from what I saw, primarily has a bigger garden window and a glass enclosure for the shower. The Superior room, located in the newest annex, is even more costly. My Garden Facing room had a good view, but the toilet/shower had a tub with no shower door or even a curtain, so water splashed from the tub over the floor when showering. It really should be upgraded with a shower enclosure or curtain. The Standard room that I stayed in for one night was almost the same price as the Garden Facing room; however, it is unattractive, with no view from the window, no closet, with a desk but not even a small suitcase table, and with the smallest bathroom of any guesthouse I have stayed in; the shower head is above the sink and toilet (see photo), which floods the floor. It was a mistake to book it. Be careful about the booking, since the Standard room is not always distinguished from the Garden Facing room.
Also, since our return flight was later in the evening, we asked about late checkout. The only option was paying 50% of the room charge additional, to stay from 12 to 6 PM. And if your breakfast was included in the original booking, the 50% was applied also to that, even though no more food was offered! Somewhat of a unfriendly ripoff. 
I enjoyed my stay very much, but my lower rating was primarily because of the high price for the mediocre quality of the Standard room, as well as the excessive late checkout fee.

This is a section of Kathmandu that has pretty much everything that a visitor would want. From trinkets to all hiking clothes and equipment, there’s a lot of competition.

There’s lots of restaurants and hotels of all levels as well if you want to be right in the heart of it.

Bargaining hard is a must like any big tourist market. 
Offer 1/3 of the asking price and don’t worry that it sounds too low as they’ll try to get a very high price initially as well. 
Also, remember that much of the “brand names” are counterfeit and will be much less than the real ones. The quality may or may not be what’s expected. 

Have fun!

It was so cool to be around so many monkeys.  We were approached by someone that was willing to be our guide but that is totally not needed.  In fact that would take away a lot of the experience.  There was a dog that was playing with one of the monkeys and something happened to agitate the monkey and next thing I know there was 7 monkeys that pounced on this dog.  The dog got a little hurt but not too bad.  It was just crazy how they can turn.

Someone else there had picked up some cookies and were feeding the monkeys.  They would hold out the cookie and the monkey would hold onto their hand and reach up to take the cookie.  My daughter bought some cookies and we did the same.

We were sitting near the water fountain at the top and about 30 monkeys ran near us.  One jumped on my lap and reached into my daughters pocket and pulled out the remaining cookies.  

It was truly an amazing experience.  Maybe a little scary at times but we really were never in danger and it makes for great stories and memories

OR2K is okay.  It's not great.  The location and decor are attractive.  I can see why some people would like it.  It has a real chill vibe.  It's the type of place you would expect first time backpackers to go to.
The music didn't really match the rest of the atmosphere.
The menu is vast.  It was hard to pick just a couple items.  I've only been once and cannot speak for the entire menu.
I had a juice that was good and a turkish sampler plate.  The food was honestly disappointing.  The hummus has a hard dry layer on top because it wasn't freshly served and it mainly tastes like tahini.  The bread was just ok.  The tomato sauce was very plain.
The service was bellow average.  It took a long time for anybody to take our order.  They dropped off our food 20 min later and never checked on us again.
   Overall, lunch was disappointing.  We expected much more from a  place with so many great reviews.  Lesson learned - consider the location of the restaurant when evaluating reviews.

The staff were friendly and welcoming too.

One downside for me was that, although the pool is beautiful, it was extremely cold to swim in. I tried on the first morning I was there and it was freezing cold, so went later that day, around 4p.m. when the sun had been on it all day, but unfortunately it was still extraordinarily cold. I did swim that day, but had no inclination to subject myself to such temperatures again and so for the remaining 3 days of my stay there was effectively no pool facility.

Another was that I chose this particular hotel to relax in as it was in such a perfect position right on the lake. Disappointingly, the sawing (metal cutting?) noise coming from somewhere on the grounds from 7:50a.m. till 6p.m. disturbed that  pleasant idea. Sitting, reading on my balcony with a drink and a nice view was simply not an option.

A further disappointment was that I had requested a room with a double bed and was given a twin-bedded room. This was made worse because I noticed that the hotel was nowhere near full and so asked if I could change to a double bedded room, but was told that there were none available. The hotel remained fairly empty until my final (4th) night when it did fill up.

The room itself was spacious and clean. However, the layout of the room was quite interesting as the table and chairs were placed so close to one of the beds that you couldn't even get to them, never mind sit on them (photo attached). There was a damp patch on one of the walls (photo attached)  and, although this didn't smell and was quite well-hidden by one of the beds, it still should be dealt with. Some of the furniture in the room was past its best and flies were also a bit of a problem if you left the window open for too long, though there was a plug-in mosquito killer so mossies weren't a problem in the room (not that I noticed them being a problem at all, even outside, to be honest).

The bathroom was fairly standard with a shower attachment in the bath; this had lost some of its outer cover though and so easily became twisted, thus cutting off the water until it was untwisted again. Hot water was plentiful and seemed to be available all through the day and evening, but I thought it was a little mean not to have hair  conditioner or body lotion available for guests  in addition to the shampoo and shower gel.

Most annoying was that one day I came back from breakfast to find maintenance being carried out in my room, without any prior warning. There was a man with a drill  who was fixing a wall mounted coat rack onto the wall (though I hadn't noticed any problem with this before I left for breakfast and hadn't had any clothes hanging from it). I tried to ask why this was being done while the room was occupied and to find out how long the work would take but was met with incomprehension (the poor maintenance guy obviously couldn't understand English and had just been sent to do a job) so ended up just getting changed in the bathroom, going out and leaving him to his work.

A final annoyance was that the information in the hotel's booklet says that airport transfers are free, but when I reached the airport I was charged and told that it's only a one way free airport transfer! They really should change that information in their booklets as it's misleading.

So, overall it is a nice hotel, in a calm and relaxing location, with spacious, reasonably well kept rooms, however, there are some irritations and annoyances to guests and some maintenance issues should be addressed (whilst rooms are unoccupied!).

When I first came here 35 years ago, the review would have been 5 STARS. I fell in love with Nepal. Thamel was not yet well established and many tourists stayed in the New Road area. All that has changed dramatically, especially in Thamel. 
Read the 1 and 2 star reviews on Thamel below, they describe the current situation accurately. No need for me to just repeat what they already said.
Every year I arrive, happy to be back in Nepal, and after 2 days can't wait to leave Kathmandu, especially Thamel. 
Why? Traffic became a problem many years ago, so a Walking Street area throughout most of Thamel was established. It was a wonderful and much-needed change, and transformed the streets into a pleasant, safe, attractive hotel and shopping area for tourists. 
Thamel is the main tourist area of Kathmandu and should be protected as such. Streets are narrow with very few sidewalks, and not intended for heavy commercial traffic and many motorcycles driving unsafely, even crazy, from morning to night.
 But the COVID pandemic stopped tourism in early 2020, and therefore business. So the businessmen opened Thamel up again to traffic, setting up discos, and inviting young locals  in. I think that was the most atrocious event in the downhill slide.  When COVID was over in 2022, the Walking Street area was not re-established. But it is desperately needed. 
Evening on the streets has become impossibly distasteful. Very loud, dangerous traffic, and thick exhaust fumes adding to the already very unhealthy AQI. Trying to go out for a nice meal hardly seems worth the trouble. And now the discos add more uncomfortable noise in some guesthouses late at night.

I realised after she demanded 1,000 rupees for the gesture it wasn't out of the goodness of her heart! I gave her 100 rupees and left with her still giving out. 

Don't be as foolish as me!

Noisy narrow crowded streets packed with dusty shops and peaceful garden restaurants. At first, all this commotion annoyed me, but over time the man gets used to it and starts to enjoy all that stir. Rickshaws, motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians all share same narrow road. No sidewalks. In all these narrow streets you can spent days and days. Tourist area.

After reading reviews and comparing the different accommodations in Kathmandu we decided to go for KGH. Upon arriving we were immediately impressed by the lovely garden patio away from all the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu´s streets, however were disappointed by the rooms. We were given a standard room on the 5th floor - no elevators, which would be hell if we had big suitcases, but seeing as we were in Nepal for trekking we only had backpacks and weren´t bothered by climbing up a few flights of stairs. What bothered us was the noise. They had construction on our floor all day long, which was horrible as we got no sleep on our flight and would´ve liked a short nap before heading out to explore the city. We also heard the people and motorcycles on the street the entire night. The room itself was decent and had the basics, but bathrooms could´ve been better as the showers had no partition and would clog up, flooding the entire bathroom. Yes, we used slippers while showering. In general the staff were friendly, however we found that they trick guests into booking tours, transportation and guides through them for ridiculously high prices. We´re a young couple used to traveling and finding our own way around and when we travel we trust that the hotel would give us genuine recommendations of what to see/do rather than just try to sell you their package tours for 4 times the price they would be one step outside the hotel. It seemed that once they found out we preferred to do things on our own (take a taxi for 2,000 rupees instead of the 10,000 they were charging for a private car, hike through basic trails on our own instead of hiring their guide, etc.) they were uninterested in helping us or giving us further information. It also didn´t help that their internet was really slow so we couldn´t search for things on our own, although compared to other hotels around the area it seemed as if there wouldn´t really be anything much better as that´s just how the Kathmandu standards are. If it weren´t for the noise and their receptionist who tried fooling us I would´ve thought that the place is pretty decent and above par compared to the rest of the hotels.

Even though this is by far the nicest area of Kathmandu and a good place to see locals go about doing their bussiness its also really touristy with some places almost looking like Kao San road, Bangkok. And also its very very very(yes three times) busy with traffic making it at unpleasant to walk around most of the times. But still this is the area you want your hotel or hostel to be in cause the rest of Kathmandu is worse.

I have been a mountaineer on some level most of my life.  I was really interested in the  mountain history,  photos, geology,  equipment, stories, and people portrayed in this museum.  The  architecture is also outstanding

A nice hotel that we stayed in at the last minute.   More resort than hotel really, with kids playing football on the lawn beside the balcony, so not much in the way of peace and quiet, but that was fine.  The rooms were large and comfortable, a bit dark, but fine.  The real issue was the odd attitude of some of the young men waiters - eye roll and a shrug when we asked for a pot of tea rather than just a cup, seriously cheeky at breakfast then not turning up with what we had requested - it almost felt deliberate, not helpful at pre-dinner drinks - along the lines of are you SURE that's what you want, have you managed to get it RIGHT this time.   It seemed as if these young men had watched someone in management being too familiar and dismissive of guests, and felt it was OK to be the same.  It's training, that's all, but it left us as a group saying that we would not come back to face that sort of behaviour again.

I would avoid this hotel for anything.
The rooms in the annexe have walls of such poor quality, that I could hear the TV if your adjacent room loud and clear!! I could also hear all sorts of noise coming from the corridor. With the price you pay for this hotel, I could not even get a good nights sleep due to all this noise.
Then there are loads of other small problems like the flush buttons in bathroom broken, the head shower spraying holes clogged.
For a hotel claimimg to be 5 star, i dont expect such issues, especially with their room rates being over the roof. 
I wouldnt like to stay here for my next trip.
Lake Retreat is where calm meets cuisine. Fresh, wholesome dishes crafted with seasonal flavors, served against the backdrop of garden and pools—every bite feels like a breath of peace.
Just great place to have night out.Lots choice for bars and restaurents and hotel to stay.highly recommended to try kathmandu steak house restaurent.

Will never return to this hotel considering the poor wifi, TV problem, lack of variety on buffett menu and for over-charging my non-Indian colleaugue. Unfortunately pollutions are very disturbing in a "holy" square.

Good vegetarian and even vegan. The best Humus i had in Asia. Nice and professional staff, the food comes quickly. I was never disappointed.

Overall there are only few places of tourist interests in Kathmandu and this is one of them which Kathmandu people say is a tourist location. But we found nothing as such. That too old, dusty and broken homes (mostly because of earthquake in 2015). So doesn't make any sense in watching such city from this place.
Not worth climbing the steps, all of Kathmandu is still struggling with the effects of the terrible earthquake. The monument area is filthy covered with rubbish that need not be there
Amazing place. A lot of earthquake damage still, but they are working hard to repair. Still lots of buildings to see.

A pleasant comfortable short stay. The staff was very cooperative and willing to full fill all need. Bar is nicely equipped with good service food was also excellent. Overall experience good like to visit again with family

Kathmandu hotels have made big strides in terms of service and amenities; sadly, Radisson hasn't kept up with the trend. Arrived at the hotel just before 1pm and was told to wait until 2pm to check in; this was not noted anywhere on the reservation I made through hotels.com. Housekeeping failed to update my room with basic amenities over the course of my 3-night stay, and there was a leak in the bathroom. My room was an echo chamber: Doors slammed continually throughout the night, guests shouted and played music in the hallway, construction drilled outside, and furniture slid across the ground overhead. When I reported my concerns, little was done to make amends. To add insult to injury, my Nepali colleague commented that when he entered the building alongside me, he was greeted by the doormen. When he returned to the hotel alone, however, he was gazed upon skeptically and didn't receive the same courtesy. On a positive note, the sauna on the 4th floor is a nice place to relax and the gym is equipped with cardio and weight machines, yet I can't say this perk is enough to warrant another stay.

This is an extraordinary environment. Probably the best restaurant real-estate in Pokhara. A great place to go with friends in the afternoon for lunch or drinks or dinner. Plenty of outdoor seating. Wonderful indoor seating with great views out the giant windows. 

This is a vegetarian restaurant, so no meat. I was also not particularly impressed by any of the dishes I tried (Pad Thai, Veg Soup, fried rice). Loved going there to read and have a drink in the afternoon though.

We booked 3 delux room for family of three and we told my family has 2 adult 2 kids and another family has 2 adult and a kid. We were given only twin bed room and upon asking to help with extra bed we were given and asked to adjust for a night.

None of the room have an intercom and one even without a telephone set. it was extremely difficult to contact the reception in the night. 

There were no instruction what to do as we we needed extra pillow ( no way to contact reception). It was winter month and room is very cold. Our AC remote was broken and there was no way to contact reception. All we could do is yell for help disturbing other guest.

There was used drinking glass in the room. Toilet accessories unavailable and some very poor quality. Other very minor observation were adjacent room can hear your conversation, very weak wifi, miss-spelled places i.e. cleen for clean etc. ,uncooked smelly bacon at breakfast. 

Next morning we called and spoke to Manager  Mob.+977 9802810555 so that we could discuss some of the above problems and give our feedback. Hotel manger said he could meet us in10 min but did not come for 30min when asked at the reception we were told he was sick.

We decided to get up early one morning when in Pohkara to see the sunrise from the Sarangkot mountain. We had great views from the tea house but it was rather crowded. Still, the views of all the mountains were amazing.

I was in a 2 week trip in Nepal and I stayed at many different hotels. From 3* to 5*. By far this was my favorite of them all! 

The hotel looks like a palace and the personnel makes you feel like you are the Queen. 

The location is amazing and the food at the restaurant is incredible. Breakfast is basic/standard but you can ask for whatever you want. They have a wifi router in each room, so you will have good internet all the time. 

The morning yoga/meditation sessions are amazing. They are free of charge and a great way to start the day. 

This is a eco-friendly hotel, so it's very important that if you decide to stay here you are 100% aware that you won't have a television, air conditioning or bottled water. They provide filtered water every day for drinking and they use solar panels to heat the water in the shower, so the hot water will come a little bit slower but it will come. 

If you are after the amenities of a 4* or 5* hotel, this hotel is not for you. But if you are interested in a very unique experience, then I would highly recommend Kantipur Temple House. 

I will definitely use it again if I ever go back to Nepal.
Overall experience is excellent and staff is very nice polite and nice. Only improvements they need us bathrooms. Water keep blocking and taps and showers are old.

I really enjoyed the stay. The location is also good though the communication is slow due to traffic Condition. I will suggest more efficient transport if possible. Hospitality is as expected. Hope to join again in future.

There are a lot of temple there but almost was damaged. Hope they will renovate soon. Entrance fee is too high by the way

There is no place to sit if you come a little late.  yes, the mountains are always beautiful, but pick a day or season when you won't have to jossle for a view.

Must visit this place if you are into mountains. Small, a bit neglected, though demonstrating fascinating info mostly on the Nepali mountain climbing and the equipment of the pioneers conquered Everest

OR2K offers a wide range of Asian, Israeli and middle eastern food. We came here twice during our short stay in Pokhara because it was that good :) the place is cute, nicely decorated and has a big outdoors space overlooking the lake.

Check-in was a disaster: it took 15 minutes and some harsh negotiation for them to finally assign the double rooms with lake view we had booked. Only mild excuses were given and no compensation was provided. 

Furthermore, they charged Rs 750 per day and per device to get internet in the rooms which is a total rip off in 2013. The paint of the rooms was a bit worn out especially on the bathroom door. Breakfast quality and choice were quite average, but the smiles of the staff helped.

Not sure that I would choose this hotel again if I went back to Pokhara.

He was attentive and personable.
People make the experience better or worse and Milan c certainly made our time at Radisson KTM better.
All staff were great , food was good and the rooms comfortable.

The garden area is beautiful and the service is great however the rooms are small with no air con. Considering the price for this hotel- I wouldn't consider it value for money in the region and would recommend alternative. Location is very central but it is expensive for what you get- small very basic room with no air con

The restaurant is baby friendly with an option of high chair for infants.  Also, appreciate the hospitality from the staff and particularly Sabina!

I had good experience on my stay. Friendly staff, hygienic, cozy environment with nice lake view. Peaceful and isolated area. Trainee Salina Dahal was warm and respectful.however, there were some improvement needed on food & bar options and amenities.

I have stayed there a few times, one time you pay 3,000 rupees and the other 5,000 rupees. I recently booked a standard room. On arrival, they had only the luxury rooms which is not a problem because I got an upgrade. The next day I had to pay extra for my breakfast. Because I had slept in a deluxe! But this is not my fault; they made a mistake. After a discussion at the reception, I did not have to pay for breakfast. I think it's a little low for a hotel or guesthouse with such a reputation.

I also visited the OR2k in Kathmandu and ate the same meal but the one in Pokhara was tastier by far. The portion was also bigger. OR2K Pokhara had a beautiful view of Lake Fewa (Phewa) the meal was delicious.  The server was courteous and attentive. Very chill ambience, cool and laid back. The place was impeccably clean as well. Very enjoyable experience.

Dusty, dirty and hawkers trying to sell you anything and everything at ridiculous prices. Get what you have to get done and get out of there.

Some of the temples are under construction and some of them are live supported with extra wooden pillars. Its really nice hotel and awesome service its our group trip its central of the thamel its amazing place thank you so much for your service i will definitely recommend your place and specially thank you mr. Prabin (manager)i will definitely coming back to your hotel
Still suffering quite badly from the earthquake a few years ago. Definitely worth a visit but a lot of building going on. Usual problems with sellers.
could be so much better but rubbish spoils the nature of the place which is slowly getting more polluted and deforested and it won't be long before it is all ruined.

After some of the lakes out in the mountains this one is kinda average, but it's pleasant to sit at one of the bars on the lake and watch the world go by. The little boats on the lake are pretty. We were disappointed that you couldn't walk around the lake.
Wonderful experience . The staff were very polite and excellent service . Receptionist Ayushma’s service was exemplary . The room was very good and we had a very relaxed time
What a wonderful lake also temple in the middle.Many peolpe are getting occupation also but local people need be alert about its future

Thamel, the main tourist area, should be a place to enjoy, but it has become a place to arrange my trek and then leave as quickly as possible. Very difficult for walking slow and window shopping, without worrying about getting hit by a vehicle.
Thamel should be tourist friendly, and walking streets only, with allowances made for slow-moving delivery vehicles.  It would be much better for all tourists and most businesses.

Housing choice for backpacker, convenient and full of b&b, hostel, apartment choices. Easy to get shoppings, tourist information, money exchange, restaurants, cafes and bars.
Lots to see as you walk around and the vast number of pigeons flying around and cows wandering are fun for photos.

It was a beautiful square to be in especially during Happy Holi festivities. We hired a guide for a nominal fee which was great to get a historical perspective. Lots of damage from earthquakes, and lots of rebuilding.

It is a run down hotel with an old casino and dysfunctional room amenities. The good part is the casino is right on the entrance yet it does not disturb your stay. Hire a bike and go around the whole lake and it is the best way to see it. You will need to go via the peace pagoda

He is very good at spotting birds and monkeys and took us to the best places to see them. It was very peaceful and scenic to be on the lake in the morning while there were few other boaters and there were lots of birds to see.
Take a taxi at 04:30 for a 30-minute ride to Sarangkot and see the sun rise form behind the Himalayas. It's a great sight. The taxi will get you back in time for a 7:00 breakfast at your hotel.
I visited Sarangkot mountain top to see the sunrise and the Annapurana mountains. The sunrise point was really crowded with tourists and locals to see the amazing sunrise over Himalayas.

Maintenance has been ignored for too long and due to the downturn in tourism to Nepal the hotel have been selling heavily discounted packages to Indian tour groups. I am informed that these groups largely comprise employees of Indian corporate houses who send their people to Nepal on incentive holidays. Thamel is the main tourist center of Kathmandu.  It is a constant whirlwind of dust, noise, taxis, tuk-tuks, motorcycles and street vendors. The hotel reception is an open 'hut' type of space located in the middle of the resort which you can see on their website homepage (about 30m from all of the rooms) and you can hear EVERY conversation the reception staff have on the phone.  So when it starts rining at 4am and the staff speak at the top of their voice, and walls are paper thin, there is nothing that will put you back to sleep.

I found it quieter when I stayed in a cheaper hotel in the centre of town 20mins up the road at a fraction of the cost of this place.

My lesson learned is that in future I won't compromise perceived 'luxury' for the cultural experience.  I wasted my money on this hotel and would have preferred to go back to the cheaper hotel in the middle of town for better sleep and location.

I was quite skeptical towards the concept of the "international", because it is very hard to deal with the whole world's mountaineering history in one go. You have to decide for yourself if the institution manages to deliver in this respect - for me, it should be "National Mountaineering Museum." You can see the different hill tribes of Nepal, their regalia and tools, so the section in the beginning is more of an anthropological exhibition. Later on there are sections dealing with the mountain regions of some countries (Japan, Taiwan, Slovenia...so supposedly those nations who could provide/donate a small exhibition for the museum). The exhibition that shows the first ascents for the 8000ers is really interesting, with original equipment, small stories, pictures, and routes. Since I am interested in mountaineering, I would really like to see more of this (even things from later expeditions), and then the museum would be perfect for me. The garbage-themed section is good as well, and I enjoyed the information about the wildlife too. Definitely worth a visit, but it is not only about mountaineering. It is about the mountains.
