Need to buy tickets but different rate for SAARC and others.

Beautiful gardens welcome you at your arrival after the messy roads of Thamel, they represent a real oasis. BUT, if you have a room on the non-renewed aisle of the hotel, be prepared to a very basic interior atmosphere and to an uncomfortable bathroom, even without hair-dryer (you need to ask for it) and fridge; coffee and teas are available instead.
Spaces are not well cleaned.
Wellness center (on surcharge according to the services) is very good.
Wi-Fi works on and off depending on electric power that frequently fails.
Breakfast is of great variety and really good, with gardens’ view and walk of fame! The plus is surely the historical atmosphere of this place.

The hotel building is beautiful with deep Nepalese architecture, but don't let this fool you. Where to start? The staff here at Kantipur certainly donâ??t bend over backwards trying to help you. We stayed for one night and wished we never had.

After registering our names after arrival at hotel, we were made to wait for over 40min at the lobby, with no information on when we could check in. When we asked when we could check-in, the lady rudely barked that they were extremely busy with check-out clients and couldnâ??t help for another hour or so. Had they told us earlier, we would have been happy check-in in the late afternoon, or leave our luggage there. 

We had a lovely room on the top floor, level 4. However, outside our front door we were greeted with a stained mattress that was edged on the window. Permanent ugly housekeeping reminders.

Donâ??t expect any service on travel advice or directions either. They donâ??t give out tourist map. 

At the hotel restaurant, we ordered the buffet menu but was then later told we had to go outside to the garden and get the food ourselves to then bring back inside the restaurant. After agreeing to this, when we went to the garden, the chef advised that the buffet dinner was now closed. You can imagine the shock horror to the start of our dinner. Things just got worse when they completely missed two courses of the dinner and tried to charge us for something we didnâ??t have! And to top it off, we were made to feel like we had to rush our dinner because their kitchen closes at 9pm. 

The next morning at the hotel breakfast, we kept getting pestered by scammers who wanted to be our tour guide, and handed out dodgy business cards. On the last day, the hotel ripped us off by setting a ridiculously high price to a taxi driver to take us to the airport. 

A day after we left, we received a courtesy follow up email from Kantipur. The email itself was nicely worded and sounded warm. However, they obviously didn't even bother to proofread it as the email asked us about some tours we didn't even go on. 

All in all, despite the delightful heritage building, the hotel service leaves a lot to be desired. In terms of service, it was one of our worst hotel experience ever.
It was a so so activity, though based on rating here I expected it to be much better. I was missing some great mountaineers on display to give it a more generous information.

Where the hell is this place had me walking around for ages if this place is closed then update it accordingly!!
What a waste of time
Patan Durbar Square is much better and less crowded. Most of the buildings in Kathmandu Durbar Square collapsed after the earthquake and they are still repairing them.
A highlight in Pokhara. For a trekking/mountain enthusiast, this is a great place to spend a couple of hours.

Me and my friend had booked to stay here for 3 nights. When we arrived, we were shown a dingy, musty room with a broken window in the middle of the freezing January cold! When we complained about this, we were told we could just shut the bathroom door, which of course didn't shut. We were then shown a different room, which was equally as cold and had no heating. The bed was literally a bed frame with no mattress and the bedding was mouldy and disgusting.There is no hot water in this hotel either and it runs cold and brown from the tap. 

The next day after this nightmare first night, we were moved into a third room which was dingy, damp and smelly. After half an hour in it a huge cockroach appeared and started crawling up the wall. This was the final straw for us and we left this hotel and headed to Pariwar B&B, which is a much cleaner alternative at the same price. 

The only redeeming feature of this hotel is the very friendly staff, who were very helpful throughout our stay. However, I feel that people should be aware that the majority of reviews on TripAdvisor are misleading and that this hotel is VERY cold and uncomfortable.

Museum is great and informative. It has lot of artifacts which displays various cultures of Neal's mountainous region. They have a short movie screening every hour. Factor in couple of hours. A bit far from the city centre so plan accordingly so you do not get late for lunch. It will take more time if you read every bit of information.

Unfortunately this lake is now so polluted I'd not want to take my young kids on it. The cost of the boats seems a little on the expensive side. Walking around it lakeside is good if the air quality is good.

Completely avoid this place at any cost!
They apply 10%sevice charge and 20% government tax without telling you in advance!
Service extremely rude and incompetent staffs! The restaurant was completely empty now I understand why!
How can they cook italien Indian and Chinese in the same time! 
To avoid absolutely juste a wast of time!

Don't misunderstand me here . It's a holy place but I enjoyed the sushi served at one of the restaurants and the view offered by the roof top restaurants is truly beautiful. 
You can see a lot of people praying on the lower levels. A windy place and the eyes of the Buddha reach out to all the four directions . This is a good place for shopping and the market is on the outer  periphery of the stupa. Entry fees for Indians is 50NPR

This place is worth a visit, the information and artefacts are well presented. 
The building is impressive.

Friendly staffs and excellent environment, food was great. The location and the overall cleanliness was outstanding. But at the time of check in there was no welcome drink ( there was a drink in the lobby by no so good)

Don’t go on Buddha’s birthday if you are not Hindi/Buddhist as the temples were packed to capacity celebrating Buddha’s birthday. I enjoyed the colour vibrancy and feel of celebration of the crowds, but the congestion of foot traffic was difficult to navigate.

The setting of OR2K in Pokhara can't be more different that that of the Kathmandu branch, but it works. Situated right in the centre of Pokhara, it's light and airy with lovely views of the lake. Seating is at tables or on the floor, and even during the day the ambiance is great.

The food is to die for - varied, fresh, well-presented. Any vegetarian's dream, but also for lovers of middle eastern dishes. And the portions are huge. No really, they are HUGE!

I would suggest that the service be notched up a bit. Although very friendly and helpful, it did take some effort to attract attention and the food took quite long to make its appearance.

A solid recommendation though. Getting hungry just writing this review!

Convenient to all the shopping and restaurants in Pokhara. Not at all what I would call luxury. Pleasant environs, staff OK, not overly solicitous, quiet, terrible breakfast (but then again, this meal was not a high spot in Nepal) that was included. Rooms decent, spread out into lots small buildings. No shelves in the bathroom to put anything, mildew sink/shower, amenities poor (no conditioner, no facial tissue), wifi terrible, concierge could use some schooling. It works though.

The resort type property is not exactly lakeside but a good distance from the lake. There are a number of single storied huts and as well as double storied ones. Our room was large enough but the small capacity Air conditioner could not work effectively during the daytime. The food was quite average. Will look for other options next time.

amazing, you can see the best view of lake in this restaurant, lovely design, delicious foods, free wifi, good service, etc.
I highly recommend this restaurant.
I liked the museum. It has all it can possibly need. I would like more activities, but it's still good.

The hotel certainly has some character. But their cheaper rooms in the old wing leave a lot to be desired. The (separate) toilets are not clean and the showers have no mirrors. Rooms are just so..so. I stayed in 2 of the rooms and both had broken fans. Plenty of better value nearby. 

But that's not the worst. All the doors of the rooms on the left side of the old wing (of at least the first floor) have pretty wide vertical slits in them. I saw a waiter peeping through a slit into a room where I knew a couple of girls were staying! Ladies have been warned.

To be fair, we ate here two weeks ago, and the food knocked our socks off. The goat cheese pasta and veggie sizzler were top-shelf.

Last night was a different tune. The mushroom soup was pretty much pure garlic and no salt. The mayo, which I think they make in-house, was just not good, and the same went for their house-made butter, which I found to be inedible. We had found ourselves really amazed by the soups, butter and mayo at their Pokhara location, so we were surprised to find that all were pretty bad here in Kathmandu.

We found the staff to be majorly apathetic and abrupt, and a majority of the ten servers stood around texting and fixing their hair. 

We won't be returning to this location, but I would recommend their Pokhara location for some great eats if you don't mind that the wait staff are a bit abrupt as well.

Great place to learn about the forefathers of mountaineering such as Edmund Hillary, Tensing Norgey, George Mallory, etc. It has many pictures where you can gather so much knowledge about mountaineering, history of Nepal, etc.
A very good place to learn more about the history culture customs of Nepal. Very informative, easy to see, well sign.
Rooms very spacious with air-conditioning and bath tub with restaurant and bar.  Location opposite taxi stand on Main road

Very nice temple with many layers up high on the mountain. This temple has many monuments besides the main stupa that are really nice along with shops and a place where paintings are available that are reasonable and local.

The Temple Tree Resort is a beautiful place to stay.  The food is good, also.  The problem is the next door construction.  During the day all you hear are saws running and people hammering.  I stayed November 2014.  I would advise anyone to wait several months for construction to finish before staying there.  If you like a hard bed, you'll love it.  If you like a soft bed, this is not the place for you.  One other complaint I had was that although the front desk staff spoke tolerable English, the room service people nor the laundry service did.

It’s quite empty and dark for a museum. Some mountaineering gears in display and faded story boards. For all the history and adventures that have been written about the Nepali mountains, there should be more substantial exhibitions for the better.

Great stay at waterfront we enjoyed a lot that we even extended and stayed more the food was amazing the people were welcoming. 
Front desk was so helpful Ms Rakriti ,Biswas, nabina was so helpful .we are great full for there service .We really enjoyed and we loved here !!

Although there is a little bit of rubbish around it, the lake is well worth a visit as it is very picturesque and there are a lot of nice restaurants and cafes situated around it.  You can sit and watch the paragliders. 

You can hire a boat to take you across if you choose.

I greatly enjoyed reading about the historical aspect of mountaineering. The museum also displayed historical  artifact  of the region & its people.  i could have stayed longer, but the museum closed one hour earlier - no reason given.
I thing very beautiful place and you must visit (this place is must have). There is entrance fee and not much. Lot of temples and monuments. I recommend this place.

it is a colourful area and with good ambience.  a lot of shop and restaurant.  club and pubs. the streets r nice and good. may not be clean and bit noisy. but i liked it. as tourist, u need to come here many times for many needed. i visited this place many times. be careful while walking as streets can be really busy.

Issues plagued my stay from start to finish. The room had maintenance issues, however some of the bar staff were rude and appeared displeased to be serving me. To top it off, my 'private' car to the airport, which came at a premium, was a minibus, and I ended up in a taxi due to other guests being late. Maintenance issues aren't ideal but happen, however poor service is inexcusable.

Durbar Square is a must visit for anyone staying in Kathmandu for any length of time. Reach it by New Road or by walking through narrow busy back streets full of people and activities from Thamel. Square has antiquities for sale, museums nearby and temples all around. Enjoy!

This hotel is very central just off the main shopping area and lake.
Rooms are spacious and clean with lovely bathrooms.
A nice small pool bit with not to many sun beds (12).
Breakfast and lunch menu limited compared to some large chains but food very good.
Coffee at breakfast like hot water.
Only thing let's hotel down is the staff friendly but don't seem to have much management so dirty plates left lying around and if you want to eat breakfast outside need to find your own cutlery etc.
Good be excellent with some staff training !

Woke up at 4.30am to be ready for departure. Be clothed warmly.

A much awaited moment with many gathered together, whispers and chatting amongst local friends and tourists. Worth a trip to see the Himalayan Mountains.

Dirty town full of crap copy North Face gear

Dont waste more than day here

The shops all sell the same gear. Its ok. But not for anyone who wants any variety. The quality is pretty low

I have visited this site a few times over the last 15 years but this time was disappointed to see how it had changed. Walking up the steps to reach the stupa you are stopped and made to pay a 300 rupee entry. I don’t mind paying but as the price for “foreigners” is more than three times what others pay I find this unfair. It happens on sights all over Nepal and also India and its disappoints me. Once I reached the top I was shocked to see that this holy sight has just become a souvenir shop! On this visit I got no sense that this was a religious site as I had experienced before. I know there has. been some impact from the earthquake and some rebuilding work is going on but the atmosphere was different to what I had experienced at other sites impacted more by the earthquake. 

I wouldn’t suggest people don’t visit here but I personally was sad with how it has changed.

The Hyatt Regency claims it is a luxury 5 star hotel.  It may have been when it opened but not longer should make that claim.   On the plus side, the outer building and grounds are beautiful, three tennis courts, great pool and lovely lobby.  On the minus side, the hotel needs both maintenance and renovation.  Windows are not clean, restaurants are mediocre, there is no bartender at the bar, rooms are fine decor wise but the mattresses feel old and not supportive, the door key often does not work, the AC at the coldest setting still leaves the room too warm even thought it is only mid 70s during the day and cool outside at night, common areas and restaurants also too warm so sit outside if you can, shower design makes it a challenge not to get lots of water into the bathroom, and service while ok is not at the level one expects for a Hyatt Regency.

my husband and i stayed 2 nights via point redeem.  luckily, the reception simply upgraded our room without asking.  the first night was so great because the hotel isn't located in Thamel district so it was so quiet and the room itself was so nice and cozy.  however, the 2nd night was a bit terrible: the night clubs surrounding hotel played music crazily and our room was right in the opposite to one of the most crazy night club.  we could dance with their music in our room!  we complained 3 times to the hotel will 10pm but they could not really manage external parties.  meanwhile, something wrong with hotel hot shower so we couldn't take hot shower before 10:30pm. we shared our needs of having a quiet sleep to the reception and they were kindly offering us another room for one night sleep without repackaging our stuff!  furthermore, they offered us a free late check out which was super generous since our flight was 11pm!
我用點數換了兩晚住宿。入住時reception直接升等。第一晚超棒的，因為飯店不在熱鬧繁華的Thamel，所以安靜而舒適。然而第二晚變得很可怕，因為飯店外的夜店以全區共同開趴的心態大放音樂。因為我們房間正是夜店正對面，音樂大聲到我們在房裡可以隨著音樂跳舞了！跟飯店抱怨了三次，然而我們也清楚這不是他們的問題。屋漏偏逢連夜雨，當天熱水器出了問題而要等到10:30pm左右才能洗澡，但我們真的累壞了，只想早早睡覺。所以飯店提供了另一房給我們睡一晚，而且完全不用搬動行李！甚至還給我們免費的late check out！
Beautiful lake spattered with colourful boats. And a lot to do here, watching sunrise, hiking, paragliding...

Great food - an abundance of choices - all vegetarian. Plenty of seating (at tables, or on the floor), indoors and outdoors. Service sometimes a bit slow, but friendly. Good value. Wifi is sometimes a bit sketchy, but most of the time is OK. But for the food - one of the best in Pokhara!

A very good stay in katmandu, hotel with good installations and service, i will stay herre again if its possible, the service in restaurant and grill excellent, and a very tasty food.

I need to add that the location was very good. 

All the family love it !!

Thanks a lot Radisson.

We stayed here for 4 nights, in a standard room booked to have a double bed (for a couple) but got two single beds. Room was clean with hot shower in private bathroom however very noisy with thin walls, easily woken up in night to other guests. Staff were very friendly and rooftop garden was a gem we had to ourselves every sunset. There was no social vibe if looking to meet other travellers or trekkers though.

Thamel is a must visit to feel Kathmandu. A traffic free zone having some great cafes and bars. We were family of 4 and went in the evening. Someone said, the area is not suitable for families in night. I don't know how true it is, but I didn't visit this area in night after hearing this

I visited this place this month. Place is just nice according to me. 
They charged Rs 300/person INR as entry fee. Just after entry, they asked for Rs 50 INR for a very small museum but I left that place. 
Palace was built with small size mud brick which is somehow maintained with various support. 
Another things I disliked most was usage of palace places as restaurants. Few buildings were in such condition that you can go and 1st floor but all were either occupied by Restaurants or Hotel etc. Why they have charged me so high!
Another noticeable things inside palace was market. There are many shops inside palace. 
Overall, I have not felt like I am in Palace.
But, when I Kathmandu, you can visit there so that you know that you have been to Kathmandu. :)

First of all for everyone to know, remember, mostly in the the packages offered to u by your Travel agent(indian), sarangkot is optional,so confirm first, and sunrise trip is not included, so negotiate accordingly else u will have to arrange it yourself, shelling out another 2000npr for taxi. Secondly paragliding etc starts at 10am, So u will miss sunrise, if you select paragliding thinking you will visit Sarangkot anyways. 
 
Try reaching the venue at least 45 minutes before, as there is a steep stairs you have to climb.  Not recommended for young and old ppl, as it quite taxing. There is another view point at the base,  but exactly not the same view.

Weather plays a important role, if its very cloudy, it can be a spoilsport and also carry proper woolens etc. 

Overall sunrise in sarangkot is  a highlight and not to be missed.

Entire stay with Radisson was amazing. Staff is fabulous. I loved their morning breakfast specially Manita. She can help to make any possible help if she can do. All cleaning staff are great to make necessary adjustments to make your room clean.

The visit to the old city, of now known as Durbar Square, is the city that has been standing there for centuries. The main city that ruled the country during the kings time. 

The square is full of ancient temple, and a place. Unfortunately at the time i visited the temples and the place was closed, as it was late night. 

However, walking along the alleyways, and the old city, you do get an aura of beauty and the skills of the ancient architecture. The building are adorned with many wooden beams and pillars which have been carved. 

Even though i visited the place late in the night, the place was active with people, and few wondering animals.

Very comfortable hotel situated in the heart of thamel in terms of location, price and friendliness. Stayed here one week on the top floor room have enough facilities like home. Accommodating staff and had all the time hot shower. Hotel have very minimum rate to mid range. most stay in standard room or deluxe room for better functional rooms. contact directly to the hotel for best price and service.

Yes ok, walk through the streets, get the vibe, sit in one of the quirky courtyards with a local beer BUT if you plan to do shopping, don’t bother doing it here! It’s so ready for the tourists that the prices are HIGH! Go to Ason Bazar and get everything, with the same or better quality and cheaper!

The hotel is good and staff is courteous. I have visited the hotel a couple of times which were quite please. The last visit was not so comfortable and hence writing this review. During my last visit there was a group of guests accomodate on my floor, having some party with room doors open, awake all night drinking and making noise which made the sleep really uncomfortable. Would appreciate if the staff can take a note of it and prevent such inconvenience in future. Although I did report this however not much was resolved except for some intervention which helped for a few hours. 
P.S. Do visit the casino if you are staying.

Amazing property, very warm people and good hospitality. The staff is very courteous and forthcoming. Food quality was good and reasonable. We were travelling with our 5 yr old daughter and the chef made sure that she was well take care off. The hotel was neat and clean. Swimming pool was good and overall felt safe. It does need to upgrade the infrastructure a bit especially the toilets and common areas. HK was a bit casual and lacked the discipline and quality of premium property. 

Overall had a good experience and wonderful memories. Chef treated us with a speciality Nan made of Carrot etc, it was very unique and amazing.

This place serves the bare minimum for food, the establishment isn't that clean, and it's mostly young college students looking for a place to recharge or get online. Good to hangout, not great to eat, at all.
The breakfast was really good fresh and hygienic. The service is very good friendly courteous and smily staffs. The rooms are really clean

Beautiful, tranquil resort accomodation at the quiet end of town. Traditional feel, warm hospitality, comfortable beds.
Spa offers lovely massages.
Buffet breakfast included - a nice surprise. Highly recommend and will stay again.

I stayed at the Hotel for 3 nights. I selected this hotel based on its authentic look which appealed to me. 

The hotels location approx 20 minutes from the airport ( at night) was quite convenient. Set back from the main road down a lane  avoiding the noise of the traffic and within easy walking distance of a number of restaurants and shops ( hiking gear, tshirts, tourist bits). There is also a supermarket 10 minutes walk in a nearby mall.

As per the pictures on the website the hotel and its grounds provide a pleasent visual.

Upon arrival staff were friendly and helpful.

I booked a deluxe room which was quite spacious. The rooms dont have aircon and instead have a fan which was quite loud but this is probably my only gripe. The room was otherwise perfectly adequate.

Breakfast was included in my rate and a buffet was provided each morning which again was ok.

For dinner i also tried the restaurant, the pricing seems inline with the restaurants nearby but i was not overly impressed with my main dish. I had the sekuwa, the meat was perhaps overcooked and therefore quite dry.

In conclusion, for the price the hotel is perfectly fine and i suspect better than most in the same category. If you are looking for a clean, reasonably priced and authentic feel to your stay then this is the place for you.

Visited twice for dinner
Found food to be quite nice and simple

You could sit down at tables or sit down on the floor on rugs and cushions at a low table.
Service was fast and staff were easy to talk to
At night they played a movie in one half of restaurant while you ate

I had gone into this shop to purchase an item which has 10%discount. When I paid for the goods, the sales assistant didn't return me the 10%. I had to ask. my rating reflects my personal experience, as the day we visited the weather was not good, really cloudy, and we couldnt see anything from the view point. I m sure that the travel agency knew it, but they took us anyway... Touristic attraction, recommended for the people who visit Pokhara for a couple of days and only if the sky is clear

There’s the usual monks and merchants selling their wares all around. Also will see people spinning the bells around the temple for good luck. 
Many monks come from Tibet to visit this. If you find it fascinating to see people praying in all their different ways, then you’ll find it interesting. 
I love the dogs all around lying in the sand soaking up the suns rays! 

Howard S.

My flight got cancelled, and we were transferred from the airport to this hotel.
Private van pick up, night and all meals included.
Room was very nice, with great view of the city, hot water in the shower, comfortable bed.
Nice spa area and swimming pool.
Staff very busy with hundreds of people arriving all in once from the airport, so quite stressed at the receptions desk.
Buffet meals for dinner and breakfast.

Lake side is one of the famous in Pokhara. You can find here bars, restaurant, street food. As well boat rent is available and has many options. We took the boat to Piece Stupa and it was calming and relaxing ride. Must visit in Pokhara.
This “monkey temple” is fascinating. The religious buildings and surroundings are historical and beautiful. Definitely worth the visit.
Very nice and friendly  good environment and room are soo good and food .Staff are friendly and polite .  I highly recommend alll ❤️

The KGH is the landmark hotel in Thamel - which seems to mean that they don't need to try very hard to attract guests.  In particular, this place is popular with the organised tour companies.  The main plus is the lovely garden, which is a quiet respite from the streets of Thamel.  The newer (top-end) rooms in the newest part of the building are quite reasonable although the bathrooms are already getting tired.  The "standard" rooms are pretty shabby - and there are plenty of other hotels in Thamel charging far lower rates (half, or less) for rooms just as good, or better.  After several stays at the KGH over the past few years there are far better options in Thamel, and I won't be going back again.

The grounds leading to the museum are not well kept and the building itself is like one huge barn with only half the space fully utilised. The exhibits are badly lit and there appears to be no logical sequence of displays

KGH is located in busy Thamel, behind a well protected gate.  There is a courtyard garden with a coffee bar, music some nights, and outdoor dining.  Inside the hotel complex feels safe and comparatively serene given the bustling area outside the gate.  The hotel is staffed with helpful people, and is in reasonably good condition.  A few in our party experienced difficulty with heat and or A/C.  The AC is useful to help clean the air a bit as it can get stuffy and dusty in the room.  The heat is useful as the temperature can drop drastically at night.  There are troubles with consistency of electricity and hot water, although this is typical across all of Nepal.  I think they do a good job trying to keep everything running--which is no small task.  

There are multiple grades of rooms.  I think I was in a pretty basic one, but the bathroom had been updated and had a nice shower and sink.  I asked for a hair dryer, and the one that arrived had a plug that didn't fit in to the outlet.  It took quite a while to find an adapter that worked.  

Breakfast is included and was ok--nice people who made you feel very comfortable and welcome.  The dining room can be pretty cold first thing in the morning.

I had a massage at the "spa" that I think is part of the hotel, but it is hard to tell for sure.  I don't recommend it.  The room is c-c-cold (the window doesn't close all the way) and the towels on the table were damp and didn't appear clean.

Free wi-fi is usually available but often slow--but sometimes just fine.

For about $50 a night, I think it is a reasonable place to stay.

Swayambhunath Stupa is a must-visit place in Kathmandu. If you want to enjoy the bird-eye views of Kathmandu valley, Swayambhunath is an ideal spot. Swayambhunath is one of 7 UNESCO world heritage sites in Kathmandu valley. It is perched atop a hill overlooking Kathmandu valley. It welcomes hundreds of tourists every day. The historical and religious significance of Swayambhunath stupa dates back to more than 2000 years. This place offers peace of mind in the serene aura. You can find many monkeys lingering around the stupa, numerous religious shrines, and few shops selling incense and prayer flags. Visiting Swayambhunath instills a peculiar desire to visit it once again.

Kathmandu Durbar square, also known as Hanuman Dhoka Durbar, used to be the residence of the Nepali royal family and administrators. This square is still the center of the old city and a glorious world cultural heritage of Kathmandu. The square preserves the 16th--19th century monuments of Nepal. There are dozens of temples and palaces. The architecture of the red bricks is very characteristic and worthy of savoring.

This temple is home to about 2000 monkeys who have free range of the area and plenty of space to roam around x be careful of eating food or carrying food as they will jump all over you x worth a visit x lots of stalls to buy typical Nepalese gifts like singing bowls but also a lot of tut!!!

Ambience was very nice and laid-back, with low tables, carpets, cushions and candlelight. There were also power points available for you to charge your devices. Free wifi as well. Food was average and nothing to shout about. We ordered the platter which came with hummus,  tahini, salsa, falafel, naan, focaccia, etc. it's more than sufficient for two pax. As a snack, we ordered the chilly fries.

I am staying in this hotel now and will be changing it tomorrow. This is a bad choice for winter. There is no heating in the room, lots of humidity, no hot water. The monkey temple, one of the most historic and religious place here at Kathmandu, near Patan Durbar Square! You can come with family and friends. You may find lots of monkeys around the place and some gift shops.

There is a small entry fee, a reduced rate for SAARC countries and a higher rate for others.

This place is really amazing for stay with family, friends and colleagues.
 neighbouring to phewa lake. Impressed with the ambience, food amenities and the staff highly recommended place for future stay.
Thank you ms ayushma for the hospitality.

Great food and an amazing selection on the menu! Was difficult to choose just one thing! Try the fresh lemonade for something refreshing on a humid day! And the 0r2K platter for something full of flavour and filling! 
Nice relaxing atmosphere with great service - good place to chill and play one of their many board games for the afternoon!

I stayed four nights here, two at the beginning and two at the end of my tour of Nepal. It is a very beautiful hotel, built in ther traditional Newari style. It is ideally situated at the southern end of Thamel, about 15 minutes' walk from Durbar Square. My room was delightful and comfortable. I had both breakfast and dinner in the hotel every day that I was there and the food was superb. The staff were very kind and extremely helpful. I thoroughyl enjoyed my stay and recommend this lovely hotel very highly.

This is the touristic disctrict of Kathmandu with the best shops and restaurants. Big chance your hotel is in this district, otherwise you have to go here for at least half a day. Have a lunch at one of the delicious bakeries.

Having been a conference organiser for many years, arranging events in many different countries,  I have to say that this hotel is absolultey brilliant. Since i came up to Swayambhu for the first time in October 2011, it felt for me like most wonderful place on earth. It is my beloved place up to now.

Not only historical value for the Kathmandu valley, not only panoramic view, amazing structure, also great people up there.

Bear in mind there is no lift so if you're up on the 4th floor as I was it is a bit of a walk, one which I didn't mind.

All in all a lovely place that I would stay in again without hesitation.

5 a.m we start our trip to climb the mountain to Sarangkot...

a hill on the western side of Pokhara with an altitude of 1600m. Sarangkot is known for panoramic Himalayan views..

This tiny village just north of Pokhara is known for its stunning sunrises over the Annapurna Mountains. . Visit the Shiva temple tucked away on the mountaintop, soak up stunning views of Phewa Lake and look for indigenous birds, leopards and tigers roaming through the natural landscapes. Adrenaline junkies can also paraglide from Sarangot, or fly down the world’s fastest zipline, which starts at the top of this famous mountain.

Visiting this temple was one of the most fun things I did in Kathmandu. On the day I visited it was extremely hot outside, nearly 30C and humid. Climbing up the stairs was exhausting, so if you are there on a hot day, I recommend bringing a bottle of water or taking a taxi. Along the stairs you will encounter numerous sellers who will try to push their wares on you, but if you don't want to buy anything, just ignore them and they'll leave you alone. The temple complex is fairly large and there is a lot to see. You even get a fantastic view of the entire city since you are on a hill. The monkeys were so cute and playful and it was an absolute delight watching them jump into the water to cool down. I've heard that the monkeys often steal food or money from people if they have it in their hands, but they didn't bother me at all. They seemed to be doing their own thing. The entrance fee isn't very high at all (200 rupees) and is well worth it for a couple of hours of visiting an interesting cultural site with adorable monkeys.

The information about the mountain people, the climbers and their support teams as well as issues regarding global warming are informative and educational. There are lifelike mannequins, tools used in climbing and by the various indigenous peoples and magnificent pictures of the mountains. We spent 2+ hours there and could have stayed much longer. Would definitely go back if we return to Pokhara.

A good collection of mountain/mountaineering facts, equipment and more. Also cultural and ethnic materials. You can easily spend a couple of hours there although I don't recall a good canteen and the museum could be better-managed. A must-see if you're interested in history and culture.
So beautiful and gorgeous. Would love to see it again. Nice neat clean and majestic. With love from Pakistan.

It's a nice viewing point over pokhara. If the weather is clear you can see the whole city! I think maybe  the stupa is a better place to go if you want to see the Himalayas. Really fun place to paraglide from!

This temple is another Unesco site. It's quite a hike up to the top. However, there are multiple easier entrances you can drive up to. The panoramic views are spectacular. Locals believe if you make a wish and circle around following the local rituals, the wish will come true. It's a very old holy shrine. There are many monkeys, hence "the monkey temple" name, and they are not shy. That's something different and to take into account.

The "Monkey Temple " is atop a hill which you reach by climbing 365 steps. The cost of entry is 200 rupee. Wikipedia says the temple was first built somewhere between the 3rd and 6th centuries and is a very important pilgrimage site for both Buddists and Hindus.
The temple itself is quite impressive but some buildings are not in a good state of repair. There are no explanatory signs to enlighten you about this site. I imagine the only way to get this information would be your own research or from a guide. We noted many of the latter with groups of people .
The experience was also spoiled by innumerable hawkers trying to sell souvenirs and watching the ground to avoid dog poos. The monkeys are cute and interesting to watch.
One good thing to do is go to the rooftop, via the stairs, of the art school, to get an excellent panorama of Kathmandu and surrounding hills. This art school has several floors of better quality local art works and tapestry.
In summary this is an interesting place to visit but for me once is enough.
Big hike up to the stupa.  Get a bus there or a taxi.  Sunset views are a good time to go.  Monkeys were not a pest at all.  Picturesque and beautiful.  An impressive stupa.

plenty of shops to do shopping, eating, walking around, lots of bargain buys, and tons of food, booze and shopping. most happening place.

Visiting Swayambhunath Temple in Kathmandu was a serene experience. The ancient stupa, adorned with fluttering prayer flags, offered panoramic views of the city. The peaceful ambiance, coupled with the temple's spiritual significance, made it a memorable journey, blending culture, history, and tranquility atop the sacred hill.

The temple and shrines are interesting but are sadly ruined by the touristic setting. 
The views are good though (if dusty); go to Cafe d’Stupa for decent iced coffee and lassis, and peaceful views.
If you are vegan or vegetarian you will have boundless choices of delicious food. Modern well designed restaurant with friendly helpful staff.

We got a driver from Nar-bis Hotel to drive us to the top of Sarangkot to see the spectacular sunrise over Annapurna. Definitely worth it, it's a once in a lifetime opportunity to see the sunrise over the Himalayas. Absolutely breathtaking.
When in Pokhara, this should be in your bucket list if you are an adventure lover. Coz this is the spot for all the para gliders. You definitely can't miss it.

Taking a guided tour through this ancient and fascinating temple was really fascinating and intriguing. All the buildings and steps and bridges, the history to were interesting to look at and learn about. We looked across the river and saw groups of people lined along the banks. These people were conducting funerals and rituals for their loved ones. Open cremations were being held and once finished the remains were sent into the river as per the beliefs. What I felt uncomfortable about was standing on the other bank and almost looking at all of this as a “show”. I didn’t see the same type of display of grief that I would expect at a funeral here in Australia but in any case it is not up to me to say how anyone should grieve. I certainly would not appreciate being on “show” at any funeral I attend. 

If you visit please be mindful of what many people are there for and put yourself in their shoes.

I think the IMM as a microcosm of modern Nepal. Foreign governments sweep in with good intentions, nobody communicates or coordinates, and what you get is a royal cluster of half-baked ideas and unfinished projects. 

The building itself is spacious as an airplane hangar. Split level open plan design. Over here is an exhibit about Nepali cultural groups. Over there is a bunch of stats about the "8-thousanders," followed by relics of historical expeditions. And here's a thing about Korea. Around the corner is a stuffed yeti. On the top level is an inexplicable photo gallery about Israel... no idea why. 

The outside is nice, especially if you have dogs to run around. There's a climbing wall but it didn't seem to be in use. There's a cafe but no one cares if you want to eat there. 

I guess the best part of the museum was being outside of it. I don't think that's worth the price of admission.

The Kathmandu Durbar Square is a great place to visit for a look into Nepal's culture and history. Though most of the palaces are now vacant, each building is unique and still changing with time, as many are being currently (at the time of writing this) rebuilt due to the destruction caused by the earthquake in 2015.

The entrance fee is 1,000 rupees, but I paid an additional 850 rupees for a personal tour guide. It was off-season so there weren't any other English speaking people in sight to share a tour with me. When I tried walking around by myself and googling things, it wasn't really an effective use of my time since it was too difficult to understand all the history/stories while trying to locate all the artifacts. At the end of my hour-long tour, I felt like the ~$8 USD I paid for a private tour was worth every penny - he even held his umbrella over me so I wouldn't have too much direct sunlight and took pictures for me.

I was brought into one of their schools of art and got to watch someone handpaint a Thangka. They obviously wanted me to buy something but were not annoyingly pushy when I said I wasn't interested in buying one.

The coolest part was when I got to see the living goddess, Kumari, come out to the window from her temple and "give us her blessing" (aka peer out the window and look at us for a while). There are certain hours she does this (I think 9am-12pm and 4pm-6pm most days), so go during one of these windows to see her. I was in disbelief but it's actually a little girl who has not gone through puberty yet that lives inside that temple with some people who are not in her family that take care of her as if she's the living goddess. It's a very unique thing to witness.

-ve:

3. When I asked for a king size bed. They just joined two twin beds and put a slim matress on top in front of me

Overall a very average stay. Could be because I expected too much from the hotel.

This is a gorgeous hotel with outstanding staff. The restaurants are excellent and the service is top notch, just as one would expect from a Hyatt Regency. We enjoyed our location. We had two rooms for our family, with one overlooking Boudhnath Stuppa, which I enjoyed; otherwise, the rooms were the same. We tried multiple dining locations on site and found them all to be of high quality. Truly outstanding, except for one caveat of poor communication and management. Upon checkin, we were offered to pull a prize from the fishbowl, which was a free laundry service. We were not planning to have laundry done on sight, but since we had won it, we thought why not. There was no mention verbally of what the service covered. We put several items together for two people and when the representative came to collect it, we told him we had a coupon for free laundry. He indicated that he did not need the coupon and made no mention of the limit on laundry, nor did he have us complete any form.. He simply took the laundry to be done. When we went to check out and presented our coupon for free laundry, we were told that we had exceeded the amount allowed and we were asked to pay $150 USD. My husband was very angry and I was trying to get this taken from our bill, for it felt a little like "switch and bait". You have won, so we had laundry done, and now you have to pay an exorbitant price. The manage on duty, ended up giving us a 50% discount but still we did not want to pay $75 for laundry, nor would we have, if we had been fully informed. I suggested that the staff make the "winning" of free laundry much more clear verbally to future patrons. We paid the $75 which we should not have incurred, and left in a sour, angry mood, at the end of what was otherwise a wonderful experience at this hotel. Moreover, I sent a letter of complaint regarding this experience to Hyatt Regency Corporation, hoping they would make amends in some way; however, they did not even respond to my e-mailed complaint. I would have otherwise given this hotel 5 stars, and I am resisting giving a much lower score in fact due to this caveat. I am chalking it up to poor communication, but really Hyatt?  I must include that we did choose to have laundry done, a lot of laundry done, in the exquisite Rachamankha Hotel in Chiang Mai  and it was a tiny, tiny fraction of our "discounted" price at Hyatt Kathmandu. The hotels are of comparable luxury. I suppose I would give the hotel and general staff 5 stars, and the management sadly one star.

Swayambhunath, also known as the Monkey Temple, is one of the most iconic and sacred places in Kathmandu. Perched atop a hill, the stupa offers a breathtaking panoramic view of the city below. Reaching the top requires a bit of a climb — over 300 steps — but the spiritual atmosphere and stunning scenery make the effort well worth it.

The moment you arrive, you're greeted by the watchful eyes of the stupa, colorful prayer flags fluttering in the wind, and the sound of chanting and prayer wheels spinning. The area is dotted with shrines, small temples, and statues of Buddha and other deities. The scent of incense fills the air, adding to the meditative ambiance.

One of the highlights is observing the local devotees and monks performing daily rituals. You’ll also encounter playful monkeys around the complex — they add charm but be cautious with food or loose items.

The mix of Hindu and Buddhist symbolism throughout the site shows the religious harmony of Nepal. There are small shops around the base and top where you can buy souvenirs, religious items, or enjoy a cup of tea.

I recommend visiting early in the morning to avoid crowds and witness the golden sunrise over the city. Whether you're spiritual or appreciate cultural landmarks, Swayambhunath is a must-visit site that leaves a lasting impression on the heart and soul.

The scarce information that there was was written in half English,  with plaques more often than not containing typos and unfinished sentences. 

The exhibit on the mountain itself was a joke, with pixelated images and short blurbs from Wikipedia. 

The conservation/animals of the mountain section was actually quite scary: the taxidermy of the animals was absolutely abysmal. There was barely any information on the animals or the environment, only conservation posters meant to demonstrate how much the government and other organizations dedicate time and resources to protecting the environment and empowering the locals... This is all propaganda from what I gather since the locals here think it's BS.

Honestly, you could learn more by watching a documentary or spending 20 minutes on Wikipedia. Waste of time and money.

The monkeys are regarded as holy as the local legend described that these monkeys were transformation of head lice from Manjushri, a Bodhisattva of wisdom and learning. There is nominal fee to buy food to feed the monkeys and pigeons. There are toilets, cafes and souvenirs shops within the compound of the stupa. Without question Thamel is THE tourist hub in Kathmandu. Here one can find hotels, bars, restaurants, travel agencies, clubs, ATMs, shops selling everything from camping, hiking and mountaineering equipment to local handicrafts and winter gear. This place is bustling with life from mid morning till very late at night. Mostly Thamel is where the foreign tourists flock to, but lately local youngsters have started to visit this place in numbers - especially in the clubs and bars. LOD (Lord of the Drinks) is one such club but there are many more. There are some nice rock pubs as well. Food and drinks are not exactly cheap (by Asian standards) and a certain amount of haggling during shopping can be done. The pandemic hit this place quite hard, as it did the whole tourism industry of Nepal which is the lifeline for this Himalayan state. However everything seems to be back to normal. Hopefully it stays that way - for the Nepalese sake!

walkable distance from thamel.. filled with locals and tourists.

A wonderful stay at this hotel, very special people, we feel at home, the best food, they have exceptional service with an spectacular view, we will return to this hotel. Thanks to tidos pir for their excellent service. We recommend it 100%.

Recently spent the lesser half of a day exploring the Swayambhunath Stupa and the surrounding parks, monastery, and monuments - the "monkey temple". The Stupa itself is magnificent, but I found it overshadowed by the less than pleasant company. This place is completely crawling in beggars, stray dogs, touts trying to sell you unnecessary tours, and merchants peddling mediocre, tourist-grade junk.

It wound be one thing if this was all just on the way up the stairs, but these occupy the grounds of the temple as well, to the point where you can hardly appreciate the beauty of the place without being approached by a merchant or a prospective tour guide, not to mention the physical, visual obstruction the stalls offer. On the off chance you can find a clear spot, the views of the surrounding city and the stupa are excellent.

The stray dogs were sweet and mellow, I had no problem with them and even made friends with a few, but the monkeys on the other hand... they seemed to alternate between harassing the poor dogs in noisy rows, and trying to steal bags, food, and water from the visitors to the site. The place is covered in graffiti and garbage in a lot of places in the typical Kathmandu fashion.

All in all, I'd say its worth seeing, but keep your head on a swivel and check your expectations because you might be disappointed.

Embark on an enlightening journey with Global Nepal Trekking to explore the iconic Swyambhunath, also known as the Monkey Temple, nestled atop a hill overlooking the bustling city of Kathmandu. As you ascend to this sacred site, our experienced guides will accompany you, sharing fascinating insights into its history, culture, and significance.

Swyambhunath is one of the oldest and most revered Buddhist stupas in Nepal, dating back over 2,000 years. Its gleaming white dome and gilded spire, adorned with the all-seeing eyes of Buddha, stand as a beacon of spirituality and enlightenment. Legend has it that the valley was once a lake, and the hill upon which Swyambhunath now stands emerged as a lotus flower, symbolizing the creation of the universe.
