We will definitely be back next time we visit Nepal.

I drove from my Hotel near Fewa to sarangkot. Visited Bindyabasini temple on the way and took the hilly road. Its good road and once you reach the height you will appreciate the beauty of Pokhara.
Its here where you can book and start your paraagliding experience in Pokhara. If you are afraid of heights (like me) 
go there and watch people start their paragliding by running off the cliff side. ;)

Poorly managed and maintained property.I stayed for 3 days. Wardrobe were about to fall, phone not working, no one answering, dirty windows and what not. On top of that servive team has no reply to why property is not maintained properly. It seems like a 3 star hotel and not at all a 5 star Radisson level property.

I had 4 days in Pokhara and this was one of my favourites. I had the oasis bowl, double eggs, shakshuka, mushroom burger, mung bean strew, smoothies, teas and coffees. Everything was delicious and really healthy - no excessive oil, salt or sugar like many restaurants around. Just genuine, good, tasty food! Amazing after trekking 3 weeks! Free movie night was also a great plus!
An Amazing place to enjoy the beauty of Annapurna Mountains. Be there early morning, wait for the sunrise, I ma sure that you will get your efforts worth,a mind blowing seen awaits you.

Online payement is not applicable, you only find out once arrived, and the alternative is to fill a document with all info about the card, and provide copies, with no respect to security and possible fraud!
When my work booked the room for me, tgere was no mention that I will have to present a card once arrived (they entered all info online when booking, thinking, logically,  the card will be charged for my stay)

Been to this cafe for the well know falafel. It came with some side salad, tahini and bread. It was okey, but nothing to go back for again. The staff was rude and didn't care about their customers. 
It's a great space, but I wouldn't go back neither recommend it. 
You can find better falafel if you get back onto the main road and it's the little kebab place on the right which serves delicous falafel wraps for 150rs.

We booked Kantipur Temple House in advance of our arrival in Kathmandu and we were not disappointed. Their front desk service is great, as are the morning buffet breakfasts with unlimited french press coffee and tea.  Most importantly, KTH is on a side street which is very quiet at night. The beds are quite comfortable compared to others we stayed in in Nepal/India, and the nightly hot water bottle for your bed was an extra treat. They held our bags while we went to India and came back to once again use it as our homebase. We were particularly impressed with their enviro-credentials: they filter their own water so you don't have to buy plastic bottles, they don't change towels/linens unless you ask, even the waste baskets in the room are lined with newspaper instead of the ubiquitous plastic bags. Only downsides: the rooms are dark and the bathrooms could use a remodel. The wi-fi was a little finicky. Also, the price is a little high for Kathmandu.
It was very learnsom and intresting to learn about. But there wasn't much to do( like in most Nepali museums) and it was not close to the lake. I wouldn't advise going here with children.

We stay there for 3 nights. It was fantastic.very good housekeeper Mr. Yuvraj gurung kind and humbble person. Fantastic service.ambience qas good. Good food. Restaurant team was also nice. I will be definetly back for this place. Thank you radission team.

The hotel is excellently located, making it convenient for exploring the area. The room was clean and comfortable, the food was delicious, and the service was outstanding. The staff were exceptionally friendly and went out of their way to accommodate our needs.

International mountain mesuem is a mesuem located in Pokhara. It is located near the Seti river. It is the mesuem where we can observe the culture and costoms of Nepalese. You can enjoy with Nepalese cultures and traditions.
The rooms are very beautiful and clean as well all the service and all the staffs are very friendly and respectful and polite
If you manage to get up here on a clear day you will get some great views otherwise not much else to see.

The stay this time was not as it used to be previously. Understand that COVID restrictions are applicable, but things could be better still. The gym can be made operational with limited persons allowed.The property has vast open area, sadly all beautification is lost. the grass is no longer green, the flowering plants are not maintained, the pool is very dirty although cannot be used, but still can be kept clean, or leave it empty rather.

Wow, what a city full of friendly, happy people, totally amazing.

You can purchase everything you need for trekking at a fraction of the cost, you can also knock the prices down.

Great food which is inexpensive and suitable for all as there's a wide variety. Alcohol is a bit expensive in most places.

Thamel has an amazing vibe with lovely twisting, winding streets full of tiny little shops.

Crowded alleyways kinda take away the charm. The place looks alive, more so, during the evenings, and the crowd adds to it. However, crowds aren't always fun, and more often than not, you'll find only shops and eateries.

A bit unsure if I liked Durbar Square, as it is expensive compared to the other sites and you get bombarded by tour guides. Once it is rebuilt it will be a beautiful place to visit, wish it was less touristy.

If you are lucky with the weather go to Sarangkot. Hiking or driving as you wish... I stayed  in the hotel there and was hiking down from Sarangkot  to lake side for 2 hours. Morning meditation or sunrise yoga .. what can be better?!
And fly from there! Paragliding! Amazing feelings!!

I used to think this hotel was one of the best in Pokhara but my perception towards this Hotel totally changed after i went there. Wifi was very poor, and the A/C was not working properly and the staff were not very friendly.
the buildings seemed like they were from China, and they were interesting-I liked it lots- nice buildings!

Thamel is the spot where all tourists go. It is not a good representation of the rest of the valley at all, but there are great accommodations and good, safe restaurants. There are a lot of fun things for tourists to do plus a lot of little shops for anything you might need. I find the locals there to be quite pushy which is not at all how Nepali people usually are. I really feel a bit objectified whenever I go there, but still find myself going back quite often.

The paragliding at Sarangkot is amazing! The view is superb with Fewa lake and green mountains all around. If you’re lucky to be at Sarangkot on a bright sunny morning (early) you can even catch a glimpse of the Annapurna range!

I did not find any mechanized boats . You can rent life jacket and sit in the country boat being rowed by an experienced person.Listen to his warnings regarding how to sit, where to place your hands etc(in broken English). Better not to take children for ride. The larger boats are better and you can sit comfortably. 
Look around and judge for yourself.

You will be hounded to pay 1,000 Rupee to visit a world heritage site that hasn't been touched since the earthquake.
I bet they accepted the offer to clear the site by volunteers at the time without charging them.
Best you can do is don't go as it's a rip off.

Visited Kathmandu after 16 years and chose to stay at this hotel, coz back then, when we had visited the hotel for lunch: the memory of the immaculate property never left our minds. Now the hotel is in dire need of renovations and refurbishments. The hotel rooms are tired and the bathrooms are dated. The carpets need a change and the hotel lawns need to be really looked into! Didnâ??t expect to see dusty trees on the drive up to the hotel. The location is a good 10-15 mins away from the City centre. We used the back entrance of the hotel to visit the Boudhanath stupa every morning.. (its a comfortable 6-7 mins walk from the hotel). It's a MUST DO!
The wifi is spotty in the rooms but good in public areas.
Also the food is good. Loved the lavish breakfast spreads (special mention to the live dosa counters and yummy cappuccino) and club room happy hour treats. We had dinner at the hotel once and the indian food was delectable! Loved the Indian breads esp the naans!
The club rooms are on the 6th floor and one can avail of the evening snacks from 5:30 to 8pm.  The Club house chef used to go above and beyond, serving us everything that we required!
Hopefully next time around, this once beautiful property will regain its splendour!

Ya know, the food at this place is good. I enjoy the shakshuka and the fact that they have options for gluten free and vegan is a definite plus. However, the service is mediocre- it's almost as if they ignore you when you ask for something. You have to keep reminding them and a lot of times they are all just standing at they front counter chatting. Step it up, especially for the price.

I was staying here for a couple months for business. I dreaded being in a hotel that long, but the staff at Radisson made me feel welcome every single day. I enjoyed each day of my stay and was actually very sad to leave. If I’m back in Kathmandu, this is where I’ll stay without question.

This colourful, relaxed hotel is 5 km from the Pashupatinath Temple and 5 km from the Boudhanath stupa. 

Refined rooms feature free Wi-Fi, flat-screens and minibars, as well as desks, and tea and coffeemaking equipment. Upgraded quarters include sitting areas; some have access to a private lounge offering breakfast and refreshments. Suites add black marble bathrooms; some have living rooms. Room service is available 24/7.
Breakfast is available (fee). There's an informal rooftop restaurant with a terrace, as well as a rooftop pool. Other amenities include a gym, a spa and a garden. There's also regular live folk music, and complimentary parking.

The rooms were great & the food was amazing too. I had one of the most comfortable sleeps here. The staff were very sweet and assisted us well. They had go veg options for breakfast too as opposed to what’s written in their other online reviews. Overall a very solid stay!
Much more than I thought here.  Learned about the many indigenous peoples of Nepal.  Also enjoyed the geology displays.  Of course the mountaineering displays were fascinating.

This resort is very well located near Fewa lake in Pokhara with a very good market nearby. They serve excellent food including authentic Nepal, Thakali, India and Continental dishes. The staff is friendly and courteous. The beautiful garden with swimming pool enhance the tourist experience. It is recommended to stay. 
We have been touched by the friendly service by Premgiri at the restaurant.

The hotel was excellent. The service was outstanding both at the reception and in the restaurant. Everyone was kind and took care of everything we asked for, even when it wasn’t part of their job, like grinding coffee beans we had bought. We received amazing attention with everything we wanted.
Highly recommended to visit — we hope to come back here in the future.

If you get a lake view room then it’s perfect, hope they use better blanket comparing to hotel and price they use cheap blanket,breakfast was ok no fresh juice even during fruit season,staffs are very friendly good service,if you are looking for fun at night bit far from the center,if you are with family than it’s perfect Hotel

We visited here after reading some great reviews... But found it to be a little disappointing... Maybe we ordered poorly... 
I got the hummus with naan and my husband ordered another middle eastern dish...my naan was quite tough- and my husband found his quite plan in taste.... 
I decided to order the apple pie with ice cream for desert and after a wait it arrived without ice cream... The pie was good though- a generous size. 
OR2K is a nice place- lovely feel/vibe and I would recommend a visit but just a heads up to order wisely!! :)

Greetings & Namaskar. We are here a Pilgrimage Trip, under Alpine Eco Trek. I take this opportunity to Thanks You ALL The Team Members as Whole of The Radisson Kathmandu Location on behalf of My Wife & I (#404). So far we had an excellent positive experiences, starting from Bell Desk, Door Man "Shri Krishna", Front Office, Housekeeping Department, Restaurant Team, and of course The Culinary Division, for all our Meals throughout our stay. During our stay We wanted Honestly highlight "✨️"SHREEMATI MANITA" of the Culinary Team, for outstanding performances toward US., giving personalized but professional services to us. I definitely acknowledge recommend. Thanks Miss MANITA for all personal efforts and made our stay very memorable 💖 as well as The Whole Radisson Kathmandu. Thanks.

Manita represents the high quality professionalism and customer service that Radisson is known for worldwide. She is a young energetic individual who is destined for many successes in her career! Her customer service skills and smile were always welcome.

we are accosted by a 'guide' right at the entrance.  After confirming the price with him three times he kept insisting that we only need to pay what we are happy with & we can tell him to go at any time.  While we don't really fall for this stuff, he told the story that the Government don't help the poor & he was helping the poor.  While the guide was helpful, we didn't need him as the Temple has signs all around of where photos could be taken etc.  The guide took us into stores & made us sit through lectures of stuff we just were not interested in & we were bullied into buying a painting.  When we refused his attitude towards us changed.  At the end, he then told us what he wanted us to pay him, which was way more then the hourly wage in Australia.  We reiterated our conversation with him which resulted in a heated discussion.  We walked away completely unhappy with the experience which kind of soured the tour.  The Temple is a good site to tick off & see but do not let a 'guide' fool you into needing one.  It is completely achieveable without one

It was a very informative museum. It is just that it is getting lost in time. I hope international volunteers come up and help fix the exhibits; or, that companies sponsor the technology used for presenting the museum's information. I just found a lot of great facts and materials there that will probably engage people more if it was presented in a way that appeals to our time and generation.

We had a great time at the Temple Tree. Beautiful facility. Breakfast each day was amazing. We are at the restaurant in addition to breakfast and it was good. Staff was friendly and very helpful. We would highly recommend this hotel. It is also very close to Main Street with lots of restaurants and the lake.

Fascinating place. Had an awsome 1 hour there. So many infos about mountain and mountainaire. Also the geographical facts are amazing. 
Must visit if u seek knowledge about beautiful mountains surrounding all over the world

A must-see area of Kathmandu, World Heritage Site (1000 Nep rupees entry) full of temples many of which were badly damaged in the 2015 earthquake but have been repaired or are in the process of being rebuilt by local craftsmen who use the old techniques and can restore the buildings to their former glory. Most fascinating was the home of the Kumari, young girl who is considered to be living goddess, reincarnation of the goddess Taleju. 
Difficult concept for us Westerners, to keep a very young girl in effect 'locked away' from the world until she reaches puberty, then expect her to pick up a normal life again!
Hidden gem, nice museum with an international quality audio guided tour and a good summary of the mountaineering history and diversity that Nepal has to offer

The best thing about this hotel is location, but that is it. We first got a double room with garden view and it was horrible: small, dark, smelly. The basin, shower and toilet had no separation. Staff was friendly and we upgraded to a deluxe room. Acceptable, but still rough.

We booked a tour to Patan and Bhaktapur (U$ 100) with the hotel and the guide tour was the worst I ever hired. He was nice, but didn’t have a clue about how to do a guided visit to those places and his English was poor. Better to choose a guide onsite.

In the course of 5 weeks of our stay in Nepal, we were guests in Kantipur Temple House on three occasions. The fact that after our first stay in this quaint hotel, we did not look for another one speaks for itself.
The hotel is in a beautiful building. The architecture and the woodwork that we admired in many buildings in Kathmandu is right there. The rooms are simple but elegant with nice details and a sitting area in front of the windows. The bathrooms are pretty old fashioned, but the shower and the space were good. 
There are long corridors with nooks, a lovely inner courtyard, an outside lawn, and a terrace where free yoga classes are offered to the guests.
We ate tasty breakfast and good dinner a couple of times.
Last but not least, the staff of Kantipur is lovely, always with a smile and ready to help with any needs we had. They even paid our taxi fee to the airport since we had to leave before our check-out time.
We liked the feeling of returning to the place and people we knew. We would definitely stay again in Kantipur.

Even the Thamel has changed due to covid 19 ,  some of the shops I often visit when I am in Kathmandu was sadly closed and change the location . Few restaurants were on fully operation like Kathmandu Steak House , Road House, French Bakery and more . Its good that all the bar open.

A must visit place if you are willing to shop something related to handi craft of nepali traditional items, or willing to enjoy the night life, cafe, pubs discs. But a strict no-no if your travelling with children in evening ( Hope you understand ;)

There are series of short roundabout areas that I saw before finally reaching the Durbar Square. Entrance fee is 1;000 NPR and was given a green ID card to wear.

There are several temples to visit here, all unique in their own different exteriors, shapes, sizes, etc. Noted some locals offering flowers and other stuffs to their Gods. 

Because the Holi just happened the previous day, local cleaning people were busy cleaning the streets, washing off the stuffs they used for the Holi. Results = wet and muddy streets. Also noted shops, restaurants, other commercial buildings on both sides of the street leading to this Square. Watch out for the motorcylists who drive very fast here!

This is a magical place but of course it has suffered from the earth quake and needs your support in the way of visiting and buying a ticket. It is much better than last year and much progress has been made with the restoration and you will be able to take photos without scaffolding now, do go

Overall a slightly disappointing experience. On the upside, the staff are really very good - and few bartenders in Nepal can make a negroni, so full marks here.  Food alas, isn’t great - a Pad Thai was about as Thai as i am, and had four overcooked prawns on it, a salad boasting feta had two minute bits of feta. Dinner was a bit better, but a tandoori trout, was nice, but more like a trout in a Mediterranen sauce. Paneer was at best average. 
Rooms are nice, but the bed linen is really showing its age. So we decamped to Pavilions Famhouse - similarly priced, but better. Sorry.,

I loved the OR2K combo and Alice Buddha Bowl. The hot cider was a great winter special! Definitely suggest eating here for some healthy eating. They also have many vegan options if that's your kind of thing. Just remember to look up,  as it is not on the ground floor and could be easily missed.
Service of this hotel is very nice and comfortable. Staff from reception , bell boys and house keeping are exceptional.

The entire experience was one of warm hospitality and courtesy. It was value for money.  The breakfast buffet had a delicious spread, suiting every taste. Housekeeping services were exceptionally good. I would unhesitatingly recommend the hotel to visitors in Kathmandu. Location is in the city centre with major shopping areas a short walk away.

Kantipur Temple Guest house is well situated near Thamel and Kantipath .Its located on a quiet side street but within walking distance of the central tourist hub . The hotel is in the traditional Newar style and there are some nice touches with the use of carved wood and traditional fabrics . The hotel has a nice well kept garden and the restaurant serves a good range of Nepali cuisine . 

However , visitors should be made aware of the electricity problems in Kathmandu .There are at most 4 hours of electricity a day .There is a schedule for electricity but it is often on at inconveniant times ( i.e midnight to 4am ) .This may or maynot effect your experience but the hotel in keeping with its supposed eco credentials has chosen not to invest in a generator meaning no electricity for up to 18 hours .Due to the design of the hotel and the use of dark wood and brick it is very dark .There are a few sporadic emergency lights but the rooms are very dark .This means that if you like to relax and read for example it makes it impossible .Having just returned it was also becoming very hot so it was not possible to use the fan in the room .I imagine that over the next few months this could be an issue with the increasing heat . 

I stayed in a deluxe room which was clean and nicely decorated with wooden furniture.I did however see the standard rooms which were small and without charm .
Overall I would have appreciated the Hotel informing us of the electricty situation beforehand and I do think that the rooms are overpriced and not worth what is being charged .Once you add service charge and tax the costs mount up.The rate does not include breakfast which I do think the hotel should reconsider . 
The hotel also should also make more of the roof top area .It could be lovely but seems a little neglected . 

Overall a hotel with charm but needs to reconsider its prices and inform guests of the electricity situation

Indira thapa and ram bhandari I loved their behaviour and service I suggest you to go there for your next trip Nice breakfast and foods too good gym also swiming pool!!Loved it its sok beautiful and service is amazing

Great location , amazing service!! Perfect family resort!!! 
Highly recommend!! 
Spa service is a must!Babita from Spa is amazing at it. Loved the in-house restaurant and the food is great!! Its a great hotel for the ambience and location! Thank you for the service and great trip❤️

My wife and I took a boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Barahi Temple on an island on the lake. The temple was not that interesting but the one-hour trip was very pleasant and refreshing in the afternoon heat. The cost (which included the rower/guide) was just about $6 USD. Nice views and well worth it!

Arrived at this hotel on 4thFeb'17 after a 36 hour journey from the U.K. The hotel was booked by a family member who had not actually stayed there but has used the gardens on previous visits to Kathmandu and eaten there. The standard room was charged at 50$ per night was exceptionally disappointing. At best it was very basic(I have stayed in better tea houses than room 502 at this hotel). It was very small and cramped. Booking dot com stated that the room included wardrobe, iron, hairdryer etc, non of which were present. It was in desperate need of refurbishment. If there has been any restoration to this hotel since the devastation due to earthquake of 2015, they haven't got to room 502 yet. When we expressed our concerns to the hotel the following morning, they were indifferent and showed no willingness to change our room- saying only that a standard room was what had been paid for and that is what we had been given. If we wanted another room we would have to pay extra. The gardens are lovely and whilst the food was pleasant to eat, it is certainly no better than the Northfields restaurant almost opposite KGH across the street. The attitude of the hotel seems to be take it or leave it and I for one will certainly be leaving it. (We needed a room for one night as a base for our return to the UK the following day and stayed at the DOM Himalaya-the KGH equivalent of a deluxe room for almost half the price 40$@DOM-75$@KGH. (DOM only opened 01/02/17 and I will share my experiences of DOM shortly)There was no wheelchair access in the part of the hotel that housed room 502. If I seem very critical it was because it was a horrible experience and one I hope not to repeat.
The lake is a peaceful place to explore the culture and people of Pokhara. Best times to visit the lake are early in the morning 6am - 8am as the sun rises and in the late afternoon after 4pm.

The iconic Phewa lake in Pokhra catch everyone's attention always. Though traffic on the road adjacent to lake has increased over the years, one can still enjoy a leisurely walk and also a boat ride. Enchanting views of mountain ranges surrounding lake remain in one's memory forever. The shops, restaurants lined across the road is another good attraction.
Interesting place but very dirty. Still under construction after last earth quake. Holy men ask money to take their picture and many try to sell you something.
Place is great but the surrounding are very dirty already. This place must be cleaned, it is really good but definitely need a lot of changes.

Thamel looks like an imported tourist town in Nepal, but it is the creation 'out of demand' by travellers. All you need is here. Please do not forget to visit the Apsara Boutique Hotel and Ankur Garden Restaurant in this district.
Thames has a cool vibe and great shopping with spicy food and friendly peoples. Great for supplies and equipment for trekking in Nepal

We spent in the hotel 4nights me and my husband and son. The service and the stuff were excellent and kind, the food was very goof and well designed. However, the hotel itself and especially the rooms were old, not adequate at all and don't deserve being considered as 5 stars hotel. We have been traveling a lot all over the world and this was one of the poor Hyatt we've ever seen. If you're looking for luxurious hotel in Kathmandu, go to another hotel like Duarika or else.

Nice people in the hotel. 98% of the staff warm and friendly. Especially Nirmal at the poolside dining area. Nice rooms/clean, air conditioning. Pretty grounds.  Two things I took issue with. If
Misplace your keycard the charge for another… 500 rupees! really? For a piece of plastic. I have never run into this before. Secondly: offered a ride by the hotel for their driver to take us to a museum in the town. Quoted 1500 rupees for one way. Used InDrive for return. 849 for the ride back.  Took the edge off of nice. Had I known the difference, I would have taken InDrive there. No worries, but these are the things I remember. All in all a good experience.

this area is mainly for tourists booking tours or shopping for nepali cultural products ec. it is somewhat clean but muddy when rains.
 narrow roads and laneways are a bit confusing especially at nights. easy to get lost but it seems a safe place to walk around

This was my most expensive hotel in Kathmandu. The outside of the hotel is nice and looks like an old temple. The room is large. There's however nog airco. You don't get you room cold with the old fan that is in the room. I complained about the fan. He was so old and squicking that I couldn't sleep from the noise. The second fan squicked less but still made a lot of noise. There's no bottled water in the room. Everything is eco-based. Fine, but not when I pay so much money for a not fresh room with lots of noise. Being good for the enviroment is one thing but I will not recommend this hotel. I see a high income and low value hotel and surely recommend another 3 star hotel in Kathmandu but certainly not this one.

When hiking down from the World peace pagoda a boat trip at Phewa lake is included. 
The trip is nice and short the lake beautiful and many boats cross the way as it’s a very busy place for locals. Must see while in Pokhara but normal and not outstandingly exciting.

We walked in to this resort hoping to stay there for a week because of the good reviews but were utterly turned off by the attitude of the staff at the reception desk. They seemed to be uninterested in serving Nepali customers. Save yourselves the hassle as there are plenty of higher end hotels in Pokhara for the same price.
I have no clue how this place has such high ratings.

Great location in thamel,centers of the thamel really pleasant and clean rooms .staff are so frindly and hotel manager mr.saroj kindly ,rooftop was very nice and see the eveing time sunset view ,definitely i will back with my family next time .

Radisson is conveniently located with very friendly and helpful staff .
We had forgotten our personal belonging which the staff had preserved and handed over to us promptly when we went back to check for it.
The breakfast buffet is tasty and has a nice variety for indian palette as well.
In all , a pleasurable experience
Place a world heritage site. Lots of encroachment and shops in the monument. Can be kept clean as the place is a bit dirty.

My partner and I had booked a stay at Temple Tree for two nights, and like many of the reviews here - the hotel is excellent, but the customer service (namely its travel desk) could definitely do with some improvement.

Checking in was fairly easy as it was not peak season when we visited. Our room was absolutely gorgeous, with a hammock right outside, which I spent the afternoons lazing on. The hotel may be located in town, but it offers a very relaxed atmosphere and green grounds, and is generally very quiet all day. The poolside and restaurant staff were super friendly, which made my stay very enjoyable.

Before we checked out, we decided to approach the travel desk for advice on our trek up Poon Hill - namely, for transportation there and for our trekking permits. Like many, we had done our research beforehand, and even had friends who have climbed the hill tell us that we were able to complete the entire trek in 2-3 days. However, the guy at the desk kept insisting that we HAD to hire a guide with them, despite us telling him many times that we only wanted to book a taxi and get our permits done. He told us that it was impossible to climb Poon Hill in 3 days without a guide (which we did, of course) and got very angry before saying: "You think your friends are very clever, why don't you just ask your friends?"

I was EXTREMELY offended and was ready to kick off, but my partner (being the kind and patient one) maintained composure and insisted we only needed transportation there and for our permits to be done. Long story short, we did not come to an understanding and ended up hailing a taxi by Lakeside. 

This incident really put a damper on our otherwise very pleasant stay. In some way I wish I didn't approach the travel desk for assistance, as his brazen had comment upset me a lot. I would recommend staying here, but keep away from the hotel travel desk at all cost. 

And yes, you can definitely trek up and down Poon Hill in 3 days without a guide.
temple architecture is unique. place is clean and gives divinity. easily accessible. many places nearby

Walking at the lake boarder after some days or weeks on a Trekking trial is relaxing. Enjoying the numerous people visiting this lake is great fun. If you like nice photographs this environment offeres countless opportunities. A great place to go!

The same restaurant as in Kátmandú, but here the food isn't good. Anything special, without taste, without esprit, without whatever. The interior of this restaurant is fine, with interesting view, but  you usually go to the  restaurant for eating, not for viewing.

This is a fantastic lake with entertainment in every corner. We enjoyed a relaxing boat ride where you can see views of the Himalayan mountains (if weather permits) and then world peace stooper.  There is certainly a lot to do on and around the lake (shops, restaurants, park, boating, temples) and each sun down their is a wonderful event / dance by the local monks which bid good night to the day. Stunning.

From the time you first encounter the hotel and until you leave, each experience is worse than the other. When the complimentary pick-up at the hotel doesnâ??t show up at the airport and you have large bags and are tired after a flight, you have started off on the wrong foot. Meeting the designated driver at the hotel makes it worse - he tells you your flight was delayed and he could not be expected to wait. Post check-in, you get a room that is obviously dated and needs redoing immediately. The wooden flooring is patchy due to long years of use, the bathroom tiles similar. Staff at the restaurant are limp and disinterested - they would rather be in some other job, it appears. 

The only redeeming feature is the relatively quicker response of the Housekeeping Dept. No other friendly or professional experience elsewhere.

Parting shot: asked for an envelope at the front-office. They said they didnâ??t have any at the property. Never heard that one before at a hotel of this level.

Checked out mid-booking and moved to a friendlier property. Never going close to this property again. In facf, after this horrible experience, staying away from all Hyatt hotels in future.
Good service  specially  name is sanam sabina nabina binita alishwa  was very polite   and locations  was very good . Breakfast was so good
Im big fan of coffee.i try almost evdrywhere i go. Breakfast set and organic coffe is good people can go and try
We went before noon to the top. You could see the high mountains but we saw already nicer views of the Himalaya's.

Vegetarian menu only. Tried the humus, falafel and fettush salad. Were OK but nothing special. Serves cocktails beers and wine (had Shiraz and was good). Cozy place, sitting is on cushions (shoes must me left at the entrance), has good wifi. Non- and smoking sections. Indoor only. Friendly staff.
This is quite a pleasant thing to do, and I would rank it as a must-do when you are in Kathmandu. Spiritually, it`s very interesting.

OR2K has excellent food. A huge selection of vegan and vegetarian dishes, some hearty enough for carnivores, and some light enough for those wanting to taste something fresh and pure. 

However, there is a rule that visitors remove their shoes to sit on the floor-level cushions. Fair enough - it should keep the floor clean. However, the first thing I noticed when my bare foot touched the floor was that sticky. When we walked onto the rugs, they felt almost greasy under foot. Back at our hotel, we saw our feet were darkened, presumably by the gunk for thousands of other feet. 

Whilst the floor-level tables look appealing, they are not at all comfortable for me, and I imagine for other people who are perhaps revering from hiking. 

I was not happy with the service. Because of a long-term shoulder injury, I wanted to avoid sitting on the floor. I was even wearing a sling, but the waiter insisted the only table with chairs was for a group of six. So we turned to leave. Only then the waiter said we could sit there. 

If you are visiting Pokhara, I would go to OR2K there and skip the branch in Thamal. 
There are more chairs and it is possible to keep your shoes on (and in any case, the floor was clean). It has great views of the lake, and the staff are super-friendly. 

If you visit in Thamel, then wear thick socks!

Go to Thamel if you have couple of hours to spend walking around the street. I walked around for 2 hours, bought nothing, took few pictures, soaked in the ambience and loved it. Lots of nooks and corners for food, coffee, bars and deals of all kinds to be made :-) Just a nice buzzy fun place. And very safe....

Varied menu including Middle Eastern options with generous servings. Tasty and well presented. Seating inside or outside. Elevated views over Phewa Lake. Sister restaurant in Thamel Kathmandu. 13%VAT and 10% service charge added

I went paragliding with the tandem paragliding team and they were very professional, going out of their way to make this once in a lifetime experience memorable. We took off from Sarangot and paraglided over pokhara lake, flying with the eagles and at the end of our 45 minute glide we were given a CD with a video and our photos to show for it!

We stayed two nights here after the EBC trekking. The room is spacious and tastefully decorated, and the beautiful garden make us feel pleasant and relax. We also enjoy the Yoga class and guided walking tour offered by the hotel. In addition, we really appreciate the attentive and warm hospitality provided by Kriti and Sajana, they are the best!

This is truly the hidden gem in the bustling Thames, we definitely will come back to stay here again in the future!

Thamel runs for a few squares, it has restaurants,rooftop bars, shops, and a bit of chaos too! Don’t feel pressured to buy in the 1st shop you come into, as they say “ looking is free” and the locals are friendly enough to understand that one has to look around before committing to buy!

Firstly this is a very busy area with both local and tourists,second its expensive for a ticket,but they need the funds for resteration.thirdly there is a lot of damage/destruction from the large earthquake which hit the Kathmandu region,so some temples/buildings you cannot enteror they are being rebuilt,apart from all that its a large complex to walk around and there are some great historical places to see,statues/buildings/carvings/monuments you get in where you can and there is many colourful places to behold,as well as the locals,who will hassle you but just wave them away unless you want photos then its a small fee with the holy men.There is a large temple complex that has just been partly re-opened which you can go ,follow the walkway through the temple to the gardens and museum around the back ,also watch out for the pigeons around here there are thousands of them.A large open air bazzar is on the streets outside in the square near north/east enterance to Durbar square,the whole temple/kingdom area is well worth a few hours visit,just to soak up the historical culture and history,and to mix with the locals,

This hotel claim they are four star, my personal review is two star maximum. I checked in lunch time and immediately order a Nepali dish, unfortunately food was very bad and dirty. But their location is good and hotel is also very beautiful.

He did not do a tour guide for us but we have been to many of these places in our journeys around the world and trip advisor and lonely planet really tell you all you need to know

The majority of the seating area is carpets and cushions and rugs on the floor, with very low tables. I think the idea is that you sit cross-legged. There is limited seating at a bench from what I could see. The food is good and reasonably priced. It is a nice atmosphere. It also seems to be a chill out zone, I saw people with their laptops charging in the wall and using the WiFi.

If you are staying in Pokhara you cannot miss the lake but spend some time on the water. There are many options for getting out there. I rented a Kayak and spent and hour just paddling around by myself.

The service were okay the staffs are best the food was very tasty the rooms were comfortable and the location was convenient

so knowledgeable, information guide sumita so good in explaination. just walkin distance from our united hotel @pokhara.

Definitely worth seeing for its cultural heritage and the history behind it

Lie in the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu Valley, this place of attraction is not to be missed if you have time in the capital. 

Even though ticket fee is quite pricey (1000 NPR for foreigners), the trip here is worthy of the price paid. We get to see and imagine how the Palace Vicinity looks like in the 18-19th century. 

There are a few temples and courtyard which are prohibited from visiting. No proper attire code stated, however, do dress up respectfully. 

We also get to the Living Goddess, Kumari in Kumari House. Look it up on the internet about the goddess information. We were just in time before she goes for her long break. No photos allowed in this vicinity. 

Also, the old square where traders sell and exhibit their souvenir and handicraft is equally picturesque and unique.

We were walking from Durbar Square back to Thamel and stumbled upon this "neighborhood Stupa" -- kids were playing soccer, residents were passing the afternoon. A real slice of life in Kathmandu. And no entrance fee! Highly recommended.

I had mixed feelings about the Guest House. First it has a long history, the pioneer in lodging in Thamel I believe. The service is great, food is good too, but it feels a bit artificial, like it doesn't belong in Kathmandu. I recommend it for people looking for a clean place with good food, but I'll definitely try another place else more "authentic" next time I'm in Nepal.

Nice rooms, balcony  and comfortable beds with spacious bathroom.  Pretty setting around gardens and pool, off lakeside road to the South so quieter than main tourist area. Slightly pricey but worth it.  Breakfast ok and reflects the mainly Indian clientele

visited recently. Unique hospitality with unique ambience. Excellent resort in pokhara. We really found Thamel amazing and the area to stay at when you visit Kathmandu. So many amazing sites and it really captures the essence of South Asia!

The service was really good, the swimming we really enjoyed with our baby. The staffs are really friendly And cooperative and the food really good. The rooms are comfortable. Highly recommended to all friends and family….. best wishes to the team

Great place to visit, day of night, don't be afraid to barter for something if you like it there's always some wriggle room. The streets contain great bric-a-brac stalls, clothes, food and pubs (we enjoyed a few in the Irish bar whilst there) really interesting to walk slowly around.

Manita is a very good omlet maker and i like her good PR with guest as well. All staffs are of this hotel very helpful and supportive. i like to recommend in cooimng future to others organization as well. Hope for the  more best for upcoming days. Have a good day. Thank you
It seems sadly 4 years post earth quake no work has been done to restore this monument group. So we aren't sure where the expensive foreigner fees for entry go.

Hotel is really good for short stay. Good food, spacious rooms and the staff is really traveller friendly. Location is perfect and all the amenities are in close proximity. Bed was comfortable with clean sheets.

This interesting museum is worth a couple of hours. Impressive building. Large interior with so much potential to improve and expand the exhibits on display. The mountain climbing history was particularly interesting. Some great photos to see.

You can buy tour ticket go and return share with other tourists, Than go to the small island with temple; cost only 100 Rupees  for person. It mean the boat ticket just 1$. There are some local tourists and some students. It is must to do in Pokhara.

My recent visit to Kathmandu Radisson was made unforgettable , From the moment I stepped in, the warm hospitality of the staff made me feel right at home. 
The well-appointed room provided all the comforts I needed, and the delectable meals at their on-site restaurant call "The Fun Cafe"  was  a treat for the taste buds. The breathtaking views from the   swimming pool area , perfect for unwinding after a day of exploring the area.
I highly recommend Radisson Blue Kathmandu  to anyone seeking a tranquil and rejuvenating escape. Can't wait to return!
The hotel is nice and comfy. The staff members are also very helpful and cooperative. The pool water was clean and the breakfast was amazing. Must visit!!

Stayed at Temple Tree in Pokhara 3 times over 2 trips to Nepal in the last 2 years (2023 and 2025).  Comfortable, beautiful and relaxing place to stay after a week or two of trekking.  Service, food and cleanliness is impeccable.  Staff very helpful with suggestions of things to do, directions about where to go/get things and arranging transport to/from.  I have no need to look anywhere else if I want a great place to stay in Pokhara.  Thank you to everyone at Temple Tree!

After two days of staring at it from our hotel room we finally had the opportunity to visit it as part of the tour. This meant that we were able to get as close as possible to the entrance and then walk the handful of stairs to the top. Apart from the beautiful view of the city, we were also lucky to see a religious ceremony and, with the help of the guide get a better understanding of the place.

Amazing Breakfast ❤️

Great Coffee & Tasty Breakfast!
Cozy and welcoming café with amazing coffee and a delicious breakfast buffet, The staff are friendly, and the atmosphere is perfect for a relaxing start to the day. 

Special Thanks to Subba , Mannish, Ratna, Vijay , Anoop for taking very good care of the guests.
The center of the city for tourist which has a more relaxed vibe than the other parts of the city. Best place to eat, drink relax and plan the next adventure.

I picked OR2K for dinner for our group of 10 older to senior age group.  Not recommended for older people and those with knee issues.  You have to sit on the pillows on the floor.  None of the dishes we ordered were good.  We hardly finished our plates.  The rating must be high because it is very popular with the trekkers.  If you are looking for a nice elegant restaurant that you can sit down and enjoy a meal, this is not it.
This lake is the Gem to Pokhara. A pristine lake with clean whitewater. Available boating Tours. Fishing is also possible

The atmosphere is buzzing here but the food truly mediocre.
There are many restaurants that serve better food but lack the buzz so it all depends on what matters more to you.

You can get some bargains here but like everywhere you need to be wise. There are beggars and it is better to offer to buy food or milk etc for them than give them money.

Being next to the Boudhnath Stupa it is obviously an attraction for Buddhist tourists. But, the distance and traffic from the main city makes it an inconvenient location.

You will find OR2K in the 3rd and last floor of a commercial building in the lakeside road of Pokhara. You will be rewarded by the view of Phewa Lake and refreshing scenery of the mountains. The restaurant looks well-maintained and have enough sunlight coming from the outside. The food are delicious as well! I had the Healthy Salad which was served with fresh vegetable that comes with a tasty bread. My friend tried their Dal Bhat and he was very much satisfied with it. We also tried their pizza which we ended up taking home because it was too big and we were quite full. If I ever find myself again in Pokhara, I'd come back in OR2K for the great views and wonderful food.

I have been there for business purpose, before i went there i called thrice about me and my visit n reservation,  when i went there i had been followed every where upto rest room also i have sit and walk with guards who don't speak English also, they said they don't even have online payment system,  this is torture 5 hotels of Nepal though have to pay 500 $ per a day what the....

Radisson Kathmandu is a perfect hotel to stay in the city of Kathmandu. The staffs are welcoming and exceptional most especially the staff Prajeena. She can communicate well, so generous, and compassionate. She took care everything and exceeded my expectations in Radisson. Because of Prajeena, I had an unforgettable stay in Radisson. Breakfast and dinner are sumptuous, most of the facilities such as body massage, fitness gym, pool, sauna, jacuzzi, steam bath are available also. Definitely this hotel is highly recommendable to my family and friends.
My frirnds and me went to the sarangkot for the sunrise, we were so lucky that we could see the mountains.

Excellent option for before and after trek. Great service, super-comfy beds. We had somebody working in a trekking shop in Brisbane, Australia recommend ‘Monita’s breakfast omelettes at the Radisson’…..what a a great call! Rooftop pool is great for sunset.

The history of this place is mindblowing..but the damage From the 2015 quake  means that most og  the former beauty still is rubble or partly destroyed buildings.

When and if it gets reconstructed it will be worth a visit again

Well out of all our stays in Nepal we had expected the most out of this property and it turned out to be the highly disappointing one.. the front desk did not seem at all friendly to accommodate even our driver I.
