This lake is such an asset to the city but it would be much more pleasant if there wasn't so much rubbish everywhere. You can sit and people watch on the lakeside with a fresh juice or lassi but expect to be approached by people selling their wares. They could do so much more to bring tourist dollars into Nepal if they used this asset a little better, without over-development.

Incredible temple, with monkeys providing entertainment, but rather ruined for me by the crowds of tatty jewellery sellers and concrete buildings being constructed mere metres away from the ancient stupa.

He shopping district in Thamel is probably a bit different than european people are used to. It's a bit of a bazaar, not thaaat clean, you feel like the cars or motos are hitting you every second walking there along the shops (but they don't) but  the Nepali people are super friendly and nice. Also you can't believe hiw cheap stuff is in Nepal. So if you wanna go shopping for outdoor gears/clothes or just souvenirs - Thamel is the place to go.

Phenomenal experience. Was a pity the roads were littered with thrash on our way up. The actual view captured in a photograph doesn't do the actual beauty and experience any justice. We stopped by a b&b on the way down for breakfast. If you have just a day in Pokhara, make the trip there.
Best place in katmandu, backpakers place. Dont hesitate in crushing there because its the place to be in the city.

We had a good experience in waterfront resort.The pool was so clean good food  there is a varities of Indian in breakfast.room is so neat and clean....and the aquabird restaurant staff are so helpful specially Binita,Sabina,Sante and Alishiva thank you so much we will definitely visit again.....
Even with all the great outdoor attractions of Pokhara, this is a must see.  From culture, to climbing and geology, this museum has it all in a new and very well organized manner.

I stayed here with my family for 5 nights and we had booked two rooms. The rooms were not ready even when we arrived after check-in time. You can see the Boudhastupa from the hotel. All other tourist locations were nearby but took us sometime to reach because of the traffic. Hotel staff was courteous.

Now the disappointing part. The food service at the Cafe restaurant was very slow. They took ~1 hr to serve food which was just some salads. The hotel has wooden floor, is slippery and makes a lot of noise when you walk. Housekeeping staff were not proficient. They entered our room even when we were in the room without our permission. Wifi was very poor in the room. Pages like google took a long time to load and the internet was very very slow.

Hyatt is a good brand, however, the Hyatt regency in Kathmandu has to make a lot of changes to match the standard of the brand.

Nice square with some temples and museum.
Some buildings under construction in renovation.
There is a charge to be on the square. You can walk around the square with no charge.
More spacious and quiet then other temples and squares in Kathmandu

This is my fourth stay at this wonderful hotel and yes the experience has been excellent.. Ms Sabina and the foreign interns were excellent with their service and hospitality. I recommend this hotel if anyone wants to visit pokhara and experience the relaxation and comfort this hotel has to offer. :)
It's nice area with lot of historical views and sites. It's sad that earthquake did so much damage to the building.

Shan Singh Bhandari and Deb Nath are very attentive and pleasant. They are always offering to help with local suggestions etc. 

Thank  you both for all your help.

The hotel provided excellent hosting arrangements for our conference meetings. But the most important part for me was that the rooms provided an excellent comfortable sanctuary when the conference was over. I valued the convenience of the hotel to a couple of restaurants in house and outside. The staff were fantastic on check in and check out. Food at the conference was great (I had a vegetarian week with some of my favorites regularly on the menu), and staff were constantly attentive and available as needed.

We planned to stay in KGH with a high expectation. But ultimately its was a didmal experience. The front desk guy showed unwelcoming and irritated  attitude.The rooms were a bit shady with pungent odour. Breakfast experience was also horrible. Rain water was dropping over open food served not noticed by  caterers and found mosquitos  within food. Overall hotel showed a noncaring attitude to its clients.

Swayambhunath temple is one of the oldest temple and important religious site. temple is on a little hill and it is revered by both Buddhists and Hindus. The stupa consists of a dome at the base, above which is a cubical structure painted with eye of Buddha looking in all four directions.
Visible damage of the earthquake. Many buildings are already a ruin and left unattended. Monkeys around makes the visit quite interesting
If you want to experience breathtaking view of Himalaya just hike up to sarangkot hill early morning. It is the highest viewpoint easly accessible from Pokhara.

Every possible souvenir of Nepal is available many times over in the maze of streets making up this area. It is crowded with tourists from early to late, always felt safe and the people watching is as much fun as the shopping.

A fairly tired series of faded displays and random climbing paraphernalia from Nepal and around the world.  They do at least have a stuffed yeti ... sort of.

If you’ve got an hour to waste and haven’t got anything else to do, then realize into Pokhara’s suburbs for this delight.  You’ll probably enjoy a stroll along Lakeside much more though.

we stayed twice this year having first stayed over 20 years ago. A haven of peace away from the dust and traffic.
. On our first stay small but adequate room but pigeons outside noises all night plus noise from a local club. Second stay we paid for an inside garden room and were told we were being upgraded. Great room but on ground floor next to the gate so again noise with people coming and going. Had to cover tv with a coat as screen glowed when turned off. Minor irritations perhaps but main annoyance was Internet speed. But would still stay again for location and garden but careful on choice of rooms. Please also do away with plastic water bottles and provide filling statigons for guests to re use a bottle

As with many things, foreigners do pay a higher price; however, for the squares in Kathmandu it gets pretty pricey. 1000 NRP for entry. 
It's a beautiful square but you won't need more than 30 minutes there to see it all, so this price is definitely excessive. 
It's such a shame as it is a nice area full of history.

We had been looking forward to eating at this restaurant after reading lots of good reviews but left feeling extremely disappointed.

There was no one to greet us when we arrived so chose a table ourselves. We were given a menu but had to wait about 20 mins for someone to take our order.

We asked for a bottle of water with our meal and it was just plonked down on the table. The waiter didn't even look at us. We had to ask for some glasses...and then again...and then only 2 glasses turned up for 3 people...

The food was ok but quite tasteless and reminded me of school dinners.

I found the atmosphere here extremely uncomfortable. The tables are squashed together with no space for bags or coats and we were not made to feel welcome at all. They try to make it a "cool place to hang out" but it feels very false.

I went to pay at the desk and no one bothered to speak to me. I just got handed a bill. There was no thank you or even a smile even when they gave me my change.

We will not be eating here again.
There are so many shops here and they all want your business but it is a must visit place.  Remember to barter

last week me and my friends went to nepal for trekking that time i just heard about thamel 、there is many street 、local shop 、club 、bar 、restaurent 、prime location the main things is  restaurant is also convenient every dish we had just perfect  and the choice is not missing

You will get hot water between 5-10am and 5-10pm only. The provided blanket and bed in the room are not comfortable compared with the price. You will only get wifi in garden and pool area when you once back to your room it will ask username and password again and again.

The AC is not warm enough and when I asked the hot water bag to keep under blanket, they only provide the bag itself, I have to manage hot water by myself. Breakfast is average. Staffs are quite friendly. Personally, I just feel like it is overprice compared with the facilities.

Let me start with the negatives I have and get it out of the way. My room was pretty tired and would've benefited massively from a lick of paint and a good hoover. I did get a chance to stick my head in some of the other rooms (whilst being cleaned) and they looked lovely, with wooden floors, Newari architecture and a view over the courtyard. I'm presuming the internet rate I got was the reason for the room I was allocated! I did ask for another room but was told there was nothing available. It was also pretty noisy. I don't think the walls are terribly thick and if you are unlucky enough to be next to other guests lacking in the consideration of others department, you could be in for a bit of a noisy stay and not particularly good amounts of sleep. Having said that if you mention said noisiness to the reception they are more than happy to diplomatically speak to the offenders!

On the plus side, my room not over looking the courtyard meant it had much more natural light and despite it not being the best of rooms it did have a comfy feel and was a good size. The beds I thought were very comfy...not too soft and the free mineral water is a nice touch.

The staff are friendly and helpful and taxis can be booked via reception to take you off on trips around the city and surrounding areas. It was majorly convenient to do it this way. The taxi drivers I got we're all very pleasant and rather skilled at dodging the motorcycles and pedestrians that seem to rule the roads here! 

The hotel location is particularly good. It's only 5-10 mins walk from central Thamel, so you have all the shopping, eating and drinking etc very close at hand. It's within easy walking distance to Durbar Square, The Garden of Dreams and the old town (and OR2K which is a fantastic laid back veggie/vegan restaurant with a great menu and hygiene, nice staff and prices...genuinely going to miss that place!). 

Breakfast was average. I've had worse and better but you won't starve and there's enough to give you the energy you'll need for exploring around Kathmandu valley. The restaurant is open 6-10 morning and evening. Outside of these hours you will not be able to get room service. One evening I wanted a coffee and called down around 10.20pm to try my chances but was told they were shut. 

Despite power cuts the hotel has its own generator so you are always with light but not necessarily the power to charge phones/cameras etc. Although, that's actually a whole lot better than a lot of other hotels so I heard. There is always hot water but you will need to leave it to run for a little while to work its way through. 

They have free wifi around the hotel but it's pretty weak in the rooms. Reception and the restaurant have the best speed. 

Over all I would definitely recommend this hotel, but not for those who are used to 24 hour room service and all the trimmings that come with larger hotel chains. 

It's a beautiful building, in a good location with nice staff. I would just recommend enquiring about what room you are being allocated, so you can really immerse yourself in the atmosphere of the place and make the most of your stay.

This is the best experience I had in such a long time. The whole Team did a speculatar job from Regency club . A big shotout to Aastha to provide such spectular service. We would definitely be visiting again for sure.
One of the best places in Pokhara. This museum is VERY informative. If  you like mountains and museums, this place is heaven.

Great place, really wort to visit. Many temples and old buildings, street shops and restaurants... unfortunately, соме of them are ruined in the last big earthquake and haven't been repaired yet. 
Also, there is an entrance fee, 1000 rupees, I think they are charging it in order to collect more money for restoration, but it seems like that process is going really slow.
Check all temples and their amazing architecture and details, and don't miss to visit some of the great rooftop restaurants and cafes. Food is good and they offer great view on the square and surrounding city

We only had an hour to visit the museum so the review is based on what were able to see and absorb in that time. There was some interesting information about cultural groups in the Himalaya and a section about people who have climbed Everest which was really interesting. The museum though feels a bit tired.

Nice to be by the water but not in it (though maybe by one of the little boats). Several locals told me it’s nice to swim but water is very dirty so I wouldn’t recommend it. Lots of cafes/restaurants along the waterside which are good to hang out, but the actual lake is kinda whatever
Good place to buy your hiking equipment for a reasonable price. And to buy a gift to your loved ones back in your place.

Nice and welcoming staff!! Ready to help for information or any other query you might have. I was there on my own. Unfortunately, wifi did not reach my room! Bathroom could have been more clean though.

After reading good reviews we landed in tis property for 3 nights in a Regency Suite, which offers club benefits, The club is not at all offering quality services and food and drinks were substandard. the room furniture is worn out and sleeping mattress was worst giving backache, did not expect this from Hyatt, they need urgent upgrade , The hotel has a beautiful campus but stay is not worth the money they charge per night. The club addition is a fiasco , please do not expect any quality drinks here, even a fresh juice or cocktail is not provided in the cocktail hours, the wines are the worst possible

Good hotel but room dusty and not properly cleaned.  No service at pool.  Rox bar very good but out of the way behind what seemed to be a locked door - led to bar entrance but which was actually on floor below.  Quality of staff was saving grace.  Drawikaâ??s hotel also used during stay and much better.

The "monkey temple" may be a very holy place with a long history, but I was surprised and disappointed to see the temple in disrepair and surrounded by rubbish, especially given the entrance fee. It's perched high on the hillside of the Kathmandu valley, with an epic staircase to reach it's main gate, however despite this, the temple felt soulless. A stark contrast to its brother Boudha, on the other side of the city. Even the view, which deserves to be spectacular, is currently ruined by the haze that currently inhabits Kathmandu. I dearly hope Swayambhu can be returned to its once great glory.

An interesting combination of exhibits on the Nepal culture, different dress codes as well as a lot of information and pictures of the Nepal mountains.
Perhaps it is a little bit old fashioned but there is plenty of interesting gems to be discovered.
Fantastic large picture of Everest showing the base camp through to the summit

The poor breakfast worse it could have been. We checked in on 9th June with a hope to enjoy the long pending vacations memorable in a beautiful looking property in the valley of Pokhra . But to my shock I found few things in this hotel really below the mark .
Cons :
1. Breakfast : On both the days we found the breakfast really stale , The parathas. Chole bhature without any taste , the inferior qwality of breakfast included a dry poha and watery Upma no options for vegetarians for live counter .
2. Regular Power Outages : there were regular power outages made at times unbearable due to hot humid weather 
Pros :
Loaction : location on the lake side road just a small walk to lake
Pool : beautiful pool setup 
Landscape : the landscape of property was nice with lot of greenery around

A most do in Kathmandu which were a bit deceptive. There's a lot of monkey, a beautiful view but also a lot of tourist and more than a lot of shop! This spiritual place looks more like a local shopping mall than a temple. 
Easy to access and not too expensive recommande it nonetheless.
The museum was dated with a lot of mountain information but I wasn't interested. It is not worth the visit.
I ordered breakfast and cappuccino coffee here. It is amazing taste and odor. The taste is totally different from the others coffee shop. I don’t want to leave this place and sence.

Been there 15 times to see the Annapurna Himalaya ranges and beautiful sunrise but never enough,recomemded to visit in the early morning as you could see crystal views .Also pokhara valley can be seen from there including,Dhaulagiri,Nilgiri and Manaslu Himalayas ranges.

we were welcomed by a very rude and unpolite staff. disappointing. we stayed before and requested already for the same kind of room. altough it was confirmed the room was not available. disappointing. in return they offered an upgrade to a very spacious suite room. nice. on the other hand that roon was located close to the streets so the noice and loud live music from the streets comes into the room (till 23h00). that is really bad when one wants to go to bed early. breakfast is ok. the garden on the other side is a real treat and a plus to the hotel. the fact that the staff is unwelcoming and the fact that one can really "join" the live music from the bar next door (in the hotelroom) made it our last stay in this hotel.

It is close to the city of Pokhara. Evenings are over crowded and we had to walk till the end of the lake to hire a boat.
 But we really enjoyed the boat ride. We hired for an hour. We enjoyed the boat ride alot. It was amazing to see many boats and hotels around the lake and temple inside the lake in an island. You can also enjoy the songs sung at the bars by great singers while you are on the boat ride. Can't forget the evening.

We booked a room here for 2 nights, Dec 30, 31 for 10K a night. An hour into getting the room, the washroom smelled of cigarette smoke and soon the whole room was filled with the smell. Talked to reception and their casual response was that there maybe someone from another room smoking (this is a non smoking hotel apparently). The staff are aware of the recurring issue based on my conversation with them and seemed absolutely clueless on a fix. A very irresponsible management to not address such a recurring issue. 

They made a number of silly excuses such as there might be small holes between rooms causing the smell to seep through lol. They also blamed the residents in the room above us. When asked about taking action, they were reluctant and admitted that they didn't know for sure.. We asked for a different room and they didn't have any that met our needs. They didn't offer any resolution or an ounce of apology (maybe some training for the staff on conflict resolution/accountability/responsibility?). I had to ask for an upgrade room and they offered a "Suite" room for a night as it was booked for the 2nd night. Although the "suite" room didn't have the smell it was overlooking the entrance of the hotel.. the curtains didn't even cover the whole window causing outside light to come though at night. All the walls are so thin, you could hear someone sneeze outside. Don't really have to mention that we couldn't sleep properly. We went back to our original room the next morning and it smelled good for a while and then the cigarette smell came back. Requested reception folks to spray some fragrance and ofcourse they ignored it. We had to "sleep" through the smell. Even if you are a smoker, I am pretty sure you wouldn't want to sleep through that. They wanted us to pay extra for the upgraded suite room even though its an inconvenience caused by the hotel. At the end of our stay, there was no apologies from the reception staff and no discount offered for the inconvenience. On the other side, the housekeeping staff and bell boys were absolutely friendly and helpful. 
Dont book this hotel if you dont want to go through this or ruin your perfect vacation..

We really enjoyed our 5 night stay at Trekkers Home. The staff is freindly, the location is excellent and the view from the rooftop area is great! 
In particluar the hotel manager Saroj was very kind. He helped us finding places to go in Khatmandu and gave us advice for our first trek in Lantang Valley. 
Would definitely recommend.

Kantipur offered us an amazingly relaxing home for over a week as I recovered from mountain illness
whilst hiking in a remote area of Nepal. Staff are so friendly and helpful! Breakfast is a delicious choice  and the chef was happy to modify for my special needs. Rooms are spacious and quiet with large bathrooms, yet you are located right on the edge of Thamel! Built 22 years ago in Newari style, lovely carvings greet you at every turn.  A huge grassy area and paved outdoor area allows instant refuge from the bustle of Thamel and to enjoy the warmth and breeze. Highly recommended if you enjoy a casual and relaxing space
of beauty.

I've stayed there twice with my family and the neighboring building looms worse each time.  If you're near that side, prepare for small, dark, dank rooms.  Even the outside area is being ruined by the construction next door.
That said, the hotel is in a great location, good service, and a good breakfast.  The other food and drinks are over-priced--there are so many options nearby.
For the money, I'm sure I can find something quieter and less claustrophobic.

We stayed total 4 nights and had overall positive impression. The garden is nice. Sometimes it's a bit noisy even at late night. The ensuite was too small and impossible to prevent shower water on the toilet seat, which was very annoy.
Densely packed streets but a fun place to shop. A lot of variety. We were  bit rushed so couldn't shop much.
It was an awesome experience that i have got after visiting this place nature , Beauty but Boat riders make fool to foreginers for Boat Ride

We took a row boat two times. Once to go around the lake and another time to cross for hiking to the peace pagoda.

It’s very nice to go down to the lake and take photos especially early morning or at the evening. Lots of nice restaurants have a view of the lake also.
Swayambhunath Temple is a very good hindu religious place. I visited this place myself. One will love this place.

Must visit place
Take a guide who charges 150 INR per persons for 2 hours. Negotiable. Lots of monuments with history behind each. Under renovation with help of China and Japan after a huge damage due to earthquake in 2014. Kalbhairav statue is awesome. Shooting of Amiabh starrer Mahan took place here. Very nice Doms and tops of temple. Krishna temple, Shiva temple. Cost 100 INR

This hotel is great for providing a simple oasis of calm in the bustling, polluted city centre. It's extremely close to the tourist area but on a quiet sidestreet giving you some sense of much-needed tranquillity (important for sanity in Kathmandu!). Most people seem to complain of noise from their hotels in Thamel but here, that was simply  not a problem. 
It's fairly clean, a very elegant hotel built in Newari style, with decent rooms and hot showers. The small garden provides a downtime area and the free wifi is a big plus. 
However, the service could be much improved. The receptionists certainly don't fall over themselves to help you or to make you feel welcome.
The hotel is dark, and while their eco concept sounds great, perhaps it is also the reason why our towels absolutely stank. 
Also, unfortunately their standard double room is actually automatically a twin, ie two single beds. So couples either have to fork out for the posher deluxe rooms, or sleep next to one another in single beds!
The coffee was awful, so we didn't venture to try the other food.
So all in all, it's probably one of the better choices around Thamel, lovely Newari design, also has all the basics, and a nice garden. BUT it's nothing to write home about, and the atmosphere isn't the best.

We took a boat on the lake and our boat man was great he took us all round the lake we saw monkeys in the trees and the Temple in the centre of the lake, fish eagles in the trees and at a distance swooping to catch a fish it was just so relaxing he told us it was a man made lake with the dam further up the river it was such a lovely trip well worth doing.

It was great! Great service and really appreciated the good care. Special thanks to Star & Sabina to make this trip unforgettable.

Would definetely recommend the resort. Best hotel I have been in nepal so far. Very good bar service and quick laundry service.

Super comfortable and with all the services and friendly staff I could want pre= and post trekking! The ultimate breakfast and atmosphere. Great location away from the traffic, easy walk to attractions

The museum is a well laid out display of the various peoples and cultures of Nepal, along with a wealth of artifacts of life in the mountain regions. Photographs of the various Himalaya mountain ranges along with data on climate change makes one wonder what the future holds. A photographic exhibition including color prints of Sir Edmund Hillary's Everest Mission in 1953 was fascinating. A must visit.
Best Place for stay and touristic hub in Nepal. In Thamel you'll find a large variety of local food vendor stalls and markets, restaurants and cafes.

Terrible place.

They didn't send a pick up as I arranged with them previously. I spent all my phone credits having the taxi driver ask them for directions.

The hotel itself is filthy, it looks like it was never cleaned ever! The room's electric appliances are dusty and don't work. The bathroom is tiny you can't even shower in it.

The mattress is PAPER thin, and the lighting is depressing. We arrived with MASSIVE bags and asked to be taken to our room. Instead they started asking me what kinda room I wanted even though I had already booked over the phone. Still the man at the desk took us on a tour. I went along because I was curious of the other rooms, however he was just showing us all kinds of rooms he had instead of taking us to one according to what we asked for. Eg. took us to the darkest room ever (not just hotel room, but among all rooms I've ever seen in my life) even though I asked for a well lit room.

Loved OR2K so much we went 3 times in 4 days for breakfast/lunch/dinners. Its got a great view, wonderful healthy menu for vegetarians and meat eaters love it too! Highly recommend the Hummus with mushrooms & onions, the Dal Baht set and the Dosa- so delicious!!!! A must visit in Pokhara.
The food is very good, the swimming pool is very clean and rooms are also very nice the bed is very comfortable and there are various others things like spa, gym etc
A great restaurant! The sitting areas are so nice and comfortable. The best dish was the Combo Platter, with homus. falafel, salad, labanne, baba ganoush and tahini. Don't miss it!

We very much enjoyed the food and view at OR2K.  The Turkish dish we had made us want to go to Turkey on our next trip!  The Hummus was great and the Chocolate soufflé was very well done with a small pot of Nepali Masala Milk Tea.  We left very happy.  Check out that view :).

Just a relaxing paddle trip. Not much to say.
You can choose paddle boat or canoe.
You can go solo if there is no one fishing otherwise you need a guide.

This is the most preferred place for a traveler around Kathmandu, It has good shopping area, and also has good place to eat. I love HimalayasCraftNepal in thamel to buy singing bowls. It also have good hotels. The area is clean and tidy with good security also.
Has good food and service. I prefer the old restaurant before they 'did it up'. The staff were friendlier and the place less formal and more comfortable.

The food was very good, and we all had a pleasant evening until it came home to pay. We gave the cashier 5000rs expecting 270 in return, and we are surprised to hear him say that we owed him 1000rs more. My friends are very confused because they were certain that they handed him 5 notes of 1000. Unfortunately for the cashier, I know this scam. He wore a big jacket which allowed him to trade two of the bills to 500 notes. After pressuring him for a little while, he caved and gave us our change. He just wanted us to get out and avoid giving away his trick!
Beautiful place with so much history.  Still a lot of construction trying to fix buildings from the earth quake, but you felt like you where in a place where so much history began.

The lake covers most of the town of Pokhara and is really big. Its periphery has been maintained well and immediate lake shows has been developed enough so that it is a good place to sit and spend time looking at the calm waters. A boat ride in the lake takes you amidst true natural beauty and if you are lucky you get to see water of the lake in backdrop of green mountains with snowy peaks at top - Simply a picturesque view. The safety is also considered to full and there is a watch post which maintains close vigil on the tourists and we ourselves witnessed their rescue operations when a tourist boat was caught in rough weather.
I enjoyed everything in this place (delicious food, nice environment and staff). I highly recommend Falafel plate and vegeterian sizzler
Nice place to relax and have good food. Good music, good choice of food and drinks. Prices are not very high.

This time i am check in this hotel 3rd time. previously I like this hotel services and ambiance so this time also I choose this hotel.  I always prefer staying in good hotel and higenic rooms with peace enviroment.  This hotel is in a city center and easy to access my all customers and also better to travel airport.  Thanks SACHINA TIWARI for warm welcome and evertyhing.

Terrible Terrible Terrible room and services. 
Room was very dirty and had to waited 4 hours for check in. I think they do differently for Nepali guests and foreigners. Staff was not friendly and extremely expensive compared to what we received.

Another Unesco site with a beautiful market full of gorgeous pieces of art. Make sure you bargain. Based on your nationality they increase prices, but most vendors have similar items. Some items are traditional Nepali I have not seen in other places. The site is beautiful to walk and explore.

My third year in a row to Pokhara. Fewa Lake is a centerpiece. This year walked a good way along the lake. Mountains and view in background make it idyllic. Had coffee on the pier and soaked in the night sights/lights. The fish from this lake are so tasty also (ate some at Landmark Restaurant).
A good oplae to see the Annapurna range and Fishtail Mountain, from the Viewing Tower, good place to paraglide from, few eating places and tourist shops, but quiet apart from that.
Looks very unclean and lots of weeds. The pathways are also not clean. Seems like this lake is dying a slow death

The little boats, the surrounding hills, the changing light make this a delightful focal point of the little town.  Be sure to cross the road and enjoy some lakeshore time.  I am sure if the clouds had been clear and we could have seen the Annapurna range it would have been spectacular.

You may want to rent a boat and the lifejacket, but besides the exercise part of boating,viewwise there isn't much.The water is quite opaque, hence one cannot view any marine life.You may sight a couple of Monkeys on the far side shores.
Amazing place. Parts destroyed by 2015 earthquake. But still lovely and must see. 1 hour drive out of Kathmandu

Beautiful swayambhunath temple in Kathmandu ☺️☺️
Just be aware of the monkeys 🐒. It's also known as the monkey temple!!

Extremely rude staff. I really don’t recommend anyone to stay there. Not worth the price at all Really not typical service for Nepal. There are much cheaper better places in THAMEL. Really low quality hotel. Do a favor to yourself & go to another place

Walked here from Lakeside (1h+) tricky to find as no signs! 500Rp entry (tourist) large 'un-Nepalese' building wastefully under used on the upper floor. Jaded old photos and displays. Looks like an 'externally funded' Euro type development which has had under investment since build? Worth a rush around on a spare day - perhaps...

One of the most unique shopping experiences 
Genuine and knock off antiques, clothing of all types for everyone, great restaurants, fun stuff and friendly people 
Many markets outside the walking center and plenty of choices for entertainment
Sabrina and all the others help me to have a very Time in this hôtel . I ll be back with pleasure.see you again room was so cleaning thank you for everything

The temple is a great thing and in my opinion a must see in Kathandu. However, the stairs up are not suited for everyone and the traders there can be annoying. The temple itself as well as the statues around are really nice but lots of rubbish as well as irresponsible building is cutting it a little. The view over the city is great.

If your are in ktm then you must visit ktm durbar  square. You will see lots of temple.  Taleju temple,  Kaal  Bhairav statue,  Kumari are among the best. And don't forget to have matka tea, narayan dai ko local  jhol  Mo:Mo.

The monkey temple was near from my hotel and we decide to go by walking about 20 minute in the morning time by waling in the local path . 

the temple is in the top where you need to get many upstairs but you can see the good view of Kathmandu and the morning sunshine was the best part of the place.

you can see lots of monkey on the temple and beware of the food you catch in your hand .

Sarangkot is almost 30 min drive from pokhara amd usually visited for sunrise & paragliding tours. Road to sarangkot is not so good, Very steep & offroad at many places. I booked my paragliding through a local Pilot, who took 8K NPR and took me up, Fly and left me at hotel (all Insurance, videos & Photos included). Paragliding was awsme experience tough it was not sunny so we couldnt gain much altitude, So i would recommend select a sunny day for paragliding, when one can go high due to thermal effect. Take off & landing was awsme, It was great view from flight especially of Phewa lake & Peace pagoda. And Paragliding is easy and is recommended to a any healty men/women.

Great hot water
Beds a bit too firm
No tv
Wifi was good
Friendly staff
Central to thamel
Small balcony was covered by the new building next door
Pictures on website don't really look like the room
Room was clean

The Thamel area is great for buying local handicrafts or sampling the local food.
It is a very busy area with narrow streets & you have to keep your wits about you as motorbikes & taxis do drive down them at speed with little warning!
Despite how busy it is, we felt safe & were welcomed by the local stall holders although you do have to barter a lot to get decent prices!
A must for any visitor to Kathmandu if only to soak in the atmosphere!

I really can't understand the 4 and 5 ratings accorded by some reviewers. This place is in the heart of Thamel but there is little else in its favour. It is a grungy dingy place with service staff sleeping in the lobby and the breakfast room ( when we walked in for breakfast at 7.15 am), The owners are exploiting their staff as well as guests by such unethical practices. well if you like staying in an hotel with smelly bathrooms!! rooms that smell off mold!!! Sarangkot is one of the easiest places to get to outside of Pokhara and one you will probably never forget. We hired a local taxi to get us close to Sarangkot, then we hoofed it up to the viewing spots.  Sarangkot is undoubtedly THE location for the finest views of the Annapurna range  of the Himalayan Mountains. From this vantage point you can see close to 30 peaks over 6000 meters (20,000 feet) with one - Annapurna I over 8000 meters (26,000 feet). The view is spectacular as you take in the view of these massive peaks. The Annapurna Range is in the Annapurna Conservation Area which was the first and largest conservation area in Nepal.

From the viewpoint, you’re afforded uninterrupted, panoramic views across a number of the most striking Himalayan peaks, including the imposing Dhaulagiri (8167m), the triangle peak of Machhapuchhare, Annapurna II and Lamjung.  The light show here is incredible, as the peaks turn from bright pink, to orange, and finally white.

Visit the temple and hop in again on the boat. The view itself is breathtaking. This is one of the best things to do in Pokhara. It's calm, serene and beautiful.

Absolutely mind blowing seeing the ancient temples of Shiva and seeing the Living God Kura..!! The most interesting place I have been so far.. Very unique and so much culture, sights and sounds to take in.. The nightlife is awesome as well..!

I have been going to Nepal since 1998.  Thamel is completely different now. The restaurants are not cheap (and I got food poisoning).  The shopping is a rip off. DO NOT BUY SOUVENIRS IN THAMEL. Walk down to Asan Tole and buy them there for less than 1/2 the price. "First sale of the day, lucky for me, lucky for you" "it is the off season and noone is buying, I will give you a good price"  Baby yak blankets.... look at the amount of blankets and think of the number of baby yaks in the whole world. Most shop keepers are a bunch of smiling thieves. I even speak Nepali, so  I could understand what they say to each other. KEDAR CRAFT in Asan Tole sells things for 1/4 of the price in Thamel.  Buy from the women's collectives that have fixed prices.

We ate 3 time good service good and
 relexing atmosphire, exellent food. Really enjoyed the vegan food there.

So we chose to go to Sarangkot after the sunrise crowds had left. We got some great views but honestly it wasn't much better than what we had from the Fishtail Lodge. Sarangkot is not de rigueur. If there is a more exciting alternative, do that.

This place is steeped in history of the Malla dynasty which ruled Nepal in the 17th& 18th Century. Beautiful architecture has been marred by the damage due to earthquake however the restoration work is being carried out diligently. A must see place for all visitors to Kathmandu

It was an okay trip to Sarangkot.
As we expect : we saw the range of the Annapurna, we had touristic price for the food and we met a lot of people.

I was originally provided a room in the old building. It was in need of some updating. There were insufficient power outlets; the internet was weak; the fuse for the rooming was triggered three times in 15 hours. i asked to move and was placed in the new building. The room was of international standard.  Breakfast in the Fun Cafe was disrupted by tour groups of 50+persons arriving at the same time for breakfast. Kitchens and wait-staff could not cope.  You can find better hotels in Kathmandu for an equivalent price.
The lake can be overcrowded on local holidays and weekends, The boatmen tend to fleece foreign tourists.

we have been there for 2 days. everything is perfectly amazing, best service, amazing garden, even they have conference hall for event. staff were amazing and beautiful atmosphere. overall we enjoyed our stay there. specially thanks to whole management run by Mr. Monmohan Operation manager. will back soon.
Fairly clean and well-run boating/canoeing, great for sunset viewing. Lots of amusement activities, great people watching. Touristy but fun spot.

another must see, little out of the center, still easy to access by bus, or with Patao motorcycle (cheaper than the taxi), full of monkeys (its called Swayambhunath, or Monkey Temple), view of the valley from the top of Monkey temple (lots of people on the weekend, go during normal weekdays!)
cannot live only in thames without visiting this place while I am in Kathmandu. Always good place to scroll around and good to see natural habitat of monkeys in the middle of crowded city.
Traffic, dust, narrow roads, no pedestrian space to walk. But the people are very friendly and pleasant. Not at all pushy for a sale. Small cafes and food places are quite good.

Property is old and the rooms are not well maintained. Needs major upgrade and the service team needs major orientation in providing superior service. Foul odour, equipment and fittings didn't work to name some of the problems faced. Thank god it was only one night's stay enroute to Pokhara!

Great food - Great service - Great entertainment evenings - what more could you want! 

After eating a few different places in Pokhara this is by far one of the best places that I ate food.  

Very relaxing vibe and comfortable pillows, they put on movie evenings when, I was there they plaid “Meru”.  They have a selection of different movies throughout the weeks so take a look and see what they have to offer you! 

Sunset views from the balcony are fantastic. 

Whilst I was out there it was my birthday and the manager brought out a tasty cake and a round of drinks for the friends! 
Customer service!

Being in Kathmandu and not visiting Durbar Square is a mistake. This place is like going through centuries and seeing how the Nepalese lived, their architecture, their customs, one of the best excursions in Kathmandu.

very enjoyable stay at the Radisson Kathmandu..my first experience..hotel was recommended to me by a work colleague.  Staff were very friendly.  Hotel was ideal situated to my business meetings.  Breakfast was very good. Airport transfers went very well.

What a let down for a five star hotel.
Room (507) dated, furniture tatty, dampness and mould on wall outside bathroom.  Bathroom extractor did not work. Tap falling to pieces. Tiles and walls discolored with dampness. I can go on and on. Called the manager to show him the state of the room. His attitude was unbelievably complacent. Thankfully on this occasion I was not paying for the room or I would have walked out..

Often, we find ourselves the only patrons in restaurants in Thamel and elsewhere because we don’t use TA or a guidebook to choose where we go. Walked into this place randomly and at first sight of being packed full of Lonely Planet types we wanted to run. We stayed only because the gentleman at the door had already made contact with us, we didn’t want to lose face, and sometimes it’s good people watching in places like this. Everyone there was having the Ultimate Nepal experience and was so impressed with themselves, taking selfies, food photos, and staring at each other to figure out who was the coolest and most in touch with Buddha. Food was slow to arrive, bland, and overpriced.

I got food poisoning, was up all night expelling myself, and am just coming back to life. Skip this place!

This is just a a word about the pool and the gym.
The pool in late November is open. The water is dang cold (+16) but the patio by the pool is still warm enough for chilling in your swimming shorts.  It will also be find in December I'm sure. Daytime heat is a bit over 20 degrees and it feels warm. There are decent covers for the lounge chairs and the towels are solid too.
The gym is alright. A solid 5/10. IT costs about 20 USD for one time use or 200 USD for a month. It has nearly everything you need and is run down as the rest of the reviews suggest. The cardio machines face some TVS (some English channels if you can swindle the locals) are mediocre and they're essentially overlooking the pool while all the other gym facilities are two stories lower. Odd but it's adaptable. The sauna, steamroom and jacuzzi are a fair 2/10 and rather appalling frankly. The steamroom is overly intense (zero visibility) and the sauna is dark (freaaaaakay). The hot tub is bubbling and hot but not at all tempting especially if you have any open cut as it's an incubator for diseases I'm sure. Everything else is like it's been trapped in the 70s and barely kept up. But hey, it's a gym and a pool in Kathmandu so that's rightfully worthy for some acclaim. Live the DReam!!!

I’m very impressed with her services !

I’ve wonderful experience with this hotel !

Kathmandu is the filthiest city that I have ever seen. The streets are strewn with garbage, the river is so choked with garbage that it barely flows, and the air has enough dust and smoke in it to be essentially unbreathable. The centre of town has no sidewalks or crosswalks, it is chock full of motorbikes, cars, and tuktuks, there are scammers and beggars on every street corner, and there is scarcely a tree in sight. I would recommend avoiding Kathmandu at all costs; its physical and auditory pollution will shorten your life.

The wife and I booked a garden-facing room online for three nights in May 2016, which ran a shade over $50/night. We arrived, were shown to our room, and found the room to be... unpleasant, to put it mildly. Even taking into account the slightly-reduced standards in Nepal, this room was bad, especially for the extremely high price (other hotels provided much better quality for half the price). Had we stayed all three nights in that room, I would've given KGH one star. 

After the first night, we haggled a small price increase so we could stay in one of the suites in the main building. This room was excellent, had AC, and we had no qualms with it. Other pros: the courtyard was very nice and provided a reasonably quiet atmosphere, the breakfast (included) was decent, and the restaurant was good. The hotel staff all spoke very good English and were very helpful. At the end of the day, however, we spent way more $$ than we should have for three nights. 

Final thoughts: bad value for money in all rooms, though the overall experience in the suite and restaurant was very high.

We had the share platter that was very nice in deed. The restaurant is beautifully fitted out, service very good and food very tasty- very happy.

I had eaten at Olive Garden once before for a large group, fixed-menu meal and it was fair.  We tried it for dinner last night just for a regular weekend dinner and we left very disappointed and still hungry.  The "Crispy calamari" had more crispy than calamari and was overcooked.  The beef was the toughest beef I've had in Nepal (after living here for 1 year).  Nepal is a generally Hindu country, so beef can be a challenge, but La Sherpa, Chez Caroline, and even the Shangri-La hotel consistently have very tender beef with great flavor.  The Olive Garden's was really tough, had little flavor, and (unless you count the three leaves of garnish) no vegetables.  Both of our main courses were small portions, presented very nicely on overly huge plates.  Sadly, despite the appetizer and mains, we left the restaurant $50+ poorer and still hungry.  

Main point: don't waste your time or money at Olive Garden.  If you have transport try one of the other places around.  If you don't have wheels, just walk up the street to Vino Bistro.

We visited Durbar Square on a busy Sunday afternoon with a guide. Seriously damaged in the 2015 earthquake, the area is in various stages of reconstruction. Scaffolding, buildings braced with supports and piles of rubble/stone/debris are everywhere. Locals (and the homeless) lounge on monument steps. It feels like there are hundreds (maybe thousands) of pigeons. Sadly, I didn’t feel the magic of this UNESCO World Heritage Site where Nepal kings were once crowned and lived. Still, there’s plenty to see so it is still worth a visit. For me, the highlight was a glimpse of the Royal Kumari (Nepal’s living goddess) from her window in the Kumari Ghar. Our guide said there is a published schedule with times of her regular appearances. These are approximate, as she decides when and if she will appear. We waited about 20 minutes past the scheduled time, then suddenly there she was, peering out into the Kumari Chowk (courtyard) for a few minutes before moving away from the window. The current Kumari is now about 4 ½ yrs old. The 3-story courtyard is itself worth a visit with its intricately carved wooden balconies and windows.

Had visited this beautiful lake in Pokhara a long back ago. This lake is surrounded by forested hills and is a popular tourist attraction.

This beautiful lake is the second largest lake in Nepal. It is ideal for boating. There are colorful boats docked near the boating point. Also, there is a view point for viewing the lake and had to pay a small fee to enter this point. There is a Tal Barahi temple located on a small island in the lake that can be accessed by boat. On the other side of the lake, there is a dam. There is a charge for boating for 1 hour as well as half an hour. It is visited by locals as well as tourists. Its so peaceful and tranquil. However, fishing can be done in this lake. It is a good place for photography. However, this lake is a bit dirty.

This beautiful lake is an ideal place for families, couples as well as friends. It is a must visit place and should not be missed while in Pokhara.

In terms of lake frontage this hotel is as far from the main hustle and bustle of the main city as you can get - at the very outskirts of the lake. The lake is in front of the hotel and it was a pleasure to view skydivers and hanggliders descending just a few hundred meters away - and seeing groups of locals doing their best to catch fish as the sunset. A series of farms surround the hotel which made it feel like being in a more remote rural setting (cows). And a new building was underway adjacent to the hotel which was a sllight distraction to the otherwise serene vista. But the location is too removed to walk back into the main shopping and market area that makes this part of Pokhara so interesting. I think this hotel is good for a those wanting a short getaway. The pool looks great. The restaurant is quite good and staff friendly. Bring a good book
Excellent service. Outstanding resort. Staff is friendly and professional mr prem and mr nishan is smile face and helpful.

I went here really to see the temple from the enigma video in the 90s but that temple is a little further away. Enjoy your walk!

However the service is not in line with its peaceful mantra - the front desk staff were unwelcoming, the restaurant staff pushy and the management always trying to sell you some trip or other. The Welcome to the hotel was perfect. With FREE Transfers arranged from Bun Station.

We got a Quite a nice room, and we were happy about it. But When tried to view outside saw a staff of hotel throwing garbage into artificially made lake around the hotel. Did inform the management about this and they told its just they have to educate there staffs more and did apologise.

I am aware that you cannot expect first class service in a poor country like Nepal. A country recovering from a catastrophic earthquake in 2015. But you should not be expected to pay a very high over-price when the service you are getting is corresponding to the standard of the place where it is located.Typically when you pay for a Superior Room you expect to be paying for the room, irrespective if it is single occupancy or double. Here you pay a high rate only to find out that you are just paying for yourself (your wife has to pay extra 30USD/day) and that you are not even getting breakfast. Which is served at 15USD per day. Which may not sound too much to the standard European traveller, but if you think that dinner for two in one of the top restaurants in Kathmandu will not cost you more than 25USD (including drinks), then you feel that you are being ripped-off.Going back to the Superior Room. Well, be aware that it is located in a different building than the rest of the hotel services. This means that, if you want to swim, you will need to get out of your room and building, cross the street half-naked, and then make it to the fourth floor of the main building (after showing yourself off around the lobbies of two different buildings) before you can enjoy a refreshing splash! Maybe you are overheated and would like to have a relaxing bath. Well, you can't. The Superior Room does not have a bath tube. Moreover, the shower has a nice see through glass to the room and if you want some privacy there is a thick curtain that insulates the shower area. Very nice (ans sexy) indeed. But it becomes less nice when you roll down the curtain only to find the is mouldy and (very) dirty. Getting to a new country some times can be a very stressful experience and you may like to be fetched by your hotel's shuttle from the airport. Well, while this is typically a free service in most hotels around the world, in Radisson Hotel Kathmandu this comes at a price. And at a price which is twice the standard taxi rate!If you are coming to Nepal, it is very likely that you are planning to do some trekking. In such case, you may be willing to live your more bulky pieces of luggage in the hotel and travel a bit lighter. Well, be ready to pay Radisson Hotel Kathmandu 15USD. Why? No reason. Just because the feel that they can take advantage of the needs of their clients. Any other hotel in the city will provide this service for free.The staff is lovely and diligent.

Top 3 best things about Kantipur Temple House -

1. Architecture - built in 1998 inspired by Ancient nepali woodwork and architectural elements. We were just mesmerized by how calm and relaxed we felt at the property. 

2. Service - The staff is extremely helpful, we were never disappointed by them. Whenever we needed any help or a recommendation, the staff were there for us. They really made us feel comfortable and welcomed. Especially Suman, you rock man!

3. Location- The location is in the centre of Thamel, the bustling tourist centre of Kathmandu. It’s located within minutes from the best restaurants, cafes and shopping places. Very convenient!

4. Food - We had breakfast included with our room and they kept it simple, which is the best thing. Organic eggs, fresh yogurt, fresh fruits, delicious Nepali coffee and the lovely staff always put us in the right mood every morning.

5. Atmosphere- The hotel is silent, calm, peaceful and relaxing. After walking through noisy Thamel, reaching KTH was always a delight. It always felt like we can be home. 

There’s so much more I would love to write but I’ll leave it to you to experience this place for yourself. 10 stars for KTH if I could give them.

Thamel is a very unique place. There is a lot of nice feeling about it for great foods and architecture. However, there are many people looking for tourist for the services. In the first day I arrived there, one guy approached me to be a guide without license. Beware of what they expect you to pay.

- WiFi is a disaster. In 4 days of stays, we never found a decent wifi speed, even mail attachmentments took hours to load. 
- Restaurant's food quality is pretty average. We have tried different cuisines but most of them are tasteless or not properly prepared, except Nepali Thali. After 10PM, there is no food, no room service nothing. So if you need midnight snacks, you better prepare yourself well ahead. 
- Breakfast items are seriously basics like dull cabbages, hashbrowns etc. and cold most of the times if you come bit late like 8.30am. There is no other restaurant, except that.
- Spa was a disaster. It is smelly and without any courtesy or comfort offered by service providers.
- The road leads to property is a very rough one with no lights at all and most of the taxis charged us high price to come to the hotel even from lakeside. 
- The neighboring location is very poor with a vast bare land just behind of the property so if you don't get front facing rooms, you are really in a mess and can't even use the balconies. 
- Outdoor swimming pool and staffs are pretty rude maintaing it. 
- Only plus point is the vast lake view and that's it. But the pics given in agoda/booking.com with snow capped mountains can be seen from the property are not the real view. 
- Rooms and beds are very comfy though but if you just want a very basic hotel with little expectation, this property suits you. But if you want bit of relax atmosphere and moderate luxury, this will definitely not be a good option.
- For people with need to check emails and connected to internet all the times, this property is no where near a catagory B even. 
- So overall our experiences were very basic and we are sure not to chose this property next time we are in Pokhara. We would rather chose Temple Tree or Brahi which was one of the mistake we have done this time :(

The gym is a nice perk but expect morning and post-work crowds. If you like to eat a lot, the breakfast buffet will keep you going --- otherwise order room service or sit outside by the pool (morning dining options are limited). We hired a covered boat and were rowed around the lake...saw many birds including a kingfisher. The lake is very clean and people friendly and kind.

We visited the International museum of Mountaineering at Pokhara.
It depicts the details of the pics, implements, maps,& names etc of people who tried ( at times lost) to scale the highest peak on earth, "The Everest"("Sagarmatha"). 
It is interesting & intriguing to see the heavy loads, primitive implements, mountaineers carried in early years,  compared to the light weight & more sophisticated gadgets & implements now used for scaling the peaks.
Worth a visit. It is a pleasure for a hiker/ mountaineer to hang around this place, & get a whole surge of adrenaline.

After a day of sightseeing, lounging by the pool was the perfect way to unwind. Every member of the staff was thoughtful and attentive, making us feel genuinely cared for. Most of all the staff there were so welcoming and helpful, particularly Suman who helped advise us and arrange logistics for our trek and holiday. I stayed in Hyatt for two nights with my 5-year-old daughter to attend a business event, and we both got ill the first night after breathing the terrible air inside the room. I had noticed that the heating system was too noisy but recognized only later that their air filtration system was faulty. I developed severe headache within hours of staying in the room and high fever and lost voice cord by midnight. The next day I flung the window open and let the chilling Kathmandu air come in, which is when we both began to feel better, ironically.

I later learned that several other people who'd stayed in Hyatt for the same event, had fallen ill too. Especially as we are considering corona virus threats, it was very irresponsible of this so-called five-star hotel to be so careless about its air filtration system. 

Other "minor" glitches: We'd checked in late in the night and it took three rounds for their service staff to programme their entry cards correctly so we could enter the room.... The room phone was broken which they never bothered to fix... Their spa timings were written incorrectly in the room-book so I could not use the steam room when I turned up with unbearable sore throat and high fever (and lost voice cord) and the pressure of a public speaking engagement the next day.

It's one of those glitzy but third-class hotels which does enjoy amazing location and infrastructure but showed absolutely no interest in individual clients. Won't recommend this to anyone.

Now don't get me wrong, OR2K is good and when you've been in Nepal months and are craving something a bit different it's great- but it's never quite right.
We've eaten in OR2K Pokhara twice recently and OR2K Kathmandu maybe 6 times in the last 3 months.
We like it, obviously, or we wouldn't keep coming back!
The Pokhara branch is the nicer of the two, newer, cleaner and that stunning view. It's lovely to sit and chill here and just enjoy.
Everything is vegetarian and there are plenty of vegan options.
The menu is very multi national with a lot of Mediterranean, Israeli food plus some Indian / Nepali style dishes. It's the sort of place where you feel confident eating salad.
Sadly everything we've had there has not been quite right, always something that they just aren't spot-on with.
This often comes with a menu that is too large, too varied and staff that don't really know what each dish should be like.
It's something my husband ( an executive chef) has seen many times, first hand in the laces he's worked and second hand in the thousands of restaurants we've tried in the last 6 years of full time travel.
It's quite expensive here ( for Nepal) and they slap on all those extra taxes, so keep an eye on cost.
So good, very good, but not perfect.
They do good dosa... but the sambar and chutney aren't so good. Eggs for breakfast are fine, but the bread is way too big and chewy, dal makhani is nice, but the naan is dry and just...not perfect. The mushroom burger sizzler was the worst of the bunch. The mushroom burgers need review although the sauce and potatoes were good. My son loved his breakfast smoothy bowl, it was his first ever so he has nothing to compare it with, but he loved it.
Decent coffee, good wifi, ( unlike Himalayan Java on the floor below, where the wifi is unusable ), places to charge your phone or laptop.
It's a good choice if you want to spend a little more, but don't  expect perfection.
Managing expectations, I think, is the secret to enjoying your travels best.

The ambiance gave us the home like feeling. Its natural resources and lights are amazing for our family. The staffs were very kind, informative , and efficient. We enjoyed the pool so much. The plants and nature around feels much natural. Thank you Temple tree family for the amazing hospitality. We highly recommend this hotel.

Stayed at the hotel on several occasions. This time we stayed there for 5 days.

I lost my laptop inside Radisson Hotel in Kathmandu during my stay there on Nov 1 to Nov 6, 2016, but the hotel dealt with it very badly. 

What happened is the following. On November 2, at about 6:30am, I checked out my room in Radisson hotel, because I and my team had to take an early morning flight to Bhairahawa for a site visit. I stored my luggage at the hotel and only carried a small backpack with me. Then we had our breakfast in the hotel. At about 7:15am, we left the hotel. The Government of Nepal who invited us to visit the country kindly provided a government vehicle to send us to the airport.  By the time we arrived at the airport I realized that I left my laptop in my room in the hotel. I immediately called hotel and informed the reception about it and ask him to send someone to collect it and keep it for me. I left my local phone number to the person and asked him to call me back once they get my laptop. About 20 minutes later, I called the hotel again. This time another person picked up the call and again promised to check my room and call me back. About 10 minutes later I called again and this time the person at the reception told me that they did not find my laptop in my room. Since the boarding has already started, I told the person to report to hotel management and search it for me. On Nov 4, at noon time, we came back from the site visit and checked in Radisson hotel again. I asked about my laptop and the reception told me they did not find it. Then I went to see the duty manager, and the duty manager apparently was not even aware of the conversation I had with The reception on Nov 2. After I explained what happened, she first suspected that I may have kept my laptop in my luggage which I stored in the hotel. So we opened and searched the luggage together and did not find the laptop. At that point, she said she would ask the security officer to carry out investigation including checking CCTV footages. Then I went out for my meetings in different ministries in the afternoon. In the evening when I went back to the hotel and asked for results of the investigation. One security officer came and explained to me that they checked all CCTV videos and did not find anyone carry anything out from my room in the morning of Nov 2. I asked if I can watch those videos and the official said yes. So my colleague and I went together with that security officer to the monitoring room. He showed to us the video clips from the cameras that were installed on the 4th floor where my room was located. We saw that after I left my room at about 6:15am, one housekeeping person (the same person) went in and out of my room three times, at about 6:30am, 6:40am and 7:06am respectively. On the third visit, the house keeping person spent about 2 minutes in my room. When he came out of my room his hands look empty. But when he walked towards the elevator and got closer to the camera, we ( three of us) saw clearly a square shape hard object on his belly underneath his uniform. We replayed back that video several times and we (including my colleague and the security officer) can conclude there was an object hiding inside this person's uniform. I asked the security person to protect this video from being damaged and deleted and he promised he would do that and he would also report it to his security manager. On the next day, I reported the loss of my laptop to the metropolitan police, and the police immediately sent two inspectors to the hotel to check those video clips. However when police arrived in the hotel, the hotel's security officers refused to show those videos. They said they could not play the videos because they were encountering some technical problems, and they need at least three hours to resolve the problem. So police and us left. About 4 hours later, When my colleagues and I came back to the monitoring room in the afternoon, the security officers of the hotel told us that now they can play the videos, but the video clips for the period from 6:35 am to 8:00 am, the most critical time of the incident, were lost. Moreover, only the video clips of those three cameras on the 4th floor where my room was located, and only that 1.5 hours video clips got lost. All other video clips of all cameras are still there. Apparently someone deliberately deleted those critical video clips. At that moment, I think something totally wrong was happening in the hotel. It is no longer about one individual of the hotel who may have done something bad. I think something much bigger and much more systemic is going wrong in the hotel. It is also not about my laptop any more. It is about security and safety of many more guests and every guest who would visit Nepal in the future with very good expectation. Before I left the hotel, I requested for a thorough investigation on this case and get to the bottom on what exactly happened. Unfortunately, up to date, the hotel management has given no single word to me - no apologies and no explanation - as if nothing had happened. I am a frequent traveler, and I used to stay in Radisson a lot when I travelled to India and other countries. With this bad experience in Radisson in Kathmandu, I don't think I will stay in any Radisson any more in the future.

We had people running around shouting a yelling in the bedroom corridors at 4am in the morning - I have never heard anything like it - no sleep for my grandchildren ! I have never seen or heard anything like it.

Having said that, all of us would have no problem staying here again if and when we return to Pokhara - I would just check first if any bus tours were due in - or ensure that they were kept under some sort of control.

I stayed at the Kathmandu Guest House (KGH) after reading a review online .. unfortunately it was a really disappointing experience!
I stayed at this hotel over 2 periods: when I first arrived from Singapore, and again when I returned to Kathmandu from Pokhara, after a few days.
1. To start off, they have a very biased (& a little bizarre, in my opinion!) airport pick up policy - they will ONLY pick u up if u arrive via the International Terminal. When I arrived from Singapore, I was offered the airport pick up. However, they would not pick me up when I returned from Pokhara (via the domestic terminal), even though the domestic terminal was right next to the international terminal!
2. I had asked for a double bed on both instances. The first time, I relented when they gave me a room with 2 single beds. The second time, I was again disappointed to see 2 single beds when I went to my room. This time I demanded they give me a room with a double bed. To my surprise, they joined the 2 single beds in the same room to form one bed. It seemed like a very smart idea initially, until I realised much later that the light switches and power socket were now blocked (as they were located between the original 2 single beds!) ..
3. The toilet/shower: when u shower, the water runs from the shower area to the rest of the bathroom. All they need to do is put in a small kerb to keep the water in, & the rest of the bathroom dry. The basin area and the floor mat is permanently wet and soaking all the time as a result of this poor design! Too much work to put in a kerb u reckon??
4. This last point is a little controversial. But I wish to state my observation nonetheless .. I am of Asian origin, & an airline captain - I have travelled to many a destination and stayed at dozens of hotels. I have always been received warmly. Unfortunately I find the staff at the KGH less welcoming of Asian guests .. I must have walked past the KGH  reception area quite a few times, nodded and smiled .. yes they nod back. But they way they gush and fawn over guests from the west is incomparable! Be it a warm friendly “good morning” or friendly banter with new guests, the difference is so stark, when compared to guests of Asian origin. I am not saying the staff were rude or contemptuous; its more the case where they were very “different” with Asian guests. I did not feel anything remotely close to that when I visited restaurants, shops in Kathmandu, and even when I stayed at a really lovely hotel (Glacier Hotel & Spa) in Pokhara. I have always found Nepalis to be very kind and warm. Perhaps it’s an organisational culture that needs to be looked into ..? I can’t say for sure ..
Anyway, like the header of this review says, it was a very disappointing stay at the KGH.

Swyambhunath Stupa, also known as the Monkey Temple, is a Buddhist temple located in Kathmandu, Nepal.

The temple is situated on a hill and offers panoramic views of the city. The temple is an important pilgrimage site for Buddhists and is considered one of the holiest sites in the country. The stupa is comprised of a dome-shaped structure that is covered in shimmering gold and decorated with intricate carvings and colorful prayer flags.
The temple is surrounded by smaller shrines, and visitors can observe monkeys roaming around the temple grounds. The atmosphere at Swyambhunath Stupa is peaceful and serene, and a visit here is a unique opportunity to experience the spiritual and cultural heritage of Nepal.

I wanted to love this restaurant. I heard a lot about it. I liked the ambience generally, and the wait staff were friendly, but a little insistent.

What I am most disappointed about is that I spent an or more of my time drafting a very polite email to the management of OR2K on ways they could improve the menu for vegans (there is a real lack of options and some vegan options were not available in the forseeable future). Its easy to make small adjustments, but I am really disappointed I did not get any response, when I took so much of my own time to be helpful. These are my main suggestions:

- Have a vegan icon, so we know which food in the menu is vegan.
- Have some vegan desserts! There are many vegetarian restaurants these days that do all vegan desserts (they are so easy to make - heaps of recipes on the internet!!!) so that everyone can eat dessert.
- I love babaganoush! But I’ve never had it with mayo. I make it with tahini or just oil and lemon and its very delicious. It would be great if you could have babaganoush that we can all eat! There are a lot of people that are dairy and egg intolerant (meat eaters) that couldn’t eat this either.
- It would be great to have savoury vegan breakfast items! So many recipes exist, (New Orleans bar has a very delicious tofu energy breakfast!).
- Its super easy to substitute oil for butter (for example the couscous - oil instead of butter and pesto - without cheese - its cheaper and very very tasty!).
- Its also super easy to make bread using non dairy milk.
- It would be great to have more substitution items on the menu and I understand its quiet in Thamel at the moment, but when there are limited vegan options, having vegan meatballs available would be awesome.

I even offered to come spend time to show the chefs how to substitute (I was there for 5 weeks). But no response. 

I found much better vegan options at Places (highly recommend) and at New Orleans (great breakfast and great substitution options - very impressive)!

Its just so disappointing that a vegetarian restaurant cares so little about making their menu accessible for non-dairy consumers and vegans.

Swayambhunath Stupa, also known as the Monkey Temple, is an extraordinary spiritual site in Kathmandu, Nepal. With its tranquil ambiance, captivating views, and rich cultural heritage, it is a must-visit destination for spiritual seekers. The towering white dome, adorned with prayer flags, creates a serene atmosphere for reflection. Intricate carvings and colorful murals depict Nepal's cultural legacy. Friendly local guides enhance the experience with their knowledge and passion. Swayambhunath Stupa offers a profound connection to spirituality and is an unforgettable destination for all travelers.

We visited Fewa Lake, essentially Pokhara downtown is poised on the parameter of the lake; you can walk along a toe-path that stretches' for many kilometers around the circumference, with many bars and attractions backing onto the lake.

From afar the area looks like a place of great natural beauty but up close the ravages of over-tourism and blatantly evident; the the Lake itself has been polluted by the accesses of tourism, with huge numbers of mostly visitors from neighbouring countries and some western visitors too. The water is littered with garbage including plastics and a film of diesel fuel. You can hire boats and navigate the Lake either with a guide (rowing) or hire a boat and row yourself, there are also diesel chuggers that can take you around the lake on mass. We opted to do neither. I suppose for me Fewa Lake is an example of unsympathetic and exploitative tourism, and has caused an area of amazing natural beauty and habitat to transcend into a rundown, unloved and neglected body of water with the primary aim of fulfilling the thirst of the tourist trade at the detriment of the environmental preservation.

Fewa Lake and Pokhara are beautiful, I have been here nearly a month and walk and run by the lake daily in the early morning. It is quiet and peaceful and littered with plastic carrier bags, plastic bottles and plastic wrapper.

The local Nepali swim, bathe, wash their clothes and fish from the water in the picture I am sharing with you. There is no waste management system here so the plastic bottles we buy and throw in the bin, or the carrier bags we readily accept from the shops to carry the smallest of shopping in is either burnt (the toxic fume are overwhelming), or tipped into the lake.

There are 3 SIMPLE things every tourist could do to reduce this avoidable waste.
1. Bring a resuable water bottle from your home country, or buy one here and top it up at multiple locations in Pokhara for only 10 rupee. This reduces the demand for individual water bottles and will prevent waste
2. Bring a cotton shopping bag from home, or buy one here and say NO to plastic carrier bags everytime they are offerred
3. Fizzy drinks are sold in glass and plastic bottles. Bycott the plastic and buy glass bottles which are recycled.

In my time here I have done the above daily and saved about 60 plastic bottles and 90 plastic carrier bags. Every little helps, please can you help too?

My visit to Swayambhunath Temple was a highlight of my trip to Kathmandu. Perched atop a hill, the temple offers a stunning panoramic view of the Kathmandu Valley—especially magical at sunrise or sunset.

The peaceful atmosphere, fluttering prayer flags, and the gentle hum of chanting make it a truly spiritual place. The stupa, with its iconic all-seeing eyes of Buddha, is both beautiful and symbolic. The steps to the top can be a bit challenging, but well worth the effort.

The temple complex is a unique blend of Buddhist and Hindu elements, with friendly monkeys adding a touch of liveliness. It’s a place where culture, religion, and nature come together in perfect harmony.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Kathmandu—whether you're spiritual, curious about Nepalese culture, or just in search of a peaceful escape with breathtaking views.

The village overlooks Pokhara and it would take us around 30 minutes to get there by van. It was raining. I told the guide I would not leave the van if the rain didn't stop. I have read about the muddy grounds in Nepal when it rains. Apparently, many tourists flock to Sarangkot to see the sunrise so there was traffic on the narrow winding path up the mountain. Our van had to park to one side of the road and my fellow travelers got off the van to trek up. The rain had subsided a bit by this time but it was still drizzling. I was wearing a hooded jacket anyway so I decided to climb with them. However, I stopped on the next slope and returned to our van. After Huangshan last year, I realize I am not made for mountain trekking. The traffic cleared and our van driver decided to drive all the way to the top where the viewing platform was and on the way up, I saw the "sunrise" moment and we were thrilled. I saw the same thing without having to climb the mountain. The grounds of the parking lot were really muddy so I decided to just stay in the van to wait for the others. I made the right decision today. Nothing lost. A sunrise is a sunrise. I saw it in Nagarkot a few days ago and I saw it again today. But if my Crocs got mud on them, I swore I would have left them in Nepal.

I stayed at Thamel during my stay at Nepal. I was really surprised to see that all of the people from Kathmandu came to hang out here. There were many pubs and clubs. Party and music never stops here.

Stayed for 30 days.  Rooms in new building much nicer than larger older building, but there is a bar nearby that plays very loud music.  Housekeeping is poor and unresponsive.  Be careful on the treadmills, especially in the 6pm to 7pm hour.  Electricity goes off fairly often, and though the hotel generator usually starts up 10 seconds or so afterwards, if you are on treadmill, it stops abruptly, so you can cause harm to yourself.

We only managed one night here, but it is a very good location near the lake, and has good facilities, although could do with a bit of updating. The pool is good size, and there is a pleasant bar adjacent. Breakfast was very good. Our room was on the first floor (there are no lifts, which you should bear in mind if you have restricted mobility, with a balcony looking over the garden and pool. Perfectly comfortable, but showing its age, and in need of an update. Staff were friendly and helpful. An enjoyable stay.

The stay was pleasant. Property is beautiful surrounded by lake. Hotel Staff is so kind and helpful.
