damaged after the earthquake. interesting suite to see and the living goddess is her temple which you can view twice a day

A number of people recommended this place - and upon mentioning it to locals, they seem rest assured that the KGH is one of the best places to stay while in Kathmandu. Hmmm...While the rooms are OK, you definitely won't be see them featured in Vogue Travel or Conde Nast Traveller any time soon. My room, in the older section, had a ceiling fan that mysteriously turned itself off after an hour of use. When I mentioned this to reception, they casually informed me that it was just part of the daily power outage which would last a number of hours. Be aware of this if you're planning on charging up your cameras or phones. The outage also meant showering in the dark as the bathroom is internal. As the shower and toilet are in close proximity, expect everything to get wet when showering - toilet, toilet paper......

My second room after coming back from a trek was in a quieter area - at my request. The view was of a brick cul de sac with a few pigeons cooing on the eaves. By early evening, the population of the 'rats of the sky' had grown - along with their noise and crap. I had to change rooms. Initially I was told there were no garden view rooms available but when I insisted, miraculously, there was one at $10 more per night.

Breakfast in the courtyard is sufficient and free wi fi throughout the guest house is adequate. The masseur is very good. Friendly and great for a post trek treatment. There is a free water cooler just off the garden and many people take advantage of this before setting out by filling up drink bottles. Reception staff are friendly. Would I stay again? Well the location is excellent - set in a little off the bustling street but I'd look elsewhere first. I did get a good discount as it was off season but you do get what you pay for.
Thamel is a street where one can get good food and best place to shop trekking gears and accessories. One can get local products also but have to bargain for that.

Everything in Pokhara revolves around the lake. It's simply beautiful. It's a popular place to  walk at any time of the day or you can hire a boat and relax on a water. The pictures with the lake also look so nice no matter where they are taken from...the air, the hill or your hotel room, cafe located near by.

I think we had a dahl bhat set, it was great ! Very flavourful :)

I recently stayed at the KGH for 4 days on a business trip.  I usually stay at a more oasis type hotel close to the airport but decided to give KGH a try after recommendations from a couple friends.
My overall impression is that it's a good hotel for nightlife and being in the thick of the Thamel district.  A lot of trekkers were staying at the hotel during my stay.  I was on business and found it not very business friendly.  Wifi was spotty and you can only be one device at a time with the login and I was constantly being kicked off in the middle of work.  There is live music every night in the courtyard.  This is great but not if your room is over the courtyard and you have early morning meetings.  The staff is fairly friendly.  I think they do overcharge for their car service and arranging taxis.  If you know the area and have an idea of a fair price you are better off going out to the street and flagging your own taxi.  Meters are not used.
I was disappointed in the breakfast.  There are not many choices and the bread was stale each morning. 
The hotel is still completing some renovations so perhaps this will solve some of the mentioned issues.

So after hearing positive reviews about this hotel from my boss, and reading the online raving about this hotel, we felt like even though it costs a bit much, we should stay here. So we booked the tickets online from our country, confirming payments and all. We contacted Ms. Shaguni, who arranged everything for us. Initially, we booked for 23rd night (standard room), 26night (deluxe room) and 27th night (deluxe room).
Later, our trip got a bit changed and then we requested them to change the dates and the room type. We wanted it to be 23rd night (standard), 24th night (standard), and 28th night (deluxe). So the number of days were same, just the two dates and room types had changed. So we asked for the difference for a refund since that was still so long before the trip (like 2/3 weeks before). BUT, they said they couldn't do it since the payment has already been processed online. So that was our first bummer. But 
Anyways, we reached the hotel. HOWEVER, the staff over there did not seem to know about our changed dates. So he had to spend time by rechecking everything. On the 24th, we went to Last resort for some activities. When we came back, and entered the reception area, there was another employee of the hotel named Mr. Juju telling us exactly these words "Oh! you guys came! We were waiting for you guys to check out. Another person has booked the room 3 weeks prior tonight." The words do not seem to be harsh, but the way he said it was very rude. 
We were like "WHAT!" So we confirmed with two employees of the hotel and still on the second day this guy is being rude and indirectly telling us to get out cause some other person came. We told him that there must have been some misunderstanding, cause we booked it way before tonight and confirmed it with his colleagues. 
He then went on checking on his computer and calling several persons and at last, he said "You are lucky. The person has postponed his trip." I don't know how we became lucky cause we booked this room almost 3 weeks before and now we just became lucky that our room was available on the second day of our staying. Awesome...
After the "joyful" encounter with him, we went back up to our room. When we tried to open our room, it did not work. My husband and I tried for at least 10-15 minutes and it did not work at all. Luckily another room was open and I requested to use their phone to call the reception. The reception said that he would send someone immediately. 
We sat on the carpet for 15 minutes. And then my husband had to go downstairs (there is no lift by the way, which is totally fine by us. Just giving a heads up in case someone has problems going up and down the stairs) and it was raining a lot. It was hail storming that night. In order to get to the main reception area, he would have to pass the garden in the middle of the rain. So instead, he went downstairs and talked to guards of this building so they could call them from their extension. 
Surprise! They still did not come!! My husband went down for the third time. There he waited for the guy to actually show up and then brought him upstairs. he then unlocked the door. And this whole "keys-not-working-properly" happened twice in the standard room we were staying in. 
Anyways, for the last night, we had our deluxe room. I requested a room with bath tub. Good news is, there was a bathtub. The Bad news is: it does not work. It just doesn't hold water, the cork does not fit in the hole properly and you know the drill...
And that is not the worst part.
Since the bathtub was there, there was not hand/push shower for the toilet. Which was odd because usually, the Asian/Indian countries have them. And even the standard room had it. But the deluxe room did not have it. 
These were the big problems. There were also minor problems like after I was done with the shower, I wanted to dry myself and discovered a big gaping hole in the towel. I wanted to have ice cream, and the hotel said they did not have any (seriously who runs out of ice cream?). And when I went down to ask if they had any bubble bath (that was me before knowing the tub does not work), I was rudely told that there is not such thing in this hotel. 
Another major turn off of this hotel: we did not get any double bed. Even in the deluxe room, we got two single beds. 
Now there ARE some positives about this hotel. The hotel actually looks nice. They have worked hard to keep it beautiful and pretty. The travel information desk was VERY helpful. The guy's name was Suraj. He helped us with information about what to do in Pokhara and in Last Resort. He also helped us booking the bus to Pokhara. And He was a very friendly guy. He would usually ask us how our day went whenever we entered the reception area. He was a genuine, sweet guy.
Considering all these above, I am rating this hotel as poor though. Because for the price we paid, we expected a lot more. Especially for the deluxe room. A hotel needs to have two things: beauty and staff coordination. Kathmandu Guest House lacked very much in the last one.

Thamel is a brilliant place to stay, to shop, to wander, to eat and to explore. You can walk all over and share the narrow winding streets with rickshaws, motorbikes and the occasional car.  Some streets are car-free.  Shops stay open to late and cheerful shopkeepers invite you into their shop with a welcoming “Namaste” and if you don’t want to buy they are very polite.  Everyone is so friendly and helpful.  All kinds of street food, cafes and restaurants.  Definitely try a rickshaw ride. They are so smooth and a great way to travel through the streets fast while still feeling part of the crowd.  Lots of cashmere shops and trekking shops and shops that sell the gurka knives called kukri.  We loved our four day stay in Thamel.

As a big fan of Or2k Thamel since 2013, I was very happy to find one in Pokhara on my return to Nepal in 2015. And with a great view of the lake! Over the years they always assisted me with ensuring meals met my dietary needs but now they have the best gluten free menu in Nepal and vegan options you can trust.
One of the best historical place in Kathmandu divided by hisroty and culture lord buddha statute is located here which is biggest in Asia

After visiting the OR2K branch in Kathmandu, we were hooked. We mostly had Israeli food, which is all made from scratch. The food is very tasty, fresh and light and a nice break from Nepali food. The staff is friendly and the view from the outside terrace is just breathtaking. Especially around sunset. A must visit when in Pokhara or Kathmandu.
went to visit Thamel for spa and restaurant all the time it went well and everything is just right next to each other for trekkers

v nice hotel w good amenities; overall v good value. Nice breakfast. Divided between two buildings but pretty seamless. V friendly staff v v nice spa. Gym, pool, and travel desk  not entirely up to standard.
Travellers paradise in Kathmandu. Everything available nearby. Loved the grocery stores for the local snacks and the souvenir shops. Gets crowded after 11pm. A safe place to stay!
Gritty, dirty, felt safe but definitely a red light district vibe, need all senses on high alert. Very very busy and tourists targeted by child beggers and scams
We just loved the monkey temple.  If you have any food with you, look out because they will steal it from you!
My favourite place to walk and relax, love the sunset and the activities there. Always good to be there.

i was amazed how the beautiful the building is.. i spend almost 2 hour to strolling around the square
it is very worth it to visit nepal

Swayambunath temple is also known by the name of monkey temple, because there are many monkeys that live there and also in the hill.
From the thamel district where i stayed, it is easier to get there on foot, by bike or by taxi. 
it is very easy to climb to the top of the hill even if some steep slopes
This temple is very beautiful.and is  frequented by the faithful

Interesting seeing the Monkeys slide down the rails of the stairs. 
Nice 30 min walk from Thamel and to stop at one off the roof top cafes on way back for a view.

Staying at Radisson Kathmandu was an unforgettable experience. From the moment I arrived, the hospitality staff made me feel welcome and pampered. The service was impeccable, with every detail attended to with care. The highlight, however, was the amazing staff like Anu and Manita at The Fun Cafe. Overall, my stay at Radisson Hotel Kathmandu exceeded all expectations, thanks to the exceptional food and hospitality staff.
the food was delicious it was late at night but still you served us fresh and hot at the night the ambience is very good the resort is lovely
Left sat waiting for staff to bring a menu for 15 minutes while they all played on their phones. We left and spent our money elsewhere.

First night we had a room where the shower floated the bathroom, the second room (we switched) had a window who was not closing, after we told them they didn't fix it until we left (5 nights). And in november it can be pretty cold in Nepal at night.
The room was okay, it was clean and the service was good. The roomprice is not that cheap, i sleeped already cheaper in pretty the same environment or even better. The breakfast was to expensive for what they offer (1500 Rupie is way to much). Nothing more to say.
Amazing property. Best hospitality. Staffs are very polite and helpful. I have visited here thrice and feels like home.

Prepare to bargain, look around first, very chaotic, many restaurants. Outdoor/Indoor kiosk after endless kiosk.  Really don't know where to buy. We went mostly for sales inside stores. Better quality in stores.  Good buys on puff jackets, scarves, pashmina, cashmere, fleece. Easy to get lost, GPS sometimes difficult to follow, so ask someone the direction then follow GPS. For restaurants we liked Fire and Ice, The Olde House, Toko Japanese, 1905.

The view,music and especially the food are 
.just right! Defently best vibes in Pokhara
You can come here just to chill in a sunny afternoon with a delicious ice coffee and enjoy the perfect view on the lake.

Please make it a stop on any trip to Khatmandu. You can still see a lot of its former granduer, and the small entry fee goes towards the restoration.

You can also see the efforts going into restore this place. The other noteable, is that we found the best Lassie's in Nepal around here.

It is only a short walk from the Thamel markets, so enjoy the stroll, soak up the atmosphere, and buy a few unforgettable trinkets along the way...

- This hotel was a good choice. The decor is nice and the rooms are fine. There is a good amount of space in the rooms. The food is decent and the location is good. Te drawback for me is the sewage smell that comes from the bathroom. Your must remember to keep the toilet seat down and the sink closed and the bathroom door closed.   The staff was fine. overall a not a bad choice.

Walking up to the temple you are surrounded by statues and monkeys 🐒 don’t feed the monkeys. Once you climb to the top you have an outstanding view of Kathmandu.  Be sure to walk around the entire complex.

Never ever take their complimentary food services. Its so boring n simple. Everyday the menue is same. Food items in dinner are boiled nad hospital type, not which is sought after in vacation trips. Even my kids refuse to swallow them up.

Rooms were large, need a little bit upgrading, the bed was creaky, suggest you remove the card in the room giving a number and email address for any service issues, as i did complain about an issue at the CAFE, however I did get a call at end of the day around 2039h, I told the lady concerned was busy with overseas call on my mobile to call back after 5 minutes, never heard from her ever again.

Overall property is good, needs little upgrading, it was much better than the Crown Plaza I stayed last year, however service levels poor,
I visited The Cafe only once, decided never to visit it again as basic black tea was not served, after asking twice, this is standard at property like Hyatt Regency, not sure what to expect from others.

It was really nice stay loved the chole bataura here. The staffs were really nice especially nabina she’s really kind and really helpful she’s really friendly too. Hope every staffs are like her. Thankyou very much for everything. Appreciate it. Xoxo

We stayed in the Radisson Hotel apartments while in Nepal for a friend’s wedding. Highly recommend this hotel to anyone (especially foreigners who want to feel comfortable). It is a great area to stay in. The rooms, the spa, the services, and the hotel breakfast buffet are all so lovely. The staff is very kind and professional. Big thank you to Anu for preparing a hot drink to soothe my sore throat while I was under the weather.

-Review by the wife ;)

Honestly, I am not sure why this place has this good a rating over here. Maybe, it's only because of the ambience, the decor and setting. If that's the only thing that you care about, you should go here.

If you actually care about the food, then, I can only describe this place as 'Meh!'
The hummus was watery, babaganoosh had tonnes of garlic in it, the yogurt used in the tahini sauce was bitter. If one prides themselves to be a mediterranean place, they should at least know how to cook the most basic of mediterranean dishes. In addition, the food is priced high and the place did not accept credit cards even though they "proudly" display that accept it! Also, the staff took 20 minutes to get the bill after we requested for it.

I give place two stars because of the ambience. But, for food, I would give it a one star. I have had much better mediterranean food for much less a price in other parts of the world.

Reached down a narrow sidestreet barely wide enough for our bus. Collected our room keys and queued for the one working lift. Other one having 'temporary repairs’. Eventually took the back stairs to our room on 3rd floor.
Room pleasant but all fittings/finish were to a very poor standard. Bathroom tap wouldn’t turn off. One tap very stiff. Shower taps were loose. Shower itself sprayed everywhere and water was very brown ! Chair in bedroom falling apart.
Had to phone reception to get wifi password etc. Line very poor. Could barely hear. Not sure why this info could not have been given with key.
Went to the bar across the car park. Just missed Happy Hour which was a shame as £6 for a bottle of local beer is a rip off. Seems to be the norm as most hotels in India/Nepal charge ridiculous prices for alcohol.
Dinner was very average with a choice of Chinese (lots of them around), Western and the normal token Nepalese dishes. Some of our party had earlier complained that the hot food was cold. The staff offered to microwave their meals. Reheat the food ! Totally unacceptable in a hotel of this supposed standard.
I find it strange that a worldwide chain such as Radisson does not regularly check the quality of its hotels.
Lake gives a very shanti atmosphere but don't even think of swimming :) All lakeside sewage is going directly there.
Our favourite place in Nepal, Pokhara. Beautiful lake, beautiful weather amazing scenery. Take a paid boat ride to a small island on the lake where u can visit a temple. Simply beautiful.

Hoping to see ancient Nepali pagoda architecture and explore the history of the Nepali kindgoms and monarchy? Kathmandu Durbar Square ain't it. Sad to say, it more effectively highlights all the negative aspects of Nepal. 

Entrance fees to a public square that are collected to line the pockets of corrupt politicians? Check. Poor upkeep, garbage everywhere, and major pollution? Check. Aggressive and annoying merchants and guides EVERYWHERE peddling goods and services not even worth the time of day? Check. Earthquake damage the government hasn't finished restoration of despite collecting plenty of entry fees and foreign aid? Check. 

The museum is closed off, many of the pagoda are destroyed and nowhere near rebuilt, and there's spots where you won't be able to take 5 steps without being hounded to buy a guide or some chinese beads. From my understanding this square offered a lot of charm in the past. That charm is gone, and what remains is a corrupt tourist trap in poor repair. My honest recommendation is to just stay away and save the 1000 rupees it costs to enter, put it towards Patan or Bhaktapur Durbar Square where things are maintained and actually offer great exhibitions of old Nepali architecture and culture.

The Stupa and entire complex and the view are awe inspiring.  Suggest going on a clear day...smog was pretty bad the day I went.  You could see the city fairly well and a faint outline of the mountains.

At the end of our first full day in Kathmandu, our guide took us to the famous UNESCO World Heritage site of Swayambhunath Temple.  We aimed to arrive for sunset.  As we approached, the entire area was teeming with people.  Turns out it was a festival day and everyone was headed to the temple!  Usually a fantastic thing to stumble upon, but in these pandemic times, it was rather uncomfortable to be in such a huge crowd.  Rated this "average" because of the crowds--and garbage.

However, the colors and local life surrounding this temple are not to be missed. There are two entrances, and because they were limiting car access due to the festival, we took the stairs.  Lots and climbing, but nice views along the way.  The disturbing this was the amount of garbage--just thrown everywhere.

Once at the top, you'll find the stupa with the eyes and many more side stupas on the extensive grounds.  Allow yourself enough time to walk around and absorb the candle lightings, blessings, and the views.  It was also noisy.  Our visit ended with a nice sunset.

Although I was caught off guard by the size of the crowd, this temple is a must-see while in Kathmandu.

Overall poor and run down condition and furniture in rooms were run down and poorly maintained. Leaking walls and peeling wooden floors. Poor heating in room with smell. Carpets on corridors were dirty and run down. Similar breakfast everyday, no changes ..
Good introduction to mountain climbing in the Himalayas including the negative environmental impact to the range.  Worth at least a couple of hours your time.

the temple is situated at top of a hill, you have to climb several stairs to reach there. this temple is also known as Monkey temple due to the presence of monkeys. It is advised not to touch them.  there are lots of antique shops, painting shops at the top. the place could be better if they maintain cleanliness.

You get a good impression of the history of the Himalaya region and you get a better understanding of the impact of the climate changes. One hour can be a little bit to less to visit the museum. Try to visit it in combination with Gupteshwor cave, Devids´s fall and the World Peace Pagoda.

This is part of Kathmandu that has many trekking stores, touristy shops, narrow streets and annoying traffic. 
However we spent a few days in the vicinity and by the end I had come to love the area. 
If you wandered off the main streets and stepped into small courtyards or temples, it was like a different world, quiet and peaceful.  I loved the small shops all wanting your business,  but in a friendly way. We used Google maps to make sure we didnt get lost. We were there during the festival of Tihar which made the area vibrant and exciting.

This restaurant was one of my favourites in Nepal. It looks out onto the lake in Pokhara so the location is perfect. We visited in the afternoon for a relaxing drink and a friend I was with had the best cake (kiss from Zuri cake) I've ever tasted. We had already eaten at another location but the menu at this place is so varied and I could've chosen so many options from it. They also serve vegan and gluten free options as well. I would recommend that anyone visiting Pokhara makes a stop at this place. Wish we had discovered it earlier.

We were lucky to have a Airbnb apartment near the Lakeside center of Pokhara which overlooks the lake. A very nice sight to wake up to.

There are lots of places near the water to go out to and have something to eat or have a party. Realize that sometimes a beggar might come by. Regardless of if you give him/her something or not, they won't bother you too much. 

If you have the time I'd recommend taking a boat and go on the lake and enjoy calmness away from the busy lake side of Pokhara.
If you want touristic tat, for cheap souvenirs then this is where to come.     Cheap T shirts and ornaments.    Not much to delay us here.

If you have any interest in mountains (especially the fourteen 8000 m peaks), then this is a place to spend at least 1/2 a day. You can get to climb Mt. Manaslu too, or at least a scale model. The only real negative thing was a lack of any good bookshop - but then Pokhara has several excellent bookshops with extensive mountaineering sections.

With a nice view over the city and lots of monkeys to see, I was glad I went for a short visit to Swayambhunath Temple.  

Like many cultural attractions in Nepal, I found there was little explanatory material at the temple about how and why it is of cultural and/or historical significance. So if you want to know more about it, I'd suggest doing some research before you get there. 

It's a big tourist attraction so there were lots of souvenir stores up the top of the temple, as well as some vendors scattered around selling food to feed the monkeys. I'm not a fan of stores like this stayed well clear of all of them all.  

Most of the monkeys seemed relatively relaxed in the main area, however, they came much closer to and were more actively interested in people who had food. The increased attention scared some of the small children that were visiting the temple, so it's something to keep in mind if you're going with anyone who is a little uneasy about monkeys.   

While the areas off the beaten path are quieter and more nature filled, I suggest steering clear of them. I explored a little into the forest area off the beaten path, to try to get to some quieter spots. When wandering back up the hill I accidentally walked close to a family of monkeys with a small baby. One of the parents was (understandably) upset and started getting quite close and agitated. I quickly ran away and all was ok, but it was a somewhat frightening experience (I'm keen to remain rabies free!) and really wished I had paid a bit more attention as I was exploring so that I hadn't unintentionally intruded on their home turf! In the quieter area I also stumbled upon some local men who decided that the bathrooms were a bit to far of a walk up the hill, which was a rather awkward experience.

Whenever I visit Pokhara, I visit the lake side which is most famous tourist spot in Pokhara. I really feel wonderful and peaceful by visiting the place. The place is in my first priority whenever I visit Pokhara.

This is the place not to be missed and I only wish I could have seen it before the 2015 earthquake. There is still a great deal of work going on and looking at the scale of destruction, I did not begrudge the entrance charge. This was part od a walking tour for our group and it was useful having a guide to explain the functions of the various buildings.

Overall good hotel.
Booked thru travel agent for two days but first day after travelling of 8-10 hrs from Kathmandu I was told since hotel is full different hotel is arranged for one night stay. This was not informed to me or my travel agent other wise we would have changed our plan. Hotel arranged was clean but room was too small did not have electricity from 10 to 12 pm.

Complementary dinner was offered to us. 

Milk Sachets were expired six month back. Upon request also it was not changed. Shoe polish are not kept in room. Size of Soap provided in Bathroom is too small. Morning only after request Generator was turned on.

Sarangkot is a moderately challenging day hike from Pokhara lake side. For a person of average fitness it shouldn't take more then a maximum of three hours to walk. Although the path is poorly marked, if you use your common sense and your phot you shouldn't get lost. Sarangkot offers panoramic views of both Pokhara and the Himalayas which is its main draw although completely dependent on the weather. Excellent warm up trail for people planning on trekking
The meal service at lakeside retreat was fabulous due to  Nishan, Najin, and Kareena. We will use their service again. Overall we were happy.

I can't praise this hotel enough. The staff were excellent and extremely attentive. Very nice room; a little cold, but I was provided with a hot water bottle, a heated blanked and a heater! Great restaurant, and very nice courtyard. Also provide drinking water without plastic bottles in order to help the environment, which is a great idea.

we stayed here prior leaving for our trek to Poon Hill. Good looking property , well located near the quieter part of the lake northwards. You won't see any snow mountain views from here though. Staff is helpful and service decent. The food is also quite decent but nothing to write home about. Try and get a corner room near the lake if possible. We did leave our luggage with them and all was returned intact. If you want a change and want to eat out you will need to ask the hotel for their drop to town which is provided free as is the pick up. This is easier for lunch rather than for dinner for which you will get a one way drop only and will need a cab to return. Walking would be an option if you are willing to get dusty and wear a smoke and dust mask. It's scarcely a km out to the town centre.

Thamel is full of clubs, bars and over priced restaurants. It’s also one big market full of stores that all sell the same thing (which is normal for Nepal and India). It also has the nicest street dogs. My girlfriend and I walk around with dog treats and can get a big group of loving street dogs around us. Lots of drugs, too.

Massively overpriced for what it is. The place is in ruins, few buildings only. Not worth paying and going inside the same you can see from outside nothing to miss. My tour lasted 10 minutes while being annoyed by various 'experts' trying to offer help.

Great place to stay with one of the best service. Ayushma the desk relation lady was very very helpful & made us feel homely . Super delux room was with a good view. The pool and jacuzzi with bar was also a plus point. Would love to come back again.

We stayed here for a total of four nights. The hotel itself is modern and clean, but the staff really need to up their game...

- When we checked in our room was dirty. Someone elseâ??s garbage in the bin, toiletries opened and used by someone else, and someone elseâ??s pee in the toilet!! The front desk had Housekeeping come (we were still waiting for our bags anyway!) but it was unpleasant. 

- At breakfast it was impossible to get coffee. You could ask three separate staff members and still not get it. Disappointing.

my stay with Hotel Radisson was superb in one sentence. I would recommend everyone regarding this. the hotel was clean and tidy. the dining space was neat and all staffs were very friendly. Pantry staffs were very cordial and rooms were very cozy.

Thamel is the main tourist shopping precinct. Loaded as it is with handicrafts, t-shirts and the like, it can also be useful if kitting out for an expedition. 
Prices are great, there are lots of food places and it is fun in small doses.
A Kathmandu must see.
Huge place consist of many buildings got damaged due to earthquake. Marvelous architecture, carving on woods and museum was awesome. Must visit place.
Well worth the visit and the price of admission. I learned a lot. Great tribute to the people who inhabit the area and they men and women who chose to challenge themselves there.

The hotel is set back from the street in Thamel. It's set around a central garden area, and is far enough away from the street that you don't hear any noise. Rooms are comfortable, but could do with a bit of work. Ours had a dripping shower and getting the water to a reasonable temperature took a bit of fiddling with the various taps.

The staff are very helpful, but boy does the hotel charge top dollar. We asked if they could get a taxi to go to Patan for a few hours. Instead of calling a taxi, they arranged their own car and tried to charge us 5000 rupees. If you need a taxi, just step outside the gates and hail one. Even when we were heading to the airport at 4.30am there were several parked outside.

Overall experience is not good at all,rooms are not up to the mark does not fit as Hyatt properties , swimming pool is good ,staff was not very courteous so overall experience was bad what they charged was not at all worth it

The Radisson Kathmandu was a highlight of my travel this past year.  If you have the status for lounge access, that is a major benefit here, as the food and drinks there are wonderful and the lounge manager is a delight.  I prefer the old building to the new one--the new one is very nice and has excellent amenities.  The old building just feels more like a Kathmandu experience to me, and I moved there part of the way through my stay.  I had a minor issue after departing getting credited for points for my stay.  I finally got it resolved but this tarnished an otherwise amazing 2 week stay.

We were staying in an hotel in this area, it is a very busy area with lots of shops, restaurants and bars. There are few paths to walk on so you have to be very careful as there are lots of cars and mopeds.

Had a wonderful time . I had an amazing stay at this hotel. The staff were extremely friendly and welcoming, the rooms were spotless, and the service was excellent. Every detail was well taken care of, which made my experience truly memorable. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for comfort and great hospitality.

There is the hustle and bustle of the city. It looks like everyone is live here cheek by jowl. You might also think this is a chaotic place. It is not. What seems like all the madness around this temple complex is in an order. There are married couples taking photos with their nuptial entourage, people just going about their business, hoards of tourists taking photos and people like us: soaking in the magnificence of this calming place. The temples and the work that went in making them a grandure of wood craftsmanship is unmissable and strikes you with their craftsmanship. Awesome place.

Had two club rooms 537 & 529, which were great. My kids had fun swimming. The breakfast spread was impressive & servers were attentive at sesame restaurant. Special shout out to Subash at the regency lounge who took good care of our group. I’m glad I’ve been able to check out this property every time I visit Nepal. Never disappoints..
Everything was wonderful. Great service, food and felt like such a luxury after a 5 day trek! Very friendly and attentive staff. Enjoyed an amazing massage which was well needed after travel.
Keep away way from roasting heat at lakeside,this place is cool and beautiful  senaries surrounding pokhara.

Lovely hotel. Although not on lake front, is easily walked or taxi ride. The room was big, clean and the bed comfortable. The staff very friendly and helpful. The breakfast had a large variety. The made to order omelettes delicious. The garden area tranquil with a large swimming pool.

When you reached the top many vendors invite you to take seat in their places facing the city and mountains. But sun rises from east not from west. Take a compass or some devise to know where east is.
Its a beautiful lake in pokhara its cool freshing place. Cycing around lakeside is superb. There are so many good restaurants around here
It was awonderful experience at this beautiful and amazing resort..The ambience was at its top level.The brekafast was better.I want to come here again and again

Trekkers Home is a perfect spot for solo travelers!
I had a great stay here—the rooftop is amazing and offers the perfect place to relax, meet fellow travelers, and enjoy the view. The vibe is social and welcoming, making it easy to connect with others. Highly recommended if you're looking for a friendly and chill place to stay!

Long que for darshan but it was good with temples of Lakshmi Narayan and Radhakrishna. Strong vibrations of positive and spiritual energy. Early morning darshan is a good start to the day. Wonderful experience

Based on middle estern food, hummus, falafel, salads and so on, it caters to vegetarian. On the menu also some Italian dishes, but would not recccomend those, as other members of my group were not impressed. Good value for the price, nice view from the terrace. Service is hit and miss.
Very relaxed stay, staffs were over all very hospitable, breakfast spread was also pretty descent. Will surely come back.

Safe and Clean hotel in Kathmandu. Presently a good service and overalls satisfaction. Staff are friendly and helpful. Room is clean and comfortable. Breakfast is a good choice for in house guests. Will come back again

We LOVED our stay at this place! It is quiet, peaceful and beautiful. About Rooms, they were perfect and comfy. They have best views. Everything was well maintained. Hotel staff was very warm, welcoming and we were really impressed by their hospitality and politeness. Each and everyone was humble from security guard to the hotel staff, receptionist, restaurant staff..everyone! I must say, I didn't want to leave this place if I did't had to as felt home here.

Its an old heritage site and a must visit one when you are in Kathmandu. It used to be very beautiful, full of beautiful temples and architectures but now most of them have been destroyed by the earthquake of 2015. However, restructuring / renovating works are being carried out which make the place look little messy currently.

Ate breakfast here, a delicious sandwich that tasted like pizza. But because of it being a vegetarian restaurant I was very surprised when they refused to fill up my own water bottle with water from their tank. I of course told them that I would pay for it but they refused and told me that I would need to buy their plastic bottle to get some water. Many people are vegetarian because of the environment and therefore it was a big disappointment that they could not provide water in my own reusable bottle. All of the other restaurants we’ve been to have been able to provide this service so we were shocked. Please change this policy!
We picked up a paddle boat from the smaller launch site near lane 8 off of lakeside drive and had a lovely paddle on the lake.  We even picked a few plastic bottles out of the water.

The stay was with my family (mum and child) and it was absolutely amazing! The Hotel team are incredibly helpful, informative and generous with their time. Extremely patient and adaptive to changing situations. We are truly appreciative of them.

A really friendly place. Nice people, a great rooftop  (with live music on a Wednesday) and close enough to the extraordinary Dhurbar Square. Rooms are comfortable and well appointed. Special thanks to Biendra, Edusui, Ramesh for your terrific attention.

Fell in love with this place in Kathmandu after a rave review from a friend. Ate there a handful of times before journeying to Pokhara where we then continued to dine here for most meals! Always left to try new things, but couldn't help coming back often! Fantastic food and the best atmosphere!

NOT to be elegible for being a Hayat member. Allmost all staff are freshers with zero knowledge 

Person at recpetion does not know what cousine is served in the restaurants. 

Person in restaurant does not know what portion is served in one serving. 

The girl escorting us to our room looks like a college girl, not even knowing on which floor we really are, And where is the room. 

Person at swimming pool does not know where to get tube. 

Everyone knows anything. Just few freshers hired by Hayat. 

Very bad experience of big brand like Hayat
By all means, rent one of these colorful boats and paddle around Fewa Lake, it was a wonderful experience.

Nice place, but you have to visit it early in the morning or in the evening, because at daytine there are no monckeys. They are all in the forest) ticket costs 200 rs for tourists. Walk from Thamel takes 35-45 minutes. Stupa is beautiful but there are a lot of selkers aroubd and it looks like market.

This is the tourist hub here in Kathmandu. This place has narrow streets, with hotels lined up in almost every building. Shops one after the other, food places, pubs, bars and even night clubs. If you go to Kathmandu, Thamel is a must visit even if you are not staying there. The nightlife is vibrant too but most food places close by 10/11 so try to get dinner before they close. Pubs stay open till around 12 ish but some stay open longer. Around 8 pm ish, street food vendors also start setting up. The street food didn't have much variety but the food wad pretty good.
An interesting museum - I particularly liked the section about the effects of climate change on the people and way of life in the Himalayas.  Thought provoking
Thamel is the city of Kathmandu you can see many different thing there very interesting tourist hotel restaurants food and many handicrafts make you amaze for the first I liked it

This placed is so chilled. Up on the third floor overlooking the lake mid main street, it's a popular Pokhara hidden gem. The mint lemonade is a gorgeous way to end a hot day. The desserts are to die for, particularly the apple pie. My husband loves the pizza here. It has a laid back Moroccan feel and is the perfect location to relax alone, as a couple or with friends. It is a vegetarian and vegan menu. Must visit location in Pokhara.

Dear Radisson hotel team,

A very warm greetings and namaste i would like to thanks from my heart to all the team of Radisson hotel for making our event successful by providing best hospitality and services special thanks to sital ji, sujit ji, sunam ji, Silas ji and all the front office team and food and beverage department

The climate changed to a cool gentle breeze as soon as we reached the para gliding site. We liked it so much that we went there twice! Though we didn’t paraglide, we sat and observed.. the daredevils and the view of Pokhara.
A must visit place.

One of the highlights of Nepal let alone Pokhra. Lakeside walkway is the best way to enjoy the true beauty of lake and activities around it. You get great food and drinks along the way. Just go for it.
The lake was beautiful and peaceful. Mr Kiran who row row us across  was such a nice gentleman. We had a good time enjoying the lake view.

It was a Tuesday evening and we certainly didn’t expect there will be a buffet at the Hyatt but we were pleasantly surprised with not only a buffet but a huge selection of food.  It was very enjoyable for our family. The waiter was super attentive.
Love this place for good vegetarian food despite being a non-vegetarian. The ambiance is good and its not that expensive either.

I recommend getting a hotel or guesthouse that has a nice, unobstructed view of the mountains from their rooftop. Then you can check the weather in the morning. IF it's actually clear and not smoggy, hazy like almost every day in Nepal with all the air pollution, then you can hail a taxi to take you up to Sarangkot. In the 2 months I was in Nepal, I only experienced 3 days that were not smoggy and hazy. You can see the mountains from Sarangkot, but it's very hazy and unclear. It's not any better than a view from the city. If it's a nice, clear day - definitely go visit Sarangkot and get that prized photo. But otherwise, it's a waste of taxi fare to go there since you can get just as nice photos from Fewa lake boating, or other places in town that have nice unobstructed views of Fishtail and the Annapurna range.

We stayed at Temple Tree for 3 nights while in Pokhara. Overall, it was a comfortable place to stay. Positives- The rooms are small, but very nice. Staff is very friendly and helpful. The location is excellent! The grounds were beautiful and clean. Negatives- The hot tub did not work the entire time we were there. We got a couples massage and the two women chit chated the entire massages making it difficult to fully relax. There was construction right next to the hotel that made it a bit noisy. We only tried the breakfast buffet there, but it definitely left something to be desired. 

After all is said and done I believe the hotel is pretty overpriced. I most likely would stay elsewhere if I went back to Pokhara, but did find it adequate and comfortable.

Boating on Phewa Lake is a must do activity for all tourists. You can take a boat and start rowing as long as you like until the evening. Given that the allure of Nepal has so much to do with mountains,  the museum was a big disappointment.  Looking back I can only recall the names of a few peaks in the Himalayan range from my visit to the Museum.  

All the information was simply printed out,  framed and hung up on the wall.  There was an overload of information in black and white to absorb. Any use of recent technology was completely absent.  

Once in every two hours or so a documentary was aired in a studio.  The "documentary" completely blends in with the rest of the Museum in its absence of any use of recent technology.  

All the information available at the museum can be absorbed in the comfort of ones armchair. I hope that the Tourism authority in Nepal would look into investing in the museum. It truly has a lot of potential.
Unfortunately the earthquake  took its toll and a lot of the buildings are scaffolded There is a charge  of 1000 rupees for foreigners .  Overall just worth the effort and price.

It was listed in the UNESCO World Heritage Monument List in 1979.The history of the Valley, according to the legends, the lotus mysteriously radiated a brilliant light, and the name of the place came to be Swayambhu, meaning 'Self-Created or Self-Existent'. Bodhisattva Manjusri came across a beautiful lake during his travel. He saw a lotus that emitted brilliant light at the lake's center, so he cut a gorge in a southern hill and drained the waters to worship the lotus. The lotus was then transformed into a hill and the light became the Swayambhunath Stupa. Men settled on the bed of the lake and called it the Kathmandu Valley. From then on, the hilltop of the Self-existent Lord has been a holy place.

Hyatt Regency is possibly the most iconic hotel in Kathmandu but the compromise to make if staying there is that it's aging, in fact very aging.  We stayed there almost a decade ago and it was already quite worn off then; now it's even worse because not much has changed in the rooms, if at all.  Some public areas have been improved such as the elevators but not the rooms themselves.  

We had a bi-level suite which was not convenient and even dangerous with young children, prompting us to decide to check out early and go to another hotel.

Service was quite subpar especially during breakfast in the restaurant which tended to be a chaotic mess.  Part of it can be blamed on the hotel policies because they do not offer breakfast in the club lounge which would at least help some guests escape the crowds by choosing the more quiet venue and reduce the number of diners in the restaurant.  But they offer nothing at all in the lounge in the morning so there is no alternative.  Thankfully late during our stay we gave feedback about the service and after that service got significantly better.

For happy hour in the lounge the drinks were decent but food was similar fried stuff as many years ago so it was still a bit weak.

Before we boarded our plane to Lukla for our EBC trek, We stayed in Thamel, Kathmandu for two days. And another four days after we were back from Everest region. Thamel can be described as a hub of tourists coming from across the globe for a spectrum of activities. It’s flooded with a range of accommodation options from cheap hostels to swanky luxury hotels. It is also home to mirage of eateries, cafe and bars. One can enjoy authentic Nepali, Indian, Chinese, Continental and cuisines from all over the world. 
Having a reputation for being a tourist’s hub and being close to Tribhuvan International Airport, Thamel has an incredible nightlife. Here’s where you can buy anything and everything you would need as a traveller. The narrow streets of Thamel is always bustling with people & you gotta be careful of your belongings. We were scammed by a thug being a bit careless. We found a million shady dance bars (not go go bars) all around in Thamel. 
Personal advice: Don’t go to Nepali dance bars unless you have a local friend. We were looted 17000NPR for two glasses of orange juice.
Also, shopping in Thamel is a bit expensive in comparison to other places in Kathmandu. Don’t hesitate to haggle and be careful of what you buying as you’ll find counterfeit stuffs of every brand you can think of. 
So, Enjoy Thamel for its proximity to the airport, mushroomed up tour agencies, restaurants, nightlife, shopping and beautiful stupas you find at every junction.

Very lovely lake with stunning views on the mountain range. You find boat rentals along the lakeshore. However, if you go a little further north you will find boat rentals which are less busy and allow you to row yourself, which is more fun and romantic.
There is a small island with a busy temple which can be reached in a few minutes. It makes a nice stop-over for your boat trip.
The walk along the lakeside is also enjoyable. You find outdoor restaurants and cafes, and there is small fun park at the northern end.

This museum is large and covers many topics from ethnic groups to geology, but the displays are fairly rudimentary, so keep your expectations moderate. A highlight was the display of various climbing expeditions and their gear, showing the increasing sophistication since the 1953 Hillary/Norgay Everest expedition. There were a lot of Nepalese school kids and young Indian students and they seemed to be enjoying the museum very much.

We arrived on a rainy day in the valley , and despite giving multiple reminders of our flight arrival time , there was no person / placard of the Hyatt Regency to be seen. Made a few calls to the hotel , but nobody picked up. Then tried contacting the 'airport representative' , only to be told he's on leave. As the airport police did not let anyone stand near the exit , we were left drenched in the rain for a good 20 minutes. Finally the hotel did pick up my call , but by then the car had arrived , thanks to a few helpful guys ( from other hotels ) who knew our driver.
As we had booked the Club Rooms , we were checked in at the Regency Club Lounge  , by the very courteous Ms. Nitya. We had placed a request for rooms with the 'Stupa' view , but surprisingly , "they had no such room left on the 6th floor" i.e. the Club Lounge floor , which was disappointing considering that we had asked for it well in advance. Thus , while they upgraded one of the rooms to the 7th floor in their Club 'Deluxe' category ( which has nothing different apart from a balcony ) the other room was assigned on the 5th floor , which made movement between the two rooms quite hectic.
The rooms are nice , but there is an acute shortage of power points , and even those require adapters to be used. The bathrooms are quite big , but the showers have a dysfunctional temperature control , with hot water taking almost 5 minutes to come at the start , and then stopping intermittently , a phenomenon one does not expect in a Hyatt.
The Regency Club Lounge is spacious , with a friendly & courteous staff , but service can be painfully slow even for a cup of tea/coffee. Unlike club lounges across the globe , where you have cookies,fruits,etc. available throughout the day , this doesn't seem to be the norm here. I was quite surprised to learn that they don't have the concept of 'Afternoon Tea' , which precedes the evening round of 'Happy Hours' everywhere. Coming to the latter , while the variety of alcohol might be satisfactory , a teetotaller like me has to settle with just 2 options - Coke or Gingerale. On our first day , the canapÃ©s/snacks were being frequently replenished , but it was the complete opposite on day 2 , with empty plates ( for some items ) seen just half an hour into the Happy Hours , right till the end.
Breakfast at the main restaurant is utter chaos , with staff trying their level best to streamline the process , but to no avail. The Indian selections are not impressive and are presented poorly. The 'Juice Corner' is sloppy , and no matter what fruit / vegetable you choose , they use the same jug again & again resulting in a messy concoction every time.
The Hyatt Regency Kathmandu unfortunately has a long way to go in my opinion. I would easily get much better service & hospitality , at this price , anywhere across Asia.

I’ll start with the positive. Lovely garden, despite noise from the construction of the new building, lovely service, good breakfast, despite having to wait for cutlery and crockery as other reviewers have mentioned. 
Now the negative. I booked a basic room but this was so disappointing. It was more basic and unwelcoming than any of the budget rooms on the rest of my stay, including my stay in a monastery!

I know it was a basic room but there is no excuse for this shoddiness. Especially at $40 per night. I have since stayed in Kathmandu and have had far far superior rooms and amenities for that price bracket. 
In short, a disappointment. An establishment should pride itself on the quality and cleanliness of all its rooms, whatever the price bracket.

All in all, I would never recommend this place. And even though it's slightly cheap there are several others I. Kathmandu who are more friendly, helpful and room won't make you I'll.

Phewa Lake in Pokhara is truly a picturesque and serene destination, perfect for couples looking to spend some quality time together. The lake, with its calm waters and stunning backdrop of the Annapurna mountain range, creates an ideal romantic setting. Whether you're taking a leisurely stroll along the shore or simply sitting by the lake, the peaceful atmosphere makes it a great spot to relax and enjoy the beauty of nature.

One of the main attractions here is the option to go boating on the lake. It’s a wonderful activity to engage in, offering a unique perspective of the surrounding landscape as you glide over the tranquil water. For couples, it’s a delightful way to spend time together, taking in the views and savoring the quiet moments. The boats are easy to rent, and the experience of being out on the water adds a special touch to any visit to Phewa Lake.

Around the lake, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants to explore. These establishments offer a variety of delicious food, and we found the prices to be quite reasonable, especially considering the prime location. Whether you're craving local Nepali dishes or international cuisine, you’ll find plenty of options to suit your taste. Many of these eateries also have outdoor seating, which allows you to enjoy your meal with a view of the lake, enhancing the overall experience.

We found that the best time to visit Phewa Lake is in the evening. As the sun begins to set, the lake takes on a magical quality, with the soft light reflecting off the water and the surrounding area coming alive with a pleasant, relaxed vibe. It’s an ideal time to take a walk, grab a bite to eat, or simply sit and enjoy the serene beauty of the lake.

Overall, Phewa Lake is a must-visit in Pokhara, especially for couples. The combination of natural beauty, peaceful surroundings, and nearby amenities makes it an unforgettable experience.

I started my hike from Lakeside to Sarangkot when it was mostly sunny.  The hike was somewhat difficult as the path got muddy at times, bushy at others.  (Apparently, most people choose to take taxis or motorbikes to Sarangkot, so the hiking trail is overgrown with bushes and gets confusing at times.)  By the time I reached the viewpoint, the sky was dark with clouds.  It was clear there would be no view of the mountains at all, but the jerk at the ticket booth still wanted to collect 60 rupees (foreigner ticket price) despite there being nothing to see at that time. While that's still pretty cheap, it's the principle of the thing -- so, I just turned around and headed back down the hill.  

By the way, people should note that taxis generally charge between 800 and 1200 rupees (round-trip from Lakeside).  But, if you hike to the top, you can then catch a jeep back to town for about 150 rupees.  (Every hour or two the jeeps that bring the paragliders to the jump-off point return to town and pick up riders to earn a few extra bucks.)

Stayed at Base Camp Resort in Pokhara, Nepal in October 2009 during a tour of North India & Nepal with my fiance. Overall, the hotel is not a bad place to stay, and some of the rooms are great. Many of the service staff were wonderful... but our experience was greatly tainted, and I'm outlining it here to try to be helpful to other travelers.

Because our stop at this hotel was part of a greater tour, our room had been booked in advance by at least two months by the tour company. When we checked in, everything went smoothly until we were brought to our room. For our stay in Pokhara, we really wanted to ensure that we had a decent room, preferably with a view, so we booked one of the nicest rooms available in this hotel - Deluxe, double bed, view of the himalaya... What we were brought to was a closet-sized room at the very back of the hotel with a view of other rooms from one window and and view of a public balcony from the next. The bathroom had a window that adjoined our room to our neighbor's room (via a small corridor), who had a really nasty cough, which we heard from early morning. We were only traveling with our backpacks, so it was pretty disappointing that we hardly even had enough space in the room to place our bags down. The two twin beds in the room were also a bit disappointing, but we could have gotten over that if everything else was on par. Worst of all -- the room had an abundance of moth balls -- beside the bed, beside tables and cabinets, near the bathroom, etc. etc. The smell was disgusting, but more importantly, by morning, we felt sick from the smell.

Before settling into the room, I spoke to the front desk staff about not getting the room we had pre-paid. They simply told me that the hotel was fully booked that day. I had to borrow their phone at front desk to call our tour operator to make them aware of the issue, and it took the tour operator's constant complaints to hotel management over the course of our first day at the hotel for the hotel to agree to move us on the second day. 

Once we were moved into the second room (the one we had paid for), everything was fine in the room - and it was a decent place to spend the night. But bear in mind that the difference was stark -- so when people on this site say the "rooms" were fine, they may have had a decent room to begin with. We know from personal experience that not all the rooms are fine (at least in our opinion). 

When we were checking out after our second night, I wanted to confirm with the front desk staff that the hotel would be working with our tour operator to refund the difference in room rate for the room we pre-paid vs. the room we received for our first night's stay. Not only did they refuse to refund the difference, they insisted that we pay for the phone call we made to our tour operator to report the issue. 

At the end of the day, it certainly wasn't the money that was the issue for us, but we do believe that if you have pre-paid a room, then it should be available to you, otherwise the hotel shouldn't have accepted the money for a room they couldn't provide.... And for this reason, I would not stay here again for lack of trust on their business ethic.

My first impression of this property was "wow"!!! The infrastructure is nothing short of spectacular. So, in one sense, the hotel is fantastic.

However, my overall impression was of deep disappointment. Why?

It is obvious that the owner has chosen not to keep investing financially into the hotel. Almost everything is worn out and dated. For example, when is the last time you saw a boxed television at a brand name 5 star property?

From the rooms, to the fitness center, to the spa, to the public spaces everything shouts out, "I need a massive renovation."

I've stayed at this Radisson 8 times over the last 4 years, each time as part of a trekking package (3 with World Expeditions, 1 with Trek Climb Ski Nepal).  They consistently deliver a very good, although not perfect, level of service.  On the most recent stay, I had two nights in the new wing and 1 night in the old.  The new rooms are perhaps a little better furnished, although I note only the old room has baths (important distinction if that's part of your post-trek plan!), also the old wing is more convenient for accessing the gym/pool.

Facilities are quite good- the gym has a good assortment of machines, the pool is small but suitable for some sunbathing, fruit infused water is at hand at the health centre desk, and food/drinks can be ordered at the pool desk.  On this visit the jacuzzi, steamroom and sauna were all working.  While on trek I safely left my passport in a safe deposit box at reception and bags with the concierge service.  

The buffets tend to be of a high standard, although the room can feel understaffed- the service is sometimes a little slow at clearing tables and restocking, or there will be no one immediately available to take your breakfast vouchers.  The omelette station at breakfast is great, there's a big assortment of fresh pastries on offer, the fruit selection is a little underwelming, the juices/smoothies are good and the eventual offer of tea/coffee for the table is greatly appreciated.  

I paid approx AUD$100 for a delayed checkout of 6pm.  

Power in the room requires the door key inserted in the wall switch.  Solo travellers should ask for an extra key if they wish their devices to continue charging when they leave the room.
