This place has good history of the Himalayas and Nepal. Its pretty old school but worth a visit if you have time. Could spead about an hour here
Really interesting and well worth visiting. There has been a lot that has been repaired but unfortunately still a bit to go - a very expensive and time consuming job.

Had a really good time at Trekkers Home, the staff where very helpful and pretty happy bunch of guys. the rooms where comfortable with powerful showers, great for after a trek,not luxury and not pristine but you have to except that when in Nepal because its not always going to be. The trekking centre down in the lobby was brilliant for organising  our trek. Trekkers Home is in a brilliant location right in the heart of Thamel, near brilliant restaurants (road house) and some good fun bars (Tom & Jerry's). We walked to the main tourist things but it does take sometime, but seemed pretty safe to do so. 
really nice rooftop area as well which we didn't find till our second stay after our trek but gives really nice views.
 The hotel also offers a place to leave your excess bags while trekking.

We had a fantastic stay at Temple Tree Resort. The property is beautiful, and we loved the authentic Nepali-style mud construction—it felt so unique and charming.

The location is perfect, being close to Phewa Lake in Lakeside, making it easy to explore while being a quiet retreat to come back to.

But the real highlight was the staff. They were incredibly friendly and attentive. We loved being greeted with "Namaste" everywhere we went—it felt authentic and created such a warm and welcoming atmosphere.

A truly relaxing and positive experience. Highly recommend.

The hotel looks very good, everything is modern, very clean, quite and safe place, rooms and big, beds very comfortable, they have good options for breakfast as well as other meals, SPA treatments, very nice employees.
Myself and my wife visited this lake and went boating to the temple located in the lake. It's nice but the boatman was really struggling to row us across. The temple is nice too.

The main attraction of Pokhara is this lake which actually dominates the city.. All around there are very nice restaurants were you can sit and have wonderful Nepalese dishes and the famous momos. The lake also is the landing ground for the hang gliders from Sarangkot. Boating is done from one corner and is also a thrilling experience.
The swimming pool in the temple tree resort is very nice and there is jacuzzi and its very nice part in resort Staff is very nice Aayushma was very good and friendly
We took a boat from the lakeside area to the other side and hiked up to Peace Pagoda. It was a beautiful ride with amazing views.
You can take a public bus up there, but there is no taxi for return after the sunset. You can walk down for around one hour. If you are lucky you can find others for sharing taxi.
Despite 360steps up, the stupa is full of positive energy and beautiful colours, extremely impressive wood carving and silly, curious monkeys.

Stayed here for just one night before our return to the UK at the end of our trip. Our room was comfortable and clean with all amenities and the buffet food was good. Staff all very helpful indeed.
The hotel has a very good shop which was useful for gifts to take home and is also down a side street where there are other shops which are good too.
The Garden of Dreams is just a short walk away.
Traditional market..colourful. joyful people. Crowded but safe. All sorts of shops ..twists and turns.  2 km long.

Thanks to all guess Radisson. I have feel very good and all guess have good think. I am happy to say that i am no facing any problem in the hotel. Good cleaning, good services, pick and drop service excellent.

I have coeliac disease so have to be very careful when eating out.
I was so pleased to see gluten free pasta on their menu and to read about gluten free options in trip advisor too.

I explained my requirements to the waiter and checked with him numerous times when ordering and also again when he bought the food out.

He assured me it was gluten free so i went ahead and ate a whole bowl of pasta. Turns out he had got mixed up and given me normal wheat pasta (instead of rice pasta). 

I was extremely ill the next day and was very upset that this had happened. 

I am therefore sorry to say that I would not recommend this restaurant, especially if you have coeliac disease or any allergies.

the hotel is located away from the main town in Pokhara. its about a 25min walk (uphill on the way back) and the road doesn't have too many lights. the hotel does provide a shuttle service to and from town.
ask for a room that faces the front or the lake and the view we had faced some deserted fields(not much to look at). they have a gate that opens to the lake and you can rent a boat there. the hotel was kind enough to organise a trek and paragliding for us (little more expensive than booking them in town).
the room was clean and the staff gave us two bottles of water everyday which was sweet. they are trustworthy (we left some valuable around once or twice). the pool looked amazing but it was to cold to swim (we went in December). 
breakfast was lovely. they have a good selection of food so you dont get bored. we even had lunch in the hotel a couple of times and dinner once. the chef was kind enough to give me ginger when my throat was bad in the morning.

Overall this hotel offers good accommodation and amenities. I stayed in the new wing. The rooms show signs of wear and tear though are adeqate. The hotel offers escape from a hectic city. The surroiunding area is chaotic and there's little to see within walking distance. The staff were friendly and competent. The highlight was early breakfast on the 3rd floor which offered great city views and a peaceful and tasty start to the day.

After travelling around Nepal finally have come to a place of outstanding beauty the lake is eye catching with the mountains and little colourful boats all going around to see different places great experience and on a clear day you can see the white capped mountains beautiful

Go very early in the morning by 5:30 am and find a suitable place to stand. It gets crowded. Sunrises at 6:15 am but worth the wait. Slowly all the mountain tops start getting visible. They are snow-clad which turns golden. Very nice view.

Hi,
I have visited this place in late December 2016. It has a very nice and friendly environment, very clean and nice staff. BUT.. the food was.. plain... I got much better food ( dhal Bat) at corner restaurants than this one. Honestly I would have expected a much more exquisite dinner compared with the prices and fame. So ... if you want to eat in a clean safe cosu place.. if you care more about looks than taste than this is the place for you.

We did enjoy the visit to Thamel while we were in Kathmandu.
We had booked the hotel in Thamel. The night life of Thamel is what you must experience if you visit Nepal.
Mass hysteria.Nothing outstanding, really.Darjeeling and Ghoom offers better views.

Thehotel/restaurant is in the centre of thamel so its a good location if you want to shop or be near lots of nice restaurants.  The restaurant in the hotel caters mostly for European options and the food is very average for a reasonable price. Serfice was slow, and in my  case they made a mistake and i had to wait an extra 15 minutes for my meal. It wasn't my choice to go here and I wouldn't go back.
Loved the area narrow streets rustic atmosphere . So crowded and many souvenir shops on the sides you can get good deals but negotiate and check other shops before you buy .

This was recommended to me from friends that had done it two before. So we booked a taxi to take all the way to the top of the viewing area. We left at 5:30 in the morning and the ride up there is an adventure in itself. Lots of traffic on a very narrow road,most of it going the same way we were. Once at the top its 30 rupees to go to the viewing area. On this particular day Mother Nature was not cooperating and it was an overcast morning so not so spectacular but I have seen the pictures and other people I have talked to say this is a must do trip if you find yourself in Pokhara.

The hotel was generally very nice and comfortable. My only concern was the space of bathroom. However All the staffs were very friendly and have amazing service. The food is very tasty and fresh. But I couldn't get enough time to enjoy my stay.

We hiked from lakeside, which was a good 3hr steep walk up many stairs and through some forest and nice villages. It's definitely worth walking up but we wouldn't recommend staying overnight unless the weather is very clear and you want to see the sunrise over the Annapurna ranges.

perfect location and my experience of staying at this hotel for 3 nights was good..everything in thamel is at walking distance around this hotel. it is a heritage property. good food and location and value for money..
Early morning ride to the top of the hill is so peaceful experience. Really enjoyed the view, it makes your eyes refreshment.
Thank you for the wonderful decoration we had a great time thanks a lot hotel temple tree and family thank you. The was very good. Wonderful stay enjoyed very much

It was an awesome experience! Couldn’t stay longer because I had a flight back to deheradun. Next time when I come to Nepal my first preference will be radisson hotel! The experience was amazing! I loved the swimming pool too

We checked many hotels but Water Front hotel caught our eye with its mesmerising lake, mountain and cloud view. Staff is also accommodating as they customised many meals for us, special mentions to Sabina, Binita, Nabina, Sante, Salina and Alishwa. They were very sweet and helpful. Overall, a must try resort.
Very friendly people. Lots of really good places to eat and drink, and bargains on trekking gear and gifts.

It was a wonderful piece of history but the 2015 earthquake left a lot of the Square in rubble... the rebuilding efforts are on the way. I believe the entrance fee of only $10 fee goes towards the  rebuilding  and conservation efforts.  
Please bring a good dust mask from home ( we went in December) as the dust in Katmandu is intense.  The museum in the square will show how things were before the earthquake😪

Took a taxi from Pokhara to the first viewpoint. Then took about 40-60 to walk up the road to the main viewing platform. We went up on a clear morning and the views toward the Annapurna range were spectacular. Definitely worth the trek. We walked back to Pokhara
This is a nice spot by the lake for a bit more upmarket food and a somewhat decent wine list. There is free wifi.

excellent location, excellent staff and excellent Radisson quality as with all other resorts by them.. Casino was also nice. Overall it was one of the best experiences i've had right from check-in to stay to check-out.. Thanks to the whole team Radisson..

Best hospitality and best service I have experienced here.

Staffs are so friendly and helpful:-
1) Binita and Sabina mam (I’m happy with their service and hospitality)

This is one of the UNESCO HERITAGE site- there are 3 darwar square in Kathmandu Valley. in few yours time- after the completion of earthquake devastated building, this is going to be one of the best heritage site in the world. Square itself is a huge complex with varieties of the architect around it - one must visit whenever you are in Kathmandu

Excellent...
Pleasant stay.
Was here for the second time.
Annapurna restaurant was good. Food was delicious. The staffs were best.

See you again
Not very well maintained .. Still it is under construction and not much to see . But tickets are very costly compare to what we see.There is a museum inside to see.. Not great but you can visit..

A must visit place when staying in Kathmandu. Thamel is a vibrant and colourful shopping area where you can buy a multitude of traditional Nepali crafts. It has eating places to suit all budgets and tastes. There are rickshaws to ride and taxis always available - one piece of advice is to agree the cost of your taxi before you take the ride but all drivers are friendly and open to bartering. The atmosphere is amazing and the sights, sounds and smells will arouse your senses and make you want to revisit.
Beautiful place of old temples and statues. Got some nice and cheplap souvenirs from here. Totally worth to be visited.

One of the things I told myself in travel is "If I don't go to tourist restaurants in my country. why the hell do I have to travel thousands of km to do so!"
I don't in Kathmandu.
You're better off spending the money at nice Nepali restaurant and still walk away with some change.

Food was really tasty! Great place to chill out with awesome lake views. 
Although a bit expensive compared to most of the places in Pokhara as you’ll be charged an extra 10% and 13%.
Staff was nice but do not expect to find the best service in town.

Room was spacious and well furnished. It had great views of the lake. The service was fabulous. Both the dining service and the room service front desk were very helpful. People were very, very nice and pleasant and it is a great place to relax and come back too after a day-long trips easily. It is accessible to various sites in Pokhara. Highly recommend this place for staying relaxing and traveling around pokhara. 

Breakfast was par excellence. Great variety of western, Nepali, Indian dishes. Plenty of fruits, vegetables and desserts. The masala chai was superb and so were the varieties of different types of coffee. The host, waitress and waiters were very courteous and did a great job waiting and serving their clients.

The hostess and training Salinal provided fantastic service for us. She was very pleasant, kind, smiling and courteous.

For the price we paid of USD 90 the room had no amneties. No tv, no kettle and not even a bottle of water. Most of these we received at â??cheaperâ? $20 hotels during our stay in Nepal.

The hotel is picturesque with a large garden and comfortable rooms  in the heart of Thamel.

Went here to have a look and it's just the usual really all the same food vendors shops and activity's the views are though very good! Plus it's not a lake you can walk fully around which I like! There are some sections to walk around but they are very crowded!
The last visit on a day tour and sadly it hammered down. Not a huge amount to see but we couldn't get into the side temples.
We visited there few days before, thereis looks  very beautiful  but all building is rebuild and but very feu people  visiting  hope it will be much better .

Had visited Hotel Raddison Kathmandu for lunch with my family.Nice ambience,yummy food and superb hospitality.One name needs special mention,Reeta Singh who was the Manager there,she took special care of us all in all possible way.Highly impressed.
We have been twice in OR2K. It start with the great view to the lake, amazing atmospheare and the vegan food. Even those of you who are not vegan will engoy here so much.

The people were very kind, and they offered yoga classes in the morning, which was a beautiful way to start the day. We were very well taken care of. The people at breakfast were very kind, they helped us with our laundry and gave us local tips to walk around. 

Towels and bed sheets seemed a bit old and used.

Busy market, narrow lanes, good for shopping for trekking gear and gifts. 
Some hidden eating gems too. Found a great Veg/Vegan restaurant - Aniyor. Great spicy fòod...
It is in fact in Patan. A historic site with temples and narrow streets to walk around.  This is a much better area to stay comparing to Thamel, the Kathmandu city center.

Beautiful place. Awesome views. And lots of options in souvenirs. Must visit. 
The place is well maintained and extremely clean despite the heavy foot traffic. Not crowded. I tried the wishing well. Missed it though. Loved the experience.

nice to see OR2K in pokhara wings.... lovely space and view. vibe is little low then thamel but can be make more nice and darker ..... hummus is good but Pitta bread is Nan bread please improve that. over all good . see you soon and highly recommended

Manita Bisural at the breakfast buffet counter was really helpful with had a bright smile.
my daughter thinks she made the best waffles she had.  extremely friendly and hospitable.  thank you for making our stay great.
we stayed in business class rooms and it was fresh and well maintained.
did self yoga session at the gym studio and the staffs there were polite and helpful.
I didn’t enjoy that much my dinner here. Too many tourists and they serve a kind of food I don’t like very much (too many sauces).

One of the must see temples in Kathmandu.
There are 2 ways to enter, the first is for the fit people as there are 365 steep steps up and the other involves only a few. Also known as the monkey temple as there are plenty of them.be careful to show any food or water bottles as they will snatched.

Your experience is highly dependent on the weather especially the presence or absence of cloud cover.  We visited Sarangkot with an eye to see some of the Himalayan mountain range.  Unfortunately, despite visiting in early October 2019, we we met with dense cloud cover since Nepal including Pokhara was expiencing an extended moonsoon.  Apparently the sunrise is supposed to be fantastic?
Thamel is where it’s all happening! If you want to eat, go to Thamel. You want to drink, go to Thamel. You want to shop, go to Thamel! It’s a must-see :)

Kathmandu Durbar Square is a historically and culturally significant site in Kathmandu, Nepal. It is one of the three Durbar Squares in the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal that are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Kathmandu Durbar Square is an old durbar square in Kathmandu. Also known as "the Museum of Temples" because there are over 50 temples in the square.

a wonderful temple to visit though not clean. it's worthy the climb because at the end you will have a very nice view that will let you have nice backgrounds in your pictures.
if you have a driver with you, ask him to drop you off the further he can if you do not wish to walk a lot, because there are two ways to get to the top: either you walk the whole way and climb the whole height or the driver drive the half way... you chose.
there are a variety of shops but please be informed that you have to bargain: at least 30% of the price requested at the first attempt
you will need also to mind the naughty monkeys :-)

Beautiful garden and rooms, good breakfast, nice personnel. We took a massage - that was also memorable after a long trekking tour.
The location is quite calm and still very close to the center and lake.

Wow, the food and the atmosphere! 
I had the bowl “Alice” 3 times while only staying in Pokhara for a few days, I think that says a lot. A lot of food, fresh veggies and super yummy falafels! All tums up. Friendly staff and great overall vibe as well!

We stayed here before our EBC trek and found the location and facilities perfect. The breakfast buffet was great and they let us store our bags while we were away. When we came back to collect our bags we had a late night flight and the staff let us use their emergency room to shower and clean up before our flight for free. The staff truely go above and beyond! Thank you Kantipur Temple House, I would definitely recommend you to anyone staying in Kathmandu.

Nice and comfortable hotel with great amenities and friendly staff. Perfect central location but down a quiet street so it is relaxing. The gym is large and very well equipped with sauna and jacuzzi. The spa was nice but not the best. 

Only negative comment - THE  “FREE” WIFI IS HORRIBLE! If you need to do anything online you should look for another hotel OR pay USD $20/day for WiFi “upgrade” (totally shameful).
What a lovely stay with a wonderful restaurant and atmosphere and very child friendly and lovely staff - recommended!!!

This is less than an hour's drive from Pokhara to see the sunrise and the white capped mountains of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I,II,III and IV and Muchapuchre, If the weather is clear, it is a beautiful sight to watch the mountain range as well as the vast Pokhara valley below. The scenery is  worth a visit. One has to start at 5 am to reach the point in time from Pokhara hotels. There is an entry fee of Nepali Rs. 50/- per person to be paid for going up the Sarangkot hill. Locals have made rooftop restaurants where hot tea and coffee is available at a price. Some also keep Yakwool blankets, Pashmina shawls and stoles etc for the tourists to buy. Do not forget to negotiate since the prices are jacked up to keep a margin for negotiation.

Swayambhunath is a historical & ancient Bouddha Stupa located on a small hill-top.
There are a number of steps to climb at Stupa. 
One can have a great view of Kathmandu valley easily
Stupa is seen from many tall buildings easily also.
Take care of monkeys, they wont atke a single second time to snatch eatables from you :D 
Plz see the image in which Stupa is seen from rooftop in the city.

Booked & paid for this hotel through Goibibo (Indian based booking site). Received confirmation of availability & booking but the hotel refused to accept the booking on the basis I had not paid enough money. A long process over several days, numerous emails & meetings with Hotel management with them firstly saying they had no booking (I provided them with  booking confirmation), then that the rate was too cheap, then that they couldn't contact the provider & finally just out and out refusing to accept my booking saying that it was "my problem" & they would do nothing more! The kicker is they have now been paid the amount for the room & are denying they have it- so this supposedly professional hotel (part of a much larger chain) not only refuses a valid booking because they claim they weren't getting enough money, then adopted a "not my problem attitude" & lastly have taken my money for the booking & denying they have it!
 I have no idea whether they have  good product or not but they certainly have a very serious customer service problem (plus my money of course!).There are many options in Kathmandu- my advice is to stay somewhere else.

No hot water complained on numerous times from 19:30  never got resolved was always given a story.Down graded to another room just to bath across the road with hot water.But I was told initially that the hotel’s boiler is same which clearly was not.When asked if water was not hot I was asked if I wanted to move to a smaller room.No one helped us with our things across we felt so embarrassed walking the way we did.Only had supper after 22:00.Very dissatisfied with the radisson staff and water.Beatiful hotel set up and restaurants.Very nice casino which is child friendly.Not to bad but can better the standards.

We have visited the place on a Saturday afternoon, which we regretted. Pretty Much the only weekend in Nepal. Upon arrival at the bottom of the temple, there was a sudden influx of visitors locals and tourist. The place was pretty crowded and noisy you won't have space to breathe. There was an entrance fee of NPR 400 for non-SAARC national if you will use the main entrance but if you use the other side you don't have to pay anything. There is no way they could check it even if you are using the main entrance. There is no proper process on this as we have noticed on all the temples we visited in Nepal.
The steep stairs going up was all worth it especially if you visit in the afternoon. You will see one of the amazing sunsets plus the whole Kathmandu Valley as its background.
Next time you visit, bring a hanky and water.

I was bored and dont knw where to go. But i saw TripAdvisor.com and found or2k is the place in pokhara that will solve your problems. This is the main place to have dinner with nice classical 90's music...
It is the roof of the Pokhara from where you can get 360 view of Pokhara and  entire range of Himalaya... Incredible place, Please do not miss if you are around the valley :)

I was put off by other reviews on this website, but found the hotel not only in a safe area but with delightful helpful staff and charming touches. The food was excellent but let down by the ambience. However you do need to be a committed 'green' to stay here as a relief generator was not switched on at night since that is not ecologically friendly...nor are lifts. The place was imaculate, decorated with local textiles, internet was free, breakfast was outside in a delightful garden and full instructions were given for finding my way on local buses.....but in the end I found not being able to read at night was a handicap.

As Kathmandu was the last destination on our travels, we decided to splash out on this hotel. At $100 a night (about 10% of the average monthly pay check in Kathmandu) we expected a lovely stay.

Issues we experienced:
1 - no standard rooms came with a double bed. You have to pay $20 a night extra, even though the hotel was less than 50% occupied
2 - they have no cold drinking water. It comes lukewarm from a dispenser with dirty towels on it (picture attached)
3 - the building is a fake, just an imitation of an old building
4 - the food was horrible - breakfast was stale and dinner was overcooked. They also got our order wrong despite repeating it to us correctly
5 - the room is like a drug den from Trainspotting - cold, dark and dingy with a burst mattress 
6 - the shower curtain was mouldy with no natural light or ventilation in the bathroom. The water was a yellow colour and you had to run the sink tap to get a warm shower.
7 - they try to charge you for everything!! 3.5% fee for using a card, 23% added to all bills
8 - there is limited space to unwind or relax given the size of the hotel. They have a nice roof area but it's covered in dust and appears to be under construction so it's not in use

Good points
1 - decent location

Overall, I'm astounded how many of the good people on TripAdvisor would give this place five stars. Perhaps I have unreasonable expectations in life or others have just had a really tough time.

Do yourself a favour and avoid this place. Kathmandu is a energy sapping city and you want somewhere nice to relax. This is definitely not it.

Its always a great experience staying here as the staffs are very friendly and cooperative. I usually stay over there for business. Manita from "The Fun Cafe" is one of my favourite. Always professional and always attentive on what she does. Never misses a smile on her face.
The lake itself is beautiful, but it is polluted and one can see plastic bottles floating around. Something must be done to preserve its beauty.

This was my third stay here at Waterfront Resort by KGH and this time I was here with my family. We loved their service (superior as always) and the amenities. Our daughter's become a fan of their huge lush green gardens and the play area. All of us had a good time. The Indian Tandoori dinner is a must mention, kuddos to the chef.
On the day we went it was raining so we had to wait until it cleared. We stayed at the best hotel in the area for buffet breakfast and they had this great viewing deck. It was worth it anyway.

A new addition to the hotel scene of pokhara, well planned site and awesome view, decent food too,
however the staff was not well managed, awfully rude manager at the time, didn't know the basics of fine dining as well, otherwise its a great hotel, quite premium for the area, easily approachable too!

Hotel condition, hospitality, service etc  post covid needs to be geared up. No one right from the front office staff to the Directors are not taking responsibility and only big talks. It is a luxury hotel and not a 1 star property. 
Medical facilities need to be improved ASAP.
this is the besta places to see beautiful sunrises with lovely views of annapurna mountains and lovely views of pokhara..

The lake is great when seen from above during an ultralight flight, for example, however, when you get closer, you can see all the trash thrown by people, which is always very sad to see. The lake shores could use some work and cleaning. 
It is, of course beautiful. Too bad people ruin the beauties of nature...
Very nice area of the Kathmandu city. Thanks to the local authorities, some streets are suitable for pedestrians.
Beautiful view with lake n hills.Best part was boating in the lake.Reasonalbe pricefor boating.highly recommended.

-Hyatt blocked NPR 100,000 on Day one. My Bill was NPR 64000. But they charged 100,000
-Washrooms of the rooms were smelling
-No curd in the Buffet
-Old fittings in the washroom
-Cups directly kept on the cabinet surface. No tray
-Rickety ironing board

Disappointing visit really. Many of the temples are in a state of disrepair and overgrown,  at least in Patan there is active repair going on. We couldn't access higher points to have good views ( you can in Patan) and the museum is very closed, not sure what we paid our 1000 npr entry fee for.
Once inside the palace you have some calm in the inner squares to admire the carving and gilt features.  Yes it is amazing but as a UNESCO heritage site there is sadly little active reparation . Continuously hassled for guiding.
This place is huge. It's a bit busy but locals visit to pray at the temples as well as us tourists visiting. The street hawkers are a bit annoying but everyone needs to make a living.

Maybe afternoon visit was not a good idea, maybe we have visited too many lakes, this lake looked average to us. As it was hot and humid, we did not take the boat. The guide told us if the sky was clearer, we could see the fish-tail mountain, but we did not have the luck.

We did the boat ride in the evening on one of the days in Pokhara. As far as the boat ride itself is concerned, it is nothing great. What is good though is the temple in the middle of the lake and the surroundings of the lake which look nice in the evening and on a clear sky one can see Mt. Fishtail from the boat. It is important to choose what type of boat one wants to go in as the small boat we went in could manage only 4 people and none of us were sitting next to each other. We all had our backs to each other in a row. We took the ride that took us to the start of the lake and so were about 40 min in the lake.

Best hotel in thamel kathmandu nepal. its amazing place very quite and clean room I really enjoy in trekkers home it is feel like my second home. staff very friendly and helpful I will recommend all my friend.
Thoroughly enjoyed the atmosphere and great food. A good range of choice on the menu around a eastern Mediterranean theme.

We Had a wonderful breakfast experience at the hotel! The food was delicious, with a great variety to choose from, and the service was top-notch. Special thanks to Rupak and his team, for ensuring everything was perfect and for his exceptional hospitality. Looking forward to returning!

Situated in the 'Western Hub' in Thamel area, near a lot of restaurants and shops.
I went inside the hotel grounds to and got a tour to inspect the rooms to get an idea of room sizes and prices etc...
I didnt like the room sizes and the bathroom areas as it did not meet my expectations, therefore I didnt stay here.
Price was around USD$50+ for double bed room.
The large hotel garden areas is magnificent and you can simply chill out and relax with a book and a drink on the seatings inside the garden.
Overall the hotel presentation is nice.
This hotel is 2 minute walk to a large supermarket named 'Shop Right Supermarket'.

This hotel is like historical palace to live in for few days. It takes you 19th century back when you enter in the hotel. I was spell bound by the theme of the hotel i.e. historical design and great architecture. Everything was on point food, staff ,hospitality , clean and warm coozy room.
One of the finest hotels in Kathmandu with the best front office staff and Chefs on board. The restaurant team and the front office team is ready to go to any limit to satisfy their guests

Went on the cable car. Fabulous views of Pokhara and Fewa Lake. Found cafe where owner had her own weaving loom and sold items she'd made herself. Not much in Sarangot other than a few hotels and cafés,  but pleasant to walk around and on a clear day you can see Anbapurna. Company that runs the cable car offers adventure sports as well. View tower/restaurant at top of cable car.
All the paragliding items are made in this area. one can directly contact here with pilots and have low price paragliding !
Excellent sunrise view from top of Sarangkot.  Good view of Annappurna and Machapuchare Mountains.  Got to see the town from top of the place.  Windy place to visit at early morning.

Very crowded and narrow. They wanted 1000 Rupees each to walk in the area. Seeing how most of this area is closed and damaged following the earthquake a few years ago, not good, and especially as all the locals just walked in and around! We just went around and there are lots of ways into the area without being accosted for money. Dissapointing as so much damage and little to now visit.

The hotel itself is in 2 parts physically separated from each other and you get sent across from the main lobby to a building across the street as premium rooms are separate in a new building. (but you come back to the old building for breakfast). 

The inexperience of the staff is very visible in almost every thing they do. I once stepped in and told the front office lady how to print my boarding pass which I had sent to the front office by email !!(after waiting for it for 10 minutes)

You also get service when you personally "ask" for it. More responsive service will help this hotel.

This place is seeing is believing. If you are not here you can’t appreciate the beauty of Kathmandu Valley. We hired  Doonga , a colourful boat to visit Tal Barahi temple on an island  in the middle of the serene and picturesque Phewa lake . We observed the reflection of the snow-clad Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in the        crystal clear water of the lake .   In the far west was the Dhawalagiri Range with Mt. Dhawalagiri peaking at 8,167m. In the middle and extending all the way to the east , the views of the Annapurnas: I (8,091m) , II (7,937m) , III (7,555m) , IV (7,525m) and Mt. Machhapuchhre or Fishtail (6,991m) , were simply gorgeous. It was truly a sight to behold .

Phewa Lake is the second largest guitar shaped  lake (1.5 km wide and 4 km long) encircled by Sarangkot and Kaskikot hills , in Nepal . It’s depth varies from 6 m to 22 m . It has 21 species of fish including Cavasius , Chagurius , Channa Garchula ,  Danio Devrio , Daurias , Garra Gotyla , etc . 
 
There are hundreds of hotels , lodges , restaurants , shops , travel and trekking offices , and other tourist related service centres on the east bank of the lake . The west bank of the  lake is surrounded by green rolling hills and thick forests through which there are many thrilling trails , one of which leading to Shanti Stupa on Anadu Hill .

Has a modern metropolitan  plan and was probably originally internationally designed and funded. Its vast walled garden grounds are surrounded by small tin roofed shacks of an entirely different style and level of funding. There is a differential entry fee scale  with highest fees for foreign visitors and lowest  for locals. Staff are friendly and professional.  The displays in the main building are an undermaintained mix of cobbled together and very planned. The mountain  theme includes ethnic displays of local  and a few foreign, national and local geology, geomorphology, geography, etc..  Many displays rely heavily on graphic images especially photographs. There is also a mixed display of some mountain climbing gear, some old, some not so old. This includes the coverage of what may have been a misfunded treasure hunt climb for antique momentos of old climbs in the guise of of an Everest garbage clean-up. In addition, there is a Buddhist worship room. Outside there are fun photo oppurtunities to pose with a many hand polished bronze yak  and a climbable mockup of the reagions fishtail peak. The whitewash snow of the mock peak will give a reminder on hand and cloth if brushed up against. The on grounds shop  and/or a recreated thatched mountain structure had closed  already after we exited the main building, but we had arrived late in the day on our own just a couple hours before closing. The restaurant in a similar mountain village theme decor was open. The food was good and they did not rush us even though the closing time had past after we were served. I could see there was also a belay or free climbing structure, but I did not get information on the limit of its use. 

Overall the experience was pleasant, but not as it appeared from the road and advertising. It seems to be underfunded or managed in an alternative way than it was originally planned. The displays are less interactive and more photographic exhibit based than I prefer. The price for foreigners was rather high on a local relative scale. I enjoyed the ham photo oppurtunities of the yak and mock mountain most.  If one likes climbing and all related to it then maybe it is a peak experience.
