There is a stone path that runs alongside the lake parallel to the main road of Pokhara.

I read the mixed reviews about this place and thought I would give it the benefit of the doubt, there was quite a bit of information about the mountains and geology but a lot of the museum didn’t even have lights on we had to use our phones torches just to see half of it... Also it is 500npr for tourists (much higher than a local rate which I believe is wrong anyway) and is quite expensive for what it is...

nice outdoor terrace bar restaurant beautiful sunset view. terrace staff was friendly and attentive .excellent service by Manhari  and restaurant staff. excellent  food and cocktail service. we enjoy food lots of choice of Mexican food.
Food is great (vegetarian), service is good, but be aware of the "Specials" scam: they advertise a few dishes as specials (450 rupees), and charge them as in the menu (680 rupees). Shame on them!

Overall pleasant stay. Quality of pillows and shower could be improved. pillows were too soft and not appropriate for sleeping. Shower was leaking all over the place and gave impression of not being properly cleaned for some time.

Was glad we visited, but not my favorite destination.  You don't have to take all the stairs, there is a road where the taxi can drive you almost to the top, and then you walk the final 40 steps or so.  When we visited, it was overrun with tourists, very crowded. The monkeys were interesting, but overall just felt it was too touristy.  Really preferred the Bouda Stupa, which felt more spacious and peaceful.

Rather typical Asian city. Surprising if you are not familiar with Asia. Streets are very narrow in Thamel and often lined with shops. Many motor bikes so walking is irregular. Navigation is tricky at first as the streets marked on map tend to be very narrow and are unlabelled. A little practice and it becomes clearer. The sort of town that grows on you.

If you've come across the world to visit Nepal, this would not be on my list of things to do.  It's a lake.  You can rent a rickety boat with an oarsman.

If you live closely and are looking for a nice afternoon activity this might be a good option for a relaxing time

hotel the room was absolutely poor, the size of the room was small and the furniture were old. I was not allowed to take my friend up to the room even for 5 min because she was a girl. they happily disgraced me and humiliated my friend. My friend is a social worker who helps women in need and they treated her so disrespectfully. Please do me a favour, do not waste your time here.

Before my trek and after trek i stayed in Thamel which is city center. Thamel is touristic area where you can find Shopping; Restaurant; Travel agency; Pub and many hotel. Its very nice for crazy day trip.
I like Thamel and recommended to visit this place.
once you get to the top there is an amazing 360 degree view overlooking two valleys. you are above the place where the para gliders start so you can see para gliders below you for once.
Relatively clean, markets after 4.30pm fun, lots of history in the temples in the town and alleyway living. A management part of Kathmandu where it’s possible to walk

excellent central location and close to airport. nice fitness facility. swimming pool is not heated. rooms are correct and big but somewhat old fashioned and old. very good food services and choices. stuff very polite but not alway efficient.
Beautiful lake, bit crowdy but you will pass through. Negotiate before getting in a boat in terms of both money and time. Take life jacket form the corresponding office.
The property is beautiful from the outside, run down in some rooms, and lacking basics like A/C in summer months. Friendly staff.

The museum has an interesting collection of historical high altitude mountaineering equipment and its evolution over the decades.  The main takeaway for me was just how primitive the equipment was that was used to first climb some of the highest mountains in the world.

The walk to the main building from the parking lot and the fish pond in front of it can provide nice photo opportunities.

The museum is good for a walk through, but unless you are into serious mountaineering, there are better ways to spend your vacation time in Pokhara.

Good spot, on the lake. 
Really nice staff.  Most of the times can talk good n clear English.  
The food is amazing. You can find here simple middle eastern food,  combining some classy dishes and good drinks.  
every week they have live shows of friends  n performance from all over the world. 
Price r ok.  A bit more then the usual. But  honestly worth it! 
Have fun;)
get a good eye view of kathmandu from this point. nice place to relax and get close with the locals and culture
Nice museum showing the beautiful mountains of this beautiful country Nepal such a nice place it is highly recommended for all
I often visit this place for varieties of vegetarian food. Himalayan Goat Cheese salad is one of the best food for me.
Beautiful part in Kathmandu was Thamel in our trips have a here night time view was so beautiful and must busy areas in Kathmandu valley visited here and get your experience

I am still shocked how a Radisson can be so pathetic in guest experience. I stayed there for 2 nights while I was on a trip with my family (a large group of 25 ppl).
The hotel felt like a torture chamber where we had to call up at least 5-6 times to even get simple things like room cleaning done. The kids in our group starved while the food order took more than 2 hours to get delivered with rubbery and cold naan that they simply refused to replace.

One day we were to visit the nearby Temple and requested to  pack our breakfast or extend the breakfast timing by 15 mins in case we got late. They simply refused. Repeated requests were made and repeated insults were received.

The list goes on and on...

Radisson is a reputed name and getting a service so poor is just not done. I hope they do some massive restructuring and trainings to improve the non existent hospitality. Till then, plz avoid the place. It is a hoge disappointment.

I've been to Sarangkot many times & always enjoy going there. An interesting road leads to the top passing typical Nepali homes along the way. Great vistas overlooking Phewa Lake & Pokhara to the south & if you pick the right time great views of the Annapurna mountains including Macchepechre  (Fishtail) to the north
There are tons of boats offering rides (either paddle or peddle boats). It's a fun, slow trek across the lake. Nice views of the lack and city.
Pretty, peaceful lake.  Rent boats with rowers or rent your own.  Or just walk around it to enjoy the view!

Located on the of Pokhara city is the hill acknowledged as Sarangkot. It provides one of Pokhara's biggest views of the Annapurna Himalayan mountains peaks. Sarangkot is a village just above Pokhara, acknowledged as a one-night destination as most people just give up in to see the lovely break of day over the Annapurna range and leave. It is great viewed at sunrise or nightfall due to the staggering red and orange colorings the mountain range takes on. View from Sarangkot at Sunrise - click to see large picture of dawn at Sarangkot There's a non-descript village just earlier than the fiew factor which is based totally atop an historic fort. Sarangkot is also the popular vicinity for paragliders to launch from in Pokhara. Though that is where publications lead human beings off target as many exhibit up right here looking forward to just to come for one day and favor to remain longer. If you are going trekking in the Annapurna mountain vary then view Sarangkot first instead than after the trek! It's one way or the other better to seem at the place you are going than the place you've got simply come from. Aside from chilling out and taking in exquisite views of each the mountains and Phewa Lake on the other side, Sarangkot affords a exceptional glimpse into the peaceful, slow village lifestyles and more.

I stayed at the Lakeside Retreat as part of a package with Explore. The setting, rooms and design are all very nice but do not order a toasted sandwich in the restaurant as it will be cold and so too will the accompanying French fries - despite sending it back to be re-grilled (it came back even colder and the bread was stale). Our laundry came back late, damp and with items missing, items which they could not locate before our departure. Compensation was woefully inadequate.  I would not chose to stay at this hotel again. Even the water in the bathroom was cold.

Great place to unwind after trek although the mojitos were pretty disappointing; we didn't taste any alcohol so the price wasn't justified.  Food is an international mix of veggie options.  My friend was very happy with her dal bhat whilst my food was average especially as the falafel was very dry.  Service was slow; the bill took ages to arrive.
You can't swim in it (a pity with the weather they have for most of the year!) but you can paddle to the top with a bottle of bear and enjoy the views - recommended;)

OR2K was amazing and we'll be going back. Set upstairs with beautiful views over the lake it is an amazing venue to watch the sunset. A varied and interesting menu with food from Nepal, the Middle East and Europe. All presented to a very high standard, all very very tasty and incredible value for money. Would highly recommend middle eastern food - delicious. We'll be coming back.

Okay, I am in Kathmandu, and I have to visit Durbar Square, just because it's there.  I went to Bhaktapur the day before, and you don't want to miss Bhaktapur.  If you only have limited time, you can pass Kathmandu Durbar Square, but not Bhaktapur.
Perfect stay .enjoyed ,staff is friendly. Food is excellent .on time service with a smile .Thanks Navina and sante for a great time in breakfast. Will be back soon .

If you are only In Kathmandu for a short stay, I would go here for the city views, and sunset is nice if the sky is favourable. Practice your night photography if you wait til it’s dark.

Lots of people walked kora (circle) and spin the many prayer wheels.
There are lots of small shrines and small temples but I am not sure how many. I didn’t see everything as I was there for the views.

There is an entrance fee right near the top. 
Apparently there is a back entrance too, without the many stairs.

I’m afraid of monkeys so practically held my breath up the 365 stairs, but they left me alone as I did not carry food. There were lots of monkey fights and screeches, so be warned!

It was a busy with locals posing for selfies the afternoon I went. It was close to 5pm so the stalls had closed up so less people will hassle you to buy they bracelets and souvenirs.

I took a local taxi here for Rs300 and easily found a different one to return at 6pm. Do bring your hotel map and phone number if it’s not a big name hotel. 

The all seeing eyes of Buddha are ubiquitous to Nepal and this stupa is no exception. Enjoy!

Don't exoect too much: chaos of pubs, restaurabts and shop; you will see life but more on the streets than in the pubs - at least when we went in June was like this - but it is where you have to go at night.
The museum is relatively nice, I liked the parts showcasing the traditional village life from different parts of Nepal, as well as the exhibits of old mountain gear from first ascents.

This site in central Kathmandu is still suffering from the after effects of the 2015 earthquake that struck the area.

Many of the buildings are still being repaired and under protective cover. It brings home the gravity of the quake.

I felt the hotel very over whelming. The security and the peace environment was seasoned. The staff and the Receiption were very helpful and cooperative. Anyways I felt that The lunch should be more in term of items , curry and the rice. I would prefer the hotel again.
Phewa Lake is lovely. We took a boat across the lake from Pokhara NRs 1260 pp to visit the temple on the lake and the World Peace Pagoda at the top of the hill.

I recently visited Phewa Taal in Pokhara, and it was an unforgettable experience. The lake is surrounded by stunning hills and offers a peaceful escape from the busy city.

I went boating in the early morning when the water was calm and the reflection of the Annapurna range on the lake was absolutely magical. I also visited the Tal Barahi Temple, located in the middle of the lake, which added a spiritual touch to the trip.

There are many cafés and restaurants nearby, perfect for relaxing after the boat ride. The area is clean and well-maintained, and boat rentals are easy and affordable.

I recommend visiting around sunrise or sunset for the best views. Don’t forget your camera — the scenery is breathtaking!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) — Highly recommended for nature lovers, couples, and anyone looking to relax.
This place could be an absolute highlight of Nepal. It has an energy. But the whole place is so grotty,dirty with this horrible smell. It looks like it is not maintained at all. Pity!

I came to the museum hoping that it would be really something exceptional, needless to say I was very disappointed. Most of the museum consisted of laminated documents stuck on the wall, there was only a handful of actual historical things to see. 

The admission is about $4USD,  If it was actually informative I would have given it a thumbs up, I felt it was a waste of a few hours.

A lovely hotel in old temple style.  My room was very spacious with a view to the courtyard.  The staff were wonderful - so friendly and helpful.  As the nights were chilly we got hot water bottles and heaters.  Breakfasts were great.

The property is beautiful. However both the quality of service needs drastic improvement. I got a broken iron board and had to wait 2 hours and make innumerable calls before it was changed. The hot chocolate had spoilt cream topping and the buffet was very average in taste and display. The room was clean but toiletries were awful. There was no toothpaste and brushand the shampoo , moisturiser etc were not good either. Lucky for me i carried my own stuff. Check in and check out was quick .

This was surprisingly awesome. It starts with the different ways mountain people lived and clothes, instruments, which is nice. But what is really cool is the mountaineering section. There are many donations from previous climbers which make this museum just a treasure trove. The pictures of sir Edmund Hillary are epic and the various expeditions shown through the old camera shots make you feel you are in a national geographic magazine. Also after recently finishing a large trek the realisation that this was achieved less than 70years ago with such basic and very heavy equipment makes one feel that we are now very spoilt and privileged. Defiantly worth haggling with a taxi to take you out there.
The view from the lake is awesome. We got the boat for 1350 NC for  8 people for 1 hr. The lake is 50 m in depth, you can also take single boat or boat for two.
Excellent streets to walk and do shopping.  You get all sorts of souveigners.  You can bargain.  Must place to visit in Kathmandu
You should walking from Durbar Square to Thamel. Most of roads in Thamel are walking only. You will see so many shops and can buy almost anything. Also if you want to Nepali brand then go to woven.

We came here with group of 12 . The resort is amazing. The staff was very courteous. We were taken very good care. Food was very wholesome and healthy. Staff was always willing to help. Hygiene was of very high order. Hope to visit again
Manoj Sharma

Super nice restaurant and cafe! You can sit on the floor on pillows and take a rest of running around all day.We had fruit juice, Coffee and a Hummus dish,everything was perfect! The free wifi was good to plan our next steps of our vacation and to connect to our love ones at home. Thank you!

This Restaurant is awesome. The food ist very good, nice to sit there and rest after a hard tracking day. The service is also very good. We habe been there twice and we trink it is better than in Kathmandu. Tanks alot for your Choila :-)

The hotel is generally ok. Beds are very comfortable. The hotel could overall be much better maintained. Cheap decoration. The swimming pool area is sad. The sauna is old/doesn’t work properly. The steam bath is genuinely disgusting with humidity stains everywhere and stinky- could not use it.
Staff is friendly period. No commercial zeal. 
Overall, a price too high for what is is.

We really loved their food... We went two times there. First in Thamel & second day in Pokhara. We tried diff food there - pizza, Turkish hummus, Turkish platter, fired rice etc... And all were good :)

I really recommend it for all :)
Storm was threatening. Lots of families out enjoying the lovely evening. Nice festive family vibe. Nice restaurants and bars along the lakeside.

Stayed here 6 nights while I'm in Kathmandu. Centrally located and room have hot and cold shower. Wifi working ok. Prices is just more then perfect for the location. This place have nice rooftop and have many different types of rooms suits for different types of travellers.

Very comfortable, the staff is excellent and very polite and helpful . The hotel could do with a little refurbishment of the rooms , it was very clean but old . And the room needs to have more light . Other than that it was great.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Pokhara, far more better than the one in Kathmandu. The staff here was very nice, friendly, and attentive, they still maintain the good nature. The food was decent, portion was much generous than the Kathmandu one, for example, Hummus with Mushroom and Onion, was great and quite a plateful, good enough for 2 persons to share, as the Kathmandu one, the same order is more like an appetizer. The layout and the view is very nice. Great for a meal, a drink, or just relax, enjoying the ambiance.

Our recent stay at Waterfront Resort was absolutely wonderful. The staff's hospitality and service were truly exceptional. They were consistently courteous, attentive, and went out of their way to ensure our comfort. From a seamless check-in to their helpfulness with every request, the team made us feel incredibly welcome. The level of care and professionalism demonstrated by the staff significantly enhanced our experience, making our time at the resort a truly memorable one.
Well worth visiting when in the area. And interesting and informative guide to the area and people. Recommended.

It was a nice place with amazing view of the Kathmandu Valley. The monkeys were everywhere and that kind of kept me on alert because I have read they can be aggressive. It seemed like a place that is very popular among the locals.

It certainly is one of the highlights to visit, but I got really emotional about the place. I was here 21 years ago and back then ofcourse it wasn't destroyed by the earthquakes. And although there was rubbish everywhere and monkey feaces there was also a peacefull athmosphere. And the mixture of all the different buildings was stunning, besides the views from up there and the amazing steep stairway at the main entrance (you can approach by car thru the back and fewer steps will lead you to the top). But now, first I was shocked by the destruction and the fact that nothing has been rebuild after 2 years. It looks like they are rebuilding, but they are not. I know this from Nepali friends who come here frequently and joined us on our visit up to Swayambu. Frustrated to say, but this goes for ALL the destructed places after the quakes. And I got stressed out from the many people finding their way between piles of stones and other construction material left there for reconstruction, a lot of garbish (like at many places in the city), monkeys everywhere and vendors. 
So, you should visit, if it's only to pay the fee and in that way help with reconstruction, although I always wonder where the money actually goes to in this country. But don't expect a quiet and peacefull place (maybe at 5 or 6 am) and try to focus on the beautiful shrines and temples that are still standing and try to ignore all the nasty things.

We came down from the Peace Stupa and boarded a rowboat for the peaceful trip across the lake. There's a Hindu temple in the middle which we didn't visit. Gorgeous December weather. A modest amount of tourists. Did you know this is a man made lake? Wow!

It's an okay place. Prices are alright, about average. Would be a good place to hang out if I wasn't alone. I didn't like that there's smoking inside. I got the hummus with naan, was good, not filling but I wasn't expecting it to be. With a bottle of water, it's about $3.
Beautiful and serene ...gets crowded and noisy near the temple and boat jetty. Great place to catch a mountain view but make sure you go to the dam site.
A bustling and lively area, full of tourist shops, cafes, bars etc. A great place to hang out if you're only in Kathmandu for a day or two.
We can see 3 types of structural architecture in single place. Commonly referred as "Monkey Temple" and one of the must visit place

Best location and service, good room. I can recommend this place to any tourist who would like European comfort and customer service. The breakfast was not so perfect for the price. There was nothing that I did not like, everything was perfect.

we quickly visited durbar square bc the museum was closed due to the holiday— it was deepawali. no sense in paying $10 when there was nothing to see, but the square was alive with color, festivity preparations, and bustling with excitement. a definite must-see!

This hotel is well located, offering a quiet and peaceful retreat in the busy Thamel area of Kathmandu. The building is newer than it appears, having been built in the local traditional style and it offers much potential which, sadly, it fails to deliver in a number of respects. This is not a cheap place to stay and, contrary to suggestions on their website the rooms have no fans, no hair dryers and extremely limited toiletries. Our first room was characterful but extremely dark, even with all the available lights turned on. The excellent lady receptionist did arrange a new and lighter room for us for the remainder of our short stay. Breakfast was OK although unchanged throughout our stay and not very well replenished towards the end of the session, also seating appeared limited and unable to cope with the number of guests.
In summary we felt that the hotel has great potential but fails to deliver on a number of fronts, making its higher than average charges poor value for money. On a positive note the airport pick up was reliable and not excessively priced at $10, it was reassuring to exit the airport and see the waiting driver waving our names immediately outside the door.

Also known as the monkey temple, the climb up the steps is definitely rewarded with spectacular views and and innate sense of tranquillity. A November visit avoids the crowds, leaving you with the local faithful and the hum of their prayers.
A mountain lake, which was probably lovely once but is now merely a tourist trap full of hawkers trying to sell their wares.  Not much else.
Incredible site of historical importance.  You may want to agree to a guide since they have info and are really not that expensive.  Walkable to Tamel through more of the local markets.

This is situated in Thamel which is sort of  a backpacker's district. A great place to be. 
The service staff is nice and helpful. The hotel let us keep our bags for 10 days without any charge. 
The rooms in real life were a bit underwhelming compared to photos on Tripadvisor. 
For the price, it is decent but I assume that there would be myriad of other options.

PHEWA Lake is one of the best lakes I have been to in my entire life. This place is mind blowing. It's a true Paradise. One would feel completely rejuvenated after visiting this place. The boaters were amazing. It would be even more amazing to visit during the winters.
Hats off to the Nepal Government for maintaining the lake and its surroundings.

We were promised of a spectacular sunrise, better than any place in Nepal, but the weather cheated us. However, with some patience and wait we could view equally astounding view of annapurna range with machhapuchhre (fishtail) mountain with golden glow from the rising sun. Later the sun that we saw was ordinary. Sarankot hill provides an ideal space paragliding, small trek besides sunrise. Byapta

this museum has no engaging stories or information. It summarises mountain conquests on posters, has a few dioramas of the mountains and environment, and a video with no commentary of mountain locals. I got nothing out of this visit, it is a waste of time and money.
Beautiful lake and most importantly it was lake festival during our visit so it was absolutely serene.

Very well decorated typical Nepali rooms. Breakfast could have been better. The owner was very kind. It was overall Ok experience. Very good large rooms, friendly staff, Eco friendly Hotel ð??ð??ð?? We enjoyed our stay at Kantipur Temple House ð?¤?

I had wanted to visit here for a really long time, and the actual experience was so much better than could ever have expected. A particular highlight was when i got to see the living goddess... which was an experience beyond words.

The Temple Tree resort is not a bad hotel, but the reception staff has ruined our stay.

We had booked a "nice view, second floor, double room". We got a room at the ground floor and without any view. We were told that the hotel has no room with a view - which is a lie as some rooms have wonderful views on the Annapurna chain- and was fully booked - another lie as the room next to ours stayed empty during all our stay. . After discussion we were told that we were "upgraded" to a Super Luxury room. This room was on the second floor, fine, but without a any view, and was one of the only ones without a balcony ! Upgraded ? Another lie. From my surprise I was told that this room was the :honeymoon room" ??? Maybe because basically the shower is ... in the room ? Hard hygienic experience for the newly married :-).

Then the reception has no small change (imperative service in Nepal) at the beginning of the afternoon, one of the ladies did not know how to print a flight ticket, another one told us that she did not received our e mail (sent 3 times) ... Well ? the reception staff lies all the time. Impossible to trust them any time. Their only goal is to send back the customers far away from their desk.

Training imperatively is needed if the Temple Tree was to pretend itself as one of the best (?!) hotels in Pokhara.

Rooms are now comparable 18 Th century . Restaurants has least possible menu . Bathroom fittings could not have been worse . 
No where near Hyatt . They even charge for steam and sauna to in-house guest which is very funny too .

Excellent hotel. Stayed 6 nights. 3 of those i was woken before 6.30 by a football game being played next to the hotel. Another night i was woken several times by a dog barking in the same are. I also had one of tglhe worst pizzas i have ever eaten which is a pity as the breakfasts were superb. Staff and particularly housekeeping were outstanding
Thamel has everything a tourist would need. Street shopping and an array of restaurants! Heart of Kathmandu!

There's a good stretch of walkway where you can enjoy the lake and also the chaos of the town. Countless bars, restaurants and such line this walkway with mostly guys trying to lure you into their establishment with phrases like, "Happy Hour!" and "Local music!". The locals hang out here as well, so it is a nice mix of tourists and people from Pokhara. There's part of the promenade that covers the granola, vegan hipster smoothie shops and such. If that's what you're looking for, keep walking to the end. Didn't go out on the boats because the lake didn't look that clean and I have an acute fear of drowning, but many people paddle and row their way into the very center of the lake. The mountains surrounding the water help make this a very serene and unique place in mostly dry Nepal.

Our guide Sony from VYAS TREKS suggested that we visit around sunrise to really enjoy the view of Kathmandu city and the temple.
On a clear day, it is a must to spend at least 2 hours and to listen to the mantra playing and dancing in the wind.
The monkeys are not what this site visit should be about
Clean airy spacious, with plenty of room to view the exhibits at leisure. The information cards are clear and concise. We learnt a great deal about mountaineering, particularly in the area.

I stayed 3 night this hotel trekker home. it's nice hotel and they manager mr.saroj very friendly.  They too much help us. I request to everyone if you visit nepal . You can stay this hotel. Definitely  will back

Unless you are going to climb Mount Everest, don't even bother going to Nepal. It's so dirty and polluted. People spit in the streets and blow their noses into their hands in the streets. the dogs are walking around with their skin hanging off and open sores from skin diseases. I have been here 3 times and every time I come I get some type of infection and end up in the hospital. Back home I NEVER get sick and I am generally very healthy. 
You could go to Switzerland and see the mountains and more beautiful places and won't have to worry about pollution or health problems.

The Swayambhu Nath Temple is one of the most important Buddhist religious site in the world and equally important for Nepalese Hindus. But to be honest, I must say, the people in-charge and taking care of this site are, the world's biggest corrupts. The temple area is broken everywhere, dirty, disgusting & smelly (probably monkey poop). It is definitely 1000s of years old but it has been hardly taken care of. It seems like not even 1% of the money raised from entrance fees and donations is being uses for keeping the temple area protected. The sight I saw a month after the earthquake has not changed in more than a year and half. The temple has only been a place where the corrupted in-charge and monks make insane amount of money from nothing.  If I were to pay an entrance fee or if  there was no view of the city from the top, I would never go there. I feel really sorry for the temple and the country that these people are ruining this historic site. But hopeful that things will change.

Its a huge lake, and catchment area for a dam nearby. It all depends from which side of the lake you are watching the lake from. There is a temple in the middle of the lake and a small boat ride will take you there which is nice.

Looooots of shops here and some pretty cool stuff to collect. A few amazing restaurants throughout at cheap prices. Unfortunately the shops are kind of tourist traps, and lots of scammers on the streets. Also omg the pollution! 

We got sick of the endless shops and tourist traps eventually but a day or a half day here would be worth a visit. Try not to get hit by a vehicle. Beware of randoms asking if you want a massage, restaurant, weed, tiger balm, “free” tour, flute, look-in-my-shop, taxi, where-you-from?, shoe shine, guide, nice necklace you-like?, porter, cotton candy, fruit, bike carriage, speed/opium/crank, laundry service, hairpins, help-me-practice-my-English, nuts, prayer flags, or directions (never accept this offer). 

We got some good trekking gear here for cheaper than back home, but the really cheap stuff is terrible quality, go for medium priced (ie if it’s $150 aus back home then $70 will be ok here but $25 won’t). We found that the prices went down by sometimes as much as 2/3 when you say you’ll come back to their store later. Geez. 

Also please be wary of people just wanting to give you free tours, go for guides through a reputable company, check their credentials as well (they should have a permit).

Best part about the hotel was its staff. Receptionist was specially very helping, staff was well behaved. Restaurant offered great food. Pool was perfect. Spa was really very relaxing. We stayed in cottages to house 3 people in each room. Cottages were spacious, hotel is maintained well. Loved the concept of open air reception surrounded with water.

beautiful and maginificent hotel. at the time of covid, the staff is not plentiful. so services are not as per the expectations. but the staff and managers are very good. food is very tasty. needs improvement with the wash rooms. very good experience.
Fascinating temple complex on the hills.  Great view of the Kathmandu valley.  Beware of monkeys that can be quite aggressive
The lake is beautiful and the views of mountains from the lake and the boats are superb. Must visit here.

Salina our trainee host was fabulous .
Polite and courteous, very attentive personalised service. Made our experience very special

Cheap and comfortable hotel, stayed for two nights and enjoyed very much!!keep recommending friends and family for this budget hotel in Thamel.Restaurent in first floor Kathmandu steak house was really handy for us, We can even ordered food at our room and all service were ok during our stay.

The food was excellent and staff were very polite and caring. Well managed clean dinning room. Special thanks to Anu and Supriya for good hospitality. The nice ambience with authentic Nepali food brings in the best of what a good host can provide.

The Durbar square   is at least a place to take refresh in kathamndu.Because Kathmandu  is so busy and so much people. This place is beautiful  but surprise that after earthquake it is still not  reconstructed. But chiya ''tea" is perfect over there.

We had a two day workshop here and was disappointed in the support, it was pretty disorganized, and we didn't have a point of contract during the workshop. They got the tea time wrong at one point and tried to argue with us about it. They didn't have our room reservations, etc. Also the beds are incredibly hard, making it hard to sleep.

By far one of the best find in Pokhara. The views are just out of this world & great choices of cuisine available. Visitors can hv an option to hv Veg, Non Veg, Vegan dishes of their choices... try to reserve an outside sitting during afternoon as its beautiful.

If you are looking for a nice boutique hotel in Kathmandu that exudes charm, this is the place.  The decor is genuine Nepali and authentic.  And, something that is not to be taken for granted in Thamel, it is very quiet ensuring you will get some rest after arriving.  

The staff is professional and attentive.  They were very helpful in locating our lost bags which can be cumbersome when you don’t speak Napoli.

Took a boat ride around the lake. Lovely views. No motors are being used to power the boats so it remains relatively clean. My ride took about 45mins. Stops in the temple right in the middle of the lake.

We have visited in the evening time and mostly the shop were closed. May be because od less business but we are hopping the time will be nice soon. 

Hope everything will be nice and we can buy nepali handicraft for memory of visiting nepal. Great to be here
Maybe the most famous Square in Nepal. Not sure if the most beautiful but indeed fascinating. Definitely need a guide.

Great and friendly staff breakfast were great
Clean rooms with great house keeping services 
Great location to restaurants and shopping

Gym and swimming pool great the only thing missing was pool service for drinks

Also would have love a out side jot tub
But there is a hot tub for men and women
In there own areas
They’re still doing a lot of construction after the earthquake so much of the area you are unable to go to.

The Kantipur Temple house is the best hotel in Kathmandu— I stayed there for a couple nights before a trek in April 2021, and came back for a second visit with my family in October 2022 and stayed 2 weeks here!! It is a BEAUTIFUL hotel with traditional Nepali woodworking throughout, comfortable beds, large rooms, lovely spaces to hang out in, and all the amenities you could need during your stay. The entire staff is incredibly kind and extremely helpful, and the food is EXCELLENT. I highly recommend this hotel.

The Kathmandu Guest House is the grand dame of guest houses in Kathmandu. It has been the Kathmandu base of countless trekking and mountaineering expeditions for decades. The sense of history is writ large throughout the hotel with photos of some of mountaineering's greatest achievers throughout the main building. The hotel also celebrates some of its more modern and recognizable celebrity guests like Ricky Martin with small tiles engraved on the floor of the beautiful and tranquil garden courtyard. The hotel location is unbeatable. It feels like the Thamel district is centered around this institution.  

But the KGH rests on its laurels and provides a relatively poor service offering at a price that is 30-40% more expensive than hotels that provide comparable room quality and service. The wifi is slow and frustratingly inconsistent. The breakfast is average and the staff throughout the hotel can generally be described as brusque. 

If you feel the lure of history and desire an unbeatable location the KGH may be for you.  However, know that you can get substantially more for substantially less if you try another hotel that is earning its keep and your custom in a hugely competitive market in the Thamel district.

being an indian, such mixed markets are so common there, it was not at all impressive or exotic.
 no, you do not feel anything of good, old kathmandu here.
fake products are common, as expected.
heavy bargaining for over-priced goods and foods also, as expected.
lots of accommodations for foreigners, not at all cheap but better than hotels.
if you have time to spare, just stroll and write home about an imaginary thrilling by-lane experience.

We stayed at Hotel Water Front for four nights and had a truly wonderful experience. The rooms were clean, comfortable, and cozy, making our stay very relaxing. Although the rooms could use a bit of soundproofing as they were slightly noisy at times, everything else was excellent.

The breakfast was simple yet tasty — but what truly made it special were the amazing people who served it. A heartfelt thanks to Benita, Sabina, Salina, Sanskar, Sante, and Saurav for their warm hospitality and genuine care. They made us feel so welcome and turned our stay into a home away from home.

We would definitely love to stay here again on our next visit to Pokhara!

I am very pleased by the service especially the housekeeping who keep my room clean and the staff named Reeta Singh who was very professional and always eager to help if I need anything. Thank you very much for exceptional customer service.

I do love this place! So fun to bring my 2.5yr old daughter here. Plenty of lakeside food offerings and activities. The locals are friendly and the weather is often perfect! The only reason I give this 4 out of 5 is because of the liter. It’s much easier to take in the nature when there’s not so much human impact.
Still, highly recommended. Next time we are going kayaking!

No 1 food option in town: OR2K.
You can miss this beautiful place while looking for it. It's 10 meters inside the little market in the main part of town, lakeside. It has the most beatiful view of the lake and food-sumptuous. They also have a live band on some days. Run by an Israeli guy and his French wife... Great place don't miss it...

The place is ok. It's pretend to be a cozy hippie place, but actually not so comfortable. You sit on the floor, but not much space for legs. Food in not fantastic. Especially if you tried good israeli food before. Average level of food quality. A service is so so. They bring food randomly. So if you come with friends, some get food first and some need to wait for a while.

In perfect weather I'm sure this spot is probably the greatest thing ever but with clouds and rain there was a total whiteout and nothing to see. Ask your hotel to take you here - Takes around 40 minutes and costs a little bit but would be worth it if it is a clear day

thamel is the most touristic place in kathmandu. it is very crowded and noisy. everyone us trying to sell you something - ver anoying.
But for 1-2 days it is ok before start your trekking. nearly every hotel is placed in thamel and there are a lot of trekking shps in this area. also you can enjoy a few trinks here and meer other trekkers

The Kantipur Temple House is a perfect place to stay while in Kathmandu.  My wife and I stayed there before and after trekking and could not have been happier.  Spacious clean rooms, plenty of hot water, fabulous breakfasts, quiet outdoor sitting areas, friendly and helpful staff, drinking water you can trust, and an ecologically sensitive philosophy.  Best of all is the staff: smart, quick to humor and always willing to make our stay more enjoyable.

It’s worth the climb. The temple is really lovely to visit and you get a good view of the surrounding area.  Lots of boisterous monkeys so beware of belongings, but they are fun to watch. Plenty of opportunities to buy souvenirs at the top too if you wish and even a cafe.
Contrary to previous review it is 200 rupees for foreigners to enter.  Easy to walk from Thamel area.

This is my 3rd time staying here and it has once again lived up to expectations. 
The breakfast options are great. The coffee is excellent. The wait staff go above and beyond. As do the pool staff , reception, bellboys. 
An easy flat 10 minute walk into town. Close to everything. 
The pool area and upper viewing deck are great for views of the Annapurna mountain range. The pool isn’t heated but it’s very refreshing. 
Spa treatments are also available af a cost and quite affordable. 
Also a great carpet, shawl and scarf shop… with Numan as the salesperson you won’t be disappointed… he knows his stuff! 
Enjoy!
This is such authentic place it's a very old town lots of shops to help the people who live here & a insight to how they live a place to visited

We stayed a couple of nights here and would recommend it. The room was a good size, clean and well appointed. The grounds were nicely laid out and the hotel is close to the lake. We ate in the restaurant one night and the food was excellent. Breakfast was good and the staff very friendly and helpful. We asked about hiring a taxi for an afternoon to visit a friend out of town and they hired us their hotel car and driver for less than I expected the taxi to be!

I had a wonderful stay at Temple Tree. The overall experience was great. The ambiance was relaxing, and the service was exceptional. The staff were incredibly warm and helpful throughout my stay. Special thanks to Bibek dai and Krishna dai for serving the best drinks  they really made the evenings even better! Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a comfortable and welcoming stay.

Durbar square used to be so beautiful, unfortunately the earthquake took a huge toll and destroyed majority of the buildings. Yet the entrance fee to the rubble is still 1000 rupees. It would be more reasonable to waive the fee and have donation box there, as many people would prefer to donate than to feel being ripped off.

Feels like my second home in thamel. Come here by online and now ended as like a family. All the staff were friendly and location is the best part. I enjoyed everymoments here. I am very happy to have such a nice place on recent visit. Definitely the right place to be in Kathmandu

The lake is part of Pokhara. You can stroll past many restaurants and bars along the lakeside parallel to the main shopping street . Also at night local people have small stalls selling food.
We walked around the lake in an easterly direction passing fields and local villages for about 6-8 kilometres.The road is dirt in parts and very dusty especially when cars, trucks or buses pass by. We went as far as a "peninsula " jutting out into the lake where a lot of the para gliders land. I am told that a bit further on is a suspension bridge over the river. 
We also walked out of town along the lake in the opposite direction, eventually crossing a small stream before going over a suspension bridge below which the locals do their washing. We did not venture further but you could follow forest trails from this point. An old sign warned to go trekking in larger groups and not to carry valuables. 
The lake itself is pretty and you can hire boats from several points around the shore and cross the lake to then follow forest trails.

This is my 4th time to Nepal and I had eaten at this fun, quirky place on 2 of my previous visits. I was so excited to show my spouse and friend this sweet little restaurant. This time however it took forever for our indifferent server to come, then another long long time for our food to arrive. Two of us were long done before the third meal arrived. I am sorry to say even the food was disappointing!

We stayed here for a couple days after our arrival to Nepal. The building is beautifully maintained and full of amazing architectural features. It's convenient to many things while being set just a bit away on a quiet street. The garden was an unexpected but very welcome relief after the dusty chaotic streets of Kathmandu. The restaurant was delicious at every meal we ate there (which was several - it was convenient, reasonably priced and very tasty) and the staff friendly. Some minor downsides... The bathroom is a little dated and the beds/pillows are mediocre. All in all, no real complaints and we would definitely stay here again.

Before heading to the airport, my colleague and I walked to this UNESCO World Heritage site, which is currently under renovation due to the damage it suffered from the earthquake of a few years ago.

The journey to the area was as interesting as the square itself. Once you get to the square, there will be shrines and temples of different sizes to admire.

The hotel's gardens are a lovely spot to enjoy the tasty buffet breakfast or a coffee from the espresso bar. The rooms let the hotel down a little as they are quite tired and in need of modernisation. Great central location in Thamel, and the surrounding area is now traffic-free which makes an evening stroll possible without dodging motorbikes and being honked at!
Water front resort was nice view . services  was good specially name is sabina and saline . Good was good . location was nice  perfect  very peac full

We spent a night in Sarangkot. Compared to Nagarkot, Sarangkot appeared more crowded and there are a lot of hotels and more are sprouting up.

When we were there, the sky was cloudy and foggy so we couldn't see a clear view of Annapurna Range.
It was an interesting place to visit, but without knowing what you are looking at it could be a very average visit.
The boatmen were rude before we boarded the boat. But once on the boat, our boatman was very nice. Recommended!

If you are looking for a beautiful Hotel with very polite staff and lovely rooms which take you away from the hussle of Kathmandu and you don't mind paying similar prices to Western Hotels - then this place is perfect. We booked this Hotel for when we returned from our trek; thinking that we would like a little more comfort and fuss after roughing it. It was very nice. However we felt that reserved and quiet nature of the staff and the other guests seemed a little uninteresting after our exciting trekk and the other guest houses we stayed in Kathmandu; I suppose we got used to lots of travellor talk and staff interaction. We felt this was lacking at the Temple. But if you are not looking for this - Kantipur will suit you and you will not be disapointed. Warning - the shower takes between 5 - 10 minutes to warm up in Winter - a bit of a waste of water.  And as other reviews have said - the rooms are very dark - which means you use a lot of lights to see anything. Eco friendly doesn't seem to be working in these two cases.

The Waterfront Resort Hotel came through in a pinch to accommodate my stay a few weeks ago.  The rooms are a good size but could use a refresh.  Must say one of the best things about my stay there was one of the young bellman - Santosh.  His greeting when I arrived, lovely hellos every time I bumped into him, and his very genuine "hope to see you again" when I left - wanted me to stay longer at the hotel.  I hope the Waterfront senior management recognize and tap into this young man's energy, people skills and dedication to the hotel and do what they can to keep / train him up.
Great place to experience, relaxing environment to just stroll around and take in the Nepalese people and culture.

Thamel is the most busy section of the entire city of Kathmandu. We stayed there for two days. This place is full of shops and stores of different things starting fromNepali handcrafts to Kashmiri wollen things to Tibetan store for Tibetan arts, books and crafts. No shortage of foods/drinks. 

Most importantly beautiful, innocent and friendly people of the oldest hilly town.
Comfortable stay and lovely staffs. Good food making my mood good.  Good location and clean environment. Overall great stay.

It is a must visit place for those who wish to know the history of the Himalayan range, its glaciers, people living in Nepal and their culture, other high mountains of the world and knowledge about mountaineering equipment etc. very informative and interesting. Needs at least 1.5 hours to go through all the information presented in an interesting way.
The best place to spend your "alone time". The sunset was amazing and the sunrise was superb. The minimum one hour trip into the lake is worth it.

The resort is nice and quiet but the pools unheated so not usable from Nov to Feb unless you come from the Arctic. The grounds are well maintained and the staff courteous but the rooms are small and showing its age. WiFi is unstable.

For $105 / night BB plan it is expensive for Nepal or may be my expectations were high. With all different taxes a local beer costs   Npr 800 or $8 approx. 

Overall I felt I overpaid for what I got, and Pokharas got heaps of options in the same hotel category.

I wish I could say this hotel was great but sadly it wasn’t.
Location is good, up a quiet lane and away from all the hustle and bustle of busy lakeside and only a short walk to everything.
The pool is also a welcome feature especially for the kids.
But what usually makes a great stay is the staff and they were terrible here.  No real welcome despite there being 12 of us arriving for a few nights.  We got scowled at, no smiles and when you asked for some advice etc you felt like it was an inconvenience. 
Our rooms which were right out the back, presumably because we had kids, were a bit dingy and the bathrooms very dated.
Would like to say I’d be back especially for the pool but probably wouldn’t stay here again.
No word ...I love the places.....it's peace city....for fun .....for identifying your self.....I love my journey

Kathmandu is my most favourite city in this world that is very close to my heart. I know this place so well that I can walk around this city blind-folded. I decided to stay at Kathmandu Guest House the last time I visited Kathmandu. I made online booking through their website for my stay here. It is a beautiful property and used to be very popular among leading Hollywood celebrities. But my experience wasn't the greatest. I was disappointed that the room was smelling very bad and had mouldy walls. Then later at midnight I woke up with cockroaches crawling over my head. I walked to the reception and asked to speak to the duty manager. I expressed my concern and manager insisted that I was making up my story. He then went back to his office saying it's not his problem. After few minutes he returned and told me that he is willing to offer me an upgraded room. I was disappointed with his initial reaction therefore I requested for a refund. He said I have to deal with my credit card company. Credit card company said the hotel must process refund at their end since they had already charged the card. I was so disappointed that I left from this hotel at 2 am same night. I received email from the hotel after my follow up that the refund isn't possible because it was my choice to leave the hotel. An extremely disappointed customer!

Its quite complicated to write about this resort/hotel. 1st, they receive you quite warmly and after you finish your welcome drink, they will guide you to your room. For newcomers, they always want to Ditch with the "Problematic Rooms". These problematic rooms as per told by a Reception guy secretly, you wont get mobile signals, No Wifi signals, No view, etc. And when you Speak a bit louder about this unfairness, they will try to compensate you. Very strange attitude !!! Food quality is ok. Reception staff seems unhappy with their jobs, Hence always Rude and unwelcoming at later stage. They wont even respond to your issues. The reception staff and other lower staff always try to hid the issues from Hotel Management. But once you have access (I strongly advise to get in touch with hotel manager), they get screwed too. The pool facility is nice if you get the chance of having access to its CLEAN water because mostly its occupied and urinated. Bar near pool is the most appealing one. The waiters are cooperative and the food quality is better than room service. Overall, The hotel management need to look into their Reception staff rude attitude, train them or kick them out.

We were taken here as part of the tour we were on, great place loads of history & great views looking over the city but look out for the monkeys they will try & go in your bag or try & take sunglasses

The lady in the reception was not good or cooperative. If you ask to see your friends or clients to that guest house they would not tell you that you are there to see her/ him. you must contact with your own channel.

I recently spent a month in Nepal. During that time I did a trip of a lifetime that included a 17 day trek to Everest Base Camp followed with three days of down time relaxing at the Pokhara Lakeside  Resort. Whilst the trek was outstanding the three days was spent in sunny tropical weather.  The property has a great vista overlooking the lake and was a welcome relaxing time. 
My room was clean, comfortable, and everything thing I expected. The food was very good and the breakfast plentiful. I spent a lot of time at the pool just relaxing with my feet up and the service for food and beverage was friendly and quick.  The staff arranged a day out on the Zip Flyer which was thrilling and a must do! There was an airport shuttle which made it very convenient.  
As a former Hotel Manager I can say I was impressed with the hotel, their facilities, great staff, F&B, and location. No hesitation in recommending this property.

First impressions are great, nice outside area, with bar, pool, and tables to eat at. The planting is well done and presented well. The staff are attentive and keen to please. 

The rooms are ok, nothing exciting but clean and comfortable. A bedside table both sides would be nice. 

However there is a major issue. The one thing that a hotel is about is sleeping. The sound insulation between the rooms is not good, you can hear other rooms switching lights on/off, toilets flushing, showers and people walking around. 

Also while having the pool and bar outside they are located near the rooms and the hotel should have a policy that guests are at least quieter after say 10pm as loud noisy guests disturbed my sleep until around midnight. 

Also breakfast is a buffet type thing which was ok but nothing special. However when the breakfast room is busy there simply isn’t enough room and the process of getting some food is a bit of a pushing a shoving affair. 

Overall if this was a 3 star hotel I would have given the review 5 stars but as this is a 5 star hotel I feel the review can only be be 3.

I have been in Nepal for a month now and had a hard time finding good proper green salads. This place exceeded my expectations! To be honest, I didn't have any) Goat cheese salad was great, and then iced coffee and sachlab - apparently, Israeli traditional dessert, were great too. Chilled ambience, sweet waiters, highly recommend it
One of the most reliable and best place to stayby in kathmandu while travelling in nepal. Recommend hotel trekkers home for nice stay.
It was a pleasant stay throughout and the staff were quite friendly, polite and diligent …overall the service was outstanding.

Sara Kota is the most popular place to view sunrise in Pokhara. It is not the sunrising which is important, but the rays hitting which is the most important. In clear days you can have the panoramic view of whole Annapurna range which you cherish in your lifetime.
One morning during our trip I was able to capture this heavenly sunrise on The Annapurna Circuit.  The morning was freezing cold but the view was breathtaking. Totally worth it.

We rent a wooden boat with driver.. a bit boring trip and you can't move that much once you stepped in to the boat. It will shake easily and unbalance. The driver can't speak English that well and didn't give brief explanation about Phewa lake.

It was very good. I liked it so much there were some small shops & many restaurants near by,
it was a really good experience. it’s so pretty.  You can get cuisines from all over the world. We even had some bubble tea in Himalayan bubble tea, it was excellent.

This was my least favourite site in Kathmandu. Got shouted at repeatedly by officials because you have to pay to enter, and this was while standing in the one spot trying to work out what you could see and whether we wanted to pay. Couldn't even stand at the perimeter of the paid area. I felt unwanted unless I had money. We left and visited one of the nearby rooftop cafes and spent out money there.

Our daughter had visited OR2K in Kathmandu and while we were in Pokhara with her we saw that there was one here as well.  We enjoyed the OR2K combo platter which was a delicious combination of dips and and various flavored hummus with naan and other bread.  The service was a little slow, but the food was delicious. We had sat down next to a wonderful couple that we enjoyed some good conversation with while we enjoyed the view of Fewa Lake.

First of all if a/c and/or a TV is important to you look somewhere else as neither are provided. But that's exactly what I like about here, it's a step back in time. 2 electric fans are provided, I found 1 was sufficient fitting my stay in September when it was about 23C outside. I had a courtyard view room and it was very quiet, even with the window open. The rooms are quite dark unless you have the main ceiling light on. Staff are very friendly and helpful and my only complaint is that while in days of old a lattice window meant you could see out but no one could see in doesn't work with a light on in the room. People can see in with the light on. The bathroom needs a light on and the shower is directly in front of the lattice window.
 The breakfast is about $10 for a buffet
Phewa Lake is a freshwater lake in Pokhara Valley. You have to take a return boat ride to visit the Barahi Temple which is situated on a very small island in the lake.

We recently stayed here for 2 nights and it was a good stay.

What I liked about our stay:
- Welcome drink and cold towel at check-in
- Quick, efficient, hassle-free check-in
- The resort is extremely beautiful!
- Lots of greenery
- A picturesque swimming pool
- A cute bar by the pool
- Plenty of outdoor space
 -The traditional cottage-type setup
- Cozy room, with a pretty painting on the wall and a nice balcony overlooking the resort 
- Good options for breakfast. I liked their chocolate banana cake. The scrambled eggs I ordered were done perfectly!
- From the restaurant, I liked the mini-chicken burgers which were like sliders-the chicken patty was very juicy and yumm. 
- The cocktail from the Island Bar was pretty good too

Could be improved:
- For a resort like Temple tree, I think they can still do a better job with the food. It wasn’t bad but it wasn’t great either. 
-The sockets by the bed in our room were loose so we had trouble charging our devices. They need to be updated too.

Overall, it was a pleasant stay. We were lucky to have great weather while we were there, so the views were amazing! This resort is a good place to relax with friends and family.

Details of stay
Room type: Deluxe Room
Duration: 2 nights
Price per night: $90 (discounted price)

This place left me breathless observing the masterpieces of the woodcarving and the surrounding architecture. Even this area had been badly hit by the last earthquake, Nepalese did great job restoring it. Highly recommended place to visit

The first time we visited I was struck by the attentive staff, beautiful ambience and impressive portion sizes! The second, third, fourth and fifth times we returned I was blown away by the delicious food and drinks. OR2K is a great place to go for any meal, as they have a huge selection of vegetarian and vegan options. Everything we tried was delicious, from the pizza, to the hummus platter, to the banana lassi. I'd definitely recommend the dessert called "Kiss from Zurie" (or something along those lines) as it was amazingly decadent and delicious. Overall, we had such a great experience at this restaurant and hope to return one day!

Spent a lot of money on breakfast and they wouldn’t even give me more than a single glass of drinkable water. Absolutely poor excuse for service and even tried to add a service charge on the end which I wouldn’t pay for bad service. Bad pop music playing the whole time, bland and basic food, overpriced.

OR2K offers sweeping lake views combined with a fun, retro, 1970's decor complete with low cushion seats. A few of the young clientele look like they fit right in. Whatever the case, the generous food servings are tasty and wholesome while the service is courteous and efficient.

The misuem it self located in a beautiful area of Pokhara. The collection of mountanering stuffs and historical artifacts make this a must for pokhara specially, if you are nature lover. The view from the musuem of the himalays was...wow!

This place gets great reviews - but it's quite ordinary, badly designed standard hotel rooms, all OK, but nothing great. Impersonal staff, lots of groups using the place - not for the independent traveller. There's a pool if you want to get stared at by the punters hanging out at the bar, and the grounds are OK - but nothing special for the price!

The  best place to relax and delicious food and the hospitality is too good specially Praveen and Prem and I will recommend my family and friends in India.
Specially I enjoyed the swimming pool very neatly maintained.
Rooms are also too good as per our expectations

We did boating in fewa lake and it was very very nice,The wind and the reflection of the Himalayas in the lake is breath taking,

Thank you me Suman for a wonderful time,

A good hotel in a really good location. The food was having an Indian touch and accommodation was extreme satisfactory. In the heart of the city reachable from all important places of Kathmandu. For me it is all time fix place now

Positive side: very clean and proper.

Negative aspect: Staff trying to smash the hotel door late night (even the nails came out). We locked the door and tried to put chair in the door scared. When asked next morning for the reason they cooly replies" we thought you will leave without paying!!".

I would prefer to sleep in little less proper hotel than being scared the whole night...
Worth a visit. Sit and absorb the atmosphere.  Lots of back alleys to explore too. We enjoyed our visit.  Morning best time to go.
1000 rupies is quite much money from turists to see this place. If You have seen this before earthquakes my advice is that this is not worth of seen now. I did not like those beggers.

Its a UNISCO stie..it is well maintained by the UNISCo..world hertiage site....one can see the old histroy before 1000 years...one can see the beautful Museum...lot many Hindus God temples...with histroy...Hidnu and santan dharm is the oldest relgion..the glory of Hinduisam..one must know and watch..Beautiful..require 3-4 hours to see all the monuments in Darbar Square..
Good experience with colleague in Nepal during Breakfast and Dinner and the services of Bhandari was very helpful and i appreciate his hospitality
Unfortunetly the lake is dirty and need to be fully cleaned and protected by the government.great view from the lake, but im scared that it will be just worst and worst year by year.

Excellent Service, Very good foods. I found the staffs were very polite and hospitality was great. Rooms are very nice and i had a very good sleep during a week. Hospitality at conference hall was also wonderful.
The durbur square ihas been destroyed cause of the earthquake of 2015 but they are rebuilding it super fast.

A very nice lake, with a lot of restaurants, and a good (partly) promenade. There are boat services, one can take a boat or rent it. The pity is, that people don’t swim in this lake, I suppose, because of the pollution. All in all a good place to take a short walk.

Food is very good and restaurant staff was very humble and cooperative but hotel staff and housekeeping service was bad.  TV qas not working. AC Remote was also nit working and any extra items like water or creamer etc was declied and ask to pay.

Loyal no more.
Been enjoying KGH since 70's but no more unless changes occur.
Food and restaurant still impressive, not the accomodation.
Bed uncomfortable, bottom sheet did not cover mattress, sheet ripped in more than one place, mattress cover not attached so slightest movement made cover crinkle.
Television could not be heard let alone seen, internet did not work, and toilet did not flush.
Housekeeping spent half an hour in room fixing toilet, leaving an audible flow of water going onto bathroom floor.
Changed rooms at 10p.m. All inconvenient while getting organised for departure next morning.
Of course there are worse problems when travelling in a developing country, particularly one that has had such huge problems in recent history. However, price no longer reflects service at the KGH. There are better options available.
Did we want an airport transfer arranged at an inflated price???
"Goodbye, hope to see you again." No apology for inconvenience.
Disappointing to say the least .

location with fantastic service for the costomer.i had a great hot shower everytime. every time have a on time service especially mr.prabin(managerr)is the great guy he solve all the problem on time this is central of the thamel so you have a great time here so i recommend to all of you
Joined a national paragliding competition but i'm not there for any prize at all, fly over the mountain, along with eagles, never forget.

Spent 9 days here in between trekking, its a busy, bustling, loud, dusty Tourist trap. Try and get away from the insane tourist prices by following some of the back streets. There's the Top Town Bakery 50 rupees for a Pepsi or Mountain Dew, 300 rupees and we were kitted out for 2 days worth of pasties, croissants and sweet bread, there's the little pharmacy just down the road from the bakery to buy your diamox or antibiotics, the fruit and veg seller all in a little square within Thamel but without the tourist prices.
Thamel is an area where you can walk to Durbar Square, Monkey Temple, Garden of Dreams, Kings Palace.
A popular tourist spot in Kathmandu with many temples, city views and close observation of monkey lifes than any zoo.

Walking through the streets to get there is wonderful. Lots of strange things, lots of people, motorbikes and a few cars to watch out for. Still suffering earthquake damage, one can still experience the amazing place it is. Close to cafes, sit on lounges and peek out over the street. Great experience.

Well i could not experience fully but i got to taste food and drinks, it was really good. I hope i would visit the place again someday and experience exclusive services.
Thankyou for you service.

We stayed here twice during our trekking holiday to Nepal, the beginning and the end of the trip. The hotel is located in the heart of Thamel and a great spot for restaurants and shopping but to get anywhere in Katmandu is a nightmare because of the traffic, including the airport.
Our first stay was after a 24 hour day and all we wanted was to eat and sleep, it took us 12 hours to get hand towels despite asking several times. We were just about to leave on our next leg at 06.00 in the morning and the receptionist said I had not paid my bill, which I had the previous night and my receipt was in a very rammed backpack. Over the two days we came to the conclusion that the management was poorly organised.
Second stay was at the end of our trek and we needed to get some lunch, soup with homemade bread, a wrap for me with french fries. The soup turned up with two manky slices of white bread and my fries were uncooked, my wife asked for the homemade bread and the waiter turned up with a small sweet bun. The fuss that followed was incredible for an international hotel, didn't ever get any bread or cooked chips. They are charging top dollar here and I can tell you we had better food on our trek in places with poor facilities. How you can call yourself a chef and not be able to coordinate some potatoes is beyond me, the manager didn't seem able or willing to sort it out. Suggest eat out, breakfast is average but adequate.

If you visit Nepal will be a must to stay in a hotel with local Architecture, design, beatutiful decoration that will ggive  the local taste and feeling of being in Nepal that you cannot get if you stay in modern city style hotel. I traveled to Kathmandu, Nepal recently (April '23) and boy, was I impressed with my stay at Kantipur Temple House! Staying at the hotel for two days, its location was a great jumping point for an exploration of the heart of the city (the famous Durbar Square is nearby). An eco-friendly hotel that focuses on reducing energy costs by using no AC or central heating, the climate in the hotel posed no problem for sleeping as the weather in the city was (and is) quite temperate throughout the day and night. The hotel also uses safe, reusable products that don't hurt the environment (local products only and no plastic bottles).

With an ancient, rustic look, this hotel was built to resemble a Nepali temple. One almost feels it could be a temple, or some ancient building that was recently converted into a hotel, but no, the building was in fact built only twenty-three years ago! Such charm it has.

I believe that with the rooftop yoga sessions, the clean mineral water and masala chai, the warm and friendly staff, and the delicious breakfasts, one can easily reconnect with their inner self and expand their peace of mind. Definitely a go-to place if you want a relaxing and invigorating stay in the city of Kathmandu with your friends and family. Thank you, Kantipur Temple House!

...I would say that the astonishing view over the city is the prime one. Others include the beauty of the temple at the top; watching the monkeys playing and frolicking; working off all those momos on the steep walk up.

It still has a wonderful authentic Nepalese style and feel which we loved but they were doing a lot of construction work in the center courtyard which was unfortunate. That work was only done during the day which wasn’t an issue for us because we were out exploring anyway. They provide free drinking water and refill your containers upon request in an effort to reduce the number of plastic water bottles destroying the environment. Kudos to them for that! No air conditioning was a down side though because we had difficulty sleeping one night due to the heat. They provide fans but they are very noisy and detract from the zen vibe they have going on. Room was clean but a bit dark which wasn’t an issue for us. The food at the restaurant was excellent and the staff really went out of their way to make sure we were looked after well. Overall a good stay for the start of our trip. I would recommend it for those that are looking for an authentic Nepali vibe in a great location with top notch staff.

Beautiful Experience. The staff is very Hospitable. Manish really took care of us. The food was excellent . Sitting outside in the moonlight enjoying the kebabs was a different and memorable experience . One must go to the kebab Factory in Radisson Katmand

When I visited Kathmandu, one of the highlights was the Swayambunath Stupa Buddhist pilgrimage site tour. It is a vast complex that consists of a central stupa, several temples, shrines, and the enormous, mysterious Buddha eyes on top of the dome that stares over the entire valley. There were numerous guides at the site, and I did not hesitate to sign up for one to guide me around. I was informed that Swayambunath is more than an ancient religious site, but an active living one with pilgrims performing clockwise circumambulations around the stupas. The stupas are hemispherical structures, focal points for worship and meditation. I did climb the long flight of stairs, despite the monkey's erratic behaviour at every corner along the way, which most visitors found to be a pest. Still, one is rewarded once you reach the top and view the thirteen golden pinnacles that symbolise the thirteen enlightenment stages of Buddhahood.  
The four million residents in this city rub shoulders amongst the different religions and seem to abide in good spirits. A vast majority of the population is Hindu, followed by Buddhist and small followers of other faiths. Once out of the main drag the outlying districts are choked with motor vehicles, motorcycles, plenty of garbage and heavy pollution, plus cattle and stray dogs that seem to roam around at free will. Apart from the general chaos all day, the people are kind, generous and extremely hospitable. We walked around soaking the views, inhaling the incense, watching pilgrims making donations, and praying to the enlightened one. Apart from being the hopping off point for many trekkers to the Himalayas, Kathmandu is an essential cultural experience not to be missed.
