The other thing I found was that I came down for the breakfast at 8a.m and it was just about gone, I asked 3 times for toast and it was delivered to a table nearby rather then put into the buffet. The omelette tasted amazing though, don't expect much more from breakfast. Be early!!

We stayed here as a treat as it was expensive, I felt that it was standard not at all deluxe with lots of service staff expecting tips constantly which I found rather infuriating. People who did give tips. Got amazing service, the rest of us not so much.

I asked staff member to scan something to my email, she asked for money to do this which I gave and which she shoved into her handbag, felt a bit cheated as service was lacking unless you paid and paid some more!!!! 

I hate dishonesty so this is why I have rated so low. ok... (Lady in reception needs a reward though, she was what made this place get 1 star from me :)
It was a peaceful stay at this wonderful resort.  Staff are very friendly and helpful and breakfast buffet was yummy. Highly recommend this hotel in pokhara
such a good time here! went here many times while in Pokhara but the best night was on a Friday night when there was live music on, was incredible!! (also best duffle everrrrr)

The stupa is situated on the top of a hill. So, you have to climb around 60-65 stairs which is a bit hectic. The whole complex is good. However, the most enjoyable thing is that you can see the view of whole Kathmandu valley from here"

I had a decent stay at annapurna radisson on my way back from gonghrel. location is goos, quite close to the city and airport. airport shuttle is available free of charge. rooftop swimming pool on the old block alongwith sauna, steam and jacuzzi enable a good relaxation
Small town fỏr the tourist to vísit and eat where thểre are many restaurants as well ás if someone like to by some gìft.
The exhibits were pretty dull and dusty looking. The atmosphere was unfriendly. Exhibits on the outside were broken down. It was just OK.
Beautiful view of mountain range during boating excursion. STopped by an ancient temple on the way. Weather was nice and fresh. Def a must to add to anyones itinerary while at Phokara

I feel it's not worth your time for the following reasons :
- it's not within walking distance from Thamel; you have to take a taxi there
- entrance fee for foreigners is a whopping R1000 (abt US$10)
- the temple grounds are badly maintained.
- the monkeys are of the common variety, nothing special abt them

The whole lakeside is beautiful as it gets but the row boating experience was the worst we got in whole Nepal, they start counting the time just after they book the ticket at the counter and we can get on the boat only after 5-10 mins. The lady who was rowing us started to go back only after 30 mins and when we complained she started cursing us in Nepali, my mom got scared and started to cry, later we complained to the manager present there named "Sammar B Nepali" and he folded his hand and said "Aapko jo ukhadna hai ukhad lo" which means "Do what you want to, I don't give a crap". No help from the other authorities sitting over there, pathetic as it gets, these guys are scamming and looting in open, had the old lady gone more angry she could have thrown us from the boat, please avoid the row boating near Aarti ghat in front of Tal Barahi temple. And someone launch a complaint against the manager "Sammar B Nepali" if anyone can, thanks.

If I'm honest, my friends and I expected more for our last couple days relaxing after trekking.
The hotel was indeed good, staff were polite etc. But the food was a bit of a let down at the prices they commanded and I feel we stayed in two other hotels that were at least as good for far less (in Kathmandhu & Nagarkot). The pool is the only difference in reality. I'm sure many people love it here but it was not exactly to my taste.
The service is very good. The location is good too. The daughter loved it. The breakfast was also good. Room feels like a little bit small

The food was tasty here and the atmosphere very relaxing and chilled out. The best part of the evening though was watching the sunset across the lake from where we were sitting. A great place all round
you can have a ride of this lake, nice and beautiful lake. you can take self pedal boat of with driver.
Well located in thamel. Service was great and friendly staff. Liked the food , but not for those who like the ethnic spicy taste of nepali taste...

Terrible service in sesame restaurant in hyatt regency, they only catered the buffet customers but did not cater other customers very well. The food was only 5 on 10. Very bad service. I would not recommend visiting the restaurant. Initially they said food was available later after an hour they said not available. Terrible restaurant for fine dining

Hello Greeting to everyone, from my point of view and that i like most in  kathmandu durbar square and my recommondation do not miss to some place.
the first one is The Living God of Nepal Kurmari, who lives in Kathmandu durbar square at kumari bahal house so you should not miss.
Secondly, the muesum, you can find the historical and cultural collection from the ancient period time 
please do visit

Don't get me wrong, it's impressive and, behind the scaffolding, you can just about make out some of the grand temples, but the whole place is chaotic. There is a fairly expensive fee to pay, yet you can quite easily walk right past the booth, in fact, you could easily miss it. There are also dozens of persistent street hawkers trying to part you with your cash. A little deflated leaving here.

I came here on my first night of my visit to Kathmandu and it quickly became my regular thing.  Whenever i wanted to absorb the vibrant life of the i walked here and spent hours looking around and buying what ever caught my eye.  you can nearly anything you  will need for your visit or trek.  The people were friendly and not pushy to make you feel welcome.  I always felt safe walking around the streets of Kathmandu and instantly felt a deep attachment to Thamel and Kathmandu. Visited in November 2016.

If you like watching the sunrise, or a bunch of folks jump off hills on a parachute; Sarangkot is your preferred destination. The place is about an hour and a half drive from Pokhara and sits atop beautiful hills overlooking the city and the lakes. On a clear day, mountains too are visible. Recommended for a visit if you like taking pictures of mountains in sunrise but are too lazy (or feel too cold) to trek to the base camp.

You really can get lost walking around all the streets here, but you will keep on bumping into sights to keep your camera busy, Kathmandu and Durber Sq area does not fail to deliver, the smells, the sights, the shops, the spices, utterly mesmerising.
Thamel is very busy. Don't forget to wear mask, because of the dust and pollution. Trekking gears are available throughout Thamel. Wide variety of restaurants, drinks, etc.
Polluted water and hazy sky, barely saw the mountains once, and I was there for ten days. It's a good break from Kathmandu craziness though

O dear! Thamel is just to much. Here are some good restaurants and you can do some shopping. Its sort of a must see when in KTM but I havent stayed here for long - ok for dayvisits or hooking up with friends.

I visited this site as part of a City Tour of Kathmandu.
Whilst you pay to enter the site you can explore all of it.
The highlights include the monkeys on the site which give this site the common name "Monkey Temple".
The whole site is very interesting. Impressive stupas and prayer flags. Good variety of shops around site.

A "Must See" location on a visit to Kathmandu.
Highly Recommended.

- Building design is very long lasting
- Warm welcome of shown for hospitality
- Food was very good
- Staffs are very helpful

Two girl of frontdesk Sajana and Kriti are amazing and another gentleman suman . I also take pictures with them.
Some point of view about cultural, about death and live, about people, about you, can be made you a big supprises.

Excellent hotel, rooms are very good value for money. The staff are really friendly and professional, they couldnt do enough for me during my stay. Its also in a great location, close to the resturants and shops. Id definitely recommend it.

Very nice hotel in thamel  location was perfect.the staff are very friendly and helpful.Manager Mr.Ranjeet amazing person he was helped me everything about trip of city . Room is very nice and clean I really like trekker home

This hotel can only be defined as "pretentious". It claims to belong to the top league but it's sad, dark and far too expensive for what it offers. Rooms and bathrooms are very cold and with little natural light allowed in. Common areas are practically inexistent. 90 $ for a so called deluxe room is frankly far too much
If you love ancient culture, this place will be a must to visit. Make sure you go alone to be able to contemplate all the surroundings that this place has.

We stayed here twice in between treks and found the location great and outdoor gardens excellent but that was where it ended.
Both rooms were very small with hardly any room to turn around in or store any luggage.
We paid $80AUD per night with no breakfast for a three star and only had power and heating intermittently, the decor in the rooms was dated and worn and the shower sprayed water everywhere across the bathroom soaking all areas.
We have stayed in other hotels in Thamel for a quarter of this price with better rooms and breakfast and would not stay here again.
This hotel is not good value for what they are charging if compared to others in the area.

If you are really into climbing then you will enjoy the visit much mor. The movie was nice and worth entering. The best part is the second floor with the big windows to the beautiful mountains view. Not sure it's worth the 400 Rp. entry fee.

After a yoga class at Mudra I stopped for coffee and breakfast at OR2K. All the positive reviews are correct. The coffee was delicious, and the Oasis smoothie bowl was a refreshing break from the carb heavy breakfasts I ate while trekking. The views from the cafe over the lake made for a peaceful morning. Definitely recommend everyone have at least one meal here!

The service was fantastic, every people was very nice and we has all their help in every time.
Very good location because we could go walking to every where in the city. 
The room was confortable and clean and people was very very helpful with all our needes.
And the best was the staff at the reception, restaurant, etc.!!!
It’s a quick visit, there are stairs as well as a road the leads up. A huge stupa and a couple of temples around it. Its a good place to visit.
I Found Swayambhunath temple is listed in the world heritage and this is also called ed as monkey temple. its a very enjoying place. we have to climb on the top and is situated at the top of hill.
Fine place, great view on the lake. Food is normal, not perfect, but if you want to eat, yes, there is not a problem.

For the fee they are charging I was expecting a lot more. The place is in shambles! Absolutely disgusting. They should be ashamed of how much they are charging tourists and what they have done to their own national heritage. They think tourist are walking ATMs whiles their own people walk around and litter everywhere. Would skip this place and Kathmandu in general.
This site is a bit overpriced for the condition of the attractions, however, the earthquake recovery is possibly only with tourist dollars, so think of it as an investment in history.

Beautiful newari architecture, very clean rooms. Wonderful garden. dramric lighting in the evening.

We stayed in one of the superior rooms (the better value rooms were all booked) which we feel are overpriced compared to the general price/quality range that is usually found in Nepal. 
The breakfast bill comes on top of the room price and does not reflect the value of such a bland meal.
The taxi that the hotel had organised charged us double the usual fare to the airport. The staff new this but ignored it.
The dump site next to the Kantipur Temple House should be removed as this does not add to the experience of arriving at the Hotel.

Very disappointed from the time we landed. They took so long to fill in the forms. Then the AC was not working. No mini fridge in the room.they said they'd repair the AC and kept disturbing us in the room from 3 until after 7p.m were still waiting and hoping they'd give us another room
Great and best place in public area visited nice place clear water enjoyable and happy moment .......

Really loved some of the chef Pradhan made dishes like beet root naan where we haven’t seen anywhere. Nice hospitality
Pleasant stay .
Great food & good service. We are vegetarian so we loved this place. Plenty of food on the plate so you can share if you're not a big eater.

Nice place to visit. You will definitely LOVE this place. Lot’s of Monkeys and hence called Monkey temple. Don’t carry water or Coke bottles. These monkeys will snatch it away in a Jiffy. We saw it 
really happening and a funny memorable experience.

Donâ??t even bother to book a room here itâ??s only name nothing of hyatt standards rooms stinks bed are broken and too low for comfort attitude of staff as bad as hardware.
They are famous as they claim to be biggest but donâ??t go by name stay at lesser known hotel rather staying here
If you planning to visit Nepal, this is the place you should stopover before you go other part of the country.. the most busy place and convenience for anything you need ..

One of the best place to meet friends and get tasty food. It is pure vegetarian restaurant with great chief from Israel. Amazingly to get european service in the center of Himalayan. Delicious dishes with the greatest view to the lake, cozy pillows and good service make this restaurant on of the top list in Pokhara.

Amazing lake, still waters on a clear sunny day and very peaceful and serene even on a cloudy day. Magnificent views of the hills and glimpse of the mountains when skies are clear. Hire a boat to the stupa or the temple or self paddle for a relaxing scenic time. Definitely not to be missed.

Kathmandu guest house has a great location at the heart of Thamel. Darbarmarg is just a few minutes walk from the hotel. Amenities are moderate, not bad for the rent I had paid. There are a number of restaurants around. Although surroundig areas festure nightlife, the hotel itself appeared family friendly.
The place has awesome views and the food is amazing. Go with time because the lunch takes time since you ordered but you will enjoy it a lot and you feel really full 😃
Beautiful place , you can spend the whole day just watching the beautiful view. Nice lake side shacks serving cold beer and tasty food

You cannot miss this lake when visiting Pokhara. There is a sort of boardwalk (Peace Foot Track) which you can use, and it'll take you past many bars and cafés. On a sunny day the many colourful boats will give it an extra take-a-picture-of-me level. During the day it can become hot, and some locals open their small businesses at the shore. You'll even stumble across Disneyland here :)

Was here for a conference enjoyed the facilities and services, used rear door entrance as well to sneak through locals. Impressed with service and foods, nice walking tracks as well, enjoyed the masala tea, reception wad good too  would visit again

OR2K is a nice place, with good vegetarian food that is reasonably priced. Having said that, they should up their game when it comes to the service. There is more than enough staff around, yet it can take ages before they take your order, bring you the bill,... This is mainly because they seem to be pre-occupied with chilling at the frontdesk and checking their cellphones, rather than keeping an eye on their guests. 
If you are not in a hurry, I'd recommend the place nonetheless.

All comments agree this hotel is excellent located, it has beautiful peaceful grounds and acceptable service.
Even though Price and Service is not the best opportunity cost, it is ok when you think in resting from all the noise and people outside (just crossing the door)

This place was not in our itinerary still we made it a point to visit thinking that it'll be good. I would say that it was an intuition which turned out to be great

Lot of details inside which will educate and inspire you. Right from the different expeditions, mountain people, mountain gear and above all rare photographs

Loved the details about the first Everest summit . The building is situated in a large compound which itself gives great photo opportunities
It wasn't that nice what I had expected. It was okay and nice to see but I wouldn't go there again. Place was clean and there were lot of monkeys.
This place is a sacred one for me.I felt the lost connection with myself accompanied by music playing ( Om Mani Padme Hium ).I would like to go the Swayambhunath Temple again.

Great location in Thamel, beautiful architecture of the building, nice and relaxing garden. However, our room was very dark and showering a bit difficult due to the way the shower system is built. As it was often the case for us in Nepal, there were extra charges to pay on the room price, on the food price and for paying with the credit card.

In Kathmandu thus is one of the must see attractions. If you are a Buddhist or Hinduism is your religion: do visit this temple. Even if you are not religious it is also a great point of interest in Kathmandu.

Food so nice, we ate there twice! Really insanely delicious platters (Turkish and OR2K platters). Very relaxed vibe and comfortable setting. An easy place to go for healthy and yummy food. Also great to spend time there chilling/relaxing with great views.

This museum has a lot to look at. It is quite remarkable what has been achieved with some of the more rudimentary climbing equipment compared to what is available to the modern day climber particularly in lightweight hi-tech modern clothing.
There is a short video that is definitely worth watching. Some of the photos of the worlds tallest mountains are just amazing. This is a good place to slow down and take it all in
Room and food service was excellent staffs were attentive for all needs and or actions needed while staying here. Staffs constantly have smile and eager to help from all members of staffs

We came here after having an awesome experience in pokhara. We were a bit disappointed, food was no where near as high quality as the pokhara location. The seating area wasn't as nice either. Still a decent feed, but left us wanting more.

This would have been an amazing place in its het day. So many beautiful carvings and buildings etc. It is a real shame that the place is just in such a mess though, i could not see that any thought must go into looking after what is already there leave alone carrying out an efficient restoration of what is damaged. Worth a visit if you don't mind the downside.
If you have an interest in mountains and particularly the Himalayas this is a great place to visit in Pokhara . Lots of interesting things to see and to read about . Definitely recommend

Recently my wife and I returned from a wonderful trip to Kathmandu Nepal. We stay for three nights at the Kantipur Temple House and I would highly recommend it. It was very clean. The hotel staff was super helpful. We ate breakfast each morning in the hotel and one of our evening meals there as well. The food was delicious and delightfully served. The location is excellent with the ability to walk to many nearby restaurants. There is an ATM 50 feet from the hotel. We met the charming owner and have attached a photo of the three of us. The hotel provided the name of an excellent tour guide and set up all the arrangements. I highly recommend the Kantipur Temple House for you stay in Kathmandu.

Yum. Was in Pokara for 4 days and visited three times. The food was fresh and there were so many options. I felt safe eating salads and other fresh options. The atmosphere was relaxed and I loved the low seating on cushions with low tables. I had Middle East and far east dishes. It was all good
It's just ok. Not much at the top, not even a cafe to sit at. You can only see Kathmandu on a clear day which is rare. Disappointing.

Stayed in the newly constructed part of the hotel. View was good with very good breakfast. Staff very caring and hospitable. Terrace garden caffe is goid for evening coffee or dinner. Adjoining area is full of shops and restaurants. Main hotel lobby is good for meetings or gatherings where one can order drinks and snacks etc. Ask for a higher level room for a better view.

Great atmosphere, great food and good service. You have to take off your shoes before entering the restaurant, not troublesome but not really a fan of it. So make sure your feet doesn't smell if you're planning to go to this restaurant.

This hotel is a friendly and calm oasis in the midst of the busy lakeside region. The staff is very welcoming and accommodating. Laxmi helped us plan our outings and arranged for a driver and a knowledgeable guide. The breakfast is lovely and the pool provided a welcome relief after walking all around town. I highly recommend this place. The entire staff goes out of their way to make sure that you have everything you need.

The lake is nice once you get away from the shore. The water was pretty clean. My friend and I rented a dunga (sp?) for a half-day for less than 1,000 rupees. It's a great way to spend an afternoon and escape the heat of the city.

The location is ideal, as everybody knows. The charm of the surroundings is better, since the renovations following the 2015 earthquake. The rooms are still good, and overpriced - again, for such an institution as KGH this is ok. HOWEVER, I found the service has dropped in quality. We were a big group coming in dribs and drabs, from our trek. Most of us did not have towels and even anything from the bathroom kit (soap, shampoo, facetowels etc) in the room. When this was pointed out to the reception, instead of sorting the problem, they put us on to call Houskeeping (which rang out, no reply). Only after ringing Reception a couple more times and starting to express deep dissapointment, finally, towels arrived but they took a long time, even then. It was the Senior Manager's day off, admittedly, but that should not be an excuse for KGH. I hope they lift their game, else I might look elsewhere next time.

Unfortunately it was clouded over so the views were poor. This is quite a hike after you have been dropped off by taxi. I can see that on a clear day the views would be stupendous but we were there at the end of the monsoon season.
I like Israeli and Arab tastes, so I can recommend this place. Try their Hoummus, Moussaka and coffee.

Definitely a “don’t miss” attraction in Kathmandu. Very photogenic. A guide can explain a lot and is very useful for taking photos ( especially if traveling solo), but if you just want  to see it, and are not interest in Hindu and Buddhist stories, then you could do it by yourself. Persistent hawkers will follow you trying to sell necklaces and bracelets, etc, for thee to four times the items actual value, but you can pick an acceptable price and stick to it, and they will either give in or leave you alone.
Very informative places greate photos and interesting history about climbers. Highly recommend to visit specially trekkers and climbers.

This is the area of peaks and hills from where you take off for paragliding. We were told that the point from where we took off was 1650 meters. It was mostly rocks, stones, grass with moderately steep slopes. From there we can get a magnificent view of Pokhara down below. We reached there through winding potholes narrow roads. Interesting experience.
nice to just walk around and no- one is bothering you about guiding you. Just greeting you and offering tea. Nice, quite and relaxing square in the middle of a busy neighbourhood.

Absolutely exquisite accommodation with the most courteous and friendly staff always ready to go above and beyond to meet the unexpected needs. The Fun Cafe serves delicious meals with something for everyone.
Can’t wait to come back!!

There is Lakeside streetside and Lakeside lakeside. When you follow the footpath along the lake you will enjoy many things. 
Relaxed and always great views. Mountains, Lake, peace pagoda. 
Nice little bars to eat a small meal or snack. 
Just walk, sit, and breath it all in....
amazing place for paragliding. it is unique in that you glide over the vast fewa lake located in the steep hills of the Himalayas. thrill and ecstasy doing paragliding here.
The food is pretty good. I've eaten there many times but the problem is at the end when you pay. One of their cashiers tends to give you wrong change. They're constantly trying to shortchange you.

If you are visiting Kathmandu and not visiting Thamel, your journey is incomplete. Thamel is a Mustique place. It narrow lanes are enchanting. Restaurants provide world food, no matter from which country you cime, they have a plate for you. Budget hotels and gust houses abound. Whatever be your budget, Thamel will embrace you. You have visited Goa, Amsterdam, Bangkok, now enjoy the nightlife in Thamel. You will not be disappointed. Pubs and bars with or without music - all your choice. With or without live performances, entirely your choice. Sex is illegal but pimps abound. If you are ready to fork out some penny, you will certainly get your choice. Spa and massage parlours is there in every alternate house - a great relief for trekkers when they come back tired. What else you need. You need to be in Kathmandu, you need to be in Thamel.

Thamel hosts many shops mostly appealing to tourists with fake hiking gears but some are of good quality and reliable at fraction of originals. However, cars, motorcycles, bicycles and jeeps alike shares the same narrow pavements which are dusty too.

Rooms and garden sitting area ate the only things that I Like about this hotel. Have stayed here few times with my groups. Once I was given ground floor room, it was old room n noisy due to activities happening outside. Curtains were very thin so No proper privacy. On day 2 of stay the Air con in my room fell off n was hanging.. Management fixed it but again in evening it fell off. Staff is not at all friendly else their room cleaning staff. You can't sit at peace in garden at times, the waiters from restaurant keep coming n keep asking u to have coffee... Very forceful in this matter.. No doubt they r located in heart of Thamel n easily accessible to anywhere u wanna go but it's not d best.. I gave 3* only for their rooms in new wings which r really nice.

The hotel is great. The downfall that i experienced this time is the set up of breakfast buffet. The management i think must keep the area hygienic with or without covid. 
I saw plenty of guest standing next to the food corner having their food in the same area using their hands and take more food holding the serving spoon with the same hands. 
I think hotel staff must notify the guest to have their food in the table as a courtesy to the other guest. The hotel must also be proactive in cleaning up the excess food and sauce that is all around the serving area.

-allocated a dark and gloomy room over looking staff quarters
-room and bathroom very old and not that clean 
-woken in the very early hours by staff activity & pigeon noise
-moved to a slightly better room after complaining
-replacement room not fantastic
-regret not impressed with this hotel - there are much better options closeby
-it appears to be living on a past good reputation - which has not been maintained
-certainly does not match details & comfort portrayed on website
-good points=nice garden if you need that and some staff are friendly
-I was in and out of Kathmandu a few times during my trekking & wanted to use this hotel as my ‘base’
-regret, one stay was enough
-NOT RECOMMENDED

Disappointing. That's pretty much what you can say
After having looked at the reviews and photos I thought Waterfront was a quality hotel
My first night was a nightmare - the aircon machines outside of the window on the balcony were loud like if someone was running full engine. When I asked o be moved it took them ages to come, next room they showed me had the same problem. The second was seemingly quiet. Little I realized the aircon turns every 10 minutes with a loud boom sound. Next day I said I need this sorted out and I requested either change or fixing. They said they did although I was suspicious cause it only took them 10 minutes. We they likely turned the aircon on and off. Overall the staff looked bored and uninterested in any service. All they were interested is your money and Namaste. When I said that as a gesture they should at least take care of my dinner bill (which was seriously disappointing - I didn't know you could actually screw up palak paneer but you can) they said they couldn't cause it was already billed. 

On top you need to remember: you will be overbilled for everything (taxi, sports etc) because of the name - the hotel is considered upscale and far so your foreign face gets you even bigger premium. There is no proper road there so the taxi drivers claim its difficult to drive. 

Fundamentally the place look good only on the photos. Do not expect any actual service

We were shocked at the price to get in.. the ticket booth just to enter this area charged us 1000 nrp. The area was under a lot of construction and we didn't feel that the experience was fulfilling despite the beautiful bits which there still was!

When you're charging the average guest 3-4x more than the surrounding hotels, you would expect a different level of customer service.  Unfortunately, this wasn't the case at Temple Tree Resort.  Upon entering, the front desk was very curt, and a representative of the spa handed us menus (with no prices), while a woman whisked us away to our room.  When we got to our room, we thought it would be a good idea to head to the spa for deep tissue massages.  At 4,000 rupees ($40usd), which is VERY $ for Nepal, you would expect a semi decent ambiance & treatment, but this wasn't the case for either one of us.  In fact, it was the WORST MASSAGE/SPA experience of my entire life.  The room was freezing, there were people speaking loudly, and the masseuse had no idea what she was doing.  After that, I realized that my wifi in my room wasn't working, so I went down to the front desk, where the man said because of the location of my room, this is often a problem, but I can stand outside if I'd like.  Um, it's 5c outside... are you kidding me? then he suggested I just stay in the lobby the entire time...really? only after seeing my expression did he offer to change my room.  We then asked for a cab to town, and they told us we can walk.  When we insisted on a cab, they huffed and puffed and finally the man at the front desk called one (which arrived 30min later).  They just didn't want to be bothered, or maybe I caught them on a bad weekend? beats me! The only (I mean, ONLY) reason I'm giving it an average rating, is because the only people that got it right were the restaurant staff! they were attentive, professional, kind, and all around great! the mixologist, Puskar, and the waiter, Deeojyoti were hilarious, kind, and inviting.  So much so, that we ended up going back 3x in 24hrs! I suggest they move those two to the front desk :) oh, & try the Guava Chili drink! YUM

Thamel is a tourist area for a reason. Good food and good shopping. I always have fun walking around seeing all the small shops. My favorites are the painting shops! Definitely a place to explore for tourists.

We stayed at theTemple Resort and Spa for 2 nights.   The hotel is quiet & clean although the roads leading to the hotel might make you a bit wary.  But once you enter the hotel you tend to forget the outside world.  The hotel rooms are cozy and clean. The toilet was perfect, had everything you need minus the bathrobes.  My room view was gorgeous, I could see the greenery surrounding the resort which is well maintained. Staff are warm and friendly.  An area of disappointment was that we had asked to be woken up around 7AM however the wake-up call only came at 8AM! An hour late. The wi-fi wasn't particularly great as well but I guess that's the case anywhere in Pokhara.  I was disappointed by the quality of the food.  We had Breakfast & Dinner at the hotel and it was nothing to brag about it.  Even the dessert wasn't satisfying!  Because of this I wouldn't mind trying another hotel if I were to visit Pokhara again.
Went to Kathmandu, Nepal for the 2nd time. But this time around decided to hang around. Discovered Thamel. Fun place, good place, bargain like crazy and have an amazing experience
Nice place to visit if you are interested in Nepalese culture and history. It has been damaged heavily during recent earthquake.

This was the first DurbarSquare we visited and it was highly disappointing. It was expensive for entry which was basically a flood of people walking in with a security guard stopping and charging any Western looking people. The site itself was still heavily damaged from the 2015 earthquake and local homeless people were sleeping all over the monuments some even urinating on them so it was not the nicest of views or smells. 

The museum was a building site very unofficial and dangerous and all the info was about the recent earthquake not the actual buildings. 
I’ve heard better things about the other Durbar Squares so hopefully they won’t be as underwhelming as this one. I suggest you save your time and money and do something else in Kathmandu.

Friends of ours have stayed here and liked it, but maybe they visited in a warmer month or in a better room.  To start, the hotel promised to pick us up from our night arrival at the airport, but never did.  So we took a taxi.  The hotel was completely dark - we fumbled our way to the check-in where we didn't even get an apology for not being met at the airport (although when we spoke to the manager next day, he did refund us the taxi cost).  Our room had a single very dimly lit bulb near the front door - the light didn't extend to the washroom, so we blindly unpacked and tried to sleep.  It was very cold, but the hot water bottles they gave us helped a bit.

Visiting Sarangkot was an amazing experience, but a little preparation is key. Here are some tips that really helped me:
•	Leave by 4:45 AM and aim to reach by 5:30 AM. This gives you enough time to climb the stairs and find a good spot to watch the sunrise over the mountains.
•	Before you go, check if stars are visible. Only head up on clear mornings, otherwise you might not get the sunrise view Sarangkot is famous for.
•	Tell your driver to take you to the upper viewpoint (next to where the stairs start). From there, it’s about a 10-minute climb. There are lots of coffee and souvenir shops around the stairs.
•	One view shows, the mountain range catches the first sunlight and the sunrise is beautiful, One more angle of view where you see the sun clearly like a red ball.
•	You can see stunning views of the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges, and Manaslu too.
•	There are toilets available at the site, which is convenient for early morning travelers.
Highly recommend starting early, checking for stars, and asking for the upper viewpoint for the best experience. Enjoy Sarangkot!
