I guess is cool to see it and offers good nightlifes wiht bars and restaurants but to it wasn't interesting at all.

There was so much earthquake damage here and it is still being repaired. When we went there were only about three temples or palaces you could visit inside although there are dozens in the area. A lot are hidden by scaffolding or even tarpaulins and even when you get inside only one courtyard is open. The temple of the Kumari (living goddess) is certainly worth a visit as it is in a better state than most with lovely wood carving and if you get to see her it will be a special memory.

You have to pay even to walk through the square and you shouldn't miss doing it. Just think of it as a donation to reconstruction.
amazing temple at a great height. great specimen of art and architecture. you need to climb up 200 steps to reach the stupa. a must visit place.

The complex is still so damaged from the earthquake... it’s heart breaking to see. But it is still really beautiful and worth the look, the small donation to enter goes to support the rebuilding effort that is evident all around as you explore. Well worth time time, is a bit far from Thamel central so do yourself a favor and take a rickshaw! Such fun. Tip well your rickshaw drivers!

Thamel is the hot spot for tourist. You will find everything here. Budget to luxury hotels, restaurants, bakery, cafe, pub, dancefloor, shopping center, movie theatre and what not. 

Though the roads are narrow but it is full of local and foreign lives. 

Tip: dont get puzzled with the booking/agoda pictures. Hover some hotels (all are mostly nearby), bargain, check room and hot water…..then lock your stay.

Entrance is $2. During our visit there were many locals and Hindoes and Boeddhists who were truly executing their religion. So nice to see this and be a part of it. Everyone walking, talking, ... in peace. The monkeys are ok, they didn't searched for any attention. Many tourist shops around the stupa.

We checked into the hotel tonight (room 41). The hotel grounds and property seem very nice and the staff is friendly. Unfortunately the room is not as great. The beds are very hard. Hotel staff came and added a comforter or something, but it’s still very firm and I’m worried I won’t sleep well. Also the shower water was hardly coming out of the shower head when we took a shower. They sent someone to fix that and it was fixed. Also the air conditioner is making noises occasionally and blowing pieces of black stuff onto the bed. They came and messed around with the AC and picked off the pieces of stuff from the bed but then they left and it’s still doing it. For a “fancy” hotel, I am surprised that we have to deal with all of this. We are suppose to stay here the whole week and just did the long drive from Kathmandu and we were really excited to get to the hotel, but now just disappointed that we didn’t book a cheaper hotel. I will update this review at the end of our stay if anything changes.
Very difficult road up to Sarangkot, especially at 5am, but well worth it for sunrise over Annapurna

I had a conference to a attend in Kathmandu at hotel Radisson and was booked to stay at the same hotel.
I landed at the Tribhuvan international airport at 20.45 hours and reached the hotel in 20 minutes .
The checkin was smooth.
The room was spacious and the bed comfortable.
the bathroom is a little tiny especially;;y the shower area . There is a  rainwater shower and a handheld shower but the water flow is not good - seemed to alternate between hot and cold water all three days.
The staff are helpful.
The dinner at the Terrace on the 4th floor under the open sky with heaters was good.
The breakfast spread at the coffee shop was adequate with live counters for eggs, paratha and dosa.
The check out was smooth as well.
The good part was the airport transfers were taken care of by the hotel.

I was in Pokhara with a group of students (been bringing students to Nepal since 2007). We have our 'go'to' restaurants but we try a couple new ones each trip. OR2K will definately be one of our 'go to' restaurants from now on. Most of the group were not vegetarians but everyone found something they enjoyed. The people there were friendly and the restaurant itself had a relaxed and friendly vibe. I had the mushroom paneer choila and loved it. Much of the seating is on cushions of the floor, which is what we did, but they also have tables with chairs.
It was awesome fantastic time service was great theme is great marbolious and food were delicious the peace is also nice along with stunning view
As I heard it does not remain the same as it was earlier. It was more impactful before the Nepal earthquake.

You come to Nepal to see the ancient architecture and the Mountains.  So of coarse Nepal has a Museum displaying information about the Mountains of Nepal and the mountain climbers and equipment used to climb the mountains.   Very informative displays in a multi-story museum building.
Once you are done seeing the museum exhibits, you can go outside and be amazed by the views of the mountains that are in the background of the Museum - very stunning views!

Rooms are VERY comfortable—we have stayed in the newer front part of the hotel many times and absolutely never have been disappointed!  Spotless rooms, prompt and pleasant service, EXCELLENT breakfast with good variety, made to order omelettes, Indian, Nepali, western selections.  We have eaten in two restaurants in the main building, Olive Garden for Italian and The Fun Cafe, very happily for dinners.
It’s very convenient to work out in the main building with weights, spa/sauna, and a nice treadmill room overlooking the city to the north.  Hotel is convenient to Thamel, Asan, Pashupatinah, city center.
Price-wise I wouldn’t consider this hotel a deal, but actually a pretty good value for high-end experience!  Highly recommend you stay here in Kathmandu!

The food at OR2K is definitely above average for Kathmandu. I have been here 5-7 times and had the chance to try dishes from all over the menu. 

Overall, OR2K is doing a good job of hitting the flavors they are going for. Some of the ingredients they are using, like the cheeses, elevate the price. I think with all of the awesome farmer-artisans making cheeses, etc. in Kathmandu, many of the restaurants will (hopefully) transition to using local ingredients that will both help cut costs and pass the savings along to their customers, while supporting local business!

Hummus is pretty good, although the naan they serve alongside it is always hard, stale, and cold. If they could make that fresh, the experience would be a lot better!

Pizza is nice, as is their version of the cheese pie, which has a yummy crust.

I did have a salad here with a huge roach sitting in the middle, initially hidden beneath some lettuce with only its antennae sticking out, which I first thought were human hair and just planned to pick out and let be (that's totally normal for dining in Nepal and I have gotten used to it after 4+ years here). However, when I realized it was a roach, I wondered how they could have properly cleaned the lettuce and not noticed it. Since this is not "local" dining, but caters to tourists, I did point the roach out to my waiter and was not charged for the salad.

good environment, clean room . 
food is good, family friendly , pool is beautiful, good service , kind staff .
overall good place
Quite interesting. Plenty of photos. Some great 3D models of the Himalaya. Lots of detail for people who are really fascinated by mountain regions and mountaineering.

A beautiful sensitive environment for the traveler who cares about the world. We arrived tired and exhausted from two weeks visiting the beautiful but tough terrain of rural Nepal. We were greeted by the warmest and friendliest of staff and shown to our really comfortable and restful rooms.  The bathroom was perfect with plenty of hot water. We enjoyed yoga on the rooftop each morning and after four days our flexibility had certainly improved. Breakfast and evening meals were delicious. We enjoyed the best Dal Bhat since arriving in Nepal. The best aspect of this hotel apart from the beautiful atmosphere was definitely the warmth and kindness of the staff., nothing was too much trouble. We enjoyed every bit of our stay and will certainly come back.
Loved going to this venue!! The sitting on the floor, gives it a relaxed home feeling... and the food is incredible!!!

I spent 3 days in Pokhara, and did the touristy things. Of all the things I saw, the lakes, the sunrise and this museum stands out. The waterfalls are OK - I have seen better ones in India. The caves are OK - but caves in say, Shillong, India, are better. The Museum is wonderful if you are into technicalities of mountaineering and history. If you aren't that type, you will get bored. I just loved it. Budget at least an hour to do justice to the museum

This place's mostly sites are damaged during the 2015 earthquake. What is left is the good to see. Great architecture of wooden work. At the front of Entrance you will see Makhan Mahadev Temple. After entering you will see a big statue of a lord, I forgot the name of that. Around the Darbar Square you can see the big market where from you can buy the everything in the reasonable prices (you must know how to bargain). Overall good place to visit.

This is the main lake in Pokhara and is 2.5 miles long and width 8.5 miles wide. average depth is 28 feet. I went for a boat ride on it. It is very scenic with colourful flowers, green hills and sparkling white of the Annapurna mountains

Very well organized museum. It covers extensive mountain ranges of the world with detailed maps & photos of those who hv been able to conquer. Showcases of Sherp's who hv sacrificed their lives as well as the tools used to climb these majestic mountains. If time permits its an interesting museum to visit.

I wouldn’t swim in there as it’s not very clean unless you have an amazing immune system. It’s the key reason to come to Pokhara which has much cleaner air than Kathmandu or even the dusty paths of the Everest trail. Pokhara whisper it quietly though is a little boring after a few days.  Stone me if you must

Very nice resort with cozy environment, we could see the lake from our room. There was a staff named Binita , she is so nice! All the staff members were really helpful. They even gave us a small farewell treat at our last breakfast. Loved staying there!

We spend two night in this hotel. Hotel is old and needed a bit of maintenance in the bathrooms. Need to improve cleanness. Wi-Fi you can only receive network, can not open even Facebook. Finding hotel is too difficult, specially if you go by taxi.
It was a wonderful visit during the most difficult time for Nepal, but the visit feels like a family visit... coming home filled with live and warmth.
Worth a drive to the top (or a long hike) to see the sunrise or sunset. If the clouds are gone you will have an unrestricted view of fishtail and the Annapurna massif.

Magical. No other word can more aptly describe what I witnessed today morning at Sarangkot Pokhara. The sunrise over the Annapurna ranges is absolutely magical and mesmerised me.

Annapurna Cable car starts at 4.45 am (i hv heard). I bought ticket at 5.30 am. Takes 10 mins to reach the top and further 5-10 mins walk to reach the vieweing point (there are many, farther up the better).

Reach the vieweing spot 15 mins before the official sunrise time.

It may be cloudy in the valley but due to its height sarangkot may still have clear views.

Probably one of the best spot in Kathmandu to get your hiking equipment before trekking. Also, there are plenty of variety of restaurants to choose from. 

Asian, Western, Fusion, Italian, Fast Food and everything. 

Souvenirs, handicrafts, clothes, shawl and everything under one roof.

Plenty of shops to get souvenir and ebc gears. All at good bargain. Lots of dining options too. I bought a down jacket at only npr2000 and quality is good. Money changers are aplenty. Road is very dusty so it's good to wear a mask.

Resting atop a hilltop overlooking Kathmandu Valley, Swayambhunath Temple is a sacred Buddhist site with holy stupas, shrines, and monkeys. Climb the stairway lined with prayer wheels and stone carvings to reach the main stupa, which is said to be over 2,000 years old. Take in panoramic views of the valley as you walk around the complex. The peaceful atmosphere fosters introspection and spiritual contemplation. The temple delivers a tranquil sanctuary from Kathmandu's bustling streets. Swayambhunath is a must-visit for a glimpse into Nepal's Buddhist heritage.
This is the lake  about far from city, but worth the visit for the beautiful view around the lake. I liked this one more than the city lake. The boating is not crowded.

As we all know Pokhara a must visit Destination in Nepal and I've no words to explain the beauty of Sarangkot. Woke up at 4am in the morning and went to see the sunrise the view of the Annapurna Range and the sun rising above it was a unforgettable experience of my life.

Very pleasant Hotel in the middle of Thamel. Spacious rooms, very clean and a superb room service. Nice restaurant with various delightful dishes. Despite busy Kathmandu city it is a very quiet hotel. We enjoyed our stay very much. Every wish we uttered was fulfilled hardly that we told it. Reception was most helpful to find places we were looking for. In addition to that it’s a hotel trying to work without plastic in regard to our environment. And that for some 20 years now, not just recently due to present discussions. All in all thank you for 10 days of luxury and joy.

i would like to say that. if you planing to book this property on the name of Hyatt. then dont do this. its spoil your day. Not good atmosphere very old property and rooms and beds look like 1star felicity.

THIS is what I had come to Nepal to see, mountain scenery at its best.
I wasn't disappointed as I stumbled to put clothing on after a very early call at my hotel.
We then bumped and bobbled our way up narrow rough roads to a parking spot below the view point before getting out and slowly climbing our way up on foot past little shops, people's homes and little hotels.
There was more climbing when we reached the viewpoint to clamber up staircases to the very pinnacle of the site at Sarangkot.
My reward for all this effort was to be the first person there, my guide quickly grabbing two chairs to give us the best position to see dawn come up over the Annapurna range.
To start with there was little to see in the darkness, just a hit of dawn to come and a vast sprinkling of lights dotted about way below us.
The light began to strengthen and the range peaks were picked out in early sunshine while we far below were still largely in darkness.
Eventually we turned slightly to our right and the first twinkle of the rising sun sent spear of light over the foothills and more distant ranges, the sun getting stronger and stronger in a breathtaking display of scenic beauty.
Far over there were vast banks of fluffy cloud or mist, but the mountains were clear as a bell and the sunshine slowly crept up towards us in a brilliant range of colours.
This was an unforgettable experience, something I will never forget, and I would strongly urge anyone staying in Pokhara to make sure they book themselves on to a mountain dawn sightseeing trip for some stunning memories.
Great way to start your day, fresh everthing!! and excellent service...Allthoough a little pricey, nice treat before and after trekking

Overall, the hotel is quite comfortable, with a full range of amenities,  and in a good location. However, their security was extremely slow to respond to a security incident at the hotel, leaving my colleagues and me feeling unsafe.

A small lake of two by four kilometres. There is a walking path along the lake which provides an enjoyable walk around the whole lake. The lake provides boating activity. Along the lakeside are several restaurants which serve food and drink with good music and a lakeside view. On a clear day the reflection of the Annapurna mountain ranges can be seen in the still water  of the lake. The access to the lake is open day and night but the lighting through the road access is very poor. It might be advisable to use the access through the marketplace where there a small roads between restaurants leading to the lake.
Impressive and in a very vivid neighbourhood (kind of hidden, though large venue). Small entrance fee to foreigners, but worth it.

Look I know it's a wonderful spot. And definitely come here for sunrise to see the mountains. But it's crazy crazy busy and you will struggle to see the view. Get there early otherwise you will get stuck in traffic and need to walk up the mountain.
This museum is quite unique to me. It is quite informative about the Himalaya mountain and climbers from many places. I also learnt that there are many tribes in Nepal. Interesting.
Unfortunately lots of damage happened during the earthquake.  They are putting in lots of effort to  restructure it as soon as possible.  Right now it's not in a condition to be considered.
Tourist area to grab souvenir, singing bowls and eat some Momo's. Also all the hiking gear can be found and bought here !

Clean, great location at the center of Thamel  excellent staff: helpful, kind especially Sagar Pandey. I stayed around 7 days there and felt very welcome in a place far away from home.Hotel also have their restaurant in the first floor they serve the delicious food.The breakfast was so delicious.I enjoy the from the rooftop garden of the hotel.The hotel have great facilities like hot water 24hours and super fast internet.

nice hotel and staff but tranquility spa sucks, they have no sense of hygiene at all, i left an expression on the bill no one bothered to ctc 
what a waste of money 
the best part of the stay was from the house keeping, the girl was too good, she took care of all my needs

This is a great accommodation.  The room was great.  The location was perfect.  The staff was outstanding.  The food in the restaurant was very adequate.  They have a really nice pool.  I will stay here next time I'm in town.

It was very busy when I visited as it was "Diwali" . The room was comfortable, the food good, and service good. I think it would have been better when it wasn't so busy. The views are worth seeing, and worth the journey.

Admission 1,000r. The 2015 earthquake damaged a substantial number of buildings in Kathmandu’s Durbar Square, and although the buildings have been made safe, and many covered and protected from the elements, restoration work is barely evident.
You can visit the home of Kumari, the Living Goddess and may even see her at prescribed times, but it is not allowed to photograph her.
Hopefully a large part of the admission fee goes towards the ongoing restoration.

Kirtipur Temple House was the first place I stayed in Kathmandu and it was a wonderful place. I was picked up from the airport, which made my travels less stressful. My flight was very late and staff were still there to meet me hours later. This hotel is beautiful with intricate wood work and a nice outdoor garden. It’s quiet at night and was very relaxing after a day out in Kathmandu. The food was better then any food in the surrounding area. The head chief was friendly and accommodating. I was spoiled with local food he made. The staff are friendly and most importantly nice people who are easy to communicate with. I felt safe here and would stay again if I was to take a vacation here.

A nice restaurant with european styale food . Waiter was very kind and helpfull ..           
Just you can visit ones time in this restaurant ...you never forget that's service then good food ..

When researching my trip to Nepal I saw so many people speaking about Thamel and saying it’s the best place to stay. I have come to find that these people are liars. The locals just haggle you, scam you and try to sell you hash. Go to Pokhara instead, it’s far more relaxed and you can enjoy the local culture without being scammed or pestered.

We passed this viewpoint both on our way to and our return from our three night trekking adventure. On the way out, the views back to Pokhara were wonderful, but on the way back the skies were full of pesky paragliders.

Woke up early to catch sunrise but it was very hazy. Unable to see anything. Wasted money and disappointed 
Make sure check the weather before going up

Went to have dinner here during our visit. We were told by them that they serve indian veg food. But when we went, their menu only had 2 veg dishes....one paneer and one dry potato. Had to order both these. The food was not good. Did not enjoy at all. Were greatly disappointed.

I loved the ethos of this eco hotel. No plastic water bottles or bin liners, no air conditioning which was not missed, we still slept comfortably. The hotel is constructed in with traditional materials and has beautiful reclaimed windows and wooden beams.
It is peaceful and cool, has a great included breakfast and the staff were lovely and very helpful. We will be back.

I'm sorry to say but this is by no means a 3* hotel. There are 2 sections to the hotel new and old.  I can only speak for the old  - here goes we spent 3 nights in this hotel located in the heart of Thamel, The garden area is nice and relaxing but as far as any other amenities that is about it!  We first arrived and was to have 2 garden facing rooms, we were given rooms on the first floor.  The old section has no elevator so if you are upstairs you need to climb with your luggage (which I guess is ok if you are a backpacker!)  We arrived at our rooms to find that the first room for my sons was not a garden room.  The floors are very uneven and the room had not been cleaned.  The next room had a balcony overlooking the garden but no windows to the garden.    The old towels hadn't been changed from the last customer.  There was no sink in the bathroom you had to use the sink in the little kitchenette area.  I personally went to the front desk 4 times to ask for towels and finally the gentleman behind the counter asked me to go to housekeeping myself.  Needless to say the very next day they didn't change the towels again and did not put any toilet paper in there either!.  The room was never dusted (and trust me Kathmandu in February is dusty!!) only the bed was made.  The manager really had nothing to say about the poor service and was not willing to change the price even though they gave us the wrong room type.  My sons room had no hot water and even if it did it didn't matter as there was no water pressure.  This was not the case for just my rooms either; as I asked several of the guests in the same section and their response was worse.  I generally do not like to complain on these reviews but the only redeeming quality was the fact it is in the middle of Thamel which makes it easy to shop and eat. I am not a 5* resort person either but expect for $95 a night per room a lot more than this!! I generally put off negative reviews  saying it is someone looking for nothing but please take this seriously - this is not a hotel for anyone!!

It was nice feeling at pokhara,specially while you are in lakeside with panoramic view of Fewa lake however still could be better just keep it neat and clean all the side of lake to attract the peoples.

This was also one of my choices when I was in Kathmandu. And it did not disappoint me at all. But if you don't like monkeys I suggest that you do not go for this. Though, to see Kathmandu from a short distance of your hotel which is usually in Thamel, it's great. Loved it.

As a vegeterian couple, we're used to having to compromise somewhat where variety is concerned. OR2K was such a surprise and delight as they have a very extensive, multi-ethnic, vegetarian and even vegan menu. We tried a couple of other places in town, but we kept coming back here again and again. This became our virtual kitchen table and we tried a lot of things on the menu. my favorites were the Falafel, Antipasti Salad, Vegetable Sizzler, and Mint Lemonade. Nice coffee bar. Good prices on beer, wine, and mixed drinks too. All served in a cozy, bohemian atmosphere with kind, attentive staff. Offering movie nights too! Highly recommended.

Mahesh, Rajesh, Ramhari and Rubak, they really take good care of their guests and infact helped me a lot through out my 7-8 days of stay👍👍  Will definitely recommend this hotel as well and i am coming next week again, and i’ll be glad to see them again

Lovely lake but soo polluted you can not take a swim :( 

Plastic plastic plastic garbage everywhere and the water is brown. Very sad to see this. 

Other than that beautiful lake and boats. Barn but nice stroll along the lake

No matter how beautiful your property, if the service fails, you fail. And sadly the service at Lakeside does not live up to the standard that one would expect from such a well-appointed hotel.

There is lots of good: the hotel is an oasis of calm, the property and gardens are well-maintained, the décor is tasteful and the rooms and public areas spotlessly clean. The pool needs a special mention - you could spend hours just lounging here, especially after a few weeks of strenuous trekking.

On arrival the staff were marvellous - there was no problem with the early check-in and the formalities were taken care of in a friendly and efficient manner. 

But then the staff must have run out of steam, because from there on it seemed that they were constantly understaffed and/or overworked. Small things start to grate then, such as the overall chaos at breakfast on both mornings, waiting in vain for the complimentary snack that was supposed to be served with my drink, 5 staff members staring at me as I drag my bags to the car after check-out without lifting a finger to help or even saying goodbye.

Yes, it's a beautiful hotel and probably one of the best in Pokhara, but Nepal is known for it's friendly people. So next time I might compromise on the standard of the hotel and choose for the standard of the staff. I guess it depends on what your priorities are.

Getting around Kathmandu is a challenge but it is worth walking ….   Durbar Square is such fun!  If you have a guide who can fill you in on the history that is best!
Seeing the young Goddess is rather special!

Pros - nice pool and close to airport.  Good bars at the pool and the lobby terrace.

Cons - with the exception of Rosheen's help, the hotel's front office administration is terrible. Arrangements confirmed in advance by email were ignored. Arrangements made/confirmed at front desk were forgotten or incorrect.

The rest of the staff in the hotel were friendly and keen to help (especially the bell hops/ luggage and transport desk)

Some of the rooms are extremely noisy - low numbered rooms near the lift are subject to the constant banging of the corridor door from 05:00 as guests head out for early am tours, so no need to set your alarm.

On one stay the room had plenty of towels and toiletries. On the second stay it felt like rationing had been imposed on these items.

Pool area was great with a nice bar.  Changing rooms were shabby with lots of used towels dumped throughout, and with the shower gel and shampoo dispensers empty.

You probably won't need to use the gym if, like us and several other guests, your key cards don't work, as you'll be going to and from the front desk to get new ones - our keys stopped working 5 times in 2 days.

Despite the friendly staff, this hotel was a disappointment given the brand and the cost.

This place was recommended by a friend who has stayed here some time ago. The gardens and reception look fine so I signed in. They offer 2 levels of room at 40 or 80 USD a night. I opted for the cheaper as there are many local hotels available for less. The room was small and it smelled of damp. There is no sound insulation at all - no need to add to that! The bed was uncomfortable, and the breakfast was poor. Biggest surprise was the seeming lack of interest from the staff. For example there were 4 staff members at breakfast who stood in  group chatting. When I asked for coffee, the coffee pot stand was pointed out to me and the chatting resumed.
There was one exception, and I can't remember his name, but he went out of his way to help me find the Phat Kath bar - and when I still couldn't find it he took me there. Just great! Shame he was the exception rather than the rule.
Everything was perfect food was good the breakfast time should be exceed by 10:30 9:30 is too early for us. The service was good the staffs are coperative and kind
Awesome place to chill out with the Love one. Spent 10 hours boating on lake really miss that time. You will feel like heaven when you have a chilled beer and a partner on boat.

This hotel looks flashy; nice reception area, gardens, uniformed staff etc. But the rooms are standard KTM fare; tiny, shower over toilet, no heating, no kettle or tea and power cuts most of the time. We were going to stay longer, but we figured out we could get an equally small nasty room across the street for a third of the price.
We also had a bad experience with staff; we assumed that for the price our room would include breakfast, so we ate the buffet, then were told we would have to pay the exorbitant rate. We said, fine, we'll pay on check out, but were then chased back to our room by a staff member demanding cash payment on the spot.

Not really sure what there is to see here, there are some market stalls that all sell the same thing and nothing different to what you would find at any generic shop in Thamel and there are some nice buildings but most are under construction.

We checked out Durban Square on a recent trip to Kathmandu. Many amazing buildings and temples. Unfortunately it was hit hard by the earthquakes in 2014(?) so many of the buildings are damaged. There was a lot of reconstruction/restoration work going on which was promising. Definitely worth was stop if in Kathmandu.

I stayed here twice during my trip to Nepal - once before and once after my trek.

The first time I stayed in the older part of the hotel - and the second I had a room in the newer part of the hotel.  They were quite different in quality, comfort and amenity.

The older room was less spacious.  The bed was okay, but not great, and the shower was over the bath...

The newer room was far more spacious, far more comfortable and the bathroom far more functional.

In terms of location, it is probably okay for business travelers, but not particularly good if you are in Kathmandu as a tourist / traveler - unless you are with a tour group on a bus...when I imagine location doesn't really matter as much.

Stayed at this hotel for three night whilst visiting Kathmandu.
Good, comfortable hotel with nice breakfast, just as you would expect from the Radisson chain.
It was our 40th wedding anniversary whilst we were there and the hotel kindly decorated our room and brought us a cake and fruit. 
Kathmandu is an amazing city, all be it that they are still recovering from the earthquake of 2015 but there are still some wonderful places to visit.
Sadly the cities roads and pavements are not to western standards and there is a lot of litter and rubbish in the streets which needs to be addressed before the year of Nepal in 2020.
My top tip would be get in a taxi and venture out to the old capital of Bhaktapur. Its fabulous temples have not been damaged by the earthquake as much as Kathmandu's, it's much cleaner and full of mystic charm.

As in the title, this hotel is in a great location in Thamel, more toward the central city area which is less than 10 mins walk. There are plenty of shops and eateries in this more touristy area. The twin room we had was also very reasonably priced. That said, the room was very damp (we were offered a different room), had little natural light (great for a lie in!) and all round just OK. Very friendly and helpful staff on all occasions.
The hotel was very comfortable and well-designed. The room had everything needed for a nice stay. I didn’t use the pool but it looked amazing.

A beautiful place to roam around and explore. The central place for an old empire where you can find old temples and buildings . Mostly wooden and stone . It suddenly seems you are time traveling . Some of the temples are closed though due to the earthquake damages. Strongly suggest patan darbar square also.

This place is supposed to have a relaxed atmosphere. All sitting is on the floor. We visited for lunch as we had fond memories from year before.
This time it was difficult to place order as servers were running around and no time to look at you. After we managed to order our dishes, we were one dish and that too cold. Couldnt protest as server was not visible. The second dish never arrived...

Well, this is a beautiful, beautiful lake in Pokhara. I must say that I fell in love with it instantaneously. It’s nice, clean and well maintained. There’s an island temple of Lord Ganesha and Goddess Durga in this lake. Serene is the word for that place. So peaceful and beautiful. You could even buy fish food and feed the fish in the lake around this temple complex! Must visit if you’re in Pokhara!
Good views, boat ride OK but nothing extra-special. Lakeside itself has one or two reasonable restaurants but is somewhat touristified.
You can't miss Fewa lake when you visit Pokhra. Though it lost its earlier charm but still a great attraction of the city. Enjoy a boat ride or sitting on banks of it.

I had great time at trekkers home while travelling in nepal. I come as guest and ended like a member of family. Definatley i have had wounderful experience at trekkers home. I booked city tours here and everything was fine. Centrally located in the heart of thamel walkable distance to the everything you need for trekking.

As the rebuilding after earthquake going slow it’s so dusty and noisy. 

Hopefully they will make this place nice again .

Climbing up to Sarangkot is a good training before a trek! The landscape around is visible as much as the Annapurnas when the sky is open (which seldom happens in this season); when it's good weather, you are just stuck!
A beautiful lake in the heart and center of the town. Many trail nearly. I planned on staying here 2 days which turned into a week

As soon as you come to this place, they will ask you for tickets, while you are just trying to figure out things...if you don't have the tickets they will ask you to get lost. I understand there are rules and one should buy tickets...I am ok with it...but the management here shud buy some manners and hospitality classes with this money for their staff

Stayed there for two nights snd took two rooms. Only positive thing about this place is that room is clean and you get a lake view from balcony. Apart from that:
1. Between the lake and the resort is a garbage dump with a drain.
2. To add to this they have a sewage treetment plant right on their lawn. The air is filled with sewer smell as expected.
3. Their travel desk guy is ready to con you by every chance. Will make you pay 3000 for a bost ride of 800.
4. You might get lectured by their staff on not wasting food from time yo time.

There is a general lack of sense of hospitality in Hotel in nepal and be ready to be fooled and conned on every instance. This resort is just part of that nexus.

Avoid at all cost

Stayed for 5 days for a conference.  Facilities were good although the hotel is ageing a little and it can be seen and felt in the room.  Room itself standard comforts although housekeeping was excellent.  Food at the conference and in the restaurants was amazing in terms of selection, quality and taste.  Missed tasting more Nepali options but there was a wide variety of cuisines to choose from.  Staff were excellent, well-trained and polite.
This place is supercrowded and the streets of thamel have loud music all over and the night life is the best ive seen in the city.
In sarangkot we can see the city and we can see sunrise if you lucky because usually so many fogs in the morning

In a privileged enclave, facing the lake, we were several times dining and each time the food and the views were better and more amazing. Dishes well harmonized in flavor and sufficient quantity even to eat between two diners. A pleasure for all the senses. Really recommendable.

I have gone to this restaurant several times since I moved to Nepal. I would normally have nothing but good things to say about it, but last night put a bad taste in my mouth (not literally - the food is awesome!). 

After I told our friends about how amazing the restaurant, food, and atmosphere was, they all wanted to go and try it out. We went as a group and was having a great time. It wasn't until we asked for them to pack up our left over food that things became very disappointing. The server told us they were "too busy to pack our food"... I asked if they could just bring the bags over for us and we could pack them ourselves, but they said it was "not possible" because of how busy they were. 

I understand they were understaffed due to the Hindu holiday that was going on, but does that really make it okay to tell a paying customer that they can't pack their food cause they don't have less than one minute to go and get a bag and bring it to the table to pack? It is not okay. 

So because they were "too busy" to help us, we had to leave our perfectly good, half eaten food on the table and walk away without being able to bring home the leftovers. 

I am definitely going to think twice about recommending this restaurant to others or at least warn people that the staff is not willing to be hospitable to their guests they have coming to eat there...

International Mountain Museum is one of the best and informative Museum of the country which can attract its visitor in cultural, historical and mountaineering parts. This museum has been carried the historical and adventured propaganda and give the educational consolidate as well.

Phewa Tal can be busy during the season. There is plenty of little bars and bar restaurants by the banks of the lake, offering beer and BBQ (many of them). I haven't seen many vegan options but if you explain you may fetch something nice.  

What I preferred more than settling in one of such bars was to walk along the whole side of the lake and settle by the water on one of the build stairs there. Towards the end of the day it was a bliss watching the sun setting down. There is a small 'Disneyland' type of patch on one side where the music plays and kids come along.  but you can still find quite places there along the lake.

Beautiful! It’s located on the top of a hill, therefore you have a nice view over the city. 
There are monkeys everywhere. The temple is amazingly beautiful. A place of faith. Just be aware of the steps, there are many to go up and down.

Lovely hotel in Kathmandu, peaceful area but close to the bustle of the city. Staff could not have been more helpful! The early morning walking tour was excellent! Our guide from the hotel was very knowledgeable and took us to places we would not have found ourselves. We will be back!

Many trade activities here: selling crafts, handmade items, ....., the items serve trekking activities 
Night life’s also so active: live music with many kinds: Rock, pop, ballad  👍

The overall experience staying in this hotel was very nice. 
The wide selection of food in the hotel restaurant was perfect.
We also enjoyed the hotel pool and gym.

Stayed here for one night before our trek. Good central location and friendly staff, decent wifi. the room was very basic which is ok for what  you pay but our toilet seat was completely broken and unusable, the water was disgusting and brown and showering made me dirty rather then clean. It was also really noisy with what sounded like staff members singing and talking loudly in the morning. We found cheaper and much nicer accommodation elsewhere in thamel so unfortunately I wouldn't recommend here.
This place needs to be on your list. Great vego food. Beautiful view from the balcony. Helpful staff.
Dhansingh Bhandari, Deb and hotel staff never hesitated to offer the most warm and comforting experience. Looking forward to staying with them again.

From the first moment I liked the Temple House style . 
Everybody gives you a warm welcome . 
Rooms are very spacious and comfortable , with a sitting corner right at the window .
Fresh water is provided at any time , plastic free !
Breakfast was very good , always fresh fruits .
We had also dinner and you can rest in the garden with a cold drink .
Every morning , there is a free walking tour , which helps to walk easely to Durbar Square etc. Question are welcome and we got a lot of advises .
Also every morning there is a free yoga class , an excellent start in your day .
But best of all are the beautiful people , which are working there for your comfort . 
It was our first time in Nepal , they give us so many advises , they organise everything ( privat car , mountain flight etc. ) . 
We can only say : Thank you so much ,would definetly choose Kantipur Temple House again !
Namaste

Its definitely worth the trek up to the Monkey Temple in Kathmandu. Not only to experience the culture/ history of this religious place, but the views are amazing, and as is in the name, there are monkeys everywhere. Was a great experience. There are locals selling gifts, and there is a restaurant at the top as well.

below average I was not very pleased when I saw that you were taking more than 30 mins to serve a thing (even for a chapati) you didn't even have the required staff and you also took more than a half of hour time to give the bill (when there were no one in the restaurant except us) it was below an average experience in the food but if I talk about the bright side the hotel was magnificent for it's beauty and the room was fine too so it's a below average review for me

This is actually a very small compound so we do feel it’s more crowded with people and animals...mind the animals (dogs, monkeys) as they are everywhere sleeping or just sitting there. There are lots of monkeys of course. Getting to the top, again encounter many crowds jostling for the same angle and view to take photos. Lots of incense burning , different Hindu idols as well makes nice walk around, but space is rather small so take care of belongings. Top level is very touristy with few shops selling the trinkets, art, etc also a coffee shop offering “rooftop view”. There’s a small entry fee as obviously they stop foreigners while we observed locals just walk straight in.

Chef Padam and team have made the awesome food and sweet were well balanced and next to perfection. 
Praises for all of them.

This is a great place to go.  Probably one of the top tourist places to go in Kathmandu.  The temple and stupa are very beautiful.  It isn't all that far outside of the city.  Cabs from Thamel area will run you about 400 rps and if you ask them they will wait for you to finish to take you back for the same price.  You can probably find a taxi to take you back, but they will wait free of charge so why not ask them?  

If you don't like monkey's then don't go here.  There are hundreds of the little things running around and are quite the nuisance.  They will try to steal things from you and get too close to you.  Just something to keep in mind.
Great place to stay to explore the natural beauty, hundreds of hotels to choose from, lots of places to eat, good base for travelling around

We went to watch the sunrise at Sarangkot and so glad that we did!
Started at 5:45 from our hotel at lakeside. It was a cold morning and our young kids were whining but seeing first Sundays hit the peak of Annapurna was completely worth it!
Highly recommend it!
Overall experience was very good....very cordial staff....,nice location ,quite place no disturbance at all
This is a pretty and wide lake. There are boat tours to take as well as boats to rent. Everyone who visits Pohkara ends up walking a part of its shores.

Hospitality is best of best in waterfront resort and the room is so nice and the environment of the outside area is very beautiful and nice view of the lake and you guys also visit once in you life in nepal pokhara and if you want to see the lake view you will stay in waterfront resort...
So my experience is soo nice and the best part of the waterfront is they have a very helpful staff and they are so sweet to us and will especially restaurant staff nabina binita haruka and Sabina this girls are lovely.

I booked 3 nights at Katmandu Guest House 6 weeks before arriving.  I arrived at the guest house at 10 PM from an international flight. My room had been cancelled, whilst I was in transit,  24 hours before arrival. The management were not sympathetic to the issue.  After a lot of demanding they finally found a room for me for the night but would not guarantee the next 2 nights.  I had to pay AGAIN at an inflated rate!!!
The rooms are sold at a premium as they have a long history in Katmandu.  But the rooms are not clean and the shower water pressure is poor. There are cheaper and better-equipped hotels in the area.
Down the street, I met another VICTIM of overbooking at Katmandu Gueast House!!!!

We chose this one for budget stay. Though we felt the price they were offering us was high for such budget hotel, but we stayed as we were too tired then. They said it will be a standard room! But I am sure, itâ??s a basic room and they charged us the price for a standard one!
We said, we will stay for 1night only and that is why we were treated like this!
The room smelled bad, it was damp and dirty, toilets were more dirty! Luckily, bed was okay. Construction work was going on inside the hotel, I hope they will renovate this room as well.

Good part is itâ??s location, itâ??s at the heart of Thamel. So many different restaurants, shops and travel agents are available there. Just 10mins walking distance from the bus stop (from where Pokhara buses start).
Popular tourist area. We found the area is convenient and have all the services you need in the area, however it is very dirty and very crowded.

Stayed in thamel at trekkers home where have access of plenty of options. Trekkers home just in the centre of the thamel and enjoyed our stay here. Thamel is nice place to stay for pre trekking arrangements.

The area has lots of ancient monuments still showing elaborate and beautifully carved woodwork. Due to the devastating earthquake of 2015, some monuments collapsed and you can see bamboo scaffolding around the Dhoka, along with images of how it will look once restored.  The ground is very uneven, so you need to watch where you walk.

Some aspects of this old temple complex have seen better times It was worth the visit, shame so much as been damaged by the earthquake. It's useful to have a guide to have a better understanding of the history.

Ok but really not worth the journey out there. Filled with school kids when I was there, so noisy as it is a big echoing space.
Sorry... exhibits are dull
So many shop and restaurants but very confused to get nice restaurant  , local people is very  kind   but littlbit  unclear place.

I have a great stay here - nice and warm staff, with great ambience and this allows me to rest well between my activities. The breakfast is really great with a lot of Nepali traditional culinary, and still a lot of options for continent or Asian breakfast 

Special thanks to the house keeping staff Ms Indira Thapa - you did excellent job in making my room tidy and cozy
Thamel has been the centre of the tourist industry in Kathmandu for over four decades. It contains numerous hotels, restaurants, and shops that cater specifically to western tourists.
Very interesting. The million resident monkeys really are fascinating. Earthquake re-building up there nearly completed in Jan 2020.

Didn't enjoy this trip. absolute waste of money. Every time I ordered tea it was super cold. One time ordered 1 cup but I was charged for two

I called at reception regarding the overcharged. they were not bothered to call back
Nice location close to shops and restaurants. Nice atmosphere inside with pool. Good breakfast choices. Overall experience, it was cosy and a nice stay with good service

I enjoyed my stay in this hotel. It is a bit rustical but very original and interesting. It has on offer super-friendly employees and a good location in Thamel on a little and quiet side street. One does not get disturbed during sleep, despite being at the heart of this lively and busy district. Every evening when I returned to my room, I received a hot water bottle, which I found very touching and thoughtful as the nights in Kathmandu can be very chilly. The hotel has a beautiful front garden and offers yoga and meditation courses in the mornings. I definetely recommend this place.

We stayed here the last few days of our trip to Nepal.  The courtyard is beautiful and so inviting, the staff friendly, however, the rooms were less than desirable.  Although the showers were hot and the beds were clean, the towels were dingy and tattered.  Wifi was spotty at best.  It met our needs, but we were ready to check out.

Don't bother buying all your trekking equipment on the UK. Arrive a day early and grab yourself s bargain. Prices are in most cases negotiable. Be polite and fair is my advice.
On Thamel you can shop til you drop, eat like a king ( so many different cuisines on offer and at different price points) and even book tours. I had all my tours booked in advance which saved me the stress.
As a single female I felt safe even in the evening. Watch out for the crazy traffic. Not a people watching spot. 
Also many supermarkets around. Smaller corner shops are not much more expensive either.

There were too many people there so you couldnt really experience the  peace up there. There are a lot of people trying to sell you something, and you need to watch where you step because of all the trash on the floor. It is not the experience I wanted... But the buildings thar were not damaged in the EQ are nice. Also, dont overpay your taxi to thamel. They tried to chare us 700 one way (the actual price is between 200-300 rs)

The famous Phewa Lake remains a beautiful natural attraction. Although the part at the lake side sometimes looses its serenity due to loud tourists, it’s still great to visit. Rent a boat, drive to the start of the Pagoda trail, climb up and down, all in all a nice day trip. You could also descent from the other side and return to Pokhara by bus, or just walk while visiting the Tibetan Refugee Center. Lot of options, including camping on top of the hills...

Having been to Bhaktapur and enjoying the magnificent Durbar Square, the Kathmandu one was such a let down. I know the earthquake in 2015 hit hard BUT having to pay 1000 rupees you expect to at least be able to go in some of the building and be blown away... you aren’t!

Good easy lounge. Lakeside is on front. Can sit in and outside. Can eat and drink lovely. Food is not special but fair price. Drinks are good and nice. Also regular special themes at evening. So definately good place to stay when wants to relax in phokara.

I will start by saying the staff is very pleasant but that’s where it stops...I got in quite late (11:30pm) and the car was not at the airport even though they said it had been arranged.  Had to take an over priced private taxi.
They stuck me in on the 5th floor walk up (even though they say they have elevators that is not true!!) literally at the dead end of the hallway...I’m not sure you can get a room that far away so that might me a good thing for future guests.  The up side is I got in a lot of steps lol.
Because I was in late (9:20am) to the buffet breakfast it was 95% gone and they said they had a full house of guests so that was the reasoning.  Though they did try to accommodate the flies made me think twice about asking for more food so I passed.  Although that can’t usually be helped at an outdoor buffet.
I’m here primarily for work so I spent the day working in the lovely private  garden until 100 teenagers showed up for their trekking event and then the WiFi went from decent to absolutely horrible.  I also ordered lunch and I did think the prices were high but wasn’t about to uproot while working.  Then I get my bill...$16 for chicken tikka, a beer and nan.  That’s more than I pay in Shanghai (top 10 most expensive places in the world).  That was because they tack on an extra 450 for service and tax which isn’t explained when ordering.  
Then to round out the stay the we’re confused about how much I owed, took so long to figure out that I had to miss the breakfast again and jump in the car back to the airport.  Thank god I only stayed 2 nights!  Will be going back to my regular spot next time!  Too big and too impersonal for my taste in a very hospitable city.  But maybe I just had a streak of bad luck!  I do recommend the ambassador garden just a few doors down.

OR2K has a stellar reputation for their Kathmandu location, but the view from Pokhara makes this place a set above. 

Menu is similar with many options across gluten free, vegan, veggie, Indian, Nepalese, continental. 

Everything is delicious but for starters, we recommend the sharing platter (falafel, Breda, hummus, etc), and the hot chocolate soufflé is a treat. 

Overall, brilliant views, atmosphere is tops, food is thoughtful, delicious and inventive  prices are fair and this restaurant should be on your list for Pokhara. 

Also- they show movies via projector from 8:30 (not sure if all nights).

Hyatt Regency - Kathmandu
The hotel is very grand with extensive lush gardens in the center of town.
Our room was spacious and comfortable and the bathroom had a bath which we appreciated.
The hotel obviously struggles with maintenance due to its age, threadbare carpets parting at the seam…but charming nevertheless.
Our suite 417 had very heavy lime scale deposits around the faucets, the creaky shower hinges were covered with limescale and the shower head was clogged and needs a limescale remover soaking.The sink need re-enameling.

They also have a serious pigeon problem, as our exterior window ledge was smothered in bird droppings which was disgusting (the droppings can have a fungus, Cryptococcus which can cause serious breathing difficulties….the Hotel should address this issue.)

The public facilities in the lobby need a good cleaning the stalls on the Men’s floor edges are encrusted with ancient dirt and grime, they all need a good “power electric wash” and hinges were loose with missing screws, not a 5 Star standard.
We enjoyed their Sesame Restaurant which had a good Al A Carte Menu and Buffet, their Italian Restaurant - Rox was a delight for dinner one night. We also enjoyed their lobby bar where we had pre-dinner cocktails and extensive nibbles.

The staff were all very pleasant and eager to please , a good stay.

Ignore the moans of so many others: the fact that this place even exists after the earthquake and impresses tourist from around the world is nothing short of incredible. Yes it’s busy, yes there is scaffolding everywhere, yes there are lots of pigeons but the buildings are still beautiful. “Oh no, but I had to pay R1000 to get in, what a rip-off...” stop being so cheap. How much was it to travel to Nepal in the first place? How much was your hiking gear? Anyway...definitely worth seeing; support the restoration!

Really nice vegetarian restaurant overlooking the lake. A bit pricier than other restaurants but nice to go with a group of friends for dinner & drinks one night. I liked this one better than the one in Kathmandu, but I heard other's say they liked Kathmandu better - so try both and make up your own mind ;)

It's a pretty place but for what you pay and get its over the top. To expensive...!! Very basic rooms, nothing extra and it looks like the more you pay the less you get. Staff was ok though and location as well. Place is clean and has a nice garden. Won't go back unless the price changes
Had an amazing stay. Service was prompt and efficient. Very responsive and friendly staff. Wonderful breakfast set in beautiful grounds.  Great place

We went to OR2K in Kathmandu which is similar but this one in Pokhara is such a nice, chilled atmosphere. It has amazing food; I ordered the moussaka pie which comes with a baked potato - absolutely delish!! Staff are really nice also, big menu which is excellent for vegetarians as sometimes there isn't much on the menu. Would definitely recommend
What a beautiful lake it is simply loved the time spent here such clean water and wonderful boat ride here
Such a wonderful eco chic resort.  I felt like a queen after trekking in monsoon season.  The staff and spa were wonderful.  The accommodations were luxurious.
We hired a boat just for an hour to go to the temple, and watch the sunset.  If there were boats with larger sun covers we may have considered it for the day, but the sun was too hot for us

A 10/10 experience at Kantipur Temple House! I stayed here for over a week with a group of 10 for a University study tour. From the minute we arrived we were warmly welcomed by the beautiful staff, assisted with our luggage and were made tea. The owner is the loveliest man who went out of his way to check in with us any available chance. The room was so comfortable - hot water bottles at night time were a highlight! The food at the hotel was absolutely delicious - we didn't want to eat anywhere else! The chefs do an amazing set Nepalese meal but also delicious chinese, thai and indian inspired set meals. Every morning you have access to a lovely buffet breakfast to start your day. The staff were so helpful, so kind and always took time to chat to us. The location is perfect! I have absolutely no complaints! I miss the staff very much!

This is my second review for this hotel. Almost an year back I wrote a review highlighting several shortcomings of the hotel. Sad to say nothing has changed since then, or to put it more bluntly the situation has deteriorated even further.

My experience.

Event : Annual gathering of friends
Time : 6-10pm
Bad experiences :

1. Forcing us to have snacks at the restaurant when we were having a pool party. Extremely inconsiderate as the pool and restaurant are at two extremes of the hotel. The change in plans were not informed earlier and was a spontaneous decision taken by the management.

2. A menu was decided by us and was discussed and finalized with the the staff at the resort. The management has the audacity to change it on their own personal accord, once again without any prior notice whatsoever.

3. The hotel staff decided to switch roles with the paying customer insisting that the spilt food was to be cleaned by the paying customer. It was surprising that the management didn't ask us to wash the dishes also following the party.

All in all, I personally WOULD NOT RECOMMEND this resort to anyone. Think twice before planning any event here as you will be in for unpleasant and unwanted surprises provided to you as a compliment from the highly incompetent staff at waterfront.

This place was on my to-do list and it did not disappoint in the amazing temple views. However be prepared for people sending their children to you to have them beg and for sales people to not leave you alone.

Stayed here for 3 nights at the end of a gruelling 3 week 12 man motorcycle expedition around Nepal, during which our accommodation had been rather basic, so this was a significant treat for the group.
The staff are very efficient and welcoming. The rooms spacious and of a high standard in relative terms and our rate was very good value considering the relative luxury and excellent central Thamel tourist area location.
Special thanks to the charming Kriti and Sajana for their very efficient and delightful handling of our departure, patiently dealing with our numerous demands with a smile.
I shall be back.

Sarangkot is a great place for paragliding. There are many outfits to book from and many hotels can advise on that as they know the people. 
The village is also a good place to watch sunrise and sunset, but heavy cloud cover might often obstruct the views. 
We found it an ideal place to relax, enjoy local organic food and go for walks. Very kind and cooperative local vendors and hosts.
Lakle Fewa is a beautiful green-blue lake that has colorful boats you can use to paddle to the middle.  It was worth the awful windy bus  ride to get there from Kathmandu.

We heard about the amazing views at Sarangkot viewpoint so we booked with a guide to go.  It started raining as we were trekking up to the top and it didn't stop raining for the rest of the day.  The steps up to the lookout point were really vertical and very slippery when wet.  While I"m sure the views of the lake and mountains are amazing on a clear day I would not recommend going if it's raining, even if you've already booked it with the guide. Cancel your appointment and wait for a clearer day if you can!

Lovely place to while away some time away from the noise of the traffic. Go for a walk along the bank or rent a row boat. There's also a nice park where the locals come to play football. Unfortunately, the Nepalese don't seem to respect or value the beauty of their country and there is litter along the shoreline. This spoils the area.

A clean, tranquil location on Street 6 off the main drag, i.e. within 10min walking distance to restaurants and shops.

The hospitality is warm, earnest and unintrusive.

It is in high demand during the climbing season during the year end so book early.

Wonderful atmosphere!!! That's for 2 stars. The other star is for the service, because they are very nice. And they are very prompt . They did, however , bring me the incorrect change ( both times in their favor), 2 out of the three times I was there. 

I kept going back, because it was a great vibe. But the food was below average for the price that you pay. And the cocktails that I was so looking forward to were not very good at all... Sorry .. 
Maybe it's like a movie that you hear so many good things about and you go see it, and it's just not as good as you thought it would be.... Maybe my hopes were set to high..

Did this tour with Green Valley Treks after EBC.
Arjun had organized a good car and driver who patiently took us around.
Swayambhunath is amazing 
The peace and tranquility one feels in the presence of Buddha is indescribable

Go to the lake! It only took me five planes to get there! But worth it. What a beautiful scenic spot! So awesome to sit across and enjoy a cold beer! The vibe is wonderful. Quite a euphoric, special place to enjoy with a loved one!
Very colourful market, after visiting others I can also say it’s relatively clean, felt more comfortable eating around there. It’s of course more pricy as it serves only tourists.
Exhibits about mountaineering, Nepali culture, climate change, etc. Very interesting and informative for such a small museum, and beautifully built and landscaped as well.

A lot of people trying to sell crap to a way too high price. Beggars. Street dogs. Sewers draining into the lake. So much garbage thrown everywhere i wonder if it's a dumpsite or a holiday destination. It's a mystery to me how people can like this place so much. It's really ugly and dirty

I come to Kathmandu at least twice per year and KTH is “ my home”  there!  It’s a beautiful hotel with the most caring and friendly staff.  Suman, one of the managers, is a gem.  He has helped me several times with figuring out how to accomplish the ideas I come up with while I am in town...if I need something, he picks right up!   The food is organic & delicious... always consistently yummy.  Their location (?right on the edge of Thamel) is quiet & peaceful, with no barking dogs or loud clubs nearby.  Someone said it was an “ oasis” and Kantipur Temple House truly is !

My wife and I enjoyed our time at this property but it was because of the service we received. The people working at this hotel are outstanding. They go the extra mile (and then some) to make you feel welcomed and attended to. The recently renovated restaurant, Rox, located just off the lobby offers delicious homemade pastas and impeccable service.

The resort itself is in a beautiful setting but it's getting very outdated. Our room was spacious and comfortable but it could use a serious update. 

During our stay there were two large weddings (back to back) that meant large crowds of people in the lobby and at the breakfast area. It was chaos when the wedding groups were around. If it weren't "wedding season," I'm sure the experience would have been more serene.

In Kathmandu, the Hyatt is among the best places to stay. This resort doesn't align with other Hyatt resorts we've visited but all that's missing is some modernization of the rooms and facilities. Otherwise, this is a good place to spend a few days.

This place was is said to be a palace once. In the midst of business area, the location is the best part of this hotel. Shopping area & airport are nearby. Also the famous temple. 
The rooms are small & the house keeping is average. The bath area is cramped. The restaurant is good & good food is available,
i had a family trip with my family.i enjoyed a lot in phewa lake.we did boating in the late and went to a mandir.There we feel good while sitting in phewa lake.Night visit is too intresting here.

Poorest breakfast of whole visit to Nepal, poor service no cutlery and plates and bowls, milk etc , hotel in good location but very noisy second stay as near club on Friday night, you’ll need ear plugs to sleep , this could be Kathmandu though as noisy city . Depends which room you get first stay quiet 
In main tourist area and close to temples  if walk about 1.5 miles , rooms clean but toilet drain smell
Nice garden sitting area

We wandered in and through several times during the week we were in Kathmandu and the surrounding area. You might consult with the Lonely Planet to make sure you see all the nooks and crannies and know what you are looking at. You need a ticket to enter the square (and wear it around your neck). Your ticket will include entrance to the Lohan Chowk - amazing wood carvings adorn the courtyards inside.

BIG TIP: when you first enter, go to the Tourist Police office (listed on Google Maps), take your passport and a copy of you passport picture, and you can get a pass for the length of your stay. This allowed us to walk in and through over the week without having to pay each time.

One of the few ‘must see’ sites we were made aware of in Kathmandu. If you plan to climb all the steps give yourself plenty of time because you’ll also want to stop and watch the monkeys, take in the great views of the city from the top and have a drink/ice cream. Plenty of shops to browse too, if that’s of interest.

The Hyatt hotel at Kathmandu is great place to stay if you are visiting the area, the location is close to the main city just 15 minutes. The staff is extremely accommodating. The only issue i faced while on the property is the Wi-Fi not always working well

Spend 2 hours here but could easily have spent longer. Lots of fantastic photographs and interesting information about mountains with a focus on the Himalayas and famous expeditions, geology, ecology, the environment, the people. Fascinating and definitely worth a visit assuming that the mountains are at least one of the reasons you are visiting Nepal. I have ticked the box saying that the attraction has a restaurant, as I saw one in the grounds, but I have no idea what it is like!
Hyatt felt like second home because of Rohit Bhatt’s heartfelt services. Every corner here feels like magic. It gave us beautiful memories to cherish.

after the earth quake i have been there. its very beautiful and interested place to visit. in kathmandu you shouldn't miss this place. very beautiful cavings and ancient buildings.pity government docent take care enough this place
beautiful stupa and you will see the whole Kathmandu from there as temple is on the hill. Big negative for me was the strong smell of piss, ruins the ambiance of the place.
I stayed at Thamel and this place was awesome. This city lives and breaths. Streets were beautiful and the ambiance surrounding the place was really amazing.

Durbar Square is full of rich history, including structures and buildings that are about 500-1000 year old.  Incredible sites including the house/courtyard of the living goddess Kumari and Hindu statues.  If you enjoy architecture and/or history and/or people watching you will have a great time.

Things to be aware of: 
-This is not cheap, at a $20 USD entrance fee for foreigners (as of Jan 2019).  
-If you stand out as a foreigner (e.g. you are white), you will be approached excessively by both tour guides and "tour guides", hoping you'll pay them for a tour of Durbar Square.  I was approached enough to the point that I got very short with people towards the end.  I didn't realize this would happen, and I did pay for a 20-30 minute tour which I enjoyed.  It was overpriced, I believe he was asking $15-20 USD, but I talked him down to $10.  It was worth paying for, I felt, but not worth $20.  The only time I felt a little creeped out in Nepal was with a guide who had zero social skills and started following me for a little me before explaining that he just wanted to see if I'd like a tour.  
-There is devastating damage from the 2015 earthquake.  It was a good opportunity to ponder how wonders like this we can never take for granted, how delicately everything is intertwined on this earth, and how lucky I am to live in a location that is not earthquake prone.  There is an exhibit- I forget in which building, but one of the few you can walk around in- that has peoples' stories from the earthquake written on a note card on the wall, many of which are written in English.  It was humbling and was likely the most memorable part of visiting Durbar Square for me.

After visiting Kathmandu Durbar Square, I’m truly impressed. The intricate temples and palaces are even more stunning in person, with their detailed carvings and historic charm. The Hanuman Dhoka Palace and the Taleju Temple are standouts, showcasing the incredible craftsmanship of the past. The square’s vibrant energy, with locals going about their daily lives and vendors selling everything from snacks to souvenirs, adds to the experience. While some parts are still being restored from the 2015 earthquake, it’s clear that a lot of effort is going into preserving this cultural gem. Overall, it’s a memorable visit and a fascinating glimpse into Nepal’s rich history and vibrant present.

Most of the reviews all talk about the same thing.  Touristy, overpriced items, trekking, etc.  I'm going to tell you things you will NEED to know while you're in Kathmandu.  1, expect stomach issues.  I've been religious about bottled water, eating cooked food, etc., and I'm still having issues.  So, plan on it.  Bring Pepto, Imodium, etc.  And something like Preparation H, because you will wipe yourself raw.  Which leads me to my next point.  2, you will likely find yourself out and about and have to use a public/restaurant restroom. They vary from ok to disgusting.  Two of the ones I had to use didn't have toilet paper... only the squirt nozzle.  Put a pack of the flushable moist wipes in your backpack and carry them with you.  You'll thank me later.  3, while Nepalese food doesn't seem as spicy as Indian food, ask if you aren't sure, especially if spicy food isn't your thing.  They can accommodate.  If you just go with it as is, well, reference numbers 1 and 2 (no pun intended).  4, do not be afraid to haggle.  The best technique I've found is  to throw out what you want to pay, and if they say anything but ok, act a bit angry and walk out.  I've even said "you're a scammer" and "you're trying to steal from me".  Suddenly the price for a candle holder went from $55 to $25.  I still didn't buy it because he did try to scam me. 5, expect to pay entrance fees for any historical site.  Usually NPR1000 (about $7.50).  Some are worth it, some are tourist money grabs.  If you've seen one Durbar Square, you've seen them all.  Hiking Trails through the woods aren't worth $7.50 in my opinion because they are not kept up, with trash everywhere.  6, Nepal doesn't have Uber, but InDrive worked very well here.  You have to pay cash when you take the trip, so be sure to have the right change.  Pretty inexpensive and the drivers didn't try to weasel more money out of me.  If they do, tell them no (I yell at them "why did you accept the trip then?") , and call for another.  7, don't take any nonsense from anyone.  They know we try not to be rude and don't ask questions.  They also know we have money, and haggling isn't in our culture.  Don't let them take advantage of you.  

Have fun, bring wipes and Pepto, and enjoy Kathmandu.  It was WAYYYY better than any city in India (I was in Mumbai, Jaipur, and Jodhpur before KTM)

This resulted in power cuts for 10 hours a day while we were there, due to increase by another few hours shortly and predicted to go up to as many as 18 hours a day later in the year.  The current â??load-sheddingâ? schedule is typically something like this.  The power is out from 6.30 am â?? 12.30 pm and 5 pm to 9 pm.  The hotel used a battery to supply power to the rooms at these times.  In our room we had a very inadequate emergency light by the door which did not always come on.  We had to ask for it to be put on a couple of times and were told once the battery was down and we couldnâ??t use it.  Admittedly, we were provided with a portable light on this occasion.  Being a courtyard-facing room, it was dark even during the day, pitch-black at night (see picture).  A couple of flashlights are a minimum requirement â?? especially for the bathroom which had no emergency light at all.  There is one candle provided but this is not very useful and of course,  no power sockets at power cut times.   Oh and thereâ??s no TV at all and WIFI is not available in the (nicer) courtyard-facing rooms.   You have to take your laptop outside to the garden which is not so appealing on a winter eveningâ?¦. If itâ??s important for you to have light and power during the long power cuts, and TV and breakfast included in the hotel price, you wonâ??t find them here but you can get them at hotels charging far less.  If none of these things are important to you,  youâ??ll probably love the KTH, but consider a room at the front.  Although these rooms seem to lack the charm of the inner rooms, they are much lighter and you can access the Internet from them.

We didn’t see the views on the day we went up and apart from a tiny glimpse in the morning one day haven’t since we have been in Pokhara. Some people seem to think it is mainly cloud blocking the mountains but it’s dust and a smog haze. In addition the unchecked development at the top of Sarangkot is really pretty shocking.

I am sure if we had have seen the view it would have made it more worthwhile but I’m quite shocked how awe struck people seem to be. It is not like being up in a nature reserve it’s a concrete plinth with no birds or no thought to preserving the natural beauty. There is a temple being made now at the top which I presume is so tourists keep coming up.

I first visited KGH waaay back when Thamel was a residential area. Back then, Thamel
had only three attractions for visitors, KGH, the hotel where Hillary stayed, the Utsy
Restaurant and K.C.'S Restaurant. KGH really, can be given the credit for the start of
the now world famous Thamel Area. KGH originally started as a private home, whose
owner wisely purchased, one by one, the properties of his surrounding neighbors and
instead of tearing them down, he sort of connected them into what became an extremely quirky hotel whose rooms were all different styles and sizes on many levels.
All of its really old return guests had their favorite room which they would reserve by
room number. Unfortunately, Nepals earthquake, badly damaged their heritage house,
which was over 100 years old. Instead of rebuilding and repairing the old houses, the
owner chose to tear them all down and in their place, expand their magnificent garden,
and put up a lot of new, very generic, cheaply decorated rooms. The few old rooms
still left, are not in good repair and have been neglected in favor of the newly constructed building. All of the fabulous vibes of the wonderful old hotel have been lost,
sadly, and a new, fancier hotel, just like so many others, is left in its place. Taking full
advantage of their reputation, they have always been overpriced, but with their 24 hour
generator service during Kathmandu's massive power cuts, it was worth it. Now that
the power has returned, I, unfortunately, because of financial concerns, have now
found a new hotel to stay in with rooms similar to the old quirky ones, but at a third of
the cost.  Some of their staff have been there a million years, and I'll miss them!  I am
friends with most of the management, and respect and love them all, but I'm afraid I've 
stayed for the last time. I really wish they would have rebuilt it as it was before,as do many of its old guests. They are still spotlessly clean, with great service. I wish them all
the best, but I have no desire to stay in very overpriced generic rooms with little personality.
