Because of the Annapurna Circuit having a lot of snow in early to mid March, things were pretty dangerous at Thorung La Pass, so my guide and I decided to turn around at Manang. As a result I had several extra days for Pokhara/Chitwan and we decided to check out the Sarangkot overlook and all I can say is WOW!!!!  What an INCREDIBLE view!!!  I was hoping to do the Dhaulagiri Icefall hike near the end of the trek (which changed of course, with the pass being closed) and this view of the mountain from Sarangkot is ASTOUNDING!!!  You get beautiful views of Machapuchare, the fishtail as well. There are views of Lamjung Himal, all of the mountains named Annapurna and one named Mount Hiunchuli, which is pretty impressive as well.   You almost feel like you can reach out and touch some of the tallest mountains in the world. Fewa Lake is quite the sight, with fog above it, giving it a mystical feeling. 
    Suggestions:
     1- I recommend leaving Pokhara about an hour and a half  before sunrise to be at the viewpoint because the feeling of being there when it is somewhat dark is pretty neat. 
      2-If you use a DSLR camera, I highly recommend bringing a mid-range telephoto lens. I used my 70-200 which worked great. 
       3-The main lookout can be REALLY crowded!!!  I recommend walking down the pathway to the left of the main lookout about 200 meters. There is a really quiet lodge that will allow you to take in the views from the roof. There was only one other tourist there at the same time I was. Want to talk about peace. Ahhhh, no noisy tourists😀. I am very glad to have had my guide Deepen there👍. He knew where to go for that serenity. And the views were AWESOME from there. Just please make sure to buy some tea there for a nominal fee that is totally worth it. You might need it anyways because it can get cold up there. If you want to find the lodge and restaurant on the road, make sure to go to the left of the main viewpoint (when facing the mountains) 100-200 meters and you’ll see a white sign on the right side of the road with blue lettering on it. There’s a path you can take to the back of the lodge, which will take you to the steps to get to the roof. 
     I can’t recommend viewing the mountains from here enough. There was only one other place where the views were as good or better in all my time in the mountains-the trek between Pisang and Manang (I actually cried when taking in the views there). This is a MUST stop in my opinion!!!  Just please make sure to check the weather forecast the day before. The first day in Pokhara was very very rainy when I was there. Day two was perfect.

We stayed for two nights at the Temple Tree Resort and for the vast majority of the time it was very nice. Set a short distance from the shops and restaurants of Lakeside but away from the traffic it's in a perfect location. The hotel itself is well designed and relatively small property set in its own gardens. It has a small pool. Our room was small but comfortable with a partial view of the mountains and garden, it had a safe, wardrobe, good shower (which has a tendency to flood the bathroom floor unless you were careful), nice toiletries, TV with some international channels and Wifi. There were occasional power cuts for short periods. We ate in the restaurant a couple of times and had a drink in the bar, the service and standard of food/drink was excellent and prices reasonable. Breakfast quality is patchy and choices are a bit limited but there is always something you can eat, whether it is fruit, cereal, toast, eggs (made to order) etc. Our travel agent had told them it was our wedding anniversary and they went to great lengths to help us celebrate with a cake and our room decorated with petals, swans and balloons. Most of the time we thought the Temple Tree was very good, with only a couple of minor drawbacks, for instance there are no lifts so if you have mobility issues there may be a problem, the room was dark at night with not a lot of light so reading was difficult, there was a clash of music between the bar and restaurant at times which was irritating and we could have done with more space in the room, but overall things were good. The major annoyance with the Temple Tree Resort was on our last morning. We had been told by our guide the day before he would collect us at 8-30am. We checked out and were sitting in reception when a lady came over and told us he had rung the night before to put the pickup time back to 9-30am. They had kept this information to themselves rather than leave a note in the room or find us in the restaurant, where they could have easily found us, as all the waiting staff congratulated us on our anniversary, so half the hotel knew who we were and where we were. We would have welcomed the extra hour in bed or a more leisurely breakfast as we had a nine hour drive back to Kathmandu. When we pointed this out no apology was offered just a request to fill out a feedback form. I wrote the above on the form and I hope that they will learn to pass messages on for future guests. It left us with a very negative impression of what was otherwise a good stay.

The Waterfront is a nice, if overpriced, additional to the wide variety of hotel accomodations available in Pokhara.  It is outside of town on a private road so it's a bit quieter than Lakeside.  You will have to bargain hard with taxis to go out there though.  The view of the lake is pretty and the hotel has all of the mod cons.  As a Nepali-speaking, long-staying visitor in Nepal though, I thought the room was overpriced.  I paid about US$80 to Gokarna Forest Resort in Kathmandu, arguably a nicer property with finer amenities and the US$150 I paid to the Waterfront Resort just didn't seem to go as far.  That said, the Manager of the property, Santosh, is friendly and ever-present.

What we weren't terribly pleased with was the car service up to Jomsom that we hired via the hotel.  I was told that US$350 for this service was a very good price because the road is quite bad (it is) and the driver would not be able to find return passengers.  Incidentally, the gas up to Jomsom from Pokhara costs about US$50.  And, while US$350 may be a good price, I would recommend that other travelers take a flight.  The driver we had was quite capable in the driving department, but we spent 3 hours in Beni because the Myagdi District Committee would not let us pass. Our vehicle did not have permission to pass.  Our driver told me to stay in the car and not speak Nepali, but after 2.75 hours with him simply saying that we should wait in the car, I got out and asked him what was really going on.  At that point I had to go over and yell at the committee representative for 10 minutes and only then were we allowed to pass.  This meant that we got into Jomsom quite late, well after dark and it meant that we didn't get to walk to Marpha on that first day as planned.  Then, the next morning, as we walked to Marpha, our driver passed us with a car full of people.  Not only that, there is clearly no difficulty finding passengers who want a ride down from Jomsom and we all felt completely taken for a ride in terms of the price paid.  It was insulting to have paid so much for less-than-stellar service and then see that it is quite easy for drivers to find return passengers.  On the way back we arranged for a ride from Tatopani to Pokhara quickly and cheaply.  

I have spoken with Santosh about this and he was quite apologetic, but, in keeping with what seems to be Nepali tradition, offered no compensation whatsoever.  He did say that he would refrain from recommending this particular Jeep service in the future.  I would too.  The owner of the Jeep service is Mr. Raju Dahal, who runs the Bedrock Hotel in Lakeside.

The atmosphere is very crowded with loud music so if you're after peace and quiet then it's not your place. The last night we came here we ordered hot chips just prior to the kitchen closing and were given some old re-heated chips. The bread that came with my soup was half eaten.. So while the food can be very good, the service drops when is busy. To get a smile from a staff member is like trying to make a worm smile... would be a great place if they were a just a bit more attentive!!

The Swaybhunath stupa located atop the hill in Kathmandu offers really good view of Kathmandu valley. I really enjoy it going out of hustle and bustle of Kathmandu city and pollution, really superb place. I avoid the stairs and use the road on backside.

Food is great and atmosphere is also very lively. You sit at small tables on the floor and are asked to take your shoes off. The black lighting provides a little extra zaz as your whites glow. The chocolate hot cake was delicious and a must to try!. 

The meals are very heavily bread based so would suggest ordering less than you initially think you need (can always order more later and finish with the chocolate cake)
It was a wonderful stay here. Ayushma ma’am assisted us very gracefully. Overall, the stay was cozy, peaceful, and pleasant. I will definitely recommend this place in the future
I felt really sad to see the deterioration of this place. There were so many trash everywhere. Poorly managed or not managed at all by the local government.

visited recently, easy location, lots of space, beautiful garden, wonderful swimming pool along with suitable for kids too. Clean rooms, beautiful ambience. Freiedly staff. When we comeback we will stay again. Definetly recommend to all. Thanks retreat.

It's a good and cheap hostel, the owner is kindly abd friendly, the area of this hostel it's very good, everything about you, restaurants and cafes and markets, there is housekeeping twice in the week if you at rooms.

Beat of the best hotel in kathmandu so far. We had great time staying at the hotel. Location just in the middle of the city very easy access to everywhere. Love the place and around. When back to kathmandu will definitely choose here.

The museum is located in a very large area. I feel much larger than it actually should've been. The exhibits are well spaced around and gives a very detailed explanation of the local ethnic groups and about their livelihood.

The section that I admired the most was the section on mountaineering and about the 8000m topping peaks. The information and details of all the big names in mountaineering, the tools they used and their stories captivated me.

Only feedback is the poor lighting of the exhibits for photographs. Almost impossible to get a picture without reflections from the surrounding. Other than that a must visit if you're in Pokhara for an extra afternoon.

Temple Tree is a beautiful and peaceful retreat that offers a perfect blend of nature and comfort. The surroundings are serene, with well-maintained gardens and a relaxing ambiance. The rooms are clean, spacious, and tastefully decorated. The staff is friendly and attentive, always ready to help with a smile. The food is delicious, with a good variety of options. The pool area is a great place to unwind. While the overall experience was excellent, a few minor improvements in service speed would make it perfect. Still, it’s a wonderful place to relax and recharge. Definitely worth a visit
To see how the kings used to live and the interesting buildings surrounding the area is a must to visit

Any awe and reverence you might be inclined towards as you climb the many steps towards Swayambhu is immediately evaporated when you reach the top and realise that it is really not a lot more than a gaudy market for cheap tourist tat.

There must be 30+ stalls selling the same rubbish (and ironically you're not allowed to take pictures of the tat). Totally ruins the mood and what the place is meant to represent.

I reserved a single ordinary room for my stay in Kathmandu. I loved the outdoors but my room was not like another four star hotel somewhere else. Bathroom was pretty basic without vanity. Smelly due to some drainage you could tell. I did not get my toiletries in time and had to ask the reception. But other services were great. Reception was very helpful. Food at the restaurant was average to very good on different days and at different times and also depends on what you order. Portions are quite big though. Considering the country's resources these are excusable I guess. Air conditioning did not seem to work either. When it was pouring, corridor downstairs was flooded. Poor hotel staff had to mop and squeegee. Everybody was friendly and helpful. I guess lack of resources both human and material are the causes for low level of quality even though it was rated four stars. I would like to go again despite the little things I experienced for the reasons:  outdoors, helpful staff, close to the shopping area, global ATM in the premises.
The falafel combo was beyond my expectation. It really fills up your appetite. The best vegan restaurant in town. The ambience is very relaxing, we stayed here for hours after our lunch.

Beds, pillows, toiletries and room amenities very good. Hairdryer a disaster, one of the ones attached to the bathroom wall with  a pipe blowing practically no hot air. Attached with one screw so was wobbling, you could not blow dry your hair with this type of hairdryer, please Radisson Kathmandu provide hairdryers suitable for 21st century. Pool area has 8 white plastic sunloungers with no mattress pads, impossible to lie on for any length of time, again Radisson Kathmandu buy 8 mattress pads for the beds. Over and able this the evening buffet and breakfast buffet were superb, best we had in Nepal.

Hi all, its been a longtime I am travelking to Nepal and trvalled before and right after 2015 earthquake ... Was totally shattered to see the destru tion that it caused several thousand people died... But as always God Bless Nepalese.. Hard working tough and bold they are the reconstruction Work is in full swing and in a year or two it will all look good as before... Do come to Durbar Square and feel the Royalty...!!
Food was really nice. Good view from there waiters are very mannerable. Good and very peaceful environment.

We stayed for three days during our trip,the tour of Nepal. Modern, clean,luxurious in the heart of Kathmandu. The stuff was really friendly and always with a smile on their face. Breakfast and dinner were excellent too, with a great variety of local and western selection. Of course I  can recommend this hotel.

The fun cafe at Radisson Kathmandu was exceptional. Food is always good but staff (Anu & Supriya) always goes out of their way to make our guest stay most comfortable and memorable. As a expedition company owner and our guides always look forward to staying in Radisson Kathmandu. Hopefully we can continue our partnership for many years to come.
I likebating in beautiful fewalake in pokhara, one of the main attraction and famous landmarks of pokhara city. recommend to explore.

Perfect for boating in and around the lake. Combine it with the visit to the temple that is located in the middle of the lake. If you book a small boat, you pay about 6 dollars an hour. Alternatively, pay about 60 cents to use a larger boat to travel to and from the little island temple. Please note that the latter won't get you around the lake.

As everywere in Pokhara the Himalaya mountains are vert impressive. When the water is smooth you can see nice reflections. Without these mountains it would be a very ordinary lake. Like there are so many. We took a boatride for one our. Not very special but relaxing.

For an afternoons fun and relax, hire a boat (no guide) and paddle yourself around the lake. I got the kids to do the work, LOL! We saw Eagles, Kingfishers and some other birds we couldn't name! Great fun. They provide life jackets but keeping them on the kids was hard as it was hot.

Excellent service Good behaviour  Clean and tidy rooms Helpful reception Fantastic hospitality Active and very punctual housekeeping Excellent  ambiance  Food quality can be improved slightly if proper vigilance is maintained before serving in future.

We walked around the area, had rest in the hut...Museum itself is very informative! One hour is not enough to explore it fully especially if you are willing to read description, watch photos and elements of exhibition, they also show movie there. Definitely worth going there if you are a fan of museums and love mountains

Visited this chic trendy place in the heart of thamel a couple of times. Absolutely unique atmosphere offering very alternative and healthy choice of food. Could have been my favorite restaurant if not for the service. On my last trip, I asked for a single seat and was just gestured to sit anywhere. Just after I sat myself down, a group of 6 or so westerners came in. The waiter asked if I could sit somewhere else. The issue is, there were many seats available but he wanted to offer my area to them because it was the most comfortable. I moved myself somewhere else and then ordered a pumpkin soup and phad thai. In a few minutes, both the soup and phad thai were delivered at the same time. You could imagine how difficult it is to enjoy both meals whilst its hot. I asked for the bill not long as I don't feel welcome anymore. That took a while and then, i checked with one of the waiters, who asked me to go down to the cashier below to make payment. The previous visit I made didn't require me to do that. All on all, this place is colorful on the outside but black and white in the inside.

The hotel , location and ambience is very good . We visited here as a group of 10 with kids . food was good - breakfast has a vast spread and so is the dinner buffet.
The staff were very well mannered and pleasing . The room was also service was very quick .
Overall a very pleasant staff 
Chef - Subendu Roy and his staff catered to all our requests .

After completing our stunning Mardi Himal Base Camp trek, we finally got to an hour of leisurely boating down the Fewa Lake in the early morning to escape the heat.  Lining the lake was beautiful purplish Jacaranda trees which made the ride more serene.  Our group of 5 ladies were so at peace with ourselves and at the time enjoying each other companionship.  There were other kayakers and we even witnessed a wedding celebration along the lakeside.

For first timers to Pokhara, highly recommended to take the boat ride.

Best place to stay in Katmandu. You can buy pretty much everything for the trekking trips. Lots of good restaurants, laundry service is available, accommodation for all levels of luxury.
I bought the momento here.

The Lake offers plenty of photo motives.
Part of the shore is clean of trash and garbage.
A boat ride is recommendable.

“My fifth stay in this place and every time the environment is more superb with very friendly and loyal staff. Worth to stay every time with no regrets. Breakfast and services always outperforms in every visit.”
Service: 9/10
Environment: 9.5/10

It’s not your mountain serenity. You can like thamel only if you are looking for hustle and bustle of a city. Lots of gift shops , restaurants and caffe . You can roam around and spend quality time . The bus stations are also nearby. Your stay can be a bit noisy though.

We were only there for a night on the advise and recommendation of a friend. It was quiet and the rooms were big but the service was lacking. For the rate they were charging per room per night I would have expected more. The breakfast in the morning was good. The hotel is located right in the heart of Thamel. All the shopping, clubs, restaurants, bakery is right outside the gates. As we were there for only one night I can't say much. Oh yeah it takes ages to mix the hot and cold water, either its too hot or freezing cold. If you ask for ice, they don't have it. You are better off getting it from the shops outside but please note the rooms dont have a refrigerator. At least not the ones we got.
So much history, you can spend many hours walking around Durbar Square. Repairs after the earthquake are progressing slowly.

Unparalleled Luxury and Personalized Service in the Heart of Kathmandu with Best Staff (Aalex – sales, Srijana – front desk, Anjali – Spa, Sunita - Dining)
The Hyatt Regency Kathmandu isn't just a hotel; it's an experience that begins the moment you arrive and continues throughout your stay. What truly sets this property apart is its dedicated staff who go above and beyond to ensure every guest feels valued and cared for.
Location and First Impressions: - Conveniently situated near Tribhuvan International Airport and the sacred Pashupatinath Temple – It started from the sales team, with special mention to Aalex for her promptness in booking and accommodating all our needs and helping us with the best view room at great price.
Check-in and Room Experience: - Srijana from the front desk provided an exceptional start to our Nepal experience - Personal escort through the stunning lobby to our well-appointed room - Attentive service addressing all our needs smoothly and efficiently. We opted for Bodhnath Stupa view (suggested by Aalex) and trust me it was worth it. At night just switch off the lights in the room and then right from the big glass wall of the room you see the stupa – wow ….. you wake and that whats you see again, it was really calming and so spiritual.
Dining Delights: - Sunita in the dining area made us feel truly valued - Catered to all our food requirements with grace and attention to detail - Special mention to the authentic Nepali Thali, a must-try for all guests - Chef Padam Singh's north Indian delicacies were a culinary highlight
Relaxation and Wellness: - Oasis Spa offers a rejuvenating experience, with Anjali providing top-notch service - Perfect way to unwind after a day of exploring Kathmandu both foot spa to my mother and aunty brought them the energy back.
Additional Staff Recognition: - Sujata at the front desk contributed to the overall excellent service experience
Amenities: - Beautiful outdoor swimming pool set in lush gardens - Well-equipped fitness center - Multiple dining options catering to various tastes
The Hyatt Regency Kathmandu excels not just in its prime location and luxurious amenities, but in its commitment to personalized service. Each staff member we encountered, from sales to spa, from dining to front desk, contributed to making our stay unforgettable. 
Whether you're in Kathmandu for business or leisure, this hotel offers the perfect blend of Nepalese hospitality and world-class luxury. The attention to detail and genuine care from the staff elevates the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu from a great hotel to an extraordinary destination. Our primary reason for choosing Hyatt was because of its cultural architecture, the greenery and calmness at the center of the city with all the hush hush around.
For tourist they go beyond their services to help with local currency (max limit in a day per room is 5K NCR) so that guests don’t struggle on currency conversion when staying at their property, also they have 2 ATM machines for any cash withdrawal .

Most amazing, vibrant place fill of life, colour, heritage, art and architecture.
One can spend days here strolling through the beautiful streets and amazing cafe's set amidst beautiful surroundings. Excellent experience.
I loved Thamel

After our trek I booked to stay here having previously visited and a look around the beautiful garden. I was ready for a hit of comfort after staying in the mountains. The staff were lovely, Its perfect location and the garden was very nice but the room were not exhausted. We were there for 6 nights. The first room we were given was a garden view room. It was so small. The bathroom was a wee closet. If you opened the curtains anyone walking  by could see in. We did get moved to the top floor of the old section. It was much better but still very old and tired. We had no hot water for two days. The shower flooded the bathroom floor every time you turned it on. And it was very noisy. I didn’t get to see what looked like the nice rooms. I did book 9 months in advance so it wasn’t like it was a last minute booking. So very disappointed. Not at all good value for the money.

We love the traditional style of the building, the service hospitality specially the front desk and breakfast. The coffee one of the best of Kathmandu. The dinner was very good too.
It is very well located.
I will warmly recommand it to my friends if they visit Kathmandu.

Sarangkot is easiest and shortest hiking hill from Pokhara. If you have additional day in Pokhara, Sarangkot half day hike from Pokhara will be perfect for you. The hill is the best for sunrise and mountain views.

Visited last month with friends,  they serve Organic , healthy food also they had own organic garden,  clean n greenery garden which is the best, clean and comfortable bed and best service. I will visit again. Highly recommend.
Full of shops, and tourists. A place to explore a bit the night life and a variety of restaurants. You can find everything and anything walking through the roads.

Very good much cheap never been there come again

Not know what to write need 100 minimum Still not enough now good

Walked into a dated and empty restaurant on the 2nd floor....toilet was clean but had a foul smell...
The menu was extensive, but nothing was cheap....for the quality of service and interiors this is a super expensive restaurant...the food is average to below par in my books...i would not suggest a visit.
NOT RECOMMENDED..
bhagwan

You definitely take your life into your hands walking around here! But, there's no place I'd rather be in Kathmandu! It's colorful, loud, smoggy, manic and just full of life! The streets are narrow and sometimes it's shocking that 2 cars can pass each other without taking off wing mirrors, or taking out pedestrians! Lots of good shopping and great food! 

Give yourself an afternoon to just wander about and get lost...and trust me, you will get lost!
If you love mountaineering or trekking this place is must visit for all the adventure lover with lot's of Info and history

Hotel trekkers home is very good and nice hotel 
I’m very happy to stay there . I was feeling it’s my second home the stuff are very friendly and helpful. Mr. Ranjeet is very good and helpful person he always help me for my destination and my tour thank you so for your help.
All the staff on the pics are gd,always gd attitude with smile,enthusiastic n helpful:),food here is gd also ,nice experience.
Hotel was so good nice experience staff was so good very friendly specially named is Sabina service like 10 to to  see you again
Great views, be prepared to climb some stairs! Entrance fee paid near top a very reasonable 200 rupees. Lots of aggressive vendors selling everything Nepal.  Worth a look on a nice day.

An excellent restaurant with a unique atmosphere situated on a magnificent view point overlooking the Fawe Lake. These are the main ingredients of OR2K experience we had.
Seating on low or high chairs enjoying the Mediterranean Cousine while the lake turns gold during the sunset was a great ending to our Nepal adventure relaxing after a long trek...
Soups were delicious creamy and hot served in beautiful covered copper bowls with a warm roll and butter...
We enjoyed the Sizzling Veg dishes and the Alfredo Penne dish ....great staff!

As usual Radiason staff is courteous and neat and clean hotel with strategic location..just room service is bit delayed for service..rest all is ok..good buffet..value for money

Rooms in the old block are little old design but neat and clean..New block is newly made with fresh global interiors.

Central location very close to the restaurants and pubs specially all the things just near by within the walking distance. Hot water and wifi working well and room are specious for the price I paid. Rooftop was great we had great sunset view and chill beer with frosty glass was nice too

We visited when much of the area was under reconstruction after the earthquake damages. Could imagine how nice it was before. We could not see the kumari puja because it was sat (sat is their weekly holiday) and the kumari did not have the mood to come out for the puja. Too bad, we wanted to see it. Overall very impressive place.

We had to leave our hotel at the Lakeside at 4.30am to be early enough to get a good viewing spot for the sunrise, before the crowds came. The weather at this time of the year is not clear, so the views were not breathtaking. Nevertheless to see the Annapurna mountain range was still a sight to remember. Highly recommended when visiting Pokhara.

Excellent stay.  Safe, clean and good location. I would recommend the hotel for anyone for business or pleasure.  Very pleasant staff.  Nice food.  Good shops.  A great base for any traveller.  Highly recommended .

I stayed in Kantipur Temple House from 26th to 31st January 2020. The hotel is located in the heart of Kathmandu, but in a very peaceful environment. It is an Eco-friendly hotel, no unnecessary appliances for travelers such as TV and Refrigerator in the room which I really like. Friendly staff, good food and easy access to taxi. Highly recommended.
we rowed to the temple in the middle of the lake . something to do the day before trekking. It was fun.
Stafss are very friendly and curtious and the service is excellent. The grounds are extremely well maintained, beautiful and serene
Nice place for boating, lots of nice lave view restaurants beside. Awesome sunset view, Lots of boats, you may take one, local Nepali people will take you for a tour. Nice experience

This hotel is in good location in the city. The room is clean and well maintained. However, the room I stayed was too cold. It was 18 degree celcius and could not be adjusted. I called the front office and someone came to take a look at it but nothing had been fixed after that. I should have changed the room but I did not. So I needed to turn the A/C on and off a few times that night. Other than that, I enjoy my stay there.

We had amazing views of Phewa Tal from the Peace Dragon Lodge which overlooks the lake (and Annupurna Ranges when the mountains come out from behind the clouds). We went for a boat ride over to the Temple as well which was absolutely delightful. There are a few restaurants lakeside where you can grab a delicious lunch with a beautiful view.
At the entrance they demand from western tourists outrageous amount of 1000 rupee to enter while locals enter for free.

Urmila was outstanding in the breakfast area always knowing what we needed and providing the food and drink day to day. I appreciate how hard Urmila worked for us. I also thank the rest of the breakfast staff including Rajash and the bell desk people, Kasir, Vinod and Yeshpal for always helping and assisting us.

After trekking, my husband and I were craving some fresh, delicious food and OR2K delivered. The Goat Cheese Salad and the Falafel were delicious and the portions were very big. The decor of the restaurant is beautiful - just the type of place I love spending the afternoon at. We will definitely be back!

Was nice to visit and take a look around, however was very dirty and a lot of people harass you/try to sell you things as you walk up the stairs (although this may be because I was a lone female traveler). Cost of entry for foreigners is 200 NPR.

We basically didn’t make too much movements. I wanted to be in a quite place in midst of nature. It met all out expectations. Anyone can have boat ride in the lake, from where u can have the breathtaking view of Annapurna Range.

Thamel is an old area of Kathmandu. Lots of narrow lanes, interesting shops. The more commercial area of Thamel is geared up for tourists and the older area is a typical Nepalese local shopping area. Lots of temples and many many old buildings are to be seen.

Wonderful experience,food was amazing,environment was very friendly and we had a very beautiful memory 
Thank you ,The Lakeside Retreat 🙏🏽

This Temple is considered the  place to be for locals who want to spend a few hours in a pleasant, green space, high above the city.
Many local people visit and seem to spend the day.
It's a bit of a hike, so be prepared to climb once you get there: you can do the steps directly uphill--I didn't, I went through the bus entrance. Still steep, but NOT like the other entrance.
Lovely views from top. 
Got my best  typical Nepal picture here--looking down and included green hills and prayer flags.
Watch out for the aggressive monkey population!

Excellent Hospitality by the staffs, Especially special mention to Mr MD Rahmat wonderful service by him. Top class Professionalism at his work. Kudos to him.

Rest you stay was very pleasant.

I wish him all the best!!!

Cheers,
John Wycliffe

Don't expect first world sophistication on the the displays, but DO spend time here.  Maybe a few hours! There is so much information.  There are displays about all the ethnic groups and where they live in Nepal. There is a big section on the geology of the Himalaya.  And of course, all about the main peaks, who has climbed them and when.  Also an interesting phtographic comparison between the people of the Alps and Nepal!  Very interesting. The free films each hour are also worth it!  There's a small restaurant on the grounds so if you need to stop and eat you can do that, too!

We stayed at the Temple Tree for two nights in December.  The hotel itself reminded us of a time share - condominium style, very basic/no frills.  Our observations:  
Internet - terrible wifi connection, down more than it was up.  Only so many people could be on at once, so we found ourselves constantly waiting for someone to drop off so we could connect. Even then, it was slow and unreliable.  
Sewage smell - wafting into the patio/bar area.  We couldn't escape it!
Bar Service - painfully slow... took our bartender 20 minutes minimum to make our drinks.  When we politely questioned where our drinks were, the response was a surprised "they're coming" as if we were crazy for asking.  
All and all, given this is one of the most expensive hotels in Pokhara, we did not feel it was worth the money or hype.

The architecture of the hotel is fantastic and is really very unique and authentic. The staff is extremely nice and helpful - they gave us so many suggestions on things to do, they were always welcoming and smiling. At some point we had to leave Kathmandu and come back few days later to go to the airport so the hotel offered to keep our bags and also gave us a free of charge room to freshen up, shower, and change our clothes before we could head to the airport.

Enjoyed my visit to Kathmandu. My stay in  Thamel was good. Next time I go I will spend a little more on a hotel.
The one thing that  drove me  nuts was the lack of street signs.

We are interested in the mountains and the animals and tribes of Nepal. The museum is well laid out and has a video introducing Nepal and another special one about Mallory and Irvine.
There is an on-site Cafe and a small souvenir shop.
Plenty of photo opportunities too.

Shopping in Thamel is great fun. It is increadible huge, you can find everything and more and always to very high starting prices.... They like to bargain so you have to do it. They sell fakes and local prodacts. We focused on typically nepalesi products and found counless shopping opportunities. In case you like to buy brands there are all well known sores from all expensive brands available. We felt extremely good in that area that is completely overcrowded with people, scooters and shops in combination with unique architecture. In case you lost your destination there are bike rikschas that will bring you to your hotel. If you are in Kathmandu it is a must do.

This is an OK hotel, but do not expect "Global Hyatt" standards.  It is comfortable, clean, good food and staff as a whole are very friendly.On the other hand, rooms are a bit dated - bed is not the best.  The curtains are not fully black-out, lot of Indian tourists who make a lot of noise (raised it with hotel staff who did nothing about it).But then again, I do not believe there are many other choices in Kathmandu.

This Square shows an excellent variety of historic monuments even though it is apparent they are still repairing after the earthquake.  The fun part was all the markets in the middle of the square where you could buy anything from hairy facemask to a local board game of tigers and goats. Dont miss it

Hotel good, nice room with a veranda, good location and nice breakfast (stayed a couple of nights and breakfast buffet options changed).  Lovely Himalayan coffee.  

Restaurant staff very good and after checking with chef were able to adapt menu to suit.  They definitely make the stay very good.

Booked 50 minute manicure as a treat, therapist did not speak English, despite booking a manicure, stating this twice she started to do a pedicure!  Walked out after less than 5 minutes after she cut index finger nail ridiculously short, it will take weeks to grow back!  Ended up borrowing a nail file and clippers to finish the job myself.

Complained at reception who said they wouldn't charge!!!! Offered another therapist to complete manicure but declined.  I advised I would put on Trip Advisor and hotel receptionist recommended I did (she said spa was new and staff had come from Katmandu).  There weren't standard health checks carried out either so I would be really dubious about any other treatments.  I can see spa reviews are mixed and my advice would be to wait until staying in a different hotel.

I’m very happy with the accommodations, service and support 😊😊 All the members and staff are very helpful. I will again visit and recommend all to visit this Hotel 👍. The location was very good and very easy to find . Regarding from my opinion everything thing was best here. The  food was very good and especially thank to the Chef for making such a delicious food 😊😊😊.

Thamel area is the primary tourist area in Kathmandu. There are ample hotels catering to all kinds of budgets. Thamel area is quite safe to walk around till 11-12 in the night and has regular police patrols. However, do not plan to buy things from here as they are really expensive. If you look around a bit you will find places where the same things are being sold for half the price.

Lovely place to visit. Nice stupa with all that accompanies Buddhism.
Got some great photos of the surrounding valley. A must see in Kathmandu!
Incredible view in a lovely setting with great coffee and food. Sit and watch flocks of paragliders over the lake and the occasional one that goes in. The food here is some of the best around.

We like the room, but the bathroom gets wet allover after every shower. Also they run out of water one time. Front desk seems disorganized. Breakfast could be improved as well. They have a good head waitress and service at breakfast was outstanding.
0R2k is very nice restaurant they serve very delicious food very nice place to have vegetarian food at 0R2k.

We had an absolutely wonderful experience at KGH Waterfront Resort! The serene lakeside location, comfortable rooms, and peaceful ambiance made our stay truly memorable.

What stood out most was the exceptional hospitality and support we received from the staff. A special thank-you to Sabina, Chiz, Binita, Santa, and Alishwa for their outstanding assistance, warm smiles, and professionalism throughout our stay. They went above and beyond to ensure every detail was perfect and that we felt genuinely cared for.

We highly recommend KGH Waterfront Resort to anyone visiting Pokhara — it’s the perfect blend of comfort, natural beauty, and heartfelt service. We will definitely be returning!

Slightly dated Museum but logically laid out and trying to cover a lot of information from across the world. Comparison of the peaks in Nepal was interesting as was the section on the the 7 peaks. Perhaps more storyboard information about all of their first ascents and photography would be better. Similarly. The ticket office clerk had no change whatsoever.

I visited Kathmandu twice in the 1990's and thought it was one of Asia's great lost magical places. I was horrified at what it has become. Noisy beyond belief, deadly air pollution, traffic jams and a sense of greed and low level scams palque the tourism industry. The trekking/insurance scam is a disgrace. Rat poo in visitors food to garner a benefit off insurance companies? Nepal has entered a new low in tourist rip off's..

A delightful quiet walk for morning stretch and evening sunset pics. The south end of the lake, near the outlet, has a boat rental business, as well as the business in the center of Lakeside waterfront. Buy oranges from Tibetan women, then head back to the hotel.
people are used to see too many tourist but it is also the departure of paraglading ...

Beautiful, authentic, clean hotel located in the heart of Thamel. Extremely helpful staff who are very attentive. As it was cold outside the staff went into our room and put on the electric blanket and placed a hot water bottle inside so when we came back in from the cold we were very cosy! A perfect place to stay in Kathmandu!

We headed here after seeing great reviews on TripAdvisor. The food that came out was sensational - absolutely delicious!! Full of flavour and colour and the serving size is huge. The price is cheap as well. 

The VERY BIG downside to this place is the smoking inside. We had a smoker 2 tables away from us who continually blew smoke in our direction and it ruined our dinner. This is unacceptable in modern restaurants and I will not be returning until smoking is banned. 

The service is standard - it took a long time to have our finished plates cleared and we had to actually call someone over to order a drink. It is very busy inside and everyone is crammed in. Being a vegetarian restaurant, there are a lot of stinky, unwashed hippies in there as well. 

Overall, great food. The place has potential, but the smoking, service and clientele need a fair bit of work.

This is one of the popular shopping area in Kathmandu and attracts most of the tourist for shopping. The market has local shops and sales complete range of product for all age including garments, shoes, jewellery, gifts wooden at reasonable price. 

A must place to visit when you in Kathmandu and looking for good stuff without spending lot of money.
We got up at 5am and trekked up to one of the observation points. The sun lit up the mountain range.... a must see if you are in Nepal.
For the entrance fee we paid, we expected a bit more of the museum. All in all the expeditions looked old and need in our opinion some modernisations.

We arrived prior to the dinner rush and upon arrival were underwhelmed. The doorman did not look up from his phone to greet us and only nodded when we asked for a table. Our waiter was less than attentive and playing on his phone. The bartender played with his beard non-stop and another member of staff drank straight from  the communal water jug on the bar. Halfway through our meal we joked it must be a non-verbal restaurant as no one had actually spoken to us yet. We had to chase a waiter to get our bill and leave. The platter was delicious but we didnt stay for a main due to the issues outlined above. We had much better interactions with other nearby establishments such as Forest and Plate.

Room was overheated and option for reducing the temperature was not working. Rather than giving other room they advised to open the window and switch off the heating. Nothing worked and whole night we were suffocating, thought to spend night in the lobby. Additionally door to the room didn’t lock itself and it can easily opened by a push on door. Really felt so vulnerable. Has not expected this poor quality from Raddission.
Beautiful temple up high with great views looking down at Kathmandu valley. Entertaining monkeys everywhere - just don’t try to lay out a picnic!

We loved this place, the location with amazing views of the lake and surrounding mountains, and the very chilled comfy sitting areas-indoor low cushions and tables or outdoor tables and chairs.
Service was ok, few confused waiters but the food made up for it.
We ordered Vegetable pakoras,Peanut sandeko -nepali speciality,Falafels and fresh
Carrot and beetroot juice and mixed fruit juice and best dessert of chocolate souffle with fresh home made ice cream!
The portions are big and choice of food is amazing.
Best vegetarian place in Pokhara.
They also do free movie nights on certain days so worth going in evening to chill out!
Highly recommended!

I was excited to visit the museum however it was average. We only stayed an hour. There are some interesting posters of information but I think you could learn more or if not just as much by reading some of the better mountaineering books or online. I wouldn't recommend it for children either as it is just large panels of written text.

We booked a 3 night stay for end-April 2011. The location is within walking distance of the lake, along a dirt path, which we would not recommend walking alone late at night. The Temple Tree was built on a small plot of land and this shows because everything was very cramped. The rooms and washrooms are ridiculously small, the latter in particularly poorly lit. It was done with plenty of design factors in mind but the execution was poor.

We were put on a 1st floor room right outside the pool. At 8am in the morning we were woken by the sound of labourers working away (hammers, chisels, lots of talking) and the sound of kids screaming in the pool. The distance between the balcony and the pool is so close I could have literally jumped into it. I opened the curtain to see what the noise was all about and 3 workers who were taking a cigarette break turned to look right back at me; luckily I was dressed!

After that we were just fed up with the whole experience and decided to find somewhere else because we could not imagine 2 more nights here. We contacted reception who said no problem, we can check out early. On this basis we made arrangements to move to the Shangri-La. However, at check-out we were told by the desk manager to pay for all 3 nights (at USD150 a night). After a bit of haggle and the realisation that the hotel did not have any of our credit card info or a deposit, we paid for the one night and left. We suggest that anyone still considering Temple Tree not to leave any credit card details in case they want to leave early!

On the plus side things are quite new and the decor is very different compared to other, more "corporate" hotels.  The staff were on the whole genuinely friendly people, with the exception of the concierge (who basically saw only dollar signs and was very rude when he figured out that we knew better).

We initially thought that this hotel was associated with the hotel chain of the same name from Thailand but were told on check-in that this was not the case - they are completely unrelated.

A great place to wander the shops and cafes of  Kathmandu . Every kind of souvenier  can be found here along with accomodation  and top cafes,  allow  at least a few hours  for a visit  as you will find it hard not to want to  check out all the interesting  shops. A must see area of Kathmandu
Probably the coziest resort in pokhara, the service and management of rooms, swimming pools and food were incredibly done and we had a pleasant experience!

Here a new part for me almost unknown of most of the tourists who have only few minutes to visit Swayambhu temple. Therefore take your time , at least half a day and go to the far back of this temple and discover ....Buddhapark....an other quiet place in Kathmandu.

Great, friendly service from reception, and a bright airy room, which was big and had a good sized shared balcony, sold me this place.

the promises of 24 hour hot water didnt materialise though, so have to know points off for this, plus the water smelts so metalic. this was the same in the other budget joing - pariwar b and b so it might just be the area.

there was some dog earedness, and the bed was one of the most hard and uncomfortable ive slept on.

a 5.5 /10 based on receptions helpfulness and the size and feel of room in the daytime.
Was really not expecting a museum of such a high calibre. The whole place was simply fascinating and importantly presented a balanced view including some of the challenges of the Himalayas.

This is the old part of Kathmandu.  It is a collection of temples and government offices.  Many are in disrepair due to the 2015 earthquake and long term neglect.  International organizations are funding much of the repair work.  There are many religious festivals and government functions that merit a visit.
This is a market place for anyone that requires mementoes or keepsakes in memory of their trip. Make sure to bargain with the locals...it is expected

My three sons and I spent several nights at KGH both before and after our Base Camp Trek.  During our first stay we appreciated the service of the staff and the peaceful oasis it provided from the madness of Kathmandu.  During our second visit, after the trek, we loved the feeling of luxury compared with the tea houses we had become used to.

The size and quality of the rooms vary as do the views from the rooms.  During our first stay our rooms over looked the beautifully landscaped gardens of the hotel.  During our second stay our rooms looked out onto the streets of Kathmandu.

The coffee shop and restaurant are very good.  The coffee is excellent as are the iced coffees.  We discovered a delicacy in the restaurant consisting of cubes of cottage cheese cooked in a tandoori oven.  Absolutely delicious.  We had been told that the breakfast buffet was excellent.  It wasn't included in our room rate but we decided to try it anyway on our last morning there.  Unfortunately it was somewhat disappointing.  It should be said that while the food in the hotel is very reasonably priced by Western standards, it is expensive by Kathmandu standards so if you are feeling a little adventurous, there are many bakeries, cafes and eateries within a few minutes walk of the hotel walls.

Overall our visits were very enjoyable and we wouldn't hesitate to stay at KGH again should we ever return to Kathmandu.

Its a good place to spend an hour or two if you are staying in Pokhara for a few days. The exhibition is a bit disorganised but you can get a feeling of what they want to tell. The location is a bit far from the lakeside (we walked there, but wouldnt do it again), the taxi back costed 400.
A beautiful location to photograph. The boats, light and water. Cannot be beaten. Plenty of bars and restaurants to sit outside while you people watch those on the promenade or on the boats.
I spent the morning walking around the lake and having lunch there before my Yoga class. I found the lake a beautiful place and the facilities just right

The International Mountain Museum is the place to go to learn about the mountains you’ve been admiring. The museum contains three main exhibition halls: Hall of Mountain People, Hall of Fame and Hall of World Mountains. There are numerous exhibits dedicated to the famous Nepal peaks and the mountaineers who climbed them, along with interesting displays about the life of mountain people. A short 18-minute documentary film runs on a regular schedule. When we checked our watch, we were surprised to find almost 2 hours had flown by. If you’re planning to trek, this place will get you in the mood!

need to do better in food verity , and improve  room services, if you are western and asian, you will get bore eating everyday indian food, if you are indian you will be heaven, overall is great location and nice place stay in busy city.
Theres literally many things for all the desires when you come here! You will pick and choose what you love and you will find it. Must visit and must see place!
There is a LOT of information in this museum but unfortunately it’s not made very interestingly. You’ll come across all the famous mountaineers along with their date of summit and pictures.

Went out on the lake in small boats for 3 people.  Although the shore was extremely busy, once on the water it became very peaceful. This is where we got our first glimpse of the snow capped Himalayas.  
The evening atmosphere is great down by the bars on the shore.

Crowded and dusty like any other place in KTM. Done of the buildings for quite damaged during the 2015 earthquake and area no longer open to public. You need to pay am entrance fee of Rs1000. There are numerous houses offering their services, but you don't really need them as the place is not that big and as long as you read the flyer they provide you at the entrance or have a lonely planet with you, it will be more than enough
One of the great place to visit in kathmandu. Close to the thamel and walking distance from hotel I stayed
For the cost of entry of 1000 NPR, I personally found this place to be underwhelming and it seems that tickets are not checked nor enforced and there were people who got in without paying.

This may not be for people interested in just light tourist fare, but we found it fascinating. The origin of the Himalayas, descriptions of the dress, religion, and culture of the various mountain people.  And of course mountaineering history. 
It's a little out of the way, so one easy way to get there is to get a car from your hotel for the round trip.  They'll quote a round trip price which includes the driver waiting in his car for the 2 or 3 hours you'll be there.  The lot was full of waiting drivers when we arrived. Waiting is what they're used to.  Hint:  give all your drivers good tips; it's the right thing to do.

Expect the best and worst when entering.   Lots of aggressive street hawkers, but at the same time, there are some amazing food stalls and restaurants in the area.  It's all a bit of a gamble in terms of where and what to prioritize.  Do your research and everything should be fine.  Highly recommend walking as much as one can depending on the ground level pollution.  Lots of nooks and crannies.

The place was amazing. The temples were fascinating.
we reached around 5:30 PM. Saw the Kiosk selling entry tickets. Asked the Ladies if we had to buy tickets, she said yes and we bought 6 tickets.
Latter we came to know the tickets were for museum entry and the museum closes at 5:00 PM.
The Ladies sold us tickets at 5:30 knowing fully that we could not use them.
CHEATING at Official Level.

I hiked up a few days ago. It was clear when I started out but the weather clouded over before I reached the view point. I walked up from Sedi Bagar, which I found to be a little challenging because the path and the rock steps were slippery with leaves. Coming down was harder than going up. I do recommend having a hiking pole of some sort. If you want the view, plan ahead and leave really early in the morning.
The hotel is one of the most peaceful place in Pokhara. The ambience is wonderful and the swimming pool is one of the best in Pokhara.
Phewa lake gives a pleasant boating experience. Situated in city limits of Pokhara, this is one of the must try activities.

I am not a very spiritual person but I did enjoy this place...sure it’s dusty and polluted like all of Katmandu but the views are beautiful the people are lovely and this just do their thing and you do yours which is how it should be

Never ever thought the best feel at home experience i would receive out of my country. Everything i thought would be hard to handle,became so easy ,thanks to the Hotel. Be it comfortable sleep,local travels,guidence to the sight seeing,medical facility,i was at perfect place.

We arrived at Sarangkot view points around 06:00 am. Try to reach early as lot of vehicles go there at early morning and chances of jam is also there. Once sunrise starts, you can see clear view of Annapurna ranges and Machhapuchhre. Amazing experience. There are shops at top where you can enjoy your tea-coffee with snow peaked mountain view.

If you are looking for a nice atmosphere with good Middle Eastern food.. this is the place to go for your dinner! We had the OR2K combo platter which is a good selection of Middle Eastern dishes and we loved it! This place it is worth a visit if you are in Pokhara!

I can't stress enough how good this place is. They offer fabulous service and amazingly large meals. I'd rate this one higher than its sister outlet located in Thamel, purely because of the amazing location located near the banks of the river. Do yourself a favour and spoil yourself in Polkhara for a night.
A great place to chill, have milk tea, coffee, lunch, read a book, etc. Mountain view, cosy atmosphere what more can you ask for!!! Friendly staff and good service. A must go to place in Pokhara!

Amazing lake in Pokhara valley with beautiful view of snow clad Mountains in the north, beautiful forest in the south and TalBarahi Temple in the middle of the lake make it a real heaven. As I heard from tourists and local, it is regarded as the hub for honeymoon trip. Reflection of world famous mountain like Annapurna And Machhapuchhre( fishtail) lures people around the globe. A must visit in Nepal and especially in Pokhara.

The location of the hotel was convenient as it was in the downtown. There are two blocks in the hotel cross the road from each other. The staff in the reception of main hotel sent us to the other block and vice versa. We booked a twin room and we were given king room. We waited in the reception area more than 1/2 hour to resolve this issue. The staffs behind the reception desk were busy chatting themselves rather than helping the guests (typical customer service in Nepal).

this hotel s really good, the food is awesome, room are really amazing and service is in the top level. i do prefer to refer people to check in so they can experience the level based hospitality and you will enjoy it for sure
Absolutely loved the sunrise  at sarankot hill. We can see amazing view of Anapurna range. Worth to spend time to come here.

The Radisson Hotel Kathmandu was my least favorite of three properties I used on this years vacation.
I had requested a twin bedded room, and on arrival fairly late in the evening was  told we were "upgraded" to the new Tower, located across the parking lot. If this was an upgrade from the main building I would worry about the quality of those rooms. Room size and cleanliness was ok, but we were given a king rather than twin.
In fairness when I raised this question the following day I was offered a change, but on a two night stay chose to remain.
Restaurant was clean and breakfast was good. I didn't try other meals as the menu was high compared to the local restaurants.
My other concern was a slightly racist response when I entered the lobby with my Nepali companion- he was challenged by the doorman and told to report to reception. We did straighten it out with a sort of apology, but it left a bad taste.
Probably would not return there as there are better options.

The pictures have been very inviting so that we gave OR2K a chance for dinner time. The place is very cosy and having a look on the glowing menu you are sure to have made the perfect decision for the evening. However, the food has been 50/50, meaning that one dish was ok and the other one (vegetable sizzler - pictures are uploaded too) just awful. The fries! looked sickening and the overall presentation would have been enough for not even start eating it. As veggie places seem to be getting overall great reviews for just being veggie I really want to let this other people know. My dish (some kind of Arabic plate) by the way was fine but nothing spectacular - the sweet yoghurt dressing wasn't self made for example. The self made drinks have been great, ambience also but service not very attentive and the food we already talked about. People next to us made the same experience. Overall a nice place which is missing more passion for veggie food.
If you are party person then you will definitely love it. There are dozens of nice clubbing bar here. Good music , lighting, good food. Live music was just wow.
Everything was excellent, the food was fantastic we really enjoyed the swimming with our family. Excellent behaviour of all staffs

Lots of interesting information about Nepal & it's mountains including a good video about the life & nature on the mountains.
It is worth spending a couple of hours walking around-we learned quite a lot!
The toilets were absolutely filthy & let the place down badly which was a shame otherwise, we enjoyed our time here.
Not as large an area or as much to see as I thought there would be. Didnt think it worth 1000rs ticket. Would have liked to see before earthquake.

quite desapointed hotel. stay one night only because located not far from airport as very early flight next morning. located next to a famous stupa  . beside, very old room and hotel. old bathroom. not worth it the price they charge

The Swayambhunath Temple is located high on a hillside in Kathmandu, and because of it's historical significance, it has been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site of which Nepal has ten (10) such UNESCO sites.  To get to this Temple, you can either take the strenuous 365 steps up the hill, or take public transportation up the hill on the backside of the Temple - much easier!

Nice looking temple/stupa on a big hill that overlooks the whole Kathmandu city area - very nice scenery and photo opportunity here at this location.

Paid Rs200 per person as foreigner to come in here so not very expensive. Nice temple with monkeys running around. Bit of a tourist trap as lots of little stalls selling souvenirs though it didn’t detract from seeing this place. Lovely views over the city so worth visiting - we got a taxi and could pay for him to hang around and drive us back, we spent 30 mins here which was more than enough time

The Kantipur Temple House is a beautiful authentic hotel in the centre of Thamel, in a lovely quiet area. The staff is very friendly and helpful.  We had one of the larger rooms, and they are beautifully decorated, with a nice alcove. As we were there in winter, they foresaw a heather in the room, an electric blanket and hot water bottles for the bed. 
The food was also very good: the breakfast buffet, lunch & dinner, the homebrew coffee and definitely try a Nepali dessert. 
Just remember to bring your own shampoo.

This is nice hotel, right in the heart of thamel.  Watch your booking here as we booked and paid big money for a room before our tour started and when we arrived they had no room available, this also happened to another couple in our tour party.  However they did find other accommodation for us.,.the location here is very good
Very good restaurant with tasty food and huge portions. Very nice view over the lake too. We ordered two dishes each and it was hard to finish them among the three of us. Would come back definitely!!

My partner is disabled and uses crutches and we wondered if we would be able to manage this, but we did it slowly. We ate at the roof top café and were amused by a monkey stealing the sugar jar and taking it off to bash it open and eat it's contents. The fried momos were very nice as was some sugary lemon drink I had.   On a more serious note it was quite sad to see people giving the monkeys sweets wrapped in paper which they adeptly opened, and watch the monkeys drink from discarded pop bottles. I am not very religious, so maybe failed to capture the religious aura, but thought that any religion that attracted so many followers could have paid more respect to fellow creatures.
This the area for restaurants and nightlife but ultimately it's loud and dirty with little charm. Maybe I would prefer this area if I was 20 year old backpacker but sadly, I'm not.

Dear Sir /Madam

Good morning. 
we are the world Hyatt member and most of the time, when we travel oversea, and our first choice will be Hyatt hotel, because we have stayed in Mumbai, Malaysia, Beijing china, Chennai. The environment and service will be excellent. However, this time we travel to Nepal and as usual we book hotel in Hyatt regency Kathmandu unfortunately, we had a very bad experience with Hyatt regency Kathmandu Nepal. Only the entrance view is nice. 
We stayed for 3 nights with 4 days. 
1.	Our room water supply was very bad - water flow very slow (we unable to shower with hot water flow with hot suddenly change to cold and back to hot again) I brought my 2 years old son I found it so unhappy with it.

2.	We found lizard in the room while we sleeping at 1am. we manage to take picture as a proof. 

3.	Same break first menu for every day, no much variety to choose. 

I think this will be the worse stay in Hyatt. Very much disappointing. After this Hyatt wonâ??t be our first choice of hotel anymore. Hyatt Regency Kathmandu Nepal not up to standard for us to spend our money. Only the front desk people were good. out of it the rest was horrible.
