Having many allergies, this place was able to accommodate me with gluten free meals and also gave me the chance of having something vegan too! Super yummy, though a little more on the pricier side
Unless 50% of your patrons are smokers, I don't see why you have to make at least 50% of the others suffer the taste of harsh tobacco with they are trying to enjoy their meal

The location is perfect which is near to any recommended destination. Our first family trip was more memorable due to the good weather and good room selection. Very safe too. The rooms were clean and comfy. We recommend all the local and international tourists.
Nice stop to get N idea of the climbers and people of olden times.  Not much exile going on.  The video is a must see.  Nice layout of the major mountains in Nepal and Tibet

We stayed at Radisson Kathmandu during our trip to Nepal and was astounding by the service of the hotel. Right from Airport Pick Up, to Check in during stay and Check Out l have never experienced a more professional and brilliantly run hotel. Moreover the thoughtful effects in the room, like a weighing scale for your baggage, toiletries which are replenished without you having to ask, no questions asked currency exchange at the reception are just a few examples of the brilliant service.

We enjoyed staying at this hotel as it is very clean, well located, has a nice atmosphere and most staff are very pleasant. Ajaya and Deep were superb in the restaurant and provided excellent service. However, the spa is chaotic and the treatments are not to the standard for an international traveller. That said they are very reasonably priced. Sagun at reception was rude to deal with though we are not sure why. At first we thought maybe this was cultural difference however by check out it seemed clear that she can just be hostile in dealing with guests.

I was very disappointed by my experience at this restaurant. First and foremost, their online menu is completely out of date. BEWARE: the food costs almost double the prices listed online. This is an incredibly dishonest way to run a business, especially since this is clearly a tourist restaurant getting business from the internet. 

As for the food, I was shocked by how bland the meal was. Have other reviewers eaten middle eastern food before? Or did the cook change? I got falafel with hummus, tahini, Israeli salad, and naan. The only element that I enjoyed was the tahini. The falafel didn't taste freshly cooked and was just average. The hummus was completely bland and tasteless, which is surprising for an Israeli restaurant. Also, the Israeli salad just tasted like cucumber with mildly ripe tomatoes. Overall, the entire experience was very disappointing. To top it off, I was shortchanged on the bill and had to ask them for the correct amount of change; I'm glad that I double-checked.

The only redeeming aspect of the restaurant is their atmosphere. I won't be back though, and would not recommend eating food there.
I don’t getvwhy this place is so famous: I had a very poor couscous and a quite mediocre apple pie. There’s better around Thamel!

Firstly let me say that i am a club carlson member and have been frequently with Radisson in other countries

I was quite surprised with Radisson Kathmandu's service quality
1. Good location 4/5
2. Hospitality : the personnel at the reception are so paranoid. As soon as the customer asks for some service, they first quote a charges for the service like it is a deal in a shop. This is quite a substandard approach
3. Internet is 512kbps but it took over 45 mins to download a file of 3.7mb. for a 5 star business hotel 512 kbps is an insult. 
4. Business Centre acknowledged bad internet but insists on customer to pay per 15 mins use. Again business centre internet is pathetic. 
5. The room provided is in the premium building next to a noisy bar with lots of noise ans loud music the whole night. The windows are also not sound proof. 
6. Ask for help about directions or places to visit and the reception does not help. They direct you to the taxi stand outside . 
7. The food at the coffee shop is average. The cold coffee served had residue of bitter coffee powder. 
8. The bed mattress was hard. The hotel provided hard coir mattress with no custioning. Seemed like sleeping on hard floor. 

The building may be equipped with all advanced features but if the hospitality staff is not upto standards, the very experience is average.

We have stayed in this hotel several times over recent years as it is the start and end point for World Expeditions trips and treks. It always makes me feel comfortable and happy to return to this lovely hotel. The staff are exceptional, very kind and obliging. The trekking company booked a twin room for us but the reception staff managed to get us a double room which was our preference. 

Rooms: 
The rooms are well appointed, spotless, and very comfortable - lovely hot water in the shower without fail. Wifi can be a little slow but most of the time was fine for us. One suggestion for the hotel is to have limitless filtered drinking water for guests - guests are given two bottles a day but this is not enough and generates a lot of plastic waste. 

Dining: 
Breakfast buffet is amazing! There is so much choice which is a little overwhelming after a trek. They do omelettes and eggs cooked to order, and used to do masala dosa to order although on our last visit, this was not advertised. Coffee is percolated coffee unless you pay extra but very nice and bottomless. The TFC restaurant is also a great option for lunch or dinner - prices are reasonable (lunch for two with non-alcoholic drinks cost us 2600 Rs) and the food is very tasty. 

Location:
On my first visit, I thought the location was a bit of a limitation, but now I think it is really ideal. It is a 10-15 minute walk from Thamel along Lazimpat, and just so much quieter than Thamel. The area has lots of embassies, so there are a range of restaurants and cafes around. The street in front of the hotel has a well stocked supermarket, money exchange, laundry service, gift shops and trekking gear shops and there are ATMs nearby. There are some very cool shops on Lazimpat if you walk in the north direction (away from Thamel). It is also a short walk to Durbar Marg, which was really handy as they have a NCell office (for my local SIM) as well as banks and airline offices. There are many shops and fast food restaurants on Durbar Marg. 

Our usual preference is small boutique hotels rather than large international chains but there is something very reliable about Kathmandu Radisson and we have enjoyed our stay here every time. It is expensive compared to guesthouses but in the normal range for a 5 star hotel. We had a very average experience in a Thamel hotel that cost USD 100 per night before transferring to the Radisson and I was wishing I paid a little more for the Radisson - you get what you pay for! Happily recommend this hotel to friends and family, and would definitely stay here again.

We found this place after having eaten at the location in Kathmandu. The food here is absolutely amazing. The hummus is by far the best I've ever eaten. The staff is really my only complaint. I understand slow service when things are busy, which certainly happened. However, there were other times when the restaurant was almost empty, and it seemed like the staff was ignoring us. Still, I cannot give this place less than five stars because the food is just so amazing. Definitely worth eating here if you find yourself in Pokhara.
Stayed at the Butterfly Lodge that was 500m away from Fewa lake in Pokhara. Heaps of restaurants and shops to visit along the lake as well as local market stalls. Definitely worth the visit.
Hotel is well organized and the staff is very courteous. Gym and spa facilities are exceptional. Our breakfast experience was also good.

At the time of our visit (Oct 2019) 1000 rps was over £8, which was an incredible amount to wander round a bunch of buildings that all look the same. There were guides offering to tell you about the buildings, for a fee, but we prefer to wander and absorb atmosphere rather than facts we will forget by the next day, and this didn't fulfill that brief.
Very good quality, service and good hospitality! I recommend going there in your holiday at Pokhara @NABINA @Alisha @Salina @Shaurab

You should pay about 1000 Rupies (10 Euro) to enter the square, most of the people could walk for free. That is a really rip off!
Because in the end, only the western and real chinese looking people are paying, because the rest can walk trough.
The point is not the entrance fee, the point is the hight of it and the fact that it does not look like they use it to rebuild the place! There is not much working there and much of the temples is either support with big wooden boards or is still lying in pieces.
We choose a cafe with a rooftop terrace and simply had a look from there.
Terrible busy streets with spit everywhere. Cars, lorries and people walk on the road. Other tourists skip queues and shop assistants serve them anyway.
Nice Stupa in Town, Great place and hill, Swayambhunath is truly a must-visit place in Kathmandu, as suggested by thousands of travelers.

The Radisson is a standard chain hotel.  The rooms are a little tired; we stayed in the annex.  The breakfast was average but nothing stood out.  I held a workshop there but could not get the staff to post a sign about the location with the result that many participants wasted time searching.  This despite repeated attempts to get them to simply put a sign.  Now having said that, it is located close to the Jazz Club and the French Bistro and I enjoyed these venues rather than the hotel.  There are better top end hotels than this.

Had a really great stay here . Booked a few nights but decided to stay a few weeks instead. 
Staff was extremely friendly and helpful ,specially the manager Sudip ,and the room was very clean .there is an excellent restaurant at the first floor serving good food as well.
Always charming place to walk around and buy the gears for trekking  and climbing while in Kathmandu. Highly recommend to scroll around and enjoy the vibes

Phewa Lake is 2nd largest in Nepal and It is the only lake in Nepal to have a temple Tal Barahi Temple Tal at the central part of lake. It is amazing view when you can see lake, big mountains around. It could be just more friendly for people, more paths for either pedestrians or cyclist around. More places to sit down etc.
Many souvenirs inside the temple.  Also wear a mask, there was a  pungent smell in the air. I guess from monkey and pigeon droppings.

The hotel itself is very beautiful. The pool out front is refreshing and a great place to hang out. The rooms are small but comfy. The included breakfast is not good at all, and not what you'd expect from somewhere so pricey. We also had an issue with the hotel sending a van to the world peace stupa, despite knowing the road was very rough and the van wouldn't make it up. We waited for a long time at the top in the darkness and eventually walked much of the way down the mountain. The hotel did not reduce the price of the van despite our big inconvenience, and we ended up paying three times what a typical taxi charges.
All in all, a decent stay, until we paid the bill and realized this is a very overpriced hotel. There are much better places to stay around Pokhara that cost much less!

First off the garden in the Kathmandu Guest House is AMAZING! Its so peaceful and tranquil that you could literally spend all day either sleeping on the garden bed or simply reading a book.
This hotel has a buzzing atmosphere and I met tons of other travellers here. The buffet breakfast is real good value for money and tasty too!
My room although in the older part of the hotel was comfortable, clean and had good facilities (flat screen tv, free wifi etc). Hotel location is excellent, although as it is right in the heart of Thamel it can be overwhelming to go from the hotel to the busy streets in a blink. the guards at the front gate at the hotel are awesome: so funny and friendly.

However I was woken up by the building work currently going on next door every morning and hotel is very expensive compared to others in the area that offer same facilities. I would not recommend using the hotel travel agent.

Very very touristy. One of the vendors at the top tried charging me $400 USD for a singing bowl and when I politely told him no and that I would not do business with someone like who would be that greedy he continued to follow me around. 
Nice view but won't be going back in a hurry

Absolute must visit for Pokhara visitors. The lake shore offers a great variety of restaurants , bars and pub. Along the shore you can find some place quiet and spend the day or hang out with friends over drinks. This is one of my favorites in Pokhara. Simply, just love strolling beside the lake or watch it and soothe me

The staff were fantastic and room was spacious enough. loved the grounds and the terrace cafe. Sadly, the spa looked a little worn out and didnâ??t really match Hyattâ??s standards. The lockers were in a sorry state, towels had rusty color stain spots and the shampoo and shower gel both had funky smell like phenol. Also, The jacuzzi didnâ??t work and the toilet looked yellowish, had a strong deet smell. I really hope the management steps up and makes some changes. It is sad that this part of the hotel has been overlooked.

Not cheap by traveller standards. Get you guide to book or you will pay tourist price which is double. No backpacker accom here since earthquake.
Check you room before you unpack. First room had no phone working. Second room had no lights in bathroom. Final got a room on groudfloor. Others were on 3 with no lift. 
Still expect power cuts by generator cuts in. However when gen on no heating.....

Pokhara is a very beautiful city with mountains, lake, and fresh air. The view of Annapurna and Machhapuchhre is like a picture. Phewa Lake is calm and shining, perfect for boat ride. The city has many nice cafes, small shops, and friendly people. Morning and evening here feel peaceful and give special memory in heart.

I'm sorry to say that we expected to have very nice rooms in this hotel however we found cockroach in the rooms and cabinet and had to change the rooms. The hotel location is perfect and next to the main street, restaurants and local market. I prefer to try another hotel once I'm in Kathmandu. The food was very delicious in the hotel and they offered us 30% discount and airport transfer for free due the cockroach issue we had.

The hotel is on the best place. Very central. The room was great and very clean. Breakfast was perfect. Very good choice of sour and sweet food. People was very friendly. As specialy the receptionist was very helpfull, handsome and very cute. Her smile is wonderful😊

"A must destination island" for a restaurant in Pokhara? This may sound unusual or even won't make sense, but through my eyes it is exactly like that.
Location is super, right in the middle of main lakeside street overlooking the magnificent views of Phewa lake and the hills at the horizon. If you are sitting/resting inside on the cushions you will see it through the large window and if you are outside and the weather is clear (aim for breakfast before 9am before clouds are built up over the mountains) you will see the Himalaya summits above the hills.
The food is great as in OR2K Kathmandu. A sure bet for freshness, variety and some unique touches of Middle Eastern cuisine (Shakshuka, Falafel, Hummus and more... even Jachnun on Fridays and Saturdays). The coffee is as good as at home and the salads are generously served, which can fulfill any need for a light and healthy whole meal (try the Fatush salad).
Atmosphere is chilled and easy going all day. Travellers are meeting, socializing, exchanging information, reading a book, writing their notes, playing cards and it seems time is not an issue at all. Background music played has huge variety and fits perfectly to the whole concept of the place.
Prices are a bit on the upper side and in order to eat meet you will need to go some place else, but these are just FYI and nothing to damage the concept an completeness of this place.

So why an island? Just because this is so different than other places in Pokhara and whenever you want all that package you can just go to another dimension for a while in OR2K.
I ate majority of my breakfasts there and a dinner. As you can understand from my review I recommend to visit OR2K (at least once) while in Pokhara.
Enjoy!

Float above the waters or allow yourself to sink below the abyss, the Fewa Lake offers a peaceful place that can guide you to your soul if you let it. The sound of the rowing oar a clue to your next move. The still lake surface a reflection of self. Don't hesitate to get lost in the experience and come out on the other shore, reborn.

This hotel is centrally located and staff are great. Food is good. Just be sure to ask for a non-smoking room if you don't smoke. There is also an additional restaurant in the hotel but unfortunately it's Olive Garden of all choices in the world!!

Good view for take photo and have wayside market near pier. Almost people come this pier in order to go Tal Barahi Temple for making ritual or pray for good luck. Have only one way to go this temple by boat because this temple located center of river.

Fare: All people who get in boat must rent life jacket 10 RPN, fare depend on boat type and quantity (you can ask staff at pier).

Another must-visit site in Kathmandu. I like to go early Saturday morning with the kids, who love seeing the monkeys everywhere and throwing the coins in the pool. Lots of steps and beautiful views if it's a clear day.

Fewa Lake is extremely pretty. Full of small boats, all powered by man pedalling or using an oar, keeping free from noise and the extra pollution that oil or Diesel engine bring. One can either get a boat to go to the temple in the small island, simply explore the lake or get off at the path to three to the work peace stupa. Alongside the borders of the lake there are many restaurants and bars, serving food and drinks with the nicest view. I totally recommend a visit to the lake!

After renovations that had been necessary after the big earthquake Monkey Temple is a great place to visit again. Parts of the site are still under construction but the atmosphere is great and the view is breathtaking, especially in the morning hours. If you like monkeys, this is the right place but be careful, sometimes they can be quite aggressive and try to steal whatever they see.

Lake is very beautiful and had lots of food joints to spend a quality time you can have drinks music and find new friends 
But don’t forget to go little further to see a beautiful Aarti offering to GOD

Perhaps when it opened, it deserved a five-star rating, but today, after staying there three separate times on my recent visit to Nepal (upon arrival Kathmandu, after returned from Pokhara and after returned from Bhutan), I can definitely say it needs a reno. Dated, with old-style furnishings (my fave the air dryer attached to the wall that has limited output with a button required to hold to keep on), the beds were pretty awful. The rooms themselves are spacious and clean. We had a suite on two occasions, one with an upstairs bedroom (seriously dangerous as the floors are slippery and the treads narrow), and another also spacious, both ample. You can choose a stupa facing room (but probably not worth it as stupa is in the distance and not much to see from afar). Staff is very helpful; public spaces absolutely lovely. ATM didn't work. Restaurants decent, and offer a variety of cuisines. Ample expansive breakfast. Not their fault, but drive from airport to hotel is an experience with the roads particularly nasty, rutted. Large shopping mall outside hotel grounds, but a trek from hotel itself to the street.

Very good start of our trip in Nepal. Former monastery vibes, traditional architecture. Beautiful hotel,I highly recommend to stay here. The bed was confortable, rooms are silent and the staff is kind.

Boat trips on the lake with local rowers , trips to the hindu temple island and just walking along the shore - all ways to enjoy this serene part of the Pokhara environment . there's quite a bit of wildlife and the shore opposite the city is mainly unspoilt - the lake is a major asset to Pokhara and the area

The lakes are beautiful just a shame no seems to care about all the rubbish around the waters edge.  There are a number of cafes where you can take in the view but I would recommend taking one of the boats and just canoe around for a while.  We found the main entrance where most of the boats are is quite expensive especially if you only what to go out for 30min.  The staff were also quite rude.  We found a up the street there were a number of other venders and they were much cheaper and way more pleasant.

It was very pretty and relaxing being rowed around the lake with the moutains surrounding you.  I think you can also swim in the lake not sure I would actually do this as the watewr is very dirty.
These are very historic buildings. The earthquake of 2015 has damaged alot of them but as they are being fixed up, they are looking splendid. Pay 1000 rupees and get away from the tourist.
Everything was really good. Had a comfortable stay. Highly recommended for a family stay. Food and other facilities were top notch

Not very friendly streets for the tourist in terms of noise, dust and all type of vehicles on the same way (normally no sidewalks so even walkers). There are some streets where motorbikes and cars are not allowed which are much more convenient
Must visit....,the view of the range is great... People are polite and helpful. .... They allowed my pet dog to go for a boat ride as well

Good hotel centrally located. Staff are very warm and genuinely helpful during our stay hosting our Asia Pacific conference. The breakfast spread is great and I tasted one if the best egg omelettes by Chef Manita. It was so good I ended up having it every morning. Thank you and keep up the great standard.
I would suggest arranging for a guide to visit this square as there is so much history and stories about every single thing you will see there. Very busy.

I had thought this wold be a tribute to Everest and the climbing teams lost on its slopes. In fact it was a good display of the native mountain people of the area and a tribute to mountaineers the world over. Only 1/2 the hall is in use so plenty of room to expand in the future.

The many previous reviews cover this attraction well. I have been here five times. This is a huge Buddhist temple complex that overlooks Kathmandu valley and affords great views. Worth seeing, but know what you are in for as a Westerner. Be aware and expect the following as part of a unique cultural experience: 
1. Filthy and smelly. Litter everywhere. 
2. Monkeys running amok everywhere.
3. Beggars and solicitors will target you relentlessly. 
4. You will walk through monkey and cow manure.
5. Watch for monkeys and other pickpockets!
6. The beggars are professional and relentless.
7. Great art and trinkets shops near the stupa.!
8. The hawkers will try to guess your religion and sell you an appropriate trinket.
9. You are viewed as a profit opportunity. You will be charged more for everything. Do not be offended. The admission is well worth it.
Why would I recommend going? Because you will not see another Buddhist temple complex like this one anywhere else in the world. The views of Kathmandu valley, the cultural experience and beauty is stunning and well worth the climb and price of admission.

Top notch customer service. The staff there make you feel Royal. Professional, caring and respectful staff. Excellent in-room services, they make sure every need of your family is addressed with their best quality of services and care. They always make sure rooms are clean and their staff observe infection prevention measures whenever they interact with us.

As you enter the temple area you immediately see scores of monkeys which are quite entertaining to watch. They even sell monkey food to feed the animals. However, the temple area is quite large and there is plenty to see of artistic value. Since the main temple is at the top of a hill there are many stairs to climb but with outlooks or things of interest to see along the way. The main temple and structures around it are impressive and well worth the climb.

This is indeed a good resort. Being a bit away from the main road, it is a quiet and pleasant place. The gardens add to the charm. It has a poolside area and a fairly good restaurant. The rooms are cosy and well kept and the bathrooms clean. The shower area could however do with an upgrade. Water tends to spread over....
Kudos however to the staff who are wonderful. There is a market nearby with a host of restaurants and a variety of shops.
The staffs are very polite and cooperative the ambience of the resort is very pleasing Recommended to all friends and family already
Intresting place to enjoy golden sunshine and majestic mountain around it. Need to develop infrastructure.
If you have limited time in Kathmandu, this is one of the places you should fit in. It is 30 minutes walk from Thamel area of Kathmandu. It offers great views of the city.

The team at Radisson Kathmandu went out of their way the make my stay absolutely memorable. Surprise cake for my birthday and delivered to my room. Every single member of staff helped in making me feel at home and been extremely helpful throughout the entire stay, and made all aspects of my life easier and more comfortable. It is much appreciated! Rajiv Upadhyaya and SUNAM SHRESTHA have even managed to support me in getting PCR test at the hotel premises and last-minute helping me fill online Airsuvidha to travel back to India. Special thanks  Sunam & the team. I will be back and recommend it to friends and family, Namaste!

kind of attraction in Pokhara, but nothing special. ordinary lake with children throwing garbage to water, cows and few uncomfortable benches around. nice place to sit on the grass and write postcards.

The hotel was very welcoming. The room was comfortable. However, several messages left at the front desk were never relayed nor were the names of callers. Used plates removed from the room were left in the corridor for over 6 hours.

One of the must visit monuments while you are in Kathmandu.
This Buddist stupa atop a small hillock is a cluster of temples with concentric gold rings on the spire.
The visitors and the locals are well behaved and do not pestered you to buy the souvenirs in the many shops in the top.
Even the monkeys respect your privacy and leave you alone.
However, the visitors seem to feed the benign monkeys inspite of clear warmings not to feed them.
The driver cum guide drove the sports car upto the parking space.
One has to climb 113 steps to reach the top.
A quiet place to contemplate life.
You need to climb down 92 steps to reach the parking space.
Beautiful religious monument.
Recommended.

I stayed in a 3 floor, double room for 5 nights. The staff were always helpful and pleasant, the breakfast was good (although a bit variable depending on what time you got there), and the facilities were clean and pleasant.
Not quite 5* rating as there were a few annoyances which did not help - small things like the shower head being completely bunged up,  the air conditioning being underpowered, and one of the lights in a wardrobe never switching off (giving an odd eerie glow at night!). Overall however I was well looked after and comfortable, so can't grumble!

Thamel street  has many shops that sell trekking items; souvenirs and kashmir products. Lots o restaurants for all kind of eaters. You have to bargain a lot and double check the items you bought. We bargained for  a chess game made of wood and at the hotel we found he gave us only a wooden box with no use at all(same shape though ) Next day we didn't find him
Most of the places are renovating now, local market called ason is one of the special place to visit, the area is covered by many temples which are still good to see.
It's interesting. Many monkeys.Many vendors.Interesting view from above. An old and typical religious buildings.
Located in middle of kathmandu, It is the amazing place to view the beautiful valley. You may find lots of monkey there.

Area in the heart of Kathmandu showing the history. The area was being renovated when we visited however this made it more authentic as it showcased the damage caused by recent earthquakes. Mainly filled with locals and backpacking tourists. There is also a market area and museum which are both pleasant. Would recommend getting a spot in one of the roof bars which overlook the square for sunset.

Would note the area has a cost to enter which is poorly managed and applies before 7pm for tourists only. There is no queue checking everyone’s ID or real signage when entering the square to tell you this. A few low metal thresholds which you can cross signifying you are entering the square and booths around the courtyard collect the toll. The system means that most people just walk on by and the guards will whistle or run after people (who they feel, slightly raciest) should be paying and check if they have a ticket. After 7pm the square is free and definitely worth a visit.
This became our preffered cafe in Pokhara for about 5 days.Views of the Annapurna range and overlooking Lake Fewa.Excellent food and service by the very friendly staff.Highly recommended.

The Durbar Square is a complex of old and interesting temples, palaces and courtyards  which showcase the religious and cultural life of the people. The architecture of the old buildings are so ornate and beautiful,  like the Khumari-ghar,  it is decorated with fine woodcarving. If all of the old buildings are fully restored, labeled with descriptions, shops orderly arranged and cleanliness is maintained, the Square will be a great attraction in Nepal.

Returning from Annanapurna Base Camp, we visited Swayambhunath stupa. The stupa is a World Heritage site and certainly worth the visit. As stupa is very holy place for buddhist. We got the most beautiful views. Highly recommend this place for visit in Kathmandu.
The breakfast was very good the members staffs are very amazing thé room was fantastic as the facilities as well the service very good too

Clean and excellent service from Radisson in KsthKathm - well done. No issues encountered during 7 nights stay. 
Staff were friendly, polite and respectful through out the stay. An exemplar service offered.

The hotel was booked through a travel agent as part of a trip itinerary. Large comfortable double room with features in line with local culture. Fresh drinking water provided in a metal jug. Good choice buffet breakfast. Highly recommended.
We visited or2k multiple times and it was constantly perfect. Awesome vibes, service and food. The menu is very comprehensive even for vegans and very well priced for the quality.

An extremely exceptional experience, and the service was more than wonderful from all the hotel staff. The communication was outstanding, and the welcome was as well. I recommend going to the hotel and enjoying its atmosphere.Thank you sagar pandey especially for great hospitality.

Pokhara, being on top of the adventure list for travellers in Nepal should never worry about choosing lakeside retreat for several reasons: 
- peace and serenity within the town 
- a wonderful view of the glaziers from the balcony 
- great food 
- amazing spa to an end of a tiring day 
- close proximity to shopping and all sight seeing areas. Can never forget how much walking I did during these days.

Specifically wish to mention why we chose lakeside retreat.. Manmohan Rimal, the youngest and the most vibrant front office manager will not leave you with a choice until you choose to stay there :) 
He was extremely proactive and hospitable before we even met him person. When i was worried about choosing a place, I approached the hoteliers around Pokhara and Manmohan was the first to respond. He kept in touch ever since and guided us from transport, sight seeing, city tour, food and most important safety. thank you so much and we wish you all the best. 
Last of all, lots of credit to Pansha Himal Singh the guide and driver for the hotel who was the best ever guide we had during our sight seeing. He was with us at every spot and explained about every location which also made us safe. 

Overall Pokhara is still in my mind and I will definitely return back soon. We indeed made friends.

The dtay at Temple Tree was absolutley amazing. 
The rooms were smoothing and we had a pleasant time in the pool.
The spa was veey relaxing and fulfilling.
Manita was very generous and helpful.
All staffs were polite and punctual.
We would definetly come again and stay with with Temple Tree Resorts.
Thankyou and see you again.

Food is defintitely great as well as the overall ambience. However, the service that was extended to asians are simply underpar compare to the westerners. I was there earlier and got a table later sames goes to the food order where my order was taken earlier compare to a table who arrived later than us. All in all, I hope they know that asians are also deserving customer who pay for the food and demand for similar service! I truly hope the management would look into this.

The Hyatt Regency is a 5-star hotel considered among the best hotels in Kathmandu. It sits on an immense property which if it was managed properly would be a lovely hotel. We were really surprised that the hotel does not seem to maintain cleanliness standards at all. There were simple things like the public areas and bathrooms which were dirty. Floors and carpets that could quickly be cleaned were left messy and unclean. The many gardens of the hotel have potential to look nice but instead have no well designed trees, grass or flowers.  It seems nothing is being done to make the property look nice or clean!

The management team of Hyatt needs to pay some serious attention to hire some cleaners and landscapers. As many reviews have mentioned, hotel also needs to update its rooms as well. It's a shame this beautiful property is not being well maintained.

Interesting place to walk around but gets a little repetitive. There are monkeys walking around and stray dogs so we had to dodge the poop! Even though this is an outdoor area it can get very smokey. Lots of stalls located throughout with people selling various items.  Glad we went but I probably wouldnt go back if visiting.
It is one of world heritage sights identified by unesco famous as monkey temple as lot of monkeys and lot of stairs on the height

It's beyond my expectations. I had attend one week yoga retreats there. I have only one regret I couldn't stay longer in this paradise. All people were smiling and very welcoming. I made lots of friends from many different countries. We could feel there whole world is connecting together. Teacher are very skilled and helpful. Knowledge I gain in short period of  time is very valuable and life changing.

I left Fishtail Lodge at 0445 and reached a picturesque village of   Sarangkot perched at an altitude of 1592 m and 11.6 Km away at 0530 on 12th Nov , 2018 . I parked my vehicle paying NPR 30 only . As there was rush of vehicles going atop , I followed my driver’s suggestion , crossed the road and climbed two stairs of a commercial building whose one floor was reserved for the tourists like me who came from near like locals from Kathmandu , Indians like me and from far like Japanese and Germans , etc . One part of the floor facing the East was open for the Grand View . This part was provided with enough plastic chairs for the comforts of the viewers . The other part was fully occupied by shops selling woollens , trinkets , etc . One Nepali girl was weaving a shawl on a handloom , just to show the authenticity of the shawls displayed .

The large viewing gallery was sufficient for us for viewing sunrise as well as Annapurna Himalayan range including Annapurna Massif, Fishtail Mountain, Dhaulagiri range, and Manaslu .

I enjoyed viewing and photographing Annapurna South , Hiunchuli , Annapurna I South Face, Kangshar Kang Roc Noir , Machapuchare and Annapurna III Annapurna Iv , Annapurna II and Lamjung Kailas mountains displaying pink peaks and then the full glory and majesty of them as the sun rose .

My paisa was wasool when  I could click the Phewa Lake to the south and stunning panaromic view of "Annapurna Himalayan Range" to the North  , sleepy Sarangkot and  dazzling sun rise .

At the end , I contributed to the welfare of the owner of the house sipping hot  Chiya tea .
Really enjoyed visiting this temple.  Monkeys everywhere.  Very spiritual place.  Very visual as well.  Lots of great pictures

Had the naan specially made by the lovely chef - Subendu Roy, and it was great. It’s crisp and tender, touched with beetroot and carrot which make it visually desirable. Highly recommend everyone to try. Also the waiter - Rohit Bhatt very kind and helpful.

Top-notch location with fantastic customer service. Had hot shower everytime , price just great only 15 usd for us and everything is just surrounded by cafe, club, bar, trekking gear shops, gifts shop and so on just in 10 meters away. Love love trekkers home and will definitely come back soon.

You can choose to either walk up quite a few steps, best to calculate in at least an hour, if you're fit and used to heights you can do it in 40min or so.
Lovely for sunrise, but expect lots of people
Can see Kathmandu valley from the top and recommend you guys once you are in Kathmandu . Don’t miss it guys it’s the great place to see .

What impressed me most was the head chef Subendu Roy and another chef's Padam Sitoli ability to bring creativity to the menu without overcomplicating it. Whether it was a bold twist on a classic entrée or a perfectly balanced sauce that elevated the dish, you could tell there was a deep understanding of flavor and technique.

The hotel staff were excellent, the location is good apart from the struggle up the unmade road in the dark. They really should fix it. The gardens are lovely and the view of the mountains is terrific. We only stayed 2 nights and so managed pretty well.

However, it is badly in need of updating. I imagine it was in a class of its own when it was built but the mattress was really hard, almost no give in it all and the area around the plughole in the bath was all peeling away. I think the bath had been painted to try to give it extra life, but really time to spend some money, especially since there are so many new hotels just opened or about to open. Reminded me of old fashioned Butlins chalets.
I suppose I should declare that we are in our 60's and looking for a bit of comfort. The hotel was clean and the breakfast was good.

Thamel is one of the musts in Kathmandu. When you are there, you are like in a boiling kettle among people and vehicles. Still lastly a small part of Thamel  has been made free of motorvehicles and there you can escape when you need a rest from all the noise and polluted air.

Great hospitality and friendly staff. Location wise, in the center and convenient to move around. Very clean room at the new block but a bit unfortunate as breakfast only available at the old block (less than 50m).

While OR2K caters mostly to western tourists with its boho vibes, it is still worth a visit if you want a chill place to read a book and relax in the afternoon.  

I really like the floor seating concept that encourages you to sit comfortably. The food is great - excellent pokouda, almost everyone had it on their table and you can't beat the price for 275rupees.  The OR2K combo with hummus, babaganoush, and falafel is also delicious (must share). I went back for it twice!

Power plugs are available throughout the cafe and wifi access is pretty steady.  On a sunny day you can sit outside and take in the view of Fewa Lake.  If you have a few friends with you, you can even indulge in a round of Monopoly or other board games.

If I'm back in Lakeside again, I would definitely go back to indulge in a plate of pokouda with a pot of masala tea.

Excellent place for a long morning / evening walk or have a drink (alcoholic or non alcoholic) or smoke a sheesha by the shore the lake and gaze at the views of the hills and mountains beyond or just watch the evening hue's of the sunset fade away

The rooms and facade are old and tired.  Frontdesk wasnâ??t exactly friendly or welcoming, and the food (both Western and local cuisine) was mediocre and often too salty.  Location was its only saving grace, within 30 minutes of the airport and walking distance from Boudanath Stupa.
Thank you soo much for my hotel owner who give opportunity take part in the aarati which gives soo much peace n pleasure. It is  one of the best tourist spot of the pokhara its really very beautiful.

renovation is extremely slow with evidence of callousness in conservation in stark contrast to bhaktapur.
only the kumari chowk with it's splendid wooden architecture bears the testimony of earlier days.
kalbhairav temple will fail to arouse any emotion in you.
virtually nobody in the whole square seems to be interested in their past, just selling the fake trinkets and basking in the winter sun with bf/gf.
this area is thus is full of dilapidated buildings with even the guards unaware of the name of the buildings they are guarding. it is nothing but the extension of the business district surrounding.
you can afford to skip this picnic spot altogether.

Our stay was more than just comfortable. It felt genuinely welcoming. The very first moment I pulled back the curtains, the view took my breath away and reminded me how nature humbles us when we pause to see it.

What remains in my memory is not only the scenery but also the people. The staff carried a rare warmth that cannot be taught in training. It comes naturally from the heart. Even Nabina Shreepali, still a trainee, embodied this spirit of hospitality so effortlessly that it left us feeling cared for in the most personal way.

We spent time by the pool with our child and were grateful for the thoughtfulness of having a space created just for kids. The rooms were clean and tended to with quiet care, which added to the sense of ease. Beyond the walls and amenities, it was the kindness of the people that etched this place into our hearts.

It rained throughout our visit and the skies were heavy with clouds, yet even that carried its own kind of beauty. It felt soft, meditative and grounding. Still, it leaves us wishing to return again in another season to experience a different shade of its charm.

In the end it is the staff, their presence and their humanity that make us want to come back. Places can be beautiful, but it is people who give them soul.

It's been five years since my last visit, and it was surprisingly nice to see the neighborhood cleaner than in the past. But don't worry - it's still crazy, busy, noisy, dusty, etc. Plan to spend a couple hours simply walking the streets, shipping, people watching, and taking it all in.
Interesting to walk around and some good restaurants on the rooftops with views.  Lots of cool streets to wander about close by.

Other than the views, there's not much to see in and around the temple. A good guide will help you explain the significance of certain monuments and structures up there. And the monkeys don't trouble you much as long as you stay away from them.
I trekked on Poon Hill+ ABC thus rate average here. Actually, it has 'very good'

Great location, gym is out of date, front desk staff are robots and only looking to nickle and dime you for charges. Breakfast can be much better. Hotel staff noisily worked on other rooms throughout the night yelling and banging items. For the same price I have stayed at better in KTM.

We are a family of five with small kids.

THE GOOD: This hotel has a small apartment with two bedrooms (we couldnt find other places with a family room).
The hotel is well located at the Thamel
BUT: the hotel suffers from very low maintenance, toilets in bad shape. some mattresses are not compatible with sleeping. Overall feels like a budget hostel.

when we got back to Kathmandu

The hotel and staff were absolutely wonderful. One of the best hotels we've stayed in for a perfectly reasonable price. The architecture and decorations of the hotel are so beautiful, the attention to detail is as if from a different century. One of my favourite parts of the trip was staying here.

Thamel: Kathmandu

Location
Thamel is a lively neighborhood located in the heart of Kathmandu, the capital city of Nepal. It is approximately 5 kilometers northwest of the Tribhuvan International Airport and is within walking distance of the Kathmandu Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Thamel is surrounded by the historic areas of Asan and Indra Chowk to the east and the peaceful Garden of Dreams to the west, making it an ideal location for tourists interested in exploring Kathmandu's rich cultural and historical attractions.

How to Reach Thamel
By Air:
Thamel is easily accessible from Tribhuvan International Airport, which is the only international airport in Nepal. From the airport, you can take a taxi or hire a pre-arranged airport transfer to Thamel, which usually takes around 20-30 minutes depending on traffic. The cost of a taxi ride is typically around NPR 800-1200 (approximately USD 7-10), but it’s advisable to negotiate or confirm the fare before starting the journey.

By Bus:
For those arriving from other parts of Nepal, Thamel is well connected by the public bus network. Most long-distance buses arriving from cities like Pokhara, Chitwan, or Lumbini drop passengers at the Gongabu Bus Park, also known as New Bus Park, which is about 3 kilometers from Thamel. From Gongabu, you can take a local taxi, which would cost around NPR 300-500 (approximately USD 3-5), or opt for a public microbus to reach Thamel.

By Road:
Travelers coming from India can enter Nepal via border crossings like Sunauli, Raxaul, or Banbasa. From these border towns, there are regular buses and private taxis available to Kathmandu. The drive from these border crossings to Kathmandu can take anywhere from 6 to 12 hours depending on the route and weather conditions.

Once you are in Kathmandu, Thamel is best explored on foot due to its narrow alleys and the dense concentration of shops, restaurants, and hotels.

Why Thamel is Famous
Thamel has been the epicenter of the tourist industry in Kathmandu for several decades, renowned for its vibrant energy, eclectic mix of shops, cafes, and its cultural significance. Here are some of the key reasons why Thamel is famous:

Shopping Hub:
Thamel is a shopper’s paradise, offering everything from traditional Nepali handicrafts, pashmina shawls, and Thangka paintings to modern outdoor gear, trekking equipment, and souvenirs. The narrow alleys are lined with colorful shops where tourists can indulge in shopping for unique items, including handmade jewelry, Buddhist artifacts, and singing bowls. Bargaining is common here, so don’t hesitate to negotiate for a better price.

Cultural Melting Pot:
Thamel is not just a place for shopping but also a cultural hub where different lifestyles and traditions blend harmoniously. It’s common to find Buddhist monasteries and Hindu temples nestled between restaurants and cafes. This neighborhood is a melting pot of cultures, attracting travelers from all over the world, making it a vibrant and cosmopolitan area where you can meet people from diverse backgrounds.

Culinary Delight:
For food lovers, Thamel is a culinary haven. The area is dotted with restaurants serving a wide range of cuisines, from traditional Nepali dishes like momo (dumplings) and dal bhat (rice and lentils) to international fare including Italian, Indian, Chinese, and continental cuisines. The street food scene in Thamel is also worth exploring, with stalls offering local snacks like chatpate, sel roti, and lassi. Many cafes and bakeries in Thamel are popular for their freshly brewed coffee, pastries, and rooftop dining with a view of the bustling streets below.

Thamel is the heart of Kathmandu’s nightlife, boasting an array of bars, pubs, and live music venues that burst with energy after sunset. With cozy bars hosting local live bands playing Nepali rock and traditional music, as well as nightclubs that cater to the younger crowd with international hits from DJs, Thamel truly has something for everyone. Its lively nightlife scene is a major attraction for both locals and tourists, making it an essential destination for experiencing Kathmandu after dark.

Adventure Hub:
Thamel is the starting point for people who love adventure. It's where you can begin some of the world's most famous trekking journeys, like the Everest Base Camp, Annapurna Circuit, and Langtang Valley. Thamel has many companies that organize adventure activities such as trekking, mountaineering, rafting, and paragliding. Whether you're experienced or trying it for the first time, you can get guided tours and all the gear you need to start your journey in Thamel.

Accommodation Variety:
Thamel offers a wide range of accommodation options catering to all budgets, from luxury hotels to budget guesthouses and hostels. Many of the accommodations here are designed to reflect the local culture, offering comfortable stays with a touch of Nepali hospitality. The variety of choices available makes Thamel an ideal base for both short and long-term stays, ensuring that travelers of all kinds can find a suitable place to rest.

Wellness and Relaxation:
Thamel also caters to those looking for relaxation and wellness. There are numerous spas, yoga studios, and wellness centers offering traditional Nepali massages, Ayurvedic treatments, and yoga classes. These services provide a perfect way to unwind after a day of exploring the city or trekking in the nearby mountains.

Rich History and Heritage:
Thamel is steeped in history and heritage, with its narrow alleys and old buildings telling the story of Kathmandu’s past. While Thamel has modernized over the years, it still retains its old-world charm with its traditional architecture and historic sites scattered throughout the area. The proximity to historical landmarks like Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), and the ancient trading routes adds to its cultural allure.

Art and Music:
Thamel is a hub for art and music lovers. The area has several art galleries showcasing contemporary Nepali art, traditional Thanka paintings, and handicrafts. Live music is a significant part of Thamel’s cultural fabric, with many restaurants and cafes hosting live performances by local and international artists. The fusion of traditional and modern music creates a unique atmosphere that is both relaxing and entertaining.

Convenience for Tourists:
Finally, Thamel is famous for its convenience. Everything a traveller needs is available within a short distance – from currency exchange counters, travel agencies, and internet cafes to pharmacies, bookstores, and grocery stores. The well-established tourist infrastructure makes it easy for visitors to navigate and enjoy their time in Kathmandu without any hassle.

Patan Durbar Square is located in the center of Patan city Lalitpur and was built by the Newar People. 

It is one of three main ancient royal durbar squares in the Kathmandu Valley. Patan Durbar Square is the smallest of all durbar squares it is often referred to as the most beautiful of all. 

There are many temples and idols in the area. The main temples are aligned opposite of the western face of the palace. The entrance of the temples faces east, towards the palace. There is also a bell situated in the alignment beside the main temples, The Square also holds old Newari residential houses. 

The square was heavily damaged by the earthquake in April 2015 and is currently being restored.

The square is not to be confused with the historic Patam Durbar Square.  This area is still suffering from the 2015 earthquake although some restoration and repairs have been effected. Be warned, there is still quite a lot of dust however it is nowhere near as bad as in the suburbs and outer areas where there are thick layers of dust over everything. There are many sellers in the square. The glistening white neo-classical former royal palace contrasts with Nepalese architecture.
