I had a truly delightful experience at Hyatt Regency, Kathmandu. The staff and overall service were excellent. A special mention goes to Anjilla Bastola at the front desk, who was an absolute pleasure to interact with. She went above and beyond to ensure our stay was comfortable and memorable—right from arranging a beautifully decorated room for my mother’s birthday, to promptly changing the cake when I realized I had forgotten to mention her allergy to chocolate, to arranging transport and handling every other request with ease. Her attention to detail and dedication to guest satisfaction truly stood out.

The ambience, food, and services were all outstanding, making our stay even more enjoyable. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Kathmandu, and it will definitely be my first choice on future visits. Kudos to the entire team for the wonderful hospitality!

The best aspect of this hotel is the location - near the lake, restaurants, shopping.  The room was not very good.  The bathroom had a large glass wall that opened into the bedroom with no way to close it off.  The person in the bedroom could see everything going on in the bathroom.  Yuck!  And, if we had to turn on the light at night, it woke the other person in the room.  The design was highly unsatisfactory.  We were only there for a short stay - so not worthwhile to switch rooms.  Pool and garden is very nice.  Breakfast was just OK.
We took a reserved roofed boat for 4 persons for 400nrp. Took us to temple & back. Great view. All rides fare mentioned in board.

We only stayed one night and unfortunately we had a room right beside a windows outside which had lots of noise going on all night. The room was clean and the beds comfy. The shower was hot with good pressure. WiFi wasn't bad. I didn't find the staff particularly friendly or helpful. The room was also a bit more expensive then I had thought it was going to be.
Tremendesly interesting museum! Really big and with amazing things exposed. Located in a beautifull and huge garden! Little old...

After climbing up about 300 stairs the Swayambhunath Stupa is so worth it! Up there (besides the monkeys) you'll find a very peaceful, beautiful view over Kathmandu and a quiet place to rest from Kathmandu's busy life!

Decent clean hotel with friendly staff. Food was ok and they seemed to cope well in the bar and restaurant. Breakfast was nothing to write home but the staff filled the gaps when it was needed. I would stay here again.
I'm a photographer and the whole of Nepal is a photographers dream. Loved Kathmandu and would certainly visit other temples and shrines as part of my vacation

Fun third world shopping experience, everything within walking distance. It’s a maze!  Many of the shops offer similar items, inexpensive and poor quality mostly. However it’s definitely worth the adventure! Pick up a few souvenirs, knock-off are plentiful!

If you are keen to try too hard to be spiritual and really be connected to the universe, man, then, like, this is the spot for you. Clean food, which is always nice, but way too many patchouli oil drenched hipsters seeking enlightenment through their devices.

Absolutely amazing place to unwind after long treks in the beautiful country of Nepal, within minutes walk of the hustle and bustle of Thamel but you wouldn’t ever know it, quiet peaceful, an amazing staff full of the nicest people you will ever meet. As for the architecture I don’t think words can describe, a must stay for anyone looking for classic Nepal architecture, and a quiet nights rest. I’d give 10 stars if I could. Thanks for a wonderful stay and until next time, Namaste.
We had a great stay at this hotel.The rooms were very comfortable and the staffs were very helpful and kind.The location was perfect close to everything we needed. We will definitely stay here again.

The setting is cozy, you sit on the floor and their are candles on the table and black lights on the ceiling. Their menu is vegetarian and glows in the dark. 

We waited 45 minutes for the first dish to arrive and close to an hour and 20 minutes before giving up on the 2nd dish and our appetizers, which should have come first. We left and politely complained but the staff didn't seem to care much, as the restaurant already includes their 10% service charge to all bills, so good service is unnecessary. 

While their atmosphere is nice, the one dish we did get wasn't that good, and their lack of service and forgetting the other dishes entirely, will keep us away on future visits.

A boat ride on Phewa Lake was included in the price of our tour.  The prices look to start from 500 rupees.  A person rowed our canoe for about 30 minutes.  Some sections the water is very calm.

However, a big turn off was trash that wash up in the banks and the water isn't very clear.  Also, they can drop you off at the banks and you can hike up to the World Peace Stupa but I am not sure how long that hike will take.
The museum has nothing much and could have made much better. If you have a lot of time then visit. Nice view from outside.

What an amazing place to be at...especially for the sunrise view over the mountains of Annapurna range of the great Himalaya. The mountains on one side and he Pokhara city on the other side seen from Sarangkot top is beautiful and worth every effort to reach there early in the morning...One of the must visit place in Pokhara, Serene and Beautiful...

Food variety is good from Mediterranean to East Asian to Nepali and anything in between. Food was generally tasty.

Ambience is average. You have to take your shores off and sit on the ground. All very nice

I would ask the owner to train the waiters and servers on cleanliness. I saw food preparers sort of touching the food. Straw cover was removed by the waiter without thinking that he is not supposed to touch the tip!!! 

Also may want to cut down on greens during the monsoons just to be in the safe side.
Our guide took our group to the mountain museum as part of our trip. We spent an hour there and could have done it in 15mins. A few interesting bits but not much to write home about.
its the closest place to get the best early morning views, bus taxi or walk, it will get the blood flowing and the adventure only gets better

Nice hotel with a variety of lodging options - we went for the "new wing" at $ 120 a night but there are cheaper alternatives and all share the lovely and quiet garden away from the mad house of Thamel. Perfect option for pre trek lodging, in case last minute purchases need to be made, there is a great supermarket across the street with every thing you might need. Need equipment, forgot that fleece jacket, no problem a plethora of fake North Face, Mountain Hardware, Quechua you name it are available and most likely will do adequate service for your trek. The restaurant is surprisingly good and a perfect alternative to the offerings "outside" 
My gripe, the promised airport pick up never happened despite 2 phone calls and the front desk just shrugged it off - not a way to treat a guest. ---- OK the cab ride was 8 bucks.

We took a paddle boat out on the lake and it was amazing. Do remember to take snacks and drink with. We thought two hours would be too long but it fleshed by so quickly we had to really make for shore to be in time!
Tourist required to pay 1000 NR to enter. Unless you are inclined by the religious experience it may not be worth it. Significant damage from earthquake still.

I booked a garden facing room costing Rs 9000 a night. There was no desk, no cupboard, no remote control for tv, floor was dusty, bathroom was tiny and mouldy. Moved to different room with extra cost.

I had a very nice time in phewa lake. The lake is access from lake side pokhara anywhere. I took a boat to look around the pokhara valley which i really liked so much eventhough the boat was quite expensive. I enjoyed the boat riddding with the perfect view of annapurna range.you can also do it. I highly recommend it..
Loved both the taxi ride and trek to the little town. Went early morning to catch sunrise. The view of mountains during sunrise is spectacular.
This square is centre of Kathmandu. Beautiful place with temples and meseum . You can see kaal bhairav here. Beautiful place.
If you don't know you're on Durbar Square you probably walk past it. Renovated square after the earthquake a couple of years ago. Some temples on the square.

I've been here several times before the earthquake and I lovd this place. It is still worth to visit but thr entry fee is horrendous for no obvious reason. Reconstruction is terribly slow, it's full of scammers and fake guides, the maps are useless, there is no good information and no official guides, no fair priced taxi stand. So what is the entry fee for? And why is it ten times the price for Western tourists compared to SAARC? We bring a lot of money to Nepal, get ripped off systematically, but still it's not enough. It's a shame.

An amazing architecure and expression of nepalese arrs crafts: but mostly under renovation due to earthquake from few angles only you can catch the spirit of could have been this square befire the catastrophy.

All in wood, monument's structure were not made to resist to such level of earthquake.

Hopefully soon all this renovation and help from japanese and chinese organization will pay off.

- Location: you can see over the Kathmandu city from the temple and have many monkey around temple, you can see people who have faith and making ritual for pray.
- How to travel: You can come by taxi or private car and walk many steps to the temple. Have parking in front of temple but beware monkey climb on your car.
- Admission: NPR 200 for foreigners/ free for Napali.
- Open: 07.00 am. - 07.00 pm.
- Souvenir shop: Have art shop and general souvenir shop around temple but expensive price more than outer market.
Very nice place to stay and relax and sit in the different cafes and pub and have some food or just chill.

Overall experience is good, some visualization is required in rooms example visualization on switches of lights, lamps and sockets etc. Elevator required maintenance, little noisy.  Rest all parts are perfectly maintained.

A good basic hotel. My room was a bit dark and dingy and the mattresses are very hard. There was also a lot of noise from the restaurant next door and below. Nothing flash but did the job and it has a great location in the heart of Thamel. The staff are the best part of the hotel, and they are super friendly and helpful, so for that I would come back again.

I enjoyed walking to Swayambhunath Temple from Thamel, and appreciated the challenge of the steep steps up to the summit of the hill where the temple is.  I especially enjoyed watching the monkeys, my first encounter with "wild" monkeys.  Walked the perimeter of the Stupa and explored the various vendor's shops.
It's a good place to visit where you can enjoy and and find everything you need such as hotel, shopping center, pubs, bars, restaurants etc.

it is a beautiful country whose Nepalese people are very kind and helpful.  Its culture is immense and historic.  Anyone who comes to visit this beautiful country and its charming people will not regret their stay, with its beautiful landscapes, its gastronomy, its craftsman, its temples, etc.

Well August by far is not the best time to travel to Nepal due to monsoon weather. So, the lake was filled with muddy waters, and water weeds. However, I am sure that during the season this is a hub of activities, including boating, canoeing, and other water-activities, walking, biking.. name it they would surely have it..

Nice and interesting, but busy, crowded and animated, for some night life, that sector is recommanded, otherwise many restaurants in the areas, lots of stores for trekking material, or buddhist artefacts

I am staying in room no 154 from 7th June 2024. The receptionist was very helpful to me as I am a patient of young onset Parkinson's disease, he helped me manage things well. But I have a twin baby, they refused to provide us with a king size bed and asked me to manage with a twin bed. As I check in the room I find a dead mosquito in the bath tub. Then my daughter found ice cream cone in the drawer which I needed to throw immediately and I was not able to take pictures. Behind the side lamp there was a spider web. The refrigerator was not there in the room. Service is very poor. Today in the morning breakfast, we were not provided with a low height chair as i said I was with two kids and my brother two kids. Some VIPs were provided 10-12 capacity tables with 5 occupancy and we were 4 adults and 4 kids were asked to adjust with a high chair as there was a morning rush. Terrible service and response. Also in room service, I was asked to pay the bill immediately and did refuse to add on to the final bill at checkout. In the swimming pool, I asked for help to bring a towel for my kids They reacted as if what I had asked for. Not a kids friendly hotel . Even milk for infants and kids is on a chargeable basis. The plates in which we ate and kept outside the room in the evening were not cleaned and taken away till night.

We were four friends travelling to Pokhara for the first time and were just looking for a place to chill post dinner...considering most of the places shut down early like by 10 pm. OR2K was the best place we could have chosen. It has an extremely cosy and welcoming ambience with a comfortable floor sitting with great music and a chill staff. It's divided into two spaces, one of which hosts movie nights. The cuisine is mostly Mediterranean and is completely vegetarian. Travelling with hardcore non vegetarian friends...and they loving the place speaks volumes of its delectable menu.  It has awesome signature cocktails. We tried a cucumber mojito and an espresso Bailey's martini. We ordered a 4 cheese pizza which was one of the best we've had in Pokhara. This place was the last meal in Pokhara and was by far the best! Strongly recommended.
Very good experience will do come again thank you for everything. The rooms were so comfortable and service was excellent

Best Restaurant in Pokhara and Nepal, unlike the branch in Kathmandu which is probably the worst in Nepal.
Good Service, Delicious food.
Vegetarian  Restaurant
Big variety of dishes, all nicely served and good taste.
Stayed in Pokhara for 1 week and went to this restaurant for 3 times.
Must!!!

This is a place for extensive learning about the people of mountains and their lifestyle. Not just that it also lists highest peaks and their summits. A small movie is also played, make sure of the timings.

We were here for a short time and saw many vendors small to medium scale. This place has good stuffs and khurkhuri shops. If you can negotiate prices,  this is the place to go. They have silver shops, clothes, painting, antiques, toys etc. Make sure you have a hat/ Cap to shade yourself from the sun. This place is crowded with people, vehicles and animals 😊.
Great location to experience the beauty of the Himalayas. If you are in Pokhara definitely visit this site either at sunrise or sunset to fully enjoy it

This museum contains a great deal of information about local culture and history,geology, flora and fauna as well as mountaineering trips so could be highly interesting and educational. The problem it suffers from is,I suspect, that it does not have access or funds to make the most of more modern and interactive  methods of presenting the information-there are lots of glass cases with lots of tired looking writing next to them. The best bits are the posters and equipment used by mountaineers on display , the exhibits of local costumes and domestic items and the photos of the changing face of the mountain.

Very comfortable room and nice pool. Good breakfast and excellent service in the dining room. Poor service at front desk for check-in and check-out. At check-in, hotel had arranged only a single room and, despite us providing a copy of our reservation that clearly showed a double room, we were asked to take a seat while staff "investigated." At the end of our four-day stay, we had arranged for a pick-up by hotel vehicle, but it didn't show up. The front desk person asserted repeatedly that "it is here." Only after numerous requests was alternate transport (i.e. a taxi) arranged, which arrived more than 30 minutes after our requested departure time.  As we were leaving, the front desk person apologized for the delay, explaining that "the driver never showed up", a bewildering admission from a person that, until that point, had insisted that there was no problem. A very far cry from the level of service we expected from the most expensive property we stayed at in Nepal and what we actually received at a number of guesthouses with significantly lower rates.

although the place is know as the hub of tourism, at the time of covid most of the shops are closed. no point in going there. a sheer waste of time. I suggest that tourists start visiting thamel once the restrictions are lifted and market opened.

The hotel is built into a temple style and has a very attractive courtyard.  Service was friendly. The standard rooms were pretty basic but clean. There was no TV, but candles for the daily citywide blackouts (hotel has it's own generator which supplies power). Hotel was situated pretty close to everything; the main sights and restaurants. Hotel tries to be ecofriendly which is nice but I didn't like using the same damp towels for whole time. The hotel would have been really nice if the room rate would have been lower. The standard of the hotel and the rate did not match, but on the other hand I don't have more experience on the overall roomratings in Kathmandu.

Great location, pleasant courtyards, attentive staff, but hugely popular with tour groups arriving to trek elsewhere and perhaps for this reason, the rooms are overpriced. Better value available elsewhere. If the money doesn't matter, however, the rooms, though dark - all low wattage energy saving bulbs - are clean and spacious, the bathrooms adequate. The breakfast buffet's not bad, and the front courtyard a pleasant place to eat it. The location is right in the middle of the main tourist area, everything for trekking available just down the road. Kilroy's, a restaurant well worth a visit, is a three minute walk away. They raised the price of a Himalaya beer from Rs300 to Rs400 overnight when I was there, which gives a perfect example of their pricing strategy: you want to be here, you pay our price!

It is mainly shopping street for the visitors and you can buy here some.good items like shawl , show pieces . Here some great Casino also . But there is no Parking area so you have to manage the parking here.

Although is one of the most recommended places to visit in Kathmandu, the place is just overcrowded by monkeys which makes it funny for some seconds, then disgraceful due to the stinky and dirty environment. Nice views to Kathmandu from the top though. If you finally go, you’d better go to the bus parking place to avoid climbing the stairs

Wonderful heritage sight with many wonderful buildings and sights.  Unfortunately the earthquake took a toll on quite a number of buildings rendering them not only inaccessible, but also with a lot of construction material and cover around.  It’s a magnificent area that hopefully will be back to it’s original glory soon!
Awesome place to exprience hindu culture and see amazing architecture. A lot of building in the area are still under construction and rehabilitation from the damages of the earthquake.
Thank you so much for my hotel owner uncle who give us opportunity to this place it was my first time to see sun raising in the morning its very cold still me n my mom enjoying a lots

First trip to Kathmandu and we wanted to try and experience as much of the culture as possible. 
Peaceful and a clean place in the heart of the city. It's like in a fairytale opening up the main entrance door - another world opens up - perfectly carved wood doors and windows, brick walls, dressed in traditional costumes. The amazing architecture was so good that my iPhone was enough to copy its beauty, so I gave a rest to my SLR this time.
Wonderful stupa and so much culture but also a variety of shops and coffee houses on rooftops as too the little typical restaurants in the area. Recommend visit

This museum is worth a visit because its subject matter is so interesting. You can see photos of all the 8000 meter mountains and learn about the sherpas and climbers. You can see the evolution of mountaineering equipment – Hillary took 7 tons of stuff in his historic summit. However, the displays deserve some patronage to show this fascinating subject at its best.

This is the place to hang out.  You have an amazing choice of places to eat at, many at very reasonable prices.  There is a very good selection of accommodation from hostels to high end hotels.  It is also the place to shop for just about anything you might need on your trek and to trinkets and gifts for your family.

Durbar Square is a really interesting place to go particularly if you have a good guide. Unfortunately some of the structures were badly damaged in 2015 by the earthquake but they are slowly getting restored.
Absolutely the one place in Kathmandu to visit. Negative is very aggressive sellers and its dirty too. Lots of restructing going on still but also a lot ready after 2015 earthquake.
The best part of Katmandú. Lot of shops and restaurants in this area. Everything is very very cheap and people are so friendly and helpful

Hotel room was in good state but aged hotel.
Hotel staffs makes my daily stay pleasant. Wonderful staff service and with high cleanliness. Memorable stay with Radisson Katmandu. Food is very nice too.
Wonderful hotel. Great stuff. Very helpful. We loved this place. The breakfast is rich and tasty, great coffee. European style.
Totally Exceptional interms of all services that you gave to me and my colleagues stayd and meeting participants as well.

i am "observing" the lake regularely since 2012 - and what to say. there are efforts with some trash-cans (dustbins) along some walkways which are still under construction, the different shop- restaurant- and shack- owners dont respect the rules or law and build closer and closer to the lake, while the whole lakeside comes down to a crowded shopping mall surrounded by concrete-bunkers … just the the planned international airport approaching jetplanes over fewa-lake are missing to make this "natural beauty" perfect! ..sry for my sarcasm dears, but that´s how i see it ;)

There where not a crazy amount of monkeys 🐒 and the temple was like a lot of the others. There is a view of the city, and quite some stairs. You are not missing something special if you disregard this.
Back in time, watching the amazing reconstruction after the Erthquake is a humbling experience whilst everyday life goes on all around
The massage was an awesome treat coming off six day trek and then a delicious dinner was the end of a perfect day! It’s beautiful here, too!

Getting around in Kathmandu is quite challenging as there is no Uber, and the local cab drivers will try to rip off the tourists. To my pleasant surprise, Kathmandu Durbar square was just a leisure walk away from Thamel. The entrance fee is quite expensive for non-SAARC countries ($10 USD) but i reckon the money is being used for uplifting the site damaged after the 2015 earthquake. A tour guide is a mandate to really appreciate this unique UNESCO heritage.

Thamel is having a lot of options for the shopoholics.best things to shop here are colorful decorative for home, woolen wears, beads, musical bowls etc. Beware of buying Rudraksh here, you will be cheated as they are fake. Moreover it is bit costlier here than Pokhara.

The food was delicious and you can get a nice view of the lake!
We had dinner and the next day breakfast!
They also have games and movies to enjoy your stay

Historicaly significant place, however, the place has suffered some damages in the earthquake of 2015. There is a bit dirt and dust everywhere, but you should still visit this place since it's one of the most famous places in Kathmandu city.

Although still a lot of damage this is always an interesting place to visit. Going round the back rather than climbing all the stairs at the front is a better way to access the temple, then you can come down all the stairs to the front which is an easier way of doing things, particularly if you are not good at climbing stairs.

Always busy and bustling.  Toilet facilities not so good.  Views are great.  Monkeys are usually more active early morning or late afternoon.  Do not carry food or drinks as monkeys will snatch from you. There are a couple of small coffee shops where you can get a drink and they have wifi. 

Wear trainers, boots or flat shoes as stairs are steep and can be slippy when wet.
We totally loved the place. Specially the short movie they played which was really insightful. Worth visiting no doubt.

We enjoyed several nights at the Radisson while we were touring India and Nepal.  The rooms are nice, staff is very good and the breakfast buffet quite nice.  On my last day, I scheduled a tranquility signature massage and it was the best massage ever!  I have had massages all over the world and this was my favorite ever!  Ask for Kamala.

Horrible Internet service, impossible to watch a movie or a sport game!, specially now during World Cup!
Not one English movie channel, only one or two news only. The rest, all either local or Indian languages.
Room was not very well clean.
Never a pool view or upgrade available.
Pigeons on window donâ??t let you sleep at night!
We had a wonderful experience! Food was delicious and service was great. Our server Binita was sweet and attentive. We will definetly plan another trip back.

Checked in early went shopping, returned and was told there were no available rooms. I insisted. They gave me two twins rather than king I reserved, the shower wasnâ??t clean, and there was water all over the floor.  Guessing toilet plumbing fixture was leaking but had to deal with it by throwing all available towels onto the floor the two days I was there. For the money paid, this was not a good experience. I wonâ??t stay there again.

This hotel had a good feel about from the front door. Staff were welcoming and checking was a good process. Our twin room was good/clean with a view over the area in front of the hotel. We were in the older building which was good. Room facilities were very good, everything worked and not patched up unlike some Indian hotels we stayed at. Beds were clean & comfortable. Had to ask for English tv channels to be accessed. One restaurant on premises (another in a neighbouring building) but food options were very good. Great place to stay!

Interesting site where Buddhism and Hinduism live side by side. Great view over the city, and several rooftop restaurants from where you can enjoy the view while zipping to a cup of tea or fresh pressed juice. Some monkeys drink Sprite from the bottle, others groom or chase each other, but they don't seem to bother with people.

Kathmandu Durbar square was quite good shape now after earthquake 2015 but there is still reconstruction is working around durbar square. 
Must visit when you are Kathmandu.
Great culture heritage site of Nepal.

We have booked for three night at this hotel after reading all the excellent review but now seems little confuse for me .
We came late night they check in one of the worst room with so cold at night . All night we were dreadful night for us.
We had booked for double but they give us twin one which we hate all the time. Please sorry for rest of night one night was totally bad

Thamel is a very nice place to visit for world tourists. Traveller can take the feel of Thailand. Tattoo, bar, dance club, historical place are available near your hands. Very cheap to stay , food and enjoy. People will not be bored in Thamel

A hotel in lovely grounds with a swimming pool. Rooms were clean & spacious. One we had (we stayed on 2 different occasions) had mountain view.
But staff frazzled as many people coming & going, like ourselves staying for one night in transit to Treks.
Layout of breakfast buffet not very ergonomic.
We did not dine there bar breakfast

If the room rate was atleast 20-25% lower, I would have given a slightly higher rating. But comparing what they charge, they have to definitely improve their facilities and services. The worst part is WiFi, which is almost non-existent in spite of being in a room close to the WiFi transmitter. The whole WiFi system is poor since it keeps disconnecting and is a huge pain to operate. The WiFi password is easy to guess for anyone who wants to hack. There is a link given for changing the password which does not work. The breakfast is just decent enough, with only one Nepali/Indian item. (I stayed for 3 days). The Idli+Sambar was terrible. I sent a T-shirt to laundry mainly to remove one food stain, but it came back with the same and poorly ironed. I had to give it again to my next hotel.

You get zero value for the money that you spend to stay on this property. 

Service during breakfast is poor and most important the food is COLD. Even if you order from the live station, the food that you get on your table is cold. It was not even cold in Kathmandu. On all 3 days, I had same experience.

In-room dining experience was sad too, as the food takes a long long time to reach you. An ordinary pastry which usually is there in refrigerator took 40 minutes to come to my room. Not to mention, the staff is unthoughtful.

Housekeeping, slightly better than others but again slow and reminders required.

The rooms are very old and depleted. I read this in other reviews too but still decided to go ahead. I repent now.

Only saving grace was the property, huge with lush green gardens. Casino is within the premises. 

Won't recommend this at all. One can get cheaper room rates and better stay options elsewhere. Better to stay in Thamel area which is closer to most tourist attractions.

The traditional inspired architecture of this hotel was very intriguing to start with. This has definitely been one of my favourite hotel experiences ever. They are keen to promote their eco credentials with reduction in plastic bottles and some organic food and drink. Nice little bonuses were morning rooftop yoga classes and complementary walking tour around the authentic parts of Kathmandu. The staff were faultless and offered the best service I have experienced anywhere. Also, they had a nice outdoor courtyard area to relax in after a trip to a very busy and bustling city. I wouldn't hesitate in booking here again on next trip to Nepal.

We visited this site in May and enjoyed the wood carvings and courtyards of the palaces. I was surprised to find a nice museum that has lots of information and small artifacts. I could have spent 2 to 3 hours reading all the signs and taking in the significance of the objects but since I was on a tour it was too rushed. This was my favorite spot in Kathmandu.

Such a wonderful temple to visit.
The energy you get is great, and the spirit is lovely.
A must see in nepal.
A lovely refreshing cool idea to get off the streets of an increasingly busy Pokhara. Beautiful, misty, otherworldly. A magical place that modern Pokharaonly hints at.

This truly was the best hotel experience we could ever hope for! We stayed in the new building. There is usually always some issue with a hotel room in the US even if you’re staying at the top hotels. It’s usually some noise or the AC or the bed isn’t comfy. At the Radisson Kathmandu everything was perfect! The beds were comfy even for an 11 night stay. The pillows were comfy and never hurt our necks. The rooms were spacious and the shower pressure was spectacular! We came home and found ourselves missing these showers! The staff went above and beyond to help us with anything we needed. Anything we asked for, they would help! My husband got sick at a party and they even brought him medicine free of charge. I offered to pay but they said it’s no charge. The breakfast buffet is included and absolutely delicious! They have a mix of local foods and foods we are used to in the US but better. They have an omelette bar and so many yummy options. Again for 11 days we did not get tired of it. The staff at breakfast felt like friends. We took our young daughter and baby boy and the staff were always trying to make them laugh and make sure we were comfortable. Prakash was our favorite. Everyone here is so happy and welcoming. I could go on and on! I can’t recommend this hotel enough. If you’re in Kathmandu, look no further!!
Sat there watching the sunset over the hills .... amazing play of colour ... gorgeous to watch .... I spent over a couple of hours enjoying the solitude amongst the holiday revellers 🙃

I have been staying in this Hotel for a long time when it was run by different owner with the name, Base Camp but now, it's rennovated and made better. Service is excellent n ambience classy. This is by the lake and have nice bunglow surrounding a green garden. The food is good as well.
...sounds pretty wonderful and Fewa Lake does not disappoint. Beautiful views no matter time of day with forested valley ridges and the mountains overlooking it all.

It was good stay for a 4 days workshop. Staffs and service was excellent. The Manager of ground dining was very cordial and sincere . Food was delicious, specially the desserts. Reception service team was  helpful.

This hotel is in the center of Pokhara. Walking distance from the lake. It caters to a lot of international families with children. The outside bar proposed a great selection of tasty cocktails.  The breakfast buffet  was good but the atmosphere resembled  a school cafeteria. The staff at checked out seemed to be mirroring the rudeness of their European clients.

We chose the deluxe room as we were on our honeymoon, but the price definitely did not go hand in hand with the quality.  The concept is good, but it was the middle of winter and while the entire room and bathroom was freezing and uncomfortable, our bed was overheated due to the huge number of hot water bottles placed within the bedsheets, which was very uncomfortable.  The ambiance was very spooky at night and we always had a constant feeling of being watched.  The room had several decorative windows which could easily be slid open from the corridor and anyone could have looked in!  The water heater was often not working properly and in winter, the water is freezing cold, making brushing and washing up really uncomfortable! The electricity also went off at times, and no back up system was installed, which was inconvenient. We were disappointed that at the steep rate which was charged for our room, we were not even provided with complimentary breakfast! Overall, the pictures look a lot better than what the real thing is, but next time we'd prefer to stay someplace else.

It’s a pity, it would be a nice place to look at, but there is nothing super special about the temple that makes it worth the pushy sales tactics and rabid dogs and monkeys. 

People who were taking photos near the monkeys are clearly unaware that sometimes they scratch and bite - which if you do some quick research online you’ll find is common enough in Nepal that tourists have lots of stories of going to the hospital to get their rabies shots. 

Inside there is a Thangka school which is nice but they sort of pressure you to buy their lovely expensive paintings at inflated prices. You could probably do better with a street vendor if you haggle. I liked these schools initially but it got old after spending a few days in Kathmandu (they constantly try to take you to one of these schools or art houses).

On the best hotel in katjamndu trekkers home arrival at the hotel I was warmly greeted by mr. Saroj pudasaini. who welcomed me with open arms & a free room to a  deluxe top floor room with buttiful balcony.
Nice little boat ride over the lake for an hour. You have a person that paddles for you or can do on your own

What an awesome place. Very unique compared to other restaurants in Nepal. Its big, open and airy. Glass across the whole front of the restaurant to really show off the magnificent views across the Pokhara lakes. You have to take your shoes off on entering and most of the tables are floor seats with big cushions. There are also normal tables on the terrace outside. Staff are young and friendly. Menu is extremely varied with lots of choice for vegetarians, I can highly recommend the falafels. Definitely worth a visit if you are in Pokhara

Lovely staff, good service, couldn’t ask for more.

Picked up from airport by hotel bus which was great as arrived in late.

 Hotel was pleasant walk to Tourist areas. 

Good range of food onsite and close by.

Friends enjoyed the pool and some of the spa services (sadly I didn’t have time!).

Would definitely recommend as place to sta
On a clear day you have beautiful views of the mountains. Can take great photos. Road up is very rough, make your driver wait for your return  trip

This area of Kathmandu is where old meets everything,its for your shopping/eating/drinking,its for old streets, temples/stupas/street markets its a crazy area for tourists and locals alike.The culture,heritage and colour will keep you aware as you walk around such vibrant and busy streets.local people work and live here amid the throng of day to day life,and you cannot miss being part of whats going on,a lot of people just say its a tourist area,but engage in the markets,the side alley ways and small streets,the hidden courtyards,you will be amazed what you come across,its spread over a wide but walkable area,and which ever street you decide to take it will bring you back around to somewhere you have been.Lots of cafes to just sit and watch,what is going on around you,its a must place to walk/shop or just enjoy the culture of Kathmandu.

Pokhra is one of the main and beautiful city of Nepal where one can visit to see numbers of temples like Vindhyavaasini, Gupteshwar etc.  You can also visit places of tourists interest like Devi's Fall, Mahindra Caves and Phewa Lake.  It is the base for various adventurous Trek.
Exotic location.  Cordial and Very friendly support staff.  Appreciate services of Ms. pramila and Ms. sabina. Appreciate chefs culinary skills

The devastation from the 2015 earthquake is still very apparent. Some renovation has been completed, but there's still many years of work ahead because original methods are being used. Impressive as it is now, it'll be even more so when they finish the rebuild. We went in morning with guide when it was quiet, then went back late afternoon when it was packed with worshippers. Great to see the contrast.

OR2K has nothing to be compared with in Nepal so it is always unique.... the one in Pokhara has breathtaking views and a very nice room disposition with various areas and a terrace... food as always is mostly yummy.... it always depends on what you choose but the presentation is always lovely. THE STAFF ARE NICE BUT I FEEL THEY SEEM TIRED AND FED UP.... AND I DONT BLAME THEM. ARE THEIR BOSSES PAYING THEM WHAT THEY DESERVE TO DO CRAZY HOURS??

This is the typical place you should visit with a guide, if you don’t, all you see is different buildings, temples and statues but you don’t get the history behind it. Get a proper guide and learn about the culture and history.

I recommend everyone to experience this place for holidays and other functions.I really enjoyed my time there.Service are really impressive more than my expectation.Food are also delicious.Hope so I will join again.

Excellent  hotel and really nice staff and frindliy manager saroj pudasaini  the hotel manage took pickup serives bus stop.rooms are big and nice view  in balcony . Wifi was working jn room, location  was asom in thamel markets.
Great museum with some interesting exhibits of the different ethnic tribes of Nepal and the history of the Himalaya mountain range and the various peaks that have been climbed.

Very expensive in an environment which lacks all class, style and sophistication. Nothing complimentary and a wine list which reflects London Solo prices. Itâ??s absolutely ridiculous and obscene frankly

Itâ??s a corporate, itâ??s totally lacking and incredibly expensive. 

Shocking rip off

Don’t pay to go inside! You can take beautiful pictures from outside the gates for free. Once the guards leave late at night, the place is open to walk around and see for free too.
Tourists are charged ridiculous prices to enter during the day whilst they pick and choose who can go inside without paying. I completely understand the concept of making the tourists pay, however if you’re on a tight budget like us it’s not worth the money to go inside during the day!
Beautiful city to be visitet once in a year. Clean green and surrounded by mountains. Will love to see sadow of Machaapuchhre himal in lake.
Excellent location, very hospitable. Comfortable rooms and good food. Special mention Miss Naveena who made sure we were well taken care of.Must visit place in pokhara

I got really attached to this place. And I really loved Local Tea (Chaiya). Sitting on the street side looking around while sipping tea was really amazing experience. Place was full of local people and tourists from different countries. And the ancient temples and palaces surrounding the place gave different vibe to it. This place was breathing for it self. And the antiques sold on the street market were awesome.

Good service good food. Service with a smile. The team can’t do enough for you. Good rooms clean and hygienic. Sandeep  at reception and Nirmal in restaurant and Krishna bar supervisor and Adarsh on night shift food server were all outstanding in their work.

Really not too many good things to say about this place - at 20 bucks a night I still think it is over priced. The bed was as hard as the floor - the wifi worked so poorly that it wasn't worth the effort - and such little effort was made on the rooms, it felt more like being in a squat. 

Nice guys on the front desk though, and the shower was hot (for several minutes)
Definetely recommed Sarangkot when you visit in Pokhara. We left the hotel at 5 in the morning by taxi. Was totally worth it.
Sabina binita alsihwa was very accommodating and helpful, the lakeside view is stunning and peaceful, definitely would recommend.

I was very excited when an acquaintance mentioned this vegetarian restaurant, so a pile of colleagues got taken there on evening. 

The positive side was that it is fully vegetarian, so I didn't have to worry about avoiding meat without coming across too fussy.

However, the food wasn't that great at all and the place was full of stoned backpackers.

Phewa Tal is a lake in Nepal and is the biggest lake in the Pokhara. It is famous for having a lot of domestic and international tourists who visit and sail, swim and fish on the Phewa lake. The shadow of a nearby white mountain can be seen on the surface of the lake.

There is also a Talbarahi Temple Hindu temple on the center of the lake. If people want to visit the temple they must take a boat. Phewa Lake is the second largest lake in the Nepal. It is the only lake in Nepal, that have a Temple in the centre of the lake. And that temple is called Barahi Mandir.

The Kathmandu Durbar Square is everything i imagined it to be! I was i  awe when i came face to face with its main temple. Seeing something personally which you only see in TV or pictures is just amazing, what more if you see something as ancient and beautiful as the buildings in Kathmandu Durbar Square.

Really nice place to see the Himalayas. I advise to plan staying there for some hours, because starting at the mountain is healing in itself. 
Really nice place, the best of pokhara. 
A taxi from pokhara can be 1800 nrp for a two hours wait and then comeback

Awesome place to be cultured with religion and practices of Nepalese. 

Many monkeys so be very careful of your belongings as they can be quite aggressive. 
One of them tried to snatch my bag but failed.

At first we hated it. So crowded. So noisy. So polluted. Then, once we were rested and found our face masks it began to feel as if we had stepped into an amazing market place with its roots in the illustrious past of the Silk Road. There are so many treasures antique and new, outrageously valuable and ridiculously cheap, to discover here if one has the patience and the time to search in its crannies.

After reading the stories during my "young and impressionable years", it was humbling to see actual climbing gear, letters, medals, photos, and accounts of men and women who lived a very different life. Lost climbers, widowed porter families, and mountains of trash, all speak to the classic conflict of person against nature and person against themself. We would never know the edge of life were it not for their pursuits.

Moved me to three different rooms in the first week due to maintenance issues with no offer to move my belongings for me. I had to insist. I got stuck in the elevator. Hotel shuttle left me waiting for 30 minutes past scheduled pick up. Bathroom in room offered no privacy as curtains covering glass walls were bent. At no time did staff offer compensation or accommodation for the inconveniences. It would have been much better for example, had staff simply said,"we are sorry we are moving you for the second time, why don't you have dinner while we shift your belongings."

Stayed 7 nights at the Radisson during November. We usually stay here because the location is good - outside of Thamel but close to Thamel & other attractions. 

The hotel isn’t bad (stayed in the new wing) but not good either. We paid extra for a premium room which hadn’t been well maintained. The bathroom continually flooded and soaked everything on the bathroom floor, the blinds in the bathroom were dirty & mouldy & the carpet also very dirty.  We received no fruit basket or other food which we had expected & it appears other people received. 

My main complaint however is in relation to some (not all) of the front of house staff who were very unfriendly & terse to my Nepali husband. I’ve had this experience with the Radisson before when they wouldn’t even let my husband into the hotel even though he was a paying guest & have complained previously but little seems to have improved. For some absurd reason the reception staff seem to resent and be rude to Nepali guests which is totally unacceptable. This is an issue which must be addressed by the management of the hotel. I must add however that the housekeeping staff & concierge were extremely friendly & helpful & I cannot fault them.
It's known as the monkey temple which is good for the site seeing of the Kathmandu valley the it is located in the heart and you can see the full view of the city and many monkey in there

Sarangkot is beautiful place from where we can see the great view of pokhara valley. During our holiday in Nepal we fly from this place to pokhara via paragliding which was amazing and memorable. Need to go once here if you go pokhara.

This is my favourite restaurant in Pokhara!  The whole menu is vegetarian friendly and everything is literally delicious and healthy.  You can order randomly from the menu and need not to worry at all.  They also have a stunning view of the lake. You can sit there for hours reading, writing or chatting with friends.

I do like the lake with the boats and the walking trail along the lake.  It's just over commercialized for our taste.  The garbage seams a problem almost everywhere in Nepal. Pokhara itself is very clean compare to rest of Nepal cities.  So why they can not keep there best attractions clean? Maybe someone can answer that.

Swayambhunath temple is an iconic temple in Kathmandu.   Visited by many locals and tourists it is worth the climb to see the temple, monkeys, people and the views of the Kathmandu Valley.  But really we wouldn’t go back. Maybe it’s because it was so different from our first visit so many years ago when there were healthy monkeys everywhere, fewer people (ie not jam packed) and a sense of peace.  There was no sense of peace when we visited this time, the monkeys are a long way from healthy and my daughter was groped a number of times when we were making our way through the crowd.  Sad.

Visiting the Swayambhunath Temple was an incredibly spiritual experience. The architecture of the temple is simply breathtaking, and the atmosphere is serene and peaceful. Climbing up to the temple and seeing the panoramic view of the city was truly awe-inspiring. The site is beautiful and filled with history and culture. The monkeys running around only add to the charm of the place. Be sure to climb up to the top of the stupa to take in the stunning view of the city. This is a truly unforgettable experience. I highly recommend visiting this sacred site.

Kathmandu without Durbar square cant be imagine. The cosmopolitan falvour of Kathmandu can be expereinecd at Durbar sqare only. The square it slef has fascinating design and center of all attarction. The must vists place of Kathmandu.

International Mountain museum has huge capacity building where under one roof you get entire information and details about mountain and its related things. One of the must important place to visit while being in Pokhara.
Had a really good Xmas dinner spread the food was great and plenty of it very fresh and one of the better meals in Pokhara
The staffs behaviour are very nice. The food is good and we all enjoyed a lot of greenery and a village environment. Nilesh and Ayushman are very professional

As I look like a Nepalese descent, I was not asked to pay for the entrance. I just went straight in. I was exploring around 10 am in the morning and It was already crowded considering it's the 30th of December. What fascinates me is the birds that gather together in the square which is amazing to watch. The architecture really surprise me because I've never seen like it before in other country, it's like mixed with Old Chinese and Indian background. Overall, it was a nice experience walking throughout the whole square even though they are still fixing the damages from the earthquake.

Hyatt Kathmandu is a truly magical hotel, offering a unique blend of luxury and tranquility.
Located in a perfect spot—close enough to the city’s main attractions yet tucked away in a quiet, upscale neighborhood—it provides the ideal setting for both relaxation and exploration.

The atmosphere is peaceful, the surroundings are beautifully maintained, and the overall quality of the hotel reflects a high standard in every detail.

From the elegant design to the attentive service, everything about this place feels refined and serene.

Highly recommended for those seeking comfort, calm, and class in the heart of Kathmandu.

We had our best meal here. We went there in the evening. The cool and calm feeling, good crowd and music, lovely decoration, and the wonderful views of the lake - all these took our heart away. The food is really yummy.

We have stayed at this hotel for 8 nights. The staff and service is outstanding. I can’t say enough about our experience at the breakfast buffet with Manita. She is so kind and makes the best eggs I’ve had in my over 1 month of traveling. The Raddison is so lucky to have her.
We went in the evening and it was free to have a wander around. Didn't get a guide but perhaps it would be useful if you have time - really interesting, as is everything in this bustling city.

The place is good for history lovers, inside one can see history and culture of Nepal.One can see various mountain climbers statue too inside museum. There's a little theatre in which 15 mins show run from time to time.
Too many beggers. Rundown complex. Not much extra to see with paying 200r than what u see from the stairs. Too many dirty monkeys.

we were there in our first day of our trip to Nepal and  it was in the Krishna Birthday. It was amazing for us. 
have an umbrella with yourself for sunshine and rain.
Well maintained big lake close to old and new bazaar, Peach  Stupa, boating, Baraki temple mid of lake
What a buzzling street!! Full of stores, outfitters, jewellers and many more! A shopper paradise but you need to bargain your price!

Beautiful, quiet resort in the heart of otherwise chaotic and noisy Kathmandu. Lovely vistas from our 6th floor room. Helpful and courteous staff. Great area for shopping-only a 10 minute walk, restaurants, temples, etc.

I do like a good steak, but I should say that this vegetarian restaurant it's the best you can find in Pokhara. We were here before our trek and we were surprised by the service, so today we have repeated without be upset. 
The staff catch all the details, a candle to change, if I made a comment about the food they come to check, etc. I work in this industry, and it's something that I take attention to when I go to a restaurant.
The food it's great as well. Best pizza I've tried (and you can find pizzas everywhere in Pokhara).
Nice place to be relaxed, with good music in the right volume, nice illumination... great job!

The first impression in main gate before check in was horrible the gate security is rude. I like to travel Kathmandu in bike he was under estimating me cause I am in bike can’t afford 5star hotel. I am in soltee crown plaza last year also in bike for I had a wonderful experience there but in radison I haven’t and also I was not offer welcome drink in hotel

I realize that  each stupa has its own character, but this one is unique while being much like you would find at every stupa in Nepal. The interesting part if the face painted to represent Buddha's eyes (with eyebrows) atop of the shrine.  It is surrounded by many other smaller shrines. You cannot enter, but you can walk around. And there is a museum on the site.

Really nice and helpful for tourists. Many hotels clubs and restaurants. City centre. Easy to move around 
With love from Pakistan.

Great hotel in thamel ,good location comfortable place also good brekfast  ,staff are so friendly and helpful manager mr saroj , hot shower was asom .wifi is working definitely i will back this place .
The exhibits are quite informative and interesting. One can relate to a lot of science, adventure, and humanities while going through the exhibits.
Worth visiting and booking a tour guide as well. So much to see and wonderful pictures to take. hope you enjoy it like we did

Presented as the best local hotel in Kathmandu. The building is nice, but lacks elevator (that's what you get when going for old buildings).

Rooms are small, bathroom was basic, beds are not really comfortable.
Power shedding cripples the aircon following a schedule.
Breakfast was ok, but nothing fancy.

For our second night in kathmandu (9 days later), we went to Hyatt and had much better quality for a price that is not that much higher.

This property is charming in many ways be it the beautiful architecture, luscious green trees and plants, beautiful swimming pool and spa. We had a splendid time, however, there much to improve in terms of room service and maintenance. It took about an hr to deliver cutleries to the room and the room lock was out of battery. We were excited about the famous morning breakfast buffet which was quite average. But the staffs were always friendly and smiling.
Overall promising.
Love Pokhara.  Perfect getaway for us. We’re here for three days with young boys. Lots of things to do. We chose to do biking, horse riding, boat ride.

We visited the his serene lake & had an experience of boating in the evening, amidst cool breeze & fresh air. It was a lovely experience.
Worth a visit,as this lake is surrounded by picturesque hills.

.
The service is very good. After arriving at night, helping us change rooms is very reliable. Sheets and duvet covers are considered very clean in Nepal. After leaving, there is free coffee to drink. All in all, a very good stay, 3 nights in a row.
A busy place for travellers. The religious can visit a temple in the Lake. However a nice experience.

Thamel is a great old neighborhood with narrow streets and old buildings.  Many of the builders still had bracing from the 2015 earthquake.  I walked around shopping primarily for textiles (yak wool scarves and children’s clothes), puppets, and jewelry...there are numerous shops to choose from and all shopkeepers bargain. Stumbled on small shrines and stupas along the way.  Cafes are plentiful to take breaks from walking. I spent evenings and nights exploring and trying different restaurants.

We arranged to go on a paddle boat with a driver. Life jackets are required in all the  boats, so after we paid, we went to the rack to get a vest. The jackets are relatively new and in good condition. A helper came immediately to help me put on the jacket. Meanwhile, our driver was rowed out to the paddle  boat. We were told to wait at an open space, and very quickly, the boat was paddled to shore. The only tricky part was walking on the pontoon ( flat surface) to get on the boat. I was a little  frightened, but our driver helped me cross the distance to the actual paddle boat. The seats are comfortable with seat backs. No motor boats are allowed on the lake, so our adventure was very peaceful.

Came here for sunrise over the Annapurna range. Very busy, especially the tea house at the summit with everyone jostling for space. My partner got a much better view from just below with less hassle.
The views are stunning, although we did have to wait for the clouds to clear. Magnificent view of Fishtail mountain. Worth the effort but beware the incline from the car park and the steps to the summit! If you are asthmatic, take your inhalers!

I spend around three hours walking in Thamel. 
The shops were really nice and the prices were really cheap .
Unfortunately I got lost with a friend from the rest of the group and it was so hard to find them.. people do not speak good English and my smart phone did not work in their operator. 
Couldn’t use internet and had to go back alone.
I recommend staying with a Nepali person there all the time
The service is too good the staffs are very supporting the rooms were comfortable. The food was okay okay. The location is best very clean resort

Great experience..Good food, humble staffs..serence and peaceful environment..
The overall experience captures good memories with beautiful view of lakeside.

Every visit to Pokhara should include the sunrise trip to Sarangkot to  view the sunrise over the Annapurna  range. It would almost be a crime not to  visit this as  without a doubt it is  on a class of it,s own  and a one off site. Remember  your camera and heaps of  film , also  at any time of year it can be very chilly so take a  jumper and coat.   It is  around half an  hour from Pokhara city  but any taxi or tour company or hotel can organise a trip  here.  It will be  a high light of any visit to Pokhara.

The hotel is located close to tourist spots and the hotel itself is very clean and easily accessible in terms of location. Customer safety and customer service is also top notch. The rooms are clean enough, the kitchen/food is acceptable. The only thing missing from my room was a minibar and an iron, but this was easily made up for by the hotel's many other perks. In a word - I recommend to stop there during your trip to Kathmandu.
Try visiting only mountain museum in the town. You will get to know deeply about the majestic high mountains of Nepal as well as culturally Inhabitat indigenous people.

There are too many people and too little to see. It's still destroyed after the 2015 earthquake and I'm sorry to say that I don't think it's worth a visit. We expected it to be like this and we paid 1000 rupies for entrance mainly because we just wanted to support the renovation with some money. If you want to see Durbar Square, go to Bhaktapur, it's better.

My friends and I ate here twice during our stay in Pokhara. They loved the falafels. I had a garlic pesto pizza which was good and the Julia Buddha bowl which was also good. The food doesn’t come out at the same time of that is something you value. The smoothies are also very good. I asked for ice in mine. Nice view overlooking the lake.

Take a walk of around 45 mins from Thamel.

Check out the Ason bazzar, Annapurna temple on the way to the square and of course all the temples at the square. (Do read through the brochure).

Tough! As some are still under restoration after the earthquake, while  the rest on the outskirts need attention to maintain too.

Again, lot of wood craving accelerate  your heart beating!

Enjoy!
If you have any interest in the people of the Himalaya and / or the mountaineering this is a place to visit. A nice well laid out building with lots of information. Easy to spend 3 hours there.

Its a very good but tge rooms are vwry small and the bathroom also the breakfast is okay the beds are comfortable and the people and the service is very good and kind people location is very good near the centre very recomdable

Same restaurant as the one in Kathmandu (thamel), although this one enjoys a much better view over the lake. No matter wether you've been to OR2K in thamel or not, an before/after trek break at this restaurant is a must. And you'll will obviously find your favorite dishes on the menu.

We had a lovely stay at the Temple Tree. The staffs are very efficient and helpful. We enjoyed the breakfast spread. The gym was good addition too with the relaxing pool. Will surely stay here again when visiting pokhara.

Just like all temples around the world, it's a matter of taste, and I guess temples/buildings/monuments are not my taste.
It's a nice place to visit mainly because it's high and outside the city so you can catch nice views of Kathmandu.
It is not a must see if you ask me, but if you do, don't spend more than 1 hour there.
It's a great place to visit, a unsco site where you will found the history of nepal, nice architecture, and lots of temple

Good & comfortable stay. Room was spacious though a bit old construction it seemed to me. Breakfast was excellent.  Many varieties and good taste. Staffs were helpful and professional. Swimming pool was on rooftop. Nicely maintained.

Superb service and food. Special mention of Manita who took such good care of us at breakfast. Friendly,  soft spoken and skilled. She can be an asset for the hotel. Our stay at the hotel was seamless. Thank you Radisson Kathmandu. Would love to visit again.
I had been here for my last visit too. Now, many monuments has been renovated. This time I got chance to see living God Kumari too. It's recommended to explore Kathmandu.

If you’re looking for a place to have a romantic meal: this restaurant is the place to go! They have a spectacular lake view, which is great during sunset. Do make sure you’re on time, or all the best spots will be filled. Most of their indoor seats are on the floor, but they made it comfortable with big pillows. You do have to take off your shoes here, so you might want to wear socks🙂 Their menu is a delightful mix of different countries and flavors, and there's plenty to choose from! The dishes we had both tasted great and contained lots of fresh vegetables👌🏻 We’ll probably be back to enjoy another sunset.

This square which includes so many breath taking sites is without a doubt a MUST when visiting Kathmandu. The entry fee for foreigners is a bit high at Rs1500. It is well worth it. Wonder around and explore. Seek and find “The peacock carving”. It is known as the Mona Lisa of Nepal. Without a doubt as well, visit the paper making and printing business right near this carving. If you are lucky as we were, get a tour from the owner! Amazing on so many levels. Within his shop, there are so many beautiful gift ideas for your gift idea list for those at home.

Good and hyginic
Salina service is good
Location good
Rooms clean and properly maintain
Need to add more automated system such as electronic door lock, card based system instade of key based system
Atmosphere is good

This temple is extensive and very picturesque.  The steps up are steep but with plenty of photo opportunities on the way up, and the resident monkeys are pretty well behaved.  

This is definitely a must see attraction, with good views over Kathmandu from the top.
Great place to visit and to get lots of information about mountains and history...It was a informative trip
It’s seated atop a hilltop and you can have excellent view of the Kathmandu city from there. It’s a Buddhist monastery and attracts many visitors.
interesting shops and restaurants, but with narrow streets full of cars and motorbikes with no sidewalks.  It is hard to concentrate on the shops with the nonstop threat of being run over

we have visited many neighborhoods and areas in Kathmandu; Thamel is the best. it is a very nice touristic area where you can find the best restaurants, coffee shops, boutiques, ...Important advice: if you want to buy something from the boutiques or shops, please bargain and reduce at least 30 to 40% of the price you are told
it is a very safe area, too, we were staying in Mulberry hotel and we could enjoy nice night walking times and nobody bothered us, but please, do not carry lot of cash money with you

I was a little disappointed with this hotel.  I thought it was a bit overprice for what you were getting.  The hotel is beautiful made with traditional Nepalese style of building with a courtyard and garden.  It is off on a side street so it is very quiet.  Rooms are average in size and I found them very dark - especially when the power is out.  There is no generators so when the power is out, we are left in the dark.  I got tire of brushing my teeth and taking a shower in candle light.  The power never seem to be on during the early morning hours or late at night when we are back at the hotel.  It was  $110 US in a delux room - at the Hyatt it was $130 US which has 24 hour electricity and all hotel amenities.  The good at the restaurant is not very good either.

This hotel was one disappointment after another. The rooms were shabby, even by Nepal's standards. I used their travel desk to book a driver for a sunrise drive. No driver showed up for my 4am pick-up.  When I asked the desk to call the booking agent, his phone was turned off. There was no manager on duty until 8am; so no one could assist with the problem.  It seems trivial compared to the other issues, but they also neglected to make my breakfast box.  This hotel has problems in multiple departments. This hotel is not worth your time or money.
Well, there're always plenty of people here 'cause of its Ktm reputation, but still Israeli food is great and or2k special platter is the most valuable and tasty deal.

I returned to this hotel for the 4th time and definitely expected a much better experience than the one I had. They charged my friend a rediculous $15 for breakfast and the hotel is the most expensive in Kathmandu. The guy at the front desk was pretty rude about it as well.

The touristy centre of kathmandu, pick up your trekking gear here as everything is generally cheaper - aquatabs are only 250 rupees, can hire sleeping bags for approx $1 USD a day, Sportswear International has great goose down jackets for around 6500 rupees, lots of souvenir shops and eateries.

Durbar Square is the centre of Kathmandu, in the days of the Hippy Trail it was also called Freak Street. There is a large open air market for souvenirs of every type but it is the building around and about that are the real stars.
A good number of the buildings were either damaged or even destroyed by the 2015 earthquake and are ether under restoration or being held up by scaffolding (steel and bamboo).
One of the buildings is the home to a Living God and is truly fascinating.
We had the great good fortune to be there on the day of The Festival of Colours (Holi) and it was one of the high points of a 15 day visit to Nepal.

I’ve eaten here many times over several years of traveling to Nepal.   I’m sad to say the food and service has gone downhill.  Today i thought i would try 1 more time.   i sat down and after 10 minutes i asked for a menu.  despite several servers walking past me many times.   Then - 15 minutes later i asked if i could place an order.    Then - 10 minutes later I asked if I could get the tea I ordered.   Then - I asked for more hot water and was told I had to pay for more water.   The food was Ok - nothing special that would warrant putting up with the bad service.  I also went to the location in Pokhara last week and found the service bad there too.   Perhaps there has been a managemt / culture shift.   It’s  too bad really - used to be my fav place in Thamel.

I wasn't the biggest fan of this place. The place feels less pristine and holy and more just like a place for people to sell their wares. Though its not bad by any stretch of the imagination, I would still tell someone to go if they want to see monkeys or are new to this style of temple. It does have a nice view at the top though, and I was told they sometimes have some rituals there.

From what I had heard of Pokhara and it's famous lake I had high expectations of what too me a lot of efforts to reach Pokhara after a 6 hours hell ride on a Micro Bus from Kathmandu. Unfortunately the people of Pokhara are only interested in one thing: to distract you from your money with the least amount of work.

The tourist authority seems to have no idea how to attract visitors by creating a promenade with shady trees and beautiful benches for visitors to take a rest. The park in the north is ugly, littered with garbage and beggars occupy the lawns. To the south you will find the lake surrounded by fences and barbwire.

For me it was just a one time experience to visit such a place wihich seems to be occupied by backpackers trying to spend most of their time stoned with alcohol and drugs - maybe a good idea to get a better view of Pokhara.

It's a place of marketing this hotel is really nice and quite rooms and far from busy road so we gote a really nice sleep and they have very good and helpefull people who make me trip as well. I will highly recommended for this placed for stay.

Please never visit this hotel. At the very outset, their website specifies airport pick up and drop. After booking online, when I confirmed to the hotel about my arrival time and details, the manager promptly asks me to take a cab and that they don't offer any such facilities and Very rudely asks you "Sir, don't show if you want. we have got our money. Its up to you to take a cab and show up." 
The place does not have air conditioning or lifts and the manager promptly told me " This place is not for Indians. they want ac lift tv ! We give ethnic feeling !"

This place is a strict NO - GO for a family visitor holidaying . unless you want a recluse to drink amidst dark lights sitting in dark corners. ..

See the Everest mountain . Then many type of nepali  kalchure​ , too much mountain picture . Photo of yeti ,pashanlyamu Sherpa,tenjing norke Sherpa adman hilari it's fast Everest mountainor in the world

It was a nice experience to stay in this property.....neet n clean....the staff is so cooperative specially miss shilu joshi...other from restaurant staff they are also good in nature and they are so polite 😀

A former palace site and a must see tourist site located not far from Thamel. The old buildings are marvelous and definitely worth checking out. Luckily, most of the buildings weren't damaged by the 2015 earthquake. I came around 4-ish and was lucky to see the Kumari. Be advised that you are not allowed to take a photograph of her.
They charge tourists 1,000 NPR just to enter the site, which is only valid for a day. However, there is only one ticket gate that charges you for admission. You can access the site through other unpopular entrances if you want to enter the site free of charge.

After you climb hundreds of stairs, you’ll get an amazing view of the city of Kathmandu...you can buy some souvenirs, have a coffee...also, you can meet a lot of monks to who you can donate some money to rebuild their temples after the earthquake. And beware the monkeys! :)

Do not book the room it is extremely bad , behaviour of the staff is extremely bad and rude , you will feel disrespected , Manager also does not respond, food is extremely bad, chef does not accommodate dietary requirements, smelly room ,stinky room, stained room, itâ??s like youâ??re staying in garbage, front desk staff needs training, not hyatt standard, better book Marriot- amazing hotel Marriot, Little expensive but worth staying,

Best option for backpackers or bike riders in the heart of Kathmandu Valley
Have a nice cozy resturant with delicious varities of food.
Root top bar provides great views of the Valley and a good gathering or working space with peaceful environment.

It was amazing to see elements of all the cultures of Nepal, like Gurungs, Sherpas and others. Also, great to see many pictures of all mountain ranges across the world and not just of the Himalayas. The documentary of the Himalayas was also nice. A must go for all tourists!

Nice, it was ok to be a 5star hotel. The food in NYE was ok. But not amazing. The people working there were nice and friendly sometimes. 
It was ok on the whole, but I would expect much more in a 5 star hotel.
This is worth seeing, very educational but can be hard to follow what its all about. A lot if info on the different people of nepal also.

The rating said this was a 5 star hotel.  It's more like a 3 star.  Very disappointing. The property and grounds are beautiful.   But the rooms, although spacious, are shabby and need some major renovation and upkeep.  Bed was not comfortable. Room just felt dirty even though it had been cleaned.  Also, front desk all male staff were not friendly.  They appeared agitated, didn't make much eye contact, and had a rude tone. Important to know that the hotel is situated away from the local town. The hotel offers a $30 ride to get there. This is beyond ridiculous. Find a cab instead or just walk.  It only took us 15 minutes or less to get there. The spa has very limited hours and not flexible.  We couldn't get a spa appointment when we were there so book ahead of time.  I will not be staying there again.

Really enjoyed all the buildings and the history there.  The wood carving was amazingly detailed.  Not a lot of facilities so bring water and use bathrooms before hand.  It was sad to see all the damage from the latest earthquake.  Entire buildings were gone.

Thamel is the place to go if you want to see lots of interesting shops and restaurants. A hub of where travelers go to buy outfits to wear mountain trekking. I went here to check out Pilgrims Bookstore and to purchase cashmere scarves. The streets are narrow, so be careful when walking and enjoying this place, as there are motorists. The shop owners are friendly and truly enjoy your business.
If you like handicrafts, beads and singing bowls, this is the place to go☺️

I stayed here for several nights in August.  The hotel facilities and room were fine in terms of comfort and cleanliness, but this felt like a large, impersonal hotel even though it is not that big.  There were several tour groups staying here and the hotel seemed to be catering to them and pretty much ignoring everyone else, especially a solo traveler like me.

One of the reasons I stayed here was that it was just outside the main touristy area of Pokhara, but still walking distance.  The walk is about 15-20 minutes.  Part of it is on a pathway, but about half of the walk is on a narrow dirt road with traffic in close proximity.  They have a shuttle that runs several times a day to the downtown area but the timings aren't very convenient. 

I inquired about a tour of the area and the front desk didn't seem very happy to help with that and quoted a relatively high price but had no info on the itinerary.  I was able to negotiate a much better price with a taxi driver in town.

So in all, I would not recommend this hotel and would not stay here again.

Staff didnâ??t care for people waiting in line but prefer to attend guests who break line. Post check in and completion of payment I was told that the rooms were not ready.
Next evening when I came back from work I was shocked to see the room open but thankfully noting was missing. Despite repeated requests the staff took an hour to give a travel adapter.

Breakfast is very average and not really worth the dollar. So avoid paying extra for this in your room rent.
You cannot go to Kathmandu and not visit here. So much to keep you busy! Everything you could possibly be thinking of buying you will be able to find here.

Changes with morning and evening light.  Lots of actvity to view. A delight for photographers.  Lots of restaurants lining the walkways, gaily coloured boats a feast for the eyes.  Well worth a stroll.

I reserved the KGH after reading reviews and wanted to pamper myself after hiking the Everest Basecamp Trek. However, I ended up cutting my stay short due to WiFi needs.  

PROS
* The grounds of the hotel were beautiful 
    * Lots of green areas, trees, and unique inner sanctuary to get out of the Thamel chaos
* The rooms and hotel was very clean

CONS
* Crowded - I realize May is high season, but the hotel was packed.  I could rarely find a place to sit down in the courtyard
* Noisy - With lots of people comes noise. I didn’t mind it so much except it was quite noisy even in my room 
* Expensive - The hotel is very expensive compared to other hotels in the area. 
* Terrible WiFi - The wifi speed was so poor it was unusable. I wanted to upload several YouTube vlogs from my Everest hike, but was unable to do so. I even tried from the lobby and got less than 0.1 mbps dl testes with speedtest.net

The rooms are so smelly that we asked them to take away the sofas literally!  Dirty filthy carpets all turned black almost! 
Bathroom ventilation and acoustics not good. You can hear the neighbors very well. 

The staff needed atleast 4-5 reminders for  helping with basic kind of request we would make. 
The rooms on the upper floors smell of pigeon, you can even spot pigeon nested outside your window in some rooms. Near the club! 
Rooms below have stuffiness a friend I made at the hotel described how smelly smoky their lobby was, it was like being a passive smoker! they were from USA. 

Air conditioners would stop functioning at night. we practically called the staff 2 days in a row in the middle of the the night at 3 to get the Aircon working better. Even if u leave the key the entire day the room would not cool below 24 degrees. 
 
Only good thing about the hotel is that the food is very very good. Very very lavish buffet! I think they can enter some world contest and win with the number of people we saw dining there daily.  Chefs did fantastic work. 

 The hotel is at a quiet location. With xtra xtra  large gardens and pool and other things.
