Bed leg almost broken state! Study table desk legs also very shaky! Not good we asked the staff when we checked in to the room and the man said â?? itâ??s all old furniture, so it will be like that! Mam.â?
This temple is difficult to find if you don’t have map. Only 10 minutes walking from centre of Thamel. Also there is a lot of restaurants where you can drink very good Nepalese tea or coffee

stayed at months back , found the resort with preserved eco practices and best services in town. rooms were neat and clean. best landscaping resort in pokhara . staff were very helpful, meal were testy , every staff were handpicked skilled.  highly recommended and will comeback soon.
We had been to this place in March 2020. Lovely place to be in. Lots of small shops in the temple complex where you can buy mementos.

As far as over touristed districts go this is not a bad one. Nepals are pretty chill. A day to sightsee kathmandu is enough though and nothing to see here that is the normal nepal, just a lot of souvenir shops, bars restaurants and hotels.
Very beautiful lake indeed. It’s clean and surrounded by hills. You can take a small peddling boat or a big boat also.

Unfortunately we did not have perfectly clear weather so did not get the spectacular views of the Himalayas as the sun rose, but had only a glimpse. Otherwise it would be a 5.
We visited the widowed women’s cooperative there. Widows are considered to be unlucky since their husband died, so no one wants to marry them or have them in their home.  A few years ago an NGO helped them to set up a cooperative.  They now earn a living and are gaining respect in this culture. They are also gaining voice politically so perhaps one day this stigma will be no more. I purchased 100% cashmere pashminas for gifts cheaper than in shops in Kathmandu or Pokhara.  Since there is little overhead and no middlemen, the money goes directly to the women.  This I easily give 5 stars. I felt privileged to support them.

Staying here currently, never been on a more rock hard bed in my life- I think I'll sleep on the floor

Everything else is okay bit considering this hotel is expensive you would expect a decent bed. The room I had in Thamel had a perfect bed and was half the price of this place
Beautiful resort with a lot of greenery and open spaces. Super helpful staff and great service. Breakfast was amazing as well!

Visited in December 2022. We went to this place after official business hours. So no need to pay. We walked around the buildings. There are a lot of restaurants around. We were told to visit any restaurant at an elevated level in order to have a view of the durbar square. We spent less than 15 minutes here.

This temple is hard to ascend to, lots and lots of stairs. When you arrive at the top, it is just wow! The stupa, the different sections and structures, prayer wheels, statues are just breath taking! The monkeys are a pretty fun touch, they’ll come right up and swipe your food from you- so be mindful of that! Pictures say it all- just a beautiful place. The view of Kathmandu from the top will knock your socks off.

The lake itself is nice, and sunset offer some good photo opps with blue fishing boats "parked" along the shore. For sociologists, Fewa Lake also offers a good playground to study tourist and social behaviours among neo-hippies, young souls searching for their souls, or just for a place to get drunk cheaply. You won't see many nepalis around Fewa Lake, except those selling fruits or curios to tourists...

Sunrise view is not bad for first time viewer from hills .

It is not as spectacular as seen in Darjeeling or some other hill station

Well located hotel ESP for business traveller .....
Gud service and Gud breakfast buffet .
Rooms and bathrooms need to change with time .....
Beautiful new spa.
Staff Gud and courteous .
Recommend for business travelers who want to be in the centre .
Worth its price ....
The Palace was not built yet, fund so dirty and dusty. Entry fees is not much worth. This palace is closed to Thamel Area.

Sarangkot is 30 minutes drive from lakeside Pokhra. It provides great views of Annapurna mountain range. On a clear day almost all important peaks are visible and it’s fun to spot them. 
We were able to see all major peaks and that was quite an experience. 
Must do in Pokhara.
I always love to take my colleagues who are new in the Pokhara. This place got major information about mountaineering so its a one shot information center where you don't have to speak much.
Great food and atmosphere. Good drinks and cocktails and amazing view of the lake. Staff very attentive and free wifi which is helpful
You will have a great view of one lovely part of Nepal. This place remain cloudy day time also. You can enjoy many people flying, doing paragliding. It is one of the must visit place of pokhara.

It's a nice neighborhood until the locals start offering you stuff and services. They just wouldn't leave you alone. So be prepared..
But you can find many great restaurants and cafes.

Heritage pieces of architecture - shrines, temples, royal palace & Newari architectures. But sadly, some part are still under reconstruction due to 2015 earthquake still with NRS1000 entrance fee (for foreigner like me). If you're a lover of world heritage architecture well, you will surely love it.
The stay was nice comfortable the breakfast was amazing the quality was good we enjoyed the swimming pool jacuzzi should have had the strong force one

Well worth a visit. We had a succession of tasty vegetarian dishes over several days. Attentive service, great view over the lake, plenty of choice, comfortable, freshly prepared with high quality ingredients. Highly recommended.
Superb vegetarian food, atmosphere and service. Staff are so attentive and the restaurant is very clean, stark contrast to the grubby Kathmandu branch.

Every kind of food you could hope to find. Lots of souvenir, book, map and craft shops. Bustling, and a great place to potter about. You simply cannot visit Nepal without spending some time exploring the delights of the Thamel streets!
It's very beautiful and historical buildings and I have enjoyed the structure of Kathmandu Durbar Square. It's worth to visit.

Friendly, clean and quiet place to stay in Kathmandu. Conveniently located in Thamel (the tourist area). Hot water and everything close. This is not a luxury hotel by any means, but is decent and very affordable by western standards.

Though I am not a museum person but museum is informative and interesting. They covered ethnic groups around Himalayan area, global warming and of course about mountains and people/groups who concurred them first. 

It was motivation to see how some mountaineers climb so many top mountain peaks. Definitely recommended.

This is a large facility jam packed with information.  It is located outside the town proper on lovely grounds. For people interested in the topic there is literally something for everyone here.  However this is an old style museum so while it is a treasure-trove of information on all-things-mountain climbing it could use an update.  With so many museums these days having dynamic, hands on exhibits with “bling”  it will be hard to keep up younger generations engaged and interested.  Having said that, it is amazing that in a country as poor as Nepal that it has such a great facility. Nepal is synonymous with mountains and mountain climbing so it would be great if they had the resources to keep this important museum updated and current. I’m old school so I really enjoyed the exhibits, film  and all the information.  Hope a philanthropist with an interest in mountain climbing will chip in !!

Beautiful, tranquil hotel down a small back street in Thamel, the main tourist area.  This  place is a haven after a day of exploring the craziness of the city,  the staff are so helpful and will happily help with suggestions of day trips, activities or even just booking taxis or guides.  There are complimentary morning walking tours of the city and yoga on the rooftop.  The restaurant serves excellent food.  Decor wise it is very much in the style of a traditional Newari house but with touches like modern western style bathrooms.  We also did a cooking lesson making momo with the hotels head chef, which was one of our favourite parts of our trip.

Overall, it was a pleasant stay but not as expected. The room carpets need replacement, and at minimum a Smart TV should be provided. While the stay was pleasant overall, the room conditions fell short of expectations
Best location with lots of restaurants, bars, shops, people from all over the world... You will find everything you want here!

Good hotel, pleasant staff, restaurant has an interesting spread in breakfast and dinner, centrally located, close to major attractions and business, easy transport availability. Overall a good choice both for business and pleasure
Lake has facilities for boating. You can take a boat and go around the clean lake and enjoy the scenerio around.
too much touristic trap, but anyway picturesque and charming. shop after shop  with nepalese ( and chinese) goods

Rooms were old and not well maintained. Air condition made a lot of noise and sleep quality was very poor. Service was average. Breakfast was decent. Basic amenities like tea coffee maker, safe deposit locker, toiletries, etc was available. Mini bar was not functional.  Hot water took forever to come in shower. Not worth it for the price you pay.
P.S (Most Important) :- There was zero regard for Covid. No staffs were wearing mask. Not even kitchen staffs! They were not ready to wear a mask even after being reminded! So go at your own risk!!

We arranged a early morning to there to see the sunrising, but I don't think it is the best place. The mountain scenery is just so so. If you arrived too early, some young men asked for 300Rs for guiding, in fact it is only a very short uphill hiking.

A great place  to collect your thoughts.  Beautiful architecture and lots of nice places to eat  and buy gifts.  Since the earthquake the buildings are being renovated/replaced. A must visit when in Nepal

Seriously the next time one of the guys trying to flog those flute things came near me or tried to slip his hand in my handbag I was going to lose it at him. One was even waiting outside my hotel in the morning, I had a bag with clever zips and yet I could feel him trying to steal off me. Sleazy horrible flute men were not appreciated and I think the shop keepers should try and keep the thieves away from the area, it must be bad for business surely?
This is a must visit place in Kathmandu. You will feel that you have took a Time Machine. The entry ticket for foreigners is 1000 rupees and includes the entry fees for the palace.
Full of really interesting information on the Himalayas  - how they were formed, the people who live there etc.  Good history too on the 8000m peaks

Really nothing to say about that because I have seen nothing due to cloudy weather. It was 21st february when i went there. was expecting many things & also heard so many exciting experience from people about Sarangkot but i was so unfortunate. weather just ruined my trip! 

I would recommend, please choice right time and season and check weather forecast before you go...otherwise it would be frustrating.

In love with OR2K. Really great food, amazing views of lake Phewa, and the atmosphere is like nothing I’ve ever experienced. Floor seating with candles once the sun went down, great vegan and vegetarian food, and nice staff. Can’t wait to visit again!
Very nice place to visit, it is a historical place where all ancient stories where happened, it's recommended hardly to visit..
A bit hectic getting up to the boat, but once on your boat a very nice relaxing row around the lake.  Our boat driver was a nice Tamang man who kept up a pleasant conversation in Nepali.

Positive Comments

Lakeside Retreat services have never disappointed me. Beautiful garden and rooms.This was my 1st visit to Nepal got an excellent hospitality &  nice spread breakfast buffet with a good taste.. and this kind of service can make me visit again . I wanted to mention that lady name who have received us and treated like her guest Ms. Luna. keep going on and best of luck
Mr. Namraj Sharma (restaurant manager) had explained us the Nepali menu and was very kind to assist us for momos and I would suggest you to please try their momos. 
Love the vibe here as soon as you enter. Awesome people with happy faces always carrying a smile on their faces ever ready to help. Monmohan  Rimal the Front Office Manager is such a  lovely person he knows exactly what his guests want he is an asset at the Front Office. Enjoyed my short stay here. Thanks to my friends could enjoy the warmth at this place. Keep rocking ❤❤❤❤❤
Last but not the least I would also like to thank the housekeeping attendant who was always ready to assist you 24*7.

Negative Comment

We had stayed for 7 days but the bedsheet was changed only once.

I had a great experience staying at Kantipur Temple House in Jan 2023. The outside decor is beautiful, staff was nice & the location is pretty convenient. The hotel has taken an eco-friendly approach & there is no paper (except toilet paper) or disposable items used anywhere. Do note that this is not a luxury hotel, you get what you pay for. 

Breakfast was simple but satisfying. The rooms get slightly cold and I wish the heater was more powerful, but the blanket provided is quite sufficient. The lights in the rooms felt a bit dim at first, but then it starts adding to the character of the place.

My title says it all. Destroyed by earthquake - Save your time and money until restored. It is too bad they want to charge the same price as when it was "whole" because I bet most people just don't go, when they probably would if they discounted entry (and these funds could help).

A visit to Kathmandu would be incomplete without spending time in the key cultural site that is Hanuman-Dhoka Durbar Square, an amazing complex of beautiful temples and shrines for both Buddhists and Hindus, plus the Royal Palace area. 
Good progress has been made with the renovation of the major damage caused by the earthquake, but there remains much to be done to restore it all to its former glory.

After 5 days in Pokhara, most menus look the same. OR2K has the nicest dining environment, a few non-standard menu options, and an unobscured lake view. Being on the third floor cut down on mosquitos/bugs for outdoor seating. The prices are also very reasonable for the tourist oriented restaurants. They are definitely my Pokhara top pick.

I stayed here for a couple of days in October 2017, the hotel has some strengths and weaknesses however the main positive is the garden in the centre of the hotel as this is a true oasis within the busy city of Kathmandu, you won't believe our peaceful it really. 

The main draw back is that the rooms are dates, their are five stories and no lift and the drains sometimes smell. On a more positive note the rooms, are clean, you get a good range of toiletries and the showers are hot. Their is a spa on site that has reasonable priced treatments, I can personally recommend the holistic message :)

Breakfast is good and has eggs cooked to order and the lunch and dinner options are also good, the hotel has a coffee bar and alcohol bar both of which are open all day, and their is wifi however it does drop out a lot. The hotel is in a great location in the centre of Kathmandu and is surrounded by shops, bars and restaurants.

Super luxurious Radisson Kathmandu is the hotel of choice in ethereal Kathmandu. Ideally located to all major attractions, temples , Viharas , cultural and spiritual sights, restaurants and shopping.  The rooms are luxurious, spotless and clean. Staff most friendly and welcoming.  The buffet breakfast is sumptuous. The personal attention of Ms Bidhata Shreshtha , Joint manager, was exceptional.  A most memorable stay

We stayed here 3 years ago. This time our room was noisy, small and uninspiring. Staff didn't answer questions but had some general standard answers ("we know what all tourists want"). Food was presented very nicely but was rather bland.

It would be rude not to go if you are there .. lots of information and pictures of the mountains and people who live on it and indeed have climbed it.
Interesting facts and figures and some great stories too ..

Since my friend told us that is the most famous heritage area in Kathmandu, we decided to go there and saw plenty heritages, even some towers damaged by the earthquake several years ago, and some under repair. Still lots of pigeon around, make the square more active

Day well spent with family. At Sarangkot mountain today we supported women entrepreneurs- they weave wool and make scarfs, shawls etc. it’s a group of about 30 women who want to earn a living and learn a skill set. Some work from home as they are raising kids, farming in addition to weaving. I believe in women being independent  and I was so happy to support their business today. Shopping for a good cause ❤️💰❤️ @ Sarangkot Mountain

I was hesitant to come her based on reviews of high prices, but compared to our hotel food, this place is generous. Our only problem is being too full after lunch. High quality food, lovely view and cozy atmosphere.

I ordered a banana lassi without sugar and it was wonderful! The stuffed vegetable combo was fantastic too. The cauliflower pie great if you're craving comfort food and the salad that came with it is a fresh pallet cleanser. We got gluten free buckwheat roti as well- indulgently crispy and nostalgically tart.

A nice place to take a break from local Dahl bat kitchens which are also not to be missed.
The information was immense.  It gave an insight into how these people coped and the equipment they used.

Boating in Phewa lake is a good experience, though it might get boring for some. The legs might get cramps for prolonged sitting. The view is good. One can see the monkeys in the left side forest and the city on the right. As one approaches the Tal Barahi mandir which is situated on an island in the middle of the lake, one can also see the arati performance from the city side.
Really lovely place to visit. Lots of activities. Bike hire and water sports. Easy to get to from Kathmandu and well worth a visit. Lots of companies offering treks and a great place to start from.

I’m reliably informed that there are 365 steps up to the main stupa and, while I didn’t count, I can well believe it! I do know that there’s an entry fee of 200 rupees, which is pretty cheap, compared to other places. The hilltop where the stupa is located is a little cramped, and the striking sights sadly have to share space with a lot of very determined vendors. Additionally, if you want a good photo of stupa, you’ll need a wide lens to get it all in. The view over the city is fantastic - it’s worth a visit for that alone! I recommend going around sunset for the best views and cooler temperatures.

Absolutely love this place. Amazing coffee, food and vibe.
I have spent the last few days here relaxing eating and planning my next trip the wifi is solid, awesome view, relaxed atmosphere and the staff are amazing thank you for putting up with me :)

We hired a paddle boat for half a day from Fewa Boat Association @ Hallan Chowk on 12th March for fun. After spending 1.5 hours, the paddle boat was filling with water till our ankles. A passer by paddling to work across the lake told us that our paddle boat was lopsided and that we should head back to the rental place. We tried to paddle it to it but we were unable to do so. We decided that if we paddled it to the shore nearest to where we were it would be better. We reached to the nearest point and moored it. We called the rental company and expressed our disappointment and told them to come to collect the leaking boat. They sent a rude member of staff who clearly lacked manners while dealing with me. He took the boat back and told me contact the rental company for any further refund etc. We went today to ask the rental company politely for a refund. Instead of an apology, the manager of that place started lecturing me and told me that I should be grateful that they had not charged me to get the boat back. They were talking over me and lecturing me on how I should not get any money back for the leaking paddle boat rental. Customer service is poor and the manner they spoke to me was terrible. Don’t hire any boats from this place! Total rip off.
Best place for vegetarians in Pokhara. Wide menu, fare prices and a very nice view to the lake. They are very flexible when you request an adjustment to your plate

Arrived at 6.15am and all the Chinese tourists were already there! Viewpoints are the top terraces of homes/shops. You can get seats on the 2nd and 3rd floors. They will try to sell you the usual souvenirs and such. Just get a chai masala and you're fine. One man decided to be my guide and asked for USD20 before I left. You can just enter any view points for free. The view is awesome. On a clear you can see the peaks of the Himalaya.great view of the city on too!
Great central location, food was really good. Reasonably priced. Relaxed atmosphere, range of different seating areas

It’s a very nice hotel to stay.  I recommend all to visit this place once.  Restaurant,  service, Housekeeping  all is very good. Sataff are so Friendly  and hotel manager mr.saroj pudasainj very helpful .

Stay some time with out much expectations

The hospitality I received was not good as I read it in the reviews. I was on a golf trip with my friends of 12 people and stayed there for 2 nights. The way the staffs treating foreigner tourists and a Nepalese tourist was completely different. I saw the staffs being very nice and polite to foreign tourists whereas they didn't treat the same way to Nepalese tourist. They need to change this mentality after all we all are guests to them. However, rooms were clean and the hot water was perfect.

The food is really, really great (best falafel!) and the staff is friendly. But the tables are super close and the room is so packed, that privacy is not happening at this place.
I wish the atmosphere would be a little bit better. 

But if you are into hanging out with others tourists and expats, this place might be just for you.

At first it is overwhelming to all the senses but underneath it still retains a little of the charm
The shops are all over priced for tourists but that’s also part of Thamel

Try falafel burger,  phad thai noodles,  thali .
Low seating and chill out ambience. 
Slow service and not much choice in deserts.
Rate are on higher side

The breakfast at the hotel was exceptional, thanks to Susan's outstanding service. He greeted us warmly, catered to our needs, and his attentiveness made our morning delightful. We're grateful for his excellent service. Thanks for the cookies as well.

If you're lucky enough to visit during a festival, then the place explodes with even more life and colour than usual. A fascinating mix of buildings and temples, much of which is under reconstruction, it is utterly charming and a must-see.

Beautiful resort in pokhara. Visited many resort and hotel but we found our needs here for comfortable stay, healthy food , natural gargen and friendly staff. Resort manager was professional and friendly. Great to exposure time at the lakeside retreat. Overall excellent experience. Specially thanks to Manager Manmohan to make our expereince memorable. Definetly comeback again.

It is an interesting place as the temp,e square sounded by Buddhist and Hindu Temple. From the temple , a beautiful view of Kathmandu valley is seen.

Atmoshere here just WOW! You can go here to sit all day with laptop and to work or chill . Beautiful lake panorama, comfortable sofas... 

About food- only vegetarian. Its good. But not everyone would like it...

Definitely worth a visit when in Kathmandu. So much to see and would recommend getting one of the local tours, ours cost us approx €10 and the information was excellent. Interesting to see the cremation sites and lots of local history

Worth Visit .. One of the good lakes I have seen .. Go the back side of lake to get a very peaceful view of it.. Beautiful Cycle track around it.. You have boating facility available but if not great quality..If Govt develops water sports 5 star can be given..
Just fun while boating by yourself. Due to earthquake the lake was dirty but still you won't care about it while enjoying.

We rated our two night stay here to relax  following a trek average because:
Poor welcome experience where it took half an hour or more to get room keys. Our group were assigned twin rooms where doubles had been booked. 
The standard grade room was small but adequate. The bathroom smelt unpleasant and dirty towels from previous guests had been left so unsure if any cleaning had been carried out. 
There were building works ongoing on the stairs and landings so you had to duck under rudimentary scaffold and workers to get up the stairs, and the lift was out of service (so 4 floors of stairs each time and with luggage on arrival). None of this was mentioned at check in. 
Our rooms were noisy at night due to air con fans above, plumbing noises and pidgeons on the roof, as well as the distant buzz of Thamel nightlife. 

The location in central Thamel, communal areas, pretty gardens and buffet breakfast included were great. Woukd recomend an afternoon tea in the sunny secluded gardens. It's a shame the accommodation itself was disappointing compared to elsewhere in Thamel and Pokhara.

It is a very wonderful time to stay at Radisson and I love it so much. Service is perfect and breakfast was delicious. The one I like most was the pillow and I have sound sleep there. Hotel serve to place WHO paper as a greeting. This is an exception. Thank you so much, Radisson.
Had a wonderful boat trip across the lake to start the trek towards the peace pagoda. Paid NPR 750 for one way drop.

We ate at OR2K several times whilst in Pokhara and really enjoyed the atmosphere, the wonderful staff and service, and especially the fantastic food. Our daughter loved that she could get Soya milk. The combo platter and various veggie snacks are delicious. We also enjoyed a mushroom burger. The mint lemonade was delicious too. Great place to spend an evening, with background of relaxing music and great ambience.
One of the busiest and very comfortable place to stay in kathmandu . Highly recommend to stay before trekking where you have access to everything you need for trekking

While the main building is still a ruin and many of the other buildings are still being repaired this Square is still a must-see in Nepal.  There is also a large open area with tons of vendors (not clothing) if one is looking for things to buy.

one of the best hotel in kathmandu we ever stayed. Friendly environment everyone willing to help any time. our room was specious and 24hours hotshower. Hotel location just in the middle of the city very easy access to restaurant,  spa, bar, club, trekking gear shop, bank, Atm. I feel comfortable like my home.

I've had the best part of 3 weeks here at the Radisson so plenty of time to get a feel for it. I comfortable hotel which is split between gusts from NGO's, business and the constant trekking community.  The hotel is  split between 2 sites just across the road from each other and is a good standard, I stayed in the smaller of the 2, the 3rd floor dinning hall is pretty standard and the 4th floor 'roof top' bar is a good quiet place for breakfast.  I did have an issue with safety, early morning fire alarm, false, thank goodness, but escape route was blocked and not clearly signed. So top tip do your escape plan early on first day and report any issues.  Management were very responsive and I had a meeting with senior management and security to discuss the issues.  Rooms?  standard are well equipped, fee wifi, quiet and comfortable, suites are very nice, p[purpose made and have nice lounge and 2 bath rooms.  You are a 15 min walk from the famous, Thamel road shopping area where walking gear +++ is available.  Accommodation in Nepal tends to be basic but this hotel is of an international standard. You wont experience Nepal in this hotel but you will be very comfortable.
Good place worth visiting once for variety of food options in narrow market lanes... with lot of bargaining

The place is very noisy (turn the music down please!) and service is the worst.

There has been widespread damage caused by the earthquake. Many buildings are either propped up or ruined.There is a lot of restoration taking place, so in a few years time it will be back to its past plendour.

We stayed in the older part which is a bit dated.
Rooms have old furniture but comfy bed.
Tv remote had no off button.  Air con worked well.
Like most hotel rooms, not enough lights.
Our room had a connecting door, which I think was made out of cardboard - could hear everything.
Restaurant was first class.  Plenty of choice.

A beautiful street full of life, restaurant, cafe and pubs!!
Best time to visit is in the evening when tourists and locals mix.
There are many shops to buy local souvenirs.

The roads around Thamel are all mostly narrow, even for pedestrian, so you will have to navigate yourself carefully and take notice of the traffic. That said, there are lots of shops selling all sorts of things from Ayurvedic soaps and singing bowls, to Yak Pashmina scarves and Nepalese cuisines.

We went during the day and then back at night as part of a good tour. It is vibrant and busy despite many structures being under repair following the 2015 earthquake. At night it is calmer as many of the persistent hawkers have stopped. You can appreciate how serene a place it can be. If you are lucky (and we were) you may get to see the Kumari or Living Goddess in Kumari House.

Dusty dirty overpriced and still as vibrant as ever, for an Australian traveller on a budget it expensive (80 Rps to the dollar )safe for solo women travellers. This is a a good place to get vegetarian food right in Thamel, good quality and relaxed environment. Be prepared to remove your shoes...
take you back in time , improve your knowledge very educational , I advice to hire guide only $10 very useful

We dinned at the buffet lunch. As vegetarians we found the selection excellent, with lots of choices for non-veg diners too. The food was fresh, well presented and tasty. Not overly spicy. Service was attentive. Overall good experience.
Stayed at a hotel in this area while on a Gate 1 tour.  Lots of shopping opportunities and lots of restaurant choices.   Enjoyed staying in this area of Kathmandu.

Ambience and hospitality of the hotel and staffs were great. A good business as well family hotel with good spread in buffet breakfast and dinner.Would recommend this hotel for friends and dear. Had a nice experience overall
I like it but not in love with it its a nice place for taking photos and our guide told us lots of thing about this place it was way different then our culture.

Thamel is an acquired taste. It can be busy on season and quiet out of season. They have a little something for everyone. You can obtain cheap tat all the way up to quality goods, clothing and gifts. Do shop around and don’t be afraid of some friendly haggling. 
There are some amazing drinking and food hotspots throughout the City and it’s not all on the first couple of floors. Look up, down and all around as there are little gems to be found everywhere. You can get a little bit of everything here and fun can be had by all the family by getting involved. 
Keep your wits about yourself because although in Nepali Culture there is not a great deal of theft there are street thief’s in this area.
Enjoy your experience, our family had a great time.
amazing views and perfect location to observe fishtail mountain and beauty of lakes(you can see all lakes from viewpoints)
Nice place for visiting thamel city actually this city is popular for international tourist but now a days local people also visit for music food nice accommodation

Though, it is a simple museum, it is a must visit place to gather valuable information with regard to treckkers of all the top mountains in Nepal and other information with regard to different sect of people in Nepal.

I have been 2 time I’m at this beautiful hotel. What I most liked is the feeling of living inside of a temple. It is a place of calming atmosphere middle of Thamel (most central part of Kathmandu). You can walk everywhere and visit all the temples around. Please don’t miss the organic food make every day with love. The staff are reality such a beautiful people. After a few days I felt like home. I felt they take care of me. Thank you for that so much! I definitely will come back soon!

The place is peaceful and beautiful . 
Around the temple you can see all over the Kathmandu valley. It’s also known as monkey temple because it have lots of monkeys and they are beautiful. I always love to visit alone with family, and friends. Some of the temples are destroyed by the earthquake in 2015. The hotel was very accommodating and moved myself and the guests into the newly built wing. The room was very comfortable. I wish to thank personally Mr Harry Kirshner for welcoming me every morning, cleaning the room impeccably and stocking up the teabags and water. The buffet spread provided at the hotel was great - a fantastic selection for both morning breakfast and dinner. Staff as you might have guessed are very welcoming and attentive. I have no negatives about my 5 day stay at the Radisson Kathmandu - would recommend to the solo traveler or those looking to host events.
The atmosphere is nice and one can relax. The food was not bad but tasted better places in thamel. Took the dal bhat. Worth a visit with friends
All kind of things you can find. If you are looking for recovery massage,The zen spa is the best one. Nice restaurant and souvenir shops around

Visited for boat trip quite late in day when light not good, but still enjoyable. One oldish man rowing boat of 6 people,and he certainly earned his tip!

I searched long and hard for accommodation in Kathmandu that leaves the smallest possible carbon footprint on this beautiful city and indeed the planet.

At the same time this is a beautiful building that had been built to faithfully reflect and celebrate Nepalese architecture.

The staff here have been incredibly helpful and professional and I have been made to feel extremely welcome. 

The dinner menu offers plenty of options but I most enjoyed trying traditional Nepalese cuisine. As a vegetarian I had plenty to choose from. The breakfast is very generous too. Enjoyed  the cinnamon yoghurt especially.

I’ve travelled wildly studying eco-tourism so O know what’s genuine and what is just a cynical attempt to exploit tourists trying to do the right thing. 

And I come from a country - New Zealand - that could learn a great deal from places like this. 

Very highly recommended.

The food was great as well as the hospitality of the staff, however the facilities in the hotel were not great. majority of the facilities were closed or under construction or renovation. Location is good

The lanes leading down to it have interesting eateries with truly local food not available in the restaurants on the main Lakeside Road. Vast beautiful lake. Very popular. Boat rides. View of mountains all around

It was a lovely experience because of the ambience, food and of course the views!! Its located on the 2nd Floor offering a great view of Phewa Lake. Seating is indoor as well as outdoor. They offer movie nights too probably twice a week.. A highly recommended restaurant when in Pokhara..
Boating experience was fantastic. Second largest late of Nepal. Island temple, middle of the lake is prime attraction.
The lake is really nice and you can enjoy the mountains and the lake when you hire a boat or go to the temple that is in the middle.

The staff is very nice and helpful.
I have 3 nights stay, nice rooftop view from hotel.
Ranjit the hotel manager always have a good smile and lovely attitude.
I had a good stay at Trekker Home.
Thank you and will come again.

Came here with a friend and shared a pizza, which was only ok without being great. That being said, other people in the restaurant had some good looking curries, so I'd perhaps recommend sticking to those. 
Their fresh mint lemonade was excellent.

Even though many temples were damaged during the earthquake (which is still visible) it is still an impressive sight to visit during your stay in Kathmandu, I had to pay 1000 rupees to enter and if you want you can hire a guide to show you around.

the only place to visit in pokhara is the fewa lake. our guide took us to multiple locations as a city tour, but honestly dont waste your time going to those places. its boring and uninteresting.
go to the lakeside of fewa lake and either take a boat ride (which i didnt do), or sit in one of the numerous cafes beside the lake and enjoy the view or people watch (which i did) with a beer or coffee .. totally worth it.
Very nice environment and delicious breakfast with good serve by Sagar gurung was very friendly and professional. we love to come here again and again

Tourist zone where foreigners gather or better yet maybe herded into.   At some of the bars at night, you do see lots of young Nepalis out enjoying themselves.  I got real tired of all the cycle-rickshaw drivers try to sell me whatever.   It's definitely a place not to get a feel for genuine Nepali hospitality and culture.  It is a place to buy cheap, low quality souvenirs and counterfeit clothing and bags.  I'm not sure if there is an alternative area for foreign tourists in Kathmandu.

in this midst of the modern age , the allure of a classic touch endoures at the OK'd Hotel  which remains an oasis where guests can experience the best of both worlds.  Upon entering , guests are greeted by an ambience that harks back to a more elegant time. Very nice and polite staff  with good service though the  rooms  give you classic touch !!!

I came here as a group of backpackers. Whilst the super basic rooms advertised on the website at $2 looked clean and fine once we got there they would only give us a room for $15/night and it was grim. It felt extremely neglected, mattresses were dirty and the bathroom downstairs was worse than many public conveniences. For a few nights it was fine but having been elsewhere since it was an utter rip off for what we got. Sacred valley inn just down the road is far nicer for the money. The staff were also extremely unhelpful and snobby, I think they only try to be helpful to those in the posher block of rooms. Disappointed!

Room were very clean, all the staff were very supportive & always smiling. Breakfast,Lunch & Dunner had plenty of choices and Desserts excellent.
My breakfast girl Manita made Waffles for me& my wife, man it's something special. she had a magic in her hand. very Good.

Radisson Kathmandu is very conveniently located within the city and a good hotel.  Besides, there staff members are extremely courteous and helpful - Ms Ganga, Keshab, Rishal to name a few - makes this a good choice in Kathmandu.
nice walk along the lake. some good places to stop and get a refreshment and relax for a little bit. beautiful views of the hillside.
Always at its best. Thamel becoming very chaotic and busy all the time. City that runs day and night. Taking a tour and having a walk is always best option either.

Always pleasant staying with temple tree… good hospitality n service.

It was a really nice trip as we visited Temple Tree. The service here was very good and the food was also pretty good. Ayushma guided us very nicely and helped us throughout the trip.

Boating at Phewa Taal would be my favourite experience in Pokhara. At the middle of water in a boat with blowing wind, there was different inner happiness. Everything felt satisfying. You could see the mountain, people paragliding at one side and jungles and trees at the other side. I did try standing at the edge of the boat. Love the place.

Our driver dropped us off at a parking area in Sarangkot before 5am after a drive up steep slopes with hairpin bends. Whilst tempted to climb to the viewpoint at the peak we stopped about halfway anticipating a spectacular sunrise. Unfortunately there was too much haze to see the sunrise, the sun only becoming visible through the haze long after the sun had risen.

Sarangkot is worth a visit for the panoramic views of nearby mountains and valleys, and experiencing rural Nepal, even if the sky was not clear enough for sunrise to penetrate through. I'm not sure if there are seasonal times when there is less haze in the air (our visit was in mid-May). Nevertheless the altitude and period just after dawn was refreshingly cool (bring something warm just in case it is too cool).

As the nickname suggests, there are monkeys everywhere and you should watch your belongings, especially food. It was a 45 minute walk from Thamel through some non-tourist streets which made me feel more in touch with the city. A fair climb up and you can see a nice view of the city. Lots of tourists and vendors trying to sell to tourists made me feel a bit uncomfortable, I don't know if I'd label it a tourist trap, but it's on the way. Admittedly, I'm not much of a temple guy.

The hotel is new and the rooms nice, but it is a ways down a terrible dirt road from town.  We couldn't get a taxi to town for a reasonable price, because they wanted to charge for both ways.  My other complaint is my first morning the farmer next door (50 feet) killed a pig by jabbing a stick in its heart.  The sounds were horrible!  Then they butchered it right there outside my window.  I guess this does not happen every day, but the farmer had a lot more pigs running around.....

The Hotel is a great break away from the dust and noise of Kathmandu with its open design, plenty of natural lighting and beautiful lobby and door designs. The rooms however, leave a lot to be desired. The bathrooms don't have locks for whatever reason, nor do they have bidet sprays which come standard in the SE Asia region. Our key cards worked roughly 40% of the time. 

The food was so shockingly mediocre, we were wondering if the hotel had budgetary constraints. Burnt waffles, leathery bacon, chewy baked goods, dry muffins - it felt like breakfast was served as an afterthought. The hospitality is on par with any similar hotel, but everything else was a letdown.

The room was average and the wifi services was even worse. The food was the worst part and needs great improvement. Other than that the hotel employees was polite and nice. Overall it was a good stay.

Individually none of the temples and palaces made a major impact on me. Collectively - WOW- what a collection of diverse architectural styles, historical periods all in one compact area. Not to be missed.

The room was spotless, modern, and very comfortable. The bed felt like sleeping on a cloud, and the blackout curtains made sure I got a great night’s sleep. The bathroom was spacious with a rainfall shower and luxury toiletries.

The staff were incredibly welcoming and professional. Special thanks to [Staff Member’s Name] at the front desk who went out of their way to help us book tours and gave excellent local restaurant recommendations.

Stayed in centre of the thamel at trekkers home. Everything was great location, staff and price just more then fair. I will definately come back to trekkers home while coming to kathmandu. Thank you trekkers home team
...if there is a clear sky. However, from here you can further drive/walk towards west for exploring interesting villages and upon reaching Pokhara there is a great hanging bridge

It must have been beautiful and still is in a way so you need to go and see it.

The food was tasty whereas the service was excellent by rajnish. Sesame the best place to visit.

I visited on a local holiday and the museum was filled with Nepali families enjoying a day at the museum and having picnics in the sunny park out front :) 

While it might not be as fancy as a museum in Europe or N.Am., there are so many interesting exhibits to explore here! If you're interested in mountain culture/geology/ecology, you could easily spend 2-3 hours wandering around.

If the weather is nice, bring a picnic and take advantage of beautiful outdoor space! The air conditioning is also nice when it's smoking hot out, too ;)

The square is worth to visit, beautiful architecture, express the old part of Katchmandu and the ancient art. But is kind of destroyed after the earthquake. Close by there’s a market, Asan Tole, is a local market and is good to buy a couple things way cheaper than Thamel. Everything you can find there. Just don’t expect too much.

What a great collection of temples. Each with their own story. We highly recommend having a guide and plan on spending a couple hours. What an amazing combination of culture, history and fantastic architecture. 

Many of the temples have experienced earthquake damage so we would suggest mentally preparing for lots of reconstruction among this must see site.

Had a wonderful time being paddled around Fewa Lake and relaxing with friends. Our canoe guide was so helpful and friendly. We would have returned fir another ride if we were staying longer in Pokhara.
Just walk bride the lake a d enjoy the splendid views along the way . We took a boàt for 700 rupees one way to Stupa. So relaxing and satisfying experience for all of us

Thamel is the most touristy place in Nepal. There are shops selling every kind of gift you could think of taking back home. There are restaurants that serve food from many different countries around the world. There are grocery shops that sells almost exclusively imported products for everyone who insists on having their home country's products, but didn't pack it in their bags when they came here. Be aware that you'll pay an arm and a leg for those.

One thing you have to do in this part of town is bargain for almost everything you buy. The shop owners load the prices expecting that there will be some bargaining, so don't be timid. However, don't offer ridiculously low prices. The shop owners also have to make a living. 90% of the products you'll find here will be available in a shop just around the corner anyways, so if they insist on a price higher than you are willing to pay, try somewhere else.

The thing i like most about Thamel is the variety in restaurants. Within a very small area you'll find Nepali, Indian, American, Continental, Chinese, South Korean, Middle Eastern, Thai and many more options. Generally the food here is good, as the competition is tougher than in other parts of the city, so dig in!

For those who stay in Lazimpat or Patan, take the green Sajha Yatayat bus service and tell the bus staff that you want to go to the Garden of Dreams. He'll tell you when to get off, and it's only a few minutes' walk from there. The bus should cost Rs20, compared to a taxi at Rs500-1000.

You cannot leave the area without visiting the monkey temple! I could certainly do with less hustle from the street venders inside the actual premises but hey, it’s their income! Make sure you do get lost at the back of the main temple if you really want to see monkeys! And beware of the 2000 steps coming up from the east side!

I had a great experience, the staff where really great welcoming always. The best part, the morning breakfast on a request they had given the aloo paratha. The staff are top class can I thank you one of your stuff Ms.Nabina she was great at her work. Keep it up. I wish you best of luck

If you have someone who can tell you the history and logic or belief behind, it makes the visit more interesting. But I believe the neighborhood needs improvements and it looks like it is progressing very slow since the earthquake.
Good for waking around and finding good restaurants. So busy and too many bikes and cars with making noise.

This was a great place to wander round and learn about the different people that make up Nepal. Don't go expecting an all singing/all dancing affair... It's not, but it is informative. They also have a fantastic section on mountain photographs as well as the world's greatest climbers. If you have a spare few hours before or after a flight, hail a cab and pop down.
A lovely small museum about the different parts of the Himalayas. They have a very lovely garden at the front. Small fee to get in 400nrs.

A very interesting and historic spot in Kathmandu. Yes you pay 1000 to enter but that goes towards supporting its restoration and there is a lot to see while you’re in there. I’d recommend going for lunch / a coffee at one of the restaurants in the square while you’re there and watching the world go by in this historic setting
The food is very good, the swimming pool very wide. Room are really comfortable very kind staff and efficient service..
