Pity cause location is wonderful.

Had a brilliant time staying in style at the Radisson in Kathmandu. All the staff were so friendly and helpful and always gave the best customer service and always with a smile!! Highly recommend the Radisson in Kathmandu, Nepal. Food was scrumptious as well with various cuisines available.
Lots of touristy shops (some genuinely good) and so-so places to eat, this area is packed with people, cars and motorbikes. Enjoy it for what it is.
One of my favorite thing to do in pokhara. Very relaxing, clam water and a view of the mountains! It was a perfect thing to do after a morning of paragliding!
Beautiful Serene Lake! Wonderful for calm relaxed boating and canoeing. Aarti in Evening is a wonderful experience

Visited on a day tour around the main sights of Kathmandu.  Whilst a bit of a climb up the stairs we found the temple to be interesting as well as enjoying the far reaching views and watching the monkeys (be warned they will try and steal anything from you!)

Would recommend to those visiting Kathmandu for the first time.

One of the finest hotels in Kathmandu. We loved the fitness centre especially the steam room. I entered the sauna area was but jumped out immediately after seeing floating particles including hairs in the water. Our worst experience was the room, which has strong cigarette odour, but we had to live with this problem due to unavailability of another similar room.
Another must to do list in Kathmandu. The ancient architectures are very charming. Plenty of great sculptures adorn the compound.

We booked through booking.com and compared to tripadvisor there is a big gap in review score 4,5 vs booking 8.2. We found the hotel is not really up to 5 stars. The rooms are nice design and feature a well equiped bathroom with amenities. However the cleaning is really lacking, the furniture is dated (and damaged) and the rooms smell is unpleasant. The beds are comfortable. The hotel has a quiet location but if youre unlucky you might have loud drunken indian neighbours... The food was fine, rather spicy as one can expect in  Nepal, not so much western food. Staff was friendly and helpful. Pool looks nice, 10 min walk from the Stupa as well. We used the airport shuttle which is convenient also (9usd/pers). 
For the high price you pay to stay here (one of most expensive in Kathmandu) I would expect a much better value for money. A lot of work to be done to the rooms and the airconditioning system.

on online reservation, i requested a double room, then i learned they booked a single room for me. they said it is xxx usd but they asked %25 more. i called them when i turned back from pokhara but they said for today we have room for you but you need to leave tomorrow. and i went there. then the guy told me that we have cancelled your reservation because some airplanes could not take off because of heavily rain and the passangers turned back. i was shocked. i asked them that only 20 minutes ago you said that you have room and that is why i came here. they denied. they said that they would help me by finding another good hotel for me. i did not want to accept first but then i said ok. they said the price will be same and almost same condition. after i raised my voice they made a small discount. and i went the other hotel. very poor conditions, burned carpets, broken toilets and so on. but only 10 dollars less. they put me in a fool position. f course i did not stay any of these hotels and found another one which is much more clear and half the price. such a big liar and tricker! never go there, never accept anything they request. shame..

The service here is willing and good and the room is a good size. the bathroom was rather tired but plenty of hot water. The hotel is a very short walk from central Thamel but the approach is over an unmade road so if wet all rather muddy. Rather expensive for what you got.
Don't expect much from it. It is very dusty at some streets but you still can make nice shopping, just bargain all over and take dust mask with you, that is mandatory)

Located at the Heart of Thamel Market, Trekkers home is the most ideal and affordable place for backpackers and budget travellers. Rooms are spacious and clean, with all modern amenities, the bar and bistro is a happening get together place as well. Mr. Manager, Saroj Pudasaini will keep you company throughout !
Food is quite good especially for vegetarian but the ambience is a real let down. Not only is not good but frankly smell bad because of the shoes kept inside the dining hall.

My stay at Radisson Hotel Kathmandu was below expectations mainly due to cleanliness issues. The washroom and toilet were not properly cleaned, which made the stay uncomfortable. Basic hygiene and maintenance need much more attention. The staff was polite, but the housekeeping standards definitely need improvement. With better cleaning and regular checks, the overall experience could be much better.

Walking arround and seeing all these shops is good experience, i had some shopping too.
For the record all shops closes by 9 PM

Our driver acted as our guide and we had to be quite stern to deter the many individuals coming up and advising they are the cheapest and best guides. Once aware that they were not wanted, they left us alone and even walked a distance away on our return to the exit. The entrance fee was paid by the guide and therefore cannot comment on whether it is value for money, although judging by the number of visitors it is extremely popular.
If you want to see impressive buildings then these are for you, however for many the sight of props to hold the walls just cannot be ignored. What can clearly be seen is the wonderful woodwork fretwork and the stone buildings around this square. 
There are many, many souvenir shops and we were fortunate not to be pestered by the beggars, although friends of ours had a hard time getting rid of them. As always remember to haggle over the purchase; it is expected and forms part of the enjoyment even though the sums are very small.

I booked this after a long tour of India and Nepal. My tour had pre-arranged hotels, but for my last night I wanted something extra special so I chose Kantipur Temple House.

I was given a beautiful large double room, overlooking the central quad. The room was stunning and so was the hotel.The hotel is designed to look like a temple, hence temple house, but i'm told it's just an aesthetic. If I ever find myself in Kathmandu i'll definitely book this hotel again.

The hotel is trying to be as green as they can - which means no plastic. They have large fancy metal water containers in the room with drinking water in, and metal cups to drink from. I thought this was a fantastic idea - although i'd really like the water in a glass as there was a slight metallic taste to the water.

The shower had hot water and good pressure - I really appreciated that after staying at 10 other hotels in India and Nepal with cold or non-functioning showers.

The staff were super helpful - I had a mixup of an everest tour flight and needed to check out later in the day, they were very understanding and let me check out later. They also requested a transfer from the hotel to the airport for a set price [much cheaper than I could have haggled myself]

The first thing you notice when you reach the boating yard is the stinks of dead fish.
The refreshments centre at the middle of the lake is reachable by boat and stocks refreshments.
The boats are colourful and stand out in the photos.
The side walk and viewing decks are well planned and need better maintenance.
Paddle Boats are available for hire. 
You can also hire a boat with an oarsman for a Joy ride.

The lake is the centre of entertainment for families with kids.

The place is relatively hawkers free.

With proper maintenance, the lake bund could be the centre of activities for holiday making families.

Worth a visit and a boat ride.

Very nice hotel, excellent services, reasonable price. I’ve chosen this hotel for its beautiful, traditional Nepalese architecture. The services were a pleasant surprise and added to the value of the hotel.

Lobby may look nice but not a true 5 star hotel. Constantly missing stuff from my room I had to keep asking for (towels, soap, laundry bag, etc), bathroom wasnâ??t well cleaned. And aside from the lobby, rooms are outdated. Also ate the buffet restaurant for dinner and myself and 2 other people from my reservation had severe food poisoning. Youâ??d think eating food from a name such as Hyatt who claimed to be 5 star, would be safe for consumption.

Not sure why some reviewers like this, but the area is very crowded with locals just passing through to get to the other side of the square. But us foreigners have to pay. It is still is great disrepair from the earthquake a few years ago. Almost nothing was open to go inside.
the faculty is very cooperative and friendly, the pool is spectacular, and the food here is also good. Highly recommended.

The place is historic and therefore interesting to see but the 2015 earthquake left it devastated; some buildings tore down, many others seriously damaged. A fee of 1000 rps is charged to the foreign visitors, which is supposed to be for the re-building of the site (wish that it is the case). If you pay the fee you must know that it is for one-day visit only but you can extend it for free to the whole length of your visa just making some paperwork in a hidden place next to the Kumari house. Passport and an ID picture required.

Our wake up call at Temple Tree resort in Pokhara was at 4.45am and the journey was fairly tortuous but it was so worth it. Once we arrived we had to scale a series of fairly uneven steps ( not easy with a dodgy hip and neuropathy!) with no handrail, but, thanks to our very helpful guide, we made it to a rooftop which afforded us a great view.
It was fairly crowded but everyone made sure that all those there were able to get a good view and take their photographs
I understand that the weather is not always kind, but we were very lucky and there were clear views of the mountains of the Annapurna range and we have some great photographs

This is unique and big. 
However, the name international raise Ones expectation. This is in a vast area. There are a few attraction outside the building which can be acceded without ticket. Inside is the main museum. There are mannequins of tribes, historical photographs and good stuff. Some of these are educational as well for all age group. 
However, it can be improved. 
Nonetheless, as a tourist must stop by place. Please keep sufficient free time of atleast 2 hours. 
If you have interest in mountains, keep half day free.
Busy historic site with a lot of activity. Small entry fee for foreigners (1000 NPR) Lots of offers of guides and in hindsite we should maybe have got one to give us some of the detail and history.

There are only a few good things to go and visit in pokhara and the mountain museum is apparently on the list. It cost about Rs400 to get there by taxi and then Rs400 p/p entry fee. We spent about 3 hours there. If you are stuck for things to do it was interesting enough to visit.

Found the people to be very friendly most of them speaking some English which is great since I could not speak Nepali. The hotel was more than accommodating and a good value enjoyed walking the streets and visiting the shops friendly restaurants oh, just be sure to drink bottled water not from the water system.and once you did business with someone or met them they did not forget you when they saw you. This is an area of the city that you can walk-in easilyand find most things that you're looking for but it's also close to many of the temples and areas to visit. Felt very safe walking the streets.

I stayed at the Kathmandu Radisson Hotel for the first time. The stay was generally good, although their internet is too weak to do a stable Whatsapp call. Buffet breakfast was good. Buffet dinner was cold one night due to a problem with food warmers, but the kitchen kindly reheated the food for us. Noisy guests arrived on my last night and talked loudly all night, turned up TV so loudly I could hear every word, but I told reception and they called them and turned it down. Very nice staff, although door staff are clearly more respectful/nicer to white European/American tourists, than black Africans so they need some training to treat all guests equally.

Very busy but you can find tranquil little pockets of space in the gardens, still being restored in some places. Lovely museum. We were taken round by our guide. Lots of shade available in the very hot weather. Lots to see and read up about. Well worth a visit. The markets and Buddha shops outside are worth visiting too.
A mountain buff's paradise.  Fabulous setting, many unique items, pictures, stories.  One could spend many hours taking in all the details.  Awesome history revealed.

was a good place to visit and impressive site.  Quite busy as expected. Nice to see the monkeys and dogs living in relative harmony, bar a couple of squables. As with all religions still a couple of people trying to get the dogs away from their blessings who need to remember the buddhist philosophy of all beings! but generally a good atmosphere.

Swayambhunath is something everyone must visit while at Kathmandu. The city view from the top is mesmerizing. This place carries equal significance for Buddhism and Hindus. As it's one of the major heritage site listed in UNESCO it's an important destination.

Visiting the international mountaineering museum was a great learning experience for my inquisitive 8 yr old son. The venue is located a bit off from the main Pokhara Fewa Lakeside, but its worth the trip.

My secondary motivation to go to this museum was the 25m artificial climbing wall in the parking lot. Unfortunately, it was not scheduled to be operational for another 3 months.

The museum offers a large variety of information and exhibits, however the exhibits could be modernized to engage younger audience.

My family and I enjoyed the visit and benefitted from the information offered. Highly recommended for a couple of hours visit if you are looking for a casual stroll and some knowledge gathering.

Love the open environment and the displayed materials. Its a lot of history in one place. Be prepared to spend half a day at this place. 
You can go around the museum compound to explore wall climbing structure and mountains structure.
With the free WiFi and QR code it was helpful to get sufficient information.
Good place for students and trekkers.
Restaurant nearby served well too.

Very good hotel ,center of thamel ,staff are friendly  and hotel manager Mr.saroj very nice rooms are clean and perfect  balcony  rooms Asom hot shower  ,rooftop garden was very nice see the monkey temple 😀

A beautifully designed resort with small cottages with a perfect location between the Feva lake and the Crystal mountain.

The review could win more stars had there been hot water availability for 24 hours, and also a check on sound pollution at the resort due to the loud music from neighboring properties. Also a big Japanese group at the resort was permitted to perform loud group recitations in the common facilities was a breach of tranquility and peace for other guests.

The pool is lovely and the rooms are nice but the front desk service is pretty poor. We had to wait 45 minutes to check into our rooms as they were not ready (this would have been longer if I hadn’t pushed for it). They also tried to charge me extra (even though I had settled in full) previously due to a currency exchange issue. I declined reminding them about the late check in but thought that this was very unprofessional. Dead ants also littered the balcony.

It was a wonderful experience staying at Radisson Kathmandu. The property is great and the staff is extremely kind and helpful. The staff when out of their way to help us in a crisis situation. They also help me arrange a quick birthday celebration for my partner. Great place and great people !
after climbing a lot of stairs you have to pay entry. Lot of monkeys around so don´t have food or drinks in your hand
This place is best for paragliding. I did paragliding the week before the lockdown . It was the best experience ever

Please do NOT stay at this hotel. Despite the other reviews posted on this site, when you get to the hotel it might be nice to look at but you get max 3 hours of electricity and heat per day... and none of the rumoured hot water either! When its winter, that means you are FREEZING your back side off in the dark. Not a very good way to relax and take in the sites. What a rip off. For $50 one would expect much, much more. The owner must be off in warmer climes just raking in the dough from poor suckers like me.

Durbar Square in Kathmandu is under reconstruction from the 2015 earthquake.  It was interesting but I can not recommend it as it presently exists.  I would highly recommend that you go and spend extra time not spent going to Kathmandu Durbar Square at Bhaktapur or Patan's Durbar Squares.  My personal favorite, after two trips, is Patan's Durbar Square.

I have no doubt that when reconstruction is completed, Kathmandu's Durbar Square will be well worth the visit and time. I suspect that it will not be for at least 2 more years.  Right now many of the structures are surrounded by scaffolding and dust-control tarps.  It is interesting for people watching but you can do that just as well in Bhaktapur or Patan in addition to better temple/shrine/building viewing.  Should you visit the one in Kathmandu?  As we often say in Thailand up2u.  I plan on returning to Kathmandu in the Spring.  I will return to Patan, and Bhaktapur's Durban Squares but no Durbar Square in Kathmandu.
In the earthquake of 2015 many temples got damaged. Now with Chinese help they are now got renovated

The contemporary museum building and well maintained grounds are beautiful.  We took our picture on a cool mountain replica on the grounds. The exhibit is very interesting if you want to know about trekking and explorers who summited some of the highest peaks in the world.  I only gave 4 stars because the exhibits seem dated and a little dull.  Tons of interesting facts and pictures though.  Worth the $5 entry fee. Takes less than an your to see everything.

It's about 1/3 still standing, 1/3 under major repair, and 1/3 flattened and gone forever.  The entrance fee has approx trebled in the last 3 years and now stands at a hefty NPR1000 for Westerners, even though there is less to see - you just have to take the view that it's your personal contribution towards post-earthquake restoration work!  The Kumari temple house is one of the best remaining buildings that you can visit & if you are lucky, the Kumari (child living goddess) will make a brief appearance.
Very good and high quality standard and also good and coperative staff Anu and supriya is the best one...hotel pool and jaccuzi is excellent experience....i m so happy

The food is excellent but the service leaves a lot to be desired. The waiter looked as if he'd rather do anything than serve us and didn't crack a smile the whole time we were there - tall, thin young guy. Views over the lake are amazing on a fine day.
A great little streets full of nice small boutique style shops. Lots of restaurants to cater for all. Recommend you haggle when buying gifts. Nepali people are great.
Interesting drive. Good views of mountains and hanggliders, but go early, before the haze hides the mountains. A bit touristy, so preferred Naldanda.

Budget friendly hotel in the middle of the thamel. Hotel have very nice restaurant in first floor. Highly Recommend for budget friendly hotel in the centre of thamel. Hot water, staff and location with budget price room is top notch  part of the hotel.
Need to take a cab or cycle or pony to reach there. Paragliding and sun rise point are the main features. Beautiful views you get,however, the timing and whether place a role.

The overall food experience was very good, and the beetroot naan prepared by Chef Padam Sitoli was truly excellent. And Excellent management by Subendu Roy and the team.
The overall management, waiter service, and buffet variety provided a very fine dining experience—absolutely loved it, and it was a truly wonderful experience for me.

The Fewa lake is perfect for a nice day out. 
Rent a bike somewhere cheap in Pokhara. Don’t pay more than 200 roepies and buy some bottles of alcohol and ride around the lake till you find a quiet spot to have some chill out time! Recommended! 
The only reason why it didn’t got a 5 star review is that the lake is little bit polluted.
Beautiful quite lake. Nice canoe ride. There is a temple on the lake as well. There is even some wildlife like birds, monkeys and we even got to see two owls.
Best hotel in Pokhara with the besrt hospitality Nepal has to offer. They accommodated special meals for kids and were very welcoming

Friendly staff good breakfast special tanks to @ Sabina..Santa.Alishwa.Parmila.Salina for taking care 
We will visit again
We had a nce boatride on the lake to the temple on a small island in the lake. Lots of tourists, nevetheless nice. When the wather is good you have a beuatiful view on the Anapurna from the island.

Wonderful hotel! We were traveling in Bhutan and Nepal and stayed at the Hyatt Regency KTM on 3 separate nights. The check-in experience was seamless and the lobby area is lovely. As a Hyatt member with status, we were able to enjoy canapes and drinks in the lounge each evening which was relaxing and offered a variety a food. The buffet breakfast was a lovely surprise in the mornings. So many choices and the staff was so efficient and checked on us frequently. Our last morning, we had a very early flight and they offered to pack us a breakfast to go!

A special shout out to Jhapad who was working in the lounge one evening and then at breakfast the next morning. He was so nice and works so hard. Srishti from guest experience checked on us one night to be sure everything was going well also. I didn't catch the names of the front desk staff that were there at check in and check out but they were all so nice.

Stay here if you are in Katmandu. You won't be disappointed!

Aha, this is the place to be when thinking about central Kathmandu. This is the place of nightlife, food, music and having a good time. The area what we covered started from Garden of Dreams, going past the Tridevi Mandir and then going across a few shops than then taking a left towards New Market. This is long road, which has the usual restaurants, and small hotels and comes into the busy part of the city daily need stores selling pulses, housewares and so forth.
The next day, we started our Thamel tour from the opposite side towards Chaya Center mall and moved inside the small by-lanes and came across the Ramada Wyndham hotel - tucked away inside a residential area and the nightlife just picked up with lots of restaurants, music and people enjoying. This side looked better than the New market area. We did catch a movie at the Chaya Center mall at the QFX Theatre - ensure you keep Nepali rupee else the counter does not accept any other cash. Else use your credit card.
We walked quiet a lot and it got dark when returning, but there is adequate street lighting and I sawy Tourist Police ensuring the safety.

I would happily say that the Kantipur Temple House was one of my favourite hotels I have ever stayed in. The staff were amazingly accomodating and generous even after I completed my stay. The location is perfect, the architecture is breathtaking and food also very nice. I hope you will enjoy your stay as much as I did. 
Oh and for bonus points they are a sustainably focused hotel. Winning!!

There are different kinds of boats available on the lake at about two points along the edge. The rates for hiring different boats (with and without a boatman) are fixed by the local association. If there are only two or three of you it would make sense to hire a small rowboat and a boatman to take you around: unless you want to spend the day reading a book or lazing around in the boat in a peaceful surrounding. The rowboats are somewhat small and can capsize if you are not careful. If there are more of you to push a peddle/ paddle boat then you can opt for that as well. This is a much safer. Life jackets are available on hire and should be taken. A peddle-boat can be hard work, but it gives you the freedom of being on your own. 

There is an interesting eating place and hotel called The Lake Side (NOT the one called Hotel Lake Side) on the opposite side of the lake to which access is by boat. The location is peaceful but the food is just passable. They have a few rooms to let out as well. It is a nice serene place to spend some time away from the bustle of Pokhara town if you dont mind managing with beer and some basic snacks of average quality.
Lots of hotels, restaurants,  shops and tourists ; all gather together at thamel. Even have a cinema hall, and dances bar

It is roadside market winding streets, All full of Pashminas, Yak skin products, daggers, handicrafts. But One has to be expert to find out real Pashmina. Mostly is either fake or mixed with other materials. Price range from US$ 5-300 so hard to tell. Not very clean except for one or two streets. Narrow and traffic congested with motorcycles, taxis and other kinds of vehicles. Hard to navigate peacefullu but unfortunately only option for Souvenirs.

We were rarely able to eat baba ganesh & another mediterrenian item that we ordered. The taste was not good at all. Though the atmosphere was great but the food was not up to the mark. The price was also quite high considering vegetarian item.

I spent 9 days staying in this hotel. Comfortable room, friendly staffs and owner. Affordable price and the location is easy to find. Wanna come back someday.

Thank you for the hospitality. Keep going!

Located on first floor, sit on the floor setting, hippy n laid back, good ambience. This place serves only vegetarian food. We had salad, falafel (this was good!) and hummus. Good to chat and have wines with friends here. One of good dining experience in Kathmandu.
The entry fee has gone up. Two temples are still just a pile of bricks, others got scaffolding but not much seems to be happening. Still worth a visit. Just be prepared.
I'd say it was a fun quiet hike to get up there. The destination itself was a tad underwhelming but it was cool to see the paragliders flying next to you.

The staff were always very helpful very friendly and went the extra mile to make my stay very comfortable specially because I am a vegan and I do not eat onion and garlic so they make sure that I was being given meals specially prepared according to that specially mentioned to uma pawan bishal and krishna and the vivek were excellent and ever so friendly and the hotel very clean very high standard and housekeeping service was excellent and will become this hotel and hope to come back won't forget the kindness of pawan bishal krishna and uma specially thank you

Location is great, in the centre of Thamel, but without all the street noises. I booked a basic room but for the high price I paid, 1500 npr, I expected a lot more. A double bed and a bureau where cramped inside a tiny room. Also there was no socket in the room. I guess the more expensive but better rooms make it worth staying in here. Otherwise, if you're looking for a cheap room, look for somewhere else. 
Also, if you would like to take a taxi to the airport don't use the ones provided by the guest house. A ride to the airport costs 800 rupees but if you take an ordinary taxi in Thamel it brings you there for 300-350 rupees.

The Phawe lake side is very relaxing and walking around is very worthy to watch on the nature and activities.
The people are quite calmed down and more welcoming than Katmandu.

Kantipur Temple House was an oasis in the middle of bustling Thamel. Not only were the rooms and garden a quiet and tranquil respite from the hectic streets outside, the hospitality, friendliness, and overall knowledge of the staff was the best we experienced in Nepal. The breakfast offered a diverse selection and the chefs also offered to cook eggs or prepare special Nepalese breads. The restaurant also offers a delicious mix of local cuisine as well as Thai, Indian, Chinese, etc. options. But the most memorable part of our visit will definitely be the warmth and kindness with which we were received by everyone who works there.
Apparently Saturday is a public holiday and the place was swamped with people.  Interesting place to go if you have never been to one.

A pleasant place to spend some time on in a boat, stopping at the Tai Barahi Temple island, or just sitting or strolling the promenade when it's cooler. The water might look refreshing but its not particularly clean and I wouldn't recommend swimming in it.
Very good place for accommodation and food. Thamel is a popular touristic hub in nepal. Must visit place in nepal

This area is well set up for the traveler. 

Places to eat, travel agents, accomodation and shopping all in one spot. 

Please note there isn’t any foot paths as you are navigating yourself around scooters and some cars too.

Getting prepared very early in the morning for the Sarangkot view point journey. We started at 4:30AM and reached Sarangkot at 5:10AM, still one hour ahead of sunrise. You have to climb around 20 floors of stairs at 1700 meters height to reach the top viewpoint of Sarangkot. The view of Fishtail range is awesome from the top.
it is nice to climbing many steps.Holly place for Budhists and we see from there beautiful kathmandu vally.
This is the place to be. Food is incredibly delicious and the menu is most unique. The design and atmosphere is number one in Nepal.

Another must do activity when in Pokhara. Fewa Lake is truly beautiful and as one rows into the center of the lake, the Himalayas comes into view.  Just breath-taking.

The lake is calm and the water clean as no motor boats are allowed in this lake, keeping pollution at bay.

Comfortable rooms, good location. Good facilities. Down side street off main road. Good 
restaurants nearby. Range of rooms to choose from standard to suites. Quite location with good parking facilities
It is a must to visitI think and if you like cultural sightseeing. Lots of decorated buildings. Bring a mask. Lots if dust here. I recommended.

Tons of information and worth the entrance fee. I really hope that money goes to updating the facility. 
The walk there is also informative.
Unfortunately, it was very cloudy and good see the mountains and Mt. Fish Tail at Sunrise. The view point is beautiful. Provides 360 degrees view.
Best place in Kathmandu for souvenir shopping. Almost all the shops have the same products, so you can buy where the energy takes you and umyou should be ok! Very safe!

This is the famous launch for paragliding. A wonderful place to watch the take off and get a great view of Pokhara and the lake. It costs 50 rupees to enter, so be prepared for that. If you are adventurous, rent a scooter and drive up. The road is in  very poor condition. So it resembles a dirt bike track.

I was brave and tried going here via mountain bike. I  had to walk big sections due to the sheer incline. Bit well with the visit. The walking caused me to stop along the way and thus I saw much more I recon. But should I visit again I will opt for a taxi!

I stayed at Katmandú Guest House 2 nights before trekking, and 3 nights after trekking. I had a standard room, in the Southern Wing. The room was small , but comfortable. The bath room was old and very small. It smelled very bad. It's not a bathbroom for a 4 stars hotel!!!!!
Very small and old TV!!!.
The buffet breakfast was ok.
The situation, very good.
The Garden Dreams, very nice.

It's not a 4 stars hotel. For me it's just a 2 stars hotel.
As a travel agent, I can't recommend Katmandú Guest House to my custems, if they book a standard room.
Last year I stayed at the East Wing and the rooms were complete differents. All rooms were new and with a correspondance at 4 stars hotel.

Resort is nice with good location. Staffs are not well trained. We were not provided room with good view, infact our reservation was missed which we did 2 weeks back from Goibibo. Front desk almost took half an hour to provide us a room ( with backside view of cows grazing). This is unexpected from 4 star resort.

We stayed here between treks, the staff were friendly, polite and helpful while the wifi was faster than we expected.  The location was excellent as the trekking shops were all nearby and the onsite restaurant had a good selection and friendly staff.

Nice quiet setting a few steps away from busy Thamel. Red brick building gives a nice atmosphere that is also reflected in the room and courtyard. The room is spacious and comfortable against local standards. Do not expect full international standards though: the bathroom is very simple, cleanliness is a sligthtly relative concept. Breakfast is varied and (as all meals) can be had indoors, in the courtyard,  and rooftop. I would advise courtyard for an evening meal as a nice setting although the price / quality ratio does not meet other options in the area. 
The main issue was that I soon discovered that I could find (and did use) similar standard hotels for about a third of the price (in my case, namely the International Guest House).
The veiw of kathmandu city from the top of Swoyambu is amazing. You can see lot ot monkeys around. I enjoyed the evening ambience of Swoyambu. The place is very cool and serene.

We were disappointed by the lack of selection for shopping in this area.  Perhaps we didn’t venture far enough or to the best streets.  The roads are very busy in this part of the city, specifically, so be very aware when walking near the streets.

With a quaint atmosphere and low seating this place is a nice restaurant to have a nice relaxing slow-paced vegetarian meal. The hummus is great, and a large appetizer could fill you up just as much as a meal. There are so many delicious food choices you might end up here more than once.

The place has such a great vibe and such beautiful historical buildings that one can just stand in awe and adore them. The gaddi baithak and the temples in the durbar square courtyard are just stunning. The architecture is very different and unique. You can walk to.indra Chowk and shop for artificial jewellery and have the famous sweet lassi at Indra chowk. Just ask anyone , anyone and everyone knows this lassi shop. Your trip to Kathmandu is incomplete without a trip to durbar square.

I had a wonderful experience at Kantipur Temple House!

Rooms and ambiance: The rooms are old-school and the property is "eco-friendly" so there's no AC or no water bottles. Water is served in antique brass jugs and glasses and refilled on request. Fewa Lake, located in the heart of Pokhara, Nepal, is a stunning natural gem and a must-visit destination. Surrounded by lush green hills and the majestic Annapurna mountain range, the lake offers breathtaking views that are both serene and mesmerizing.

The tranquil waters of Fewa Lake provide the perfect setting for boating. Renting a colorful wooden boat or paddleboat and gliding across the calm surface is an experience like no other. The highlight is a visit to the Tal Barahi Temple, a small yet significant shrine located on an island in the middle of the lake.

Early mornings at Fewa Lake are magical, with the reflection of the snow-capped peaks, including Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), shimmering on the water's surface. It's also a hub for photographers and nature lovers who come to capture its beauty.

The lakeside area is lively, offering a variety of restaurants, cafes, and shops where you can relax and enjoy the view. Whether you're looking for adventure or peace, Fewa Lake is a perfect retreat for everyone.

My family and I stayed at this hotel for about two weeks in February 2019. The traditional Nepalese architecture of this hotel provides you with an ambiance you cannot find in any other hotel in Nepal. The staff at this hotel were courteous, genuine, helpful, and friendly and went above and beyond including the gentlemen at the entrance of the hotel, front office, restaurant, and housekeeping staff. The Nepalese hospitality was quite evident through and through. The staff were all dressed in traditional Nepalese wear and it was a nice touch to see the Nepali customs and culture being kept alive. The location of the hotel was excellent and within walking distance from the Royal Palace/King’s Way/Thamel etc. 

We stayed in a suite as well as a regular room during our stay and both were fantastic. I was afraid of being cold in Kathmandu’s February weather but we had electric blankets in the room and hot water bags were placed in our bed nightly during turn down service. We had such a comfortable stay. We never had any issues with hot water. I appreciated the attention to details in the room especially the environmentally friendly elements such as reusing of towels, eco-friendly lighting in the room, water vessel (called “karuwa” in Nepali) and glasses that were provided for drinking water and to discourage the use of water bottles. I was so glad that the rooms did not have a television because it really allowed you to disconnect and just reflect on your day. The Wi-Fi in the rooms were excellent – I was surprised at how fast and great the connection was. 

I cannot even begin with the food at the restaurant. We had a chance to meet with the owner, Bharat Basnet, and have conversations with him about the vision of the hotel. The food at the restaurant is locally sourced and organic. We ate breakfast at the hotel almost every day and they served continental as well as a Nepali breakfast. The papaya juice was delicious and the herbal tea and espresso they serve at the restaurant are the best. We very frequently ate lunch and dinner at the hotel as well. I have had tons of momos everywhere but I would vote the momos at this restaurant as THE BEST. You ABSOLUTELY cannot go wrong with anything that you order at the restaurant. No matter how much food we tried in the Kathmandu valley we kept coming back to the hotel food not for the convenience of the food but the taste and quality of the food. 

The owner even personally arranged a ride for us to the airport given we had tons of suitcases. This is my favorite hotel in Kathmandu and I would recommend you book this hotel without any hesitation. You will not be disappointed and I am sure the staff would work anything out should there be any issues. THANK YOU THANK YOU THANK YOU to the owner and each and every staff that made our stay at this hotel so pleasant without any hiccups. This hotel felt like home.

Thamel is the crazy,touristy part of Kathmandu. There are many hotels, hostels and guesthouses located here and it is noisy and hot and the pollution hangs in the air. It is crowded with tourists and many locals trying to sell you anything and everything. This is where you buy your not quite authentic outdoor stuff before you head for the mountains. Haggle for everything and have some fun. Parts of the main shopping area are supposed to be pedestrianised but keep your eyes open for motorcycles. Located less than 500m from this chaos is The Garden of Dreams, a tranquil oasis in the heart of mayhem. Only 400 rupees to get in from 9am, get a brochure from the ticket office. Created in the 1920s as a private garden by a Nepalise Field Marshall, it has had a sad chequered life of love and neglect. Currently only half it's original size, it is still a wonderful place to visit. I'm not a botanist but this is not Kew Gardens, the planting is simple and rustic but it works well with the architecture and design. There is a café and a great little photographic history in one of the buildings opposite the main entrance. In summary, the garden is well worth a visit for a little peace and quiet during your time in Kathmandu.

Also insisted that the TIMS office was only open until midday and that we needed to take a hotel car there straight away (we didn't, the office was open until the afternoon). We stayed here for four nights following a three-week tour of India and Nepal. We were looking for somewhere to relax, reflect on our travels, and as a base to explore Kathmandu; we chose well. The staff here are wonderful; they are friendly and helpful, and essentially, nothing is a problem. They helped us arrange taxis, printing documents, luggage, and other requests. The room was comfortable, allowing us to relax and sleep. It was quiet and calming - exactly what we needed. Our breakfast experience was first-rate. There were numerous options, and everything we tried was tasty and well-presented. Additionally, we had lovely chats with the staff in the restaurant, and they suggested some items for us to try. The location suited us well: off the main street, it was quiet, but we could also walk to Durbar Square in about 30 minutes, which we did several times. There is a small road leading up to the hotel with some very decent shops and eateries. We bought some bags in the leather shop, and I got three exceptional custom-made shirts from the tailors. We had lunch in the Blue Note cafe twice and ate in the Namanta Kitchen Restaurant three times - it was that good. We recommend staying here, and we would stay here again if we return to Kathmandu (hopefully will).

Swayambhunath called the ‘Monkey Temple’
It’s all to do with a group of monkeys that have lived in the northwest part of the Swayambhunath temple complex for generations.
A legend says that they came into being when the Buddhist ‘deity’ Manjushri spent time on the hill that the temples are set on. He was meant to cut his hair short but instead he let it grow long and got head lice. These lice then turned into the monkeys.
You’ll encounter playful monkeys around the complex be cautious with food or loose items Two access points to the temple, from the bottom of the hill a staircase of around 300 steps or be dropped off in the parking lot facing the main entrance at the top of the hill
There are some small shops around the base and top where you can buy souvenirs, religious items, or have a cup of tea, Best to visit early in the morning

Our room was well sized.  Plenty of cupboard space and a small balcony, but no sofa.  Bathroom was good - very clean.  WiFi was free and worked fine.  The bed was very firm, but after speaking to the front desk, they put a doona under the sheet to give a little softness,  Not perfect, but we managed a good night's sleep. 

The pool area was very popular - unfortunately a little close to our room.  Just noisy in the day - no problem at night.

Hot water was only available in the mornings and evenings, but it caused us no inconvenience.  Neither did the frequent, short, power outages.  Seems a feature of Nepal.

Breakfast was the usual buffet - perfectly OK, but very standard.  We also had lunch in the restaurant/bar area. The food was good and quite reasonably priced.

Checking around, it seems that Pokhara is mostly 3 star and below hotels, designed more for trekkers than for resort stays.  On that basis, the Temple Tree was fine.
This is a place where you can buy your trekking things, art and craft bags, Gurkhas Knives, coffee and meals.

The hotel grounds are quite nice.  There is a garden, a beautiful pool (unheated and unusable in February), as well as outdoor dining and bar.  I ate breakfast in the restaurant, which was good, but not great.  The staff members were wonderful--attentive, helpful, and eager to make sure all was well with my stay.  It is close to the lake, but off the (noisy) main road.  

A couple detractors--the wi-fi is inconsistent and kept logging me out.  I had to clear my cache every time I tried to log back in, or it wouldn't work (on a Mac).  Sometimes I had to go sit in the garden to get a strong enough signal.  The power goes out periodically (such is the case in Nepal) and hot water is available only part of the day.  

I didn't find the bed very comfortable, and the room had lots of signs of wear.  I felt the hotel grounds were a lot more appealing than the room itself.  Further, there was construction going on in another part of the resort, which was quite noisy and started at 7 am.

This is a great place if you are a "modern hippie" as it is a meeting place with floor seating and people next to you putting their bare feet within inches of your food.  We were a table of 6 and each dish came out by itself followed by the next dish for the next person 15 minutes later.  So it took 45 minutes for all of our 6 dishes to come out.  Waiter was non-interactive and unresponsive but hey, he gets his tip anyway as it is imposed!  Food however was pretty good by Kathmandu standards

We visited late in the evening and were told kitchen was still open but were taking last orders. First plate of food arrived with the bill with the expectation to pay it then even though we were waiting on more food/drinks. Waiters were rushing cleaning up and clearing tables around us. By the time our second plate of food and cocktails came we felt we were being ushered to the door without having time to enjoy (staff left but we were allowed to stay back with security guard if we wanted....) Didn't get to drink one of the expensive cocktails and left half the food.

In the afternoon during the weekend, it tends to be crowdy with locals/ tourists boat riding to the temple on the island, but it was interesting to see.  We wished we had more time in Pokhara.
