It's another durbar square in kathmandu with ancient buildings. If u have seen bhaktapur then this is a smaller version. It's next to the main mkt naya bazaar and easy to reach. Not many good places to eat atound.

Discover the beautiful Lakes Phewa Begnas and, Rupa during winter season and admire the impressive snowy Alps that surround it with a panoramic lake cruise. Enjoy a walking tour around lake side with religious flavor.

Lake Phewa, in Nepal’s beautiful Lake in Kaski District, is just a short distance from Capital City kathmandu. Nestled between the huge snow capped Alps that rise up from its shores is the fashionable lakeside town of Pokhara.

Enjoy a guided tour of the town, plenty of free time for night sightseeing, a panoramic cruise across the lake, and a breathtaking view of the lake from Lake side Pokhara.

Will take at least 90 minutes to view the museum. Beautiful collection of Asiatic mountains and non Asiatic mountains. At length description photographs and images of how Himalayan ranges evolved to what lies in future. Excellent collection of fauna and Flora. Special section on global warming and projects taken to prevent it. Nice Gurkha land. Recreation of mountain outside museum. Restaurant. Pokhara 50 years back and today. Nice video on mountains and Nepal every hourly in a mini thater.

Had a very good stay and enjoyed the hospitality. However one meeting hall had a lot of noise from the kitchen behind the hall disturbing the conference and the other hall was full of flies as they had frequent dinner parties. 
Else a very good hotel , good amenities and good rooms and very friendly staff members

Family stay at this hotel we felt safe and easy to go around thamel.Felt safe and budget friendly at this hotel.Will keep recommending to my friends and family who visit thamel.Lod bar was not far and restaurants are very close.Roof top bar was good to visit for nice view.
Went for a sunrise tour which was highly recommended. However the weather decided to play spoilsport. At the end the most memorable moment was the drive and the tea at the restaurant at the top

Phewa Talk is by far the main attraction in Pokhara, it's relaxed flat surface and clear water offer a pleasant escape for anyone on vacation or perhaps just a spot to relax by after a trek. Phewa seems extremely clean as it's clear although if you walk around it you can find coves flowing into the lake that are best described as junk yards and trash heaps so I would definitely not swim in the lake or eat anything from it or irrigated by it.

It's a large, very deep lake, supposed to have a Loch-Ness-Type monster lurking in the depths. Pretty tourist these days. I lived in Pokhara in the early 1970s and the whole area was mud and thatch farmhouses, fields and dirt lanes. At that time only the Fewa Hotel was lakeside. Today it is overly developed for the number of tourists who visit.
Truly its a Nature's paradise. Lake, Snow capped Mountain and Greenery all these at one place, what else one require from a tourist spot. Boat ride is excellent.
The staffs are very polite the food is very good the ambience is so nice the jacuzzi and swimming pool looked so good but couldn't do it because of work

this museum is most interesting covering a wide range of topics. Different cultures, many mountain expeditions etc. There is also a shocking display of rubbish collected from Everest mostly left behind by expeditions.

I would recommend a guide. I went around by myself and missed a lot of it because i was being harrassed by guides, merchant's and beggers. Every 5 steps it was something new. I ended up leaving after 30 minutes and returning with a guide a few days later. A lot of construction still happening.

The room was clean ,comfortable  beds ,.
¹hot showers  was .perfect and location, reasonable priced,and  friendship  staff ,hotel manager mr.saroj friendly with good , rooftop views  was perfect 👌..
definitely  i will recommend  this place.

I met with an old friend and enjoyed dinner and a couple of beers. After i paid we finished the last glass and waited for the change to come back only to be told that the waiter already went home and the cashier was already close. So I never got my change. Terrible service.
After the big disaster in kathmandu durbar square around are very well maintained and good historic buildings still rebuil.
The museum provides information on various aspects of mountaineering and the history of mountaineering in the Himalayas

Pros: Good bit of luxury in the middle of Thamel. Nice staff. Nice lawns/property.

Cons: The wifi was slow to non-functional my first night and was completely out my second night. Really sucks to be cut off like that when in a 'luxury' environment. Breakfast was included and varied, but everything tasted rather bland and unimpressive. Construction is ongoing. All work is percussive construction, just the banging of hammers against other things.

In the end I wouldn't recommend this place for $52/night.

I visited Fewa lake early evening. I had a nice kayak visit but it was not something unforgettable. It was also a little bit cloudy and there was no mountain view. The visit to the small lake island worths only if you want to see locals to pray in a Hindu temple.

I had such an amazing peacefull experience on this lake. i went early 7h30/8h, and i could rent a boat for 1050npr (instead of 1500) for an unlimited amount of time. I spent the whole morning in a remote place of the lake, reading and drinking tea from my thermos with the Anapurna in the background. Definitly a place to go

Barring a goof up at the reception where they blocked our access to rooms well before the checkout time of 12 noon, the experience was pleasant. The staff at the gate, was excellent, courteous and pleasant

Thamel can be referred to the heart of Kathmandu. Most of the hotels and famous restaurants are present in this area. The market area is nice but over-priced. Nice for a strolling, eating and staying options but, for shopping, visit Asan area.

Calling it Shopping Area it's an understatement. In Nepal you find shops everywhere.
'Jungle' of tea, sport-trekking clothes, t-shirts and thankas vendors. Less pollution and less bikes but still whatch out, it is not a 'motor' free zone. Plus: attention to human taxi bikers. 
Here no historical attraction; only Garden of Dreams not far - not visited yet

Thamel is just so much fun. There's great food and drink all around. There's all the different shops and local goods for sale. A couple really good book stores. Any kind of Mountain gear that you need for your trek. Overall a must when in the city.
Nice place to go for a walk. Something that is not easy to find in the cities of Nepal. Nice scenery, although it is quite crowded.

We chose OR2K for lunch and were pleasantly surprised with the menu options and food quality.
The portions are more than enough for a person.
Taste is very good.

Ambience and sitting plan is very nice, outdoors is lake side view and it is very nice ! 

middle east, south east and nepali cuisine
as usual in nepal, service time is 30 minutes.

Stayed for 3 nights in October.
Unfortunately the room did not look like the one pictured (however, this room does exist) Our room was dark and a bit damp - recon if they painted the rooms white and got rid of the damp carpets it would be improved massively. 
The location was right in the middle of Thamel so good restaurants and bars on your doorstep. That said it's location means it can be very noisy at night (unless there's a power cut!) 
The manager was really helpful and organised our flights to Pokhara for us for cheaper than advertised!

We chose the Waterfront for a few days recuperation after a tough trek. The rooms itself are very nicely appointed. Lake and pool views, separate shower with bath facilities. Room service is available and prompt. Wifi connection is good but you will pay for usage per day and per device.

However.

They tried to charge us 1,000 rupees for a round trip to a local doctor that should have cost 300 at most. 

Our lasting memory of the hotel will be the courtesy shuttle bus refusing to go a further 100 metres down the main road. We were the last passengers on the bus, carrying many bags and the bus had no where else to be for at least another hour. Having invested the money we did to stay in what is deemed the best hotel in Pokhara we were incredibly disappointed with this. 

I'm not in the business of posting negative reviews on Trip Advisor and I can see the hotel is aiming for American standards but in order for them to achieve this they need a serious overhaul of their service charter. The hotel obviously gets by on it's lake views and pool to attract guests but there are other local hotels that will bend over backwards to accommodate guests and not rip them off in the process.

I had an amazing experience at this hotel. The chef Manita at the breakfast was amazing at her job! She actually makes the best omelettes. Highly recommend this hotel and their staff. It is also convenient location for anything around. Thamel is just 10 minutes walking distance
This is yet another UNESCO World Heritage site in the Kathmandu Valley. Offers a bird's eye view of Kathmandu Valley.  2 of the stupas here were still being repaired after the earthquake.

This is a huge, bustling hotel right in the centre of tourist Kathmandu. It has such a beautiful, communal garden which provides a quiet oasis that can feel much needed in this extraordinary city. The restaurant and bar are open all day - you can eat Nepali or more westernised options - and get great coffee etc. 

The room is another matter. I was in a group of charity workers, so obviously our rooms were not going to be any other than the basic option. Basic is fine, but ingrained dirt and mould in the bathroom are not fine, even on a budget. I also noticed that the emergency fire exit option was actually the ONLY way out on my floor - so it would have had to be out of the window and into a back alley had a fire blocked the corridor. Not great when you are a few floors up. I would love to visit again and I imagine that there are much better rooms on offer - so check out what your room is like before staying!

The staff - especially those working in the restaurant and garden bar - were great.
We couldn't really enjoy this place. Not a nice atmosphere. And 6000 Rps for a fami of three is definitely to much!

It is a noteworthy landmark and worth seeing. Do your research, know where things are and what the stories behind them are. Standing idle will result in being hassled by prospective guides and they are very persistent. Use the leaflet from the ticket box to navigate and leave enough time to find your way through the restoration works into the museum.

Our stay at the hotel was truly unforgettable, thanks to the warm and professional team who made us feel right at home.

A special thank you to Star in the restaurant – your cheerful nature, warm smile, and attentive service made every dining experience delightful. You were a bright part of our day, every day.

Krishna at the bar was excellent – friendly, skilled, and always ready with great suggestions and a welcoming attitude. You made our evenings fun and relaxing – thank you!

We would especially like to appreciate Muskan, the spa in-charge. From the moment we stepped into the spa, her calm and confident guidance made us feel comfortable and well taken care of. She explained the different spa options in great detail and helped us choose the perfect treatments. Though she didn’t do the massage herself, under her expert guidance, both my wife and I had a deeply relaxing and rejuvenating experience. Her professionalism, warmth, and personal attention truly made a lasting impression on us.

To the entire team – thank you for your exceptional service and hospitality. You turned a good trip into a truly memorable one. Highly recommended and without a doubt, a full 5-star experinced !

Regards 
Parveen Mittal

I booked a Deluxe room. The reason is that the standard rooms looked a bit worn out on the website of the hotel. The Deluxe rooms should be in the new wing. Surprisingly we got a room in the old wing and I saw immediately that this was certainly not a room in the new wing. No elevator here however the Deluxe rooms would be serviced by an elevator. Front office emphasized we got a Deluxe room, however it was in the old wing. I didnt accept this room and ask for the room as shown on their website. That room was not available but they offered another room. That room was acceptable for us, however also this room looked not very fresh and elegant. The lady at the front office was a bit aggitated because of my attitude because she smashed the key on the counter. Also other staff members didnt act very welcoming and service minded. I really felt not valued as a guest of this hotel. By the way: wifi is very very slow. So if you book an expensive Deluxe room please ask for a room in the new wing. There seem to be Deluxe rooms in the old wing too and they are really much too much over prized. And be careful for the pretty arrogant attitude of lady front office and her colleagues. I don’t reccommend this hotel!
The service was very good. I liked the pool a lot and the overall vibe. I would definitely stay here again. It’s a must stay when you are in pokhara

I will review this place as excellent, because of the very friendly and helpful people that work here. The pool is big and there is also a small gym (was manageable even if REALLY hot from the sun), which was a great experience. The breakfast and dinner (didnt eat lunch, if there was any), contained a lot of different options with mostly Nepali food.

Whilst it cost a little more to let a Hotel arrange a car, it’s still very cheap by our standards (abt £10) and you have the comfort of your driver waiting . You then walk for abt 15 mins uphill and sometimes on steps and paths that look pretty dodgy. It’s definitely worth it- stunning views. Nepal is breathtakingly beautiful and this was definitely one of the highlights. You must try and go for sunrise which was stunning

The lake is beautiful, the colorful boats making it very eye catching. There are a few locations for boat rides, suggest you go to one that is less crowded. Today being Saturday (weekend in Nepal) the main boating area was crowded and extremely noisy, it is very popular with teens. Suggest to use the one opposite Hotel Glacier. Lovely photos can be taken, enjoy the view.

Booked to stay with them and cancelled my room during the permitted cancellation period. They promised to refund my payment but never did. AVOID!!!

I had numerous emails from them all promising to pay, but it has been over a year now so I've given up any hope.

The Hotel has always been very receptive. The staff is well mannered and courteous. Food is good.

Rooms are well appointed, neat. Spa is good.

Only thing to improve is A.C during winters, this works only on heating mode. The only option to cool the room is to switch off the A.C.

Quite a climb and be careful if you are frightened of heights, but well worth it when you reach the top. We had no trouble with the monkeys and the views are amazing. There are lots of trinkets stalls and one amazing shop that was crammed with bits and bobs, all at really cheap prices. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit.
Service staff is thoughtful too of guest's needs and pattern also. Specially Ayushma ji. Temple Tree is the nicest Hotel that I have been to in Nepal. Its always nice to get a few days there.

Travelling as 2 families with 3 children under 7, we had a dreadful experience with this hotel. Everyone travelling with young children knows to plan carefully and keep the local admin to a minimum. We had extensively researched our options in Kathmandu, and following much the advice on this site, booked specific rooms with specific requests. All our requests were confirmed in writing, and subsequent phone calls. On arrival, it became apparent that they had not reserved the rooms, failed to get an extra bed put in, ignored our request to have adjacent rooms on the same floor, and basically had no record of any correspondence. When I produced the correspondence confirming the specific rooms etc, they apologised but said they couldn't do anything about it. We had tired children so we decided to stay just the night and then check out in the morning. Then we found that the power in the hotel was off and the toilets didn't flush. By the time my wife and i had unpacked, out friends had checked out to go to the Crown Plaza because the hotel refused to provide an extra bed for a 4 year old. It was now 10 pm and we had to then check out and join our friends as we had arranged a 8 am pickup in the morning.

I am aware that a range of budgets and requirements exist for the traveller, and that it's horses for courses in terms of ones needs or expectations. I don't mind hotels being any standard, really, as long as they are honest and manage your expectations fairly. If I had told them that i just wanted a bed close to Thamel, and somewhere to dry my socks, i'd be on here giving them a few stars. 

Unfortunately however, although they knew we were 2 families and they knew we had young children and they confirmed the specific floor, rooms, and availability of the extra bed, we ended up in a lousy position; it was 8 pm, after 10 hours travelling, three hungry and tired children, in a hotel that couldn't accommodate us. I'd like to say that at least they were polite about it, but they really weren't. It was really shabby and extremely annoying to have been mislead in this way, so be careful when you book this place. Make sure its really what your looking for.
The word Durbar means palace and it was damaged during the earthquake and is now being rebuilt. Quite a fascinating place o visit.
Overall not only Phewa lake -but surrounding areas are so peacefull specially first thing in the morning and in the evening...one of the place to visit if you are visiting Pokhara

One has to reach much before the sunrise to get a good seat. The whole mountain range turns golden at the first ray of sunrise. We were unlucky to get that view but we enjoyed the onset of fog at the last moment. Must visit place while at Pokhara. One can go for Para-gliding as well to Sarangkot giving a lovely experience of viewing the mountains and lake as well while landing.

Horrible service, bad value and underwhelming. Rooms are old. No covid safety measures in place. Guest relations are just incapable of getting something done in time or efficiently. Only good thing was the PCR test they manage to arrange for me in the hotel.

This is a very modern hotel in Kathmandu. The lobby is grand with doormen and concierge. The room is well appointed and clean. The restaurant at the lobby provides excellent buffet and dinner in buffet style. The varieties of food served there are more than enough to satisfy the most demanding guests. The roof top of the hotel commands a great view of the city. Hotel staff are very friendly and eager to serve.

Do not pass by this place when coming to Pokhara! I went there a few times during my visit and everything I ate was delicious. At happy hour they have free sangria and lemonade for you to enjoy as you watch the sunset from their ideal location. A great place to have a few drinks at night or hang out and use the Internet during the day. Beautiful artwork and lighting, good music. A very fun place to be. And the bonus... nice bathrooms, beautiful sinks and individual towels to dry your hands!
Came with the group,Room  is very comfortable, staffs are very friendly. Swimming pool so clean. You can just sit and relax even in the rain day!Highly recommended!

I stayed in Radisson - KTM for 5 nights , it was a comfortable stay and the the staff is great specially the f&b team - Mr Ramhari , will surely visit again in my coming trips. Also the overall hospitality of the team is appreciated.

It was wonderful experience staying at the hotel. We would like to extend our gratitude to everyone, especially to rupak and moniita  for providing exceptional hospitality with love, care and happiness during breakfast. Their professionalism and dedication to delivering excellent service truly made our morning special. Thank you and see u soon

Great location. Hotel has everything you need. Renovations were going on at time of stay but did not interfere with residents. Pool clean, restaurants good, breakfast excellent buffet, we stayed in a old suite which was v good, our friend had a newly renovated room, which was excellent.

It feels that you are driving into a private club in he middle of Thamel, Kathmandu; bamboo lined driveway with a  lovely garden at the end. My friend and I had not planned much, as we were helping build five classrooms in Bhaktapur, following the earthquake in 2015. So we were made most welcome, and the manager organised a tour for us to their hotel in Royal Chitwan Nat. Park, and onto their hotel in Pokhara. It was great. The rooms that we had were average, but unfortunately we found that  the drains in the showers in both our rooms (302 & 304 similar to photo) smelled and spread to the rooms. They are renovating those rooms, so that problem should be solved. Lovely to sit in the gardens and relax. Good coffee bar.

Pokhara international museum is one of the best museum for me in Nepal.i can get lots of information about Nepal,culture of nepal , traditional of nepal,religions of Nepal and many more.i visit in this February 8 with my friend but that time i don't have much time to see all around the museum so definitely come back to see again..

Having stayed at the KGH on at least 25 occasions over the past 20 years, I've finally got fed up with it !
Its pluses - great location if you want to be in the midst of Thamel, very pleasant garden, and an interesting building.
The downside: 
I've grown weary of the 'will the rooms I've booked be available, or not' tension on arrival.
Apart from the new wing the rooms are not brilliant, and often not very clean nor well maintained.
The front desk staff give the impression of being world-weary, and having seen it all before. Their lack of helpfulness, and of manners, finally convinced me that there are other hotels in Kathmandu that are much better value.

My wife and I stayed here for a few days before and after our Everest Base Camp trek in May/June 2010.  The location is good; while not right in Thamel it is very close.  The building itself is very unique and lends itself well to being photographed; beautifully manicured gardens.

The rooms are nice and clean, if a little dark.  The bathrooms leave much to be desired considering the price of the rooms.  And the eco-friendly nature of the hotel is fine if you support that thing, although this means no A/C and limited water use.  

The on-site restaurant was great, serving up traditional Nepali fare.  And this was the only place in our three month trip that provided free bottled drinking water... a huge plus especially in the summer!

Travelers need to be wary of the cancellation policy, especially those who will be trekking without fixed dates.

For the money you can find much better places in Thamel. Booked via booking and room was totally not what I expected. Electricity and fan did not work all the time. Wifi very bad connection. But friendly staff.

This can not be considered a 5 stars hotel. Breakfast is really poor, the facilities not what expected… Rooms are ok, the the experience was disappointing. It’s the worst Radisson so have been so far.

Hotel Thamel is marvellous accommodation , full with smile , and greetings . Rooms are clean , spacious and walk to shop galleries within walking distance . Their manager Mr Karma is very friendly and kind person . We had a warm welcome .

If you are in Kathmandu, this is a perfect place to stay. What stands out is the beautiful architecture, the brick wall corridors. They are very ecologically conscious, without compromising on comfort or hygiene. 

The staff is very friendly and accomdative. The front desk Kriti & Others were prompt with our requests. They have arranged a heritage walking tour at a short notice. Our guide Suman was very knowledgeable and helpful. 

The breakfast is a must-try, especially the home-made carrot ginger jam and the cinnamon yogurt.

Situated in the center, it's easily accessible all major attractions.

The monkey temple is perched on one of the largest hills in Kathmandu. It has great views and the stupa is interesting. Tonnes of monkeys up there too. You get a feeling at the top that if they cleaned the place up a wee bit it would look 100 times better. You'll have to hike up about 200 steps to get to the top

This hotel has very slow Wi-Fi service.  At first I thought that this being a third world country, this is the best one can expect in this part of the world, until I found out that even the coffee shops around town provide faster internet service than this hotel.   As I look at past reviews of this hotel, I notice that for a long time now many other people have complained about the internet service at this hotel, and, after a prefatory apology, management has always responded by saying that they are in the "process of upgrading" and presumably this problem will be taken care of then.  Well management has been telling us for a long time now that they are in the "process of upgrading."  By now such a response becomes meaningless and sounds disingenuous.  You would think that by now, with all these customer complaints, the Wi-Fi would have long been updated if management is serious about fixing the problem.  It should not take more than 4 to 8 weeks to fix the Wi-Fi problem, certainly not years.  So what is the hold up?

The hotel room we stayed in is tired looking and in need for serious redecorating.  I noticed that this too has been one of the top customer complaints about this hotel for quite a while.  And you guessed it, for many years now management's response is that we are in the "process of upgrading."  I say, enough of that excuse.

Notwithstanding the 37 acres of gardens at this property, I would expect a lot better for the US$ 180 per night I paid to stay here.  This hotel is not living up to its brand name, and management's drone response to customer complaints is completely unacceptable.

I wish I would checked the reviews before deciding to stay at this hotel.

Stayed six months in the penthouse suite, business trip, and was totally impressed with the staff as well as the facilities.  Everyone from the front desk to the concierge to the housekeepers to the drivers were very helpful and friendly.  The location is also a plus.  Nice neighborhood with plenty of excellent restaurants in the area.  It is an easy walk to Thamel and other points of interest.  Highly recommended!

Had the 30 min walk from Thamel. High up with lots of monkeys! Lots of smaller stupas and Buddha statues. More tourists than buddhists when I was there... Nice place. The monkeys made my trip. For me the stupa at Boudnatha was a better experience because it had "more genuine feel".

It was fun to walk around taking photographs. I decided not to pay extra for a guide but I was pestered by one when I first walked in and I kept being asked by several different people as i walked through the square. It was interesting to see all the buildings and read the information about the history of the square. There was also an area where we could buy souvenirs.
I took my time and wandered around the square.  I did not use a guide, but used a guide book instead. very enjoyable.

Swayambhu nath stupa is one of the best place to visit in kathmandu. Very ancient place with whole lot of architecture and culture. From there you can see whole kathmandu valley. Better to go in day time and also in night time, so that you can feel both imaginary feelings. Just one thing please do not tease the monkeys. And before making picture look around for a notice if you can or cannot. We loved this place. Highly recommended to visit.

Booked 2 nights at this temple house for our first visit to Nepal in Dec and absolutely loved it! Photos provided depicted what you would expect. Loved the outdoor garden seating and food was good too. The hospitality was exceptional with special mention to Mr Suman, who went beyond to share his recommendations and helped us experience kathmandu on another level we never expected. Mr Ajit and Ms Shazana (not sure if we have spelled their names correctly) at the front desk were so friendly and provided help whenever we needed. We ended up extending our stay in ktm and stayed with them an extra night! 

Overall, fantastic experience and would come back again next time!
They hardly start to re-built the collapsed temples and it becomes to be reality with success so i hope for my next visit not in march but end of oct 2020 some temples will be finished.

We stayed at Kantipur Temple House before and after treking to Everest Base Camp.
Very hospitable. Excellent friendly staff.Beautiful traditional decor. Eco friendly and plastic free.Lovely garden and patio area.

Me and my partner after looong time traveling and eating only form cheap, local  kitchen, noticed this place- they have VEGAN options, so as celebration we decided to have special meal in OR2K.
He ordered Shakshuka in vegan version, with egg replacement. What he got was TASTELESS dough made from flour and water, soaked in smashed warm tomatoes. And he had to pay 60 rs extra for vegan option.
I have ordered sandwich witch tahini and tomatoes. Two slices of toast bread with a bit of tahini, slice of salad and tomatoes. Israeli salad is plain cucumber with tomatoes. For this 255 rs.
GREAT DISSAPOINTMENT.
Everything was plain, tasteless, so westernized.
After all Staff working there is rude, invisible, helpless. And trying to fool You on money, charging for something You havent order.

If You are on Nepal, for God sake go to some authentic place. Where food is served with love and passion. Where You are not just a customer with fat wallet.
This place is fake, westernized gallery, MUCH overpriced. 
Definetly avoid!

The Hotel in general is beautiful like 5 star hotel should be. However the room was really dated with leaking sink, old marks everywhere, wifi worked purely, with bad sound isolation, could hear my neighbours all the time. 
The most disappointing was the smell from the towels in the gym - like fried food - really gross. 
From the other hand the property is big, in summer time there is a swimming pool, and the Stupa is walking distance.

This hotel was friendly and inviting.  The spa was nice and the prices were great.  The food was interesting and plentiful and the bar prices were also fair.  It was nice to have access to a swimming pool, and there was a changing room and plenty of lounge chairs.
Just a short ride from lakeside, it display photos, artifacts, reproductions of houses and temples located in the mountain part of nepal. Nice

I’d like to share my appreciation for the front desk staff Ayshua. They were welcoming, attentive, and handled my questions efficiently. Their professionalism and positive attitude created a great first impression and made the experience smooth and pleasant.

Lake is surrounded by amazing nature, high mountains and forests, and it's easily accessible from the city.
You can rent a boat or take a walk by the lake, and have a meal at some of many small restaurants which offer nice view on the lake.
Locals are fishing along the shore, black buffaloes resting in the water... very relaxing if you move away from the town

First, Nepal is an amazing country with intense culture the moment you land.  However, in general the hotel standards are below par (and I have been to Sri Lanka, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, India, etc).  There is an lack of attention to maintenance overall in most of the hotels in Nepal.   

I just came back from a 10 days trip in Nepal from Hong Kong, me and my friends stayed at Kantipur Temple House for 3 nights.  We were attracted by the hotel location and the traditional architecture, but if you cannot rough it, do not stay here.  Do not let the charm influence you, the hotel is charming, but you will see (and can enjoy) the traditional architecture in all 3 durbar squares of Kathmandu Valley, there is no need to sacrifice hygiene/bathroom standards.

Pros: great location (in a quiet alley in Thamel area), staff are friendly, hotel aesthetics are great for photo opt, it's an eco hotel (plastic free).

Cons: maintenance is an issue (bathrooms are really run down-moldy, weird smell), Kathmandu is really dusty (especially after a day of exploration) but the hotel rooms have carpet (and no slipper)-it would make more sense just to have the wooden floor for easy housekeeping & hygiene (which is how the hotel is feature on website), it's an eco hotel (no bottle water, limited amenities, no A/C, no elevators...which doesn't bother me but in case you have elderly/physical disabilities).

It's ok if you can handle the bathroom, no A/C, and the uncertain carpet hygiene.  It's an average hotel at most, decent option if you plan to just transit overnight and need a place to stay with some charm.

I would not recommend to stay here for long durations.  If you plan to go to the mountains (or just come from the mountains), you will already be subjected to low standards of bathrooms, so I recommend you to stay in a more western standard hotel in Kathmandu.

Suggestion for the hotel: focus on the details and improve maintenance, use bleach in the bathroom, upgrade the bathrooms, remove carpet from rooms (can use a rug instead), provide slippers.  The hotel has a lot of potential.
Nothing great about the lake other than the restaurants around it. The lake is the centre point for tourists. You can enjoy a peaceful boat ride or just chill and have a drink!

The Pokhara branch of this restaurant has a fantastic view of the lakeside and outside seating if you so desire. Great atmosphere, friendly service, and delicious vegetarian food. Shoes off and sit on cushions inside.

Quite large portions, as well.

Where to start - let's be positive first

a) Great tourist location in darkest Thamel
b) The main hotel building and annexe set well back in their own large grounds with a delightful lawned dining and lounging area - great for relaxing
c) Most of the staff pleasant and helpful
d) Good South African/Italian wine available at reasonable prices

and negative .....

e) My room was very ordinary with a view of a closeby wall covered in pigeon **** looking down onto a similarly decorated tin roof. While i was there the roof was hosed down and made to look much better. Thamel, as with the most intense tourist centres of capital cities, is a little overwhelming. It is a focus for bars, clubs, restaurants and, most of all, shops. The aptly named  Freak Street, close to Durbar Square, used to be THE place for travellers to Kathmandu in the 60s and 70s. However with changes in legislation that scene faded away. In its place Thamel became the focus for travellers wanting to indulge their exotic lifestyle choices and the growing trekking market. In response businesses sprang up in their hundreds to fulfil that demand. Foreign travellers and their spending power created the beautiful monster that has become modern day Thamel. It is stuffed with retail outlets selling trekking gear, apparel and cultural items. Much leans towards satisfying that same demand from Westerners seeking the exotic in all its manifestations as Freak street once did. However it has grown to be so much more. There is a huge number of hotels providing accommodation from the simplest shared dorms to high quality exclusive rooms and apartments. In addition the restaurants too reflect that diversity of choice. Thamel has become, in some respects, quite an expensive place to stay and enjoy. However it still retains that backpacker feel and suits every budget. 
Maybe the biggest issue for Thamel is its popularity and density. That combined with increases in traffic makes it a very busy often highly polluted district. Efforts to curtail motorised traffic fail from lack of enforcement. The high number of motorcycles make visitors feel like they are running the gauntlet every time they step out onto the streets. That includes small alleys and passageways which are all seen as regular routes by motorists. Given the poor air quality and potential danger created by these vehicles the experience for visitors can be very poor. This is, of course, true of many built up areas within the valley. For many a few days in the capital is as much as can tolerated both in terms of the overwhelming business of the place and, maybe most importantly, health.
Within Thamel there remains small pockets or oasis’s of peace and calm. There are gardens, rooftops.. hotels and restaurants that provide shelter from the urban commercial craziness that permeates much of Thamel. Finding them is the key.

We booked two nights in this hotel at the end of our two week trip to Nepal based on the travel book by Lonely Planet. It recommended this as one of the top hotels in Kathmandu. We wish we never booked it! ill go over what we liked first before delving into our dislikes.

We paid for breakfast the first morning at Kantipur Temple House and it cost $10 a person. Most meals in Nepal are generally $3-4 a person so this was ridiculous! Not to mention, the food was just mediocre and definitely not worth it. The second day, we walked down the road and found a small street bakery for breakfast- it was just $4 for both of us and much more fun!!!

 The rooms all had two windows facing into the hallway. At night, the hall lights stayed on and light glared through the windows, making sleep difficult. During the day, the rooms were very dark and gloomy. Reading my book hurt my eyes in the dull light. 

The showers didn't hardly work; there was a minor trickle at best. Also, the water never heated up. It was too cold to shower in. Also the room did not come with shampoo or conditioner. 

The staff was not helpful, nor were they friendly. They always seemed irritated to be helping a guest and were not accommodating. The security guard outside of the hotel premises was much more helpful and friendly- always greeting us with a smile and waving down cabs for us. The hotel offered yoga every morning, which I thought was neat. Yet they held it right outside next to the generator- definitely not a relaxing place! Finally, the hotel didn't have AC or a heater. It's ok during spring or summer, when temperatures are mild, but would be unbearable in summer or winter. The power goes out for 10-12 hours every day in Nepal, but most hotels have generators to make up for it. Kantipur Temple House's generator is only strong enough to light a couple of bulbs, compared to all our other hotels that provided AC and regular lighting with their generators. 

All in all, this hotel was not worth the money. We spent much less at other hotels and got so much more out of them!!!

Fewa Lake is a freshwater lake in Nepal formerly known as Baidam Tal located in the south of the Pokhara Valley that includes Pokhara city; components of Sarangkot and Kaskikot. Fewa lake in Nepal and is the biggest lake in the Pokhara. There is also a Tabarahi Temple Hindu temple on the core of the lake. If human beings choose to go to the temple they should take a boat. Phewa Lake is the 2d largest lake in the Nepal. It is the solely lake in Nepal, that have a Temple in the centre of the lake. And that temple is known as Barahi Mandir. It is famous for having a lot of domestic and global vacationers who go to and sail, swim and fish on the Phewa lake. The lake is stream-fed but a dam regulates the water reserves, therefore, the lake is classified as semi-natural freshwater lake. It is the 2d biggest lake in Nepal; the greatest in Gandaki Pradesh after the Rara lake in the comparison to Nepal's water bodies. It is the most popular and most visited lake of Nepal. 

It is the solely lake in Nepal to have a temple Tal Barahi Temple at the central phase of lake. The shadow of a nearby white mountain can be seen on the floor of the lake. Phewa lake is located at an altitude of 742 m (2,434 ft) and covers an region of about 4.43 km2 (1.7 sq mi). It has an average depth of about 8.6 m (28 ft) and a maximum depth of 24 m (79 ft). Maximum water ability of the lake is approximately 43,000,000 cubic metres (35,000 acre⋅ft). The Annapurna vary on the north is only about 28 km (linear distance) away[6] from the lake. The lake is additionally well-known for the reflection of mount Machhapuchhre and different mountain peaks of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri stages on its surface. The Tal Barahi Temple is located on an island in the lake.

When they told me that the International Mountain Museum was the only one of its kind in the world, it sounded a tall claim at first. Then, walking around, shown around actually, by the museum director I found many gems here that I haven’t had the heart to Google the self-proclaimed title. The museum was set up as a tribute to all mountaineers who surrendered their lives to their brave endeavours and is a favourite with mountaineers and tourists alike. 
The model of the Manaslu mountain by the museum entrance is evocative of the tribute. The Manaslu, unlike most of the Himalayan peaks, was first climbed by the Japanese, giving it a special place among Asian mountaineers. Not only was the first conquest Asian, but a large number of Japanese, Nepalese and South Korean lives have been lost in attempts to reach its summit. Manaslu, which means ‘soul’ in Sanskrit, also lays claim to the largest toll on lives by any peak in the region. On a spring day in 1972, it wiped off an entire expedition party of 15 in an avalanche. 
One doesn’t have to be a museum enthusiast to enjoy this one – there is history, culture, all with a dash of adventure. The museum was established to document the developments in three areas: the origin of the major mountain systems of the world, the different people inhabiting the mountain regions and important feats in mountaineering. There are primarily four exhibit halls. They are the halls of mountain people, world mountains, mountain activities and guest exhibitions. In the mountain section there are photographs of the 14 peaks which are above 8,000 metres. Aka the ‘eight thousanders.’ Most of the photographs are taken by expedition groups who set out for their summits. There is a section for the mountain peoples, giving us a glimpse on the way of lives of different mountain folks – the utensils, weapons and other tools they used for everyday living. 
As you roam around the museum, one thing will become apparent: people everywhere are the same – the only defining factor being the borders that separate us.
If you have some time to kill in Pokhara and would like to learn more about the geography, history and way of life of different ethnic groups if Nepal? Then this is the place for you :)

Fewa Lake is a freshwater lake in Nepal previously known as Baidam Tal positioned in the south of the Pokhara Valley that consists of Pokhara city; parts of Sarangkot and Kaskikot. Fewa Lake or Fewa Taal being the 2d biggest lake of Nepal, is one of the primary attractions and most necessary landmarks of Pokhara. The lake is stream-fed but a dam regulates the water reserves, therefore, the lake is classified as semi-natural freshwater lake. Roughly measuring up to 1.5 km by using 4 km and about 47 meters deep Fewa Taal spreads across in lustrous grandeur with fish-tailed summit of Machhapuchhre (6,993m) rising grandly on the background! On a clear day one can see the glowing reflection of the summit on the lake, creating a outstanding double photo so magical that it appears almost surreal! It is the second largest lake in Nepal; the greatest in Gandaki Pradesh after the Rara lake in the evaluation to Nepal's water bodies. Numerous brightly colored wooden boats and sail boats can be seen lined up on the shore awaiting humans to take them on a leisurely and enthralling ride around the lake. It is the most popular and most visited lake of Nepal. It is the solely lake in Nepal to have a templeTal Barahi Temple at the central phase of lake. Phewa lake is located at an altitude of 742 m and covers an place of about 4.43 km2. Apart from boating and fishing, swimming is additionally sought as one of the recreational things to do in this lovely lake. The water is warm and best but with no particular guarantee of it being clean, one has to be some distance from simply adventurous to threat a dive! It has an average depth of about 8.6 m and a maximum depth of 24 m. Maximum water ability of the lake is approximately 43,000,000 cubic metres. The Annapurna range on the north is only about 28 km away from the lake. The japanese shoreline of the lake is lined up with endless hotels, lodges, restaurants, bookshops, souvenir shops for humans to select some thing interesting along with them; now that could be an object, and or virtually lovely memories. The lake is additionally well-known for the reflection of mount Machhapuchhre and other mountain peaks of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges on its surface. The Tal Barahi Temple is situated on an island in the lake.

I took local minibus from lakeside 'Hallan Chowk' to 'Zero Km' (2.1 km costing around NPR 15) and from there to 'Baglung bus park' (2 km costing around NPR 20). Here one can board local bus (guess every 2 hour) that goes to Sarangkot view point (around NPR 50). It is recommended to find empty seat on bus early on and then reserve it literally by keeping one of inexpensive personal stuff there and enjoying time outside the bus after checking it's departure time. Please do take care to track location and get down at right spot as these buses normally go much further from Sarangkot. Also there are multiple spots that shows board for Sarangkot so important not to get down early to reduce uphill steps. At the drop point, one can notice a very  small movable shop that sell cigarettes, water, bhel, paani Puri, groundnut, etc (pic uploaded). One can spend few minutes here sipping black tea and enjoying view of Phewa lake. One can spot a board nearby that says 5 min trek to Bazaar (market) and 5 minutes to view point. One can start taking the steps which would lead us to a road in 5 minutes and another board that welcomes to view point entrance (pic uploaded) and Shiva temple ( undergoing renovation). 5-10 minute steep steps would lead to the enclosure which is the viewpoint. The entrance fee is NPR 50 for non Nepalis. After enjoying the view and cool breeze one can retrun back via the same route to that little shop. One can wait here for local bus but frequency is very low ( guess last one is at 4 PM) or better walk forward few metres down the road and spot a mark at right hand side that shows start of downhill trek towards lakeside. One can follow that steps and enjoy beautiful 1-1.5 hour of great views of Phewa lake, local houses and forest like ambience ( at lower part of trail when houses disappear) and if lucky one can spot hairy monkeys too. On the trail, you will find the main road or dusty roads which may be confusing. Please stick to downhill route that has rock steps or ask any local nearby when confused. The trail would end on dusty road where houses can be seen. It further need 10 minute walk to reach main road at Lakeside.

It could have been an honest mistake, but it seems unlikely as collecting money and giving out tickets is literally his entire job, and I waited for several seconds for a ticket with no one else around. So I wonder how often this happens, and whether many of the fees (which I think are unjustified in any case) are being pocketed by the guards.

WHEN you go to Pokhara don't miss a chance to hire a boatman and go out for a paddle on Lake Phewa.
The views are quite simply spectacular and at times the surface of the lake was like a sheet of glass it was so still.
But there is a darker side to this idyllic setting  and when I chatted with my boatman I learnt a few harsh realities about commercial life on the lake.
For instance, when you walk down to the boating hire point you will have to go to a ticket office and pay a charge to hire your boatman to paddle you round the lake for an hour.
That charge for me was R900 or just over £5.50 but my lovely boatman, whose name I won't reveal to protect him from any backlash from the organisers, got just R160 from this despite him doing all the work. That's about 98 pence.
When you realise that he could only do about six bookings per day you can do the maths yourself that he was effectively working for less than £6 per day while the organisers were raking in more than £27 from his efforts.
I made sure I tipped him heavily at the end of two trips I made with him during which he showed me some of the lake's interesting places and talked about how the lake had changed during his many years working there.
He gestured to a shoreline dotted with homes and hotels and said that when he first started the shoreline was empty.
Now the very popularity and commercialism which dominates this attraction is threatening to destroy it.
He took me along the far shore of the lake and showed me enchanting little coves with small shingle beaches. At least they used to be enchanting. Now there are drifts of party rubbish, discarded bottles and plastic waste which he said he cleared when he could.
He paddled me round an island with a little temple on it and also pointed out the start of treks which lead to another temple.
You must wear a lifejacket which was easy to put on and very necessary since I saw nothing like a rescue boat.
Throughout all this mountain scenery added its own magic and I will never forget my time on the lake. I'd recommend a trip out on it for the scenery alone.

There is also extensive damage done to some buildings by a recent earthquake but it is encouraging to see the rebuilding being done with the help of other countries. During my visit to Kathmandu, one of the most memorable experiences was exploring Swayambhunath, also known as the Monkey Temple. Perched atop a hill, this ancient stupa is one of the holiest Buddhist sites in Nepal, offering a stunning panoramic view of the Kathmandu Valley.

The climb up the long stone staircase was both challenging and rewarding. Along the way, I was greeted by curious monkeys that live around the site—hence the nickname "Monkey Temple." At the top, the golden spire of the stupa gleamed under the sunlight, its all-seeing eyes painted on all four sides, symbolizing the watchful gaze of the Buddha.

Colorful prayer flags fluttered in the breeze, creating a spiritual atmosphere. I could hear the low hum of monks chanting and the gentle spin of prayer wheels as pilgrims moved clockwise around the stupa. The air was filled with the scent of incense and butter lamps, deepening the sense of reverence.

The site also features smaller shrines, statues, and ancient carvings, blending Hindu and Buddhist iconography. Swayambhunath is more than a monument—it's a place of living faith, history, and breathtaking beauty. Visiting it gave me a profound sense of peace and a deeper appreciation for Nepal’s rich spiritual heritage.

I can't imagine staying at a better hotel in Kathmandu. If you're traveling to Nepal for a trek, it's highly likely that you'll be staying in Thamel. Kantipur is located right in the heart of it, but somehow perfectly removed from the overwhelming hustle and bustle of the city.  It's like a quiet oasis complete with its own courtyard to relax and have a drink in, do yoga, etc. This is a rarity in Thamel.

Any shops or restaurants you'll want to visit visit are all within easy walking distance.

The design of the hotel is likely exact what you're looking for as a foreigner visiting the country. They have leaned heavily into the traditional style of Nepali temples with beautiful brick and wood adorning the rooms (What you won't find here is the sterile environment of a standard box hotel). 

I also can't speak enough to the wonderful hospitality of the staff who were all incredibly helpful accommodating us in any way needed during our tip. Adding to the personal touch, the owner also joins the guests at breakfast for a friendly hello. 

If you're traveling to Kathmandu, stay at Kantipur Temple House. You'll be happy you did.

Food is fresh and tasty, hot water bottles for winter time to keep your toes cosy and a wealth of contemporary and historical information about Nepal and Kathmandu if you fancy a chat over breakfast or as your return later in the day. 🌺🙏😊

The square is also home, would you believe, to a LIVING Goddess. She was on her lunch hour when we showed up, so even deities need a cup of tea and a biscuit, I suppose....

Durbar square was grand, and a must-see, but temper your expectations before you go, as so much is sadly damaged....

Reachable by rickshaw from Thamel; an experience in itself!

We came a vacation the staff members were friendly. The bar is open 24 /7 for the hotel guests. The rooms are very accessible to the health and fitness centre and Swimming pool and the property is great. Ayushma and team they really cater you well and front of the house trip us also provides a great service.
The room service is also great and really liked the array of food items in the room service menu.
The hotel is located near the shopping spree and it's easier to access good restaurants and take scenic beauty of the iconic places of Pokhara.

nobody can enjoy this beautiful, calm, hill town without strolling in it's colourful streets, all of which lead to the heart, the lake.
the Annapurna and Fishtail range of mountains play hide and seek with you throughout a clear winter day in this city and you can see their faint reflection in this vast waterbody.
walk leisurely or sit in the park surrounding. Enjoy sunshine, food, nepalese music and dance, may relax boating, visit Barahi temple in the middle or attempt hill trekking from the other bank after crossing the lake.
of course, it is crowded, mostly in holidays, but essential to float like a feather here.

This is one of many large Buddhist Stupas in the area of Kathmandu and worth a stop.  The Stupa and the people visiting are fascinating and the shops and restaurants around the Stupa are very interesting.

We went today for dinner and must say the food was delicious and came out quite quick which is odd in Nepal.

Now, the service was appalling. I asked for water and they didn't bring me a glass. I had to ask for a glass 4 times until the waiter finally brought it to me. He didn't apologise or anything for forgetting.

We were waiting long time for someone to come and ask what dessert we want it but as no-one was coming we decided to leave.

As we left to the first floor to pay (we were on the second floor), we were greeted as if we were new customers, we could've totally left without paying, that's how little attention we got! We went on the till to pay and the guy gave us the bill, without even looking at us. We paid, said thank you and he plain ignored us, not even looking up.

First time in Nepal I am getting this bad service. Yes, the food is nice but.. I would not go back at all.

I rather go to Places or Loving heart were the quality of the food is extraordinary as it is their service.

An easy walk from Thamel area of Kathmandu and you will arrive at the steps leading up to Swayambhunath. The walk to the top will take you past many monkeys and street stalls. The view from the top is excellent. If it is a smoggy day you will likely be above the smog in cleaner air.

Very peaceful lovely views,  can spent hour and hour just walking on lakeside and watching on lake. 
Lovely place to spent time with friends and family on this beautiful place.

Situated off of one of the main shopping/restaurant thoroughfares (Baidam Road), the initial impressions are very good, with a modern open plan reception, bar and restaurant, accommodation arranged in two storey blocks, with some of the upper levels having views of the Annapurna range.  Rooms and beds are comfortable with a modern bathroom, although the TV was not tuned in. Most shops and restaurants are 10-15 min walk eastward from the hotel, but taxis are cheap and plentiful. Breakfast choice was plentiful, with fresh omelettes cooked to order. Service was average and lunch service particularly slow and laboured, with food served cold (french fries). Housekeeping was weird, if you keep your room key the room is not made up ! - The laundry service is one to be missed, overpriced, creased and still dirty - there are plenty of laundry services nearby, cheaper and more efficient. Overall - good to stay, but eat in any of the many restaurants in Baidam Road. The lemon meringue pie at the Moonbeam is sooo good!

I found this Hotel to be over priced. Internet was extremely poor and the hotel food was not fresh. Room service food smelt off. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. Also I found the check in and check out staff rude.

Hotel has lot of green well-maintained landscape and it is wonderful for taking walks.

Location of hotel is good - walkable distance to main stupa and other attractions like Thamel.

Staff is good and courteous to needs. Special kudoz to the staff of Sesame - Bhakta and Jhapad were polite, attentive and prompt in their service. They ensured we enjoyed the food and time at the restaurant.

Rooms are very old and need urgent attention. Rooms need to be renovated urgently. This includes various bathroom fittings, etc. This is where value for money is lost.
If you don't have time to do trekking many days. This place would be a choice to walk from the city to the view point. Along the way has nice mountain view in the clear day.
Come here and catch the sunrise or sunset. Be prepared to climb some stairs but we'll worth the getting up early and journey to the top. Around 1500 rupees taxi return to hotel

It was monsoon and without much hope we headed towards Sarangkot early morning, at 5 to be precise. The road was bad, although the drive was short and it was very crowded. Although we got to see some mountains and the view was awesome, Annapurnas standing tall with the clouds hanging below.

Beautiful scenery of the lake and the nearby mountains. We took a boat across to the other side to hike up to the World Peace Pagoda - would recommend this on a mild day (it was a bit hot for our liking but still very fun and gorgeous).

Room: is big and clean. 
Spa etc: We ordered 2 nights expecting spa, jaccuzi, sauna as per their website.. no sauna or jacuzzi in the hotel and the spa is closed for festival. No one informed us about that. 
Wifi: does not work in the rooms. 
Breakfast: we expected a decent breakfast ... but it ia a poor breakfast  the breads are from yesterday and the food was mostly over in the middle of the breakfast serving time.
We waited for a cup to make coffee and for milk for most of time. 
When asked for napkins for our table we were sent by the staff to take them from the next table by ourselves where people are eating at the same time..... we cancelled the second night. Does not worth the money.

Very comfortable. Great breakfast, friendly staff, quiet AC. I give a 4 not a 5 as the bathrooms could have been detailed a bit more thoroughly.
The breakfast was outstanding. Hotel restaurants are decent. Staff a very pleasant and helpful . We stayed here with a tour group.

I have been to this hotel more than 5 times and the only good thing about the hotel is the view of the lake. Last time i visited there were some misunderstandings but mostly what disappointed me was the food. White chocolate mousse smelled and tasted like eggs and it was watery. I have never had a chocolate mousse like that ever in my life. The buffet was ok but could have made the dishes better for the standard of the hotel. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone for the food and services.

The room was decent with a nice balcony and the pool was nice. Good breakfast as well. The service was just ok though. The internet in the rooms didn’t work and the hot water kept going in and out. Not worth the cost in Pokhara.

I visited this particular durbar square both during the day and in the evening and i love the vibe there was in the evening when it is all lit up most especially. the temples are beautiful and very old but people watching and shopping for souvenirs outside the square is also very interesting.

Sarangkot is off the tourist map...or so l thought till the bus driven dawn crowds arrived for..well the dawn .Fabulous views of Pokhara to the South and north to the monsters of the Himalaya.An unknown gem is a local kitchen making great vegetarian Indian.A great last stop coming down

I really like Pahsminas but the rip off artistgs who have stores in Thamel put me off.  I am an expert in various countries at bargaining but new to Nepal several years ago I was ripped off and pissed off becasue the re isn't a tourist office to help you navigate the pashmina game.  I did some research and found better prices the second time around but I still do not recommend thamel for tourists you can get much better prices in other cities.  The rent is shown in the outrageous prices the vendors suggest which is insulting to tourists.  I prefer Latin American and Central Asian and Vietnamese markets and European shoppes.

A welcoming hotel with superb and friendly staff. Nothing was too much trouble. Room size excellent, food excellent, people excellent. All very professional and caring. Located within walking distance of shops and restaurants but just tucked enough out of the way to provide a peaceful stay.

An excellent hotel.  The staff at the Radisson are very well trained, and so helpful in every way.  They all wanted to make our stay here a really great experience.  The Guest Relationship Manager sorted out any issues we had immediately and was so helpful.  Any questions you have about the city can be answered!  The breakfast was a delight with a wide range of foods from different cultures and all of an extremely high standard and quality.  We also ate in the restaurant in the evenings  because the food was so lovely. We stayed here three times during our trip in Nepal, using it as a base to leave luggage in-between trips and it was a pleasure to return to after our various travels.  The quality of the bedding is lovely with very soft sheets and pillows, and the cleanliness and hospitality is excellent.  During my next stay in Katmandu, I am not staying anywhere else!

We had a nice stay at Hyatt Kathmandu. Special mention to Drishtee, Shikhar and Front office team for a cake and surprise room decoration on our wedding anniversary. Also, would like to thank Rohit Rawal and Rohit Bhatt from Sesame restaurant for preparing an outside table and arranging a cake on a short notice for our anniversary dinner. Overall great experience. Thanks Hyatt team.
It took ages to get up there on our scooter and it was quite dangerous. All for a view of an overcast sky and a brown dried up lake

It wasn’t called a Monkey Temple for no reason. They were all over! It’s okay, they won’t hurt you unless, of course, if you hurt them first.

Getting up there made you see clearly Kathmandu’s pollution.

Excellent value for money! I travel in KTM for work and it is a great deal for me. The lobby serves for meetings and the interview is excellent in room and lobby. Food is very good and has sufficient variety
Beautiful for boat rides. There is a temple in the center of the lake. The boat rides are reasonable. The boats all have life jackets.

Kathmandu Durbar Square, also known as Hanuman Dhoka Durbar. This ancient palace is located in the center of Kathmandu. It is alos a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This ancient palace lies in the heart of the city. It consists of huge Royal Palace with different temples, inside as well as outside the temple, dating from the 15th to the 18th century. Don't waste your time waiting to see the Kumari.

It was a little crowded when I arrived here, nevertheless, I thought the place is unique and interesting. Temples being rebuilt and others were restored. Although it was overwhelming for me (pigeons everywhere), I was able to see the beauty of this place. It’s best to have a tour guide who will explain to you the history of this place. Lots of nice architecture

Myself and my colleague were totally mesmerized by the experience of staying at Radisson hotel in Kathmandu. Each and everything they do is the best anyone do for you to give that wonderful experience. Food is exceptional and very rarely you get such authentic Indian and western food at one place. Those who love to Gym will be pleasantly surprised with a Hi-Tech gym that's better than most of the Gold Gym's in the big cities. Location of the hotel is just in the center of he city and at walking distance from British and Indian Embassy. Airport pickup and drop service is very good.
A bit disappointed by the square, but still worth the visit. It is in very bad shape after the earthquake, which is an experience to see. We are not super into these temple places, but you might be.
Very nice place to visit and enjoyed  roof top Restaurent overlooking Durbar square. Do not forget to visit Kumari ghar.

Beautiful lake at Phokara city with the backdrop of snow capped mountain. Unfortunately, we were there during winter and it was cloudy and the snow capped mountain were hidden in the clouds. Still, it is a very beautiful lake to stroll along the lakeside. We were told that October is the best time to come with clear visibility of snow capped mountain backdrop, but which also means that the lake will be more crowded and rowdy. Many activities along the lakeside with bar and restaurants and boat ride. The advantage to visit in December is that it is more quiet and relaxing at the lakeside since it is off peak season. Must visit when come to Pokhara!
Nice yes, but not quite Wow. The 1 hour boat ride is around $10. Take it. The scenery is pleasant, but besides the mountains there is not much. A walk along the shore is recommended.

This place should certainly be on your list of places to visit but do expect to see some scaffolding as they are still recovering from the earthquake damage but much has been done and careful photography will get rid of any unsightly scaffolding.

The temples are very beautiful and very huge place. Love the beautiful architecture and made with wooden structures and spent good time with relatives and kids. There were many temples ruined because of the earthquake and are under repair. The but few are repaired and rebuilt.
You must visit this place if you visit Nepal.
I visited around Kathmandu valley. It is one of my experience visits regarding buddha stupas, knowing about buddha culture.

Stayed here for the first time in 2017 and was excited to come back in 2023. It’s as beautiful as ever. Such a special hotel, with lovely friendly staff. Rooms are quiet, clean and very comfortable. I loved the yoga on the rooftop at 8am. Tasty breakfast and lovely menu to order lunch and dinner from. A peaceful garden to sit in after a busy day in Thamel!

Swayambhu Hindu name (Devanagari) an ancient religious site on top of Kathmandu valley toqards west of kathmandu City. A great view of the city from the temple. This is one of the sacred sites of Buddhist pilgrimage and second to Boudya to Tibetean Buddhist.

We enjoyed very much the Or2k restaurants, both in Katmandu and in Pokhara. The food is delicious, prices very reasonable, and you can feel the owner's care about high standards of food quality and higeine. We enjoyed the restaurant so much that we couldnt even try to change it. Home is not for replacement, isn't it? 5 full stars from Eshed family.

To be honest, it's not a world class, state of the art museum but it's a large museum offers a great variety of information about the mountains - from all sorts of ethnic groups, the world's greatest peaks, mountaineers of different nationalities to animals, floral, climate change and the eco system.

The most impressive content to me is the mountaineers who did not climb the peaks for personal achievements but to clean up and carry down all sorts of rubbish left behind by other mountaineers. They are the true heroes of the mountains. I am shocked see the enormous amount of empty oxygen cylinders, cooking gas tans, torn ropes, broken ladders and tools collected. 

Trekkers including myself must be aware that we are part of the culprits who damage the mountains we love.

Had a great experience at Trekkers Home.

For a budget hotel this ticks a lot of boxes, spacious room, clean, desk, ensuite and comfy bed. Great staff and has adjoining restaurant and is in a good location.

Well done
Great stay after a trek, thank you for the upgrade. The spa was quite a treat to have and the pool is good too. Dosa for breakfast was quite good too.

Bad hospitality staff, bad food and bad state of property! It is one of the worst Radisson property I have visited. Staff is not good and is not cooperating and understanding. Breakfast very limited spread and bad quality. Very old rooms.

We stayed at this place during our time at Nepal. The place was alive. There were tourist from all over the world everywhere. The place was full of fancy restaurants and clubs. It was kind of weird to know that it was the only place to open all night long in the Kathmandu. If you are ever visiting to Nepal I highly recommend that you stay here.

Everything was great and I loved staying there If my trip to nepal is in kathmandu in future too then I am happy to stay the same, I ioved it here. the staff of hotel is very good, serve their guests very well and take full care of them.

We were a couple planning to hire a boat for an hour with a boatman. The rates were displayed on a board and the price for our activity was around 550 npr. At the ticket counter though, a rather irate person informed us that our activity wasn't available and that only the numbers 11,12 and 13 on the fare list were available which were all more expensive. We then chose boating from one end of lake to another for 1200 npr. When asked about the time duration, we were told it would take about an hour and half. When we got to the boats, we were informed that we got to pay extra if we desired a covered boat. I'm quite sure the extra money would have been pocketed by the boatman. Since it was an evening, we were happy to chose a boat without a canopy. Halfway towards the tal barahi temple, we were offered to be taken to the middle of the lake if we desired, for an extra 500 npr. The boatman told us that rowing from one end to another, and back to lakeside would take less than half hour. We could extend it by paying the extra 500 npr. We paid it and enjoyed an extra half hour on the beautiful lake. The lake was very picturesque. Not sure if others had such experiences too.
I didn't find this museum that interesting. Right now there are a few posters and that's all. Needs some expansion in the display. I suggest spending the day outdoors.
International Mountain Museum is best Museum among the Pokhara's museum. It was given a great experiment.

I made a reservation for 4 days but left after 2. It was only acceptable and the price was high for this city and neighbourhood standards (it seems that you have to bargain a lot, especially when making reservation from abroad). The other 2 days I stayed in a better hotel for half the price!

We were lucky to see sunset with clear Annapurna range. Local people said that it was the first clear sunset in this season. I recommend to do some homework before to find good viewpoint. We did not know that there are more places and choosed the first one, which was full of tourists.

The complex was badly damaged during the 2015 earthquake. I had a “guide” who didn’t know much about the history or architecture but hinestly, a guide is not needed in Kathmandu. There are many beautiful palaces and public buildings with the unique Nepalese architecture and style and lots of repairs underway. This is a good place to visit and appreciate the history of the city. There is a museum on site with some interesting pieces and photographs.

Wonderful to have a place that showcase all the mountaineering history and cultures in Nepal. We find it very informative and interesting. 

We were there during one of the coldest week in Nepal and the place is cold! Dress warm if you are visiting in the winter.

I stayed with my family for a couple of days. Nice property built up in a very small area. My whole trip to Nepal was going awesome but your staff Sabina Shrestha and Bishal created a scene  and started arguing when my wife asked for A SINGLE PIECE OF BATHURA. On the top, Sabina started saying something stupid in local language to her colleagues regarding us and few were making funny faces. This is the kind of hospitality you are providing, if Bathura is not that much hot as per my wife's taste so asked for a fresh one, wasn't that a big deal. Other Staff Member - Sagar was very polite and smiling always.
"Breathtaking sunrise views over the Annapurna range! A must-visit spot in Pokhara for nature lovers and photographers."

As a tired traveler there are times when you leave things behind in hotels.  As soon as I noticed this and had access to wifi I emailed the Hotel.  They came back to me and said house keeping did not find anything and that they would check again.  No body came back to me so I had to follow up again with no success in finding my missing item- sadly this tainted an otherwise ok stay.  
The Hotel is a nice building & has a nice garden, it's guests were older groups and couples.  Food was good & they have a sister travel agency, so when I booked a hotel transfer the guide also came with the driver and asked whether or not I needed any assistance in planning my trip.

Location: This is nice and quite hotel located slightly off-road of main lakeside. Main lakeside area is 15-20 min walk from this hotel.  

Check in: Check in is quite fast and they will also serve u with welcome drink and fresh cool towels. 

Room: Rooms are clean but bit dark with no sunshine at all. Lighting is dim. All the basic amenities are available in the rooms like mini fridge, tea/coffee maker, safe deposit locker. 

Bathroom: Bathroom is spacious and include all necessary things like shampoo / shower-gel / comb / hand cream / hairdryer. Water pressure is also nice. However there is no bathtub. The shower stall had only a curtain which meant that water would inadvertently splash outside the bath area. There was also no ledge within the shower stall to hold toiletries, and it was a hassle as we had to leave them on the floor and reach down and up to use them. Hot water supply was inconsistent, which meant we were blasted with intermittent streams of cold water and hotwater.

Breakfast: In breakfast we had option of continental and Indian. Because of this, option seemed more but if u are into one type only then its basic. Taste of food is also strictly average. Choices of fruits were also basic (banana, watermelon and papaya only) and there was only 1 fresh juice (watermelon). 

Garden Area and Pool: Greenery is well kept and maintained. Pool is nice but it is relax pool only. Not good for pro swimmers. There is only 1 shower room and 1 toilet in pool area.

Wifi: Wifi is VERY VERY VERY BAD. Its basically useless. Mobile reception is also not very good in this hotel. 

Staff: staffs are polite and courteous. 

Restaurant: Drinks are very overpriced and food is average only.

Checkout: Checkout is also very fast with no hassle.

Above all, it a just above average experience. With a price you pay, you would certainly want more.
Just enjoy one sunny morning (early morning, that is :)) and walk along the shores of the lake. There is a feeling of peace and quietness like nowhere else...
Clean, Close to nature and peacefull place. Away from city chaos on a small hill top. With full lash green background. About 150stairs to climb. And a 50.00NC is the entry ticket.

Rooms are tidy and clean. Professional staff attending your needs ASAP. Highlight of the stay is sumptuous breakfast. Every morning Ms Vanitha at omlette station welcomes guests with most beautiful smile and makes omelettes to the order.
Very scenic, it had lots of rain when we visited,  could not do much, but it looks very inviting, like taking the boat rides and paragliding.

We tried the food there and it was so so... 
I think we didn't make the correct choices on the food, but the place itself was very nice and relaxing, i think it is a place for young people, cause it's cheap and friendly!
Great area for tourist shopping, restaurants, etc. Be careful of the cars and motorbikes though! A bit tight in some places.

I'm travel lover ,I love tourist hub thamel but nowadays no more foreigners, it's like peace thamel waiting for domestic and international tourists by safety mode 
I love peace thamel
This lake is the centre of attraction in Pokhara. I did a boating here, which was a great experience of my life. I would like to recommend every traveler to visit this lake.

Situated in the heart of old Kathmandu city,no tour to Kathmandu is complete without a visit to this complex.
Although damaged by the 2015 earthquake,it is being renovated and restored.
Tucked away in a corner of the square is the famous Freak Street,once a mecca for the hippies.
An open courtyard has a flea market and in the corner is the tourist toilet which is free for use for tourists.
The tourists can also get the entrance ticket(1000 rupees/$10) extended for 3 days at the municipality office next to tourist toilets for free.
The site has 43 temples and a palace all dating from 15th to 18th century except for Kastamandap(under renivation) which predates 12th century.
The house of the living goddess(Kumari/virgin goddess) is also next to the palace.
The complex has a fine display of woodcarving and pagoda architecture.
The palace cortyard is open to tourists and during office hours one can visit and take a picture of the gurkha soldier in his traditional uniform.
The 2nd largest stone image of Nepal is also here(Kal Bhairab) along with the biggest bell of Nepal.
After the visit, one can continue on foot or on a bicycle rickshaw(Rs 350) for a heritage walk through Ason bazaar and end it in Thamel( the tourist hub).

There staff is very bad behaving specially with us Indians. They don't have any system. They harrassed the foreign visiters . Persons at entry named kulbahadur and lady by name of sanjee did so bad bahavior with my father of 73 years heart patient they literally abused us both of them then when I started searching Indian embassy numbers to complain Then they came to know my seriousness meanwhile one old gentelman came and allowed us. But of them were so foolish and errogent people's that wash up hot mind that why we support nepali people's  in our country. Very bad experience with full cheating with foteigners. God should teach them lesson. I want to complaint for them ,where and how it is possible
Great place to spent your evening here , many restaurants , pubs and shopping places . All shops are colorful , friendly shopkeepers and lots of tourist stuffs .

There is just so much to like and recommend about the Kantipur Temple House. We recently stayedthere with our group of volunteer teachers from Australia, and we have stayed there before as a family.
