Everyone loved the ecologiclly responsible focus, the traditional Nepali feel, the beautiful staff and the glorious food.

The Kantipur Temple House has a lovely large block and is handy to everything and yet still quiet and private. We will stay there again on our next visit and we recommend it unconditionally.

Stay at the Kantipur...you will not be disappointed!

First impression of this place is great, with the by now commonplace traditional nepali-style decor. It's conveniently located for Thamel, while still being in a quiet area, and the courtyard is very relaxing. But you can tell very quickly that it's run very shoddily. Staff are grumpy and snobbish. We received a discount on our rooms but weren't told that this meant we weren't entitled to breakfast. Result: Kantupur recouped its discount and we ended up eating a really poor quality, breakfast without realising we were paying through the nose for it. What's more, the breakfast price was quoted to us in dollars when we did eventually find out we were paying for it. This was translated into rupees for our bill and thane converted back in to dollars for us to pay. Of course, conversion 1 was at the hotel's selling rate, and transaction 2 at the buying rate, meaning the hotel made a tidy 20% odd on our slimy sausages. This situation at least did manage to make the otherwise very unhelpful lady at reception slightly embarassed. 

As with all bad management, it's not really the fault of the staff, it rather comes straight down from the top. One of the other breakfast delights was being harassed by the owner to write a review on tripadvisor. Oops. 

If you also have the same problem with the breakfast ripoff, take a few seconds walk down the lane to the delightful ladies at "spicy affair" and have a delicious meal any time of day at a very reasonable price. More importantly, and refreshingly, if you've spent too long at the Kantipur, they're really nice people.
Awesome experience of paragliding. Sailing over the Himalayas and the lake gives an awesome view which is unforgettable

Kathmandu Durbar Square's cultural significance is also obvious from the numerous ancient shrines and temples in and around its premises, including those dedicated to various gods of the Hindu pantheon like Ganesh, Shiva-Parvati, Bhagwati, Saraswoti, Krishna, etc., besides Taleju and Kumari Ghar. Close to the famous square is a temple from which Kathmandu’s name is said to be derived, that is, Kasthamandap Temple. The wood of a single tree is said to have been used to construct it.
I often visit Kathmandu Durbar Square with friends and sometime myself. IT gives more pleasure to see such wonderful archaeology,  architecture, arts in Temple. The story of the temples and gods and goddess. Living Goddess Kumari is the most attraction here. But Nepal Government should do something as the entrance fee is Rs 1000 and there is no much facility rather after the earthquake they see destruction of the temples and building. No tourists are here to see and pay for that. Proper management of the Toilets  and also the local guides who irritates tourists who wants to travel alone. and also the local people who continuously follows the tourists to buy the things. 
but still I recommend every tourist to visit while there are in Kathmandu. Indra Jatra is one of the biggest festival that happens here,   13 Sep. 2019, There is no Entrance fee and all the tourists and local people can enjoy the festival.

I felt very safe walking around Thamel. Very easy to get lost even with a map. No street signs that I could find. I ended up getting very lost with many offering to  help I finally found the tour site on time with some good help

Our visit to Kathmandu was relaxing and the The Radisson Hotel was nestled and ensconed in such a pretty lane from where we could view the picturesque city dotted with millions of little homes and paths which were exceptionally well kept
Much preferred the Boudhanath Stupa. This one is fairly dirty, lots of tourist rubbish left on the floor. The monkeys are pretty funny though.

Kantipur temple house staff made me feel right at home by providing homely touches like hot water hotties at nighttime and a smile and a hot chai at breakfast. The staff were like family and made our group feel so safe and welcome. There is no other place in Kathmandu like it. With the big open , green courtyard, it was the perfect place to relax after a big day exploring.

a local museum, went there with our guide. Not very interesting, too many students there, and they even wanted to take pictures with us!... Watched their proudly introducted video about the treck to Base Camp - boring video. Won't go there if we knew what's waiting for us.
This is really a boring place. If you are young then go here.....nothing special...just bunch of photos which u can see from internet....so don't waste your time there

OR2K is easily the best vegetarian/vegan restaurant in pokhara.
The menu is extensive and everything we had was delicious, the seating arrangements are quirky but appealing and you get an amazing view over lake phewa.
Their fresh mint lemonade is probably one of the most refreshing drinks I've ever had!
Even my meat eating friends were keen to revisit this place!

We returned at Kantipur Temple House because the first time we had a great experience , three years ago.
We stayed there for a total of 7 nights (split between the beginning of the trip and after the end of Nepal tour). Though obviously we were regular customers, they decided to try to cheat us for 300$!!! We are a young couple,  from an outside sight we may look unwary but we are experienced travelers, especially in Asia.
We had booked through our travel agency, that had to deal with the payment, since we had already paid them the full amount of the stay. Two days before our return home, they began asking us to pay for the last three nights, because they claimed that the agency had said we had paid through them only the first stay and not the second one. After a full day spent explaining that it was not so and insisting that they should contact the agency (we did try it but we did not talk to our referent) we found that they never called the agency but that this was a staging set up to try ti rob the tourists. We just got out of this situation by showing the voucher of bookings and payments.
The hotel, apart from notable defects due to eco friendly policy which, although admirable, greatly damages the quality of the service (no air conditioning but noisy fan, no soap for shower or shampoo but only a handsoap) in general it's a nice place, still very expensive for Kathmandu standards. The experience would have been positive if there hadn't been repeated attempts of fraud (the other one happened on our arrival in Nepal, although we had paid for the deluxe room, an ancient style room with view of the yard, they tried to give us a standard room, shabby compared to the price, with view to nearby houses and two single beds).

Ther mountain museum is informative, whimsical and beautifully laid out. The 20 min movie gives a great overview of Nepal's mountains and its people as well as other mountain ranges world wide. Displays are well curated, fromn local costumes and customs to tectonic plates and seismology.

Pokhara airport closure due to bad weather meant we had to juggle our travel schedule, and wanted to bring our booking at Temple Tree a day forward. Staff and management refused to assist, despite having rooms available. We were told we could only buy an additional night, but not change existing booking. We were directed to speak to hotel manager directly, though manager failed to appear after a 15 minute wait as was "busy in a staff meeting". 
Staff were uninterested and arrogant. Need to work much harder at guest relations. We took our business elsewhere.

It is here that some public animal sacrifices are made during the Hindu festival Dashain, the most important festival of the year to the Nepalese. If you check with the locals, they can give the particular times and places for the year. However, some sacrifices are not "scheduled," like the one we saw by providence. Quite an experience for a Westerner!

We went with a group of friends and a toddler. the hospitality was great, very friendly staffs, amazing breakfast spread and the rooms were very comfortable. Dips in the pool and some refreshing drinks from the bar were some of the highlights of the stay here

In a good location. Great breakfast. Nice clean rooms although air con in the rooms don’t work very well. Great spa. The massages and hair salon are particularly good. Had the best and cheapest hair cut I’ve ever had. The hairdresser was extremely good.

BED BUGS. Absolutely awful. 

The rooms themselves are very run down, cockroaches and holes in the wall. Windows that don't shut. The amenities provided barely work, our friends rooms fan was barely holding onto the ceiling. 

Our headboard was infested with bed bugs, all crawling all over the walls. 

We were offered a new room but unable to give refund. 

A real shame for backpackers who now need to sort new belongings. 

Unsure how they have such good reviews. Also tried the restaurant downstairs twice. First time was lovely second time I would not go back.

The hotel is now very large thanks to the addition of a new wing. Alas the full choice of restaurants is only available in the older part. The rooms are spacious and the bed comfortable. The large wetroom with rain shower is a huge plus point. Food is great too. You can avoid expensive meat dishes and have some vegetables cooked in an Indian/Nepalese way.
Cousin of the Kathmandu branch.Good middle-eastern and lebanese food with very nice views of the lake.

Was an excellent experience continued till the fourth time. Special thanks to Mr. Yusuph and Ms. Rakriti for their excellent customer service and coordination. The amenities are excellent and in a perfect ambience

This is not a 5 star prooerty. It has beautiful large grounds but the furnishings are old. Furniture and decor in rooms are old and creaky, carpets were dirty and aged. The staff is wonderful and caring. Food is average.

We were told major renovations are underway. Let's hope they bring it close to hyatt standards.
Very good experience. Amazing facilities. Food and drinks are amazing. All the staffs are very supportive. The swimming pool is very nice safe for kids too.

It was a good experience. Staff was hospitable and very attentive to the requests and issues of guests. Food quality was also upto the mark. Rooms were tidy ane well maintained. Only i would like to mention that there should have been enough lights in room

We were assisted by Ayushma. Excellent hospitality. She was very thorough in explaining all the details of the facilities and amenities available. The ambience, rooms, were excellent. Will definitely come back again.

We stayed at the Radisson at both the beginning and the end of our Nepal travels in December. The location is good, near the old palace and with several good restaurants a few steps away. The staff was uniformly wonderful. A pre-trip inquiry email was answered promptly in perfect English.

Breakfast was varied and of quality, though the pastries and breads were often a bit stale, noting I found that the case everywhere we visited in Nepal. Good beds. Not quiet sleeping, with barking dogs in the direction we faced, loud street noises and weddings in other directions. Recommend staying in the new building, away from the wedding celebrations. 

We found our room on the third floor too warm for comfort, my guess about 79 degrees. We were told they heated the first 3 floors, and so requested a move upwards, after which we were quite comfortable.

Crossing the street between the two buildings requires caution. Shower has no grab bars and slippery floor. Reliable internet with decent bandwidth, though one friend's room had poor service. 

All said I would stay here again.

Shared the combo platter, excellent value, variety and quality and the two of us did not leave hungry. Very hip and young crowd and very chilled out atmosphere. Internet was slow when we were there, but you could easily pass a few hours here in comfort.
The food was delicious the service was very good very kind people And we had wonderfull stay to relax And the Spa massage was great
Interesting and informative visit - my friends and I spent a good afternoon there and even missed lunch as we lost track of time! Remember to find the Yeti...

You sort of have to go on a boat ride on Fewa Lake if you stay in Pokhara and if the weather is nice you probably have a beautiful view of the mountains. However, we had overcast skies, a babbling oarsman who seemed to be thinking of nothing but his tip, the lake was crowded and the small temple island in the middle was very dirty, very crowded and not at all impressive. Maybe our expectations were too high, but honestly we had better views (with or without clouds) walking around the lake and enjoying the tranquility. Of all the places we visited in Nepal, this was the only time I felt we had walked into a tourist trap. Do it if you have plenty of time, but otherwise consider giving it a miss.

The hotel has a beautiful garden in the centre of a very cramped location of Thamel, Kathmandu. The room are ok with hot water and a AC heating system during winter. However, I've had a very mixed service experience from the staff. 

Once I was served a foul tasting lemonade at the garden restaurant which the waiter kept arguing strongly to be a good one. 

Then I ordered fried rice I'm my room which was half cooked. After getting my lunch spoiled I asked them to take it away and cancel it but they still billed it on my check out. Again I was argued with at the reception that I must pay for the fried rice since I signed on the invoice. I told them I do not know of any hotel in the world where you taste the food first before signing in your room but they kept insisting. Anyway they didn't charge me later but it was not a pleasant experience departing.

Cool place to chill, amazing view to the lake fresh quality food 
We had a really nice time here.
Staff is friendly but needs more focus..
We were lucky with the sunrise views. The experience was brilliant. The tower gets crowded so get there early to grab a spot especially if you have a tripod for your camera.

This Durbar square was hit hard by the 2016 earthquake and is now being restored.
It is well worth a trip to walk amongst this ancient square and see daily life.

Beauty of nature at its best. While boating you can get a glimpse of Annapurna and fish tail peaks. At centre of Lake there is a temple. Crystal clear water and picturesque. You can get a small boat and you have a choice to row it urself. There are larger boats also which you can rent. Boats can be rented for a day also.

This hotel was absolutely 'not value for money'. I paid around 200 USD per night without breakfast. The location was not that convenient. 
The property is nice and big, but it became too shabby and the food was not up to the mark.

From check in to check out ,the facilities were excellent.Breakfast buffet was delicious and full of varieties..
Everything we enjoyed ,the only thing I miss in the hotel is the kids play area like billiards room,etc... otherwise just awesome...will definitely recommend this to others.

The Durbar square of Kathmandu contains 48 temples the most famous of which houses the Kumari or the Living Goddess. Kindly take a guide to know the historical significance of the various temples. There is an entry fee to this place and should take about one hour.

Most of the sites are still under restoration due to damage from massive earthquake in 2015. Still, we were able to see a small part of the architecture with interesting details of wood carvings and patterns. There were so many pigeons at the square and many locals were sitting around to chit chat and relax. One of the meeting point for the locals. There is also public toilet provided for tourists. We went into the Kumari Ghar where is the residence of the living goddess in Nepal. We saw Royal Kumari in two occasions during our visit to Nepal. Kumari is a prepubescent girl selected, which the locals believe that Kumari is the reincarnation of Goddess Taleju based on Hinduism. No photo taking of Kumari is allowed. All the tourists greeted her “Namaste” upon her appearance at the window from the 2nd floor and tourists were standing at the ground floor court yard. It was a very interesting cultural experiences with a surroundings of stunning architectural structures. Reason to rate 4 out of 5 is that it would be perfect (5 out of 5) if we could visit the entire square plus the Taleju temple which can only be done when the sites are fully restored. It is also considered one of the endangered world heritage under the threats of earthquake. So, it is a must do when visiting Kathmandu!!!

Very nice place to stay in pokhara with Lakeview in a waterfront resort and the staff of restaurants is so helpful specially nabina binita and sante sanam sabina parmila chij jevan thank you for your lovely words and friendly behaviour...
Nice view of Himalayan ranges especially at the time of sunrise and sunset as well. Remember you have climb some stairs for the perfect view.

I had the pleasure of visiting this hotel. It is located off the beaten track, close to the lake. It leads to the rocky road from Pokhara. At night it's very dark - if someone wants to go into town in the evening, I advise you to take back the flashlight. The hotel rooms are large, but very modest. Especially the bathroom. It's clean, but far from the generally accepted standard of hotel in the world-class hotels. The most pleasant place in the hotel's lobby, bar and restaurant all in one. The large pool in front of the hotel. With regard to the SPA, this is a massage parlor, outside the hotel, does not belong to the hotel. Very unpretentious and only open until 20:00. In my opinion one of the best hotels in Pokhara. If you improved standard of the rooms and bathrooms - the hotel in my opinion is a good chance to be No. 1 in Pokhara.

Good place for holiday, fresh air nice view of mountains. Just love lakeside of Pokhara!! They have bungee jump, paragliding, and etc. from Pokhara there are so many beautiful places that you can visit easily.
the food was very nice and tasty and the best i think room very nice and the place is very quite and beautiful we really loved the swimming pool and the hottub too

The lake gets busy during the day. But if you want to avoid the crowds,  go there early morning like what we did.  Just sitting still on the side and staring at the lake gave me a sense of peace and serenity.

Amazing experience visiting Nepal specially Pokhara , beautiful valley located in Western part of Nepal. The main beauty was the vibrant environment of Lake side with the Phewa Lake view and mountain view together . Also amazing street food available across the footpath.

The square was severely damaged during the 2015 and in 2018 you can still see the damage. Most remaining building are still hidden by scaffolding. And even though you have to pay an entrance fee you still get harassed and besieged by hawkers, touts trying to sell you trinkets, tours restaurant visits etc. Heavily disappointed. Give it another 5 years and hopefully the square will be restored in all its glory by then

visited recently with friends. Found next to professional Management with staffs. Superb front, perfectly treat while we were at this beautiful place. Healthy and many choice of breakfast. swimming pool, garden is beautiful. We didn't try spa. Thanks to Mr. Rimal to make our experience awesome by professional. Will comeback again. Thanks to your entire staff.

Excellent Exprience in Temple Tree Resort.
Excellent Food, the service were Excellent. The staff uis very cooprative. Ayushma was very nice.
Best Swimming Pool and Jacuzzi we our family enjyed it very much 
Best Location in the town lake was near by

My wife and I just spent four days here. It's quite impressive to look at and very large,consisting of several buildings. The staff were split into two catorgaries. Those who were polite and helpful and those that weren't interested. We experienced both, but luckily none effected the stay. Cleanliness was a bit lacking and this was a concern. Overall, by Kathmandu standards, it was ok, but could have been better for an international hotel. WE used the Tibet hotel next door most of the time, where staff where staff were more professional, the hotel was cleaner and the facilities better suited. Cheaper also. Would definitely use the Tibet ne t time, but don't let that put you off the Raddison. It's adequate.

Thamel is in the heart of kathmandu...
Very much tourist area with amazings restaurants and hotels..
We had nice and pleasant stay at temple tree and food was awesome service was superb. Location was convinent too. Thank you Ayushma specially.

I dont have anything against paying visitors fee - and I understand tourists should pay more than locals but i dont understand why SAARC tourists pay less... 

And still after you paid you are still sort of mistrusted youve paid. That sort of actually bad manners make you feel unwelcome.

However. The museum is actually pretty ok with some sort of storytelling explaining the nations history.  Well worth a visit.

This place is steeped in history even though the maintenance and renovation process should have been speedier and better. There could have been English nameplates and brief descriptions to make the international visitors understand the importance of each building. One should hire one of the tourist guides who roam around and haggle by proposing a diverse range of fees for providing a guided tour. These are lovely places which could be better organized by an authority and leadership with some sophistication, vision and imagination.

It was good to see the culture monuments but after looking at it I really just wanted to leave. There were many feral dogs everywhere biting and attacking each other which just made me nervous. But thats what to expect in Kathmandu. The monkeys were much of the same. It just wasn't my thing.

Dhan Singh Bhandari 

He is very friendly, helpingfull, humble and very do his best to fulfill our need. Im very honour to say thank you and much appreciated to him too serve me during my stay at RADISSON HOTEL room216.

It's said that Monkey Temple (another name of this temple) is a must-visited place in Kathmandu. If you really have a lot of free time, you can try. But if you do not, you should not. The temple is messy with lots of small shop vendors along the way up. It smells. It's not clean. If you're not lucky, the view to the city from the temple is foggy and you can't see anything clear.

Its a amazing hotel. I chose this hotel in the first place by the looks. I love that it looks like a temple. It had a good appearance. For me this was the best looking hotel in Kathmandu and around. 
I also saw like radisson blu from the inside and so on but just standard this is way more special and gives you more Nepal vibes. 
The staff was great made me feel welcome right away. 
Especially Sajana and Suman. 
They really helped me with making a travelplan like where to go and what best to do. 
Without them I wouldnt have visited a amazing place like Namo buddha. 
Also pick up from airport was a possiblity and early check in. 
The people working at the breakfast / dinner were also very nice! 
Actually everybody was kind here. 
The only thing missing for me was the yoga lessons who wouldnt there because of not so much tourist this time but I come back later this year so will catch up on that! 
Also great working WIFI didnt fail on me once.
Just make sure to bring your own showergel,bodylotion etc since this is a eco friendly hotel they dont have them in the shower , but its a good thing another thing I like about this hotel. The rooms looked also like a temple room. Atleast the one I got dont know about the others ofcourse. Also big bed. All was just perfect , when Im back in Nepal I will chose this hotel again for the 100%.
It was worth walking up all the steps to walk around this temple.  The views over Kathmandu as the sun was setting was really good too!

This is a historical, cultural and religious complex  in Kathmandu  consisting of temples, shrines and monuments that are key part of Nepalese identity. The site is old dating as far back as the 13th century. Many buildings are very interesting and historical. One of them is the palace of the current living Kumari Goddess. We happen to see her at 4:30 from her balcony “audience” inside her garden. 
 The square is very busy, a bit dirty and often times chaotic. Tickets for foreigners are 1000 NR for the day. You probably will need a guide since there is no signage or sparse literature to explain the sites. Personally, I found the Durbar Squares at Patan and Bhaktapur to be more interesting and pleasanter to visit. But this one should be visited nevertheless.

The Alfredo and pesto pasta really impressed me. Price is fair and
Atmosphere was pretty good. However, would be better if the seating area is more spaced out. A little too cramp for my liking.

This is probably my favorite restaurant in Pokhara.  And Kathmandu.  So healthy, the menu has a huge variety of cuisines to choose from, you can make substitutions as you like, the food is FRESH, and they give you adequate servings of vegetables (as opposed to what passes as normalcy i.e. two spoonfuls of veggies and a mountain of rice).  Try the buckwheat rotis.  I like them more than normal rotis.  The shakshuka is to die for, as is the Mediterranean combo platter.  Coffee and espresso are next level.  A+ ambiance.  The view from the terrace or inside the dining room is first class.  The inside looks and feels very spacious and airy as one side is completely open facing the lake.
I couldn't have spent a better Christmas Morning than this. Seeing the sun creep up and sprinkle the mountains with gold. I felt great for the rest of the day!

Monkey Temple, is a must-visit site in Kathmandu. The ancient religious monument features intricate architecture, colorful paintings, and stunning panoramic views. The presence of playful monkeys adds to the charm of the place. The serene atmosphere offers a chance for reflection and introspection, making it a remarkable and peaceful experience.
The Kasta Mandap Temple, and the Kumari, the little girl treated as a living goddess (in our opinion she lives in a prison). Lots of exotic pics to take!

We had 3 nights in the place and everything just about passed muster.
Room was just comfortable, breakfast was just eatable and the spa was just passable. All in all a very average hotel.
A special thanks to Sagun, a great member of staff who deserves to work in a much better hotel.

OK, so maybe I'm spoiled after 15 years of living and traveling in Asia, but this place, in my book, needs to work harder on the services they provide. The front desk staff isn't unfriendly, but lacks verbal communications skills. No questions asked on room details, such as king size bed (which booked) or twin share, which they gave us. Or preference for "noisy" room (facing the pool on a weekend with lots of families there) or quite room (away from the pool); a simple check in script for front end staff to follow would make the experience so much better. 
Hotel building and lay out is good, with a European rustic feel to it, and nice pool (with too much chlorine); why then be so lazy on the gardening side? 
In room wifi was just so slow; we got better wifi while hiking in a 2 star hostel; why can they not provide the same? 
Hotel has potential, but I think needs to feel more competition to make it work harder to keep its services top notch and pay attention to detail. 
Anyway maybe I'm just complaining a bit because my expectations relate back to the price I paid, I think a 100+ dollar hotel room in a remote location in Nepal should provide more than what I got.
I went with friends, they recommended me for a good food. I had Falafel there, which was very nice, probably good Falafel I Pokhara. and nice seating spot. with Fewalake view.

Characterless hotel in nice location a little bit out of town. Modern and clean with a bath 😊. Got shuttle bus into town and booked with driver to be picked up with last shuttle of evening. It didn't turn up. Rang the hotel who eventually agreed to send the bus. An hour later than original time.  No apology given. As we were leaving early we asked for a takeout breakfast to include some boiled eggs - sadly there were no eggs.
Not impressed. 
Did have a pool next to the car park which locals could buy membership to use. Great for locals but made it very noisy with lots of families using it.  
Wouldn't stay here again

The monkey temple is charming for several reasons. Yes, there are monkeys everywhere. It’s on a hill overlooking the city, and it is quite picturesque. Worth an hour to walk around and enjoy. I feel like going in the early morning before it gets too hot is best.

we were told that the climb to Sarangkot would take 2 hours. We set off and the rain poured down making it tricky underfoot. The climb I would consider to be  for fit, experienced hill walkers. It was uphill all the way and I consider myself fir but it took us 5 hours. We went to watch the sunrise but obviously the rain was too much. You can take the same route down but if wet it is very slippy and precarious in places. there is a longer route which could take another 5 hours. we opted for a taxi which belonged to the hotel and cost very little. Our agent would have charged us £50

The visit was beneficial for us to appreciate Himalaya more. It is not fancy and the displays are very basic except those that are funded by external agencies however other than information we don't expect much when visiting a museum in Nepal.

Remember that you can take solo boat or in group for hire. You may add your Vape or some cigarette in pocket(in case of smokers) so that you won't get disappointed later on. You can hire boat for definite time interval such as 1 hr, 2 hr etc. Need to get ticket from counter situated on the very left side of entry gate near TalBarahi Temple. If you have time then hire it for 2 hours, have some good music on and enjoy the view. 

Cheers !
Very active tourist district in Kathmandu. Plenty of hotels, shops, restaurants and bars to keep your attention. Very walkable unmarked streets that you can meander for hours.
after 2015 earthquake, most of buildings colapsed and there is not so much to see excepting  Kumari Bahal and Taleju Temple

They have some nice salads and veg dishes here. Service was pretty neutral, one get much more attentive staff elsewhere. Enviroment lacking because people remove their shoes and live them in the dining room. Smelly at best

We booked this hotel last minute for new years eve and the manager quiet humbly gave us 3 rooms, well appreciated. But when we arrived at the hotel they made excuses that 'we had booked for the next day and din't have any rooms'! Also, we had called them in the morning(about 5 times) to make sure if all the rooms were done, but no body cared to answer the phone. There was no email confirmation, nothing ! Quiet mismanaged! 
We reached the hotel at around 2 pm (post the check-in time), and they told us to wait in one of the rooms while our other rooms were getting ready!
 According to them all the rooms were deluxe but to our  realisation, we din't find them up to the mark at all. The room they gave us was small, at the back of the hotel, with small single beds and a toilet without a latch. After waiting for an hour and more, without any response, we had to literally go and fight with the staff and finally they sorted us out. I must say the staff was quiet un-cooperative and laid back. 
Coming to the good side, the other rooms they put us into were fine and spacious. There was TV with good variety of channels, they had a heater in the room and hot water for shower. Breakfast was alright. The view from the terrace was beautiful. 
All in all I would rate this hotel an average. If the staff was a little more effective, they would fetch more points ! Take a chance, if you're staying in here!

Nice place to stay; spacious hotel room, good work of waste water treatment on-site. All team members are kind and supportive. Trainee named Sabina serviced us during breakfast, she is humble and genuine. We will definitely visit this place again. Thank you.

Sacred place but dirty, filthy. Honestly didn't feel pristine & tranquil which should have been. We had heard a lot about this famous old temple but due to negligence & lack f awareness I lost my interest.

A good place to stay especially with family and for business purposes as well. The location and view from the hotel is excellent. The hotel and it's it's cleanliness are well maintained. Only thing required is to improve the variety of meals for vegetarians.
Staff are great very helpful. Location is a quiet area . Complete toiletries , clean room and bathroom .
The hotel feels very authentic.  The food served in the hotel was very good.  Especially Padam Singh Sitoli’s beetroot, carrot Naan was so delicious.

I will highly recommend for stay if you need to stay in Kathmandu for your work/ vacation/ leisure work. Feel the essence of high end hospitality. Love to stay with family. Thumbs up for the hospitality guys..keep it up.

Beautiful location with scenic beauty and wonderful atmosphere.  Room was spacious with lake view. Room service was adequate. Sabina and Binita were very cordial and supportive in providing assistancei  the restaurant.

We took a taxi from our hotel to this museum since it is located in a non-touristy neighborhood. Admission for foreigners was 750 rupees. We began our visit by watching a 15+ minute video (in English) that was interested at times, but could easily be skipped if you don't have the time.  All exhibits were explained in English with a good number also in Nepali. Some sections of the museum interested us, but others did not.

How is it even possible to charge this much for VEGETARIAN?! 

Bloody insane. Good food I guess, but the price is ridiculous.

Pokhara is a very touristy place with lots of different kinds of eating joints. OR2K stands out for being somewhat different. It is an Israeli restaurant and I do not know what exactly that means, but it does serve vegetarian and vegan options in a country where people eat a lot of meat.

One climbs up two flights of stairs on a busy side-street to get to this restaurant. Seating is available under the open skies on the terrace with a view of the Phewa Tal or Lake, or indoors at a proper table and chair or on the ground with your shoes off: basically, to get a relaxed feel.

The breakfast options are varied, different kinds of eggs along with cheese and salads; and for dinner there are interesting soups, one of which is called the Budha Bowl, which we tried. It was really good. I asked for rum and a diet coke or pepsi, but they said they do not keep diet sodas, I wonder why.

Service is somewhat laid back, I suppose because they feel that you should take your time while at the restaurant, but if you are in a hurry, I reckon this place is best avoided.

I was somewhat surprised when they would not accept the Indian Rs.500 currency notes; we had been to the interiors of Nepal and had paid our bills with 500 rupee notes without a problem. It is one of those management policies that did not make any sense.

So, while the food and ambience is good, the laid back attitude of the staff and the currency acceptance policy were irritants. End of the day, it is really your choice, what you expect from a place, and what you are willing to accept.

Thamel was a busy tourist area of Kathmandu. Many hotels, restaurants and tons of shops. Lots of shops to get trekking supplies. Main area is pedestrianised, but motor bikes and rickshaws do come through. What was not nice was all the local spitting in the street, You had to watch where you were walking.

Another country with another communist disaster story. The people's roads aren't maintained by their comrades in the communist party, so the dust is everywhere. Everyone is coughing, hocking up phlegm, squinting and there is a thick dust cloud that won't leave.
This is a must visit attraction in pokhara as it has beautiful view and great boat ride . They offer different prices for different boats and timing is from 9am to 6 pm in evening.
if u come to kathmandu ,you have to visit this place .in this place in find peace in my soul.i go there

The local people we met in Sarangkot were very personable and engaging. Great view of the Annapurna.   We went up twice from Pokhara.  The gift of a clear day gives one an awesome view.  Our sunrise view was less clear but still worth the climb up to the top. It is delightful to watch the para-gliders and enjoy local foods.

This is a most visit place in Pokhara for everyone to know more about mountains and people living in mountain around the world. 
I have been here many times. The area is wide with greenery and beautiful. You can try climbing the rocky white mountain at the garden or take pic by the yak in front of the museum.

Beautiful lake with a really nice walkway on the South end. Many vendors selling local trinkets along with numerous great restaurants. Nice to grab a Nepal Ice and watch the sun set over the mountains. Some what the hub of Pokhara. Be a lite nicer if they could keep the local garbage out of the lake. Take a boat and paddle around the lake . Pay a few dollars more and someone will paddle for you

My own visit to Swayambhunath in 2023 was a memorable experience shared with friends, as we marveled at the beauty of the architecture, observed the playful monkeys, and took in the majestic views of the Kathmandu Valley. It was a moment of connection with both the rich cultural heritage of Nepal and the enduring wisdom of Buddhist teachings.

One of the most unsatisfying check in ever in  my entire hotel stay. Worst starting in beginning of my stayâ?¦.,,, unworkable tv though it was fix after a hour of requestâ?¦,, baby cockroach found around the tv areaâ?¦,, dining experience was so bias with minutes waiting for fnb members to be attendedâ?¦.,,quality of food though..,, lack of quality services..,

Was greeted by a very unfriendly gatekeeper asking thousands of question even before entering the premises . Questions like if you have booked a room and for when have u booked it. Guess it was a hotel I was entering that too with a restaurant , made me feel as though I was trying to tress pass with suitcases and bags. Had a room booked for 2 adults from a travel website which clearly showed 2 single beds however on reaching the hotel , the front desk staff including the manager made us pay $10 extra as they mentioned it only listed a single person ( 2 single bed for a single person). They wouldn't agree and they made us pay even before we enter our room or were allocated a room. Next day , I showed him on his face by booking room for additional day selecting the desired option ( 2 Adults) and then the reply I got was " they will get it checked ". Anytime u go front desk , they first will ask u too pay if there is anything due .... Right away , regardless even if ur staying for couple of days more. 
Rooms were pathetic with the below guidelines:

a. No food in room
b. No guest in room

Seriously , felt I was staying in a PG. 

When asked for taxi to front desk for airport  , I was asked to go talk to the drivers and have it arranged myself. It's how pathetic the front desk really was including the managers . 

On the flip side the restaurant staff were very polite . 

The hotel exterior is great but the management and the rooms are pathetic .

Not a good deal....thanks to the management who take themselves as govt employees .

Hotel was picturesque, set in tranquil grounds with lovely landscaping. Location is good, within walking distance to shops, restaurants and the lake. Hotel staff was The hotel is picturesque and set in a lovely landscaped garden. Location was convenient, within walking distance to the lake, shops and restaurants. Service staff was generally polite, albeit in a "business-like" manner. Our rooms were clean and had a nice patio.

However, there are some issues that the hotel needs to improve on. Electricity was disrupted intermittently throughout the day, which was inconvenient. The shower stall had only a curtain which meant that water would inadvertently splash outside the bath area. There was also no ledge within the shower stall to hold our toiletries, and it was a hassle as we had to leave them on the floor and reach down and up to use them. Hot water supply was inconsistent, which meant we were blasted with intermittent streams of cold water - not very comfortable at all.

We spent 4 hours at the spa. The masseuses work very hard and tried their best. The body and leg massages were good, but the facial was a disappointment as the masseuses were clearly untrained in this area. The facial treatments were quite rough with lots of vigorous tugging and rubbing - not relaxing at all and probably added some wrinkles to our skin. It was also quite noisy, with the phone ringing frequently and the receptionist attending to guests and talking loudly.

Upon checkout and on our way to the airport, our driver stopped suddenly to take a call from housekeeping. He passed the phone to us, and the housekeeper insisted that we had damaged a towel with hair dye and demanded that we pay 900 rupees to the driver. I explained that my travelling companion's hair dye ran because of the hair oil that the masseuse had used during the hair massage treatment at their spa. Hence we should not be made liable for the damage. We told them that a simple bleaching will remove the dye from the towel. However, the hotel insisted that we  pay for it. 900 rupees (equivalent to USD8) is an exorbitant sum just to bleach a towel. This unreasonable demand marred our stay, and left a bad impression of the hotel.

Overall, while the stay was adequately comfortable, the service level needs to be reviewed and improved upon.

while booking this resort I thought that it would be the best in pokhra. that's why I paid so much money. but it was a waste of money. the resort is ordinary only. washrooms are average. highly disappointed. food is good.

The monkey temple will be a wonderful place to visit once the renovation and rebuilding work is complete, at present it’s a building site with hidden dangers.  Probably the one think that made me detest the place, was the never ending circle of hawkers and traders who just wouldn’t go away; someone has to sort this out as the experience was both annoying and frustrating.  Such a beautiful place being defiled and degraded by trash sales people.

Very busy and dirty.
Most of the square is still in repair from the eartquake in 2014
It' s overrated and spoiled.

We had arranged the booking for 5 days over the phone and arrived after midnight.  If we had arrived at a more civilized time we would not have stayed there for even one night. They showed us 3 rooms - the bathrooms were filthy. We chose the least terrible room. We had no choice but to stay one night as we had arrived so late. The shower was not usable as there was no cold water- the hot was scalding. They charged us $30 USD for the night. The next day we walked up the street and found a modern hotel- spotlessly clean, well run very friendly for 40 USD. The contrast was amazing.

Honestly to say ,nothing impressive.
Don’t recommend at all ! Nothing around,nothing to do ,nothing to see . You drive catamaran ,which is so so slowly.
Don’t bank on the weather being clear enough to see the Annapurna Range.  T is more likely Oct - Dec then any other time of year.

Lovely place , centrally located with swimming pool on higher floor. Try to book the higher floor. courteous staff. Breakfast spread is pretty good to suit every age group. There are shops close by to do last minute shopping.

Nepal's mountains are some of the most famous and spectacular in the world.  With so many visitors coming to Nepal to explore the amazing ranges, it's nice to have a place to visit to learn more about their history.  

The museum is informative, with information scattered throughout in both Nepali and English. While the building and exhibits look somewhat dated, they're still fascinating.

It's one of the few tourist attractions I've visited where I've felt like the written supporting materials are adequate and value adding.  

I went along expecting to be there for an hour, but was happily there for more than two. 

One of the most interesting tourist attractions in either Pokhara or Kathmandu, in my opinion.

All the food is fresh and tasty. Many many great vegetarian options. The coffee is great. Fun and relaxing vibes. The service is fast and the people are very nice. We had breakfast lunch and dinner here. Would highly recommend.

The museum is a short taxi ride from the center, and well worth the visit. Set in beautiful gardens with views, and adjoining a monastery. Very informative and spacious, although a bit dated by modern standards, for Nepal this is an achievement! You should plan for  2-3 hours there. Good descriptions in English, lots of artifacts and pictures from expeditions, all about the mountains, geology, glaciation, plus river ecosystems and climate change problems.

I booked this hotel from a recommendation that I received from friends. We had a split stay, the first being overnight and the second being 3 nights.

The first night was fine, apart from there being not elevator and having to walk 5 flights of stairs, the rest was okay.

On the second stay, we were on the 4th floor and all our rooms smelled terrible, the bathrooms were not in a good condition, the towels were dirty and my doona had a spec of dried blood on it. The linen didn't fit the bed properly either.

The staff were not very helpful and friendly, there were some exceptions - but overall I wasn't impressed.

The positive of this hotel is the location and interesting history, but standards have dropped.

When I go back to Kathmandu I won't be staying there.

A fantastic place to visit. Palaces, Pagodas, Stupas and Temples. Built in different times throughout the history and telling multiple stories... until the latest tragic royal one that ended the monarchy in Nepal. Too bad there was so much damage done in the 2015 earthquake. Almost all structures are under construction. Hope they will be restored to their original glory soon.

My husband and I stayed here for a long weekend in April 2010.  The place was packed full of charm and the staff were delightful.  The generator wasn't great but the sporadic electricity is something you just have to accept if staying at a budget hotel in Kathmandu.  

The location was perfect as we were able to walk to most of the major signseeing spots and the Greater Thamal area.

I left this restaurant feeling embarrassed and humiliated without even trying the food.

I arrived and asked to be seated anywhere on the cushion area (a chilled area with lots of space. It has a casual vibe and it is common for persons, solo or in groups,  to sit here and relax). I sat in an area on the cushions and a staff member told me that it had been reserved. He said that the reservation for the entire area had been made over the phone and the customers would arrive in 10 minutes.

I waited for 10 minutes and eventually more space freed up on the cushioned area after a group had left. I sat down, and immediately a waiter placed a reserved sign on the table (which I thought was strange after a group had just left). He then said the entire space was reserved and I must wait somewhere else. I asked him if the table had been reserved by phone, and he confirmed several times that it had been.

Shortly after a group sat down in the same area. I asked them if they had reserved and they said that they had not and had just walked in.

I spoke with the member of staff about this and instead of apologising he just spoke in nepali to another waiter and ignored me.

I find this very unfortunate and will not be returning to Or2k again.

Summary: do not turn up to or2k if you are solo.

Good location, excellent staff, great eateries around hotel, exciting breakfasts included in hotel rates.  Based on corporate agreement or just good faith, hotel provided me free airport transfers and transfers to my office everyday.
Enjoyed the place seeing the people from different countries and many handicrafts of the people and got a great experience with different club and bar

I stayed in hotel for 5 days. I am pure vegetarian and got many options in it. 
Connecting road leading to the hotel is narrow and gets congested sometimes. 
Due to my busy schedule I could not enjoy other facilities like club, etc. but all are well known and famous.

Fewa lake

Phewa Lake is the 2nd largest in Nepal and It is the only Lake in Nepal to have a temple “Tal Barahi Temple “ at
the central part of lake. 

It is amazing view when you can see lake, big mountains around. It could be justmore friendly for people, more paths for either.

We hired a paddle boat for 2 hours from Fewa BoatAssociation.After spending 30 min we reached Tal barahi.taking some nice picture we go to the main part of Phewa lake.

Once you reach Pokhara city, Phewa lake is a mustsee. Especially in the evening sitting next to the Lakeand watching sundown was an amazing experience. Do it atleast once!
The Whole Management Team Were So Incredibly Welcoming. They Were Supportive Throughout My Family Stay Making The Tours Experience Truly Memorable And Enjoyable.
An Amazing temple located in  central kathmandu. Everyone must visit while in Kathmandu. You can also see the mountain.
I love the place. Its very close from the lakeside city and can see most amazing view with sunrise as well as mountains.
Lots of constructions going on around the temple, very dusty and noise pollution. as the temple is very old its very divine.

This was my third stay at Kantipur Temple House.  I returned to Nepal after 10 years and wanted to stay here again due its central location, great customer service and charming well accommodated rooms.  Every part of this stay was amazing. From check in to check out, nothing was too much trouble and all the members of staff went beyond expectations. I would gladly return and highly recommend Kantipur Temple House to any traveller. Perfect place to make memories. Lots of attractions are close by and after a busy day sight seeing, was able to climb into a very comfortable bed!

there still remains lot of half destroyed stone buildings after the earthquake. Understandably its a lot of work to restore old stone structures. There is some work ongoing. No where close to the amazing photos from the past. My first time

One of the best place in Kathmandu  hotel  ,trekkers home .clean rooms hot shower is very good .we are stay here two night but i like this place  and more 3 nights .mr saroj pudadaini very helfull gusy .and staff are so frindily
one of the nice and old best royal place called kathmandu durbar square too menny  old and historic temple  and good safe to travel alone to

This hotel due to its history and location is really charming. We stayed there for our last night in Kathmandu and as we were a family got upgraded to a bigger room which was nice. Then the next morning we went down for breakfast which was included in our fare... first my husband got stopped by a rude man at the reception asking us when we were going to clear the bill (We arrived only 6h earlier and are used to pay our hotel bills before even checking-in) . So my husband told him that it was settled and asked him to check his records properly.. the man insisted that we didn't pay and ordered him to pay immediately (atrocious attitude for a man at the desk who is supposed to handle clientele) then my husband asked him to call his manager and after double checking the room was already paid.... no sorry of course from the rude man... Ricky Martin and other celebrities have been used to stay at this hotel... hope they had a better treatment... Then here comes the breakfast which is pretty diverse but regarding the hot drinks they offered only coffee, tea or masala chai none that children (age 2 and 5) could have. So I kindly asked them to have a hot chocolate (that we even get in remote location such as Bandipur) and the man at the breakfast repeated twice to me that I had to pay extra as they don't offer it in the breakfast. As soon as it was served they tend the bill before the kids could even have they drinks.... this hotel needs to work on their human relationships especially with families....

We were there for the busy weekend of the Dashain Festival so lots of people. The hotel felt full but not overcrowded. Rooms are very pleasant and maintained well, with check-in easy and courteous. Just a few things to brush up. The hotel obviously finds it hard to cope with such large numbers at breakfast and service fell down a bit. The plates for the serving spoons for the food containers at breakfast got covered with food, which then started to dry – very unsightly. Plus the dirty dishes started to get mixed with the clean on worktops. In short, probably more staff needed at breakfast to make things run smoothly and to give the sense of crisp service. Plus the sign at the entrance is hanging loose – doesn’t really look good for a high class hotel. But despite this, still a pleasant hotel.

The decor and atmosphere in this place is great, sadly we didn't enjoy the food. I had coconut tofu curry which was average and not very coconuty. My friend had the vegetable tagine which was beans/lentils in cream, not expected to be creamy and tasted quite horrible. She couldn't eat it so ordered humus and bread - got one piece of bread for a huge plate of humus, which was average. Great shame, maybe just avoid those dishes...people with falafel seemed happy. We met friends there for just beers the next night for the atmosphere.

Situated a little outside the tourist area, near the airport the museum is definitvely a worth a visit. The immens amount of information and artefacts which is displayed in numerous sections may cause some visitors to even come back once more in order to gather all the valuable knowledge hidden inside this big building. And when the appetite for facts and figures is gone one can relax head and body in the beautiful garden that completes the museum area.

I love it's courtyard, a great place to get away from the craziness of Thamel. The room is okay(you can find better room for the same price elsewhere), I had hot shower so no complaints. However, it's noisy if you stay close to the stairs. 
The breakfast buffet is average and overpriced, you can definitely somewhere better for breakfast.

I would like to recommend this trip to the business/holiday travellers as 1st choice in kathmandu. The service throughout the stay was great. I enjoyed the food quality & taste too. Front desk is fast enough to process the check in & check out requests. In room service is prompt & rest everything is just great
I really enjoyed the pasta..the restaurant has floor seating, or tables..very inviting and makes me want to go back to try more dishes on the menu..Namaste to all the staff.
A must visit place in kathmandu which carries a tradition and rich culture with all ancient sculptures. Great for panaroma view of kathmandu valley.

Our room was spacious, comfortable bed and bedding, Reasonably fast wifi. Hotel staff are friendly, accommodating, courteous, and provide helpful service. Overall nice ambience. Nice selection of quality foods.

What really makes Kantipur stand out from other hotels in Kathmandu is the beautiful building with the focus on traditional architectural styles, but this hotel is so much more than that. We were very pleased by the excellent location, closely located to both Thamel and old Kathmandu around Durbar Square, while being situated on a quieter side street away from the noise of the main tourist areas made this hotel a pleasant retreat after sightseeing or shopping. In addition, the focus on sustainability and locally sourced foods was excellent and a model for other hotels in Nepal. Cannot recommend highly enough.

If you love colors , bargaining and looking for authentic Nepalese stuff then Thamel is the place . Its by lanes are many and a wonder in itself. Pls remember to bargain hard at the same time not go overboard.  Nepalese are the bestest people in the world, don't break their hearts

Very complete and interesting museum with nice surroundings. A lot of different areas, going from mountaineering, geology, fauna and flora etc. The building in itself is already quite impressive. Definitely worth a visit.

What better place to prepare for a departure into the Himalayan Valleys by motorcycle courtesy of hosts Hearts and Tears MC Club.
Beautiful lakeside Pokhara with its many restaurants and bars will cater to any taste, and for the more adventurous, try paragliding or a mountain trek down through  lush jungle down to the town below.
After the chaos of Kathmandu, Pokhara is clean,  tidy and chilled.
Accomodation was found to be comfortable and affordable,  and the people super friendly.
Travel there either by road from Kathmandu around 11 hours...an extremely interesting trip but  not for the faint hearted,  or fly with the local airlines...I will let you make up your own mind as to which is the more adventurous route:)

We had booked this hotel after the reviews seen on website and also my one of my friends who had stayed here. Hotel is really beautiful with artistic rustic elegance to it. You will feel the touch of cottages with modern look to it.

Pros:

1) Great location
2) Beautiful landscape
3) swimming pool
4) spacious rooms

Cons :

1) Very very bad Wifi
2) very average breakfast
3) Rooms needs to be upgraded
4) very dim lights in room. 
5) over priced compared to present facilities. 

The staff were curtious  and warm. Would think again to visit here. All in all a good hotel.

There was a great deal of courtesy displayed by all your staff, from security, to reception, to dining, etc. Your staff's positive attitude at the reception really impressed me. For me, it was an experience of tranquility, hospitality, and customer centricity. My breakfast was delivered to the room, which was awesome. Thank you for accommodating such requests.

We got there around Nepali New year holiday, so this temple was way too crowded. The architecture is interesting, but the building suffered damage during the earthquake. The monkeys are everywhere, making the place more interesting. Touristy.

We stayed here twice as we were trying to get a visa to Tibet. Firstly the staff are very nice, if a bit old school in the way they are organized. They have all the bookings written down in a ledger book and I am not sure how exactly the rooms are allocated. The first time we stayed we had an ok room on the third floor at the end of the corridor. It was functional, had laminate flooring and the bathroom was ok ( although at various times the water ran brown,but that is quite common here ).  The next time we stayed we had a really horrible room for about an hour before we changed. It was second floor right next to the stairs and you could hear all the people downstairs as well as the builders opposite. This had a very old carpet which looked as though someone died on it and a really terrible bathroom. We asked to move and went to a room opposite with a nice double bed, duvet, balcony and the much preferred laminate flooring. On our first visit the restaurant was closed due to the holiday, but it was open the second time, although we didn't eat there. Next door is Helena's which is good,as well as the pizza place a few doors down.  My advice would be to check out the room before you hand over your cash, the guesthouse is in a good location but it will all depend on the room you are allocated.

Durbar square is fascinating with its characteristic buildings, all kind of people, "holy" men and the best is that motorvehicles are forbidden there so you can stroll there and breathe which makes this square quite unusual in Kathmandu.
A place to go every friday. Love the area. Its got a very good energy. Food colllection of restaurants, bar and clubs.

It is a bit expensive compared to other hotels but Lovely  surroundings, nice  pool. Room was clean, bathroom  was  a bit dated. Breakfast was  an optional  extra  of  7$ which  is a bit steep, most hotels  include the  breakfast in the price.

The earthquake of 2015 has taken its toll and reconstruction is painfully slow. $US 10 for a day ticket seemed a bit outrageous to enter. You can extend your ticket for free once inside for multiple day entries. I didn’t feel there was really that much to see since so many of the buildings were in ruins.

Although not too expensive compared to resorts in other countries, it is much more expensive than the average hotel in Nepal. We were very excited for a night stay here, and it was comfortable enough. However, the service was pretty disappointing, 

Me and my friend were the only two people at the pool and we no one came to ask about orders for drinks. When we placed the orders ourselves and finished our drinks, we had to eventually bring them back to the bar ourselves because ants were appearing every where. 

When we asked the front desk any thing, they always seemed confused and usually it was easier for us to figure out things on our own.
Breakfast was pretty good, different variety every day. Water, however, is not part of breakfast and you have to pay extra.

The pool is beautiful. The only complaints I have are that there is currently construction going on to expand the hotel that goes on all day and the second issue i had was that the hotel allows  day guests to come use the pool. We had a large group of local men who were day guests who stayed at the pool and took pictures from every possible angle. My friend and I were both in two piece bathing suits and very uncomfortable, we had to keep moving to avoid being photographed in the background. We paid over 10,000 NPR a night and I guess we just expected more.
Very interesting temple to vist certainly helps to have a guide to explain the gods to you. I got a few different items from the stalls, vendors are happy to bargain and are very pleasant.
It's just wonderful scenic beauty people can enjoy. Wonderful feelings during sunset. People can hire boat to enjoy scenic beauty. Enjoyed a lot
Beautiful place both visually and spiritually. Take time to sit on the roof terrace cafe and admire the views and the eagles!!
Nice view and chill out place, lots of eatery around the lake and boat activities. Sadly there are many broken sank boat around the lake area, it affects the cleanliness and close view.
Good food services was good  nice hospitality water front resort was top 10  sabina nabina sante salina????????????????????

It's a bit of a hike to the temple (a 500 rupee cab ride) and we felt it was quite disappointing. The temple is located on a large hill with two "summits". On top of each are located an old temple but to get to them you have to fight through crowds and vendors selling all sorts of tacky souvenirs. In fact, the entire temple grounds felt more like an outdoor bazaar. Some of the buildings remain under renovation and are closed to the public. The only redeeming features - some great views over the city of Kathmandu (you get a real sense of the size and density of the city) and watching the hundreds of monkeys wandering the site. They monkeys can be nasty and will try to take any food you're carrying around - be careful!  This is not a destination I would highly recommend you seeing.

Stayed here twice on trips to Kathmandu. Hotel has so much character and is an oasis in the busy city. Food is outstanding, service excellent. Environmentally minded policies make this place a winner.

This hotel is down a dirty mud track away from the shops and restaurants of lakeside, it feels rather at odds with its scruffy surroundings and squashed into a small plot. We looked at a room ( good size, clean but nothing special) but were asked to pay a higher rate than at the luxury 5 star hotel we had just left in at in Kathmandu!  ($180 per night without breakfast ). The pool looks quite nice but again it  has been squeezed into the space between the rooms and the bar  and is in the centre of the walk through to the rooms so their is no privacy , I wouldn't have felt relaxed there.  We decided to stay elsewhere and for just under half the rate asked at Temple Tree  got a lovely big comfortable room at a hotel with  a pool right in the heart of Lakeside.We did try the restaurant as we were told ( by T Tree staff)  that the chef was highly recommended. Unfortunately  the restaurant it is like a large gloomy cave, poorly lit with very hard uncomfortable chairs, it is located at the back of the bar so while you eat you see all of the pipes and fittings etc from behind the bar. Staff are clearly not properly trained - it took 20mins to get some ice for a drink. Unsurprisingly we were the only people eating there which added to the empty atmosphere. The meal was very expensive and food quality mediocre,  London prices in Nepal!  Good concept of a spa hotel in Pokhara but badly executed and poor value .
It was a awesome experience. very nice place syambhu and also UNESCO pasupathinath temmple was great. Old City of Kathmandu Durbar square was full of temples and old palace of the kings

Stayed here for 1 week. Clean and spacious. Friendly staff. However, internet was slow and unreliable in the room. Only 1 of the 2 lifts were working throughout my stay and the pool wasn't available all the time. Not up to Radisson standards.

The room and stuff was so great and soft.The staff was amazing at the buffet specially ms Monika,she treated us with great humility and respect.She was very sweet and fulfilled whatever we wanted.Everything was amazing and great.luved the experience

I had a few hours to spare before going back to work and decided to explore the neighbourhood around my hotel. At first I was intimidated by the crowds, the cars, motorcycles and narrow streets, but soon relaxed and enjoyed walking around, stopping occasionally at shops that caught my attention.

Some shopkeepers were friendlier than others (some were downright aloof), but I very much appreciated that no one was overly aggressive. It is hard to leave this place empty-handed as there is something for everyone. Haggling is allowed, although I did not manage to get significantly lower prices than the original asking price. Most prices are very reasonable and so huge discounts were not necessary.

Wear comfortable clothes and shoes.

This place has got like everything! Amazing food, lively Ambiance..just ask for what you're looking for and you have it! The night life is amazing for people like me who are night people. 
I didn't get enough of this place so definitely coming back soon!!😄🤩

No service no proper multicusine restaurant they dont have a buffet dinner served and the staff is very unfriendly they dont talk properly reception staff also dont have any knowledge and there is no pickup and drop for airport

Clean and nice hotel. Near lake and short time to city center. Nice garden. But AC not working proper. 2 times help from engineering. Breakfast tasty and delightfull. Recommended for travellers. Keep the good services

It was Monday 7:30 pm may be me and my wife went to have dinner at OR2K and found that they r offering Movie night. We ordered a combo. As it was our last night stay at Pokhara. The food was fresh and tasty. I also ordered a cocktail which was great. We had enjoyed a lot. The environment was great for couple and solo traveler also friendly for family.
the venue and ambiance in this place were amazing. communal floor seating, nice tunes, and interesting decor. great food selection, but i wasn't blown away. also not the cheapest place.

Kathmandu Durbar Square is a UNESCO World Heritage site that displays the historic and beautiful Nepalese architecture of ancient times.  The "big" earthquake that did a lot of damage to most of the structures at the square had occurred back in 2015 and we had visited on November 2019 - but there are still many structures that needs major restoration work to repair the once beautiful architecture.  There are still many structures with support braces on the walls of buildings to prevent a possible collapse of the walls should there be more  earthquake "tremors".  

Even with the many buildings needing support braces on the walls, it is still a worthwhile visit to Kathmandu Durbar Square to still take-in the sights of the still beautiful ancient Napalese architecture.  There are several palaces and many temples here to see and enjoy.

The Kathmandu Guesthouse is a very convenient place to stay – if they honour your booking. I’ve been staying at the KGH for more than 30 years, sometimes making several visits in a year with friends,  sometimes bringing with me groups of 40 students or – during the troubles- being one of the very few guests staying there.    In the last few years I have stayed at a variety of out hotels in and around Thamel  mainly because of the KGH policy of booking in 20% more guests than they can accommodate.  This month a  friend and I booked two deluxe rooms, reminded them of the flight they were collecting us from and I even emailed from the airport before I left – yet despite the staff who knew me welcoming me back and asking about people I often travel with,  there was still a tense discussion and  eventually an argument about being booked in or the rooms we had booked. We got rooms, but it always leaves you with the feeling that next time I will stay elsewhere just so that I can be sure of my room when I arrive at midnight.
Otherwise; great location, a lot of lovely staff, a good restaurant and an nice place to stay once you have the room you booked.  Rooms vary,  but the bathroom of my ‘deluxe’ room had a shower which did not drain, fluctuating hot water, and needed a good scrub and some non-rubber pillows.  At the prices now being charged you can get better accommodation in the area.

Temple Tree is probably the nicest resort in Pokhara. The rooms are clean and beautiful, the grounds are lush, green, and well-kept. There are small touches of class and quality, and the service is outstanding.
However, I have too many complaints with the resort that don't justify what they charge for a room. The food is bad and overpriced, with the exception of breakfast, which is quite good. The drinks (both alcoholic and non) are also priced very high.  
The room prices seem to be negotiable and range from 50USD to 200USD depending on whether you are Nepali, a resident expat, or a foreign tourist. I was able to get a cheaper room rate by having a Nepali friend call on my behalf. I would not pay the quoted 150USD for a room. Further, the only baby crib was unavailable so we had to pay an extra 35USD/night to have a cot-bed in the room for our toddler, which seems a bit outrageous to pay for a two year old. 
The rooms, while beautiful, are also quite small. 
Good location, There is shopping, activities, and restaurants (with much better food) within close walking distance.
Overall a nice stay if you can afford it, or are a couple, but not great for families.
We didn’t enter as were unprepared for the price to enter. I hope it was worth it for those that did.
Really enjoyed our stay here. The rooms were comfortable, the atmosphere was pleasant, and the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome. Highly recommended!

We arrived, paid our entry fee and then wondered what to do.  There was no-one to tell us what to see, or what was on offer.  And no signage of what to see.  If we hadn't spotted people entering a small door in the wall, we would have missed the lot. Once inside, it was quite fascinating - but again, no people to explain anything or suggest where to go.  Our experience would have been far mire fulfilling had we used a guide for a few hours.
There were lots of interesting things to look at in the museum and we really appreciated that it was a person centered museum with information on different ethnic groups in Nepal.

We had visited the Hyatt regency Casino on 29.09.23 with my friends. While playing blackjack, the dealer made a mistake due to which they lost the game. But the manager overturned the mistake and took the game. All the players at the table protested, but the management behave very unprofessionally. All the players decided to walk out in protest, and the managers was unmoved. I have visited all the major casinos everywhere and no where could the management be so casual about game rules. 
Casinos run on fair play and when the management can behave in such way, it amounts to cheating by the casino.

Hope this mistake is not repeated with other customers, because we won't be visiting any of their casinos again.

A special place to go visit in kathmandu. We enjoyed the walk from Thamel to this place, but we did not go through the top view point because they were asking for entrance fees which is shocking because the first time we went to visit this place ,  NO ENTRANCE FEE.
The road up the hill is a bit rocky ( literally) but one near the top there is an amazing restaurant where you can order food before ascending the steps up to the top for sweeping views
I really loved this place. Restaurant was really great and food was great. I was hoping to try them all but too bad I had to return early.
Morning is the best time to visit the great temple which situated on a small hill in Kathmandu. Climbing the step to the top is one of the most enjoyable experience.

Most beautiful view near pokhara a Must do
We stayed 2 hours at sunrise very difficult to leave This view

This museum is very informative for the following :
- The different tribesliving in Nepal with there costumes and folklore 
- The many mountain peaks and information how they have been concurred 
All are accompanied with amazing phitos of all the high mountains of the Himalayas. 
- Information about the effect of global warming on the different glaciers. 
- 18 min movie about the vilages around mount Everest. 
Mostly recommended

The site was so interesting and our local guide was a delight and showed us everything: the obvious and the hidden. The post earth quake re-build is impressive. We were fortunate to be there when the local were preparing for dwalia.

Great verity of healthy food, clean peaceful and beautiful .
Blessed by the best views existing Need to go to see, eat and enjoy,it's something in it's on standard of it self, highly recommend...

The location is great-central in Thamel. I had some problems getting there from the airport though-I had prearranged an airport pickup but my plane was late. Instead of checking the flight arrival time, the driver just decided to leave the airport around midnight, minutes before I emerged from the baggage claim. I was very disappointed to have this happen upon entering the country, and it dampened my impression of the hotel. I also wanted to book some rafting through the hotel, but the manager only offered me one company to do rafting with that ultimately didn't have another group I could join for the dates that worked for me. The breakfast was quite good but expensive. The rooms were nice and clean as well. Overall, it was pretty average.

We loved the relaxed feel and the food was great! We shared the combo platter of various dipping sauces, falafel and fresh breads. it was delicious and more than enough for two. It offers a wonderful view of the lake and inside floor seating is the perfect place to sink into a relax while eating, reading a book or just enjoying the quiet ambiance.

Loved the food, atmosphere and location, but the serving staff seemed to be unhappy in their jobs. Not sure why but their attitudes made for awkward order-taking and order-serving interactions. The food was delicious but the service attitude made us uncomfortable.

Had an excellent experience at Temple Tree. Liked the Nepali style accommodation with contemporary amenities and services. Rooms were cosy and clean.Service by the staff was beyond excellent. Everyone is friendly and very attentive. Great place to be with families.

Thamel . It’s a number of long crowded streets with 5 types of shops all repeated hundreds of times over . The people are not over pushy but expect to be called and offered drugs if you are between the ages of 5 and 50 .I did enjoy all the cheap fake The North Face clothing and brought 3 jackets home. Don’t eat the street food ! You will get sick . Eat in your hotel or the fanciest restaurant you can find .Even the best meals you can find ,cost very little .I don’t buy trinkets , wooden bracelets or singing bowls but you will find millions of these Thai imported replicas in every single shop .I wouldn’t venture off Thamel streets as traffic gets violent and scammers and beggars more popular . Enjoy

Wonderful stay.
Food, ambience service staff are outstanding. Special thanks to Sabina, Nabina, Binita and Alishwa for taking care of all of us.

Sabina, Salina, Nabina, Sante, Alishwa.

Thank you for the pleasant service
