We wanted to love Kantipur - upon first glance the grounds were stunning and we loved the eco-friendly vibe! Unfortunately, the hotel just wasn't a good value for the price.

Everything was...fine. The problems we experienced (hot water, electricity, etc) are common in Nepal. We assumed Kantipur was a nice mid-range option - assuming that at $100/night those "comfort" amenities would be less of an issue than at cheaper spots. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case!

So - Negatives:
 - Electricity goes out. A lot. As part of their "green" philosophy they don't regularly run their generator and you'll find yourself without power for hours at a time.
- Hot Water was more scare than other hotels and takes  minutes to warm up (somehow running water for 5 minutes just to get it lukewarm seems counter-intuitive to their eco-friendly philosophy?). Don't even try to shower during a power outage!
- There's a lot of construction happening next door right now, so you may hear that in addition to street noise. They are also doing demo on the roofdeck, so I imagine that would be an issue. 
- Rooms weren't amazing - our friend had a cheaper single room with a smaller-than-twin sized bed that he had to change and we had a "deluxe" double. Our room was very dark, despite having seventeen (yes, 17) different light switches - each operating a single overhead florescent light. 
- Wifi was very bad - I couldn't connect at all from certain parts of our room

Positives:
- The food was excellent! Good selection at the restaurant and it was generally pretty solid. 
- Building was beautiful and the grounds were gorgeous. Brick, traditional Newari architecture - all gorgeous. 
- Location was very convenient to everything in Thamel

So, in general, totally a fine place to stay, just not what we expected for the price. Staffing had highs (awesome security guard!) and lows (cranky front desk receptionist!). I would recommend checking out other places at that price point before you try Kantipur - I have a feeling your dollar will go farther!

We had a short stay in Kathmandu and was charmed by how the Kantipur Temple House looked and recommended by Lonely Planet.  The hotel was centrally located for us in Thamel. The hotel is eco-conscious and limits the use of single use plastics, providing filtered drinking water in a brass pitcher and cups that we could also fill our water bottle with.  Our room was spacious with comfortable beds and covers.  Electric blankets were provided for chillier nights, but we did not need to use them.  The room faced the quieter interior courtyard.  Staff was always helpful, friendly, and warm.  We were able to drop a load of laundry for the hotel to clean after their usual deadline and received them the next day as promised.  Breakfast was basic with more of a continental flair as we were told by one of our guides that Nepali breakfast isn't really a thing.  But the food was plentiful.  We wanted to commend the hospitality of the hotel, as we had a short day layover on our return from Bhutan, and the concierge allowed us to store our luggage at the hotel (after we had checked out earlier in the week) so that we could spend the few hours we had in Thamel for last minute shopping, lunch, and wandering.  Thank you for making our short stay in Kathmandu a wonderful one.

Your trip to Kathmandu should include: Dhubar Square, Swayambhunath, the Buddha Pashupatinath (the burning ghats) and the Buddha Stupa (there are so many with similar names - this one just northeast of Pashupatinath).

The Swayambhunath complex is a very old Buddhist complex with the typical stupa (gold tower with white eyes) and many shrines. It rises above Kathmandhu to the West and is part of the region's founding story in mythology. It is typically approached by a series of long stairs at the intersection of Swayambhu Marg and Swayambhu Circle Road. There are many shrines and monkeys to admire on the ascent. There are many scenic vistas from the top. And many shrines to wander amongst.

Swayambhunath is otherwise known as "monkey temple." Monkeys are common at temples as they congregate to feast on all the offerings but there is an especially large number here. Obvious don't try to feed them. Obvious keep a hand on your things and your distance. Maybe less obvious, be cautious when photographing a seemingly adorable baby monkey as momma monkey might do a parkour jump on/off your back as warning! (No monkeys or humans were harmed in this outing.)

HAVING a guide can really reward you at times and mine earned his keep on my visit to Swayambhunath Temple in Kathmandu.
The hilltop site is the most ancient and enigmatic of all the holy shrines in Kathmandu valley and its lofty white dome and glittering golden spire can be seen for miles and from all sides of the valley.
Historical records found on a stone inscription provide evidence that the stupa was already an important Buddhist pilgrimage destination by the 5th century AD.
It is also called the Monkey Temple because of the hundreds of monkeys which scamper  round at night when everyone has gone, but don't rely on that too much. I also saw monkeys during the day and some of them were big, so take care.
My guide helped me gain the best experience of the stupa by the simple process of asking me before we arrived whether I would like to do it the easy way or the hard way.
Having already had some experience of how Nepal's "hard ways" could be very hard indeed, I opted to follow his advice and take the easy way.
That involved being driven up relatively close to the temple so my final ascent could be up shallow steps. The wisdom of doing this became immediately apparent once I reached the site and looked down the alternative staircase offering scores and scores of very steep steps. Not an attractive proposition in the heat.
Having arrived I took time to enjoy some breathtaking views of the city of Kathmandu below while warily giving space to the monkeys I met who strutted about as if they owned the place.
One thing I didn't expect to come across was the TARDIS which, as all Dr Who fans know, stands for Time And Relative Dimension In Space.
One of the entrance doors to upper levels has been created in the shape of the Time Lord's police box door which threw my mental state right off at the time. It was just so unexpected and so incongruous.
Don't miss a chance to come up and visit this spectacular temple. The views are worth the visit alone. Just remember to bring water and, if you have to ascend the steep staircase, take it slow and easy. We descended this way and that was hard enough.

The Pashupatinath Temple is considered to be the most sacred Hindu Temple in Nepal.  The Temple is located on the banks of the Bagmati River on the eastern side of Kathmandu.  This is where many of the deceased followers of Hinduism are cremated, but not in a closed furnace of a crematorium.  Here in Nepal cremations are done open air, and at this Temple the bodies are covered in cloth and placed on a stone slab right next to the river bank.  Pieces of wood and straw are placed around the body and then it is lit on fire.  After about 3 to 4 hours, the cremation is complete and then the ashes and remains are swept into the river.  This process is part of the Hindu religion that they will be reincarnated.

Pashupatinath Temple is an absolute must-visit for anyone coming to Kathmandu. As one of the holiest Hindu temples in Nepal and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it offers a profound spiritual experience unlike any other.

The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is set on the banks of the sacred Bagmati River, adding to its serene atmosphere. The intricate architecture, golden roof, and impressive pagoda-style design make it a breathtaking sight. The temple complex is vast, with many smaller shrines and peaceful courtyards to explore.

One of the most unique experiences at Pashupatinath is witnessing the cremation rituals on the riverbank, which are an important part of Hindu tradition. The sight is both humbling and deeply meaningful, offering insight into the culture and spiritual practices of the locals.

The air around Pashupatinath is filled with the fragrance of incense and the sound of chanting prayers, creating an environment of peace and devotion. Visitors can also explore the nearby forest and ashrams for a tranquil escape.

Whether you're a spiritual seeker or a traveler interested in learning more about Hindu traditions, Pashupatinath Temple offers a sacred and unforgettable experience.

Into the ladies changing room to undress under the very watchful eye of the female "therapist".  I was told to keep my bra and knickers on (I understand the latter, but the former seemed unusual).

She then ushered me into a room off the locker area and told me to get onto the couch.  There were two doors into this room - I soon found out the other door led to the men's locker room, as the men in the changing room seemed to be having a farting competition!  Nice!

The room itself was windowless, hot and stuffy with no air condition, just a fan.  The couch was rock hard and had no face hole!  

No questions were asked about what I wanted or any medical issues, she just started trying to crack my spine - NOT GOOD!  I instantly asked her to stop!  She's not a chiropractor or an osteopath!  Anyone with any massage training knows you DO NOT do this!!!  Then she got the oil, I had repeatedly said at this point "no oil" but still she tried to get oil on me, after 15 minutes of her fumbling around on my back and arms I called a stop to the "massage", I could have had a better massage letting one of the stray street dogs walk on my back!

She called in a 2nd "therapist", he started work on me.  He did the same as the woman, and tried to pop my spine - I asked him to stop!  He carried on!  I turned side ways and insisted he stop, he got the oil - I said no!  It was like Ground Hog day, but with a man instead of a woman.  

Then he did his coup de grace and used his full force on my left elbow to pop it.  I nearly thumped him!  The pain shot down my arm and I stopped the massage.  

What should have been a 90 minute, oil free Shiatsu massage ended up as a 45 minute torture which has left me with an acute case of Tennis elbow in my left arm!

These people were BADLY trained, if at all, they had NO idea what they were doing and as I said to the duty manager, after I had calmed down, they were utterly DANGEROUS!  

If this is their idea of a spa, they need to go and look at some others - this place is NOT fit for purpose!  IT SHOULD BE CLOSED DOWN!!!
Interesting pagoda above the lake, but the hike there in the summer is not the best.  It was an okay experience if you have time.

The structure is, unfortunately, just part of the rip-off structure of Nepal. While thete us no charge to enter, they will make you pay if you wish to park while u visit. The memorial asks for silence from visitors. As you can imagine, most people find it impossible to refrain from mindless babble for more than a few seconds so tje entire concept if having a oeaceful, quiet sanctuary to rest, reflect and have space and a break from the infernal noise of this country, is lost. A great idea completely ruined by the stupidity of those who visit it. Great views of city and surrounding areas though. Bring lots of water and zip your tongue!

May be a world heritage site but I will not dare to go back again. 
My father inlaw took a photo by mistake ( He was not able to  read the hindi or english signs ). Once they approched us we deleted the photo. However some local guides were extremely rude with us ( probably becasue we did not take any guide ) and brought three different security guards to check his phone. Even after we showed them every single folder inside his basic phone they were not satisified. Their attitude was also intimidating and threatening. Would not dare to go back again.

You can feel so much intensive mystical energy here. This temple complex is truly a mystic religion place. You can also see a funeral on the ghats here. I still have some deep feeling inside me after I visited this place.
500 + steps to climb, but they meander up the hill and there are handrails for much of it. At the top, the views are spectacular. The whole atmosphere is of calm tranquility. Well with the climb

One thing I have learnt whilst living in Kathmandu is that service is slower than other countries.  At the Gaia Restaurant, the service was appallingly slow.  Ignoring the slow taking of order and delivery of food (which I have learned to live with), I had to ask for my bill twice as they forgot about me and then forgot about actually collecting the money.  I ended up taking my bill to the bar.  These two things have not happened once in Kathmandu until I went here (I eat out a lot).
As for the food, it was good but not brilliant.  I had Chow Mein with Coffee which was generally the same as most other places, quality and price wise.  That said, the coffee was very good though not good enough to redeem the poor service.

I just entered Nepal & have booked a business class shangrila suite with Yak & Yeti for 3 people. They offer complimentary pickup. But sent a indigo for 3 people that too broken car. We had to rent another car. When we reached the hotel there was no special welcome. Later the hotel staff also asked us to pay for the taxi. 
Poor service. Regretful decision. 
Will not advice. Bad first trip impression to nepal. 
Will post this on all websites.
World peace pagoda is situated 4-5 km outside from city centre.. No entry fees.. Beautiful scenery of Pokhara city including Phewa Lake from this Pagoda..

Beautiful place to visit special in the evening time. Thae best part of this temple premises is that it is covered with full of many temples and is easily accessible. It is one of the most popular temple of Hindus.

It is definitly important Hindu temple and very interesting place to see.
We could not see better the temple beacause we are not hindu but that is ok and to be respected.
The fact that there are a lot of very pushing people around who disturb you and follow you to sell the things and offer guide service even when you politely reject for a lot of time made us felt not so secure.

Pashupatinath Temple Is Located in Kathmandu  about 1 Km  North East of Kathmandu Airport and 4 KM East of Touristic City called Thamel. Which is Dedicated to Lord Shiva. This is only 5 faces( East,West,North,South and Zenith) Lord Shiva's Temple in all over the world. It is Situated on the bank of Holy River Bagmati. This Temple was registered in World Heritage site in 1979. It is the Hindus's Greatest sacred Temple Where only Hindus are allowed but all the other  religious people also visit   outside of it  .As I have visited several times ,i would like to visit again and Again. Its found not only sacred place but also  attractive Art and architectural Pagoda style Temples, Natural River, Forest. Love to visit again and again.  I recommend every visitor  may visit to get its, experience.

To start with, this hotel was recommended in lonely planet. As often it turns out to have a backside. I arrived at the hotel and got picked up at the bus stop in Pokhara. Everything looks fine. It's a good hotel and friendly staff that at once wants to talk about trips, taxi, tours and guides.  The young guy that seems to run the hotel always wants to scam you and this is really a big big tourist trap. 

The hotel itself is clean and ok value for the money, but don't use any other facility on the hotel as the manager will certainly try to take some extra money for you. E.g. he charged 3 times the regular amount for taxi and laundry. Whatever you do, don't arrange a trekking tour from this hotel!!!

The hotel can also be a bit noisy if there is a party there so bring something for your ears.

The atmosphere is great--very quiet, set back from the main road. The juice and breakfast are nice..the staff was lovely as well. They have books you can read--but you can't buy or take them away--so read fast!
A devine experience, very unhurried and blissful. We went early in the morning and had a good Darshan.

We enjoy visiting cultural/religious places and were looking forward to this. Unfortunately we were very disappointed, the entrance at which our taxi driver dropped us (I believe this to be the main one) involved a walk through a dirty, smelly path. Got to a point and just had to give up and return to the car. Went to the boudhanath temple next and loved it.

The stupa is high in a hill. So you need to climb around 1 hour or you should take a taxi. Prefer to cross the lake with boat and climb up the path to stupa. Although there is not much to see in the stupa, the path is full of pokhara and lake views. You can also rest in a cafe after visiting the stupa. After the stupa we visitied devis fall and majaba cave, another 1 hour walk:)

It is one of the most imprortant Hindu site but unfortunately the main temple is open only local to hindus but there many other interesting building to see.

There is also the place for the burial ceremoneys which is something unique and you get to known oother religions beleives with regards to death. 

But if it will be your first time it is kind of shock for some and thus you have to be strong and be prepared,

The Hotel has a very nice garden and that's it. My room had a big mouse in it. They caught it in the bathroom and then tried to kill it on spot with electrical shocks. Although I changed my room but, the new room also had plumbing issues in the bathroom.
The breakfast is also pretty much the same on all days.
I loved to watch mountains from this peaceful temple...it looks like a silver ..aww...the environment is totally clean n peaceful...n the statue of lord Buddha is just amazing...
It's an amazing place and must see place when you are in Kathmandu. The cremation of Hindu people is unusual for me. I enjoyed visiting this place.

The World Peace Pagoda is an understated pagoda perched on top of the hill, viewable from all of Pokhara. It’s a pleasant location to view the city and soak in the atmosphere. Unfortunately it can be a little noisy with some locals not observing the silence, but does not detract from the experience. Don’t come with huge expectations ... it’s really just a pagoda to sit and enjoy the location.

A word of caution: we’ve been told of some addicts along the guidebook-recommended forest path who will mug and attack travellers. So please ask around before attempting the route. The taxi to/fro the pagoda from town cost us Rs500 one way.

After you finish your trek, clean up and rest, this is a beautiful hike up the mountain - 45-60 minutes.  The Peace Temple has gorgeous views of Pokhara and the Annapurna Range.  You can then follow an unmarked trail down to Devis Falls.  Very nice walk.

The World Peace Pagoda in Pokhara is one of an estimated 80+ Peace Pagodas that are located around the world today.  The Pokhara Peace Pagoda was built after World War II by the Buddhist monks from the Japanese Nipponzan Myohoji organization to promote world peace.  
The Pagoda is located on a hilltop, and our small group tour had utilized a small tour bus that was capable of holding 16 tourists plus the guide and driver.  Our tour driver drove past the main parking area that was intended for the big, full-sized buses and drove all the way to a small taxi drop-off area - saving maybe about 20  minutes of uphill hiking.  If I remember correctly, the hiking time from the taxi drop-off area to the Pagoda still required 20 to 30 minutes of uphill walking.  We had arrived at the Pagoda hill before daybreak - before the big tour groups had arrived.

Once at the top of the hill, there is a small park area where the Pagoda is located.  The views from this hill-top park are outstanding - views of the Pagoda, the mountains in the background, Pokhara city skyline below the hill and the sunrise over the city skyline - fantastic views!

The hospitality was truly warm and welcoming .The staff were incredibly kind ,attentive and professional specially Susmita from reception she help and care for our comfort .From check in to checkout everything was smooth.Nice hotel.
The best thing going for this restaurant is its atmosphere. Otherwise, the service is extremely slow and the food is strictly average. If you've got the time - and the patience - stop by.

The peace temple is itself a quiet, Buddhist temple.  Its location on a hilltop across the lake from Pokhara offers great views of the city and the mountains beyond.  The journey by boat across the lake is peaceful.  The approach to the temple is quite steep

My friends and I rented a boat across the lake, then hiked up to the Peace Temple stupa. It was fun, but it was a tough hike (definitely not the 45 minutes you see at the beginning of the trail --I would give it at least 1 hour 15 minutes if not more). If you choose this option, make sure to take with you lots of water to drink and something to eat....

Stayed 2 nights and was upgraded to the Club floor, Excellent service   Booked a city tour through the Hotel desk and although the guide was very nice, it wasnt as interesting as I? had hoped. We could have taken a cab and Read signs at the temples we visited for a lot less money. But right outside the door was an amazing $13 massage-

Gaia was recommended to me by a fellow traveler as "one of the best restaurants in Kathmandu" so upon my return to Kathmandu I knew I definitely had to try it. I went for dinner one night and returned for breakfast the following morning. Both times I was incredibly disappointed by the quality of food. Though the setting is quite nice the food was bland in flavor and unimaginative. Maybe I just chose two dishes that weren't great. Would not recommend.

This massive Buddhist World Peace Pagoda (or Shanti Stupa) towers above Phewa Tal at a height of 3,608 feet (1100 m). It is one of 2 Peace Pagodas in Nepal and 80 in the world. The Peace Pagodas were the inspiration of Nichidatsu Fujii, a Japanese Buddhist monk that founded the Nipponzan-Myōhōji Buddhist Order. Fujii devoted his life to promoting non-violence after meeting with Mahatma Gandhi. Having just visited several memorials to Gandhi in New Delhi, I was delighted to experience living evidence of his influence. Not only is the stupa beautiful, but the location provides stunning views of Pokhara, Phewa Lake, and the Annapurna range. We drove here with a guide in the late afternoon, and it wasn’t too crowded. Very pretty with the sun illuminating the mountains. Peace to all.
This is very nice temple to visit. Those who are interested to see religious places and their historical aspects will enjoy to see this place. My experience is average not very exciting

Wonderful holy temple in Kathmandu - just a mile away from the Airport and gets crowded many times during peak morning and evening hours.

Have been visiting the temple year after year and the glory of the deity and the premises is intact.

Cleanliness needs some improvement.
Boated a across and hiked up, stopped at Tibetan camp on the way back. Beautiful views And great half day adventure!

A very sobering place to visit. From our vantage point on the opposite side of the river we were able to watch families bring their dead relatives to be cremated on the side of the river and then their ashes were swept into the river.. Their deep respect for the dead was evident in the way the whole process was undertaken. Swimming in the river were a number of small boys who had no concern for what was floating in the river.
Although you may have to climb up a bit , as the vehicles do not go up to the temple, but still it is worth it. The view of the entire Annapurna range is breathtaking .... Do not miss it ...
It was a good tracking to reach to this Temple. Climbing is not easy but it does pay off once you reach on top. There is a walk way of stoney steps amid the tall trees and bushes.

We had a delightful family stay at Hotel Yak & Yeti — a perfect blend of timeless elegance and modern comfort. The serene surroundings, charming interiors, and well-maintained amenities made our visit truly relaxing. But what made it unforgettable was the warmth and attentiveness of the staff, especially Miss Muskan. Her genuine kindness, ever-present smile, and thoughtful gestures added a personal touch that elevated our experience. She made us feel less like guests and more like family. Thank you for the hospitality that truly warms the heart.

My wife and I booked a what we thought was a 'Heritage Deluxe' room for $500 USD. Rather, we were given a basic deluxe room with an adjoining door, no sound proofing from the other guests, resulting in little sleep. Whilst the food, beverage and location were good, the room was a huge failure.

Pashupatinath temple is one of holy places for Hindu and it's one of 12 Jyolingas. It was sad to see how poorly temple was maintained.

No signs of directions within temple. Temple premise is not at all clean and it was stinking. It was devastating to see such a holy place in this condition. Hope Nepal tourism will do well maintenance for their leading attractions.

Everything was amazing at this temple except people inside who are not even staff would take ur cell phone if you take videos or photos and would delete everything before even you can check it, this was disgusting and not acceptable, another thing was that one old man was just showing us the place around and was forcing us to pay as he was the guide which we didn't liked, so stay away from such people and beaware of whats happening around you as this is a huge place whr you might lose ur valuables.

Death really comes close here. I am surprised how open they are and taking photos isnt strictly forbidden (as in Varanasi) as long as you are respectful.

I think its good therapy for us westeners to see this and remind ourself of death - something we try to hide from and forget of.

Anyhow a very good expericnce even though somewhat stomachwrenching...

Eye opening features of the temple.Prayers officiated by the prist filled my heart Tour of the temple and arti
 And vegetation around the templewas beautiful
Excellent menu and the food was very tasty. Seating in a outdoor area (with rain covers if required) and indoor areas if required. They have Nepalese food as well as most international options.

The hotel was top notch, great experience , clean & tidy rooms . Fantastic , good hospitality. The area was so good. I personally have hotel at Chikkamagaluru ( The holiday inn) . Highly recommend to stay here once you come to Pokhara. Manisha assist us so nicely . Helping nature people.

As #3 on Tripadvisor I had high expectations. The environment was nice and the momos were excellent but the pad Thai was very bad. I guess we should have stuck with the local food options. Service was slow.

It is well worth the time to visit this holy Buddhist site. It is a pleasant ride across the lake and a short but steep climb to the top. The stupa is peaceful and the views are excellent. 
I would recommend buying a one way ticket each way so that you can spend as much time as you like and can get a sail back when you come down. With the roundtrip fair, you wait for the same boatman who brought you over.

Friends and I took a cab here because one of my friends was having some issues with her back. Our visit was during August around 10am and it was cloudy. The pagoda itself is nice and you have to take your shoes off. There is nothing outstanding to see here but there was a nice coffee shop that sold locally grown coffee on the way up (and down).

At least this temple is well mantained and there is no rubbish around (the only one I've seen in Nepal in this condition). The most interesting thing is the walk in the woods (almost one hour) you can have from the area of Gupteshwor caves to there, climbing scales and walking through the small gardens of poor and simple farmers' houses, have a chat with them and take some pictures or have some water or a cake (always giving them some rupies, no deal), and finally arrive at the top of this beautiful hilla from where you can enjoy the view of Phewa lake and Pokhara city. If you're lucky and there is no mist at the horizon, you can also see the peaks of amazing Annapurna range. The temple itself is not accessible inside (as most of hindu temples) but you only can walk around it and climb its scales.
It's a nice place to visit as it is on top of the hill. Taxi will charge 2000 Nepali for 6 hours. It has beautiful view of lake and mountains . There are 4-5 cafes to enjoy coffee on the top.

we arrived to the lakeside ticket area around 7:30am and got in line at the booth. we paid Rs1650 for 2 people (option #6 on the menu). then you go get your life jackets and hand them your tickets. and then you get in line by the water. several times they told us we would have to paddle ourselves and just to leave our boat unattended at the other side bc they didn’t have enough captains but after 20min or so they paddled us over. it took about 15min to cross. the boat captain asked us if we needed 1,2,or3 h and we decided on 2. you prob need 1.5-2h round trip. we headed up following the signs to the “stupa” and there were beautiful views along the way including great annapurna peaks in the morning. there were 1-2 places where you could’ve grabbed a drink or snack. when we got to the top there were beautiful flowers and lotsa photo ops. you take off your shoes and head up. there is no “inside” as far as we could tell. head to the left around the top and if you don’t the guard will redirect you. stay quiet and calm. on the way down but still near the top we took a little side hike over where the sign said “himalaya views” and there was no one over there (but lotsa trash) and there were also views from here of the mountains and the city below. you’ll see lotsa paragliders. it took us about 45min to get to the top and we’re in decent shape. it took about 30min to get down (be careful, easy to slip on the rocks going down). then when we got to the bottom our driver was indeed there at the previously arranged time. we headed back across the lake and hopped off the boat. all in all, enjoyable. feel free to read up on the word peace pagodas (there should be ~100 of them by now according to the signs).

Please don’t misunderstand my low mark, it’s only related to the very expensive entry ticket of 1000 rupees and there is hardly anything you can see there.
The main temple is not allowed for non Hindus and ground around temple within the complex will not provide much.
On the other hand, when you cross the Bagmati river, you will have a magic view on the temple which cost nothing.
So my suggestion is to certainly visit but do not pay for it just enjoy the stroll, atmosphere and views from the other side of the river.

Hindu temple, one of the four most important religious sites in Asia for Shiva devotees. The largest temple complex in Nepal, it stretches on both sides of Bagmati River which is considered holy by Hindus. The golden temple is closed when we went there. Interestingly, fortunate enough to observed a cremation ongoing on the site. Two bodies being cremated while one still waiting.
Great stay………….  Service goods…. ….. Staff is cooperative & nice ……………….,..  rooms are good ……… food is good…..  spa is recommended….. thanks for your hospitality……..   gracias

God bless (help) us every time if we remember or pray with our heart.
Visit Nepal one time in your life .never miss #Pasupatinath temple#

A pleasant and wonderful stay. The staff is caring, affectionate and ensures the guests feel at home and are comfortable. The food is delicious and the spread is very tempting. I also enjoyed a Nepali massage in the hotel spa. Appreciate Des Ram, Suman and all other staff for their services. Highly recommended.

Not sure I'd put this down as a tourist site, seems very disrespectful and I found it intrusive to be watching as people cremated their loved ones - albeit from the other side of the river.  Fascinating to know about it but the guide could have explained from afar without us having to be there.
Oh and it has more monkeys running around that the so called monkey temple so beware!
Went here for dinner with my wife and friends. Staff is good and food is also very tatsy. But the quantity was less for me Atleast.
Must Visit if you are in Kathmandu temple closes by 12 Noon to 4 PM, No entry ticket can reach there by taxi and you need to walk for 5-6 minutes and you will be temple.
A very cool 5th century structure that is the oldest and most sacred Hindu temple in Nepal.  The people were lovely here and an amazing place for photography.

The hotel environment is excellent. The decor and the rooms are very spacious and clean. The greatest asset of this hotel is the staff. They are very polite and helpful. Special mention to front office especially Ms Jamuna. 
Only the problem is the shower place which requires immediate attention. Shower place has no doors and water splashes everywhere

This is a good place to go to with your family if you want to go to a peaceful temple. This temple is dedicated to lord shiva, it's intricate wooden carvings and golden spires exude timeless reverence .

This is an interesting place to visit while in Nepal. I learned a lot about Hindu culture and especially how they honor the last day of their beloved who passed away. They have to perform certain rituals before they’re cremated. Loved ones are there and assisting to finalize the cremation. People can watch from the other side of the river. The temple is a beautiful site, I think it’s perfect for the ones who are gone.  I say bring a mask if you can’t stand the scent of the smoke. Prayers to all who passed.

The Yak and Yeti is not a 5 start hotel but is fine in most ways. We have stayed in hotels across the world and have  never been asked to pay $10 per day to access wifii. 
The gardens are nice and the hotel staff are helpful. We stayed in two different rooms - the first one at the start of our trip was old and a bit damp/musty smelling - the second room at the end of our  trip was modern, bright and welll appointed - overlooking the gardens. I would stay again if the policy of charging for wifii is changed by the manager to free access. Otherwise I would choose another hotel. This was the only Hotel accross Nepal and Bhutan we had to pay for wifii.Communication is important for travellers and $10 per day is an uneccessarily high charge.

The Stupa wasn't really anything great to see, but the walk there and the view was great. Took the boat from lakeside and then walked up. No need for a guide, you can take the boat alone and the walk is easy. Lots of loud tourists at the Stupa even though there were signs telling to be quiet...

A must on any trip to Pokhara, the views of the Annapurna range and over  the lake  and city are as good as it gets. The  temple or stupa  is  a 20 minute  drive from Pokhara  but is a wonderful peaceful place to visit and there are numerous coffee shops and cafes to  take in the views while enjoying lunch. Definately  a must visit attraction in Pokhara

I was fortunate to be on a motor bike to take me to near the top of this attraction. If I'd walked all the way,I'd have been disappointed for the effort. There are cafes up there for food and drink. I did see this place after a 7 day trek so I think I'd had enough climbing for a while. View is pleasant but could be spectacular if it was a clear day.

Looking at the pictures on the hotel's website you expect an imposing, luxury hotel. When you arrive you realize that the hotel has received minimum investment for decades and the result is disappointing. Instead of luxury you get maybe 4 stars by international standards. The carpet in the room, for example, should have been replaced decades ago, it has stains everywhere. You don't even want to walk around barefoot in your own room. 

We booked a massage in the spa and were also disappointed. The spa and fitness center seemed run down and the service was not great. While we enjoy having a massage after doing sightseeing, here we only tried once and never again. 

As this is the only hotel we visited in Nepal it is difficult to know if there is anything better in Kathmandu. However having spent weeks traveling in India this was a major disappointment and would not recommend it.

I find this whole scenario disturbing. You pay to get into this world heritage site, and immediately are hounded by guides, that will continue to follow and harass you despite saying "no" multiple times. The place is filthy with trash as well as monkey, dog, and cow excrement. The holy men hanging around the temple seem to only be there to charge money for photo ops. The grounds around the temple are not that interesting, and only Hindus are allowed into the temple, which is understandable. I traveled with an American born Indian Hindu and he was only allowed in after intense questioning about his family origin in India, and after entry, he discovered they were charging money for blessings inside the temple.
The fact that people come here to witness the cremation ceremonies is the most disturbing thing to me. Death rites of loved ones as an attraction that people pay to see while on vacation? Just strikes me as twisted and sad. 
Go to may of the other great sites in Kathmandu instead, like Patan Durbar square, Bodinath, the Monkey temple, etc.

It takes a good long hike to the top if reached from the lake. There are signs everywhere saying to please respect the silense but most people don't care and talk with normal pictures as the take pictures and carry on conversations.

Never seen a shrine in the state of awfull condition. Monkey poop,trash and pheavily polluted stream. Adding to all that smell of burning human flesh from funalral pyres. Some wash their faces,relatives wash the feet of deseased and some searching for treasure in the water at the same time.
Not for the faint hearted.Advised to take precaution if you haven't experienced any thing as such before.
Definitely need a mask, avoid any food or drinks and very good shower after visiting.

for starters - PAPER NAPKINS
almost nothing to eat of substance. One night inexpensive and poorly done Chinesy type food as a large Chinese group was putting on an exhibition. Almost everything is super bland, but that's becoming common everywhere. 
4 star ambiance, 1 star paper napkins, 2 star food, 1 star self-awareness
I've been eating at the dinner buffet for 30 years off and on.
The pagoda is beautiful and peaceful and the views from here are spectacular. best to visit on a clear day

This is a very popular temple of Lord Shiva in Kathmandu, Nepal. Devotees from different countries visit this temple to get the blessings of Lord Shiva. Temple is very big and there are many small temples around the main temple.
Wow !! it is world heritage temple in Nepal. we have visite and spent few hours. we have seen many tourist came here for speritul purpose.

Such a a amazing view from world peace pagoda..One of the most beautiful pagodas perched on a hill top. You get panoramic views of the majestic Himalayas, especially the Annapurna Mountain ranges. It is a silence zone, so you will be at ultimate peace when you visit. A place of Buddhist worship.

This is a pagoda at the top of a hill. To get to it you have to walk some steps, about 20-25 mins of walking up. Its best to take stops while going up, as it is quite steep. The views from the top are majestic.
food good but very slow service!  try the ginger drinks

A must visit place. Where you can have very good glimpse of south Annapurna and adjoining Himalayan range. It is peace pagoda on the top of the hill, where entire pokhara and near by villages are visible.

Tour operators don't include this place in their itinerary unless we specifically include it. An excellent excursion in pokhara not to be missed. It can also be reached by trekking.

Best place nearby international airport Hindu temple old temple and you can see cremation of Hindu culture 
Best for history culture and religion.

We took a boat across the lake and hiked up the steps. It is definitely worth the climb. When we left, we went down the back of the hill, towards Davis Falls and that is also a relatively simple route to follow down.
At the top, the temple is beautiful and peaceful (compulsory quiet in some areas) and the views over Pokhara are amazing. 
Definitely worth the hike and the visit.

I felt privileged to visit this fascinating Hindu religious site with its hundred plus temples, hospice, prayer and cremation sites, and more. Visit with a tour guide to get as much information as possible. Not to be missed.

Charming hotel with beautiful grounds. Rooms are modern and comfortable, with large rain shower in the bathroom. Gym is small but functional with cardio, machines, and free weights. Staff are super nice and helpful, Jhapad in the breakfast team deserves a special mention: warmly greeted me every morning and remembered my order from the first day.
OVERALL WE HAD VERY GOOD EXPERIENCE AND WILL RECOMMEND TO OUR FRIENDS. THE STAFF IS VERY COOPERATIVE AND HELPFUL. WE LOVED THE VARIETY IN ALL MENUS.
Great location for sunrise and sunsets either from rhe temple or the surround area. Plenty of restaurant og little shop. You will need a taxi or other means of transportion.

I have had a very ugly experience the day before yesterday at this place. Very dangerous it is to go to shanti stupa. Please choose not to go if you are traveling alone because the beauty of any place can't be more than your our life and belongings. I left my bag at the stupa while clicking pictures and getting lost in the beauty of that place and all my id proofs, money and passport were in there. I came down and realised so went up. They were closing the enterence that time and the guard totally ignored me when I was saying that my bag is in there. Then I stood there hopelessly for another 30mins to understand that an exit gate is open now for those who are already in there. I went to that gate and started shouting for help. Thank God for this foreigner who saw me jumping and shouting and he asked the guard that why are you not giving her the bag back. He saw the guard picking it. Visiting Pashupatinath Temple was a powerful and moving experience. The ancient architecture, spiritual atmosphere, and rituals by the Bagmati River left a lasting impression. Watching the harmony of life and death—pilgrims praying just steps away from cremation ceremonies—was both humbling and eye-opening.

The temple complex is rich in culture and history, with sadhus adding a mystical charm. I recommend visiting early in the morning for a more peaceful experience. It’s a must-visit for anyone interested in spirituality, culture, or simply seeking a deeper travel experience

The Peace Pagoda is one of a series of similar structures built around the world by the Japanese to promote peace. Allow 3 hours to do this place justice. Many people do a circuit - starting with a boat ride across Phewa Lake. The walk up the hill takes about one hour. From the top you get a brilliant view of Pokhara,  the lake and the Annapurna mountains beyond. You can continue the walk down the other side to Devis Falls. The brilliant white stupa has four Buddha statues on each side, one showing Buddha at his birthplace Lumbini (also in Nepal). Look out for a grave of a Japanese monk who was killed by anti-Buddhist extremists during the construction of the stupa.
It is one of the best place to be while visiting beautiful Pokhara. It can be reached within 15 minutes ride from Lakeside. The route which leads to it shows views of the city.

Place holds lots of historical and religious value. I felt connected to spiritual side while visiting there. And Hindu culture and tradition is really something and its great and beautiful. I  would love to visit it again in the future

The Pokhara Grand Hotel team is completely professional. They can arrange tours (even helicopter flights) to suit the needs and budget of tourists. The guides are attentive, helpful, and know the area very well. They speak very good English. We had a truly wonderful time with them.
Not so interesting. You are not allowed to visit the main place if you are not Hindu. We just see the temple & the ghat from top.

2 British ladies travelling together for Tihar. Lovely oasis in middle of chaotic Kathmandu. Did not feel need to complain of feedback about any issues there and then however would like to comment for improvement reasons.
I would suggest 3 star by European standards so rather pricey / difficult to book local excursion is bus ticket to Bandipur.....much easier doing it on 'high street' / pricey and not nice wine by UK standards (its imported) / bar shuts prompt at 23.00 so no night caps (missing an opportunity?) / pool wasnt well designed ie low water and tiles looked dirty so not eay to get into, just ladders and pool coffee service was hit and miss / breakfast room was long walk but I belived was moved closer during our visit (we werent impressed with food anyway so went out).

This hotel looks nothing like the pictures on the website. Rooms in the main building are not well maintained. Service is hit or miss. The hotel charges ridiculous rates and then denies it. When asked for a restaurant recommendation, the "concierge" sent us to a group tour restaurant that takes tourists by the bus load. The food was terrible and the "show" was loud and annoying. Our better meals were found on our own. On the last day, we went to the front desk to confirm our transfer. The front desk sent us to the concierge. The concierge then called the front desk to confirm. Wow.

You can do much better in Kathmandu for much less money - avoid.

We went up here to view sunrise, and the view is spectacular, even if the clouds were obscuring the Annapurna Range.  It is a beautiful and peaceful place.  Get a ride up as far as you can, or it is a long way (in the dark for dawn).

Third time at the Y&Y.  We stay here because it's convenient to people that we visit in Kathmandu.  This visit, the hotel was busy with a large group meeting.  Though advertised as a 5-star hotel, the accommodations in no way merit this rating.  The rooms are not well maintained.  We stayed in the newer section, yet the closets have a mildewed odor, and the carpets are not particularly clean.  Only two bath sized towels are doled out per day. 
It's worth having breakfast here!  Really great with fresh pastries and an array of cuisines.  The lounge has been the best respite for us after a busy and noisy day on the polluted streets of Kathmandu.  Good bar snacks to accompany a much needed gin and tonic.

This temple is dedicated to  Pashupati, a form of Shiva and is near the Bagmati River in Kathmandu. It is a World Heritage Site It was built in the 1600s to replace the previous one, destroyed by termites

Has Gaia jumped the shark?
This resto and cafe may be resting on its laurels and the benefit of being located in the main tourist area near key hotels. We had two dinners and a breakfast here, mainly because it was very close to our hotel and it was so highly recommended. The outdoor patio, touted as romantic and enjoyable, was so noisy from traffic and loud music that it was anything but relaxing or romantic. Our chicken was tough and leathery and the wine was only okay. Bad jazz was screaming from overhead speakers making conversation difficult and cars, trucks and motorbikes constantly roared by the main gate. The poor staff were extremely harried and were running around, chattering constantly trying to keep up. For dessert we had an excellent yoghurt with cinnamon and an ordinary Banana with nuts and chocolate. The banana was not ripe and the chocolate was only semi-sweet.
The next day we tried their breakfast, but inside to avoid the noise. The prices were reasonable  and there was good variety from eggs to cereals to yoghurt. My scrambled eggs, however, had too much vegetables, peppers and onions and not enough egg or cheese.
To give Gaia a second chance we went back a week later for dinner. I had the Nepalese set meal with a peanuts and potato starter, which was okay. For our main meal we had chicken curry with rice and fried vegetables. This was the first tender meat we had in Nepal. The lentil soup, however, was plain, boring, tasteless and watery.
It's worth it to go there if it's convenient. And the breakfast is good. For dinner, I would prefer the Delices de France.

It was interesting to see the back to back cremation ceremonies through the day and it is indeed true how the Hindu's believe that death is only one stage in their lives and the body is only a medium to host a soul.
Life is embraced on one side of the river, death on the other. Bring your sense of wonder and leave a piece of your heart.

This UNESCO site has a 1000 rupee admission for tourists. The temple is only open to Hindus, but anyone else can observe the body washing and cremation rituals that take place in an open space along the river banks. There is not much shade so be prepared for to stand or sit in the sun.
The temple itself is like many others in the region, but the views from the Stupa looking across at the lake, town and mountains is rather beautiful
Needs a bit of climbing, surrounded by mountains. one of the sacred place for Buddha devotees. The view is very nice and the photos come out really well.

The lack of signage and direction is what makes this place so frustrating. We wandered around not really knowing where to go until we were barked at by staff and redirected to a poorly advertised ticket booth. After paying 1000 Nepalese Rupee each we were asked if we wanted a guide and we declined. We appreciated the offer but had already paid for a few guides at previous attractions and just wanted to go at our own pace this time. We had sort of assumed that if we made our way up to the river we would be able to see the cremations taking place but we seemed to be fenced off from the river so we followed along the fence line trying to find out how we could see the river. Other people seemed to be standing on the other side of the fence but we could never work out how they got there which was so frustrating. And it wasn’t just a matter of staring through the bars because there was two lots of fencing with a gap in the middle so we couldn’t get close enough. None of the other tourists seemed to have a guide and even though the temple grounds cover a vast area we seemed to quickly exhaust the areas that were accessible. 

There were these huge concrete steps that seemed to go on forever but we were pretty reluctant to go to the top of those. We didn’t really know where they led and we were struggling a bit with the air quality so getting up those steps really did feel like going up Mt Everest. We realised though that everywhere else was a bit of a dead end and having paid for the attraction we wanted to get some value out of the experience. Once we got to the top we followed along a path that seemed to go on forever. People were walking in the opposite direction so we were concerned that at the end of this trek we may have to turn around and the stairs had started to descend so it wouldn’t all be downhill on the return. I felt as though we were walking parallel with the river but the river was completely obscured from view, we could only see snatches of it through gaps in the trees. Perhaps there were no cremations happening that day or perhaps I didn’t really understand the point of the tourist attraction. We speculated that they intentionally make it so unclear so people resort to paying for a guide but we were too stubborn. Anyway, after walking for what seemed like forever we exited the temple on the opposite side which did lead us out to the river but there was nothing particular to see there. 

I don’t mean to sound so whingey but it did cost us 2000 Rupee altogether. Overall it was a bit disappointing.

The trickiest part is the place where thy burn dead bodies. It's hard to look at

We chose to walk up the steps and it took us about 45mins. Lots of huffing and puffing but lits of opportunities to rest if you need to and a cafe about half way. We had considered hiking another way but when we spoke to our reception they said there was a 10% chance of being robbed but we wouldn't be killed!! The boatman waited for us and so we had a deadline but it would have been good to have had more time just chilling in the restaurant. Stunning views and peaceful. I believe you can also take a taxi there too.
ok place, I don't understand why they are high ranking really. Menu looks approximately the same as other restaurants and service was maybe  bit more attentive but nothing special..
Beautiful peace pagota, with a beautiful view over the city. Very touristy, try to go in the morning to beat the crowds!

The world peace pagoda on top of Ananda Hill is a place you definitely have visit while in Pokhara.A must visit place where you can  have very good glimpse of mountain ranges.It is an excellent excursion in Pokhara which is not to be missed .

Spent a couple of nights at the Yak & Yeti Hotel following a trip to Everest Base Camp.  This was a last minute change to our itinerary from what was supposed to be a couple of nights at the Gokarna Forest Retreat.  The one redeeming aspect of the change was that the Yak & Yeti was located in the heart of Kathmandu.
The foyer entrance is very impressive, while the buffet lunch, and to a lesser extent, the buffet breakfast are a nice way to saviour the delights of fresh food again.
I was a little disappointed in the room given this hotel was rated five star. The size of our twin share was on the small side while the fittings were dated somewhat, along with the worn floor coverings, especially in the corridor.  The external gardens could certainly do with a makeover as they were looking a tad tired.
Could not fault the service staff as they were considerate and very pleasant throughout our stay.  Overall, I'd rate this hotel 3.5 to 4 star.

On a hillock , about an hour's drive from Pokhara centre, is this Buddhist temlpe build by Japan organisation , after the second world war, to promote non violence. The white coloured wonder oversees the distant Annapurna range of mountains and presents the tourist a grand breath taking view of Pokhara and its famous Phewa lake.
The Peace Pagoda is the first of its kind in Nepal, the second one is said to be in the Birth Place of Buddha.  The Pagoda is 115 feet tall and 344 feet in diameter and one of the major tourist attractions of Pokhara. It has got two tiers The second tier consists of 4 statues of Buddha gifted as souvenirs from Japan , Sri Lanka , China and Lumbini.
We went to the foot of the hillock bya cab and the walked atop for about 15 mts to reach, On the way there are some small cafes selling snacks and soft drinks.
A very good place for a tourist not to miss in Nepal.
Pashupatinath Temple is the oldest .Hindu temple in Kathmandu. It is known for certain when Pashupatinath Temple was built
Magnificent views, peaceful environment, tremendous history - it is work the hike . I can't imagine going to Nepal and not taking the time to visit this historic and spiritual place.

It is one of the beautiful temple I have visited, as soon as you enter the temple you see the Huge Nandi and the doorstep...The main shivalinga can be viewed from all the four sides, but once you are inside the sanctrum, you can see only 3 faces of Shivlinga, and for the fourth one you need to enter from the front. Main sanctrum has only natural lights which is very nice to preserve. Around the temple, you  will have small temple sof Bhairavnath and about 501 small shivalingas.

I found the temple interesting which had mix of Hindu and Chinese architecture (the adobe)
Avoid going on Saturday as it is rush day, and there is no system of queue (though is queue but it is largely mismanaged) on others days you could have peaceful darshan.

The hike was great, but the peace pagoda was average. Just one building that you can't go into, and there isnt much more to do at the top. Worth the hike, but look into other things to do in Pokhara first
The British Afternoon tea was wonderful! Nice lounge with garden views. Would recommend a visit to enjoy the afternoon tea and ambiance.
A very peaceful and well maintained site to visit. It was a calming place out of the busy and bustling streets of Pokhara.
What a privilege to visit here, sharing in the funeral ceremony of the people's loved ones, learning more about their religious beliefs and customs, highly recommend a visit.

We visited the temple on a Friday afternoon and there was a ceremony ongoing. Its good place to learn more about the Hindu culture with a guide to explain what is happening however you might feel uncomfortable witnessing the whole process of the ceremony.  As for us, we had left the area right before the cremation of the remains as its really awkward witnessing someone mourn. We were there for almost 2 hours but the ceremony was not yet finished so we decided to leave. Bring a mask with you when visiting the place and a NPR 1000/-  entrance fee for non-SAARC national.
Very interesting to see cultural and ritual of Hindu temple and people in Nepal. But they didn't clean river. Holy Spirit river

This was an interesting place to visit. 
The funeral Ghats were very interesting, but it felt a little wierd watching someones funeral from the other side of the river.
As a westerner I was not allowed into the temple as only Hindu's are allowed inside.
This was a bit disappointing given it costs USD$10 to enter the complex

The peace pagoda is beautiful with beautiful views of the surrounding areas. It is however a little under "described". There is a lack of information when you actually visit it so best read up a bit before hand!

Its pretty enough and worth a look if you fancy a walk and a look. The views are however, amazing!

I love to be in Pashupati, it’s very special holy place for locals. You are allowed to see cremations and rituals. Some Sadhus might allow you to take pictures for a little donation. 
Some of the architectural complexes are under reconstruction.

There was a time where I used to goto Gaia everyday. I loved it. But recently they've dropped the ball, the food is often sub par, at Gaia standards.
Still have good steaks, and pork chops. The 'Jhole Momo' is one of a kind in Thamel.

We had a very nice time over our anniversary. Very hospitable staff . We enjoyed Chimny rest . Special thanks to Sudha as helped give us the room of our choice . Also made our anniv special . muskan in guest relations was very helpful

this hotel was stayed for prince harry of england. the good hotel. but very cold. out of the hotel have lot of shop, japanese restaurant.  wifi need to pay if you book through travel agent. no tour board. good view of surrounding.
Beautiful views but very disrespectful tourists shouting everywhere. Such a shame. No matter how hard the guard tried people just shouted everywhere and at everything.

Every time I come here I see some kind development around the temple. Temple area is under renovation since a decade and progress can be seen. Very clean and well managed! Non-Hindus are not allowed inside the temple area, however they can have a nice view from river side where crimination is done. A beautiful view from this point is guaranteed. Take a guide and ready to hear stories and tone around. Am sure you will love this beautiful historic place. 

Hindus will definitely love every moment! If you have time, try to visit around 7pm when aarti takes place at river side. Peaceful and nice experience. 

Do not miss!
amazed by the stories told by mr. Deepak from Alphine club of himalaya, the full trip was so amazing and i decided to explore more about the hidden stories in each temples.
Great views and coffee places - nice visit. I took a taxi there and opted not to walk from town. If it’s hot out - I think better.

I was a bit disconcerted when I arrived at the airport, having confirmed my arrival and pickup only the day before, to find I was absent from the list. I was even more disconcerted when we finally arrived at the hotel, and there was no reservation for me, even though I produced their emailed confirmation.  Having travelled for over 24h, all I wanted was a shower and a bed - and after about an hour that was finally produced!

My room was spacious, comfortable, and looked down on a pleasant garden and swimming pool.  Curses! I had not thought to bring a costume, and there was no dressing gown. In fact, in 10 days, I never once saw anyone swimming.

Dinner was a buffet, which sounds boring, but was really, really good. The service was quite over the top - leave the table for an instant, and everything was cleared away, and someone might well have grabbed your seat by the time you had collected the next dish! There were some delicious soups to start; a range of curries with rice and papadums and other fixings; quite often a roast with a wide range of vegetables; salads galore; and puddings to die for.  Suffice it to say that I put on 4kg during my stay.

The location was great, a quiet paradise down an urban alley. There were occasional curiosities - the lifts sometimes hiccupped; the carpets were vacuumed regularly but really needed a good scrub; and the light switches in the bedrooms needed an expert Pelmanist to remember what did what. There was a lot of dust in the air from the reconstruction of the conference facilities - which really need reconstruction, beautiful as they are. In the Regency room there were two plug points.  Have you ever seen grown men weep in frustration as their cell phones die for lack of power? And the internet was decidedly underwhelming.

We experienced heavy dust in our room which we noticed in the morning only. The whole night we were coughing without understanding the fact that this was due to the polluted air in our room. The room was polluted with the dust coming out of the airconditioner in the room. We have stayed in this hotel several times in the past also due to its good location but this time our stay in Yak and Yeti Kathmandu can be categorically marked as a 'Life Threatening Experience' for us. People with asthamatic problems must be careful.

Not sure if this is rated 5 star but it only deserves 3 stars. It was probably a grand hotel at some time in the past. It is well located near shops and famous sites.
We stayed twice in November. first time on floor 2 which was much better than than the ground floor. The second experience on floor one which is the ground floor was very disappointing. Room smells damp, carpet is filthy, there is only one bed side lamp, wifi has to be paid for, the air-con is totally inadequate [ far too hot and cannot be adjusted], there is no fridge or mini bar  and the bathroom needs an up grade [ towels look like they are 5 years old].  The breakfast area is over crowded. The offering was ordinary. for example fresh fruit consisted of two offerings. 
There is a swimming pool and tennis court. I swam in the freezing water.
I think until a little money is spent on the infrastructure you should look for others but do it carefully for sadly there are few good hotels on offer.
I will say the staff was pleasant and helpful.

Colorful and interesting glance into another culture.  A fascinating place to wander a bit.  Complete with yogis, monkeys and vagrant dogs. Having a guide made it much more intelligible to a benighted westerner.

Pashupati Nath is an incredible holy site to visit. For families, be aware that there are bodies being cremated on the river. Having a guide can be very beneficial, just be sure to discuss price up front to avoid confusion with your guide later on.
Great experiences with view of the Hymalayas, nice and helpful staff with smiles. Food diverse and well served. Clean room. Close to center.

This restaurant is near the holy himalaya hotel where i stayed, the food was okay. Wifi sometimes on and off, have indoor and outdoor area. Ordered chicken kebab but it came out like chicken satay with curry sauce. The waiters are nice and polite.

The room air conditioner was not working and room was changed. In the changed room, the toilet flush was not working properly.I would strongly recommend the maintainance to check all the facilities in room to be on working condition before the room is allotted to any guest.

One on the most holy of Hindu sites in Nepal! From across the banks of the river I had the honour of watching as the bodies of those recently passed were prepared for cremation, placed on the pyre and set ablaze. There are about 8-10 pyres you you can see various stages of the process. Once the body is completely reduced to ash it is placed in the river which flows into the most holy Ganges in India. This was an experience I won't soon forget.

Nothing exceptional in the whole monument but the surroundings were something to really admire ... a sweep of the lake and the Annapurna range (if I had a chance to see it - it was cloudy day when I visited this morning).
Must visit Hindu temple in Kathmandu. U can see burial & prayers and it has Hindu religious significance attached to it.

I love this restaurant that one of my tour guides recommended and have had excellent food and service. They are off a side street so it’s quiet and not flooded with tourists. The hummus was delicious, the Nepali set meal incredible and their lasagna incredible. And prices are local. It is certainly worth the trip here!

Good food; nice ambience, but the most atrocious manager / cashier I have come across in the hospitality business.

Just back after an horrific experience which puts a damper on an otherwise excellent 9 day holiday in Khatmandu and Pokhara. We chanced upon this restaurant as it was outside our Hotel (The Mulberry). 

The Thupka soup and the Avocado salad we started off with were both rather nice and we decided to round our meal off with hot apple pie topped with a scoop of Vanilla ice cream. We were surprised that the so called Applie Pie was only the apple stuffing and the encasing pie or crust was missing. We brought this to the notice of the person who served us and he said he would check. He did not return for a while and we requested another waiter to bring us the manager who we could see sitting behind the cash counter. Five minutes pass by and still no waiter or manager came to us.

Finally we walked to the counter to talk to the manager only to find him absolutely defensive and claiming that a proper slice of pie was served and we were complaining for no reason. We tried to explain to him what had happened and he refused to accept our statement. He went to the extent of getting racist and saying that all INDIANS behave in such a manner at which point both my wife and I were furious.  We asked him for his name which he refused to say. We found out later from another staff that his name is Sarosh.

A most horrific experience to an otherwise lovely holiday.

Sadashiv Bhatt, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
Big and nice temple for devotees though it remain closed from 2 pm to 5 pm . A small river is at back side of temple . A must visit
This is one of the best places I saw in my trip in Nepal, you can see the lake from this place, and also the Himalayas.

Had visited this Buddhist Pagoda in Pokhara a long back ago even though it was off the itinerary. This Pagoda is located on a hill and is a popular tourist attraction. It is also known as 'Shanti Stupa' by the locals.

This Buddhist Pagoda was built by Buddhist monks belonging to the Nipponzan Myohoji Buddhist order. It is visited by locals as well as foreign tourists throughout the year. To get to the Pagoda, had to climb 400 steep steps which was the hectic part. However, it was worth the climb. Before entering the Pagoda complex, there is an entrance gate with a Japanese inscription. Also, there are guest houses, restaurants, shops etc. On the top, there was a garden in front of the Pagoda. There is a tourist information office just before the garden. It was so peaceful on reaching the top. 

This whitewashed Pagoda houses the golden Buddha. Footwear should be removed before entering the Pagoda. However, a code of conduct should be maintained. One can get amazing views of the Annapurna mountain range, Phewa lake and Pokhara city from the top. There is a Japanese Buddhist monk that welcomes tourists with a smile in the vicinity. Also, there is a seating area where tourists can sit & relax. However, there is no entry fee. It is not suitable for senior citizens having leg problems.

This Buddhist Pagoda is an ideal holy place of worship for those who would like to seek blessings. It is a must visit place and should not be missed while in Pokhara.
Excellent view point from this place   If you in Pokhara don’t miss to visit this place!!!!  You can see nice view whole Pokhara city as beautiful lake side ❤️🇳🇵💃🇳🇵😘😘💕❤️🙏

A friend and I hired a taxi from the lakeside neighborhood up to Shanti Stupa, and I'm glad we did because the World Peace Pagoda is interesting and the views are spectacular. Please respect the signs asking for silence whole visiting the stupa!

It's a great place to visit after walking the stairs to the top lined with stalls and small restaurants. Best coffee and tea can be found at one place along the way. Gorgeous stupa at the top with great views.

I have lived in Nepal for several years and out of the many tourist activities advertised in Pokhara I would the stupa to be most worthwhile. I took my family there while visiting and we enjoyed the boat ride, hike, and beautiful atmosphere of the whole journey.

We hired a boat on the lake, and then moored it ourselves and climbed up (left our bags at a bar at the base). We were 3 young(ish) fit guys and we got to the Peace Pagoda in 25 minutes. Nice that it's free entry, great views over the lake, city and mountains in the distance. Highly recommend it.
We went to Pashupatinath temple last December. The place was amazing. Got to experience other exotic culture. Hindu culture is amazing and it was one hell of amazing expereince

If you are visiting Kathmandu for the first time, you must visit Pashupatinath Temple. Wonderful group of temples with a lot of mythology around it. From temple architecture point of view as well, there is a lot to explore. You can hire a guide as well to understand more.

paahupatinath temple is must important place  to visit for all human being, 
where  you can enjoy  with  many  hindu  cultural  activities !!

This is most important reason for many Indians to visit Nepal. This temple on the bank of river Bagmati is world famous and is frequented by many Hindus for religious purpose. It has four gates and the main gate of temple opens at 4am but all four gates of main temple open at 9 am only for few hours. Apart from Pashupati main deity there are many small statues of other Hindu gods especially Bhairav Ji which is huge and unique in the world. People do religious ceremonies on the banks of river as cremations are on the premises of the temple.
A very holy place, and very interesting to watch the dead being burnt on the Pires..! Kids diving into the thilfy river for gold or anything else of value..!

Interested in seeing this ancient ramshackle Hindu temple, I took a taxi here from the domestic airport (for Rs400) and paid another Rs1000 to enter. I declined a guide. 

It was at the time of a traditional cremation ceremony, so it was quite crowded by the Bagmati river bank. The river is very polluted. There were bonfires burning as part of the ceremony.

I didn’t have a map or guide book so I just wandered around. It was pretty hot so I only stayed an hour and a half, I didn’t see everything. Also only Hindus can enter the temples. As a Westerner and tourist, a few people wanted my photo, which was ironic, since I was there to witness them. The locals seemed lovely! One girl even gave me directions to Boudha stupa.

There are some brightly yellowed dressed Shadu (holy men) who will pose for money.
The row of temples had a lot of shiva phallic idols and animal statues.
It would be interesting to read and learn more about the symbolism.
My advice, read up before you visit.
The experience you get after climbing 15 minutes to the top is not worthy. Although there's one amazing coffee shop on the way which offers amazing organic coffee with nice views.

Pashupatinath Temple is an incredible spot, especially if you love photography. The place is filled with vibrant colors, from the clothing of the sadhus to the offerings and the temple itself. It’s also a significant place for cremations, which might be intense but is part of the deep spiritual experience here. Definitely a unique and colorful atmosphere that’s worth a visit when you're in Kathmandu!

Great hospitality, food was excellent and staff is very responsive. The hotel is beautiful and an oasis of comfort. 
We enjoyed our stay

its just ok not excellent staff are nice but quality of food is not appreciate  may be keep changing cook every month so on..but people keep going there as its became one of the main hubb for local political palce where people came and talk more than then eat..just chit and chat.

If you want to have a half day walk this is a good trip. I took a boat to the other side and then walked up the hill. The Peace Pagoda is impressive but the view to the Annapurna range is impressive. From there I walked through the royal forest back to Pokhara which I enjoyed a lot.

Good food but getting the attention of a waiter to pay the bill took nearly half an hour. In the end we had to get up and go to pay because we had things to do! That was disappointing.

Best to visit early in morning when it is much cooler. Nice welcoming for the guest.Comfort and great ambience.Food is also great and nice place to have dinner with family and friends.

I took the boat across the lake to the starting point for the hike up the many, many stairs to the Peace Stupa.  It took me about 45 minutes to the top, passing through some village houses and forest.  The stupa is very nice, and there are several coffee houses and food spots at the top.  I wish I knew the name of the coffee house (it is the furthest one from the stupa in the row of shops ) because the coffee was great, and it was the cleanest bathroom (not western, sorry folks) I have seen in Nepal and had both liquid soap and water.  Took the longer way down around the lake, which was a quiet walk through the forest.

Our group of about 60 persons arrived Pokhara on 25/3/2025 and dep on 27/3/25 for Bhairahawa. We enjoyed visiting temples, museum, lake, shopping etc. Had lovely time and the Grande Pokhara hotel provided us excellent hospitality and the staff were extremely courteous and friendly.
