This is my second trip to nepal, on this trip I visited kathmandu, pokhara and Chitwan but I stayed pokhara for 3 nights and I visited all around pokhara. The world peace pagoda (stupa) its a Buddhist pagoda. It was in really amazing place we took boat and walk 45 min to reach there from lake side pokhara. A really good views of lake, city, hills and mountains from there. Highly recommended this place.
Temple is guite big but you cant get inside. Besides its a long walk up so its better to go by motor or taxi. But it is still worth to see it becouse of great view for Pokhara.

The visit to this temple was both moving and thought provoking...a guide took me around and explained that the body after death was cremated on the same day according to the religious practice...

The body is washed and wrapped in a white cloth and all the family are involved in the cremation ceremony which is not a sad event but a celebration of the life...

When the body is prepared for the cremation a taper is placed into the mouth and a male member of the family light up the taper!

An experience I shall never forget...

It is worth a visit if you are in Kathmandu and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site. On the left hand side of the temple you can see cremation of bodies. There are lot of Hindu devotees who come to visit the temple. However unless you are a Nepalese or Indian Hindu you are not allowed to enter the temple which is a shame
When we went there there were 2 bodies being cremated and 3 waiting to be cremated.  Made for a very somber visit.  All in all we are glad we went.

After a short row boat ride from the lakeside to get to the walking path, the short, strenuous hike to reach the Peace Temple was well worth it. The temple is much larger when you get to it than it seems from below. It has two levels - one for tourists and one for Buddhists who can enter the temple. The views of the lake, Pokhara city as well as the magnificent  Annapurna range of mountains is spectacular.It is well worth a couple of hours to visit this attraction.
It is new without character, it was closed after we drove and climbed up in very hot weather. Nice view of mountain peaks.

As a devote of lord shiva, I always go there on Monday alone or with my family. Such a nice temple which symbolises Hinduism. It gives a different vibes about religions . I feel blessed and happy to have Such a beautiful place in nepal.

A interesting place to see. Beware of the scamming tour guides and monks. 

Tickets are 1000 to get in.

This is a UNESCO world heritage site but is sill very active. When we visited and I presume everyday there were several cremations going on. It is a little shocking to western eyes. It was a glimpse into another culture that is memorable.

Beware!  This hotel lies beyond belief.  I had inquired about the hotel's policy on guests.  They informed me that local Nepalese are not allowed in stay in rooms with foreigners, when asked if it was the hotel's policy or the governments they said the governments.  They lie.  There is no such policy.  I continually questioned them and asked for proof, they refused and still informed me of the same thing, that it is illegal for local citizens, ESPECIALLY WOMEN to stay with foreigners in Nepal. It is a complete lie.  There is no such rule or policy in Nepal.    They refused to site specific government information about it.

I believe that this hotel just does not want locals to stay with guests, period.  That maybe there own policy, but lying about it makes them look stupid and pathetic.  

I refused to stay at this hotel because of my email exchange with them.  This hotel is ridiculous, lies to customers and is discriminatory towards foreigners.    

STAY FAR AWAY!  I am quite sure if they reply to my review that either they will deny such things from happening, I have email proof, or they will say that indeed it is government policy, but still provide either fake reports or no information regarding it just as they did to me.    I have no reason to exaggerate the truth, I was very interested in staying here until I received constant lies from them.   Again, avoid!   Stay in Thamel instead. Save your money.

The temple complex is huge and the whole place is beautiful, the nearby shops selling religious items add to the beauty and sanctity of the temple. Here Rudraksh is famous and one can see almost everyone wearing a rudraksh mala. The temple is pristine in its glory, the main temple has 4 deities of Lord Shiva carved into one single stone so one can view the beauty of the Lord from all 4 angles during the pradakshina. It is a known fact that the King of Nepal himself used to do the pooja of the lord. A must see on every visitor's itinerary visiting Nepal.

Travelling here as a group, and you're quite protected from being hassled by hawkers. Once you understand and respect the religious importance of this place and the process, it's 'not quite' as confronting. We were amazed how many locals just came here to sit and watch the cremations, I think this also helps accept what you witness.
Even though I went here, I wouldn't have thought I'd missed out if I hadn't seen it.

An eye opener. .  I went Saturday the day after 1.3m people went for the festival. 
This place is eye opening, aside from the heavy waft of weed, the Babas in their (very) small loincloths, the creepy foreigners who never went home and of course the cremations at the waters edge, this place had everything for your camera lens to aim at. .  A truly inspiring place. . Dirty and dusty ? Oh yes, definitely, but you expect that, and everyone spitting on the floor. . Welcome to Nepal .  amazing place.

I have been having Gaia breakfast several time but no time to write a review but today I am going to write now .  Gaia is very simple restaurant nice garden and good food friendly staff the Eggs Benedict I like must for breakfast Gaia also have multigrain dough Pizza and lasagna which is very tasty and different then other places. So I would really like recommend these please.
Thank you gaia team keep it up.

Pretty average all around in my opinion. Very nice at atmosphere, coffee was good, friendly and fast service, good internet. But my 390 NPR set breakfast wasn't great, especially for the price. The French bread was a little stale and tasted mass produced. My over easy eggs were underdone with runny whites, my "sausages" were cheap, gross hotdogs, beans were from a can I think. Too many good places to go back here.

Right. Pay attention. Get up early (6-7 am) Get the ferry (570 one way/850 return) across the lake.
Take a deep breath and start the climb. 45 minutes of steps, takes you to the top. Tree lined almost all the way its quite humid but shaded.
You can either return the same way and get the ferry back or...
Take the other steps down, past the shoos and restaurants. Turn left when you get to the car park and follow the 4x4 track down the mountain.
There is no shade and it will take 30 minutes to get to the tarmac road at the bottom.
It us still another 30 minutes walk back, through a village and paddy fields, past the dam and over a bridge. As people who will point you in the right direction 
I'm glad I came back this way but it is easier and quicker to go back via the initial stairs and boat.

Har har Mahadev, Every Hindu most visit at least once in lifetime.
Now many things are managed, nature is preserved too. Om Nama Shivaya

We were really disappointed by this temple. Whilst it was strangely fascinating to see bodies being cremated it wasn’t worth the entry fee (Rs 1000) which we thought we very expensive considering prices in Nepal. 

It was a 30 minute taxi journey from Thamel to the temple. As soon as we got out the taxi, we were hounded by men saying hello, trying to sell things and asking for photos which continued along the walk to the temple and in the walls itself. It was the only place in Nepal we felt unsafe (collectively we have travelled to the majority of Asian countries) due to being three female travellers in our 20s. 

The temple grounds were littered with rubbish and sadly had multiple people begging. There was also a constant hounding from workers offering a tour which we didn’t want. When ascending the steps there are multiple temples and shrines but felt unable to explore them due to the monkeys and men. 

Perhaps without feeling unsafe it would have been more enjoyable but compared to other sites in Kathmandu, it was disappointing with an expensive entry ticket.

Good to see this place. A bit odd though so be sure not to bring children.

There are aggressive monkeys. We saw a monkey bite a man in the arm as a warning. 

Lots of dead bodies being burnt everywhere along the river.

It's all part of the Hindu religion so it's expected but just be aware in case of shock.

Hindus can only go into the temple not tourists. The overall area is ok not too impressive and lots of people wandering the area with mental illness. Or guide was with us and was good.

Property is too old and its showning. Cannot call this even 4 stars. Staff is not that polite.

They do provide free shuttle from airport but one need to inform them separately as they don't read booking details.

Travel desk is ripping money, their prices are too high. I know in hotel travel companies charge more but charging 3-4times is not worth. When asked why urprices are soohigh lady responded security....... not sure for you profit u need to defame ur country.
In a small location you get a lot. The main temple - that non-Hindus can't enter. The crematoria - where the dead are burned. Many small temples. Get a local guide - there's a lot to see.

Location of the hotel is good - near the airport and you can walk to shops. The room was very comfortable and quiet with a view of the garden at the back (only minor concern was not having separate controls for bedside lights in twin room). The staff (with the exception of some in the restaurant) were helpful and efficient.  But there is no free wifi and it's expensive - extraordinary for a "five star" hotel in 2019. The restaurants (Chimneys and breakfast room) were chaotic while we were there, the restaurant service slow with only a couple of dishes suitable for non-meat eaters (in India??), the breakfast area crowded, too small for the number of guests and limited in its offerings compared to other hotels we stayed in in India and Nepal. The restaurant staff did not understand what was involved in preparation of vegan food and we did not get food of a standard we expected. We did have serious concerns about how we were treated with regard to one particular meal and our concerns were listened to by the hotel manager, thanks to our local guide, and to some extent addressed, but we left with the view we would stay somewhere else on return to Kathmandu.

I was so happy I picked this hotel in Pokhara.  My room was very comfortable and had a view over the front entrance.  The bathroom was very good and the bed was comfortable.  I enjoyed my chicken tikka masala in the restaurant - it was a delicious feast for a hungry traveller!

But what made this hotel really special was the marvellous staff.  From the moment I arrived, I was made to feel very special.  The people working at the Pokhara Grand are absolutely delightful.  

And I must mention the collection of rabbits living outside in the grounds.  They are so cute and fun to watch.
It's nice to hike up to the temple and look around but if you are short on time I would skip this one. It does give a nice view over Pokhara and the lake.

Believe me even if your driver/ guide tells you it is a five minutes walk. it is not and if you go during daytime you will sweat out the entire water you took since morning. 
Upon reaching the place, there was peace and calm in the surroundings.
This is one of the very few temples which you should not miss when you visit Nepal. Very holy and well maintained.

Quite a well organized hindu temple than most I have been to in India. It's the only jyotirlingha outside of India. Foreigners and non Hindus (only Buddhists mad Sikhs are allowed) cannot enter the temple to offer prayers. It is said if you take a round of this temple it's almost equivalent to visiting char dham as per hindu mythology. Must visit

Hotel design, heritage is very traditional and authentic. 
But the operations and service is not up to the level. 
(Hope that it can improve in the future.)

A must visit for first timer and repeat visitors. Watching a cremation is a profound existential experience. The atmosphere in the temple grounds is a constant reminder that you are not in Kansas anymore
My tour here was hindered some by the crowd and the hectic parking area.  But after the arrival a hike to and from the Temple,  it was ok.
Shri Pasupathinath Temple, Lord Shiva is the main deity and one of must visirt temple in Kathmandhu, Nepal - This is our Second Nepal Visit and Many Thanks to Lord Shiva
It was amazing experience and the ambiance was quite good. We went for dinner, it was more like candle light dinner. The atmosphere was really amazing too.

So much to learn and so much to understand. Have seen this place at a documentary and I never thought to have the opportunity to be there.
Nothing compares to experience with your own eyes.

So this place is okay, I'll be honest and tell you that I have seen much better temples in my time.

Tourists have to pay to get in can't remember how much but Indians and Locals go free.

So firstly there appears to be more than one entrance, our taxi driver took us to not the wrong entrance but one which entailed a fair bit of walking. 
(Less than the other entrance I'm guessing)
Let's just say we took the scenic route.

Anyway on our walk we saw lots of cremations, we had to tell our 5 year old they were burning logs..

My main advice is that as a tourist if a local offers to take you around, just refuse. 
He will ask for $30 AFTER he's taken you around.
It's a con, he won't show you anything you can't see yourself.
The only thing that he will do is he will take you down a back way and get a 'priest' to pray with you.
The 'priest' is also getting his share of the €30.

If you are a tourist all you need to do is put your shoes in the bag, get a ticket for them, and go for a wander around the temple.
There is the facility to wash your feet should you wish.

Enjoy!

We arrived at the bottom of the stupa via a lake boat and began our climb at roughly 1PM, the boatman advised us to be back by 3PM otherwise he would leave without us.
With that in mind we started climbing fairly quickly but beware it is a long climb and even for the fittest of people it would take 30+ mins. We made it to the top in about 45-50 with a few breaks along the way to enjoy the scenery.
Nothing beats the views and the feeling of accomplishment from reaching the top however, just make sure to be quiet otherwise you will be shushed!
Would recommend walking shoes as the steps are not all the most stable, also would  not advise walking up when it's been raining as even on a dry day the climb down caused a few slips.
The stay was pleasant and memorable. The hotel staff all around were cordial and went above and beyond to be accommodative. Kudos to staff and management.

One thing I can reviewed is the shops/market outside the temple. Most of them selling items for prayers. Love the colourful powder  where they usually use it for kolan. They were vibrant colours. The people are friendly and more than often, the younger males offer to give a tour inside the temple without being forceful (which is nice compared to other attractions).  

My friends went in to have a look but only a Hindu can enter the actual temple. One of my non-Hindu friend just went around the place and witnessed live cremation next to the river. PSA - Definitely not for the faint-hearted. 

For those who wants to enter the temple ground, do prepare 1000NPR and enjoy the activities happening within the area.

This one a bit boring for me , well we walk long way and it’s not impressing much as for example in Myanmar . It’s ok to spend there 20in max .but I would not go there again in future .. got me bored.
Very nice and great place in kathmandu.we have a great time with a family and great Shiva Puja .must visit once

To be honest I was expecting more, the stupa has an interesting history behind it linked to the Japanese and different statues donated by Thailand and Sri Lanka but in all it's glory on the hill it is a fairly simple stupa. The view back across the lake makes the trip up to the stupa worth it.

We took the boat across the lake and walked up to the stupa my son has a balance problem but did manage to walk up and back but it is quite a hike when at the top you get a wonderful view of the city and mountains and there are places to rest and eat also the temple is a good place to visit there are drinks places on the way up the mountain so you don't need to lug any extra things

the complex and the crematorium is a very central attraction and restrictions are in place not to use mobiles inside as they are strict. plenty of shiv lings inside and you may be able to see a funeral at the same time on the banks of bagmati river

It is a nice hike up there. The temple is not the most interesting. I took a boat from Pokahara lakeside (500 rupees) and hiked back through the forests. Not many people do that it seems as I didn't see anybody. It is a beautiful hike through the forest and lakeside back to lakeside.
Nice atmosphere for breakfast - charming outdoor courtyard. The food was nothing to rave about but a good value and good option for breakfast.
Locally it is called as shanti stupa, it basically show the 4 forms of buddha. Apart from that the view/location is very good.

Gaia Restaurant & Coffee Shop is a great place to beat the heat of Kathmandu. You can sit for a spell and sip a coffee, tea or refreshing cooler.

Every time I visited, there were plenty of empty tables.

The food is good and they have one of the best wifi networks in Kathmandu.

I'm staying in this right now in room 434 while writing the review. Property is definitely 5 star however level of service is not more than zero star. Extremely pathetic. While there are numerous things i can talk about that i experienced in last 24 hours, however the biggest one is AC being locked at 23degree in this summer month. I had been following up from last 9 hours now for reducing the temperature as my family of 3 could not sleep at all yesterday night due to the heat. As of now the response received is not proper. First of all, no one attended for initial 3 hours, then once someone came, he went back saying he will inform the engineer. No one again came for next 3 hours. Now, a guy popped up to inform, that ac temperature is locked at 22-23 degree and they can't change it. A manager now offered to instal and extra FAN in the room, shabby !! You pay 20k for this level of service. I'm speechless and don't know whom to talk to. This is waste of my holidays, money and time in setting up things at a so called the best hotel of Nepal

One of the peaceful and quiet place at Pokhara.
Visit to this place is peaceful, can reach by road from Pokhara city. If u like to travel alone or with friends this is the place. From top entire Pokhara city is visible, good natural view all around. If ur a photogenic person then u r at right place. Visit peace temple at afternoon.

Such a marvelous, spiritual, majestic spot.
Take your shoes off to climb to the top. Many visitors, many stairs to climb but level! Peace Pagoda resonated inside me, just filled me with possibilities!

Let's not discuss things which is supposed to be in 5 star Hotel.
I have not found anything extra or special from staff or hotel itself.
But somethings nice I could see like mini lake for geeses and monument in the courtyard ( pics attached). That's all.

One of the worst bakery I ever seen in all hotels around the world. Banana bread just for lough. 2 types of not ripe melons and watermelons. Dirty nuts. Absolutely impossible to lay done because of the flies. They are hundreds there and you can not relax.

One of the timeless classic hotels in Asia, the Yak & Yeti is a great place to relax in Kathmandu.  Beautiful grounds, nice rooms, great food and a super friendly staff make this one of my favorite places.   Plus the price point is extremely reasonable.

As we read in Trip Adviser, we were expecting not just a good food but also a good service as we entered to this restaurant with my family. that didn't happen here.  First of all we had to find our own table. Second, we saw a customer in the corner table calling waiter several times and my wife had to tell waiter that customer in the corner is calling. Third, we had to ask for menu. Drinks came finely together and I personally enjoyed, but the meal was ok.  Time to time we had to go to the counter and ask for hot water or nepkin paper. Table weren't clear until we asked waiter.  We had to ask twice for check. Cafe is quite cosy, quite and nice but bad service.

We had a light dinner  at this popular restaurant in Thamel. The chicken momos were not that good while my hamburger, which I could not finish, was tough and chewy.  Beer was ok. Though prices were inexpensive , this was not a good meal.
Tried to have cold beer but tooks more than half an hour. But the Staffs are really great.
There are different ways to get up to the Pagoda, walking through the forest is the most enjoyable one. It is a calm place with a great view - good for meditation. No entrance fee.

Gaia Restaurant, located in the heart of Thamel, truly stands out as one of the best dining spots in the area. As someone who frequently visits various restaurants with clients for lunch or dinner, I can confidently say Gaia consistently exceeds expectations.

Most of my clients are from Europe, and they often rave about the quality of the food at Gaia. The pizza, lasagna, sizzlers, and fresh salads are always a hit. Each dish is crafted with care and bursting with flavor.

The staff is exceptionally friendly and attentive, always ensuring a pleasant dining experience. The ambiance of the restaurant adds to its charm—calm, welcoming, and perfect for both casual and formal gatherings.

Gaia has become a trusted choice for me and my clients. If you’re in Thamel and looking for delicious food paired with great service, Gaia Restaurant is a must-visit!

I chose the Yak and Yeti based on location and some photos I saw online.   It's a decent hotel but the rooms are not that nice.  The wifi was very slow also.  Breakfast wasn't that great but lunch seemed better.   Employees friendly and security guards always smiling.   The room was clean and it was quiet which are important to me.   Just expected a bit nicer furnishings.
My husband and I had a wonderful meal of small plates, perfect for our late evening arrival to the Yak & Yeti Hotel.  Our server was extremely attentive and helpful.
Food was OK but it took a really long time... price was ok too. Not the best in Kathmandu but not the worst either. Can't do much wrong here. Nice garden to sit outside.
Not much to see when you get up there, but worth a photo or too. A decent climb to get up there, but you can take a taxi or bus.

I'm not a religious person, but enjoy visiting religious places for their architecture, carvings and the peaceful ambiance. However at this place the cleanliness needs to improve a lot. The vendors and priests also keep disturbing all the time. The only good part of my visit was witnessing a group of people singing prayers and dancing.

I had a guest all the way from Australia who were very keen to visit Stupa, too a ride upto the parking and went through up stairs. Wonderful smell of brewing coffee was major attraction. Found a japanese guru doing some chanting rotating stupa was awesome.

Peace temple can be reached by boat and than about one hour hike to the top not recommend is you have knee problem .other way is taxi/veh it drop you at point and than steps take you to top it's good for ppl don't want to hike .from top u have a gr8 view of Pokhara city, lake and mountains

Worth viewing but feels like you are intruding on a family's send off of a loved one via public cremation.  Surreal comes to mind.  but the historic temple buildings are amazing to see and if you don't mind fending off holy men wanting to touch you and then ask for rupees spend an hour or so there.
This is a beautiful sacred space outside Pokhara. A taxi will take you and wait to bring you back. Well worth the effort.

First, the template and surrounding area requires a bit of a walk - perhaps 1/4 mile.  Once back to the area, watching the Hindu traditional cremations along the river is riveting. You don't need to stay too long to see one start or end. Get a guide for this site so you can really get a feel for the process including those that come to die touching the river.

On the first stay the AC in the room did not work. While this was fixed the manager was extremely dismissive of the issue. On the second stay we were upgraded to a suite, which smelled like cigarettes and did not have any international adapters. Nor were any available upon request from the front desk. The front desk assured me they could charge my device and after returning after 1 hour my device had not been charged and had in fact lost power. 

Finally the Wifi Cost 10 US dollars for 24 hours which is outrageous, considering that each of the 7 hotels we have stayed at within Nepal offered free Wifi at much higher speeds. I would not recommend this hotel

I hired a kayak for 800 rupees and paddled across the lake. it's all pretty easy to ad-lib. on the other side, leave your kayak and walk up. I took the track on the left - near by "Typical Restaurant"but I am sure any trek would lead up. AFter 30 mins I reached the top. Great views, ok pagoda. Really good for a walk and to capture some views. Round trip for me was 2 hours, but it budget 3-4 hours.
staff overfriendly but fake, we arrived in grand holiday with a booking that they didn't have, room was not what we had paid for, breakfast was poor. we decided to leave after 2 days.

cleaner than lasdt year. great temple but lack of information on poojas opening hours. admin staff are not interested in selling /canvssing for poojas office opening hours do not align with temple opening hours.
Great views and easy hike up from the lake. Not much to see around the stupa, but still a beautiful site

The first stop on our trek to Mardi Himal 
A Steep climb up from the lake
Great views of phokara and surrounding mountains 
Good information about Temple’s history

This is a Holy temple of Lord Shiva. The temple structure is quite unique compared to other Hindu temples around the world. Only Hindus are allowed into the Temple. Others can be around the premises and go around it.  No photos are allowed inside the temple premises. It's believed that one should visit this temple and get a blessing before going Hiking in Nepal. We were told to do so and we did. Our quest to reach ABC was very smooth. 

At the back of the Temple is the Holy River of Baghmati where prayers and rituals for the demise are carried out. You will need to pay NR1000 for each foreigner to enter.  It's a very rare scene and if you can't take it, better not see it.

The temple was of no interest to me. I much prefer the beautiful panoramic view of mountains and foreground poinsettias to give some flair and colour to photos.
Short climb of about 10 minutes from car park on concrete steps.

I took a boat across the lake and hiked my way up. The hike is all steps and clearly marked signage to lead the way. It took about an hr and a half.
Such a beautiful place. And being silent, makes it so much more special. Check the amazing history before you go.
Excellent food, gracious people (especially Mahesh). Very attentive without being overly so. Cozy rooms. Calming grounds.

So, here is why you should visit the temple and what you could expect.
1.	It is one of the four most important religious sites in Asia for Shiva devotees. 
2.	The largest temple complex in Nepal.
3.	this is UNESCO designated cultural heritage site.
4.	The streets around the temple can show the street selling culture of the country. They sell mostly worship items and other items related to Hindu traditions. 
5.	There are also enough places to eat for cheap if you feel hungry. 
6.	As a foreigner you can experience the Hindu cremation culture. 
7.	Monkeys are also present in large numbers and they are the kings there.
8.	People swimming in the river for holy bathing as well as looking for valuable 
9.	You can also meet sadhus (sages) who have an amazing appearance. You can also meet fortune tellers.
10.	At evening, if it does not rain, then you can also experience the “ aarati” which happens just beside the bagmati river and Infront of the Shiva temple.
11.	The temple is very old so you can also experience the ancient art and architecture of the country.

If you are not a Hindu then you are not allowed to see the inner part of the temple but can just look from outside. The external part is impressive and the adjacent Cremation Ghats on the banks of Bagmati river can be visited by Non-Hindus. It is a personal choice whether you go to see people being cremated or not. It is a macabre place though. However, there are many smaller temples and these are dedicated to Lord Shiva in the same complex..

Beautiful boat trip to the island and S breathtaking hike + pagoda. 
Doesn’t take long to hike up, the view is more then worth it
It's about 40 mins walk from the lakeside to Peace stupa. Very nice view to see the whole Pokhara.  In return, we took boat back to the lakeside.

Hiked there from Pokhara, the path is slightly difficult to find. Look for the gate just after the foot bridge. About one and half to two hours from Lakeside. Views are excellent but the peace pagoda swarmed with jabbering crowds taking selfies. There are signs everywhere asking people to be silent but you that's human nature for you
great destination in pokhara.You have got two option either you go by vehicle or by boat .if you go by boat across you have to walk about 45 min.

Lots of noise and people. beautiful temple. There are funeral pyre at the back of the temple. Its really humbling as there are people of all ages being cremated. Make one think that our time in earth is very limited so its so important to be happy and do what you want to do much as you can. Good place to just watch and relfect. i always go here every time i go to Nepal. Its one of the holiest temple for hindu but it does not matter what religion you are you can still see the temple from the back. There are also holy men. However the proper sadhu are away from the temple in the woods within pasupatinath.

For the price paid, I would have expected the ability to control my room temperature instead of relying on centralised air conditioning, more toiletries and better insulated room. On the plus side, the bed was comfortable and staff were friendly and helpful.

One of the 12 Jyotir Lingas worshipped by devotees from all over the world. Most sacred and spiritually elevating place of worship. Many legends and miracles are associated with this Temple. One has to to leave shoes outside and not to use mobile phone or camera inside the premises. Pl avoid lots of touts roaming around and be careful with strangers. A must visit for all those who believe in Divinity.

We found the reception staff very offhand and unwelcoming. This is the first hotel we have visited on this trip that we were not offered a welcome drink, and this is the most expensive we have stayed at. The bar staff and waiting staff were lovely and friendly. We were told to leave our luggage in the lobby and it would be taken to our room, but after some time of waiting we had to chase it up before it was delivered. The room was very basic, the bathroom door should swing the other way as it makes getting out the bathroom difficult especially in the night in the dark! Suffice to say we are just glad it was just 1 night!
The trek up the steps was well worth it! There were little shops and cafes all the way up. The view of the mountains above and the lake and city below was AMAZING!!!

Took taxi from town lake side 16th street, was 600 one way and started at 1300 one way. No admission once you get there only a donation box if you want to donate. Taxi drops you to the car park at the bottom and you need to walk up stairs. Im no stair climber or trekker but I managed it ok. Stalls along the way, ice creams, coffees, water ect so you can stop along the way and look at the stalls. I stopped for a lovely coffee. Temple its self is another temple, take your shoes off to walk around it. Views are nice over the lake and city. I walked back through the forest to the boats. Lovely walk, again ok for a non walker or trekker. Wear good shoes or trainers, not for slip ons or thongs. Rocks steps most the way down, I wouldn’t recommend if it had just been raining may be very slippery. Took about 45mins to walk down slowly through the forest. People you pass going up and down, i would definitely not enjoy walking up to the temple.
Once at the boats the prices seem not fixed, has a sign on the shop starting at 550 -800 one way back to mainland which i got charged 500, but 2 girls got 550 for 2 people one way, so what ever you can get. From the mainland it was 800 one way so 550 was good i thought!
The boat ride back is peaceful and I enjoyed the way i did the trip up and back.

It is impossible to criticize a place of spirituality. However, I definitely recommend to go elsewhere if you want to find some real buddhist temple. Nepal, and in particular the region around Pokhara, have some of the oldest, most authentic and noblest temples ever, places full of history and in which every stone and painting has incredible tales to tell. Each of these temple has so much more to say than the peace pagoda,  that is just a modern monument. It is only a contemporary building planned by the Nichiren buddhism school, a stream of Japanese buddhism that is very popular nowdays in the western world for its desire-oriented approach. It certainly offers a nice view, and a good example of simple and modern architecture applied to a stupa, so if you have a couple of hours in pokhara you should go. However I rather recommend truly historical sites, such as the Mahendra cave, or the Gupteswar Gupha, or any of the amazing gompas around Pokhara. If you go, I recommend to take on the way back a canoe across the Phewa Lake, and keep a look at the lakesides for the macaques and colorful kingfishers!

I've stayed there twice for business, each time for roughly a week, and neither stay was wonderful. The only reason I stayed there the second time is because the nature of my work required it.

First, the good - the reception, concierge, and lounge staff go out of their way to be helpful. They tried their best to help me with lost items. Sometimes a shift change would mean messages were lost and I would have to wait a day to get them, but they were sincere in their attempts to help. The garden is beautiful despite the birds, and I do think the location is good if you want to get to many different areas of Kathmandu during your stay. The lunches and dinners I had at the Sunrise restaurant were decent. 

Now to the not so good. The entire hotel needs to be renovated- bathrooms have mold, there are regular electricity brown-outs (though after the earthquake this is probably not the fault of the hotel), fixtures fall off, and all of the water in brown at all times - do not drink the tap water. They restrict the number of bottles of water and the number of devices on wifi for each room, which is unusual for a luxury hotel. The wifi is weak at best - remembering this I brought an ethernet cable for the second trip and learned that there are no actual wires in the ethernet ports. I was very tired of the breakfast buffet early on, and noticed that I was often eating lunch around the crumbs left by breakfast guests. And yes, the birds are loud even at night and can be very disruptive if you have jet lag.

In short, the Yak and Yeti is a nice place for a few days, but if you are staying longer or need things to be easy to get business done, it's probably not for you.

Weve had a mixed experience. The hotel iteself is pleasant, but definitely not a 5 star as it is advertised. 
First, the good things. 
Decent buffet breakfast, reasonable prices for lunch and dinner. Most of the staff is pleasant and welcoming. 
The rooms vary, but overall - of a decent quality. Confortable bed. Complimentary bottled water and tea making facilities in the room. 

Now, the not-so-good things. 
You have to pay for the WiFi, and it isnt particularly fast. The 4G you can get from NCell is faster. 
The water in the tap is yellowish in colour. The lifts are antiquated and sometimes temperamental. 

And now - the really ugly stuff, and why I gave this hotel only 1 star. 
Some of our trek clothes gone missing from the suitcase, which was cling-film wrapped and only opened in the hotel to be put into the duffel bags.  We discovered it after we left for the trek. The management denied any responsibility and tried to give us a number of excuses, starting from the suggestion that our stuff was stolen at the airport from the cling-film-wrapped bag to saying that we should have counted things we had in the suitcase after we left the suitcase in the hotel room and went to dinner.  
In addition, there was an attempted break into the iPad - to the point that it was deactivated. The management suggested that this may have happened when the staff was cleaning. 
Bear in mind - the iPad deactivates if the password was entered incorrectly at least 10 times. Additional point - according to CCTV - the staff was in the room for less than 2 minutes - and in this time, apparently, managed to clean the room and to turn down the beds. 
The printouts of the room access had inconsistencies and were reprinted the next day when we asked to lodge the complaint with the police. 
The CCTV has time discrepancies with the room access system, which management had no explanation for. They told us we should ignore the discrepancies, because they are not important. They went as far as to threaten us, in case we diced to publish our experience in the review, and were very upset when we explained that our conversation is being recorded and will be available to the police. 
All in all - I will never recommend this hotel to anyone for a number of reasons: first, because of the disappearance of the clothes, and second, because of the inconsistency between CCTV and room access systems - no one can feel secure, if the security system in the hotel may be tampered with and the management prefers to ignore the problem instead of addressing it. Whats more - this hotel is an embarrassment for the otherwise wonderful Nepalese hospitality and undermines all efforts that other people put in to make Nepal attractive to the foreigners.

There are some experiences in life that as a Western traveller, you can’t really prepare for, and this is one of them. One of the holiest Hindu pilgrimage sites in Asia, there are practices undertaken here that have been happening for hundreds maybe thousands of years.  The complex takes in ten different sites including the peaceful Gorakhnath Mandir where you are surrounded by many Shivalaya’s – Shiva shrines close to a wooded area. There are several busy Hindu temples. As a non-Hindu, you can only view these from the outside, but it is still possible to admire the architecture. There are colourful dreadlocked holy men known as Sadhus, people offering meditation with healing bowls and fortune tellers all derived from the mysticism of history.
The last and most striking images are of cremation. When we visited we saw the family of a deceased person bring down their wrapped body to the rivers edge where they carefully applied purification rights to the head and feet. From here it is taken around 100 meters to a funeral pyre at the edge of the river where a wood structure was already prepared. It is set alight. When the process is finished the ashes are raked into the river. There were at least six of these ceremonies taking place when we visited. It is possible to view the process from across the river at a respectful distance.
Entry to the site is 1000 rupees per person.
