Go this temple if you are seeking for spiritual and psychological healing. Best place in Pokhara to meditate and enjoy entire Pokhara, Lake, River and Himalaya ...

Just an awful hotel, construction work at 6am to 8pm, horrible rooms with bugs in the shower, bad breakfast. Just bad - rude staff on arrival. Do not stay here. The only redeeming feature was the chimney.
If you are travelling Nepal, you see so many temples, so at some stage you do get over it. If you are not over them, then it is nice.

I paid for the ticket to get in and it's just like we're just passing through and my guide was just explained about the heritage history of the site (what a waste of my money/energy to walked esp. so hot)...and I said to him, I want to see the open-air cremation and he says, tourists are not allowed (which is a lie cos I checked online after) I think he was beginning to feel tired but I paid him for my guided tour to get to see them etc. (+tip at the end - mistake!). Interesting place!!!

interesting place despite the 1,000 rupee entrance fee. Very touristy and people asking for money. Fake/ very decorated baze's or holy people posing for a picture...Lots of monkeys as well.. saw their burial ritual.. lots of temples. Huge space. Decently priced items and clean bathrooms... it was worth seeing for the experience but wouldnt go back. Also get a guide to have a better understanding of their culture and not just take photos. I would recommend this over thamel, kathmandu and patan durban square.

Great place to stay in Kathmandu. I would recommend it to anyone. Staff, services, location, etc. all very good. Cleaning staff and guards were also very friendly and helpful. We had some issues with our bookings and they were very helpful in sorting that for us too.
The visit to the temple was nice but it is filthy with stray dogs walking around. If only it was kept clean and tidy the visit would have been better.
Nice Pagoda but not allowed to go in. A steep climb, even from the parking place! Beautiful overview of Pokhara city
One of the best restaurant in thamel with healthy and testy food. Staffs are very friendly and atmosphere is fantastic.

Beware, cheap and racist mentality of security armed guards at temple. I took photo at around 5.45 pm today 19 August and a guard at the door barked and then when I went inside the main door to temple he was standing on left side with a gun he asked me for the phone and then went into delete photos even though they were taken outside. Then when I tried to take my phone back he stared at his gun and then me to scare me, he then shouted this is Nepal, many times and that I need to remember that. Very disgusting behaviour inside main temple, they are the ones disrespecting people coming to the temple. The similar photo he deleted is attached I retook it as everyone (locals) was taking it here. Also I would say to the foreign tourists don't buy 1000 NPR tickets, it's just not worth it as if your not Hindu they won't let you in the main temple even after paying that much. That's the main thing to see the UNESCO historical building! There is nothing else to see! They don't deserve your financial support.

A must visit place for all the devotees. one of the oldest temples here and widely worshiped. suggest to go there in the evnening around 530 or 6 to see the aarati as well which takes place on the banks of bagmati river.

We hired a taxi for 4 hrs so we could visit the peace temple, Davis Falls and the Mountain Museum. The driver did not tell us the Peace Temple was closed due to the loss of life from the land slide that had occurred a couple of weeks before our visit. While I respect the decision, I felt we were duped as the Taxi driver had told us he drives up there on a daily basis therefore would have been aware of the closure. As a visitor I don't appreciate being duped so someone can make money from me!

The route to temple is very scenic through the jungle a good hiking trail even children can enjoy and trek with a caution. My 6 years old daughter hiked on its own. Very scenic view of lake, pokhara city, and annapurna range as well from the top. You may need not to have guide as hoardings are every were showing direction.

Pashupatinath is not a good place to visit. World heritage site but extremely filthy and in bad shape. Cow urine all over and smelly. There are pickpocketers around and criminals around the place where flowers are sold! Beware! The place is best avoided!

1000 RPN entrance fee for foreigners. If you can prove you’re Hindu or Indian it’s free (ie. passport or citizen card or some sort of identification). Non-Hindu people are not allowed in the main temple. There isn’t much to do in the area. Witnessing the cremations would be the biggest highlight, but I personally thought it was weird that such a private matter (mourning the death of a loved one and preparing their cremation ceremony) was publicized at a UNESCO World Heritage site, where tourists are snapping photos and exploring around. Anyway, it’s definitely once in a lifetime experience but I didn’t think it was worth 1000 RPN. It can be emotional seeing the bodies and cremation ceremonies. It’s sad to see the river, where the ashes are poured in, is completely polluted with plastic bottles and garbage which are mainly due to the local children who play in and around the river.

It was a hot climb  to the top if the steps.  Pass the temple there's the cool Elite Cafe with the view. Pass that there's a  dirt path to a smaller hill and over look.  You get a good view of the lake and the KGH Waterfront Hotel ( which we will be staying at ).  Make sure to stop at the "Peace of Mind Cafe" which is located halfway to the Temple.  It's owned by very nice Japanese Expat Mr. Takanaka and his beautiful Nepali wife.  The french toast and coffee here is very good!  Mr. Takanaka was a Paragliding Pilot in Pokhara for 9 years then he opened the Cafe.

As a non hindu i was limited to where i could to.. And that is okay. The history and tradition of the place is immense but it is weird that there is so Much garbage just everywhere in a holy Area as this.

Enjoyed the hike up from the dam side - through neighborhoods then forest. The view from the top is worth it- gives you a perspective of how big Pokhara is beyond the lakeside and of course views of the Himalayas!

Nothing can be profound, touching deeply and facing death in front of the eyes. The realm of Shiva-Mahadeva, the most sacred of the pilgrimages for Shaivites, Vaishnaviites, Tantrikas, Mantrikas and Jantrikas, and all walks of life. NEVER TO MISS!

Very disappointed. We go there by boat across Fewa Lake then walk for 60 mins uphill.  Nothing to see.... if weather is good, maybe a good location to overview Pokhara.  The coffee shop up there is not qualify as well.

The walk up/down is better than the payoff.  There was construction laying down some new masonry at the foot of the temple, employing really young children to carry the concrete.  Not so "peaceful."  There were "silence, please" signs up the temple stairs, which seemed to just be encouraging people to be louder.

It's dirty, full of people, disorganised, they charge you 1000NRS as a foreigner and don't even let you into the main temple. They don't tell you this when you buy your ticket. It's also an active cremation ground, so you will see bodies being burnt and bodies brought over. I'd rather spend my time at the Swayambunath or Boudinath temples where its peaceful and inclusive.

We visited as part of hike to see sunrise over Himalayas. Combined with the gorgeous view of Pokhara, closeup to Mountain View’s, the origin of the temple, and the resident monk chanting it was an ethereal experience. This was at 6 am so different experience with a crowd of people.

About 1.5 hours walking up the hill, you'll see this big peace stupa. The building itself is nice, though you can't climb it unfortunately. The view is very nice. If you have the time and like walking, it's nice. When you climb down you need to rent a boat to cross the lake.
I got experience guide with worm hospitality and unforgettable memories from pariwar holidays team. So I rejoined with this company.

After hearing from most of my friends about the aarti at the Pashupati Nath, I finally visited there. I felt different inner peace within me. The flowing river, wind breeze and beauty of the movement of fire lamp by the Pundits, there was different strong feeling. During the aarti, you could hear 50-100 people clapping and chanting the prayer. I would recomend to visit Pashupati Nath at evening aroung 6:00-7:00.

Was 10 bucks to visit for foreigners and was quite a morbid place. You basically stand on a bridge and u can see bodies burning on both sides of the river for different status classes and family members crying. They have bodies burning 24/7. Probably wouldn’t have gone again if I was to do it all over again. Mostly locals when I was there and mostly i guess was to observe the funeral process. Pretty sad place.

I'm sorry to say that my experience at this hotel was an absolute nightmare. Not only was there construction going on late into the night on a Sunday, but the sound of crows outside made it impossible to get any rest. Despite my complaints, the management did nothing to address the situation, leaving me feeling frustrated and helpless.

I would strongly advise anyone considering staying at this hotel to think twice. The lack of consideration for guests' comfort and the inability to provide a peaceful and restful environment are completely unacceptable. There are plenty of other options in the area, and I would highly recommend looking elsewhere if you want to avoid a similarly unpleasant experience.

In short, this hotel is a disaster and not worth the money. If you value your sanity and want to have a good night's sleep, I suggest you steer clear of this place
Pashupatinath Temple, located on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Nepal, is one of the most sacred Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Nothing about the hotel is good other than its outside appearance. Apparently it is a Old palace converted into a hotel 20 years back. It may have qualified to be a 5 star hotel when it was built but it needs serious up gradation now. It is a shame to be keeping heritage properties in such poor condition. They should learn from the Taj Group of hotels, who maintain heritage properties so well.

The breakfast was horrible. They need to shut down to renovate. I don't understand why do they still have 5 star rating. This would be a good 3 star hotel. Just being big does not make it 5 star.

We stayed at hotel kailash kuti inn which is just opp the mandir. For hindus, who go here for religious yatra, it is best option. Fully veg hotel. We have darshans at mandir 3 times. 1. First day when we reach there in the afternoon, we went to mandir around 5pm. Evening aarti is at 6pm. All the four inner gates of mandir are open for darshans. 2. On the first day  at our request hotel reception called pandit ji at hotel and we fixed for next morning. Also we purchased rudraksh malas from outside the hotel bazaar, which is the main rudraksh mkt. Abhishekam at mandir is from 9-11am. We went with panjit ji at 8.30. There he do pooja for around 1 hour in the mandir premises at some fixed place away from garbgreh. After that he took us to garbgreh and we had darshans from just 3-4 feet away from the lingam. Only mandir main pujaris are there near the lungam. They put our rudraksh malas on the lingham and give us back. They also give us two rudraaksh malas from there own. We paid our panjit ji as fixed by us. They charge inr3100 for pandit Or inr 5100 for two pandits etc. Pooja done by them was really very good. They themself got parchi from mandir for abhisekam. 
3. On the last day of our trip to nepal, as we had purchased more rudraksh malas, we went again to mandir for darshans. Pujaris there touch the malas there and return us.

Visited at 10.00am and we were dropped off at the car park. Chilled walk up the street in between market stalls. 1000 entrance fee easily paid, which we thought was worth every penny. 
Tour guide offered his services, but a simple ‘no thank you’ and off we went. 
We watched in amazement and everybody was so friendly. In total we spent two and a half hours, which we will not forget. 
Easy to get a taxi for the return journey, just head back to the car park. 
It was a privilege to watch the ceremony so closely and to learn so much about their faith. 
Definitely worth a visit, my only criticism would be the ignorant tourists with big cameras intruding. People are saying goodbye to loved ones- yes we are interested and want to share our story, but a respectful distance should go without saying!
Not something special and you pay 1000 roupies to enter. Don't try it! Also the place there isn't something special to see.
This place is heaven for me. I would like to recommend all spiritual person to go this place recharge your energy and got blessed from Lord Shiva 🙏
I had such a fun. Everything was different yet so close to soul. I recommend this to anyone in Kathmamdu, only takes few minutes from the Airport.

Very spiritual visit. Beautiful temples on one side of the river, multiple burials taking place on the other side. If you are not a Hindu you are not allowed inside the temple but the view from the other side of the river is still very impressive

Ancient and Sacred Temple located near to Kathmandu Airport. It has opening from all four directions. One can have View of Deity from any direction. However people prefer to view it from front door and many a times there is long queue of devotees. However there is a paid view where you can have exclusive Darshan.

The history of the peace pagoda is very interesting. This is definitely worth a trip and you won’t have to set aside too much time for it. If climbing uphill is too difficult, take a taxi to the peace pagoda and walk down to get a boat service back to the lake.. there is a  sign saying that it is a 45mins walk uphill but it took me and my partner slightly over an hour to get down!
Was located on top of a hill with nice views. There were some noisy groups in spite of silence boards. There's a nearby Elite Organic restaurant with amazing food.

The hotel is located centrally with easy access to the main areas of Darbar Sqaure and Thamel...the Hotel is one of the old property with huge out areas including pool and landscaping with walking  tracks and also has an In House Casino for the ones interested in it.
The room i stayed was the park /pool facing and hence enjoyable. I felt the hotel needs to upgrade/change the carpeting of the floor as they have become really old. The house keeping, rooms and food were fine .The Hotel has a spa but slightly overpriced for the services offered.

The front staff could be slightly more responsive to the guests .

Overall good for few days of stay in Nepal.

We hiked about 10 minutes down from the Lord Shiva Statue to the World Peace Pagoda, which can be seen illuminated nightly from Pokhara. It is relatively plain but nevertheless impressive in that it is more of a contemplative monument than anything else.

1000 rupees per foreigner. For this you cannot enter the temples. 
On arrival when we were told this price, we jumped on TripAdvisor to see if it would be worth it. Based on the reviews we chose not to pay this ridiculous price and instead wandered around the site. We enjoyed some buildings from further away and walked down to the river to see some burning pits. 
However not long after we had walked down to the river we were chased by a security guard who demanded to see our tickets. 
Decide for yourself if you want to go, but we think 1000 rupees is a ridiculous entry price without being certain that all the money is going towards restoration.

I was not sure if I would enjoy visiting a site dedicated to cremations, but it turned out to be fascinating.  This UNESCO sight on the banks of the Bagmati River is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.  This is where people come to cremate their dead.  Funeral pyres for the line the banks, and it was really a cultural experience.  You will even see people burning shrouds only, which means the person who passed away is not in Kathmandu and they do not have the body there.

Be sure to climb higher and higher, where you can take in the entire complex from above.  It is truly visual overload--you won't know where to look first.  Because the property is so large, it will not feel crowded.

A must-see while you are in Kathmandu.
Just spent 50 pounds on a meal for 3 adults and 4 children.  Food ok but when they left and I moved to a single table to free up the one I was on give en loads of problems
An amazing place but not for those who have trouble with stairs. There is a shorter way but stairs are still present...ask your cab driver.

I stayed at the Yak & Yeti as part of a group tour both before and after our trip. I had friends who had stayed here before and they highly recommended it. I can only say how disappointed I was in this hotel. Had it not been for the group I was traveling with that had already paid for my room I would have checked out and gone somewhere else. First of all, the hotel was undergoing extensive renovations while I was there. There was a huge cover over the back half of the hotel and their main restaurant was closed. Our tour leader wanted to brief us outside in their garden area. It was an absolute comedy as hundreds of cackling crows sit along the trees and roofline and we couldn't hear a thing he was saying! We ended up eating in the only restaurant that was open which had an unremarkable buffet which was overpriced for the offerings.  The hotel itself is NOT centrally located, You have a mile hike through dusty crowded streets to get to Thamel.  There are no convenient laundry facilities near the hotel so I had to take all my hiking clothes to Thamel. On our return trip, they booked everyone on one floor and put me in a room on a completely different floor. The room was absolutely filthy dirty. The carpets could not have been cleaned in years. There was a sign on the door to the patio to not leave it open or rats would come into your room! I went back to the front desk and told them in all my travels around the world this was absolutely the worst room I had ever been given. They said they had no other room but I could check back. I told my guide if they didn't find me another room I was going to leave and pay for another hotel. Fortunately they did find me a room (oddly enough on the same floor as my tour so I'm not sure what happened there since it wasn't available earlier).  I also booked a massage. To get to their "spa" area you descend down a concrete set of stairs into a basement area. I was led into a sparsely decorated room with a fan blowing. The massage table didn't have a place to lay your head so my neck was killing me by the time it was over. The massage itself was nothing special. I have to say it was the worst spa experience I have ever had and I communicated that to my group so they could go elsewhere for that service.  I just left here shaking my head that people think this is such a great hotel.  Maybe it was 30 years ago but not anymore.

In contrast to my expectations, the temple is small but has 4 Gates and if you want to pray God Shankar from all 4 Gates, you need to go between 8 am and 11 30am. Rest of the time Gates open for few minutes. Only one gate remains open for the Darshan time. 6 am to 12 noon and 4 pm to 8 pm. Lots of small temples around. River bagmati (in a pretty bad dirty shape) passing behind. However temple is clean and not very crowded. Queue of 50persons when we visited but may be due to Hindu New year day. There is a place with multiple shivlings which requires parikramna. Shoes counter is outside temple premises and is free so do not leave your shoes with any shopkeeper who may attract you with such offers. Payment RS 100 for Saarc countries more for others. Photography not allowed
this place is good for those who want to do pilgrimage , other wise as usual this temple is crowded and  dirty , long ques,

The view from the temple across Pokhara is wonderful but we climbed a lot of steps to get there. I think it might be possible to drive up as we saw some older people who obviously did not climb the stairs like we had. I thought the temple would be an old one but it is new.

Beautil place to regenerate onself with calmness of Himalaya, friendliness of staff and people around, very service minded and loving and caring. I enjoyes the stay and recommed for any family to come and enjoy
I'm not too much into temple visits. So the other experiences in Nepal were far more captivating. Of course, this temple is perhaps the most important one in Nepal.

My review of this hotel is a bit devided. On the one hand this is by far no 5 star hotel, even it claims it is; on the other hand, comparing with what we saw in Kathmandu and compare it with the overall impression of the city it is clearly one of the best.
What we liked
- good breakfast
- nice quite location
- good infrastructure (good, but expensive restaurant nearby, taxis always available, everything in (a bit longer) walking distance, but no chaos like in Thamel
- some very helpful people (at breakfast, in restaurant, security)
What was not as expected
- no flexibility in terms of changing rooms
- old fashioned equipment 
- pool was dirty (but nice to see, great garden)
- extremely overpriced pick up service
Would we go there again? Probably not, as we thing there are better places what offers a better value for money

Took a taxi up the hill from the city (1500rps - half an hour each way and the taxi waited for us, we took an hour and a quarter) and then walked the final 8 minutes up steep stairs. The view was incredible - the Himalayas at the back, with the lake and city in the foreground. Lots of coffee and tourist shops on the way up/down but very peaceful at the top.

We checked in on May 18 2023 for 3 nights,  it took more than 35-40 minutes for check-in, and after check-in, persons were not available to deliver luggage in the room. Room AC was not cooling and informed reception to take care at night they informed AC is cooling now. But the whole night it was not cooling. From the bathroom, drainage water was coming into the room.
We expect rooms shall be given to guests with prior checking and after complaining to their Senior manager Ms. Monika, Mr. Ajay, and Mr Govind feels this kind of situation is normal for them. We are shocked by the behavior of the hotel team.

As per our guide, all Hindus must visit this temple. This temple is for lord Shiva and biggest Bandi statue is also here.
This temple is on the shore of river whose two sides are used for different kind of prayers!

🇯🇵 妙法寺のすぐ下に、日本人が経営するコーヒー専門店、【Peace of Mind】があります。
　登りに一杯、下りに一杯。こんなに眺めのいい所で、こんなに旨いコーヒーが飲めるとは！
　心の中は平和で一杯になりました。
🇬🇧 I drank cups of coffee on the uphill and the downhill.
  It was great to drink such delicious coffee in such a beautiful place.
  May peace be on the Earth forever!

Pashupatinath temple is known as one of the most powerful temple for hindusum..
There were so many peoples out there.
this is the first time i saw how hindu people cremate the body... it is really interesting to see even from a far

The entire team of this hotel was so adorable. We are the big group but every one of us feels respected & warm feel inside Good Treatment  from everyone specially by Manisha ,susmita.
Rooms are first class. We visited twice here.... really good hotel to stay.

The red chicken curry was very good and the side salad. The price is very very reasonable in Gaia. The ambiance too and dining layout were very well thought off. But sorry guys, service at rosemary chicken really was superb!

This place is one of the must-see-palces in Kathmandu. But: If you are not Nepali you will be left with a lot of questions after your visit. So better prepare with a local (guide) – and take care of the "holy men" around, they are perfect business men. . . - but to understand Nepali life, you should go here even questions will be raised. . .

Hindu culture and uniqueness is very transparent from this place. 
Recommend this place to visit without limits your time !! Cheers

It's definetely interesting to see the rituals from such a different culture in front of your eyes. But having said that, there is nothing else to see - as the main temple is closed to non hindus. The 10 usd entrance fee is way therefore way overpriced. So, unless you have a particular interest this one could probably skipped.
This grande  restaurant  is very good for friend and family visit in pokhara  u can visit once u come pokhara here I love there hostility and service thank u

the hindu burial place, where the corpses are washed, blessed and burnt. although nothindus are not allowed to temple itself, it is a place one has to see and to be at remembering that all that was born has to die.

I arrived at this hotel today after my friend stayed one night already. We were very excited as we have been to Kathmandu before and stayed at a lovely hotel but this time we wanted to be closer to the city so we chose this as it looked decent.
We are so disappointed but unfortunately we are forced to stay here as all other better hotels are full on such short notice. The room was so dirty like nobody had cleaned in days or weeks, there was unknown hair in the bed and all over the floor as well as dust balls. We complained to the guest relations manager who tried to help and moved us to a new room, but even here - we moved the TV cabinet to get to the plugs and it so dirty. Our bed sheets have several holes and stains in it! The furniture and carpets are so old and used, the hotel really needs a refurbishment!! 
Honestly, for 30 dollars more you can stay at the Grand Hyatt and I recommend you do so because this hotel is not even worth 50 dollars.

We had a very pleasant stay at Yak & Yeti. The amanitites, ambience and service is excellent. I would like to especially mention the food we were served during our stay. The Spice Room had a good variety of food and took special care for our dietary requirements. During our long stay, the following team took great care of us: Prakash, Pallavi, Kishore, Sajan, Pasang, Pemba, Salikram, Sonia, Anisha, John. Big thanks to Man Bahadur (the Chef) who cooked us delicious food. 5 stars for the team. We will be back!

I was initially given a room at the heritage wing. There was a garden party that night that went on and on. I had to call to complain many times. I mean - who allows a garden party at midnight when you have paying guests who are trying to sleep, right? And I'm talking loud music.
They shifted me to another room at 1130 pm. See? They do try to be accommodating. They even gave me free breakfast for the rest of my stay. But why do you allow parties to go on past 10 pm in the first place? Don't you have ground rules?

After taking about 25 minute taxi, we had to walk up the steps for about another 20 minutes to get the the Peace temple. The site provides a wonderful view of the mountains and Pokhara city.  Beautiful ambience.  Please note that the site closes at 1715, and so plan your trip accordingly
Visited this place today and really liked. I never had chance to paryicipate in this Aarti Puja at Pashupatinath and glad i did it today. Don’t miss out this while you are in Kathmandu.
My husband did it, unfortunately I couldn't, as my legs were aching, I stayed at the bottom where they had some restaurants . he said it was close to 700 steps.

We were in the Nepal at march for Langtang valley trek. Before trek we had a one day in Kathmandu to Look around the Kathmandu valley and we visited Pasupatinath temple, Boudhanath temple and Katyhmandu durbar square. Particularly I am very much impressed with Pasupatinath temple. The holy psahupatinath area is the biggest pilgrimage place for hindu from all around the world. Many Indians visit pashupatinath temple in other day but special day like Shivaratri and Shrarwan many pilgrimages comes here. 
I really like the temple and its cultures. I also knew how Hindu cremate dead body on the bank of river. As our guide told us that burning the body goes on respective elements. I like the way how Sadhu were decorated there. I did not like the polluted bagmati river. Overall I enjoyed here but too many people. If you want to know something about Hinduism you must go to Pashupatinath Temple.
a very good place to see the panoramic view over Pokhara and surrounding hills.However you you do need a clear day to see the mountains

This hotel is centrally located and walking distance from Thamel and next to Durbar marg. Its great 5 star property but I feel it's too expensive for facilities it's offering. Per night room rate is USD 240. One can find lot of better places around this place. Staff is helpful , stay was pleasant.  Room service staff was excellent. Front desk experience was average. 

I was attending an event here & would like to inform hotel management that banquet hall arrangement are POOR.  I would not recommend this hotel at all for any event. Chairs are damaged and bad shape. One of senior citizen fell down while session was going on.. This is  very very sad

This property will be great if priced at 
USD 100
If you spend any time in Kathmandu - there are a couple of must-see touristy things.  This is one, from the public cremations to mingling with local regligious figures.

We stayed at the hotel for 2 nights during a last minute trip to Kathmandu during the new year weekend. The reviews online seemed to suggest it was a great property and so we didn't mind paying a high tariff. 

When we reached the hotel, the facade and gardens appeared grand and very pretty. The check in process was also very smooth and front office personnel were very warm. The room was underwhelming and small. It seemed under furnished and very poorly lit. We checked at the reception and were told all rooms have similar lighting. The washroom too appeared very old and stained. The housekeeping could have been better (room cleanliness). We asked for fresh towels and extra cups on one of the days. Only after a reminder were we given a towel and instead of a fresh cup, a housekeeping lady picked up a cup we had already used, took it to the washroom and rinsed it with water and gave it back to us to use!

The view from the room was great (overlooked a pond, beautiful garden and swans). The breakfast buffet was decent. The guys at the travel desk were also very helpful with suggestions. 

We also went to the casino in the hotel (Casino Royale) on one of the evenings. As with most other Nepal casinos, it was very small when compared to most international casinos. Very few tables, all tables with the same minimum betting limits, over crowded, poor customer service and average food. 

Overall would rate the experience as average.
It is said that if a Hindu has the resources then one must visit Shri Pashupatinath Temple at least once in lifetime.Very thought provoking.

The Yak & Yeti market themselves as a luxury hotel but the wing were I stayed was certainly not  luxury. Smell of mould in the corridor and carpets that look as they have seen better days. I had booked room and expressed that I wanted to use the free airport shuttle. Flight schedule was sent to hotel but no shuttle was there. In spite of two telephone calls to hotel no shuttle and hotel suggested I should take a taxi. I did and hotel refunded the taxi bill. The room was very dark but at least no bad smell as it had wooden floor. Breakfast restaurant is very small for such a big hotel. People at times had to wait for seats. Breakfast is ok but limited selection. Some local dishes, bread, jam ,cereals, some fruits, tea/coffee. The grounds of this hotel are nice for a hotel in this location. Swimming pool and green lawns. If you want to do shopping in the busy Thamel area this is just a bit more than 10 minutes walk from the hotel. I had issues with the reception and especially check out was not a pleasant experience.
It's really peaceful place on height... And the full view of pokhara see from this area...it you found peace and u like nature's beauty once u can come and enjoy the nature's beauty...

It’s a really good place to pray for Hindu religious people can enter in temple, others are not allowed to enter from main gate. But other religious also visit around this area. Highly recommended!!!!
As we know that stupa is the most beautiful  place where mostly peoples  are frequently .we can see fewa lake  from there and we can also see mountain view from there.

This temple dedicated to Lord Shiva is perhaps the biggest Hindu Temple in Nepal. Within the city limits of the city of Kathmandu, the temple is said to attract devotees in large numbers throughout the year from all parts of the world, particularly from India. Some say the this temple dates back to 400 BC. It is UNESCO approved heritage place.
Situated on the banks of the Bagamathi River, it was built in the 5th Century .
The Main deity is to be seen through FOUR entrances , narrow . Lord Shiva's Face is seen on four sides of the Lingam besides on the top. It is only one of its kind. 
The temple could be still better kept. Car parking is vast but dirty.
There is no fee for entrance to the temple.
A grand temple dedicated to the Almighty Shiva. A must visit place in Kathmandu. The upkeep of the temple needs attention.

Get there in the morning!! Usually it gets cloudy in the afternoon, so you can't see the mountains anymore. But if you get the chance to be there earlier during the day you get the most amazing view over the lake and pokhara.
A bit hard climb but the views are awesome from the top, the trail has well paved steps and lot of shops all the way to top
Unfortunately it was cloudy and foggy day, it would be wonderful if it was sunny day, the temple looked like Japanese style and if you are Japanese, it might be nothing special.

5 out 5 - Beautiful views and very peaceful. We paid for a boat and driver from Pokhara to Pagoda Peace Temple. 

We hiked up about 45 minutes to 1 hour. Make sure to bring the correct foot wear. There is a stop off for a shop to get some water about 20 minutes into the hike. 

When you successfully hike to the top you can enjoy views and get a coffee in the mountain cafe.

We went here based on other reviews. We had nachos, momos, and I had the fish and chips. We shared everything except the fish, my wife is vegetarian. Woke up next day very ill, ruined 2 days. Avoid the fish if you go, and I never will again.

We took a taxi up to the temple from lakeside, for which we paid 1500 rupees, about 12 euro, including waiting time. Once at the parking, you'll have to climb up to the temple. It takes about 10 to 15 minutes and the steps of the stairs are not too steep so it's really quite doable even for inexperienced hikers. The air is thin though. There are many stalls and coffee shops along the way up, so you can take your time to get to the top. Once there, the view over the lake is stunning! You'll see the mountain range as well, snowy Annapurna rising above the clouds. The temple itself isn't too exciting, the stupa has 4 different Buddhas, donated by 4 different countries. You can't go inside.

This is one of the most visit destination in Pokhara. There is a beautiful stupa with big gardens and a monastery. The view from there is amazing. You can see Fewa lake and Pokhara city. The place has banned taking videos in recent time. Shouting, making noises is also not allowed. It is not wheel chair friendly too.

The food could use some spicing up - I've had better and (much) cheaper momos elsewhere. 

Outdoor seating gets rather cold after a while.

🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
Absolutely loved my experience at Gaia Restaurant! 💖 The ambiance was so cozy and peaceful 🌿, perfect for relaxing after a long day in the city. The food was incredible — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented 🍽️😋.

Highly recommend the  their fresh juices 🥗🥭 — so refreshing! The staff were super friendly and attentive 👏😊.

A must-visit spot in Thamel  Kathmandu! 🇳🇵✨
Will definitely be coming back again! 🔁💯

#GaiaRestaurant #KathmanduEats #5StarExperience 🌟🍴

The Pashupatinath Temple lives up to its reputation as a sprawling and magnificent Temple dedicated to Pashupatinath (Shiva). As a Hindu, the Temple is sacred to me of course but notwithstanding the religious affinity, this Temple holds significance as the oldest Temple in Kathmandu and its architecture is very distinct and attractive

Hotel Grand Holiday is a reasonable option if you are staying in Pokhara. The staff is very friendly, and generally available and helpful. The rooms are quite clean and well-maintained relative to Nepal. My room had a fantastic view of the mountains that quite honestly made it all worthwhile. The major issues with this hotel were the hot water, the Internet, and the breakfast. The hot water was off and on, and you usually had to run it for 30-40 minutes before getting any hot water. Other hotels I stayed at in Nepal had consistent hot water, or at least it was consistent at certain times during the day. The Internet was also inconsistent, and not just because of the electrical outages that the entire city experiences. I frequently had to call down to ask them to reboot the Internet. And the breakfast was disappointing. So, for the price you pay, it's not a great deal, but it's not a bad choice.

Unless you’re a Hindu, it’s a bit weird. Whenever you think about it, you’re paying to see some bodies burn. Little bit weird not going to lie. Also, you’ll be able to see them burn for a bridge outside the temple (if you really need to see some hot corpses).

The temple itself must be beautiful, but paying 1000 NRs to walk around the patio and see monkeys (not even well looked after monkeys, there was a dead baby monkey!!) is a total rob. I'd understand maybe half of that to support the maintenance but paying that amount of money and then not even be allowed to see the temple (which looked incredible peering from the door) because we are not hindu is absolutely ridiculous! 
Speaking with Hindu friends I've understood the religious never forbid entrance to temples to people of other religions so I find this ban real nonsense. I'd understand not entering with cameras, touching or certain behaviours but I recommend people not to enter the "temple" area and proceed directly to the crematory.

This was my 7th visit to Kathmandu and thought I would stay at Yak & Yeti for a change as I usually stay at the Radisson. Firstly the location is great with some fantastic restaurants nearby. The problem starts with the unfriendly reception staff. Having flown in from Australia and being extremely tired, a pleasant smile would have gone down a treat, not an abrupt request for my passport. This also was my husband's  check out experience with no thank you for staying at the hotel. If you are looking for a delicious breakfast well you may be disappointed as the hot selection was miediocre.  With the number of 5 and 4 star hotels being built in Kathmandu I would hope the management of the Yak and Yeti address these problems.
On the plus side, the gardens are lovely as were the majority of the staff.

I went twice once with a friend where we got a boat and then climbed then walked back to Pokhara through the farms and outskirts where we were greeted by children and friendly locals. Despite the heat it was well worth it for the views and a look around the temple. The Paneer Butter Masala at Cafe Elite was so good I returned by taxi on my own to have again. The taxi was much more costly and I ended up hiking down to get a boat as all the taxis there were waiting on their fares.

After Bougha Stupa it was a mistake to visit the temple. Beggars claiming themselves “sadhus”, non stop cremation which everyone can see and be present, for Hindus must be their shrine, but for foreigners and not Hindus a bit creepy place... I felt heavy energy of death there... the guide also was telling about goodness Kali and which immolation people do wishing something from this goodness. Place is dirty and full of people, however if you are in Kathmandu than must visit...

This famous religious centre is a real must see to get an impression of all rituals about tradtional cremation of the Hindu. With some respect we followed the rituals from the other side of the river. Is is for western people a little shocking by moments but it's part of the culture so very worth a visit and really a must see

I saw several positive reviews here on Tripadvisor about this restaurant and because of that I and my family (Total 8) went there on a recent Friday evening. As soon as we entered the premises it felt really wonderful. The setup was done nicely. Being a friday the place was all packed but we did manage to get a table. We ordered some starters which were good and later on the main course that tasted quite good as well. 

Now let me come to the negative experience we had there. There are about 20 tables but only 10 or so Menus. We had to wait 15 minutes to get to see a menu. On top of that there were only 3 staffs waiting tables. The captain was inattentive - always busy on his phone - and the remaining wait staffs were clueless. They all lacked basic etiquette and manners. Staffs need some orientation on behaving with customers. 

For good food do go there but if you really want good experience avoid the place.

the way is nice
view is nice
we enjoy the walking
a nice air but very hot and sunny
nice flowers and view

Nice firm beds, spacious rooms, super clean and huge property.
All kinds of amenities available.
Location is also perfect.

Super delicious food at Spice restaurant. Mr. Bhojraj was so helpful and courteous. The items he suggested were superb. 
Really appreciate his efforts.

I booked a Heritage Room outside of the group that I was traveling with.  From the sounds of their comparison, I'm glad I did.  The room was fine (nothing special). Mini bar was barely stocked and snacks were minimal.  There is no hotel gift shop where you can buy any snacks or toiletries to make your stay more comfortable. Water temperature in the hotel is "warm".  They tell you let the water run for a few minutes in order for it to heat up, but after 10 minutes I was over waiting. After trekking for 2 weeks I decided to get a massage. Do yourself a favor and go to "Seeing Hands Clinic" (voted #1 on TripAdvisor).  The hotel spa is not a spa (contrary to the lovely advertisements throughout the hotel"). It  is one little room in their workout area. They play loud rock music, the massage table has no neck cradle (so you're in worse shape when you leave) and the massage therapists are not professional at all.  Mine came out of the bathroom and straight into the massage room without even washing her hands!  I had to ask her to "please go and wash her hands"!   We dined at their 5 star restaurant "The Chimney" and that was another disappointment.  Service was ridiculously slow and we were left with empty glasses for over an hour.  I had to get up and find the manager THREE times to ask for water and service at our table.  They also messed up our order and my friend never received her main course. Rather then admit error and ask if she still wanted her meal, they didn't even acknowledge their error and left her with nothing while we all finished out meals (I shared mine with her) and then they ended up bringing her main course when everyone was finished.   Service out at the pool was just as disappointing.  No towels available at the pool stand (which was filthy) and when I asked for 6 towels (as I had friends coming), they brought 2....etc. etc.  It was just one thing after the other. If you asked any questions at the front desk, they just looked at one another as if they had no idea how to answer any question we posed.  I don't think they deserve to advertise as a five star property, the service was definitely lacking all around.

During my visit to Kathmandu, my travelling companions and I discovered the Gaia Restaurant which was a short walk from our hotel.  It was a great find.  The food was delicious - from our American breakfast to Tibetan noodle soup.  The surroundings were lovely.  The staff were excellent and very efficient.  If I am ever back in Kathmandu, I will definitely be going for a visit.

Have gone down way below standard from checking in to check out everything has gone down considerably poor
Last year it was superb but now the hotel and staff both r in miserable condition 
Food and service WORST ever

The rooms itself are pretty basic but clean. Price/quality this is a very good choice as the rates are really reasonable.
Staff is extremely friendly and helpful. On some mornings breakfast was buffet style, some other days a la carte (western, Indian). Both options were decent.
After I booked through booking.com, the hotel immediately dropped me an e-mail to check if there was anything else they could help with. We organized our trekking guide & transportation to the trek and to Kathmandu with them, and were satisfied with this (both with the price as with the quality).
Would probably be nicer with water. We visited in January 2017 and earthquake repairs are still taking place.

Walking distance to shops, restaurants, and some attractions. But the rooms need major updating. On our first 3 nights, we were upgraded to a junior suite! Spacious but it had 2 thermostats one of which could not be adjusted and we could not figure out which thermostat controlled which part of the room. Large bathroom but the hot and cold knobs on the sink and the shower didnt quite work. The red colored knob seem to control cold water and blue knob controlled hot water, which is opposite of standard color coding. Then after a couple minutes no cold water comes out! Only hot water, too hot. Taking a shower risks getting burned.
On subsequent stay few days later, we got assigned to a different wing, normal size room, hardwood flooring, bathroom looked renovated. Shower was not fully enclosed, floor didnt slope sufficiently towards floor drain so entire bathroom floor got flooded . On our last day, too much noise coming from workers doing renovation! Turns out this wing is not completely renovated yet.
So beware which wing and which room you get.
Must visit temple for Hindus. Lord Siva with five mukhas. Amazing temple which transcends time. Felt lucky to be visiting.

Me and my friends hiked from the side of the Fewa Lake and it was around 30-45 mins hike from the lake. We had fun times while hiking to the Stupa after the tiredness of the hike when we reached the Stupa the view form that place was unforgettable.
Excellent service, wonderful food. I can’t rate this place too highly. Give it a go you won’t regret it 👍. Try the Mongolian chicken followed by the Sikarne for dessert
I appreciated the culture here although there are restrictions for non residents who have to pay, and then are seen as the moving ATM.

Got there at 6. 02 pm. They were closing 6pm close).  Despite obviously having climbed to see it, they wouldn't let us in. Bit disappointing, but the views from the nearby cafés are great, so we sat and had a drink.

The staff is very polite and very professional. The food is also veryy good and so delicious. The rooms are so comfortable and with a good view of mountains and surrounding. There's a swimming pool too.

I thing very beautiful place and you must visit (this place is must have). Good place for ceremony. Lot of place in this area. There is entrance fee and not much. Lot of monuments. I recommend this place.

As part of the Kailash Yatra it is imperative to seek blessings from the Holy Pashupatinath temple, so we did get the blessings by way of evening aarti at the Temple.

As is common with every place which is thronged with too many people cleanliness is something which one has to be prepared to bear with.

Monkeys are also present in large numbers and one has to be careful with the belongings and eatables like Prasad etc.

This temple has historical significance and among the most important Jyotirling of Hindus. Situated on banks of Bagmati River in Kathmandu Nepal this is UNESCO designated cultural heritage site.

Our first trip to Nepal led us to the Pokhara Grand, and it was an absolute delight! This is truly one of the best hotels you can find, largely thanks to its incredible staff. From the lovely receptionists to the amazing waiters and waitresses, everyone took exceptional care of us. The food was equally amazing, and the property itself is simply stunning. Would definitely prefer to stay here again.

We treated a local friend to dinner and chose this restaurant given Lonely Planet's review, hoping for something local and memorable...however unfortunately this was anything but...it took forever to get service, most items on the menu were unavailable, and then get served...and one of the worse dining experiences I have had in traveling the world throughout.  Fortunately, just seeing our local friend made up for the evening.  And no consideration from the staff or management which was very un-Nepalese from that which we had just experienced during the past 10-days in Nepal however wrote this experience off as one of those "never again" experiences!

We have book Kathmandu valley day tour and one of the major place of this tour is this place. We went there at evening time and lot of people worshiping there at front of temple and we see cremation on this place by burning. We highly recommended this place for short visit.
A lot things to explore here.best heritage place in the world having big area.temples,jungle,river,monkeys,many kind of birds is the beauty of this place.

Just tried to check in my group at the Yak and Yeti. Queues at reception - no hospitality, no welcome drink, one luggage boy on duty so had to bring own luggage in, no lobby manager in sight, laughed at by the receptionist when I complained. Usually put our groups at the Royal Singi hotel where we are met with a smile , sat down and given a welcome drink. Much more professional. This was one of our premium groups - doesn't leave a good impression.

The powerful feeling of the temple is outstanding. It is a huge temple. P Sometimes very crowded with Hindus on pilgrimage. Hindus only have entry into the main Shiva temple. Across the river are the cremation ghats. Very moving to see the preparations for the cremations, lots of photo opportunities. So much to see here

Was a nice place. Decent. Little walk up but not difficult.
Worth a quick visit. 
On the way down we stopped at a cafe with a Japanese barista. 
The espresso was great.
Typical Buddist Stupa. Long uphill climb with great views.
Really great food, company and atmosphere! Highly recommend and looking forward to come back! Big variety in menue and veg options available

We took a taxi from Pokhara (1800 rupees). The driver took us at the stairs, waited for us for an hour and drove us back to Pokhara. We thought at the beginning that 1 hour was maybe too long but as you spend 20 minutes climbing the stairs, 1 hour is just fine. The view up there is amazing.
Spectacular Hindu ensemble and worship place. Very busy as always. Beware of touts who bandy about with claims to VIP access and/or guided tour experience

Absolutely loved my experience at Gaia Restaurant in Thamel! 💖 The ambiance was so cozy and peaceful 🌿 — a hidden gem right in the heart of busy Thamel 🏙️. Perfect spot to relax and recharge!

The food was incredible — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented 🍽️😋. Highly recommend the Nepali Thali and their fresh juices 🥗🥭 — so refreshing!

The staff were super friendly and attentive 👏😊.
A must-visit restaurant when you're in Thamel, Kathmandu! 🇳🇵✨
Will definitely be coming back again! 🔁💯

Famous hindu temple, unique but scarry. This famous, sacred Hindu temple & cremation site on the riverbank was rebuilt in the 15th century.

Pasupathinath temple is one of the holiest place for Hindus and Lord Shiva is main deity. It is situated near Bagmati River in the heart of Kathmandu city. Temple is opening early in the morning and devotees can view from all four sides only during particular timings. Bairava and other deities are also there in the complex.  We had nice dharsan on a full moon day.

The temple is as good as its Fame. Very spacious and peaceful. 
The priests are quite helpful. Overall a nice experience
Pokara is a beautiful city and much nicer than Kathmandu in my opinion.  There is a lot to do and at a much slower pace and in a clean environment.  Definitely paraglide if you have a chance.
Great local attraction, the road up is crazy but really peaceful up top, small bunch of shops along the path.
This spot is on the top of the hill & gives excellent view of the Pokhara city, Fewa Tal & mountains. a must visit attraction in Pokhara

The Grand Holiday hotel in Pokhara is situated just 100 meters from Fewa lake and very close to where most of the action is in Pokhara. We had a first floor room with a view of the Annapurna range. The furnishings were simple and practical- quite old but fairly comfortable. You just can't compare hotels in Nepal with hotels in more developed countries. The room had an air Cond unit with heater function too. Hot water was available but u had to let the water run for a minute first. The best thing about the place were the people- Ramesh the manager was very very helpful and genuinely nice. Bissnu was also eager to serve and attend to our needs. The wifi signal was not very strong but enough for Whatsapp messages, most of the time. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone wanting an affordable stay in Pokhara.

Recent stay in late October before heading off to Pokhara for motorbike trip was alright.. Ok but quite pricey relative to other more local options. The massage after a long flight from India, was very good and recommended. Good gym for workout including swimming pool. Quiet safe and secure location. Staff were excellent

My family and I travelled from overseas to visit friends and family. I stayed at room 535, a Heritage room. It was the worst night. The room was heated at 28'C and the maintenance could not fix the AC.I was advised to keep the windows open to sleep. The room is extremely small. The TV controlled did not work. Wifi's not free and I mean who "PAYS" for wifi these days in a 5 star hotel.There were neither slippers nor wardrobe. Water flows everywhere from shower to the toilet keeping the toilet wet.

I particularly requested for a very quiet room and the heritage room was facing the main road with taxis beeping, flashing lights and the loud drum/music on the New year's eve.

Yak & Yeti Kathmandu should be degraded to 3 star or less. Apologies to costumers will not improve your review. The admin actually needs to work hard to upgrade the standards.

We had a regional conference for Asia & pacific here during November in this hotel. The hotel looks very grandeur and impressive with a beautiful garden and pool. AND all the good things for the hotel ended there. 
The management and staffs all were such un-professionals that we wondered how could a five-star hotel be like this!! We were around 600 people all together for 3 days; 120 rooms were booked at this hotel but except airport transfer no other service could be felt satisfactory. If I write this list can go on and on....
In short Never trust this hotel.We have officially decided not to choose this hotel for any event or accommodation for  our guests.... neither we recommend for any one coming to  Nepal

The Pashupatinath Temple is not a beautiful place, but a must see if you are interested in Hindu culture and religion. Watching people praying and cremating their dead is something that makes you think about some aspects of life.

We hired a taxi for the afternoon to visit the temple as well as Sarankot and the Mountain Museum. Unfortunately the weather was cloudy so what would have been an amazing view from the temple was rather dull instead. The temple looks impressive, pity though that many people ignore the signs asking to observe silence. It would be a great place to sit and reflect. Apparently it is possible to get there by boat and walk up the hill to the temple. Well worth a visit and wouldn't mind going a 2nd time for a bit longer.

Our food took 1 1/2 hours to arrive and it was cold. We ordered chow mein and chicken skewers. We wanted order more drinks while waiting for our food but our waiter never came by and when we tried to get his attention we were ignored

3 of us hired a small row boat with driver, 700rs split 3 ways including life jackets, n were rowed across to landing. Bit of a climb up but nice views of lakeside. Peace pagoda nice spot n view of mountains good. We walked down following path from lookout point near cafes. Lovely walk down came out near houses n not far from cave n devis falls. Then walk back to lakeside on dusk. Very pleasant outing. Fine clear day would have been better.

I was surprised that for such big 5 star luxury (as they call themselves) hotel breakfast is actually less than average quality and variety. Location is good. But what really surprised me is when I was charged 8 dollars per day for Internet with explanation -this is hotel policy, talk to our senior manager. We stayed in few 5 star hotels in Nepal And this was only one that  charged for internet (and terribly slow anyway). Considering how much you pay for a room, its shame and disrespect towards the clients. They should change their policy and management immediately.

Always prefer to stay in Yak n Yeti.
Excellent service . Front desk very cooperative Pratik Shradha binary.
Food is excellent .would suggest my freinds to stay at Yak n Yeti

This hotel has seen better days.  I rate it two stars at most.  The rooms and hallways smell of mildew. The carpet  in my room was filthy.  The TV did not work.  The breakfast was cold and my room service came 20 later than I ordered it.
Had willing to see this temple for quite Long, it was mesmerising you see and experience the whole ambience ... unforgettable

This has been my second time staying at the Yak and Yeti and it is everything I remembered it to be and dreamed about in the years since I came here. Arriving at the Yak and Yeti after a long trek is like being killed in war and being sent to heaven. I want to especially give thanks to the amazing staff at the Spice house, your service is impeccable. Even after being away for 2 years Sonika remembered our family and made us feel right at home! This place continues to go above and beyond in every way possible making it truly one of my favorite parts about spending time in Katmandu. Also shout out the garden staff they do an amazing job this place is beautiful.

This hotel is inclusive with the breakfast and just 5-10 minutes walk to the center point.The room is clean and nice staffing especially Bishnu, he tried to help for fixing the Wi-Fi problem which didn't much well working in my room, however it worked well at the lobby.

This is a UNESCO world heritage site and a holy Hindu temple. I was not satisfied with the level of preservation and cleaniness for such a place - they do charge US$10 for entry. 

It is old and has huge religious significance for the Hindus - they still creamate the bodies of the dead there and it was quite a confusing thought to have bodies being ferried in amongst the crowd of tourist.

Do take a hike to the top as it is quieter and a bit cleaner. I would also suggest a tour guide as the place would make more sense. I was snapping pictures of a cow and was reprimanded by someone - not sure if I was correctly reprimanded but I stopped.

The many reviews cover this attraction well. I have been here four times. The largest Hindu temple complex in the world. Worth seeing, but know what you are in for as a Westerner. Be aware and expect the following as part of a unique cultural experience: 
1. Filthy and smelly. Litter everywhere. 
2. Open cremations. Real corpses being burned in open view.
3. Beggars and solicitors will target you relentlessly. 
4. You will walk through monkey and cow manure.
5. Watch for monkeys and other pickpockets!
6. The "holy men" are really beggars dressed to earn rupees from tourists.
7. Open sewage in the river, sometimes with children swimming in it!
8. Sensory overload, and I mean all five!
9. The hawkers will try to guess your religion and sell you an appropriate trinket.
10. You are viewed as a profit opportunity. You will be charged more for everything. Do not be offended. The $11 admission is well worth it.
Why would I recommend going? Because you will not see another Hindu temple complex like this one anywhere else in the world. The contrast of filth and beauty is stunning and typifies our human experience.

We stayed at Hotel Grand Holiday and Ramesh organised an airconditioned Tourist bus from Pokhara to Tansen.  We arrived at 8am for an 8.30 bus at the bus station.  When we arrived the yard organiser told us the bus had just left & he put us in a taxi to catch the bus.  When we caught the bus it was a beat up local bus.  This put us in an awkward position did the hotel sell us a local bus at a big margin or did the yard manager sell us on for a handy profit. We need to move today so we kept going.
The bus soon filled with at least 4 roosters, 1 sheep & 1 goat. It was so overloaded that we could not get out of the bus to go to the toilet when it stopped for a couple of minutes
Travellers, please beware when being sold a tourist bus ticket and being put on a local bus.  We could not wait to leave Nepal as we were ripped off twice in a week.

I wish I could say that Pashupatinath was a highlight of the trip – it is a really important Hindu temple and it was on our must-do list – but it wasn't my FAVORITE part of the trip.  On the upside, it was huge and there were plenty of places to explore.  On the downside, it felt a little invasive and inappropriate to be exploring around people's personal funerals and cremations, and seeing people photographing these things.  If you're looking for culture, you'll definitely get a different side of it here so I would still suggest going.  But I would also just suggest keeping your distance from families who are saying goodbye to their loved ones out of respect!  Also, there are lots of men dressed as Hindu holy men who charge you for a photo and to be "blessed."  Don't fall for this...it's just a way to get money from you!

If you stay in the renovated wing of the hotel it is satisfactory. Wood floors, decent space, updated bathrooms. However, if you get stuck in the non-renovated wing it is atrocious. Vents and drains filthy. Extremely beat up. Smelled moldy. Grounds are lovely and the buffet is quite extensive for both breakfast and dinner though the great emphasis is on Indian cuisine. Nice relaxing bar area.

About an hour (1,000 rupees) from Pokhara and well worth the small hike from the pkg lot.  Views are terrific and have the guide/driver discuss the Tebetan refugee situation.  Also, there are coffee roaster little shops on way walking to top that are worth the trip!
Maybe problems in the kitchen, but there seemed to be a rather long wait for the food. They were busy. Food was good and tasty
It was peaceful and quiet up in the peace temple. Although the road up was rocky and slippery, it was worth the effort the garden was bloom with flowers. We enjoyed our time there.
Exemplary service! Congratulations! We were served by the waiter Abiral, a professional! Thank you! We felt very good!

Visit is a must but temple usually crowded. Free shoe safe available. The temple needs maitainence, proper security and cleaning facilities. The road drive to the temple is horrid with no inch of the road plane with no pit holes.

The cremation process/preparation of bodies is definitely a cultural experience.  If you are squimish of seeing bodies, probably skip this.  

I stayed for the aari lights.  I was not that interested.  I didn’t understand what was going on.  It starts around 6.  Get there early if you want a seat.

Tons of monkeys.

Can’t go into the temple unless you’re Hindu.

I discovered this help desk at Grande Pokhara Hotel. Mr. Kirti Tripathi went above and beyond to assist with my Everest mountain trip. Truly helpful, honest, and highly recommended for a Nepal tour! He was always available for any guidance

The nice stuctured Buddist Temple is standing on the top of a hill with the greatest view to Fewa lake and Pokhara city. Nice area and beautiful temple too. It is not included in main touristic visits because buses can not reach it. Only small vehicles can reach the place.
Chaotic & energetic just like The Namesake. Beautiful architecture. Lots to see. Vibrant prayer & devotion.
beautiful place but there is a restriction inside main entrance. that was kind of sad to us. yet the place to wonderful

The views from this place is simply amazing. The sunrise and sunset views from this place would be awesome. however, the crowds are less as it involves a steep climb of approx 450 steps (yes four hundred and fifty) from the car park. it is on the other side of the lake. there are unrestricted postcard views of the Annapurnas, Dhaulagiris and Fish Tail with the emerald waters of the lake in front - of course if the weather plays along....

the place is very peaceful. after the long climb you will need to rest a bit and if the skies are clear of clouds then there could not be a better place to sit and recuperate. even otherwise, it is very peaceful. all along the stairway there are shops where you can rest if you want and have a cup of tea or coffee or do a bit of local handicraft shopping. there is even a small shop with a mini coffee bean roaster of its own. 

as you come down the first flight of stairs, there is a nice cafe with an overhanging balcony - the views are great from there too and it is the ideal place to have a beer / coffee. forgot the name of the place though....

We find this hotel as a good business hotel. It is cozy . But lacks play area and environment for leisure.Rooms are clean and food quality is good. It is not very far off the city. City has much more to explore and we did not stayed longer here during days.

Pasupatinath Temple is more than just a religious site; it's a spiritual oasis that pulsates with a unique, serene energy. Nestled on the banks of the sacred Bagmati River, this UNESCO World Heritage site is a living testament to Nepal's rich cultural heritage.

As you step into the temple complex, you're enveloped in an aura of tranquility. The intricate carvings, the rhythmic chanting of mantras, and the gentle flow of the river create a harmonious symphony that soothes the soul. The temple's architecture, a blend of Hindu and Buddhist influences, is a masterpiece that reflects the country's diverse religious tapestry.

Beyond its architectural grandeur, Pasupatinath is a place of profound spiritual significance. Pilgrims from far and wide come here to seek blessings, offer prayers, and connect with the divine. The atmosphere is charged with devotion and reverence, making it an ideal spot for introspection and inner peace.

Whether you're a spiritual seeker or simply looking for a moment of respite, Pasupatinath Temple offers an unparalleled experience. Let the positive vibes of this sacred place wash over you and leave you feeling refreshed and rejuvenated.

My trip to Pashupati, Nepal, last year was an unforgettable experience filled with spirituality, culture, and breathtaking landscapes. Visiting the Pashupatinath Temple, one of the holiest Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, was the highlight of the journey. The temple’s serene yet powerful atmosphere, with the chants of priests and the sight of devotees offering prayers, created a deeply moving experience.

Walking along the Bagmati River, I witnessed the sacred rituals and ceremonies, which gave me a glimpse into Nepal’s rich traditions. The intricate architecture of the temple and the surrounding ashrams made the visit even more special.

Beyond Pashupatinath, the trip also allowed me to explore the vibrant streets of Kathmandu, savor delicious Nepali cuisine, and interact with the warm and welcoming locals. The blend of spirituality and adventure made it a well-rounded journey.

Overall, my Pashupati Nepal Tour was a deeply enriching experience. Whether you’re seeking spiritual solace or cultural exploration, this destination offers something truly unique. I would highly recommend it to anyone planning a trip to Nepal!

I felt it was really important to visit the burning ghats because public cremation is such an important ritual in Hindu life, but I also felt a little sheepish about potential voyeurism. It was definitely a solemn visit, but I was surprised to discover that next to us (on the opposite bank from the families and ceremonies) many Nepali people were gathered to watch the proceedings, and that they do not know the deceased either. We were told that people come to educate themselves so that they will be familiar with the process when they need to perform it for their loved ones. As an example, the young woman in front of me had her 4-year-old on her lap watching as an ambulance delivered a shrouded corpse to the waiting relatives. In general, once the deceased arrive, the families pray at one of the riverside shrines and then dip the deceased's feet into the river. From there they move down river to the part of the bank where the cremations are performed. We saw a religious man with an earbud and smartphone chanting into a mic. We wondered if he was performing prayers for a family member who could not attend in person.

We stayed here 3 times in the space of 2+ weeks as part of a tour group.  The first stay was for several days and the next two stays were for a single night. The second stay was in the older section of the hotel (where the club rooms are located) and that room had seen far better days.  The carpet was very old and the room smelled musty (most likely from the carpet).  The furniture was dated  with dings and nicks prevalent.  The pigeon poop on the railing outside the window was pretty gross.  I also didn't care for the fact that I needed to kill a roach in the bathroom.  On our last trip, we saw exterminators at work in the hallways so maybe that issue has been resolved.  Our third stay was again in the newer part of the hotel so the room was decent.  While there are thermostats in each room, it appears that there is a pre-set cooling temperature which you cannot make any cooler.  

Breakfast is included and maybe tries to cater to too wide a range of guests.  There was always a mixed bag of some western type foods and some Nepali type foods. No matter what time we showed up for breakfast, the "hot" food was at best lukewarm.  I saw that there were burners underneath the chafing dishes, but perhaps they were not lit.  Although the coffee was great each morning.  

The most stressful part of our trip was when we returned to the hotel after a week in Bhutan.  We had left a bag at the hotel along with many others of our tour group.  On our return, our bag was not part of the returned luggage.  Our concerns were met with, "I'm sure someone from your tour group took your bag."   Even if the bag was sent to a room by mistake, no doubt it would have been returned.  We asked if we could help look for the bag as clearly the hotel didn't have a clue.  We were led to several different storage rooms all to no avail.  The bellman who was helping us said there was one more room we could check.  We found the bag.  The "tour" tag had been taken off or fell off.  What really angered us was when the bellman helping look for the bag said, oh, that bag had been there since our tour group checked in and was never claimed on our original arrival.  Given the bag we left at the hotel, was an extra bag that we brought along so we could leave things at the hotel meant it was impossible for the bag to have been there from the beginning.

What really got me though was constantly being ripped off by the hotel on transport charges. It's as if they run some kind of junket with the taxi drivers on location. This was hardly an isolated incident. Here are some examples: 
1. We were charged $30 for an airport drop off - at this price you would think you at least got a sedan with air-con. Nope. As comparison, we hired a driver to take us to the airport, wait for us and drive us back to the hotel for our everest flight - 2,000 rupees (i.e., <$20) and with a proper sedan with ac.
2. We took a taxi from the hotel to the Boudanouth stupa - hotel insisted it would cost 800 rupees which was what we paid. Taxi back, flagged on the street - 500 rupees. And almost certainly already an overcharged tourist price. 
3. We took a taxi from the hotel to a restaurant nearby (no more than 10 min drive). Hotel insisted it would be 1000 rupees for one-way 2500 rupees for a standby. In one of those no-ac taxis. Even after we expressed unhappiness at the price, and after a lot of bargaining - finally got it down to 700 rupees. The final price when the restaurant called us a taxi home? 400 rupees. 

I have no problems paying for quality service. The problem is staff clearly prized their unethical taxi drivers (who sit around the exit all day waiting for idiot tourists) instead of the well-being of their guests. Also i would have a lot less of an issue with this practice if there were slightly more luxurious cars. Let's just say driving down the dusty streets of Kathmandu in a dirty open-air taxi, having paid 2x of market rate is NOT my idea of good hotel service.
