Overall it is a good experience but I think the price does not reflect on 5 star hotel standard its a bit over rated for that reason I will not be returning. It definitely needs an upgrade in the rooms. Please update all rooms.
Went there on a tour and it was under renovations and the streets were being repaired. Very scenic views from area and there were various monuments but I was somewhat dissatstified with overall
If you want to move away from the buzz of the city this is the perfect place to visit. You’ll catch amazing views and a quietness like nowhere else in pokhara.

I was here for a workshop for 20 days. In btw I switched rooms once. The last day suddenly I couldn’t locate my wallet with much cash and many credit cards. After a few minutes the front desk had brought my wallet out with everything in tact. I was so moved by this! Nepals, a place of faith, gave me faith. Perfect. Thank you deeply.

This world heritage site is totally amazing. Preserving the old Temple and it's structures are really wonderful to see most especially in this modern age. If you are planning to visit Nepal, don't miss out Pashupatinath to visit.
Very peaceful, sacred and splendid place from where whole Pokhara seems small. We did hiking up to the peace pagoda and  was really memorable trip with colleague. Best place to be in Pokhara.

A really amazing place if you want to get in touch with the Hindu culture. We went there on a Saturday and the whole Szenario there was a little bit unrealistic for us. On the one hand people come here to burn the bodies on the other hand people make Tiktok Videos.

A great atmosphere which is really not typical for us Europeans!

Pashupatinath Temple is considered as principle pilgrimage site of Hinduism. The temple is on UNESCO World Heritage Sites list for decades. The extensive Hindu temple has a sprawling collection of images, inscriptions, ashrams, temples and images. The temple has 275 holy abodes of Shiva as well. Temple architecture is quite intriguing as it is built in Nepalese pagoda style of architecture. The temple is located on the bank of holy river, Bagmati where cremation of dead body takes place.

We have stayed in this hotel several times in the past but qw were very very disappointed this. Having said that the staff is extremely polite and hrlpful but this hotel hasn't been updated for over 25 years. There are molds in bath tub, dirty old rundown carpet which has very bad dampness smell. I have feeling owners don't really care anout it. It's location good and convenient that may be the reason they really don't care. Sales and reservation staff need to trained. They don't have substitute of milk like soy  milk even they don't have plain yogurt only sweetened one.  there are much more than that. But the staff at FOOD SERVICE are  very simple polite and helpful. There are better choices close by who are striving to serve better.

Take a boat across the lake from Pokhara and enjoy the views of the temple on the island and the mountain back drop. The hike upto the Stupa is a bit of a pull but worth it. As other reviewers have said it is far from peaceful up there as there are so many Nepalese visiting and ignoring the silence signs. As you approach the Stupa there are fab photo opportunities of the mountains through a sea of flowers. Hike back down the other side and pass traditional farming houses and more great views.

A stout climb and a beautiful view from the top of the mountain. 

While it is a Buddhist shrine and people should adjust their behaviour to not be offensive to anyone's faith, enforced silence by police at the top was a bit much. The majority of persons who visit the stupa are not Buddhists and come with friends to take pictures and enjoy the view. Not exactly possible to keep complete silence in such a setting.

I went here with my family and friends for a meal. The location and the gardens are lovely. The food was very average and the service was terrible. We have to call the waiters a couple of times to get attention and they all seemed very laid back..

We visited this Hindu temple one morning around 9am. The complex itself is quite different than the Buddhist temples we visited in Kathmandu. It was obvious from the moment the taxi dropped us off that this would be a unique experience. 

You will need to work your way past all of the street vendors selling both souvenirs and other items for offerings. Follow the path (and hoards of people) until you reach the ticket booth. As Western tourists, we were definitely in the minority here but we were there to learn about the temple, not to worship or mourn a loved one. Someone will stop you and have you purchase an admission ticket. The cost was 1,000 rupees, which we felt was worth the experience. 

If you do not want a tour guide, you will need to stop the "friendly" local who begins talking to you and showing you the way to follow the path. If you choose to utilize the services of the guide, establish the price up front. This was pretty much how it seems to work at all of the major tourist sites in Kathmandu.

I will say that we found the guide services to be worth the rupees spent. It was a bit expensive compared to some of the other site guides, but still a decent price. The guide we had was very thorough and explained quite a bit about the Hindu religion, the funeral process and the temple itself. If you decide to go on your own, you will probably wander around without truly understanding what you seeing.

We did have the opportunity to witness a funeral. The guide explained the process to us and we found it fascinating as it is completely different from what we are used to. There are also sadhus at the complex. Of course, in true Nepalese fashion, you can take pictures as long as you give them a donation. 

This temple is definitely worth a visit, but make sure you go earlier in the day. They close from noon-5pm each day. If you want to see the funeral process, make sure to be there by 10am.

It is a small trek uphill to reach the Peace Temple. But once you reach up the beautiful architecture would surely impress you. There are small stalls for beaded jewellery and a nice tea shop also to sit and relax. The glider flights would be seen passing on top of your heads making noise. Its a beautiful view of the town from up there too. The great lake can be seen from above.
We joined hiking tour to the world peace pagoda. It’s a very energy-consuming tour. The top view is really amazing.

We stayed in Yak&Yeti hotel from 8th of Nov till 10th, first we tried with reception to get a room with toilet hand sprayer but unfortunately they have 2 buildings, one old building without this option in the toilet and another building with this option. The receptionist which was wearing traditional uniform for Nipal people responded to our request that there aren't available rooms. She took very long time to accommodate us.
The room was very old in decor and furniture.
Although the provided shaving blade was kept in small box but unfortunately it was used one ( I found hair on the blades), imagine if I didn't note and use it!!!??
I informed the receptionist same day to consider such hygienic problems with their housekeeping.
We requested to change the rooms to the new building which equipped with toilets hand sprayers and actually the reception applied our request.
The room in the new building is totally different, it's decor and furniture are new and the rooms look
 better.
The view from the room was on the pool and the hotel garden which is huge and looks well arranged.
The breakfast was good and there were many varieties.
We got our dinner 3 times in the main restaurant in the hotel which was good and actually we looked for vegetables items and shrimp items as we were afraid from unavailability of HALAL food which was not mentioned in the menu. 
The service team was amazing and their care about their guests was observed.
Check out was so quickly and better than the check in.

Pashupatinath Temple is a beautiful old structure. You can't enter the actual temple if you're not Hindu, however, it is still worth having a wander around the complex and you can see some of the beauty inside.

Very nice and beautiful temple.  Be aware there are more than several hundred steps to go up after driving to the parking lot. Also the road up is very steep and often rock rather than hard surface. It was hazy the we were there. On a clear day it would be even more spectacular.

The service is excellent and the staff is very friendly and helpful. 
The food is freshest I have ever tasted.
Very clean. A great garden!
Pokhara Shanti Stupa is a Buddhist pagoda-style monument on Anadu Hill of the former Pumdi Bhumdi Village Development Committee, in the district of Kaski, Nepal.

Mediocre location with scary busy streets to be crossed to get to Thamel and other more interesting areas of Kathmandu.  I was not impressed with extra charges for things that should be included (gym and jacuzzi).  The water was rusty and/or yellow colored at all times.  Free bottled water was nice and the staff was very attentive and helpful.

We been there at evening,  it was so beautiful and as it mentioned full of peace.  But the most irritating part was the security guard, to stop the noise from the people the guards themselves making the more noise.  That's the only concern i have regarding the place.  Rest all are  wonderful .
5 faces of shiva and they are open at different times, we went in around 2pm and was able to see all the entrances of shivas face. it is a must visit and had an amazing experience
A must for anyone visiting Pokhara! Easy to get to by car or you can make the walk up from the lake.

It was nice to walk around the exterior of this temple however after paying 2000 for two people I was not allowed in as white tourist are banned from entering, keep this in mind before buying the ticket.

Cannot stress enough how amazing this restaurant is. Staff, food, service were all 10/10. Special mention to Tilak who was the funniest and most hospitable waiter in all of Kathmandu. The rest of the team were also so great and made sure we had a good time, so much so we kept coming back. Visiting from the UK, my friends and I thought this was the best restaurant we dined at over our 2 weeks in Nepal.

After a steel 40 min walk up to the Stupa, we were really disappointed!!!! There was building work all around it- piles of rubble and bricks etc. The view is tarnished with ugly solar sticking out of the ground, there were about 4 big ugly signs demanding "silence" yet a man with an angle-grinder was working a few feet away from the stupa! The view is nothing special at all. The stupa itself was okay, but like I said ruined by all the signs stuck up the stairway! The walk up was quite fun though! Deffo felt like I'd had a work out after it. We are going to try out Sarangkot for sunrise tomorrow so hopefully we will be more impressed with those views!!!!!

We like walking so we walked to the other side of the lake and then uphill to get to the Pagoda (takes about 2 hrs to get there). Another option is to take a boat to go across the lake and then walk up. Anyway it shouldnt take you more than half a day (if you go early in the morning).
This is something you can do if you have an extra day in Pokhara. The views are not amazing...
Nice place to experience new culture and traditions. Looking at the life how it turns to end. Gives different ways of lookibg life

This was my first visit to nepal and this temple was one of the biggest reasons.
The vibe was good and there were no beggers like in any usual indian temples
We had heard rave reviews so we stopped in for lunch. We stuck to momos and beers. Pricey but other dishes looked good. Nice patio.

One of those places you can not gets into unless you are a Hindu; I understand and respect this, but why ask people to pay  for the privilege of standing outside?  The area is also filthy dirty, rubbish lying around and the sellers everywhere; someone has to sort this out, and quickly.

Pashupatinath Temple, One of the busiest place with Mass Gathering, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Pashupati. It is located in Kathmandu, Nepal near the Bagmati River. It is nice place to visit when you are in Kathmandu. Its shines Nepal culture and harmony among people.

The white Shanti Stupa, or Peace Pagoda, sits at the top of Anadu hill over Pokhara. It is a Japanese Buddhist Stupa; a monument to inspire peace, designed to provide a focus for people of all races and creeds, and to help unite them in their search for world peace. The four golden Buddha statues came from four countries. You climb a lot of steps to get to it, but the view was worth it. The Stupa was excellently maintained in blinding white with gold trim

Our stay here was amazing! The staff here was nothing short of fantastic, we want to give out a special mention to Arpan, who didn’t just make us feel comfortable but also became a friend, he made sure along with the hotel staff that we were looked after in the best possible ways. Without a doubt this place has become a go to for us for all our future visits to Pokhara! Thank you so much Pokhara Grande.

Poor service - not responsive to guests request, service not present at the restaurant (no one bothers to come to take orders). The hotel isnt well maintained. Uneven floor through out the hotel, high risk of tripping. Tripped a couple of times! Limited breakfast selection. Location is not good. Hidden in a small road. Plenty of hotel choices available in Kathmandu. For a similar priced hotel, going elsewhere might be a better choice.

The most famous temple in Kathmandu. Currently this is the largest temple premises in the world. Photography is strictly prohibited inside the main temple but allowed elsewhere. There are a lot of temples and Shiva (Pashupatinath) temple is the main one. Amazing vibes.
45 min hike up hill, nice to do by boat there and back. Places to eat and drink for a rest on the way.

As part of a tour, we did a pre-dawn hike to the summit in hope of viewing the Annapurna Range at sunrise.  The hike up was long and exhausting.  It would have been worth it, if we could see the Annapurna Range.  Cloudy weather prevented us from seeing the mountains.  The Peace temple was very nice, but hardly spectacular.  We did enjoy beautiful views of Pokara from the top.

I visited the area as part of a group tour with a Nepali guide. We were advised to keep an eye on our belongings and stay with the group. Being foreigners, we weren’t allowed to access the temple, but we walked along the river. There are ‘holy men’ dressed in orange who are keen to be photographed for a fee and a few market stalls. Our Hindu guide was excited to have us watch a Hindu cremation. It was quite confronting to watch the deceased person’s body being washed by family members and moved to the cremation alter. It was at this point that my daughter and I walked away from the group as we didn’t wish to see the body alight. Sitting a short distance from the group, we were approached by a man who offered to purchase my teenage daughter from me. Thankfully our group arrived at this point and our guide shooed him away. Quite confronting.

The drive was a little winding and you had a bit of a climb to get to the Temple- definitely worth while, though a bit slippery in wet weather.
It was certainly worth the visit.

My children were scared while we approached to the crematoria site in this Temple. It a different cultural practice from ours. I do not recommend this to Westerners or suggest them to omit this place.

Thanks!

I was looking forward to stay here. One morning i wake up..i had huge allergy because of their carpet/ moquettes. So it was a bad stay. Room furnitures were very much dated and tv aint workin well. Bath got yellow water but well its nepal. 
Its crowy lobby and bfast as well. Many manpower but not much motivated workers. Its has good size garden and good bed though. Hotel needs a lifting and new furnitures.
Had a great experiene. And loved the view and the entire temple has been amazing. Located in the centre of the heart and dedicated to lord Shiva.
This temple and surrounding made lifetime impact on us. Lots of hustle and bustle,  the crematorium, if you can call it fantastic...then it is!

Breathtaking views of Pokhara, Fewa Lake and the amazing Himalayas. There is a great cafe at the top to enjoy lunch and a beer while you take it all in.
This should not be missed!!

Pashupatinath Temple is one of the most famous places in Nepal. It is a must visit. The temple complex is very large and a lot of people visit everyday. The deity of the place is Lord Pashupatinath. It is also one of the oldest temples in the world.
One of our party found this very moving... the walk up from the lake had good views of birds and monkeys. We had a Nepali friend with us and got the local bus back. I found that more fun.

A holy place for Hindus. Beautiful temples and architecture. The ritual cremation at the river makes the visit very impressive as it is almost a violation of the privacy of the family of the deceased, but it gives also a view in the culture of Hinduism.
It was a precious experience.

A truly interesting experience. Live cremations happening right on the river and a huge complex of temples to see. We picked up a tour guide (somewhat unexpectedly - he just started talking to us!) but he was actually super informative and very interesting (ended up costing ~$30 which felt a bit steep though). Definitely worth a visit!
This temple is clean and requests silence. The view is amazing overlooking the Pokhara valley. and each sign is translated into English.

Much talked about from outside Nepal as prime attraction.  But the maintenance is poor.  Bagmathi rever on the rear looks pathetic.  Non Hindus cannot access inside temple though they are charged NPR1000 as entry fee.  No footware, phone, camera inside temple campus.  Storage facility for footware, camera and phone are available but may be crowded sometime to make the deposit.  It is good to make photos etc before depositing and leave them in your car (not on unknown taxies) with the driver acknowledging it.  Hundered of domes with hindu deities but no information displays around.  Pasu Pathi Nath.  Pasu (Globe) Pathy (the leader /cammander) Nath (dwelling place).  Hindu religion believes Brahma is the creator of the lives on earth, Vishnu is the protector of the lives and Shive (Pasupathy) is the destroyer of lives once their time on earth is completed.  Even today deadbodies are cremaated on the banks of Bhagmati river at the rear of Pasupathynath temple with the belief departed souls will reach heaven direclty abode of Shiva.  It may rain time and hence good to have an umbrella

Very nice service 
Everything is perfect very highly appreciated about your services 
Lovely hotel as well staff 
Miss jamuna is very attention about guest and very warm welcoming

I expected a lot... and I saw a not very clean temple complex. Foreigners are not allowed into the main temple - fair enough - that's also why you DON'T have to take off your shoes (someone could've told us before we did... they actually took our shoes and gave us the number, but didn't tell it was unnecessary!). Then you take a stroll to the other side of the river, you can see people burning bodies of the deceased... it all looked dirty though - the river, the bank, the stairs... everything. 
Then there are monkeys - be careful, they're aggressive and I saw one attacking a woman to get her shopping bag. There are also cows... so there's cow poop. And people walking there barefoot. It was pretty gross.
It's a pity because it's an interesting place, and if it was better taken care of (and for 10$ a ticket it really should!), it would be an amazing attraction.
The best restaurant in Thamel, great food, lovely atmosphere and amazing staff. Would definitely recommend for any time of day, always brilliant!

I felt luke we were the only tourists there. It was pretty impressive and worth the sum of money you have to pay to go inside. It's very authentic. There is some carvings you might not want children to see in some places.

One of the most important temples of Bhagwan Shiva situated at the banks of river Bagmati in Kathmandu.This temple is one of the seven UNESCO heritage sites in Nepal. A must visit temple for all Hindus.

Adjacent to the Bhairav temple, unique 525 Lingams are installed in a Swastika shaped maze. For good health and longevity, one has to do parikrama (cumambulate) walk through a maze like path touching all the lingams and then exit from a different end.Though the temple opens at 4 am and closes after evening aarti at 7.30 pm. During the day, temple is closed between 12 noon to 5 pm. Depending on the time available at your disposal, best would be to be there well before 7 pm to join the Arti and have Darshan of other temples in the compound. Om Namah Shivaya

Lovely place, lots of western tourists, lovely garden. Food is presented very well.

Pad thai was more like indian curry noodles. Still good but lacking.

A bit pricey by local standards but still worth the visit.

Great food and staff. 
Wonderful for breakfast Lunch and dinner. Carrot cake a dream.Have been visiting Gaia since it was a little coffee shop selling delicious chocolate brownies.

Har Har Mahadev.

Foreigners can give this a miss. I believe foreigners have to pay an amount to enter the temple and can go only till a particular section. Under the imposition of such condition, better not to visit.

Very dusty around. Lot of construction going on. Wouldn't have gone to the temple if I wasn't devout. From parking area to the temple, one needs to walk atleast 700 meters. It was difficult for my elderly parents but somehow they made it.

Wasn't harassed by pandas/ priests like how it happens in Indian temples. Neither is the temple area as dirty compared to temples back home in India. Went around 2pm, so I guess wasn't too crowded. Cannot even see the Shivalinga properly as they didn't turn on the lights inside the sanctum sanctorum.

However there was a sense of achievement after visiting the temple. Guess us Hindus feel that way upon completion of a pilgrimage.

Actually did not have the visit in my itinerary as was not intending to stay in Kathmandu. But missed my flight to Pokhara.. So decided to go to the temple in the evening. But when I reached, the temple was closed. God wasn't interested to have me I guess. On my way back, I again tried to have darshan and was successful.
Place of devotion, nice two Dharshan. Local priest arrange Pooja and Dharshan. Good view of the surroundings

Superb location for mountain and lake view, would advise it for sunrise or sunset. Can't tell the number of people for sunrise, sunset it was okay. There's a good amount of noise though, people aren't the best at reading signs...

Had a spiritual feelings when we entered the temple. Without any words or instructions my inner journey had started looking at ancient temple, construction and feeling the long history of the famous​ Hindu temple. Must visit place for everyone.
But cleanliness level should be improved a lot which can be done but need to change the mindset of the people. Cleanliness is next to godliness!
This is the best place to take a short hike from the end of the lake.best views and peace place .when you have been there  meditation place because of Buddha ❤️❤️🙏🙏

This temple was one of the four most important religious sites in Asia for the followers of Shiva, one of the main gods of Hinduism. A non Hindu person was not allowed to enter the temple.  It costs 1,000 rupee per person to enter the grounds surrounding the temple. Cows and monkeys roam the area.
The temple and crematorium were located on the banks of the Bagmati River.  Along the bank were concrete platforms where people were cremated and the ashes put in the river.  The general area was a mixture of emotions and activities with mourners, vendors selling marigolds and souvenirs, Sadhus people who practice extreme discipline, locals and tourists.
It's a great place to stay in the center of the city. Very welcoming staff and helpful, specially Bhola is very helpful. Overall, I'll recommend this place for all kind of stay.
Nice temple in capital Kathmandu Nepal and famous for indain and naepli Hindu people,it's looks so much interesting there  very good visit few times

I thought it would be interesting to watch the cremation ceremony, but I didn't realize it would be uncomfortable (at least for me) seeing corpse plus the smell of the smoke too. I saw some people wearing mask so I suggest you bring one. 

There is nothing much to see on the temple itself because it is for Hindu only.  But overall it was a new experience for me.

Entrance fee for foreigners is 1000. And taxi from here to Thamel costs 300. Not sure though it if is a good deal, but I think yes it is, considering the traffic in Kathmandu.
Visited this Hindu Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in June 2019. The architecture was quite interesting.

I am an geek for architectures. This one is unique as it’s a Hindu temple with Buddhist architecture. Entrance is restricted for Hindu only. 
The main temple might be closed in late afternoon. We waited till 5pm to have darshan. 
Do roam around and check all surrounding smaller temples.
Also no photography inside the main complex.

Even as we travelled a lot, we had the so called book experience for giving money for entering the inner part. Only after long talks and friendliness of a good english speaking jong man, we were lured into giving money to the babas, who are more dressed as and alternative kind of begging suits, than actually people looking for enlightenment. Of course we could not enter with the so called special list guests we would be on.
never the less we had a beautiful view on the site and the cremations and find a spot we could take pictures and meditate at the same time, just in peace.
I haven been Gaia several time. Most of the time i am with our guest, who came for Nepal trip.  The food is is so delicious. Greenery garden and peaceful environment make special feelings.

We were booked at the Yak/Yeti as part of the upgrade package to 5 star hotels during our Everest Base Camp Trek tour.  We were disappointed at the quality of the hotel rooms.  The bathroom door and cabinet doors in our rooms were old, run down and dilapidated, definitely not worthy of a 5 star hotel, more like a 2-3 star hotel.  Wifi is not free and cost $7.50 usd/day.  Overall experience was mediocre.

This is a good place to go with family if you want to spent time in peaceful place it could be the best option.
Aarati in the evening is most we liked .

good hotel but bathroom should improve, with such excellent location , it could be much better, breakfast must improve , too crowded and not enough item with price , very good staff , hope to be again

Small, tiny rooms  what they call as Heritage deluxe, can be claustrophobic for some. Clean hotel, service was better at restaurants compared to front desk. Breakfast spread was good with nice flavors. The other restaurant Chimney was just ok with very limited food options.

Three of us went here to visit what us supposed to be one of Kathmandu’s main temple attractions and we were put off by the place and the scheming people who seem to operate in this area including some that appeared to be in cahoots with the ticket sellers. This appeared to be a trend at several places in Kathmandu.

Tourists are requested to pay 1000 rupees here and you are harassed by a few men who stand around doing very little. One member of our group was actually a Hindu and was also told he cannot go to the temple, which seems to be against what I have read and the rules of the temple.

To actually get to the temple from the car park area (where cabs drop you off), you must walk along a road filled with beggars and then multiple shops / stalls selling religious artefacts, or other memorabilia.

Then once you get to the area immediately around the temple, you are told to remove your shoes - and a lot of locals do - but actually it appears that you do not need to and many people are wearing their shoes around. I believe, as is normal tradition, you only remove your shoes if actually entering the temple so try not to leave any expensive shoes lying around. There are also many monkeys around but they do not appear to be aggressive.

I think the entire organisation of this place for tourism is poor, especially if charging 1000 rupees. It requires better signage and removal of scamming locals who try to rip off or mislead visitors.

We were driven away by the misinformation and the lack of an explanation as to what 1000 rupees was for and then being offered a “guide” who could not explain much to begin with... quite sad as this is meant to be a religious place and I am sure there is a lot of interesting things to see and experience here, given the right opportunity and time.

Room service was very nice and polite staff 
During our stay it was wonderful experience One of the most impressed part us impeccable cleanliness modern facilities restaurant and attention to detail throughout the property 
Spacious and well appointed rooms provide comfortable shuttle for city tour 
Over two nights every details exceed our expectations. 
Special thanks to Jamuna g for excellent service

Its a hotel where we can get full facilities as we want. The environment of it was very clean and healthy with good hospitality.  The food items of this hotel was also good . We can get each and every kind of food items with snacks. The most desirable thing of this hotel is we can see the view of Mt. Macchapuchre from the northern part and lake Fewa from southern part from roof of it.

As comparisons to the facilities given by this hotel , price is really cheap. Facilities like breakfast, lunch and dinner, room service, and so-on is very flexible. This hotel is general hotel but service is good .I found that mostly Indian and Nepalese guests were staying in this hotel and they are satisfied by its services. 

So, I recommend that all Nepalese travelers who have planned   to visit Pokhara must go in hotel Grand Holiday which lies in lake side Pokhara.

Quiet location and friendly staff, good security, nice gardens
The rooms are ok, however food is relatively 
I am sure there are other hotels that are better value for money, depends what sort of budget you are on!
Beautiful Buddha on top of hill, it a long climb but was worth it ,the view from the top is breathtaking , it is peaceful up there .  A must see also in Pokhara
Peace pagoda where silence is maintained .beautiful view of pokhara is seen. Peace air blows everytime.

One of the most sacred Hindu temples of Nepal – Pashupatinath Temple is located on both banks of Bagmati River on the eastern outskirts of Kathmandu. I visited the temple complex around 3pm and the temple premise was hardly crowded. I could finish the Darshan in 5 minutes and then the temple doors closed. Ample of car parking space available.  No photos are allowed inside the temple premises. Felt blessed...Har Har Mahadev.
Monday's are very crowded. If you are a first time visitor, please avoid. Other days you can see the temple peacefully; spend time in each diety. Worth a visit of 2 hrs.

During volunteering in Nepal the volunteer organisation planned some tours of  many of the main tourist attractions and heritage sites in Kathmandu.

During the visit, the guide was very well informed and lived at the site in a cave directly beneath the temple. 

When arriving at the temple, there were massive crowds and we were told that the prime ministers’ wife had passed away and her funeral service (cremation) was happening at the temple with many police, army officers and officials present including the prime minister.

We toured the temple courtyard and sat in front of the cremation area for the prime ministers wife. Our guide talked us through the temple and the ceremonies. We then had the opportunity to meet the prime minster and then went to our guides cave. We didn’t enter the temple as it wasn’t open and it only allows Hindus inside. It costs 1,000 NP to enter. I’d suggest organising a guide and politely saying no to those selling things in the area.

We visited during a very important event, so it was very crowded, but would assume this would be different during normal times. It’s a very sacred place and linked to Shiva and the Hindu Gods. Definitely worth a visit but I would recommend being respectful as it is a location where people celebrate their dead and cremate their family.
The place where I saw the dead people burn after dead, that was quite sad moments. Having famous temple Pashupatinath for Hindu Peoples.

by treking you can reach to the top and the views there are amazing
it is very calm and clean area has been well maintained

We have had a very good experience with Gaia Restaurant and its food. Gaia has always focused on quality and hygiene. I must have had lunch and dinner there over 100 times, sometimes with clients, sometimes with family, and we have never felt the food was unhealthy. These days, there is a lot of competition to make food taste good, but I personally prefer healthy food without preservatives. We have also held a few club meetings there, which were excellent.

I have seen some reviews about Gaia, but I always recommend Gaia for its healthy and hygienic food, excellent service, and amazing ambience with a beautiful garden.

It is one of the more expensive eating joints in Thamel. The ambiance is quite nice, you can eat both inside and also in the courtyard, which comes with a fireplace. However, the food wasn't anything special. It wasn't bad but somehow was not worth the money.

A wish that was long pending
Had a pandit come with us and offer darshan and puja 
He acted like a guide and said which one was important.
Immense energy was fely from the sanctum Sanctorum.
An experience to remember throughout my life

Honoring Buddha can be done anywhere, but this place is special.

Inspite of the fact that this place is a UNESCO site, the upkeep and maintenance does not really tell so. It is sad to see temples with such heritage and importance being kept so badly. If one wants to understand the temple better it is always better to engage a knowledgeable person who knows the history very well.  Only then will the visit to the temple be useful.   There is so much to be told as a review will not just suffice.  However in a nutshell this is one of the places where the Pandavas went in search of Shiva seeking salvation.  The name of the temple comes from the fact that a Cow (Pasu) used to offer daily prayers by offering its own milk over the Shivalina.  The Shivalingam is Suyambu, and there are four faces that darshan has to be performed.  The four face darshan is available only in the morning after 9.30 AM.  One can wait till late evening 7.30 PM once again to see all the four faces.  Generally there is a huge rush to see this darshan.  There are several small shrines inside the temple complex.  Most important among them is the Mukthisthal.  According to the Tibetian/Nepalis custom in the yesteryears a person who wishes to attain Mukthi will come here and merge with the river flowing below the temple, in the presence of the Guru.  Even today you see people performing this in a slightly different way, where the final rites are performed on the river side in a particular way.  The temple is a very powerful one, provided one is receptive to the energy that is available.  This is a tantric center and is indeed very powerful when one sits in deep meditation.  One can definitely feel the raw energy in the place.  There is a Rudraksha tree inside the temple complex that should not be missed. Rudraksha is considered as the tear of Lord Shiva.  The Rudra Abishey is also very famous here.  You would need to hire a priest to perform this in the morning time.  Better to go with a know person.

We awoke at 3:30 am and drove to the lower parking lot.  Some other travelers were shuttled to the upper lot which lies at the base of stairs and the final ascent to the Peace Pagoda.  We walked the 2.5 miles on a very rough road in pitch dark punctuated by the beam from our flashlight.  It was steep and we stopped to catch our breath often.  We are pretty fit and it was still tough.  When we reached the stairs and final ascent the sky was just hinting at light.  You approach up a cemented walk to the base of the pagoda.  Here you leave your shoes and go up the marble stairs to a circular path around the base.  A monk did his prayers and chants here.  There were at least 20 photographers with varying size of equipment waiting for the sunrise behind the Himalayan range.  And when the sun began its ascent, you witnessed a once in a lifetime event.  The full beauty of the Pagoda and the majesty of the mountains was enhanced by prayer flags and the views across the valley.  After the 2.5 mile descent, we were ready to devour just about anything in our path!!!  Nameste.

Overall, Yak & Yeti honored its legacy while matching KOICA’s high standards, making our milestone celebration truly memorable. Highly recommended for large-scale events in Kathmandu.

Beautiful Viewpoint and Peaceful Atmosphere at Peace Pagoda

We visited the Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) in Pokhara and truly appreciated its calm and serene environment. The stupa is perched on a hilltop, offering one of the best panoramic views of Pokhara city, Phewa Lake, and the Annapurna mountain range.

The climb involves a bit of a walk or drive uphill, but the effort is worth it for the breathtaking scenery and peaceful atmosphere. The stupa itself is beautifully maintained, with a clean white structure and golden Buddha statues facing all four directions.

It’s a great place for photography, meditation, and quiet reflection away from the busy streets of Pokhara. Early morning or late afternoon visits are ideal to avoid crowds and catch beautiful sunrise or sunset views.

Overall, a must-visit spot in Pokhara for its views, spiritual calm, and natural beauty.

Take a boat from Lakeside, Pokhara, and cross Lake Phewa to the west side alighting on the way, if you wish, on a small island, where the Tal Barahi Temple may be visited. From the landing on the west side of the lake a short (30-45 min) but moderately steep (slippery when descending in wet conditions) climb (300-400 m) on a well-made path through the jungle takes you to to the World Peace Pagoda on top of the ridge. A tea house / lodge situated about half way up and others at the top provide welcome refreshment on a hot day. I did not find the large, recently constructed Pagoda particularly interesting in itself, but on a fine day it provides a great viewpoint from which you can look out across the lake to scan the Annapurna massif some 30 km distant on the skyline, follow the fortunes of paragliders as they take off from Sarangkot, identify landmarks in the city below and watch flights arriving and departing from the airport on the far side of the city. If you cannot face the climb, it is also possible to get close to the pagoda by road.

The Yak & Yeti bills itself as a 5 star hotel. I would say it's more of a 3 star, 3 1/2 if would be generous. I could see it being considered 5 stars in its' heyday but not today. With that said, they price was fair.  There were some nice things about the hotel and some issues that drove us nuts.  I would probably not stay here again except for the location which makes it very convenient. The rooms had plenty of power outlets for charging.

Pros:
- It's in the heart of the city and close to many shops/restaurants and is about 1 1/2 miles from the old part of the city. We walked most of the time we left the hotel.
- The breakfast and lunch buffet were very good with a very large selection and a large variety of foods from traditional Nepalese to Asian to American
- It does have some "rustic" charm
- They have an in-house travel desk that arranged a good afternoon tour for us.
- Bottled water is provided daily.

Cons
- They seem to host a lot of wedding receptions and parties. The first night was loud music (making it hard to sleep) until 10:30pm, the second night until 1am.  The 3rd night we got lucky and there was no party). They did offer another room at 12:30am when we complained but it was a smoking room....the smell was worse than the noise so we declined. 
- It's an older hotel with the issues that come with it:  One day the shower didn't drain well and had water all over the floor. One day the water was warm, not anywhere near hot (shower at 11am)

This is a great place to visit if the steps don't kill you we hired a taxi to take us but some people in buses had to walk up quite a steep road before the steps as buses could not get up the road, they  do have places where you can sit and have a drink and catch your breath which is good, once up there it is lovely with great views and the pagoda, they say to walk round it 3 times for good fortune which we did and just sat for a while enjoying the views. I rarely take photos I leave it to my husband who loves taking pictures while I just relax and enjoy.

I took the long way to reach the pagoda, i rented a boat from lakeside that takes you to the other side where you can begin your two hour hike. The place is very beautiful and spiritual and the view from up there is spectacular.

This is a tired old hotel that is in desperate need of redecorating. I can tell it was nice in its day, but its day has come and gone. It is dated and didn't feel clean. I would look for other options if in the area again.

Nestled in tranquility, the pagoda stands in a traditional Japanese style, radiating serenity. While capturing videos is prohibited, visitors are welcome to take pictures. The architectural design of the pagoda is exemplary, showcasing the finesse and beauty of Japanese craftsmanship. To reach the pinnacle, one must conquer a challenging ascent of numerous steps. However, the reward is well worth the effort, as the views from the top are nothing short of breathtaking.

Very airy garden-like atmosphere to sit and eat.  Prices were very reasonably.  I had the Chicken Satay - very spicy but very delicious.  Recommend coming here for a meal instead of having one at the hotel where you may be staying at.

We had hired a cab and Pashupati Nath was one of the attractions for the day. We visited just about it was closing in the afternoon and hence a piece of advice: The temple is closed between 2-5 p.m. We did make it in nick of time. The main temple offers views from all four sides and we managed most. Photography is strictly prohibited. Nearby are 522 "shiv lings" and you criss-cross them a riveting experience. Architecture is splendid and you sense a history around this huge complex. Wish Bagmati River, which flows alongside was cleaner and not clogged. It's also a place for cremation for it's believed you wash off all your sins if your body is put on pyre here.

I've been all over the world but this is one of the few places I felt unsafe and turned around. Guide book warned of robbers on the trail that leads up the ridge after you cross the bridge just downstream from the dam and there is a government sign warning visitors again of robbers as you enter the trail through the gate. 
I thought that this was probably untrue as I have always felt safe in Nepal and wandered throughout Kathmandu without ever feeling in jeopardy. 
But as you start the trail you are accosted by touts wanting to be your guide. As we proceeded up the trail, there were no other travellers or locals going up the trail and there were more lone men trying to get you to go different routes up saying the other guys were robbers. Totally unsafe feeling and made us decide to turn around and get out of there before we put ourselves in a position to be robbed. And this is leading to the "World Peace Stupa"! A real shame for Pokhara!

That is a good option of a 1 day trekking in Pokhara.
There is a great view of the city from up there, and the climbing till there is amazing, in the middle of a forest.
Easy to go, avoid any tourist guide if it is offered, unless you need some company and it looks easier paying for it that look for any other friendly tourist.

The resort is well maintained. The rooms clean and staff are freindly. Best place to be on vacation with family. Right from security guards, to  reception incharge and room service everyone is co-operative and friendly. One has to state their requirement it gets fulfilled. Good stay. Value for money. Will recomend this hotel.

Gaiya is a delightful restaurant that offers a unique dining experience, blending modern and traditional flavors with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality ingredients. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with cozy seating and stylish decor. The menu showcases a fusion of Asian and Mediterranean dishes, with standout options like their signature sushi rolls, savory dim sum, and flavorful grilled meats. The staff is friendly and attentive, enhancing the overall experience. The food is beautifully presented, and each dish is bursting with vibrant flavors. Prices are on the higher side, but the quality and innovative menu make it a worthwhile visit. Gaiya is a great spot for a special occasion or a casual dinner with friends.

At this place people are cremated. Entrance fee for foreigners Rs 1000. Here you can watch how loved ones cremate there family members. This all happens on the other side of the small river. Still having a good view. Lots of people trying to be your guide or sell stuff. 50 people are cremated here every day. Interesting to see.

A nice hotel hidden from the noisy & dusty  main street of Kathmandu but close enough to walk to Thamel shopping area. I like the old school ambience of the hotel with a garden and blooming jacaranda tree. Rooms and amenities need a serious upgrade though. Water tend to splash out of the shower as there are no curtain or door causing the toilet to be wet all the time. Overall a nice place to be if u want some quiet. But cheaper and modern hotels are coming up which will give YNY a run for their money.
you can take a boat ride and then hike towards the temple or go by car whichever seems convenient, pokhara looks so pretty fro the top its like you have an aerial view.
We took a boat (NRs 1260 pp) across Phewa Lake to walk up to this lovely temple on the top of the hill - 1 hour walk. Lovely views from the top.  Well worth visiting.
Incredible Hindu cremation place of Aaryaghat. Very nice. When you visit here, you will know the reality of life.

I had a guide and was grateful, without him I wouldn’t have gone in! We went on the last Monday of the nepal month so it was packed with women ending fasting. So much color and beauty! 

It’s a real holy place. This is where end of life ceremonies and cremation take place along the river (so you may feel a bit uncomfortable) and people are there mourning. 

The main temple is only for practicing Hindus and others are not let in. You will also be requested to remove shoes (unless it’s a madhouse like I saw!) 

There are also little shops on the perimeter. The “temple” is actually many buildings, temples, river, park and more.
Peace stupa  is awesome place to visit in Pokhara Nepal .From the peace stup temple you can see beautiful view of pokhara valley.

Worth seeing this UNESCO world heritage site. There is an air of calm that envelopes the entire stupa which if disrupted is swiftly quelled with ‘shhhhh!’. 

There are beautiful views over the valley and town. Many Nepalese people also present which is a good sign. 

If you’re up to it, walk down to the lake afterwards (much easier than walking up!). Beautiful vistas on the way down.

My husband and I ate here several times on our recent visit to Kathmandu. It had great local ambience, good food, and was a very pleasant place to relax with a cup of masala tea or a latte. The cinnamon yogurt on the dessert menu was fabulous.

Foreign tourist are made to pay more than locals and Indian nationals. And that's not the worst part, there are no clear sign at the ticket counter or no information to tell tourists that if you are not a Hindu, you cannot enter the main temple complex. I paid the ticket price only to be told by the guard at the gate that I can't enter and I wasn't even refunded the ticket!

I'm left bewildered and frustrated, with nothing to see at the entrance. I'm not alone as a few foreign tourist is in the same predicament as me. I felt ripped off.

This place is also filthy and there are dog feaces near and around the entrance. I think a UNESCO site and places of worship should be treated with the respect and dignity that it deserves, unfortunately the Pashupatinath committee doesn't seems to care about the upkeep of this place.

Until things change for the better, avoid this place, save your ticket money and go to Swayambhunath temple instead.
The Gaia restaurant offers good Eurasian cuisine at decent prices, and a quick service speed.  The non acceptance of cards is a bit of a dampener though...
A Nice Buddhist temple with a nice view to fewa lake. About 50 minutes walking up to the temple. But Nothing spectacular and not much else to do

We towed across the lake and walked up the many steps to reach the Peace Pagoda. Enjoyed a little Japanese Buddhist drumming and chanting, then strolled around the pagoda, enjoying the “silence” they ask for on all the signs. There are great views over Pokhara from up here.

The pagoda itself is nice, and the view (when clear sky) must be really great, but then the experience itself quite bad since there are many noisy tourists coming here who don't respect the silence that is required for this sacred place (there are signs everywhere but no one seems considering it). Best is to come by the lake with a small boat and to hike up ( 30 minutes through the jungle) otherwise the road to get there might be very crowded.

The food was delicious but only a really small portion of rice with the curry (which was very soup like therefore required rice to soak it up). When asked for some more they charged a lot  for another small portion. Shame as the food is really nice.

Me and my team visited Pashupathnath temple last April. And I was really amazed after seeing this place. There were lots of monkey and they were really funny. My experience was amazing. I got chance to experience hindu culture and religion first hand.

The service, hospitality and the food was just outstanding.  The staff were so kind and I cannot say enough about the food.   I am from the USA and have traveled 52 countries,  and this definitely stood out.
The location is outstanding, but the building is not unusual for Asia.  Go to see the views--it's on a ridge and you can see in both directions.

I called from the US one month prior to request additional nights be added to our reservation (10 friends traveling, 5 rooms.) I offered to book and pay but was told these could be added when I arrived. When I did arrive, I was told the hotel was booked and no more nights could be added. I tried to speak with management, no reply. The representative at the desk answered the phone during our conversation and passed the call to the second representative. They clearly had no interest in the complete inconvenience they caused our entire party of 7 physicians and their families. Go elsewhere. The hospitality in Kathmandu is exceptional.  This hotel is a frustrating outlier. Wish I had known.

Open air cremations is interesting to see but to a westerner seems a little voyeuristic. A guide will latch on to you when you get your ticket and its worth having one BUT agree the price first, we got ripped for $20 because we didn't agree the price first. Also the 'living gods' will cost you money to have a photo of or with. As with all religions you quickly realise the more you pay the better your chances of getting to their respective 'heaven' increases.....

I had to stay at the hotel for five days compulsory quarantine. However, this hotel didn't meet my expectation. I was also concerned whether the hotel has properly implemented the covid safe measures.
Very helpful and Very kind staff. Good service with nice and clean accommodation. We'll located and Very much comfortable rooms

The wonderful , kind staff treated us with love and helpful tips. We stayed here on three separate occasions - before , after our trek to Everest and after our trek to Bhutan. They made us feel at home every time, taking care of our stuff and remembering us like family. Shradha, led the team and spirit at the front desk with and Jhapad in the spice restaurant took care all of our favorite meals and details. 
We so appreciate the hospitality, and the housekeeping staff is absolutely wonderful. Rooms are spacious and lots of water for hydration.
It is one of the Jyotirlinga and on the must-visit list of every Hindu. It is 900 years old temple very well maintained and clean. The evening aarti is quite nice.
A fascinating insight into the religion and burial service our guide gave us an extremely good explanation as to the rituals.
I went for breakfast - only western options for breakfast as far as i could tell. Great masala tea. Nice place to sit with papers available.

Don't trust this hotel. The staff is dishonest and even the duty manager is hand in glove. There is no authority to look into theft. As soon as we entered we lost our money. Your belonging are not safe at all. It goes missing in your absence.
If you ask for cctv footage they will say that they can't show as per their protocol.
I have requested many times to look into my matter no one gave a firm answer. Even after returning back I was waiting for their response but in vain .
I personally request everyone please don't book this hotel its unsafe for tourist.

Best food, good services, 
Relaxed ambience.

From the moment you step through the door, it’s clear that this restaurant places as much emphasis on ambiance as it does on its cuisine. The space is thoughtfully designed, combining warm lighting, sleek furniture, and carefully selected artwork to create a cozy yet sophisticated atmosphere. The soft hum of background music adds just the right touch without ever overwhelming the conversation, making it perfect for both intimate dinners and casual gatherings.

The design strikes a balance between modern elegance and comfortable charm. Large windows let in natural light, and lush plants throughout the space bring an inviting freshness. The open kitchen adds an element of excitement, allowing diners to watch the chefs at work, while the soft murmurs of other guests create an overall sense of tranquility.

Service is attentive but not intrusive, complementing the relaxed yet refined vibe of the space. Whether you’re there for a quiet dinner or a lively celebration, the restaurant offers an environment that suits any occasion.

In short, while the food is certainly worth returning for, it’s the exceptional ambiance that will make you want to linger long after your meal.

As someone who’s stayed at many luxury hotels worldwide, I must say — Muskan Singh at Yak & Yeti stands out. Her elegance, poise, and radiant charm bring a signature warmth to the property. Always a pleasure to be welcomed by someone so graceful and polished.

Tha pashipati is one of Nepal's largest religions sites and its is also very familiar on the world this temple is very old structure there are many sculptures worth seeing here I think those who will be visit here 
       You will be fascinated by this idols so you must visite this and one thing in Nepal  that's  reason I recommend that you get a lot to see here theology of Nepal's
Peace place in pokhara.During our sightseeing program in pokhara our guide bring us here to visit,from where we can see the beautiful view of pokhara valley with fewa lake.

Magnificent hotel, which has seen its best times. Big grounds,swimming pool which all needs a facelift now. 
Staff was very polite and courteous. Did their best to make our stay pleasant. Excellent location.

I have been so many times at Gaia Restaurant with my Family and clients for lunch and dinner every time I had a fantastic service and great food service. Staff are so friendly smiling the quality of the food perfect healthy and hygiene super clean and nice garden.
I recommend Gaia place try ones Gaia foods and beverages.

Great overall experience. The staff is very friendly. The food was exceptional. Muskan at the guest relation desk was friendly and helpful from the beginning and helped us understand the various small things about the hotel and the culture etc and to get the most of our stay. I want to point out that so so many of the staff were so kind and gracious with us and I want to name them all yet I know I will miss some. My favorite parts of the stay were the people working here, the food, and the beautiful building.
The main areas are clean and beautiful. They are also comfortable areas.
There is room for improvement in the basement floors as there is some lack of maintenance and somewhat uncomfortable the jacuzzi area, etc. My experience there did not match the rest.
I enjoyed the use of the travel desk and it was very convenient. You should use it if you don't know what to do. Pick one and go!
I wish I asked for a tour of the location at the initial check-in and I wish I asked for more clarity on what came with business rooms.
Must-see places in  Pokhara here you  can see the beautiful mountains like Annapurana Himalayas as well as beautiful Pokhara city

Location - right in Pokhara tourist area near Lake side just off the main road, not noisy at night. Easily accessible to all the tourist eating and shopping places.
Service - friendly owner but the staff seems a bit distant and don't smile that much
Rooms - bed tend to sink in when you lie on it and I am not that heavy. Simple room, good enough for sleeping and that's about it. Don't expect any fancy decor. See the photos.
Breakfast - is thrown into the room rate, always the same, toast, jam, butter, tea/coffee..

Choose this hotel as it was part of the trekking package that I sign up on. So not much choice to change it. Like I said if all you need is a place to sleep then this place will do, I think the rate we got was 25 usd per night for a double bed.
Sacred place for hindu. Worth visit. Located in the bank of river named bagmati. Nice and spiritual environment.
Visit twice during my time in Kathmandu. First time it was ok but the secong time the meal they served was terrible. coffee was cold and service was poor.......

Wife and I used a bike to go up the road to this Pagoda.  The road is a winding mud and stone trek for about 3 kms... small cars would likely break their axles ... you need either a Jeep or bike and at places,  I had to ask my wife to get off so that I could take the bike across some dangerous sections of the road.   Once you get to the top,  you then need to climb a LOT of steep steps (it's quite a hike).  Depending upon your health conditions, it may or may not be advisable to take such a hike. It's frustrating to see that this place could have been such a great tourist attraction - but Nepal govt has not built a motor-able road to it. 

Once you get there ... the Pagoda itself is magnificent and peaceful place to be.  View of the Pokhara valley and Fewa lake is gorgeous from here.
A guide joined us for over an hour tour of explantions of hindu and the ceremonies. We saw 2 dead cremation ceremonies and with a guide explaination it can make sense.
as expected everything gone well. transportation and accommodation was great. helpful people are amazing

It is  situated near to Pokhara Lake. Shopping centres. It is budget hotel in perfect location. early morning go to the terrace enjoy the mountain views. Good service  and breakfast . There is no lift . need to take up the luggage, but the staff will help. 
The restrooms are not so tidy, and the wifi connection is very poor in rooms. available only in reception area
can visit this temple but as hindu .but hard to find even a toilet. the infrastructure is too old and need to repair most of the things

We enjoyed then stay very much and will be back soon.
The service was great as the breakfast. Special thanks to the team at the reception and restaurant

It starts with a very beneficial walk up many steps (gave up counting!) and ends with a simple, beautiful, serene building with a stunning panorama over the lake and the city.
Well worth the effort needed.

Fantastic food and hospitality! Love the place! We enjoyed dinner here two nights in a row and the owner is a great host!
He also spends his holidays picking up new ideas on how to further improve🫶!
We stayed at Raniban Hotel abd had a great view of the Stupa from outside our room. The stupa was below, and seeing it stand on  a hill top with the clouds below was beautiful.

The place is really very dirty and not maintained properly. Its an important historic place from the perspective of Nepalese history but the authorities need to pay attention to the cleanliness of the place. A very holy place for Hindus. You can also see the burning ritual of dead bodies behind the temple.
a little climb up and its a great view. you can see the mountains from there and the is a cafe where you can sit and relax and enjoy the view.

Went to this place with my Indian family and was not allowed to enter because I was a foreigner. They said it was because I was not Hindu, but how would they know? An American-Indian could have easily gotten in ( and be a non-hindu) just for looking the part! And even if you were hindu, if you are foreigner, you are still not allowed in! And worst yet, foreigners have to pay 1000 just to see behind the temple! If you don’t want to be mistreated, DONT GO! It’s not worth it to make the start of your day bad! These photos will be the only view you get from behind bars. Hope this helps you make a decision and if you still decide to go, good luck!

The main temple here is just for Hindus. As other reviewers have pointed out you can see dead bodies being cremated which I found very difficult to see. I also felt sad to see other tourists taking photos, imagine if someone turned up to your loved ones funeral and took photos, dark tourism, and so if you read this maybe think that's it's not juat a tourist attraction.

Wonderful views - need to get a ride there - too far from Pokhara.  Also note that once you get to the parking area it is still a ten minute climb.

Also check on cloud cover before going if you want a view.

We took a boat across the lake to the Peace Temple for the sunset views.  It was nice though not spectacular and afterwards we realized we would be walking all the way down the steep, twisty dirt path from the top of the mountain back to the boat in the dark!  We made it though my son did twist his ankle on some  loose stones. Fortunately the boat was still there since I had worried he would not want to paddle back in the pitch black.  All the other people who went there for sunset had taken the road route with taxies!

extremely expensive for no reason. The guard did not let me in to see the temple side because only hindu people are allowed. I am white, so apparently he did not believe that non-Indian or non-Nepalese could be hindu. He literally pushed me away and shouted at me until I left. Unbelievable.

Respectful on how to end one life in a open and holy place/ river.

Bachhareshwari Temple: do check it out too, as lot of traditional wood craving with eroticism, based on Hindu "Bible". 

Walk up to the hill and check out couple of Hindu temples too.

Be aware of all the monkeys in group as they are aggressive.

Enjoy enjoy
Nice place peaceful and calm and awesome view .loved it me and my son were happy going there.many tourist were there some stayed there for meditation too

We are 2 couples stayed for 3 nights.
Basiclly the hotel was ok but the last night there was a jazz concert in the hotel yard withe dreadfull loud noise that we could not stand.
Although we asked several times to lower the music we were decieved time after time and the did nothing to help us and all the other guests.
It is a scandal to organize such an outrageous event under the room windows.
Make surethis will not happen to you in your stay in kathmandu.

Not the sort of hotel I normally stay in but two nights either end of a trek were part of the package. I imagine once upon a time this was a magical place. Sadly it is now lack lustre and many areas need attention. 
My bathroom had been semi-renovated but the creaky stained bath, cracked tiles and rusted faucet did it no favours. 
My bedroom door lock failed and this took a long time to sort out. Bedroom carpet stained and furniture needing updating. Fridge was empty despite the list of drinks on offer. The staff I must stress were delightful. Helpful and courteous. All of them. No tonic to go with gin in the bar!  Internet (charged daily) is very erratic. Very busy hotel full of tourists which is great for the hotel and Kathmandu but if you like smaller, more relaxed accommodation Id suggest looking elsewhere.

We took a boat from Lakeside to below the Pagoda (NR850 return) -  fine way to cross the lake. Our rower dropped us off at a jetty at the bottom of the mountain and we started our climb. We are regular runners and walkers, but this was a tough climb. The path is very, very uneven and it was also very slippy in places after recent rain. It took us 45 mins to reach the Pagoda. We arrived hot and tired.

The Pagoda is ok, but nothing special, but the views are great. Not sure if it was really worth the climb. The path has virtually no signs and we got lost on both the ascent and decent. The descent took us over an hour. Just a few direction signs would have made a big difference. Hardly difficult to do if you value tourists.

We had a good workout, but the path was not safe and we would not recommend this route. Perhaps the taxi route is better.

The view from the Stupa is amazing, but the Stupa itself is alright. Not a lot of information for English speaking tourists here. Having a coffee at the nearby restaurant while looking at the Himalayan range is quite good though.
Not a pleasant place at all. I did enjoy the public display of cremation and our guide kept making a joke of everything.

The setting and ambience was stunning. I loved the garden area and the breakfast was great too.

My only 2 complaints are:

1. No complimentary Wi-Fi not even in the lobby. Wi-Fi is very expensive

2. Rooms were really smelling bad.

Otherwise we had a good experience. The hotel as such is beautiful.

I had booked a heritage room with queen sized bed couple months in advance but was given a modern room with two single beds when I checked in. They told me it's on a first-come-first-served basis so what's the point to book it in the first place? The power went out very frequently everyday and the wifi was highly unstable. Boiling hot water came out of both the cold and hot water taps and I couldn't wash my hair on the first day as the water was so hot! Someone told me to let the cold water tap run for 10 mins or so and finally I got cold water the second day but noticed the water was yellowish. Also, somebody was hanging underwears outside my window on my first day.

The compound is interesting and bustles with activity. Non-Hindus are not allowed to enter the actual temple though. (I wondered how they determine who is Hindu and who isn't, but I guess that's besides the point.)
From the outside it's possible to get a glimpse of the giant bull inside, but that's about it.

We weren't expecting to wander into ongoing cremations and felt very uncomfortable being tourists during such moments in other people's lives. We stopped our guide before he led us into a room to see how they handle the bodies. It was a bit much for us.
Excellent temple in Khatmandu, it is a must visit place , generally there are long queues to offer puja.

It was my first visit to an hindu temple of this calibre. It has a structured programme of offerings and prayers for devotees and the ambience of the place is simply amazing. We managed to get our pooja done in record time and the resident priests seemed to be well equipped to handle everybody's needs
I asked about their Wifi and they told me that it is working. However it was not working. So, no wifi, Food was O.K. but very expensive in Kathmandu standards.

After reading reviews in TA we decided against entering the compound to avoid the 1000 rps fee which didn’t make sense, having just came from Patan Durbar square which also had 1000rps fee. Instead we walked around outside the temple and observed the local Hindus making their way in. The streets around the temple are a little charming, plenty character and selling worship items. We are obviously foreigners but never harassed and felt safe. There are signs everywhere that the zone outside the temple is a beggar free zone, in fact quite clean vs what we were expecting considering the reviews. We didn’t see any ceremony during the time we are there around midday.

The hotel has standard rooms for a city hotel. Rooms are relatively small and deserve some update (cfr photos of bathroom door and sink). It is not easy to put away your suit cases due to limited space. There is a mini-bar and an in-room safe. Bathroom amenities are present with a hair dryer. The shower does not give a stable warm water supply. There is overflow of the water in the bathroom. Wifi works well. We had a private dinner with the group in one of the private rooms which was very well adorned. There are some nice shops in the gallery.

Best Chiken Roti ,and avocado lassi & carrot cake.  Beautiful environment fell like hole Europe here all tourist gather  here  .Very friendly staff and owner since 32 years doing  this . Excellent chef .

My stay in hotel grand holiday.
Its not clean enough, towels are dirty, inside room lights are not working. Some power plugs are working also. Bathroom is not clean. But there hot water system is good. I ask hotel laundry  cost and they said it’ll be per 1 kg 250 Nepal rupees, but actually it’ll be 100 Nepal rupees. You can go to street no.6 you’ll get laundry.
One of the most known temples in South Asia is the Pashupatinath temple. People throng throughput the year to get darshan of Lord Shiva

We went to the place yesterday after seeing the high ratings on TripAdvisor.

The menue is very basic, more or less the same as in all places in the Tourist Hub Thamel. The food was somewhere between poor and average, the fries were hardly eatable, the ketchup that came with them was gone off - they brought a better one after I complained. 

Free WiFi didn't work. 

The toilet is as dirty as everywhere in Thamel area and during powercuts there was no alternative lighting inside - which might explain the former. 

After asking for the bill twice we finally went up to the counter to pay as we didn't want to wait any longer. 

The food was disappointing, the service on the beginning good, then poor - it's really hard for me to understand how this place got such high rankings.

One very positive thing is the location: The restaurant is located in a very quiet side road of busy Thamel with a large courtyard that is ideal for children to run around. For that it's nice to visit and I might go again and try a coffee - maybe that's better.

this is oldest  shiva temple i visited. 

loved the  art and sace, river and nice temple.
being yoga student i felt good energy.

Maybe 30 years ago this was a 5-star property, but I dont think it has literally had a single update to the rooms for at least that long.  The rooms are TERRIBLE.  Two-star quality at the very most (maybe even one-star).  Honestly one of the worst hotel rooms Ive ever stayed and started my time in Nepal off on the wrong foot.  Do not stay here if want anything better than a 2-star property.  My mind is still blown that they hold themselves out as a 5-star resort.
Very large stupa worth a visit to watch the sunset. Large crowds so don’t except a lone experience. Climb up of medium difficultly.
If you have the strength to climb what felt like 1000 stairs, then you can get a beautiful view of Pokhara city. But its not for the faint-hearted.
It is interesting place where dead bodies are cremated according to Hindu beliefs.  Expect to get strong weird smells around it.

After trekking through the mountains, it was lovely to do an early morning walk to the Peace Temple whilst we were in Pokhara. 6am was a great time to start as we had our pick of boats to cross the lake and start our climb to the top. The views from the summit were stunning and views of the surrounding mountains were so beautiful.
Not worth it. The service is slow, the food is really bad, there are places that are much more confortable.
I don’t recommend this place to cuplé with kids. Burning dead people all the time 365 days. Coming by taxi from Thamel for only 5000 rupiah

It is a unique experience where you can get to see cremation of the dead by their grieving families beside the river that Hindus revere. I have had the privilege to visit the temple during Aarati time. Aarati usually occurs between 5-8 pm and around 5 to 10 Brahma performs a ritual, which includes, singing songs (Bhajan), dancing, and calling for Shiva. I literally got goosebumps while hearing the bhajan. It was a good experience, but please note that during this time the area is usually crowded as shown in the picture.

 Was directed to another part of the hotel down a corridor to use another elevator.  Unfortunately we got to our room and still no power. I took a boat at just past dawn and then walked alone up here, it took maybe an hour although it was an incredible jungle hike that was, I thought, very challenging. I enjoyed the small and humble cafes around the Peace Temple a great deal and had coffee and cinnamon rolls. The insane views of the Himalayas at dawn that were mind-bending. In January, it is all filled with huge poinsettias. Actually the Peace Temple has very nice flowers all around it. 

So go for the hike and the ambiance. The Temple itself was just like five minutes, walk around, there are a few illustrations of Buddha's life and then done. But then you go back to that sublime view and can't believe what you are seeing.

Pashupatinath means "Lord of the Animal". 

It is said that when the Pandavas went to Kashi atoned for killing the ancestors in the Kurukshetra war (To get rid of the sins of Brahman Hatya and Gotra Hatya). But Lord Shiva went to North India. The Pandavas started worshiping the Lord Shiva. Lord Shiva became satisfied by the austerities of the Pandavas and appeared to the Pandavas in the form of a bull. 
Seeing the Pandavas, Lord Shiva took the form of a bull. Bhim could recognize the Bull as Lord Shiva and tried to catch Him. The Bull started running away and disappeared. While His hand stayed in Tungyanath (Uttarkhand),  hump stayed in Kedarnath (Uttarkhand), His Face stayed in Rudranath (Uttarkhand), His navel and stomach stayed Madhyamaheshwar (Uttarkhand), His hair (jata) stayed in Kalpeshwar Nath Temple (Uttarkhand). Altogether is called Pancha kedar.
In His head part emerged in Pashupatinath, Nepal.
Pashupatinath is also regarded as jyotirlinga because it is believed to be half part of Kedarnath Jyotirlinga.

My second stay after over 10 years and we were decidedly underwhelmed by the service, facilities and maintenance / condition of rooms. Yes the grounds are lovely and on first appearance the hotel gives an impression of being 5 star with large lobby and larger than average rooms.  This is where the 5 star description should end. Service is mediocre to downright poor (upon checkout my bill was pushed towards me with no eye contact, no thank you and no questions re whether we required assistance for onward travel - we had stayed for 4 nights!). There was no recognition or greeting from any staff when we were entering or leaving (sometimes the door men would be nice but thats it).  The rooms themselves are dated and not maintained well.  Our phone didnt work, the tv is a joke and the shower curtain smelled and water leaked.  The travel desk at the hotel was poor - I was better off planning most things myself.  All of this I could somehow accept - this is after all a very poor country with limited infrastructure.  However, as a hotelier, dont charge 5 star prices and then spend nothing on maintenance, updates, staff training.  Because then you are taking advantage and dont deserve to call yourself 5 star.

We reached the parking for Peace Temple at around 5.15PM local time. We had to trek to reach the temple/pagoda on top of the hill. The trek of about 10-15min is moderately easy. The steps are not too steep and can be climbed easily. There are many tea shops where you can stop by if you want to rest for couple of minutes before continuing the trek. (Especially those who have knee pains or difficulty climbing up stairs without gasping).
Once you reach the top, it's an awesome experience of the cool air and the beautiful view of the Annapurna mountain range right across the Peace temple. Looking down below is the entire Phewa lake view and the landscape. This view is really worth climbing up the hill. As you move forward there is a white structure with a huge statue of Buddha in meditative pose. You could climb up the stairs in thw temple to get the view of the Pokhara valley from four different directions, each offering a picturesque view.

Around the temple is a landscaped garden with some garden chairs to sit and enjoy the ambience.The temple is neatly maintained and is worth visiting. The temple main gate closes at 6PM. However there is an alternative route you could use to get inside or out of the temple if you are reaching the temple post 6PM. However it is best advised to visit the temple before 6PM as the downhill trek in the dark and the transportation from the temple could be a challenge. The World Peace Temple or Peace Pagoda is a must visit place in Pokhara

Pashupatinath is my favourite place in Kathmandu. It's a sacred cremation grounds where Hindus bring the deceased to be bathed in the river and put on the funerary pyre. I can respect that some people may feel shocked since they believe funerals should be done in private, but I think it's also poignant that you can see families with their children and babies sitting on the river banks the whole day, watching mourners bring corpses to publicly and ritualistically burn them. When death is made public, the taboo surrounding it is reduced, and it becomes an easier more natural conversation to talk about it as an important part of life.

Be prepared for local guides to come up to you and start telling you about the place and the rites, and then ask for money. You may politely decline and just say you're here to watch respectfully.

You may also see cows walking up the stairs to the toilet area to have a drink of water, as well as dogs and monkeys.

I would not recommend using the public toilet here.
