The Peace Temple is a beautiful and quite place to visit. It has amazing views across the lake and local villages as well Fish Tail mountain if it is not cloudy. I would advise walking early morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat in the high season as it is exposed and with little shade.

You can get there via public bus From Pokhara main bus station take a green public bus to Chhorepatan Bus Stop (ask the driver). It will cost about 30npr pp and take 10mins. The bus will drop you off about 100m from the start of the climb which is located on the other side of the road up a dirt track. There is a faded sign which says Temple this way. 

Follow the signs and keep heading up. You'll be able to see the top of the temple ever now and then to your left. The path is well trodden and if you keep heading straight up you won't go too far wrong. I would recommend shoes or sandals to walk in.

There are beautiful views all the way up but the trek from this side is mainly steps.

Once at the top of the hill (next to Pokhara View Point) follow the path left and continue to walk to the temple. It is further along than you think.

Enjoy the views from the top and be sure to circumambulate (walk clockwise) around the Stupa to be respectful.
Greatway to ease into a short trek from Pokhara. And work out the kinks before hitting the trail stairs.

A beautiful hilltop location. Get a boat across and then hike 45 mins up steps to the top. It is pretty steep but achievable for even those who are less fit, just take it slow. Walk left ten mins on the main road if you want to visit Devi Falks and the Cave - though i think these are overated. From there it us a 40 min walk or 10 min taxi ride back to lakeside.

The staff are very friendly, kind and super attentive. The Chimney restaurant is Kathmandu's first fine dining restaurant and offers a beautiful, historic atmosphere for dining. The gym and spa are well equipped.  Yak and Yeti is truly a special place and was a big part of our enjoying Kathmandu.
Great view of the Annapurna Range & the Fewa Lake. Accessible on foot or vehicle. Best option: Hike!

definitely worth the visit coz of place's heritage value and holy vibrations.Management can be better,

If you are young and fit then climb up - about an hour else you can always drive up.You get a birds eye mesmerising view of town.

Food is very delicious.

Service very professional and kind

Went there in the morning, very nice view of the whole pokhara from the top. It feels so peaceful once you reach the top. Not much tourist when we visited so we were able to enjoy the view.

I stayed in Soaltee Kathmandu hotel for 2 days. Dined in Patio both evenings. Staff is amazing provided excellent service. Especially I want to mention Manish’s effort. The hotel complex is made up of different apartment blocks. Our block overlooked the pool but was the one that looked the oldest -  the others looked as if they were refurbished. Our room was on the top floor and had a double and a single bed. It was spacious and airy but everything seemed old and unkept. The bed covers were Dirty and had stains. The carpet had stains, my pillow cover had stains and the mattress lacked any comfort. The room quality is only a 2 star.  Walls had patches of  damp and were also stained. It did have a 14" TV with numerous channels. The hotel is conveniently located about 2 min away fromt he main tourist road and 5 min to the lake.  
We asked for the bed covers to be changed but the first call went ignored. We asked again but this time the attendant came and simply removed the cover and put it away!

It may be better in the rainy season when the fall is full of water. But they have a barrie around the fall do you can't enjoy it as other waterfall. There is a little wishing pond next to the fall and Nepali like to throw the coin into that pond to pray for luck.

A small Shiva temple inside the cave will make this meaningful for Hindus (see other reviews) but for everyone else, I would not recommend this attraction unless you have an 8 year old boy with an overabundance of energy or you are a 20-something trekker looking for something different to do. The cave is very hot, humid, and drippy. The steps are slippery and handrails are not always available. The cave is very dimly lit. There are parts of the cave where you have to climb bent over because the ceiling is so low. You meet people coming the other way, so if you do decide to go, you might choose to go at the beginning or the end of the day because there is not much room on the stairs. Sturdy, rubber soled shoes are a must and it would be helpful to wear a hat because dripping muddy water frequently assaults your hair and clothes. At the bottom of the cave you can see the back side of the waterfall which is fairly interesting but does not photograph well. We did not find this attraction very pleasant.

The service really stood out—staff were incredibly welcoming, helpful, and always ready with a smile. From the front desk to housekeeping, everyone made sure I felt taken care of.
I had a great time, highly recommended.

Take some time to walk down to the further end of the river and take in the view slowly if you are already impressed with the start of the river.

This is a very good property by Nepal standards but only average by international standards.  It did not have the ambiance Dwarika and is not as new as the Hyatt.  The grounds of the hotel is absolutely gorgeous and well kept, but the rooms and the interior is getting old and dated (not in a good way).  The hotel is located in a quiet location thus most of the rooms are quiet.  The rooms has a musty smell and there was a cockroach on my night stand.  They had upgraded me to a suite that had a sitting room and a kitchen.  The kitchen was not very clean and neither was the bathroom.  I stayed for 1 night in Sept since the Hyatt was completely booked solid.  Hyatt and Dwarika are still nicer places to stay if you are willing to pay the price.  Crowne Plaza - I would stay there again if Hyatt was full.

We checked the reviews and based on the trip Advisor feedback, we decided to stay here. It is not a perfect place, but is not too bad, in fact, I would define it as both historical & Interesting.   The rooms have seen better days but they are large and pretty well equipped,  although most items in the rooms are aged. Bed mattresses are very hard,  which i know suit Asian tastes,  but many westerners prefer a softer mattress,  including me.   The staff were pleasant,  and were very helpful with late night food. The restaurant has a very good breakfast with a lot of choice, not all perfect,  but certainly plenty of options that allows you to find something you love. Nepal is poor,  as are the staff and workers. This is reflected in some of the "rough at the edges" handling of inappropriate customers and management of unusual situations.   The Nepalese people are so polite and nice to visitors, maybe not always logical, unfortunately the same can not be said of some visitor's, with their rude crude attitudes directed at the Nepali staff.   Given what they must deal with,  i have a lot of respect for their continued willingness to serve.  The hotel is a historical palace, but was severely damaged during the 2015 earthquake,  but has remained open using the undamaged part of the hotel,  while the damaged part is slowly repaired .  We were two couples staying 2 nights then another night a few days later.  I am neutral on this hotel,  but i do note it certainly works as a convenient transit hotel when you visit kathmandu enroute to somewhere else.  It is nicely priced!

This is the neatest corner of Kathmandu. The gardens are well-maintained. There are terraces, benches, shade and sunny spots, a number of ponds and fountains. The security guard at the gate needs additional training in English. He refused to let us enter the garden after we had paid, and couldn't explain why. Turns out he thought we were part of another group who were still busy paying, and even though we told him that we had already paid, he just said, "Excuse me, don't go there." When the next group came through, he took their tickets and scanned it, and then when we gave him our tickets, he scanned it and allowed us to enter. He never asked for our tickets, and as we had not been here before, how could we know that this was their system?

One more point: You are not allowed to bring a picnic to this garden. According to their website, you may bring snacks, but not a picnic. If you want to eat, you are welcome to dine at the Kaiser Café, and although it seems to be an excellent restaurant, it's not suitable for families with small children, and its menu isn't budget-friendly.

Now, if i have to pay Rs300 to walk through a garden too small to be called a park, and aren't allowed to bring my own food, then i'm going to call it expensive. Of course, as with everything else in Nepal, foreigners pay more than locals.

The rooms were poor, the restaurant OK, and general attitude OK, BUT the location was superb, both for views and ease of seeing some "local" bits. Good massages are available a short walk away at a fraction of hotel price.

I feel so happy when I visited this place one the fav place to visit with your family friends and loved ones you will have a great experience about nature and lake views so you must go this place such a peaceful vibes and environment is just fabulous and fantastic well deserved to all the staffs were so friendly , kind and welcoming ❤️❤️❤️🥰🥰🥰🤣
not worth the visit; just a tiny cave below the devi falls. Took me 5mins and im out. Id rather spend my time on other activities

It's a limestone cave which is quite low in parts. My husband is 6'4' we reached a part which would have had him more then doubled over so we turned and came out the way we came in.  The lights were blown in areas so we needed our phone torches.
It is a very important place to Hindus.
Cost is reasonable for a tourist. 
Would like to see more lighting and height warnings.

The hotel is always in good condition. Upgrades are done often. The staff are super friendly. Good ambience. Except on the weekends where they often host weddings. The noice level can go up exponentially. Gets very crowded too ! But overall very nice and pleasant staying here.

Definitely worth a visit, but I would recommend not going alone as it can feel a little daunting. A guide would be beneficial too. I was approached quite a few times by beggars, but they were harmless.
You go through a lane with shops on both sides to this temple. You climb down the steps and then go through a cave which is slippery and narrow for two persons to cross
We went here as it was raining. The falls were thundering as it was the end of monsoon and we were able to get some fantastic photos too. Well worth the visit on a day when options are limited.

Visited here as part of a day’s sightseeing. The Stupa looks wonderful and the location is amazing. The are around the perimeter has a lovely atmosphere despite being almost exclusively tourist traps.
The Stupa and it’s environment itself is a riot of colour and is just great to look at.
The Stupa is a large building for an unknown relic. The stupa is well maintained and the shops around offer lots of shopping.

They are awesome. Their food is good. Their services were swift. 
They also have a pool and 24/7 bar which i enjoyed.    
Would come again
We had to pay admission to this place to eat dinner in the restaurant.  The admission wasn't"t much, but we couldn't see much at night.  It is small with pools and is lit prettily at night

We visited this place during the Aarti time in the evening. The temple was resounding with the chants of 
Om Namah Shivaya 🙏
The gufa had about 450 steps to go down to the caves. 
Nearby there is Tibetan handicrafts cente, from where you can buy your souvenirs and outside there are stalls selling Tea/ Coffee & Snacks.

A beautiful Stupa with souvenir shops encircling it. The Stupa itself is massive with prayer flags running to it from the surrounding buildings. 
It was very reasonably priced (Rs 400) and easy to find via the main gate. 
The surrounding buildings were arranged in a circle, predominantly tourist shops selling Nepalese souvenirs with roof top cafes - highly recommend sitting in one of these, enjoying the views, sunshine and watching the colourful hubbub below.
The Gompa was equally as stunning with fantastic views of the Stopa.

An awesome place to spend a couple of hours. Once you’ve had a walk round just have a seat and watch the whole world pass by. There are almost hundreds of small shops around the Stupa. You may visit a close by temple or just find a rooftop for coffee or quick meal.  
There a many Tibetan pilgrims walking their Kora around the stupa and this and the entire atmosphere makes the place some kind of secret.
More and more people drive the ways with their motorbikes and even with cars and make the atmosphere of the place down. I would emphasize everybody to complain about this behavior and make the place to the quiet place again.

Interesting story how this fall got its name ....

Went in winter and because of the lack of rainfall, the view is not as spectacular as during monsoon when the sight of gushing water would be more splendid.

Place is a little small and one can complete the walk within an hour or less

A very bust place full of Buddhist worshippers doing their clockwise ritual walking. Can get very intoxicating with smell of sweat and incense. Overload for your senses. Sellers at periphery of boundary. Bustling place around this complex. Over crowded.
Was a nice place to visit as part of a day tour. Great little side attractions to see more traditions and practices of the Nepalese.

The Lord Shiva is residing in a cave. You have to go downstairs to reach the God. First go through a cave and then stairs. The floor is almost always wet so have to be little careful while going down.

The Soaltee Hotel is a stunning blend of modern architecture and traditional Nepalese artistry, beautifully showcased through intricate woodwork and design. While it's a 5-star property, it stands out from the rest with its unique character and warm ambiance.
The Deluxe rooms are spacious and ideal for both couples and solo travelers, offering comfort and style in equal measure. The hotel also hosts events and has expansive, well-maintained grounds perfect for any kind of function.
I had the chance to tour the Everest Suite — the presidential suite — and it truly lives up to its name. Every detail is designed for privacy, comfort, and a true "home away from home" experience. It features its own gym, jacuzzi, sauna, private kitchen, and even a private lift — pure luxury.
The dining experience is equally impressive, whether you opt for the buffet or à la carte. The food is consistently delicious, and the service is top-notch. Every staff member I encountered was warm, friendly, and eager to help.
A perfect blend of elegance, tradition, and hospitality — highly recommended.

Four months ago, i had the best breakfast here and so i came back with whole family of 7 to stay 2 nights (3 rooms per night) at Hotel Barahi. Well, i was extremely disappointed with the accomodations and personally feel very cheated out of my hard earned money. At $92 USD per night, you get a rundown room with carpets that looks like it hasnt been replaced since when Nepal had Monarchy, the showers had permanent stain marks that i had the hotel cleaning staff (blessed her heart) confirm it wasn't dirt or water marks, the AC went out on a hot humid day that i had to call the hotel and we had to wonder out for stroll by lake to cool down, almost as illusion, the beautiful swimming only goes to four feet, basically swallow as the heart of receptionists here. They would only give you one room key. When we asked for a extra room key, they said " you can leave your room key when going out". The hotel staff had the nerve to call you on your cell just to ask when we plan to checkout the next day. They looks like they wanted us gone the soonest. My room had 5-7 switches just by the nightstand next to my bed, most of them had no functions and looks creapy. The size of TV is laughable ( about size of your Ipads) with remote that will make your finger bleed just to change the channel. My hotel room faced the opposite site of hotel and so my views was that of unfinished construction sites. Hotel lifts to the room smells of oily grease. Ugh..everytime.

I used booking.com and couldn't believe my eyes that people can be duped that badly. I bet the most clients bargains to half the prices here. Not to mention, the drinks you orders here are maximum overpriced. Visit the irish pubs couple blocks away from this hotel. 

On plus side, i liked the cultural performance  here. Those folks who sang and dance were friendly, smiling the whole time and we loved the music. 

Conclusion: Definately not worth your money for the experience here. Very disappointing and soul crushing experience for a vacations.

Its a cave temple having a Shivalinga supposedly dated back 500 years. There are a large number of steps one has to climb down to see the temple. There is an underground way from here under the hill leading to the Devi falls across the road. This passage from temple to the base of Devi falls underground was  quite dark and wet with water drops seeping through the rock above and not worth all the trouble. Civil work was going on probably to make it better and easier for the tourists.
Normally all tourist places in Nepal have a substantial entry fee but I was quite surprised to find that there is an entry fee to the temple also. People with knee or heart problems who cannot climb many steps can avoid a visit to this temple.

Although the name takes your expectations to another level but its does not disappoint you when you compare it to it's dusty and hustling vicinity. I found the Garden of dreams to be a very tranquil place until it was flooded by people. But its a nice place to sit and have a quite time with all the friendly squirrels trying to peek into your hands in search of food to munch. The over-all aura of the garden is very calm and one should not miss it during their visit to Kathmandu.
ONE you have to See while you where in KTM,  Have gone there everytime I go to Nepal , peaceful and a lot to see, every round is a different one.  Go there you would not regret it.

Great place to get away from the hustle and bustle of Thamel. 
Nice flowers and a bit of local history

I have visited this hotel recently for a workshop. The hall given was among the oldest in the hotel. It looked gloomy and dingy so was the shared bathroom near it (pics included)which was shocking as It is one of the oldest and the most prestigious hotel in Nepal. breakfast was buffet and tasty but not with a huge choices. few times before I have had their buffet breakfast which had enormous choices even buffalo milk, yak cheese, goat cheese and what not. I think this is due to the recession. Anyway the breakfast good.bakery items specially the cookies and Blackforest cake are awesome. We had buffet lunch also with Nepali and Indian food moslty and few continental items . The food was tasty. the ordered to cook pasta was really very tasty. The hotel lobby is very impressive with heavy furnitures that prove its oldness. the hotel decor was slightly changed and gradually it is gaining the contemporary look. One of the staff with a badminton rackat kind of deivce and a spray 'preying' the mosquitoes and other insects in the lobby was really amusing.[ though there were few mosquitoes flying in our hall]The hotel is spread over 11 acre of land though the location area is really maddening but once you enter the hotel it is like in the different world.
The service was so-so, not prompt. The concerned persons tried their best but......The staff ( I read his name something Prabin KC) assigned to look after us during the workshop was really very nice and smily guy. thanks to him. he did his job perfectly . I can not review about their room service as I did not use it same for their rooms. though their room seem to be very good and so was the ensuit bathroom. It won't be fair to write anything about that. In overall, I found, may be due to the recesion, its level is slightly down than my previous visits.

So here is where the water goes! So first, the area is really nice. I especially liked the colorful entrance to the cave. The cave itself looks a bit like a mine. It's super wet inside. Then you can see the stream coming from Devi's waterfall - and I feel like this part is more interesting.
It's not exactly a must-see, but it's quite enjoyable.
The cow in the cave is super weird.

This cave was small, short hike to see the water coming in with the crack in the earth close
To Devi falls. The entrance is nice! Short
Visit completes this site in 15-30
Mins.

Yes, it's beautiful and makes it look nice coz located right in the most dusted area in KTM, but it is small. Food there is ridiculously expensive. Everyone comes there to take tons of selfies so not very quiet and peaceful place. I wouldn't go there again

We stayed in a suite top floor of the hotel with a beautiful view to the pool...unfortunately you could not open the windows ... 
we paid for 3 days a total of 748 US $ - !!! 
.the room was very nice but all the house technik : Television , mini bar, air condition - heating, failed in many ways and as well cleaning of the room ....
Unfriendly employees at the reception when complaining....
Very nice temple a lot going; a lot of people praying as they walk the perimeter. Many of the Hindu we’re conducted they’re prayers “108 times”

I am currently staying here and though the hotel is undergoing renovation on the external part, it has absolutely no impact on the inside and service. Once you enter the hotel lobby you definitely get a feeling of being in an old magnificent palace. The staff is friendly and helpful and food wise - pretty good as well - even breakfast. Rooms are well equipped however the bathroom is very very small. There is 24 hour room service for food and it was extremely convenient since we went with a group of friends, we were able to enjoy overnight conversations with selections from their menu. The location too is very great, just a maximum 10 minute walk to Fire and Ice Pizzeria and Thamel :) overall the experience is pleasant and nothing to complain about.

The Boudhanath Stupa is very close my hotel.It took me 8 minutes to get there.I walked through the local alley and did not see the ticketing office.I went inside of the Boudhanath stupa directly.The Boudhanath stupa is completely white and the top is gold.the top parts look like the face of the human and so many flags there.I do not know much about the attraction.Just followed the others.The whole atmosphere was so peaceful and I walked around the Boundhanath Stupa very happily.It felt like no burden on shoulder  at all.Very impressive feeling for me.
Nice cave with small Shiv temple at entrance and then have to walk down some steps to go deeper towards the bottom of cave, slippery and low so have to be careful and can see base of Devi Falls!
Amazing place to go and see and it is nice to see the locals going there too. Obviously a place for pilgrimage.
nice but it was in very limited place it was a historical buddhist place the crowd was very much it was good to visit once
Quite nice and attentive staff, I loved the coffee and the plunger in room. I've always hated having to go for nescafe but this is refreshing too see

Adjacent to devis fall and 4 kms from Pokhara city Gupteshwar Mahadev cave situated. A rock cut cave goes to other side of devis fall and entire cave droping water drop. Here is lightning arrangement by official but advised must have a tourch because everything black inside the cave. This is beautiful and must see location for  travellers. You can see a Lord Shiva temple, statute of Lord Ganesh inside the cave.

you will feel like Indiana Jones after u pass the temple n enter the real cave.. at the entry, there is a woman who will ask u to donate some milk at the head of "lord shiva", if u say no, she will be super annoyed..
the tunnel like path is very much interesting.the cave is cold n drops of water dripping from the top.. amazing experience..

Water of the devi's falls outlet coming here so many steps down. lastly I saw light and aound of water, i have not find any attraction, except temple. Nodoubt lot of tourist are coming , but ebtrance fee, what i feel is High....

Hotel Barahi is a nice hotel near the city centre of Pokhara. The rooms are placed in different buildings. We came with a group, and most of the guests were satisfied with the rooms. Our room had swimming pool view, but it was cold at night. The rooms at the backside and in the second building had a better temperature. 
The rooms are spacious and nice, the bathroom was old, but ok.
Good food both for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
A nice bar, pool and ok service.

Boudhanath Stupa is lovely. Well worth visiting. Entry NRs 400 pp. The large stupa is attractive. There is a lovely traffic-free circular walk around the stupa with an outer ring of interesting buildings with shops, cafes and monasteries. It felt peaceful compared with the bustling streets outside.

Boudhanath stupa situated about 6 Km west north of center of Kathmandu. Its amazing largest its type of Buddhist  Stupa in the world. I have visited several times and love to visit again and Again. Unique, Peacefull environment, Historical and Unique designed. Do not miss to visit once in a lifetime. best for travellers and local too
It is very cheap so not a huge problem but there’s really not much to see, the waterfall is surrounded by an ugly chain link fence.
Not many steps but slippery. Need to be careful. Interesting Shiva worship site inside the cave. Some more steps, not all even- so have to be careful- and the waterfalls can be seen at a distance.
The stay was really amazing enjoyed the fullest… the service & dining was also great. The property itself is great… ms Dil Kumari was so helpful to meet my needs
It has little garden and a small waterfall but has long canyon inside the ground. Combine the visit with the mountain museum

I stayed at the property for 2days in December 2013...

The Hotel is located as an Oasis slightly out of town.... There is some work going on at the road adjacent and the entry is troublesome.

The Hotel premise is serene, calm, tranquil and beautiful...

The ambiance and the feel is also nice....The rooms are large enough with comfy beds, a workable "BIG" LCD TV and all necessities.

The staff like most  Nepalis are courteous and competent.

Buys, must be wondering about the average part.....

Here it is,

1) The bathroom with its half draining toilets are TERRIBLE.

2) I had to ask them to change the sheets the next day.

3) House keeping was TERRIBLE... You had to follow up ON and ON for some basics as in towels, room spray etc.

4) Breakfast spread was GOOD but some items were disappointing with bland tastes..... The bacon for example was rubbery and stiff and pan cakes were not upto the mark.

5) We were on a conference and the SOUND system was the WORST I have experienced in a hotel of such standards

I was in a group and may be the HOTEL is different with normal guests.... But I am making a trip to Nepal next year and Soaltee will not be the hotel I chose.

Unfortunately we did not arrive until late afternoon - so the light was fading. Nevertheless, an impressive structure. Many people walking around the stupa in observance. There are many nice cafe's and restaurants around the perimeter from which you can watch the whole spectacle unfold. The structure was unfortunately damaged by the earthquake so had scaffolding in places. Still worth a visit though.

Their buffet has a variety of different cuisines from around the world; Nepali, Indian, Mongolian, Italian, American, French you name it  and each has an authentic taste. 
The staff are so helpful and respectful and they treat you as a monarchy. 
A special thanks to Ragisha and shreya who took care of me. ❤️
Seems nature is god . Through under-construction steps have walk to reach lord shrine and some water fall ,, might be Devi fall.more seperate seperate structural stones build up by devotiees.
The falls are interesting as they simply drop into the earth. There was too much water for us to see the bottom - perhaps next time!

On arrival the hotel looks inviting but it soon disappoints. There are 3 buildings and we stayed in the oldest, the others may be better but who knows. Issues included - the toilet broke twice, the air-con stops and wont restart during the night, the bath was filthy, there was no top sheet on the bed, the wi-fi was better at 4000m on our trek and the carpets are thread bare. And by the way, the breakfast was very ordinary and the coffee undrinkable. It wasn't particularly expensive but it needs a lot of work.

I stayed a total of 7 nights in September.  The pricing including breakfast was very reasonable.  I was in 3 different rooms and all were very nice.  I like a bath tub and asked for one each time.  The pool is lovely.  A/C in rooms is good.  Service is very attentive.  Rooms clean.  I would not hesitate to stay again.
Airport pick up was good and I was met on arrival.  Money exchange gives a good rate.

I can politely tern this visit as one of the not so memorable one. Being a member of Taj Hotels group , my first preference is always Taj Property mostly in India.This time I went with the family recommendations to Soaltee Brunch along with my entire family n friend. My views :
PROS :
1. Well managed pool.
2. Efficient bar tenders and swift in their service.
3. Beautiful property
Cons:
1. Limited food spread.
2. Live station chef appeared to b under trainee serving under cooked food.
3. All the food in the live station was being served cold.
Overall lot needs to be done in terms of standing to the reputation.
Nice place to visit. Steps are slippery. The view of the falls was great. Nice experience. Air is not so good.

it used to be a wonderful place when I use to visit Pokhara as a kid.. there were no bars, it was scary & still is in monsoon!! There is a cave opposite to Devi's fall & u can see the other side of the fall from inside the cave and that is really amazing.. the force of river has crafted caves, nature can be really scary.. Devi's fall from inside the cave is beautiful yet really scary.. It reminds you never to underestimate nature :)

The rooms are nice, the overall quaint feel is good (the 'old palace' charm works well). Service is very good, and the breakfast is actually very good indeed for a hotel in this price range. The rooms are comfortable and amply sized. Location is decent. Its a 20 minute walk to Thamel or to King's Way, but a rather smog-bound 20 minutes that makes your head spin. At least its nice to return to the relative quiet of the compound oasis. And the pool area and garden are very pleasant, by the way. My two main problems are a) the wifi is terrible! This is not OK in a slightly up-market hotel. A complete rewiring and upgrading is needed; b) if you really insist on having muzak in the lifts, please make it a full play-list rather than a single song (Karen Carpenter) on an endless depressing loop!

Garden of Dreams is actually beautifully maintain garden in dusty part of Kathmandu just need Thamel.  Well worth a visit in you are staying in Thamel area.  Lovely set garden cafes, however staff are very aggressive which is so out of place for Nepali's.

We chose this hotel on the back of reviews we'd read, plus because we wanted somewhere with a little outdoor space for our small kids to run around.  When we arrived we were given a room facing the back, not the gardens.  It was dark and charmless.  Worst of all it didn't look like it had been cleaned in quite a while.  We complained but nothing was done - I ended up wiping something brown (i don't want to think what) off the walls myself.  

The following morning we noticed the room opposite, which had a garden view, was free so promptly moved ourselves over.  This room was the same size, although double bed inside of two rock hard singles.  It was certainly cleaner.  Don't know why but it just had a much nicer feel. Perhaps it had something to do with the fact that the mountains came out the next day - amazing!

The breakfast was fine, the gardens pretty and pool was great for our little ones.  The location is good, walking distance to the lake and shopping.  They do also serve the nicest Nepali Tea we had while on our trip.

One final thing though. I did lose a necklace while we were staying here.  I can't be 100% exactly sure what day but I am sure I had it when we arrived and I didn't wear it, but it was gone when we got back to Katmandu. I mentioned it to the hotel but they seemed really unconcerned. Not great service.

I went there on a sunny day. The place was full of people. Inside there are some spots where some Buddhists pray. There were some beautiful flowers inside a metal bowl on the wall. It was a wonderful experience.

I went here to see the gardens, and eat at the Kaiser Cafe. I was disappointed with both.  I mean, its fine.  Its a pretty garden, and it only cost 200 rupees, but it didn't knock my socks off.  If you need a break from the city for a few hours, it could be a good place to go, but if you are short on time, and trying to pack as much as you can into your time in Kathmandu, this should not be a priority.

First of all... I found the location quite nice. Lots of space inside the compound, with good restaurants. Easy 15-20 minute walk to Swanayasbhum pagoda, and about the same to Durbar Square. Through an OK neighborhood that allows you to see normal people going about their business. Not worth to take taxis from there, unless you go to Thamel or farther afield. It is Kathmandu, so it isn't a leafy, relaxed walk but it is interesting.
Where the hotel really let me down was in services... I tried 3 times to book a mountain flight, leaving my interest with the front desk only to come down a few hours later to a new crew at the reception and my request lost in limbo.
The third time I decided to go with the reception to the travel agent in house which was 2 young men who asked me to pay in advance, without giving me a confirmation. I found this quite unprofessional so I walked away.
I was very disappointed that an international hotel wasn't able to book this for me... I am sure I am not the first one with this request... Disappointed.
The breakfast staff tries hard and despite a few inconsistencies, they treated me very well.
Spire Elite and received no upgrade, last room had a window covered with a tapestry that let in a lot of light.
Next time I will try another property.

A Heritage oasis located in the bustling Lazimpat district close to  many sites of interest including Thamel shopping and entertainment area, but peacefully set back from street. The staff are definitely the crowning glory of this hotel, who consistently demonstrate care, efficiency and dedication with a smile in all departments. Nepal encapsulated at its best !

They offer clean and  spotless rooms. Staff is very welcoming. Galleries and walkways are good for taking pictures.
All the must visit places are nearby. Thamel market is 10 mins by walk.
They offer lavish breakfast. One should always include breakfast in booking.

There was an amazing set of circular stairs, with concrete images of Gods and Goddesses and vines adorning the walls. 
When it got to the entrance of the underground cave, as an older traveller and not to steady on my feet, I found this experience a bit challenging. I was lucky to have a wonderful guide with me who assisted me in the long walk down and up.
The history behind this sacred site was interesting, and the experience worthwhile.

Services 10/10, People so nice here! 
Had a super great time here!
All staff here are so nice. 🥰🥰🥰
Super great room and food also.

Its around 150 meters down. Be careful in the rainy season as stairs will slippery. You will love the cave - feel  like you have entered in an ancient world - dark and mysterious. There are some light inside. So no problem by going with out lights unlike bat cave. Overall it was a good experience.

Location is good 50m up a lane from the center of the Lakeside golden mile of restaurants and shops. Rooms are comfortable but dated. Breakfast buffet was good. 

Repeated attempts could not resolve wifi issues which we did not have at outside coffee shops.

One of the best place for sightseeing in Kathmandu, if you are looking for a rich history of ancient city. This ancient medieval town is absolutely beautiful with its rich architecture and monuments. The place is much more crowded during evening therefore if you want less crowd then one must visit at the morning.

Stopped here for a quick visit on a recent trekking trip. The site has been nicely rebuilt since the big earthquake six years ago. Lots of people, shopping and opportunities to relax with a cup of tea.
Great place to practice and witness Buddhism culture. In center location with great hotels and cafe with rooftop view of the stupa.

Despite being in the middle of (very busy) Thamel, the garden is peaceful and very pretty.

It was raining whilst we were there so we couldn't hang around too long as there was no shelter. I can imagine it would be a lovely place to linger on a dry day.

Beautiful falls and an interesting history (named for a woman who got swept away) but it is surrounded by a lot of tourist-focused stalls and very aggressive sales efforts. The litter is a bit unsettling too.

I don’t like being a negative Nancy, but it’s a stupa. It doesn’t really have that ‘wow’ factor I was expecting. Not only that you have to pay to get in. However, if you are facing the main entrance, turn left and walk round a little bit. You’ll find an alley of shops, walk down the alley way and you will be able to get in for free! So, if you’re going to go, use this entrance.

If it’s your first time visiting a stupa, it’s pretty cool. But a stupa is a stupa, they down change that much.
If you love buddhist culture, you must visit there in bouddhanath temple which is located in Kathmandu.

This was my first experience of the caves. The path leading to caves is beautifully painted. Once the caves start its dark and water is oozing out of caves so wet too. 
Deep inside is stream of water flowing heavily and one see wonder inside the earth in form of different texture on wall of caves.

I had really amazing time visiting here. Place was great food was great. I was really fascinated by Buddhist culture. I get to learn the life of Buddha from our guide and I was really inspired my his story.
Most visit place in the heart of Kathmandu. If you like to see the Tibetan culture then this is the best place to visit. Recommend for everyone
Its an awesome experiance if you are interested in cave hunting. Go all the way down and you can see the water flowing down from Devi's fall.

Majestic Stay at The Soaltee, Kathmandu

I recently stayed at The Soaltee in Kathmandu, and it was an exceptional experience. The hotel is majestic, beautifully blending luxury with a serene ambience. The spa was wonderful—truly relaxing and rejuvenating.

The hospitality stood out the most; the staff were incredibly warm and attentive. The food was also top-notch, offering a great mix of local and international flavors.

I highly recommend The Soaltee to anyone visiting Kathmandu. It’s a perfect blend of comfort, luxury, and excellent service.

I do not give easily 5 stars, but this wonderful hotel is really a jem...
Nice room, excellent service, a very good restaurant (with 24 hours room service) with many veggie options, conveniently located and moderately priced. It is a pity that it was too cold for the swimming pool.
Highly recommended!

Great drinks and amazing staff. The location is in a quiet area of the hotel with chill out live music. We had amazing mojito cocktail and there is also a big variety of drinks, wines and cocktails. Thank you very much for your service Manish. We will be back soon!

The stay was great and i would love to invite my close friends and family here as well,the breakfast has a lot to offer and varies.so i would love to give at least 5 star from the hotel accommodation to staff all very friendly

1st day we stayed in family the accommodation(ground floor) was normal interms of facilities.But on 2nd we were provided accommodation in 1st floor facing mountains (awesome).comparatively ground floor big room no view,1st floor small room but very good Mountain View.Oshin in reception was friendly in explaining about the facilities around Pokhra.

My local tour guide & driver suggested we call into Devi's Fall on Thursday 12/07/18 & the admission fee NR 30.00. A spectacular forceful water fall & many times I was tempted to jump in due to the high humidity & heat. Apart from the Water Fall not really much else to interest me within the area.

In our first room we could not sleep as pipes kept making squeaky noises all night which woke us up. Also we were right by the stairs which creaked loudly when other guests used them, which also woke us up and one of the (very hard) beds made really loud squeaky noises when you made any movement at all, which also  kept waking us up. We asked to move rooms because of the problems and the staff were very nice about it and let us switch. 

However, we were then put into a room which backed onto another property which plays VERY loud jazz at night! We were also woken up by a cleaner vacuuming the carpet outside our room at 5:45am one morning. We complained, slightly baffled that we had been moved from one noisy room to an even noisier room, but the staff just shrugged and wouldn't help. The room we had been moved to was a split level one. Don't accept one of these rooms, especially if it is hot, as the air con unit us downstairs and you can't feel it upstairs where the beds are, meaning it is very hot and sweaty in bed. Also, the ceilings are very low and you can hear EVERYTHING going in in the bathroom of the room above you! We lay awake at night listening to people use the toilet seemingly right over our heads! We're not especially sensitive to noise, my husband is actually hearing impaired and he was still bothered by these noise problems! 

The pool area is lovely, but be warned that although you will be paying quite a lot of money to stay there and hope for a peaceful swim, the hotel let anyone pay a small price to use the facilities. At weekends, the pool was full of noisy local children and its hard to find anywhere to sit or lie in the sun. it doesn't seem fair when the price you pay to stay there is quite expensive by Kathmandu standards. 

Also, watch out for the hotel travel adviser. We booked a mountain flight and specifically asked for the earliest one. We booked and provided our credit card details. However, a group from the hotel wanted to book a mountain flight together, they wanted the later flight, so the travel agent changed our booking and put us on the later flight so he could save transport costs! We found out the night before our flight and he lied and protested, even saying we were 'making trouble for him' when we insisted he book us back on the earlier flight. He did put it right, eventually and after quite a heated discussion, but we wouldn't trust him at all. 

All in all, we expected more. The hotel building looks really lovely and the staff, apart from reception and the awful travel adviser, are all nice. It's away from traffic noise, but we found it difficult to sleep or relax by the pool and those are the main things we expect when we book a hotel. Be warned!

I had a fantastic 7-day stay at the Shanker Hotel, and it was truly amazing. The entire hotel's architecture is stunning, and the staff is equally remarkable. The breakfast offered a diverse and delicious selection of both local and international items. The bedroom was always kept clean, with a pleasant fragrance and comfortable bedding and pillows. The washroom was immaculately maintained as well. However, what really stood out for me was the exceptional staff.
During my stay, I received special support from two outstanding individuals, Ramesh and Sandesh. Ramesh warmly welcomed me and made me feel at home right from the start. His introduction to Nepal and its people was captivating. Sandesh, a talented bartender, was there during all my breakfasts. Not only did he serve drinks, but he also shared insights into Nepali culture, paintings, and spiritual details about Hinduism and Buddhism. Beyond being a bartender and a member of the breakfast team, Sandesh is a natural storyteller and cultural ambassador. I trully recomend the hotel but I should say: search for Ramesh and Sandesh, your Nepali experience is going to be trully meaningful only by hearing to them.

One may be led to believe that it has become little other than an opportunity for commercial interests. An entrance fee, although best intentioned, restricts access and turns it into a tourist attraction. The Stupa and adjoining monastery can be visited and viewed in a short time. However the surrounding area is filled with accommodation, monasteries and retreats that provide for an extended buddhist community including visiting pilgrims. 
It is a wonder to see and a focus for the world’s buddhist community.

We stayed one night in a standard room and one in a deluxe room. The standard room - ground floor - is only metres away from the path to the dining room and so, unless we drew the curtains shutting out the views and fresh air, we were constantly being observed by guests on their way to eat or walking to their rooms. The deluxe room was on the floor above, in a different building, and did offer some privacy. Rooms were certainly in need of updating - old furniture, tired and dull bed covers and decorations. Carpet felt decidedly dirty. 
We ate dinner in the hotel's restaurant the first night but were so disappointed with the food, that we ventured into town and ate at Cafe Concerto the second night (a 15 minute walk and well worth it). Breakfast was again just average. Two complaints. First if you come to Pokhara for trekking, as we did, the trekking companies want to get on the road as early as possible - 7 am - but breakfast doesn't start until 7 am- If so many tourists are here for the trekking, why not open the restaurant at 6:30 to accommodate them? And second, timing of the items coming from the kitchen - you can have toast at 7 am but butter didn't arrive until 7:20; coffee and cereal were in place when we arrived at 7 am, but milk took considerably longer. While all the staff were friendly and courteous, they need training in efficiency and organization. 
Grounds - another reviewer mentioned this - were attractive and if you have a clear morning, the view of snow capped mountains is a wonderful way to start the day. A new restaurant is under construction and that constant hammering and drilling (until 9 pm) spoiled the experience for us but once complete, I imagine this would be a very peaceful place away from the hustle and bustle of the town (although only a short boat ride and short walk away).

Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave
Gupteshwor Mahadev is a beautiful cave just opposite to David Fall. A giant stalagmite within this cave is honoured as a Shiva lingam and the devout flock here to pray. Entry tickets allow you to enter the temple. For some extra money you can also obtain entry to the tunnel behind, which comes out at a wet cavern right behind the gushing Devi's Falls. Once inside the cave, look up at the ceiling and you will see detritus and branches in cracks in the rock. These have actually been pushed up there by flood waters that fill the cave during the monsoon.
