Davis fall is beautiful place in Pokhara, you can see water fall which comes from Fewa lake Pokhara. You can take car or public bus from Hotel. You will see some statues inside here where you can click photos.

Built some time around the 14th century, the huge meditative monument is said to have been created just after the passing of the Buddha. The huge offering site quickly become an focal point of worship and offering in the area.
A relaxing place with a sad story. Quite calm and reasonable value for what it is. It is especially good in rainy season.

This hotel is quite nice.  Well kept up and well maintained.  A few service glitches though.  We were originally checked into a smoking room without asking if that was ok -- it was not.  One morning all elevators in our wing were not working, and management seemed not to know about this -- seemed odd.  Our main complaint was over the A/C.  For two days we complained that the A/C was not cooling the room.  For two days we were repeatedly told that someone had fixed it, that it was being worked on, and would be checked.  Finally with a manger in our room, I asked if we had any control over the A/C and he FINALLY admitted that the A/C is centrally controlled, and the room thermostats have no impact on the room temperature!  It seems a lot of wasted time could have been saved if we had been told up front that the thermostats in the room are for show only.
I added this on the end of a trek to the peace pagoda and Tibet village and it was interesting but the falls were not that impressive.  I’d recommend a trip there though.

I stayed there for 2nights, very poor management of the hotel. Staffs were unfriendly. Carpets in room were stained and dirty. No locker/ safe in room, bed was the type that you get in cheap lodges. Room service was horrible. Breakfast was Ok. Location was good. Travel desk was too expensive.
We are conventionally accustomed to view water falls falling from a height. Devis falls is lovely and the falls when I saw was from below the ground level - it was a sight to see. Do not miss it

Its a beautiful cave with religious significance. One can explore the cave, its amazing. We can also see parts of Davis Falls from it. There are many souvenir shops near by it where you can get various beautiful handicrafts.
The stupa is centrally located and has shops all around it. Its nice walk around the stupa and good places to shop for souvenirs
Not much if compared to important waterfalls of the world. More interesting things to see in Pokhara.

Soaltee Kathmandu was excellent in every way. The breakfast spread was the best 👌. Made for a very good experience. 

BUT

The casino at Soaltee was a big let down. Didn't expect a hotel of such high repute to have a casino with cheap ambience with poor & discourteous service plus(it was like a dance bar). People need to really think twice before visiting the Soaltee casino!!!!

Simply, the location of this hotel is superb. The view over the lake is stunning and can't be beaten. Getting the boat across to the hotel is also really cool & it is incredibly quiet and peaceful.

But for the price they're charging the quality of the room isn't good enough. Everything is very dated and shabby. Our carpet had holes in it and the air conditioning made the room smell really damp. 

We stayed in one of the cheaper rooms, so I don't know what the quality of the more expensive suites are like (especially the premier ones that look over the lake) but for the price we paid I think there are better places to stay in Pokhara, especially as anyone can get the boat across for lunch or dinner and take in the view.
The crowd, the cave... it is a surreal experience visiting the cave. Lovely experience and for the religiously inclined a must visit

I had an extremely unpleasant stay at this hotel. To start with, our money was stolen and when it was reported to hotel, the staff behavior was shockingly rude and unprofessional. The MD of this place is extremely unprofessional, and so rude to women. He passed sarcastic comments on women. 

Safety was another major issue. As a woman, I felt deeply uncomfortable- staff was judgemental, no CCTV cameras, and no sense of accountability from the staff when safety concerns were raised. It was so stressful to stay here.

To top it all off, the food was ridiculously overpriced and not worth the money. Poor taste, limited options, and exorbitant charges.

Overall, this hotel failed on every front — hospitality, safety, and value. I strongly advise against staying here, especial women or solo travelers.

It was not worth a visit...hardly and water flowing and it was all barricaded and you cant even see the water.
Dont waste your time visiting this place in pokhara...there are far better places to visit

Shreejan took me to this UNESO temple and immersed me in the Bhuddist devotion both physically and through  discussion which was easily understood. He was also keen to discuss cultural issues and urbanisation , at my request, with respect.
We then went to Pashupatinath, where Hindi  traditional cremation took place.
Once again Shreejan was most informative.
I appreciated his pace and thoughtful choice of explanation.
An upstanding man and tour guide.
Ask for Shreejan.

Danielle AUSTRALIA

The entry into the property is really nice - all the way to the reception! The staff is friendly and helpful. The property itself is very nicely spread out and the exterior has a very nice feel. The lift was lit up quite weak!
The reception area and the room needed some upgrade. But on the whole is a very comfortable and nice set up. Took an early morning flight out and the staff arranged a quick bite with some tea/ coffee at the bar - on their own initiative. Thank you for the same!
Has a casino - didn't go there but - the option is there.

My wife and I visited Kathmandu in the first weekof December. The hotel. whichg used to be a royal palace, is looking a little tired now and the inner corridors are dim and claustrophobic. The rooms are dated in style but functional but few have views with most windows looking onto ledges filled with air conditioning units and cables or onto overlooking buildings.

The staff are friendly and helpful.

The bar is small and windowless, it smelled so strongly of old cigarette smoke that we had to leave.

No free wifi but you can use the business centre computers for free.

it is a short walk (10 minutes) to Thamel which is the main shopping area. In Thamel there is a Himalayan Java coffee shop open 9am to 9pm every day with food and Nepalese coffee

This was our second visit to Fish Tail Lodge, the first being in 2020 on an organised tour to Nepal. This time round we did the itinerary ourselves and knowing we planned to return to Pokhara it seemed a no brainer to return to Fish Tail. Although the Lodge was undergoing some refurbishments to some of the rooms it didn't impact on us as were were out most of the days. The food was as good as I remember and the views of the Annapurna range (when clear) were amazing. The staff were very helpful and attentive and spoke good English. The location of the Lodge means you can walk into Pokhara and find something to eat and the local shops are great for doing some shopping. I would definitely recommend Fish Tail Lodge, it's quiet, has great views, good food, great staff and gives back to the people of Nepal.

This hotel has a great location and beautiful grounds.  The rooms are very nice, especially if you are on floor 4 or higher.  However, even after making this reservation months in advance, and requesting an upper floor, they proceeded to try and give us a ground floor room.  They reluctantly gave us an upper floor, but only after we insisted, which means it was available, but they just didn't want to give it to us for some reason.  We also were suppose to stay there when we first got to Kathmandu, but they canceled our reservation the day before we arrived and luckily our tour operator was able to get another hotel for us near the Shanker at the last minute.  

The bartender and housekeeping staff were excellent.  The front desk people need to take a lesson from them on customer relations/service.  

Also, make sure you check your bill before you pay it.  They insisted we had dinner there one night and were very nasty when we corrected them.  We had to point out that someone else signed our room number to their bill, even though the name was wrong and it certainly did not match our signature.  They still wanted us to pay for it.  

Also if you like extremely hard beds (like sleeping on a board), you will like their beds, if not, don't stay here.

So all, in all, if you don't mind rude people, it is a great location and a nice room.

One of the "must visit" sites in Kathmandu. 400NR entrance fee. Whole range of people present - from tourists just aimlessly wandering around, to devote pilgrims prostrating. Was not expecting to see all those tourist shops and cafes surrounding it but try to focus on the religious elements.

After paying NPR 200 (approx. USD$2) you enter the green gardens which you're free to wander around & explore. There is a nice (albeit a bit overpriced) cafe inside that you can have a meal and/or drink. There's also Wifi which is charged at an extra cost. A good place to wind down & after a hectic day in the Kathmandu or Thamel. I can't help but also think this is where the young lovers also go to canoodle to get away from the public.
Whilst in Kathmandu, Boudhanath Stupa should be on your short list. My suggestion - do the walk around but then grab lunch at one of the roof top cafes to do some people watching.

This hotel need a lot of refurbishment. The old part is not ok, the club rooms are ok. I changed room after one night, needed upgrade to have it ok. The lady in reception should make it, but started with other customers. That irritates me. Garden with breakfast is good. But in total, the hotel can not defend the price they ask. The Summit was full else I prefer that.

Not a place for a visit in monsoon season.  First, it is very wet and smelly.  You cannot see much and are not allowed to go very far to to the high water levels.  Not worth the time and price, though minimal. Just cross the street to Devi's Falls.

Nice caves. Easily approachable. Will take 20 minutes to walk across a dead end harbouring Diddhi vinaysk statue. Way inside caves is very wet as water goes on pouring from ceiling but not slippery. It is uneven and not for very old person with limited mobility. Limited lights but not dark at all. Windy and damp but you do not feel suffocated at all. Must visit as you can feel the Devi fall roaring sound where the caves. Very nice place. You do need to bow down for a distance of few meters but do not require to crawl. Nice sculptures at t
he entry stairs and huge statue of Vishnu with sheshnaag. Do not miss

The Soaltee Kathmandu is a beautiful hotel! The rooms are very comfortable and clean. The grounds are very peaceful and comfortable. The staff is incredibly helpful and hospitable, especially Jyoti and Sajuna! 

The complimentary breakfast is amazing!!! An incredible variety of foods. So good!

We stayed at the Soaltee  for 12 days.  Whilst the hotel grounds are just lovely, in my opinion the hotel is tired.  The staff were incredibly friendly but the service was exceptionally poor- in particular- there was never any soap or toilet paper in the lobby toilets and one had to ask staff members countless times to attend to it and the toilets were always dirty; the rooms were not actually cleaned by the housekeeping staff; the bathroom was not cleaned unless we asked; a mistake was made with our account and our credit card was double charged - when I pointed it out to the night staff I got told that it was absolutely impossible and I was wrong- next morning though, when I drew the matter to the attention of the accounts department it was sorted but not with good grace; I lost count of the amount of times I asked for coffee at breakfast; the massage area in the beauty spa was not clean.
On a good note, New Years Eve Bollywood entertainment was excellent as was the buffet and the Chinese restaurant within the main hotel is certainly a cut above everything else the hotel had to offer.  The concierge was very good regarding arranging taxi service.  The shops down stairs are also well priced and offer good quality products at very reasonable prices

It was an amazing trip. Specially the dinner at kakori (the Indian restaurant) was lovely with an exceptional service provided by Shambhav in kakori. He was really friendly and has good knowledge of food. Also he has the skills of promoting his restaurant and getting the guest back.
heaven for business trip as i can enjoy my free time in SPA and serene surroundings. the food is marvellous. staff is full of courtesy. nothing tp regret about.

I was  there with my family I stayed for one week
This hotel just wonderful
Stuff so helpful and smiling 
Food was great 
I would like to thanks everyone for security in arrival 

...Reception
Restaurant 
Housekeeping 
Spa 
Thanks to all I would like to visit you again
Small, and many areas are closed  due to earthquake damage. Right in the centre of town and noise from the road makes it anything but peaceful.

An interesting trip it was good to see the strange formations but would probably be better in the rainy season. Very dirty though. Great to visit the nearby cave temple to see the falls from both angles.
Opposite to Davis falls, the gupha actually ends up showing magnificent Davis falls through a crater but that's all about it.

Nice and beautiful spiral steps of about 200 to reach Gupteswar Mhadev, a descent Shivlinga of about six and half feet tall inside the interesting  cave where water continuously dropping from the roof. Another 100 steps downwards to reach to Kamdhenu who gives us milk automatically as soon as we kept hand below her utter. Really fantastic idea and arrangement. A few steps below saw the fountain which flows continuously through tiny spaces of two stone walls and disappears inside unknown Patal . Colourful designed spiral steps , wall sculptures of the entrance and overall this cave is no doubt a visitworthy place of Pokhara . I appreciate this tourist spot and recommend to all to visit definitly.
very nice place. I loved it very much.  This is with Buddhist flavor.  I love this beautiful ancient design.
When we visited in may,the waterfalls was ok, but probably better after monsoon as would be fuller. Still worth the visit.
i love the view from boudhanath stupa. you will fill peace of mind while visiting boudhanath stupa..

Beautiful hotel, amazing breakfast, well-maintained gardens, well-equipped gym, stunning pool, and most importantly very friendly, hardworking,  and hospitable staff - thanks to special standouts Bigyan and Yuna from breakfast restaurant for impeccable service!

In a natural cave, a stalagmite was found to resemble the lingam, symbol of the Hindu god Shiva, and a temple sprung up around this phenomenon. The style of the temple is interesting because the art is quite different from the conventional Hindu iconography. Then comes the underground part, which reminded me of the title of a book (unrelated): "In Other Rooms, Other Wonders." You can see a stone cow being milked and more. If I did not give it 5 stars, it is because there is a yuck factor involved: the underground trajectory is slippery, slimy, and dark. We visited at the tail end of the rainy season and water was filtering through the soil, causing a constant drip. Possibly this may be less the case in other seasons.

Beautiful setting and right on the lake with great views.
Peaceful and very kind, friendly and accomodating staff. The room we stayed at was as comfortable. Food was excellent! Spa treatment on site was very relaxing. 
Highly recommend this place for couples as well as family with kids.
Best place to relaxing and enjoying nature on earth, excellence service, spectacular view very nice food. we love this locations so much we are going back next time at same locations.
Nice garden away from the busy traffic in Kathmandu. Relax in their coffee house.  Entrance is NPR200.
Such a wonderful place to visit and join the monks circumambulating the stupa. It is full of shops selling religious paraphernalia and is a foodie's paradise!
Not much water in winter, lots of people, huge safety rails block views and photos of the falls. Overrated. Stayed about 10 mins top.
Good place to take some pictures and have a serene environment. But for the price it is not good enough.

The circular street with its shops, restaurants and hotels surrounding the stupa is the real attraction. This is a great spot to watch Pilgrims from all over the world pass by. Exploring the maze of narrow pathways through ancient buildings and shops is the real draw here. Sunset is a great time to visit the stupa as the monks light a ton of candles for worshippers to offer to the dieties. Some incredible photos of Nepalese kids in candle light at sunset are easy to capture here. Watch for the ever present pick pockets. They are eager to relieve you of your watch, wallet or anything else you are distracted from caring for.
Great experience and love the service. Overall im really satisfied with this hotel and cant wait to be here again. Thankyou !!

I decided to stay at this former palace instead of the American chain hotels to experience local culture. Unfortunately after arriving I noticed that half of the hotel had been damaged in the earthquake and was under repair. This hotel offers amazing rates right now and this is why. I had a nice suite at this hotel and even though two of the rooms right next door were under remodel they managed to work pretty quietly and I was not disturbed by the ongoing repair work. The former entrance is closed and you enter the hotel through the side door. There is no direct elevator to the rooms, so it is not suitable for people with mobility issues. You have to walk up steps to fourth floor and then you can take an elevator. The location of the hotel is in a better part of town. The hotel is on a flag lot from the very busy Lazimpat Road. First it looks like you can't walk anywhere, but if you dare to cross the road or take a cheap taxi, it is very near Thamel road, which has tons of souvenir and other stores. Walking past the French Embassy on the same side of Lazimpat brings you to a grocery store, Radisson hotel and tourist shops. I think it is good to stay at this hotel to support the rebuilding efforts of this very earthquake devastated city. The staff is nice and they are very helpful.

This is a newly opened attraction in Pokhara featuring a waterfall into a "swallow hole" and an underground cavern system. Its impact will of course depend on the state of the water levels and it will be at its best in Spring during the snow melt period.

The only positive thing I can say about the property is its good location and size. Not too far from the airport, almost walking distance from Thamel, a large well maintained lawn and close to several other attractions. 

The hotel has outsourced its travel desk to an agency and you cant trust their services. We asked for airport pick-up and were surprised to find an old worn-down regular taxi picking us up. We planned a day trip to Nagarkot through the travel desk. I specifically asked them to confirm the type of car they would send for the trip. I was taken to the porch and a large Toyoto or its equivalent was confirmed. The payment was made in advance, however when we got ready to leave, a small Ford Figo turned up after we had waited for 20 minutes. No apologies. No remorse. This is what we have, take it or leave it. Like most of Kathmandu their travel desk is closed on a Saturday. So plan your holiday in advance or through some other agency.   

Other reviewers have mentioned "good breakfast". Reality is that its average or below average. Some have mentioned outstanding staff but all we noticed were people loitering around doing nothing. On all days we had breakfast at the hotel, the staff is more keen to serve their seniors who were having breakfast by them selves rather than assist the guests. 

On the first day itself I noticed yellow water in the taps. Assumed there was something wrong and highlighted to the staff. No action. The next day I insisted on meeting a senior person to find out the reason and solution. He simply mentioned, "we take water through borewell and even after treatment, the colour remains". He added "please use bottled water to brush your teeth!" 

The hotel willingly provides free wifi password but the network is weak in rooms and works best around the lobby.

On seeing the pictures and reading the reviews one expects a heritage property but renovated with modern amenities. The hotel claims to have old world charm. The reality is that its old, period.

Kathmandu Nepal is a stop you likely won’t forget. As we wondered around the city time has not changed a whole lot. One stop, Boudhanath Stupa is a Unesco World Heritage Side. It is one of the largest spherical stupas in Nepal and the world. A religious site and place of pilgrimages for Buddhism. During prayer people walk around 3 times or more repeating the mantra. Lot’s a small shops surround the Stupa. Great people watch site.

On first encounter the building is beautiful with well manicured gardens and great perimeter security. On entrance the staff are utterly weird, emotionless, unfriendly robots. A helpful man in pajamas took our bags to 'the room' in the basement which felt more like a cell. It was poorly lit, poorly aired and completely filthy. We had to move, reception told us the hotel was full so my wife asked for a taxi to move. Amazingly, the manager pulled a room from nowhere and we headed to it with little expectation. On entry the room was slightly less musty, still filthy but with 2 chocolates on a plate..........we agreed to stay. The next 10 hours were occupied with little to no sleep while listening to the crazy shrieking and clicking of the plumbing. Our alarm sounded at 9am, we sat bolt upright and checked out immediately.

I went to this place looking for some quite time. I came across this place while I was strolling down the streets of Kathmandu aimlessly. But I am glad I reached here. The place was amazing. The garden was beyond the dream and my imagination. I really had peaceful time.

Names after a Swiss tourist drowned here in the 60s. We went in April, and there wasn't so much water flow. The water from the flow passes through a cave (Gapteshwor Mahadev) which can be accessed from across the street.

It was worth visiting both places, however for those tourist that are tight with time, I wouldn't mind skipping in.

Every single staff member — front desk, housekeeping, even security — seems to know you by day two. They remember your habits: what you like to order, when you prefer housekeeping, little quirks, even the small challenges you’ve mentioned. It’s super friendly without being pushy; 
I wanna come back to Nepal because of this hotel and because of mountains.

- nicely located
- rooms need renovation (old but clean)
- nice pool
- breakfast ok
- expensive for the value proposition
- inconvenient way to get to the hotel (have to take a small boat to cross the river)
- Try to find Dill, a cab driver in front of the Hotel, very helpful

A tranquil, beautiful garden just across the road from thamel mkt. A very Victorian garden with lil water bodies. It's so well kep and super clean. There's a cafe inside too. Just that it's not too large and 400 NPR is a little high fee to enter. But, do go to relax or regain your smiles

Had a great food and chill sesssion at Patio! Excellent service and recommendations by Ms Sajina . Had the local Mutton Butwal and Vegetarian momos . Spicy and very delicious . Recommend these local treats !  Looking forward to come back soon with the family!

It surprises me why such a beautiful place is made all about the fall of a lady into the river. The place is beautiful and you will see the waterfall from a large underground crevice and from the cliff above. So you basically go through some temple ruins underground passing by a shrine into a cave to see the underground waterfall. then you exit and cross the street to access a nice garden to see the river and waterfall. Then drama comes in where you read about the tragic death of lady Devi. Don't hold on to the tragedy, life goes on.

The hotel staff are very experienced and knowledgeable. However, it is noticed that fine detail in certain parts of the hotel are missing. 
The first day was very welcomed. The following days, the service to the room was not to the standard of the first day. For example, A/C off during some nights, no throw overs on the bed. newspapers on some days and not others, morning breakfast leaflet missing most evenings so that clients can have breakfast in their room. The most frustrating thing about the rooms are hygiene: Toilets DO NOT flush in single go, it takes three to four flushes, the shower needs attention, for example the water trickles. 
The room was provided with fruit on the first day and I requested this for the subsequent days, however, I got instead 3  sweets somes days which is not healthy living for those clients who are diabetic. 
It is worth also commenting that staff outisde of the hotel do lack customer care. Clients sitting outside for whatever reason do not get asked if they want anything. I think there is loss of revenue here . I am sure staff would like to have coffee or other refreshment if they were offerred.
At time during the evening, bar staff outside are no where to be found. 
The 5th floor lounge was well managed on the first day and again any subsequent days, it lacked customer care. Choice of food offerred during happy hour is limited and reapted day after day.  It is annoying for clients to see that at 7:30 staff rush to put the alcohol away quickly. No client would the advantage if this was not given the priority. 
I think the reception staff, for example, Sujita and Rojina are excellent, however, their efforts are being tarnished by some minor staff which lack detail.
The morning breakfast lounge for me was very good and welcoming and they need to be congratulated.
In hope this provide critical but useful comments for the future.
Question for me: Would I come here again. Yes I think I would to see if any improvements were made  and was any notice taken of my feedback.

Kind Regards

Dr. Mohan Singh Chana

The stupa itself it simply amazing and a huge work of art. It is a must see 

The area around is a weird mix of places of worship and people selling everything from prayer flags to hiking gear

So much potential to be a great 4 star hotel is constantly missed or even avoided by casual management and lacklustre services. The ground staff exude good will but are not backed up by a well maintained hotel that is showing signs of fatigue. Most cafés, hotels and even buses provide free internet at acceptable baud rates; the Shaker charges $2US for 15 minutes of sporadic connection. Some rooms are charged at high rates and boondocks standard while the suites were left empty; we offered to pay more for the upgrade on our package rooms but that became too difficult. Grand dining rooms provided a barely adequate standard of breakfast but covered multiple cuisines. The porters and door guards were a delight and the waiters good company

The garden was first developed as a private venture in 1920. It was subsequently taken over by the government but fell into disrepair until the Austrian government sponsored renewal of the gardens early in the 21st century. The redesign was pioneered by a German architect Gotz Hagmuller who also still owns the Milla Guest House in Bhaktapur (where we stayed).
It is now around half its original size and there is a small museum that contains photos illustrating its original layout. The gardens themselves are immaculate and there is a café, Kaiser Cafe, named after the original owner that looks out over the garden. You do need to pay the entrance fee to gain access to this.
It provides welcome respite from the frenetic activity outside the tall walls that surround the garden.
Itself peaceful place. I especially recommend to buddhism for visit this place. 🤘🤘🇳🇵. Good place for short trip with friend and family
Little far from thamel but very nice place to visit. I went there at afternoon time nice restaurant around this stupa with rooftop having great view of stupa from the restaurant

We had a fantastic time during our stay at the hotel. The service provided by all staff was excellent. They were so quick and willing to make our stay memorable. My wife has an allergy to chillies and lemon. They made food specially for her. Our heart felt thanks go to the chef Gobinda and the waitress Ganga. The hotel is in amazing natural grounds with a lake surrounding us.
The fall will be missed due to the shops and market area,but for the board put on the road. It is very deep and is very nicely covered by the gouge crevices.

I read many reviews before visiting, and they are mostly accurate. The garden is a nice area to relax, read and picnic while exploring Thamel. 

Sadly, it is yet another example of grandeur gone to waste in Nepal. Yes, a portion of the gardens have been restored thanks to the Austrian Government. What saddened me was the state of the beautiful buildings which border the garden. 

TIP: be prepared to fend off squirrels while you eat and do not leave food out. They are extremely confident/annoying.
Fierce water fall, just opposite Gupteswar Gupha. Entrance fees of Rs. 30.00. Not a long trip, 20 minutes is enough.

Spectacular cave, very deep and thrilling! A must see landmark in the middle of a populated neighborhood, this cave is also a religious place and if you are lucky enough you will see pilgrims chanting and dancing traditional hindu songs.
Normal stupa. Nothing special. Might be a site good for historians. Not for tourists. Couldn't find it interesting.
The place has changed from the last time I visited long time ago. The view of the waterfall was all barred by the fence
I had stayed with this hotel for 2 nights was not a good experience. location wise it is good but the services were very bad and their was no response from the staff also.

A rather small garden but definitely peaceful and a great way to get away from the dust and chaos of the Kathmandu streets.  Lots of local lovers sitting on benches and selfie snappers. Small but well formed if your looking for a botanical garden this is not for you but the 200 rupee entrance fee makes it something to have a quick look at or even stay longer as there is a cafe on the site.

Soaltee Crown in Kathmandu is beautifully and expansively located covering a huge area with good restaurants, a casino, and lush green gardens with a picturesque view of mountains in the background.  The hotel itself is beautifully decorated with traditional woodwork.  Its a pity that the combination of such a beautiful location and so much land under a prestigious hotel brand does not make up for some of the downsides of the hotel, which with a little more attention can be completely overhauled.  First of all, the rooms in some wings are damp and dark which gives them a certain shabby feel.  I stayed in June and since it was raining it was making it feel even more damp and gloomy.  The room amenities such as toilets and showers needed a retouch and fixing and these were not looked into till I started staying in the room.  The carpetings and upholstery didn't help the feel if not worsened.  I felt that for the price I was paying I wasn't getting as comfortable an accomodation.  I also felt that the hotel didn't utilize the acres of green it had under its wing properly as during my two weeks stay I didn't see much use of the outdoors other than to lounge around.  The hotel can do so much better by organizing outdoor bar-b-q's, open air entertainments etc.  This is especially needed for a hotel like Soaltee since it is a bit of a ride from the more happening areas of the city such as Thamel. 
The plus sides of the hotel are its friendly staff who demonstrated a nack for personal attention and the wonderful restaurants, specially the Chinese restaurant it has under its roof.  The other restaurants had great food too and so did room service.
No matter how many time i come and visit this holy sacred place, i always feels so rejoiced. Such a beautiful place for tourists !!

Often Visited many times. Being stocked in room for a months and months visited Kathmandu on Feb and after 14 days of quarantine in Hotel Trekkers Home, thamel. Visited this place many times by walking from Thamel. It tooks me 1hr 15 min to be there  by foot and scroll amour the stupa after go back to Hotel. Its a kind of adventure for me. One of the best place to get peace healing.

All The staff add the bfast buffet was very attentive and helpful especially Yuna. The room was superb and the hotel environment was nice and spacious. The food was delicious even the room service. Keep up the good job and definately will come again in future.
This was my first time in Nepal & Ms. Dil Kumari has assisted me in the best way possible to be able to explore Kathmandu specially Pashupatinath temple. Thank you very much for all the assistance.
Honestly, there are much better falls than this one. It’s a small fall in a park. Just skip it and do something else, instead of wasting time.
One must visit this location if travelling for Pokhara. Very beautiful and dangerous fall . You can feel the power of this fall .

Not a 5 star property ...3 at best 🙄

They do have a decent pool, bar and restaurant. Breakfast spread is decent , nothing to rave about. Service is good. Spa service is good but the spa rooms are substandard. The front office Supervisor (guy) is a sulky faced most of the time. Should work in back office. All the other staff are polite and nice. 

Too expensive for what they have to offer...3 star facilities and 5 star rate..very nicely located. 

Wouldn't stay here again though. ...🤐
Not much to see but a different experience. The best part is when you realize that you have reached to the other side of the falls. Shouldnt take you much time, on its way to the pagoda.

As you go from the Kathmandu Airport towards Hotel Shanker, your first thoughts are that the photographs shown on the  internet must be false.

As you reach this place, all apprehensions are put to rest. This is a palace converted to a Hotel and the premise is huge. Friendly staff and excellent breakfast spread.

Very well maintained swimming pool. Highly recommended.

This review of the Hotel Barahi in Pokhara is many months late in being written and posted. Life simply got in the way! But I still felt compelled to write about a very memorable stay at a fantastic property. In January 2025, I stayed at the Barahi with a group of 20 U.S. university students who were studying global health in Nepal for the month. From the moment we arrived until our departure five days later, we had a fabulous stay. Staff members were warm and friendly, the service was fantastic, the rooms were spotless, and the buffet breakfast was fantastic (certainly the most extensive buffet breakfast we experienced during our month-long stay in Nepal). Mr. Shaw, the manager of the hotel, went well above and beyond his responsibilities when he personally drove a student and me to the emergency room at a local travel clinic when the student experienced a health-related issue. I will be bringing another group of students to Pokhara in January 2026 and certainly plan on staying at this fantastic hotel again!

This hotel is a classic from back when people were only starting to go to Nepal, but it hasn't really been renovated since 1970. It is on it's own island on the lake right next to the town of Pokhara, an transport to and from the hotel is done via a barge that his pulled by an attendant using a fixed rope to either shore. While this is kind of cool at first, it takes a while and gets old rather quickly. 

The rooms facing the lake are festooned with plaques commemorating the stays of various prime ministers, UN Secretaries General, Prince Charles, and Jimmy Carter. All of these too place in the 60's and 70's. It is telling that none has taken place since. The rooms are incredibly small and have two single beds with blankets and sheets that could be described as "adequate." The bathrooms are an afterthought that are crammed into the center of the circular buildings so that all bathroom windows open onto a small center space and you can be treated to the sounds of your neighbors in the bathroom every morning. Showers have hot water, but that's about all I can say for them. Rooms generally feel like a weird room form a US National Park Service lodge at a third-tier national park from 1980. 

This is not to understate the convenience of the lodge as a base for seeing the surrounding area or the beauty of the lodge's location. The sun sets in back of the lodge so that they Annapurnas across the lake are lit up with the colors of the sunset and are reflected in the lake on a calm day. An amazing view and one to which semi-professional photographers flocked. From Pokhara you can walk anywhere you want in the Annapurnas, including to Annapurna base camp if you have a week each way. But the options are limitless. 

Be aware that Winter in Nepal is the dry season, so the cities are socked in with smog. The first day we were there, we couldn't see the mountains because the smog was so thick. However, if you spend a little energy to hike into the hills to the North, you can get above / beyond the smog, and then the views of the Annapurnas is amazing. I'm not too sure what the other hotel options in Pokhara are, but I go tthe sense that they are all fairly low end. All in all this is probably one of the better options in the area. 

The town of Pokhara itself is overly touristy. Restaurants are good and the presence of so many tourists ensures that picky eaters from the West can find a pizza or pasta, but I don't consider this a plus. We were finishing up a long holiday with a few days in Kathmandu and wanted to have a mini splurge. Unfortunately whilst Kathmandu is chockful of backpacker digs, there really are not many good midrange options. After blanching at paying a lot of money for what looked like a very average Radisson we stumbled across the Shanker and thought we would give it a try.
We managed to negotiate a free upgrade from a standard room to a suite. Oddly however, the standard rooms may actually be nicer than the suites; the suite had a lot of dead space which we did not use and, because of its size, was not particularly cosy (which is key in somewhere quite chilly like Kathmandu). Wifi is passable (although not free unless you negotiate it) but annoyingly you could only use it on one device at a time and had to continuously keep re-logging in. The hot water was good but you have to wait a good couple of hours between showers to get hot water throughout. 
The hotel has a certain charm, with Rana wood carvings everywhere but the whole thing has a slightly old fashioned, musty air. Breakfast was distinctly average (slash poor). Service varied; the people cleaning the rooms were very helpful but the food serving staff (especially around the pool) were patchy.
All in all the Shanker is an enigma of a hotel but we would still be inclined to recommend it above its peers in Kathmandu (but largely because it is a very poorly serviced class).

{Note: on Google this is listed simply as Buddha Stupa, of which there are so many! It is immediately east of the Hyatt Regency Kathmandu.)

Your trip to Kathmandu should include: Dhubar Square, Swayambhunath, Pashupatinath (the burning ghats) and the Buddha Stupa (or Boudhanath Stupa - the one adjacent to the Hyatt Regency).

The Boudhanath Stupa is akin to a large village square, only this huge stupa is at the center and it is ringed by a road with shops, restaurants and temples. A great place for wandering and people-watching.

We visited and I recommend: Nani's Kitchen (if you are there for lunch or dinner); the Jamchen Lhakhang Monastery; and the Guru Lhankhang Monastery.

By the time you reach this stop, you could be excited or tired from a tourist attraction. This was our last stop and we felt it was the same as what we have been seeing around Kathmandu. Of course the temple itself is a beautiful architecture.

There is a spiral staircase adorned with events from the Hindu mythology as well as sculptures. This spiral staircase leads to the entrance of the cave. 

At the entrance of the cave, there is a small shrine containing the Shiva Linga. There is a staircase that leads through narrow passages. These passages had dim lights and water dripping from top. It was a bit humid inside. At the end, there is a slit in the rock that shows the bottom half of Davis Falls. Photography is not allowed inside the cave, but it can be taken. The entry fee is NPR 100 per person. It is not suitable for senior citizens.

The majority, if not all of Kathmandu's attractions are Hindu/Buddhist temples.  The Boudhanath Stupa is the 2nd largest in the world and largest in Nepal.  To Hindus making a pilgrimage, visiting this site is a spiritual experience.  To myself, it was more of a cultural learning experience.  

At all the temples I visited, I found it difficult to separate the commercial elements from the spiritual ones.  I would say the Boudhanath physically separated these elements, but commerce was still abuntantly present at the stupa.  I consistently found it strange to have so much commerce around and within various places of worship and meditation.  

Of interesting mention, our tour guide was quick to point out a "fake monk" in the square around the stupa that was accepting donations.  Hindu monks do not solicit donations actively or passively.  If you encounter any individual dressed as a monk and is readily accepting donations, beware they are likely cheating.  I am suprised their presence is tolerated at all.

Visiting Boudhanath Stupa is a truly mesmerizing experience. Located just a short distance from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu, this iconic Buddhist stupa is one of the largest and most sacred in Nepal. The moment you step onto the grounds, you're enveloped by an aura of tranquility and devotion.

The stupa itself is a masterpiece of ancient architecture, with its striking mandala shape, the all-seeing eyes of Buddha, and the vibrant prayer flags fluttering in the wind. Walking around the stupa (known as the kora) is a deeply spiritual experience, as locals and pilgrims chant mantras, spin prayer wheels, and make offerings.

The atmosphere here is peaceful, with a sense of reverence and calm that is rare to find. The surrounding area offers a variety of Tibetan shops, cafes, and small monasteries, perfect for exploring and soaking in the local culture.

Whether you're seeking spiritual enlightenment or simply a peaceful place to reflect, Boudhanath Stupa offers an unforgettable experience. A must-visit for anyone in Kathmandu – it’s an awe-inspiring and serene place that leaves a lasting impression.

Background: As part of a two-week escorted tour of India and Nepal, our group passed by the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave in Pokhara. At approx. 8,500 feet, it is said to be the longest cave in Nepal.

PROS: Located near the town centre along Siddhartha Highway, it's easily accessible. It is just across the street from Devi's Fall that the two can be combined in one 2-hour trip (or half-day if including a hike from the World Peace Stupa). Technically, it is an easy-grade cave. The main shaft is nearly horizontal in nature, no side branches, not requiring SRT (single-rope technique) training or any extra special gear of any kind, in-cave navigation is very simple, the path is lit, no ladder pitches, easy to access from the surface, and is a short trip of less than one hour, well suitable for the complete beginner. 

CONS: To be clear, this is NOT a cave for spelunking (cave exploration). It is set up more as a Hindu shrine and a tourist attraction. And my use of the term "attraction" is already quite a stretch. Before the ticket booth are numerous souvenir stalls selling overpriced wares. There are no cave guides, but you can just follow the endless procession of people ahead of you. After descending a wide spiral staircase, you will enter the cave to find it dark, damp and dingy. Whatever illumination you find is provided by a sparsely strung-out series of small, dim light bulbs. As you inch past the Cow Shed, you reach one of two chambers. This main one is dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva; it has a large stalagmite which resembles (or is symbolic of) the deity. Watchful guards forbid photography here. And if you wish to pay your respects to Shiva up close, you'll have to line up, remove your footwear, step on poop or what-have-you, and walk barefoot up to the shrine. (No, thanks!) Now, past the shrine is the cave's second section, where you gingerly inch forward over uneven slippery rocks plus a slippery single-lane metal staircase to see the bottom part of Devi's Fall. This section is often crowded and is closed during the rainy monsoon due to flooding.

Verdict: It goes without saying that, if something is not worth seeing, it is not worth visiting. And having to pay NRs100 for foreigners, it feels like a rip-off. Not unless you're a devout Hindu or feeling mightily philanthrophic, in which case, be my guest. Don't get me wrong but, with all due respect, no thanks. Grade C-minus.

This is one of the world’s largest stupas and home to a large Tibetan Buddhist community in the city.  Admission is 400 rupees payable as you approach the main square. On reaching the stupa, the first thing you see are crowds of people all walking clockwise around the perimeter. It is important to walk in this direction as this is a sign of respect. Access is also allowed on the first tier; shoes must be removed. Here devotees are prostrate in prayer, the whole experience is very moving

Gifts of rice, sweets, biscuits and money are handed to Buddhist monks, the food is placed in a large vessel and mixed together while one monk recites scriptures and others playing various wind instruments creating a solemn atmosphere.  The food is then placed into bags and at the end of the ceremony, handed to devotees as gifts.
Aside from the temple, there are shops and restaurants all around the site, there were huge crowds in the square at the time of our visit and the atmosphere was palpable. A memorable experience.

saw some negative reviews about this place, may be they didn't saw the beauty of it like I did. Lies in a convenient place and is clean. 
Pro tip: Visit during monsoon when the water is at the highest. you will be covered in mist as the water roars and enters cave.

Devi's fall is one of the famous site in Pokhara,Nepal. At Pokhara people normally stays near Lakeside. We have hired 3 bicycle for a days and went to devi's fall. It is almost 20 min to half an hour ride to the fall from lake side. The fall was really huge with a big noise of water. In front of the fall there is another important place, we which is gupteswar gupha. So it's worth going to the place.

Good service by masta bidur Prakash buddhiman 
Good service and good environment clean natural beauty we will come again
With so much else to see in the area, don’t bother with this place, especially with their blatant  two tiered pricing policy towards tourists.  Extremely small place and garden

FishTail Lodge in Pokharra has one of the nicest surroundings I have ever seen. The small island is green and lush, the grounds are well kept and the views are spectacular. It is a pity thought that the hotel quality does not match its environment.
Fishtail lodge badly needs some major uplifting. The room was pretty old and tired; the carpet is completely worn out and smelly. The bathroom was damp and clammy and ants were running all over the place. The bed was very hard and uncomfortable. The place is definitely outdated!
I was not impressed either by the food quality either and had much better meals in town.
WiFi is inexistent there. I paid close to $ 15 for a day of service but the internet never worked. 
Unless the place goes through some major renovation, I would not advice to stay there, especially at the price (close to $ 200 a night).

With respect to the processing of personal data, the principles of lawfulness and transparency are completely fundamental. I have been to this property for fine dining with a friend. In this case, we have concluded that the CCTV cameras filmed more of the restaurant's premises than necessary and covered guest seating areas in the restaurant. Restaurant guests have a legitimate expectation of not being filmed while they are dining there. In places used for relaxation, recreation and social gatherings, the privacy of guests must therefore be accorded considerable weight.

From the airport till the hotel I had an amazing experience all the staff are very humble and welcoming. The customer service is on another level and the facilities in the hotel are very satisfying, not only me but all the crew were happy and satisfied. Looking forward to another visit.

The park is quite nice and peaceful but it’s so small that I don’t think is really worth an entrance fee of 200 rupees unless you are looking to spend a few hours there reading a book or having a peaceful afternoon as it can be easily done in 10 min max. Within the park, there is a coffee shop and also a couple of building which didn’t have anything in it when we went. One of them had just been painted so not sure if it was under renovation or simply an empty property. There were a few abandoned buildings that you could see from the park which seemed to be very damaged from the earthquake too. Gorgeous but abandoned.

I stayed there because of the pool, service was good, the room out dated, small beds, noisy due to construction next door, internet took hours and some help to connect, pool and servce was good, the buffet breakfast ordinary, I paid too much 100 USD for the are is way expensive but I wanted to swim. I will swim the lake the next time and stay for 30 USD.
You can barely see the water flowing in winter season. I have came during rainy season and it was fantastic. We have visited the cave opposite to the fall, which is impressive.

Among many places of interest in Pokhara , Nepal, this is the best I would suggest, Situated on the main road, it has hidden withi itsekf a great tourist attaraction. A mahadev temple, has a Jal Narayan in a pond majestically. A  colourful staircase leading to a chill narrow cave inside is awesome. The Mahadev shrine is in the very first stage. Beautiful. Then as we go inside we have a GoSala. And deeper and deeper inside we see a ferrocios gush of chill water roaring. The place is reasonably protected for viewers. The gushing water comes from a great water falls which is just across the Main Street outside.
A wonderful Place indeed.

This fall is great during monsoon. less then 15 minutes by taxi and has meditating feeling specially listening to the sound of the water fall. There is a tibetan camp nearby which is also great to visit.

St Devis fall was a little disappointing. Saw it from the cave first which was a lot of effort for nothing really. And then crossed the road to see the fall from.the outside. It's pretty but not as big as I expected, possibly because of the time of the year. And there is alot of railings etc that obscure the view. But it is definitely worth going to see
LORD SHIVA under the caves is very beautiful. you keep going below the lord statue there is a beautiful water falls.
A very refreshing place with the mist off the falls and the sound of the gushing water. There isn’t that much to see, though, so you only need ten minutes.

I stayed at the Soultee 3 nights as part of a guided trek in the Everest region.  We were supposed to stay 4 nights (2 before the trek, 2 after) but we got stuck in Lukla thanks to poor weather.  I had been to Kathmandu 25 years ago and stayed at what was then considered one of the best hotels (the Malla) - but was surprised at the poor water and electricity outages there back then.  I was very glad to find that the Soultee was definitely up to par - good water (although we were told to only drink bottled) and great electricity/internet.  The hotel provided extensive glass-bottled water and was doing an excellent job recycling glass and not adding to the extensive plastic problem.  The rooms were very nice and very quiet, all looking out onto this huge private courtyard/gardens that were very well maintained (the hotel sits on 12 high-security acres and there are many other buildings - like a full spa and casino).  The beds were very comfortable and I enjoyed great nights of sleep.  The breakfast was extremely good - I especially liked the many different lassi drinks and yogurt, the fruit drinks, the bakery items, and the Indian fare (e.g. pakoras, ginger chutney, and masala/chai tea).

Visiting Devi Falls is always a must on any trip I make to Pokhara. Probably the best time to visit is in summer during monsoon season when a rainbow is always visible over the falls when the water is high. Still, anytime of year is worth a visit as it is a peaceful, relaxing place.

Set on the lakeside you couldn't want for better views in Pokhara.  Rooms are spacious and comfortable but the food is very disappointing - much worse than lower cost hotels elsewhere in Nepal. No local dishes and badly cooked western food was all that was on offer. Other negatives are expensive wifi, the A/C didn't work and the staff are mostly quite surly.  Accommodation is mostly in round lodges in very nice gardens but most rooms don't have lake and mountain views - you have to go into the garden for that.  You approach the hotel via a rope ferry and it's a short walk into the bars and shopping experience that is Pokhara lakeside.

We were amazed as we looked at the views of Devi's Falls.  It was completely different and spectacular compared to the other falls which we had seen.  We stood in amazement as we marveled at God's beautiful creation.  Each viewing  points gave us the opportunity to see the falls from a different angle.
The Boudhanath Stupa is breathtaking! Its serene ambiance and intricate design are mesmerizing. A must-visit spiritual sanctuary in Nepal.
Definitely a cultural thing to do while in Kathmandu, a touristy place but at 8:00am there are prayers going around the stupa praying transmitting peace and tranquility.

At the end of the underground water fall tunnel like structure one may reach a cave named Gupteswar cave. Visitors may have to buy a ticket for visiting this place by paying very less money. Very adventurous cave tunnel it is. At the end part of the cave one can see the ancient limestone structures in the cave.

We arrived to the Fish Tale thinking that the service and the rooms will be amazing. In reality the service was mediocre and the room was damped and not clean. If you want to stay in the Fish Tale it's only beacuse of the location; for the rest it's not worth it at all. We wanted to stay two nights and suddenly they said the hotel was fully booked; the next day, when we had to leave they said that they had rooms available and we didn't need to go, if the service or the rooms were what we expected we might stayed but after looking around in Pokhara for hotels we saw that the Fish Tale its not only overpriced but not worth it. In fact with the money you spent in one night in the Fish Tale you can stay 15 nights in the Sacred Valley Inn in Pokhara.
Nice city garden to visit after shopping in Thamel. Beautiful flowers and buildings, also many cute squirrels. They have restaurant too

It is always a joy to find that an attraction you visited years ago, still retains its charm. This is certainly the case with the Garden of Dreams which provides such a contrast to all the business outside its walls.  The road outside might be clogged with traffic, but once in the gate, and ticket bought, all is calm.  The garden is beautifully maintained, often by gardeners on the hands and knees paying huge attention to detail.  Walking round the visitor is presented with 'mini views' through arches, or under arbours, and there are plenty of seats for resting in the shade, or chatting with friends.  It is an entirely delighting place and well worth visiting.

It was really good hotel. When I first entered Nepal, the roads and all were soo damn choked, traffic at its best, you gotta be a god to drive there XD. And then when the taxi entered the hotel, it was like a heaven on earth. Its totally different from the outside world. All my parents and all wanted to roam kathmandu, but the hotel attracted me soo much, that I just wanted to stay and then go downstairs and checkout the restaurants and have fun there itself. Its a super cool hotel. I absolutely loved every part of this. Just a little sad that the pool was under some work when we went, so I couldn't really enjoy that (P.S. i visited soaltee last year, so it should be all good now). , but apart from that, everything was TOP-NOTCH.
Just a little story. I have a friend here in Adelaide, Australia, he is from Nepal, he is a front office manager in a hotel, and he has actually also worked in Soaltee, so he advised me to book it, and it was really worth it. LOVED THE EXPERIENCE. When I went there, the on site manager was a guy named Krishna, he was super helpful. I however, dont really know if he still works there. But he was a gem of a man. :)

This garden is just a few minutes walk from the main tourist centre of Kathmandu and provides an oasis of calm amongst well tended gardens and pavillons. The contrast with the bustling streets all around is remarkable-great place to chill, read a book or just relax

The first time I checked in, they put me in the main tower, the access is closest to the main lobby. The room was old as was the shabby furniture. I would rate this a 3 star room experience in the US. The other main issue was the noise from the weddings that were going on outdoors almost every night. Apparently, it was the wedding season before the wet season. One night, the loud (I mean club level loud) thumping noise was unbearable, which lasted until 2-3 AM. Ear plugs did not help. I complained the next morning but the front desk said that they knew nothing about this. I found this hard to believe. A colleague who was staying a couple of doors down could not sleep either. They changed my room to the new tower. This was a much newer facility. I was told that this was where Qatar crew was housed. The rooms were new with new furniture and updated decor.
The best part of the property was the outdoor bar/restaurant area. The service was excellent as was the ambience and the live music every night. Of course, you had the weddings going on next to it in the evening, but I rather enjoyed watching the extravagant affairs. The restaurant and the free breakfast was also excellent. Those two things raised my rating from a 3 to a 4.
Another negative is the neighborhood. There is nothing to do in the immediate surrounding. You had to take a taxi or inDrive (kind of like Uber) or walk quite a ways.
I would consider staying here only if I can get a room in the new tower.
Provides an interesting view of the cave into which Devi's Fall disappears. The "Cow Shed" ?? is not worth bothering with!
Room is very clean n most importantly smells good. The breakfast was awesome! Staff r be RT friendly n nice. Keep up the good work! Will definitely come back again 😊

The place is rather interesting , but very noisy. Water in a waterfall rushing with such great speed into a crevice that very fascinating but we have to speak loudly , to share impressions))) Near the waterfall is a small Park and shops with souvenirs.

Group of ten stayed at this nice hotel while on two days trip to pokhara. Front house service was good. Used the restaurant where main course served before the starter. 45 minutes for the cup of coffee ☕ and all our orders served in different times taking almost hour and half while the kids went sleeping on dining table. Next day decided to have a room service but the room service attendant was very rude and told  me to order all at once and I don't understand what is the meaning of room service. Hotel located in the good surrounding nice and clean and breakfast was very good but again services definitely need reshuffle.

Amazing place with an incredible atmosphere! The food was absolutely delicious, and the service was wonderful. The employees were really, really nice (Yukab and Ajay) and went above and beyond to make the experience unforgettable. Highly recommend!

I am a flight attendant staying in this hotel regularly and I must say, the hospitality and service are just wonderful! The staff are very attentive and polite! Especially Kesano who was delivering room service for me, went back and forward several times to accomodate me as good as possible. His service and professionalism are outstanding! Thank you so much! :)

One  thing  I have  noticed  in  Pokhara  was  that  the  rivers  are  mostly  underground  or  scarcely  made  their  appearance  or  look like  a  narrow  stream deep  down  . Devis  fall  is a  transition  phase  between  lake  to  river  , a  deep  and  narrow   gorge  ,  water  splurging  from  all  sides  , ultimately   cutting  the  stones  , creating  mist  in  nearby  areas  , a  beautiful  spot  for  nature  lovers  but  not  properly  maintained .The  calm  n  quite  waters  of  fewa lake turns  into turbulent , noisy , forceful giant  at Devis  fall . Pokhara  is  more  or  less  like  our  Panchamarhi  (Madyapradesh –India) hill  station with   Jatasankar(fall) , Mahadev  gupha(cave) ,  Apsara vihar ,  Dhupgarah  (sun  rise  and  sunset  point)  .

Ideal location, good restaurant, cultural programs and decent swimming pool. Mr. Ram Bhandari at FO is extremely helpful and requires a special note of appreciation. However, we had bad experience with service staff who seem to lethargic and careless. We raised the issue to Hotel management. Rooms are well maintained with great views of the mountains. Bad service stuck out like sore thumb.
Amazingly beautiful location for dinner....  great food.  Great ambience...  nighttime lighting is spectacular. 👍👍👍👍👍

Very disappointed with this $110/nt hotel passing itself off as a quality property. We booked a suite, which was large but all widows were at knee level! So no view to speak of.  The shower was oddly angled so the floor got soaked easily and when I mentioned this to the desk, they said that the maintenance guys said I was wrong! Basically a corporate run front desk with reception folks who don't understand service.  Not a bad place per se, but more if a $75 a night spot.
Very peaceful stupa in the central of city! When you enter from the gate, you will feel you are in another world. Thank you Breakfree Adventures for organizing such a great tour for us!

I stayed here in May 2013 for 3 days 2 nights. The hotel is located 2 mins walk from the main road. Nice rooms but no elevators. Ask for a room with mountain view. The cultural program is good if you like traditional stuff. The staff is very helpful. The air conditioner does not work 24 hrs,

Nice area to stay. 
Walking distance to Thamel & Motorcycle shops. There are many other attractions nearby.
Comfortable and clean. 
Staff are very helpful. 
Beautiful garden & swimming pool to relax.  
Restaurant has a good selection of food.

I have been into the Guha, its about 200-300 ft deep into the ground.  Breathtaking scene of waterfall inside the same.  During Dec 2017 there were some construction going on and it was little slippery to walk

This was one of the deepest falls and the gushing sound of the water was amazing.
The place is surrounded with lush green trees and plants. Well maintained by the government.

Everything at this hotel normally falls in place except for the room service. It is shoddy, imagine placing the order and someone ask you everytime if they food u ordered needs to prepared immediately or after a while. Tell them immediately and prompt comes the reply, we are very busy . The food at room service is slow and gets cold by the time it's delivered. The rooms are nice, clean and modern. Staff is generally helpful and accommodating, though the room service (F&B) needs to buckle up. Lovely property. Great big lawn, nice pool and tennis ground. The casino is nice as well!

Gupetswor cave is the longest cave in asia  very cool place inside the cave.You will find the big shiva linga and if you will more deep inside the cave you will see the big splashing end of the devis fall....just go and explore the cave...no need to worry about any thing you willnot have any breathing problem...

We started early in the day, weather was good had a comfortable hike through a suspension bridge and rice farms!

nearly 4kms from phewa lake.

very near is mukteshwar temple you can visit that too..and then take a cab to International mountaineering museum which is a must visit place too!

Give preference to visit this cave instead of the dissappointing Devi's Waterfall outside park, opposite the cave. The cave´s first part is nothing special, but continue walking to second part where you can see the Devi's Waterfall falling inside the cave. Really nice.

A large Buddhist stupa surrounded by both small and giant prayer wheels. You can't actually go inside the stupa but people walk around it in a clockwise motion, some of them reciting prayers or prostrating. I went in the evening so many people were lighting butter lamps. They were also burning holy herb. Opposite the stupa is a temple that seems to be dedicated to Padmasambava, the guru that brought Buddhism to Tibet. I received a blessing from the head monk. It does feel a little pressurising though that the other monks were talking to me about my home country and making me write down my name and give a donation all whilst the head monk was praying over me. (You can choose your amount but most people in the list wrote down 2000NPR so I went with that.)

Around the temple grounds are shops that you can explore. It gives you a feeling like you're immersed in little Tibet. There you may see monks going about their rounds, having meals and even meeting with friends from lay-society.

I was on birthday dinner date with my friend , we ordered grilled fish and chicken pizza , me and my friend really liked the crispy crust of the  pizza. Service was on par with what we expected at the first place, enjoyed the quite atmosphere. Mr.Surendra and Ms.Ganga really served with utmost care and we really appreciate that.

It was definitely worth the 30 Rs per person to enter.  Maybe because of the monsoon we had a lot more water flowing into the fall. So we got a decent view. But that’s it. There really isn’t much else to do or see there.

Gupteswar caves are 250 ft below the ground level and you must experience the same. Please do visit when you are at Pokhra. 
Advise aged and people with knee problems not to dare. 
At the end of the cave you will witness Devi falls  which is another attraction of pokhra.
Mystery solved  as where water of Devi's fall disappears; it's all in the cave & is made up of rocks only rocks.

Devi's Falls, although morbidly and ironically named, offers little more then an anecdotal side trip from Pokhara. The walk there isn't particularly interesting either and once you make it to Devi's falls it's so ripped off you can't even see down the falls anyway. Moderately entertaining, worth visiting for a little exercise on the walk there if you have nothing else to do.

i expected an easy experience with getting a room and checkin in......check in took a long while.....i had lunch first - mind you...no shower for many days in clohtes that smelled....-

Fantastic place and restaurants with views are just awesome. There is a lot to see and discover around and there are bunch of monasteries nearby.
It was a very nice experience. The property is also very beautiful and it is worth staying. The food and the hotel workers are also very nice.
A green garden in Kathmandu. Rs 1000 entrance fee for foreigners. There's a overpriced cafe. Young couples go here to meet each other.

I have stayed at the Shanker 4 times, when I was on trekking in Nepal. I will check out tomorrow - for the last time. Net time it won't be the Shanker. Since last, a lot of things have changed. I have a very dark room, with a small window. It is almost claustrofobic.I know tha they are redecorating the hotel, but I tried three times to get a new room, but unsuccessfull. They offerd me a biggerroom but still no light - so I gave up. The staff is either too old or to young (incompetent) and speak poorly english. The cleaning is fine and the food is medium (evening buffet and breakfast), The morning bacon is not fried at all and seem undelicate and uneatabel. They try but they do not succeed...sorry.
Nice walk up the stupa with monkeys. People selling singing bowls and pushing a little harder perhaps of hoping to earn some tourist income.
It was a second visit,  and is a nice hangout with friends and family. One place along with many hangout places in Pokhara which takes just few hours.
mandatory to visit because is a UNECO heritage stuff, thats all, lot of shops and roof bars entry 200 rupees..
This was a nice place to escape the sound of the city, however its likely much pretty in the spring.

There is a ticket fee to enter the garden but there is no time restrictions. The garden is a nice place to take a book and read or stroll through, just a nice break from the crazy city life. We spent about 30 minutes here and checked out the different flowers and plants. There isn't much to see otherwise, there is a cafe in the garden but it is quite toursity based on the prices!

Across the street from the Devi's Fall entrance is the entrance to the Gupta Cave. Craftsmen are building and restoring a beautiful circular staircase to the entrance of the cave. It will be beautiful when completed. Full disclosure: I did not enjoy the cave experience. There are stairs through most of the cave, railing is in place, however, lacking a high safety standard, especially in the lower level. I was more concerned with the minimal lighting, and in places where there were no stairs....there are impressions in the stone that are very slippery. Footing is unstable. While the cave promotes religious significance, I would suggest this stretches the imagination and would call it tacky.  For the lower half of the cave, you cannot see - rather - hear the water (this may be different during monsoon....so it's really a bottomless gulch.  I was the only person in the lower half of the cave, with unsafe footing, poor railing and diminished lighting. This was the most vulnerable I felt during my entire time in Nepal.

I have visited caves in previous travels....so this was highly disappointing.  If you are at Devi's Falls, observe the reconstruction of the staircase, make a donation to the ongoing preservation....save yourself the time of going into the cave.

We ate here for dinner. My third time here. Nice atmosphere and Bollywood type music. Excellent food - very tasty. Licensed, so beer and liquor available. Service was exemplary with lovely combination of starters and a main. Ask the Maitre De’ to recommend your meal.

we spent two nights here at the end of our trek. It was a 50th birthday treat for my wife. We were looking forward to our stay there but we were very dissapointed from the minute we arrived. The reception staff were rude and unwelcoming. The porters refused to leave our room until they had a tip. The hotel is very expensive but provides no refreshment making facilities in the rooms and charges extra for everything including wifi and even the use of an umbrella. We would never stay there again and would advise anyone against it.

I feel very good. Excellent environment in hotel campus. Ms. Sakshi deals very good on reception. Morning breakfast is also very good always. MY staff feels very fine. Staff of the hotel is well disciplined.

What warm welcome by the Team with greetings with welcome cloth. Great food and location, to reach hotel you need to get into Boat. I am short of words to express for their hospitality. Rooms are very good. In fact this location used by various country heads including India, Prince Charles and UN chief

Bhintuna,sandhika and Anjali shreeya 
It was very pleasant experience.
Starting from staff,rooms, food everything top notch.
