The river is very slim and norrow, sunken deep into the earth , we can see the water falls and flows into very deep and dark hole but after that we cannot see the water anymore because the water flow deep under the earth. The river wall is very tall look like canyon.

We visited this during our Nepal trip in December 2010.This is a cave with a naturally formed Shiva lingam. One has to go down a spiral staircase to go inside the cave which is dimly lighted with droplets of water dripping all over the place.Pics cannot be taken inside the cave and a small entrance fee is required.

This is supposed to be a place where we are supposed to see beautiful waterfalls, but the view is not good. but if you are interested in local shopping, definitely you will find something interesting.

The location of Shanker is superb, within 10 mins walking distance of Thamel and the Durbar Marg shopping street. 

For a hotel with such a big name, my expectations were maybe a bit too high...the matrasses are a bit too hard to have a comfortable night of sleep, the staff operates quite bureaucratic (eg. bring your laundry to the front desk and they send you back to your room as it should be picked up there according to procedures). If you are tall (1.93m) you will not be able to stand straight up in the bath tub while taking a shower at breast height. 

Positive remarks are the very friendly staff and the wide choice at the breakfast buffet. Overall the stay was ok, but for this price level a bit beyond expectations.

This was a quirky,somewhat nicer Kathmandu hotel outside of the hustle and bustle of Thamel.  However, we lingered at the pool after sight seeing and ordered off the menu there. Some also ordered some room service during our three night stay. At breakfast each morning, we would receive word of who had become sick overnight. Six of our group of eight fell ill. We linked it to this hotel.  We won't stay there again, sadly.

A really beautiful garden. I went in the evening, and we took our books. It’s a stunning spot for photos and just very relaxed. A real sanctuary in the middle of Kathmandu. The cafe and restaurant looked really good, a little over our budget so we didn’t eat but for people travelling with a bigger budget it would be really lovely to eat here.

Quaint architectural entrance with spiral steps featuring murals of shiva-parvati on the walls that lead down to the mouth of the cave. Inside the cave the first feature you will note is the underground temple dedicated to Lord Shiva (correct me if I am wrong). Signs indicating 'No Photography' apply only to the temple, not the rest of the cave.

Steep and slippery steps through the cave follow down through small tunnels (you may need to bend over if you are tall, and those with weak knees beware). The tunnels are often wet from water dripping from ceilings and on the floor (so don't wear your best clothes and shoes). At the time of our visit construction works were ongoing so expect a lot of scaffolding and pipes in your way. At the end of the cave you can see the Davis waterfall flowing into the underground river.

After the visit you could walk across the road opposite the entrance to the cave and enter the park above ground (pay separately) that has a limited view of the Davis waterfall from the surface.

Worthwhile to experience a taste of Nepal underground.

Boudhanath Stupa has never failed to consistently inspire wonder in me. The magnificent stupa stands tall and transcends time, enveloping the air with tranquillity. This sacred site is not just a visual delight but also an enduring spiritual legacy of Buddhism. However, it would have been wonderful if the sacredness of the place is preserved without the intrusion of various shops. This might also make the place less crowded.

One of many waterfall options to visit in and  around Pokhara .
Tourists pay more than locals but it doesn’t cost  very much for the entry. There’s markets and refreshment stands nearby .
The actual site is named for a European woman who some time ago whilst bathing with her husband was accidentally swept away in the currents and later when her body was found they named the falls after her.  
There is a naturally beautiful rock formation and waterfall worth seeing spoiled a bit by the construction of the tourist site on top of it but it does  make for safe viewing.

Hotel is very nice. All the amenities are way beyond the expectations. Also customer service is out of the world. Specially Garden Terrence restaurant staff was excellent particularly shout out to SAKAR his service was beyond my expectations. I will personally prefer this Hotel for my all Kathmandu tips.
Huge stupa rebuilt after the earthquake. Area was quite clean and very colourful. We enjoyed walking around people watching and browsing through some of the shops. One hour was long enough for us.

This is an underground cave diagonally opposite to Devi's waterfall across the road through a market place.You have to go down the stairs into the cave underground.After going down into the cave to certain depth is the Shiva temple.You can go further down through narrow stair case to a place from where there is a long slit opening through which the water from Devi's waterfall come.Its damp and wet inside and one needs to be careful.It needs maintenance .

It is a very nice hotel especially the breakfast. A lot of choices of food. The service staff Sabita Thapa and Sakar Sugam Basnet are very very worm and enthusiasticly introduce local customs and provide various support. You will feel at home in this hotel.

I don't know much about Buddhism, but I can see why followers consider this holy. It is well-maintained and peaceful, even though there are tons of people around you.

I don't know where else you would see something like this in the middle of a city. Definitely worth a visit.

We were 3 adults, and we got the third bed under the tv desk, we told them that we couldn't open our luggages, so they changed it and put it next to the big bed for two... the result was an uncomfortable three bed that occupied all the space in the room. I think that solutuon would be good for a family with kids, not with a 21 y/o daughter. Anyway, the breakfast is absolutely amazing and reading by the pool is fantastic, you also have relaxing music coming from the bar! Unfortunately we didn't have enough time to try the spa

I reserved a 'club' room since the ad invited me to enjoy browsing the Internet in the exclusive club lounge.  In fact, I had to pay extra, and the connection was painfully slow, even slower than at most other hotels in town.  I had to argue with the front desk in order to ensure my breakfast was included. 

On the positive side, it is one of the few hotels in town with an exercise room (not a priority for trekkers, but perhaps a requirement for some business travellers).  I also had a QUIET, comfortable room. 

Most of the guests seemed stressed by this hotel - but maybe I'm just projecting.  The service is pretentious and overdone. It's a burden just to track down your luggage to get the porter to carry it to your room.  Then, just try to get someone to collect your collect your luggage when you check out!  

This is all very strange to me, since I know Nepal very well and its people are so charming!  So, don't judge this wonderful country based on your experience at the Soaltee.

A place doesn't become good only with beauty, rather people managing it.
Garden of dreams is a beautiful place with awful staff.
My young son's reading glasses were stolen, and instead of helping, staff were more interested in making us go away, since it brings their inefficient ways out.
Disgusting is, once you see couples are given mats to indulge in uncivilized activities on public display post sunset.
I made a mistake by going there with family.

Nice clean hotel but lacks charm of other Nepalese hotels. I found that the staff were more interested in tips than anything else.
Very good breakfast and reasonable western style bar if you want a quiet escape.

I read another review (albeit after already having been to the cave unfortunately), which said that if you have ever visited another cave before then don’t bother visiting this one. I’m inclined to agree. 

The one cool thing about this cave is that it is in the middle of town. When our driver pulled up I thought he just wanted some snacks from the local shops. The staircase leading down to it is also quite ornate and may be worth a look which you can do without paying the entrance fees.

The cave itself was small, packed, hot (even in winter so I hate to think what it is like in summer) and smells like manure.

Located just opposite Devi's Falls so I guess anyone visiting one will inevitably visit the other. There is a small shrine in the first level of the cavern. You can pay the full entrance fee and venture further down the cave, walking downwards deeper underground. There is lighting but it's not very bright and is slippery so tread carefully. Some parts are also very narrow so those who are claustrophobic should stay well away. The finale of the visit is the sight of a waterfall (presumably the water from Devi's Fall).
The entry fee far outweighs the length of time spend at the stupur. It is ok in itself, and worth a visit, but don't expect to get much value. There are lots of cafes close by.

It is well maintained garden also architecture is also good to see but very high charges to see which is not value for money 
As it finishes before it start 
All could be seen from entry point

I have been this place after my launch but spend more then 6 hours. This garden located heart of Thamel, once I entered here, I motions calmed into peace of mind. Beautifully decorates with full of history. It’s worth to visit this place, this is highlighted sport of traveller.

Stay was a total disappointment. We booked this hotel thinking it's one of those luxury hotels with a contemporary touch. 

Our room was dirty with sticky floors, and really low ceiling that gave a suffocating feeling. Bathroom was cramped with no separate shower space, and had stains in the bathtub. Upon complaining, we were shown another room which was equally filthy. We could not muster the courage to take shower throughout our stay. The room had an extremely small window with no real view. 

The breakfast buffet was just as disappointing. Food and fruits were definitely not fresh. We decided to instead have breakfast in a nearby cafe.
Not quite as peaceful as I had expected.  A nice place to visit, menu in the cafe not cheap - but nice food.

We travelled as a large family with 8 rooms booked.  Check-in was a complete mess. Smoking rooms for us with kids etc. 
Took a half hour to get a room. 
We, with our 4 year old had requested an extra bed. 
No surprise that they were surprised that this was on their system already. 
We were told the best was for us to proceed with our dinner plans and the bed would be ready. 
How easy they made it sound.
Come back at 10 pm to our room and needless to say the extra bed wasn't there. 
Called the reception and the most inept answers are given. 
Finally have to go down myself and they end up saying I have to pay extra.
I say, please send the bed, my wife and kid are waiting and we need to discuss the charge as all was pre organised.
Nope. Agree to the charge now!
After losing tempers they claim I haven't given ID for 3 people in the room. I'm like you took 3 passports! And they dig and dive and finally say we sent the extra bed to the wrong room. 
Tbh they are extremely calm and composed. You could say unconcerned, but that would be a tad of an understatement.
Absolutely zero service minded. Money minded only.
The staff think they are doing us a favour by having us there
And the whole place is falling to bits with major renovation needed.

Avoid at all costs!

I read so much about the Garden of Dreams that I made it my first stop at Kathmandu.  What I saw was quite ordinary - nothing spectacular.  And the male staff around the counter was not helpful.  I asked how I could get to Tridevi temple by showing him a photo (actually it was just across the road but I had my bearings wrong) and he just shrugged his shoulders

Was upgraded a complimentary deluxe room on the 2nd level of the old wing. Room size okay, toilet is a bit small especially the narrow bathtub. Decor is a bit old but in good working condition. Annoyed by Intermittent noise caused by water pressure from the concealed water pipes from nearby rooms. Pest control strongly needed, rats or cockroaches been creeping above the ceiling at night. Rooms have very thin walls and housekeeping starts early in the morning with the sound of vacuum cleaner that may deprive you of extending your sleep further. For breakfast, Coffee & Tea don't live up to the IHG name. Hyatt Regency Kathmandu has better tasting coffee & tea.
Nothing here to see that is memorable. This is a very small waterfall with slow running water that you had to pay a small admittance fee. Maybe “Devi” means “crap” in Nepalese!!
The Stupa is still being reconstructed post earthquake. Foreigners are charged a fee to see the Stupa even if you're just shopping in the area. Many homeless people and people begging here.

We were quiet disappointed after reading all the excellent reviews. The location is great and the little boat trip to the hotel is cute but our room was really disappointing. shabby, clammy and waiting for renovation. the beds looked like already used and the bathroom - you tried to shorten the time inside.

It would be ok if it's much cheaper but the prices are on the top end and you get much better value in other hotels in pokhara.
One good thing: the bar is great.

Thank you for complimentary nimbu pani. We always enjoy to stay here special thenk to front and Guest relations team....,......................

Soalter hotel should open in India.
Enjoy a lot hotel ..........

See you soon.😆
Thank you.
A place to visit. The spectaculair view where the water is going in to a dark hole. If the name would be devil's fall you would beleave it also.

Yes: the biggest stupa in nepal, surrounded by shops. I was really expecting something better. They are doing some "renovations" so you cannot climb the stupa, you just walk around it and do some shopping. The shops around the stupa and the restaurants take away what could be mistical and religious about the place. Definitely not worth the visit. There are way better places to go to in Kathmandu.

Spent about 20 min here--- mainly about the story of the lady who fell to her death here about 100 years ago.    But the rock formations and water erosion is also beautiful!     Make sure you then walk across the street to see the Gupteshwa Mahadev cave--- to see the falls from underneath---very special!

It is winter so I guess it had a huge impact on out visit, but we paid entrance and it was so small and nothing special to see. Have visited so many nicer gardens before. It was ok to waist half an hour tho.

For its price, hotel Shanker was definitely a disappointment. For example, the airport pick-up (for which they charge 20 USD - a local taxi will run you no more than 6 USD and would be more luxurious), was literally a 25-year old Toyota Corolla with no seatbelt, and a driver who had one hand on the wheel as he was constantly on the phone. When I expressed my surprise about this at reception, I was basically told that this was just the way it was and if I didn't like it I was free to book something else. Hardly what I expect from a hotel in this price range. 
Experience with the rest of the staff was also very mixed. Half of them were actually very polite, whereas the other half were downright grumpy and seemed to just be bothered by our presence. 
The actual hotel (as in, the building itself) is definitely beautiful though, and the breakfast was good. The service however, was downright poor, and made the whole thing feel like they are just riding the fact that they've got a nice building.
There are many other accomodations where your money will get you a better experience.

Oldy worldy hotel, nice grounds and very smart security staff. walking distance to town so avoided the noise and bustle. Beware the flying foxes poo'ing on the pavement. no drying facilities for wet clothes during rain. Good breakfast bar, evening meals average and pool / bar service was a bit slow but hey we were on holiday. Rooms a bit tired and bathrooms cramped, but this wasnt purporting to be a 5* hotel. Cheap and cheerful. Can only give it 3* based on other standards but would we stop there again - yes probably. Will we be going back to Kathmandu? been there done it so, no. If going up to Lukla - allow for weather delays

Very nice building and nicely renovated. But the beds / mattresses are not so good. We also had to ask 3 times for the extra bed and it took them 2 hours to come and set up the bed. Bathroom is very small and showering in the bathtub is not comfortable. The breakfast hall is very big, but the selection and quality of the food is average to poor. If you want to stay just to be in a heritage hotel then it's okay, but for the other things not worth it.
Big stupa of lord Buddha. Place is very quiet. Om mane peme. I captured few pictures in there. I visited many monks.

A huge temple complex with Tibetan influence. Possibly the largest stupa (hemispherical mound built as burial mound or receptacle for religious objects/relics). The piercing blue eyes on each of the 4 faces seem to follow you wherever you go in the site! Do visit the onsite monastery - permissible even when monks are praying/meditating. The statues and artwork inside are simply breathtaking - sadly no photographs allowed but understandable. Visited with an excellent, very knowledgeable local guide - the facts and information were hard to take in, in one session but utterly fascinating.
This place is very nice place for sightseeing. Its a wonderful view of water fall falling no where...you cant see where it falling but its falling.

Nice place to visit when in Pokara. The fall was not very strong but all the same liked it.The place around the fall is nice neat and clean with shops all around. Overall it is a nice place to spend a few hours there and do some small shopping as well.

We stayed at the Soaltee Kathmandu – impeccably managed by Mr Avinash Deshmukh - from the end of January until early February 2025 to watch the women’s cricket at Kirtipur stadium. Being frequent travellers I can say that this is one of the best experiences of our lifetime and highly recommended. Staff is super friendly and alert. Obviously eating out in the city is cheaper, but we highly recommend the Chinese restaurant Bao Xuan (opposite the reception desk) which we visited twice, as well as the delights of the northern Indian cuisine at Kakori – only a short walk towards the swimming pool. The gym, massage salon, jacuzzi etcetera are also well-equipped and impeccably maintained. Breakfast buffet is a feast. Should there be more cricket events in the future, there is no doubt that we will return to this amazing oasis of peace and quiet.
Easy to go in and out because of the stairs - otherwise few people could see it. Well illuminated inside. Beautiful speleothems (stalactites and etc) and well maintained.

Not much of a fall but nice views of the water falling not from a big height. It was hot weather but even then there was a big crowd. Heard a tale behind the name 'Devi's Fall'. Says that a Japanese young lady was visiting the falls and she was so enchanted, she kept backing up & unfortunately fell into the water and died. Yes it is enchanting!

This one is a must see in Pokhara, it shouldn't take more than 30 mins overall. Entry ticket is around 100 Rs Nepali (for SAARC) and 50 Rs Nepali for locals. At the beginning of the cave itself, some priest charges Rs. 10 for holy milk (its optional) for the deity, but one way to make money. Another attraction is the natural formation of Lord Shiva Lingam, its mainly for Hindu's. Finally we could see the water falls at the end of the cave. I saw more water in this cave than in "Devi's falls". If you wish to see the waterfall during non monsoon time, better visit this place (cave) than Devi's Falls. 

Its quite dark at some places, so its little difficult when climbing the steps. So please carry some torch light or use flash lights from your mobile.

Those who are interested in Cave Photography, this place should be of some interest.

Like all hotels in Nepal - you will be sold the fact that Prince Charles of the UK once stayed here amongst many other celebrities. But that was over 25years ago - an it appears no money has been spent on this hotel since. The flowers surrounding the garden in this place and the lake view are pretty, and the ferry man takes you over to the small island upon which the hotel sits. You can hire a rowing boat (extra charge and row your beloved out across the lake to see the mountains) But the illusion of comfort ends there! - the hotel rooms themselves - are very damp (and in my opinion as an asthmatic were dangerous to my health as they contain spores of fungi and bacteria.) The blankets on the beds are damp and the rooms themselves were constructed of painted hardboard - and the rooms very tiny. The shower being a tiny room with black mould in the crevices. We were initially not provided with a kettle or tea making facilities and told that this would be an extra $50US per day - we were paying around $130!USDollars. In Nepal - the hoteliers have no idea of Western Hotel standards and have every intention of charging over the odds for poor facilities and bad service and generally ripping off tourists. The Restaurant food was buffet style and represented very poor value for money being barely edible. The swimming pool was smaller than my duckpond, dirty with missing tiles and generally useless. The hotel ads show you viewing the mountains from this pool - which was impossible when we were there in April 2013. The employees at the hotel seem to be having a better time than the guests, I smelt dope being smoked by one of the gardeners!
So that my health didn't deteriorate we checked out after two days and continued our stay at the Pokhara Grand Hotel - which gave us a huge suite with a view of the Annapurna Mountain range from our windows - they also offered more reasonable trips, microlight flights and paragliding all at cheaper rates than those offered at Fish Tail.  All hotels in Nepal are effected by poor hot water supply and poor electricity supply - so you can expect to be stuck in lifts and eating of using the bathroom in the dark at random times during the day. Sadly I have nothing good to say about Fish Tail - it needs bulldozing and rebuilding again! Its surviving on past memories of glory when it was probably the only hotel in Pokhara!
specially while you are in kathmandu, you must visit this place. its very quite sarounding.listed world heritage site ..... its a symbol of peace.
FYI, gupha means "Cave" in Nepali. Being there, do not forget to take a picture inside this cave.Inner view and geography of Davis fall is worth-capturing. Enjoy your time.. :)

I went there expecting a mediocre waterfall. As it is set directly in the City and is well known as one of Pokhara‘s main attractions, I thought it will be worth a visit but honestly if you’ve ever seen a waterfall before just don’t bother going. The „waterfall“ is surrounded by a fence and the angle of the view platforms surrounding it won’t let you see the fall. You can hear that there is indeed a waterfall but I didn’t even get to see it. Locals seemed to enjoy the park and took pics in front of the fence but if you’ve only ever come close to another fall I wouldn’t recommend even spending the 30 cents they take as entry.

Good;

Hotel premises are about 200m from the main road so no traffic noise
Comfortable room
Decent bed
Hot shower with power (and tub)
Led Tv with international Channels 
Good food (we ordered room service several times)
Nice garden with dito pool
Very friendly and service oriented staff

Bad;

WiFi is either not working or superslow, unacceptable for such a business hotel!!

Only a quite limited amount of hot water

Remarks: they are renovating the lobby but we weren't bothered by this

Hotel looks a bit run down, needs an overhaul/make-over.

A quaint  garden at the junction of two busy streets, with lots of quiet and greenery and a bit of history worth reliving.
There are a few friendly squirrels around and it is entertaining to watch them.
Do visit and spend some time away from the hustle. There are benches in the shade where you can sit and read a book, or simply meditate.
Every visit to Pokhara , should not miss the nature bound and the cave is always awesome with new maintenance on .

This is actually a review for the restaurant downstairs (the one with the buffet breakfast). The breakfast was AMAZING!! (and it really deserves the capital letters). A lot of options, and the staff was so helpful and genuine, whenever the plate got empty, they cleaned it immediately, and whenever you wanted something, they provided for you. It was .... yeah, it was AMAZING! So good, that I wanted to check the dinner service. I asked for a ginger tea with honey and lemon, and I think it was juat a made up drink of mine, because the staff looked confused (I guess was not in the menu,  but in my demanding head). I was surprised when the lady reconfirmed with me, and she got me a ginger tea with honey. I really want to convey my regards to Shriya, who made the impossible be possible for me. Oh, the food was good as well :))
Was interesting, but not very spectacular due to being just before the rainy season, so not too much water in the falls.Could imagine it gushing in the monsoon period.

if you arrive Kathmandu late at night, this is a good choice. otherwise, there are other better ones in town which you may consider.

but I think it's a good place to stay overall...the bed is clean, the breakfast is decent. 
Though the toilet in my friends' room didn't work.

Not a big place, just a small garden with some water features to perhaps while-away an hour at early-evening. 
It's pretty, not substantial, $2 entry-fee. Easy walk from Thamel.

This is a lovely spot of tranquillity amongst the hustle and bustle of  Kathmandu. It was within walking distance of my hotel and I spent a while there looking around but also sitting, with my book, reading!

On booking the room online, the photos appeared to paint a wonderful picture of a beautiful, large sized room.  However on arrival we were given a shoebox of a room.  Very disappointed for the amount we paid!  We would suggest to walk 5 mins down the road to Thamel where you can find many varieties of accommodation options. We stayed in a hotel which cost $20 USD per night which was more spacious, staff were more friendly and much more convenient to walk to the heart of Thamel. 

While we were given an amazing complimentary breakfast as part of the package, that really did not make up for the cost. 

The grounds are meticulously maintained and from the outside it is a beautiful palace.

I returned from Nepal to HK last Saturday. My friends and I had fantastic time in Nepal, the local people are beauitful look and kind. Overall we like Nepal! 
I stayed in many hotels in my nine days journey,  I would like to share with you of 2 hotels. 
1. Fistail Lodge Hotel in Pokhara
The scenery and environment is so beautiful, the design and location of rooms are well done, perparhs the hotel has estiblished for sometime ago, the bath room is pretty run down, the most dissappointing matter is the staffs have no or can't represented such a well known hotel. The front desk staffs are certianly rude and inpolited, they were not helpful and spoke bountly to the guestes, the general staffs can be helpful if there is tips involed. In such a well known hotel, suprisingly there is no fee wi-fi provided and charge for umbrella, shocking!
2. Temple Tree Spa Hotel in Pokhara
This is a new hotel, it builded sometime 2011. The hotel is big and beautiful, the rooms are amazing, the staffs are absolutly friendly and kind, whenever you see them, they always carried with the sunshine smell on their faces. Next year when I return Nepal Pakhara, I will definitly stay in the Temple Tree Spa Hotel again for sure.
Good luck.
Amy
Devi's Fall is a small but interesting water fall. The water suddenly disappears inside the rocks and can be seen again from Gupeshwar Mahadev temple
Amid the traffic, dust & exhaust fumes of Kathmandu, this park offers some respite. The restaurant  (while pricy) serves excellent burgers.

A pointless "attraction" really. A fairly small place and there is nothing uniquely Nepalese about it.  There aren't any greatly interesting plants and its proximity to a main road hardly makes it a sea of tranquility. Don't spend NPR200 (foreigners) to get in. This would be better spent on a decent coffee.

Iit is a tourist attraction so if you have the time then please visit but be mindful it is nothing earth shattering. We visited as it was included in our tour itinerary but I wouldn’t have travelled far to see it.
it is beautiful site to see natures beauty, underground falls with good landscaping,  there are many small stalls with  Nepali bangles and beaded necklace etc

Spent an afternoon exploring this amazing structure. It was everything we thought it would be and incredible to watch thousands of pilgrims performing their ritual circular movement around the stupa.
Colours were amazing with the prayer flags complementing the white of the stupa. Well worth a few hours of your time.

Roopesh Ji  has coordinated my MBA & MCSIT Orientation to get it done smoothly. When there was lack of time & uneven resources ; he managed it pretty smoothly. Later on he even engaged our students with the exposure of hospitality field. About the Soaltee in particular.

Sadly, the teahouse/restaurant inside has closed, but the garden is still a restful little park, with some nice architectural features, and a good place to retreat from the hubbub of the surrounding streets.  There are cute little striped squirrels scurrying around the flower beds, which will give some entertainment.

I traveled alone, so I thought that the caves would be a fun idea to keep me occupied. It is a lot of stairs down, so if you are not in ok shape, then you might not enjoy it. There is a Temple in the middle that has a "natural shape of Shiva", which is protected by gates. A man will put a Tika on you, and you can go look at the Temple. You aren't allowed to take pictures of it, but I snuck a few! I was unlucky to arrive during the time that the Devi's Falls was too wild, which means I did not get to enjoy the entire trek down into the cave. But, over all, I enjoyed this experience. If you are traveling to find yourself, or get more involved in spirituality, definitely do this.
you have to go under ground a long way and at the end you shall see a falls. There are lights every where, but water seeps through the cave ceiling making you half wet. Old people a strict no no.

We stayed as part of a tour. The rooms had non functioning AC as experienced by us and other members of our party. I suppose it could be related to frequent blackouts in the city and the use of backup generators. Anyway the staff seemed not to understand when I complained about the heat. The beds were comfortable and bathroom was nice with large shower. There is a safe in room and room is quiet. Large number of english language channels on room TV. There is nice varied buffet breakfast.

This was the most disappointing place we visited on our three week trip to India, Nepal, and Bhutan.  There is simply nothing to see. It is a tiny little stream off a street in Pokhara.  Also the associated caverns, Gupteshwar, are like walking through a city sewer tunnel, dripping water, low ceiling and once again nothing to see.  If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites in a cave, there are none.  Both places are simply a waste of time.
Amazing nature... build Pokhara very beautiful with such amazing things. One of the beautiful part of the World.

Stayed for 3 days 8 to 11 March.Beautiful property where u can pass enormous time.but had bad experience of service.Breakfast was mostly continental.complaint regarding bathroom not addressed to.wanted to meet manager in this regard but declined by front desk.I think Indians should avoid this hotel.Hyatt is better property on these rates.

This is the best place to be fresh during the evening 
I always come to this place when I m in Kathmandu.
Nice stupa and good food around with stupa views 
Namaste 🙏
If you are traveling to Kathmandu, one time you will visit Buddha Nath Stupa. I would recommend Bouddhanath to go to places around Kathmandu

This is not a four star hotel.  Not even three. They block trip advisor which made it difficult for us to find restaurants and things to do. They block it because they are mad about the poor reviews. They were nice but the room was old. They gave us a free upgrade when we were going to leave. Gave my husband a nice cake when they heard it was his birthday. But the lobby bathroom was disgusting and the room to eat breakfast was dark and gloomy. Notw worth seventy doolars.

If you get a confirmation of your booking from the hotel, there should be definitively a remark:
May we attract your attention to the fact that we are renovating our hotel and the building will be under construction in the next time.
Because nothing happened like this I arrived without prior notice of the actual situation.
All the works beeing conpleted the Shanker might be a good traditional hotel in Kathmandu, with friendly and polite staff.
I visited this temple and found it eerie due to its location. It is deep inside and right at the bottom of the cave, one can see a waterfall through the gap in the wall.

Your everything was very nice and the food quality was also good and one of your staff named Vigyaan in restaurant was very nice and his behavior was also good.

One thing I didn’t liked was your room ambience. It was not like a 5 star hotel type. You can renovate it.
A normal natual fall with greenery all over.The place is protected in such a way that you can't actually look into the bottom of the fall. It s located in a nice street full of shopping places.

Compare to other two caves in Pokhara - I suggest to spend time here since it is newly rennovated with good light, nice walking trail. Wonderful view of Davis fall from inside the cave - I just loved it. This is most recommended place to go.

Boudhanath Stupa is one of the most beautiful places to visit in Kathmandu. If you haven't already, I would highly recommend you place this destination on your itinerary. There is much to explore in Boudhanath, from the temple to the local cuisine and local environment. Its enormous mandala makes it one of the biggest spherical stupas in Nepal and the world. I actually stayed here for a whole day, from morning to afternoon. Highly Recommended!!

Excellent service and food  Great hospitality by surrenders Krishna zenisha bushman and Ganga Ji 
Will definitely visit again

Wonderful staff who was always respectful and attentive.  Great private views of Lake Pehwa and the mountains.  The hand-pulled raft to get to the hotel was a treat too. Both breakfast and dinner were more than plentiful and we were even offered seconds at dinner yet we couldn't finish what was served!  Our room was comfortable and cozy.  We didn't have hot water one morning but this was fixed within 5 minutes.  All in all,a great stay and we would recommend.

This is advertised as an oasis of peace! However the construction of a block of flats right next to the garden means there is a constant level of construction noise in the daylight! It is smaller than I expected. Still very cheap and relatively relaxing considering how busy the city is!

We saw sign posts for Devi’s Falls when leaving the Peace Pagoda. The sign said the falls were 30 minutes away. We walked for 10 minutes, only to find the next sign which also said was 30 minutes away. This happened a third time and we began to lose faith. When we eventually arrived we found it to be an overcrowded, unorganised tourist hot spot. We don’t mind the tourist as we are tourist, but a bit of organisation from the staff charging you to enter would have made the experience far more pleasant, for example having only a certain number of people in the caves at anytime so that people can walk through without being pressed against a damp cave wall. More importantly the waterfall was massively unimpressive. You cannot get close enough for a decent photo, and so you have to look at it in a crowded, small viewing platform roughly 100m from the small, sorry waterfall. All in all I wouldn’t advise anyone to make the journey to the location if all you’re going for is Devi’s Falls

We got a great room, loved the service in the property. The swimming pool also is well maintained.

But they make a couple of mistakes
A) dinner buffet closes at 9 
B) the restaurant closed at 9.30
C) there is no room Sevice in the night.

So if you are hungry and get to the property late you will struggle through till breakfast next morning.

Also given that the property is across the lake any need to get some food is atleast a 15 minute river cross + walk across... Fairly a significant effort when you are hungry and sleepy. 

So you stay in a fancy place but stay hungry. To be fair to them wen we called first time they said kitchen closed and when we calls again and literally begged for food a sandwich was sent our way!

But the buffet breakfast is decent.

Best property by location on the lakeside

Walking off the street in Kathmandu and into this garden is like walking through a portal. Noise, heat and dust is followed by an oasis like garden with ponds, birds and even a cooler micro climate. You really should check it out.

A great place to bring a book and lie on the grass and even people watch if that’s your thing.

The cafe and restaurant is nice, slow service but the food is good. A little on the pricey side but find somewhere else this tranquil in KMT!?

SCAM. This is at best a public park. Why is there a charge and ticket? I do not know. Boring garden. Not even large for a walk. Good for teenagers to bring a date I guess but nothing for the visitors.

So peaceful place, I felt like time stoped while you are around Stupa. View is amazing surroundings by hills. Buddhists music gives this place special atmosphere and energetic. One of the best places in Kathmandu.

The place is very clean.
Staff are very friendly. 
There is verity of food as buffet and also ala cartie and all are good. 
The tour of the historical palace they offered me was valued for money.
Overall I enjoyed my stay at this hotel and strongly recommend it.

Hotel is quite average given it should be a more high-end hotel. However, you don't have too many choices here in Kathmandu. 

First room had power sockets busted. Second room had the light dials missing. 

Food was quite average as well. Nothing to shout about overall.

Best waterfall of Pokhara, not far from the city. Monsoon is best time to visit. I visited many times with different guest from different countries and all of them were happy to visit. It is a natural waterfall and attractive. Highly recommended to people.

Had a wonderful stay! The staff were friendly, rooms were clean, and the food was excellent.
	2.	Very comfortable and relaxing experience. Great hospitality and service.
	3.	Everything was perfect — from check-in to check-out. Will definitely come back again!
	4.	Loved the ambiance and cleanliness. The team was very helpful and polite.
	5.	Excellent facilities and well-maintained rooms. Highly recommend this hotel.

There was no waterfall visible during the dry season. We only heard the water way down in the rocks. Nice shopping around the falls. Very inexpensive to enter ($0.50)    so we did not mind that we did not see the falls.

The service here is amazing. The decor is beautiful. The stay was so comfortable.the staff is also so friendly. The environment  is so calm.It was a amazing service in hotel. The staff Ganga helped me a-lot. She guided me to my room. And made me feel so special.
Not much thing to see except the concrete structure inside a bazar.Located in the midst of a market.

Comfortable room, food menu was limited but is ok. Staff are very friendly.    

 Lovely places to visit. Changragiri hills was our favourite place to visit. 

Pashupati was also very nice, peaceful and organised. 

Dream garden was a bit of disappointment.
We went there only to say we were there but when we encountered the scene we were shocked all. You must visit it in monsoon to feel the reverse rain.
As every time I am touched by the view, the peace and easiness going around. The mixture of devotees and travellars and in this covid times still the easiness of going around and doing your own.

The flow of water was at its peak, tht maybe due to rains, but again the steps & the pathway reaching towards the fall or view point needs to be maintained by the local authorities. Its a shame tht visitors even after paying the ticket price hv to be very careful if they don't slip or fall.
Pleasant reprieve from hustle and bustle. Great restaurant (pricey) and bar looked nice. Best part is wandering through garden - there were mats available to lie in the sun.
Old architecture & statues to see. The most interesting part would be the natural AC. Wanna know what's it ? Go & experience it yourself. Worth it.
Expected a huge waterfall but only saw a mini stream of water . Can skip if you only stay for a short period in Pokhara

The Crowne Plaza Soaltee.

This is a grand hotel with many rooms. In Kathmandu  There is a huge lobby.  The staff is competent.  However, while we were waiting in the clearly marked No Smoking lounge an Arab in full regalia sat down and lit a cigar at a table clearly marked No Smoking and the staff brought him an ashtray!  

Food in the buffet dining room is always divided between vegetarian and non vegetarian or local and western.  The food is of good quality.  Wifi access is by fee only and is pretty expensive.  There is no free zone in the lobby as in many hotels.  A local beer is more than 250% than can be obtained in local restaurants.  This is gouging.  

I have no idea of room costs here as we were assigned by our tour, however, wifi policies would tell me to not return.

If you do come however, accept a room whose numbers run from 01 to 37, preceded by the floor number.  Eg, 416 is room 16 on the 4th floor.  These rooms are in the newer wing and are better equipped electrically for recharging.  Other room numbers higher than these are in an older wing, which, according to us, smelt of damp, plus one definitely needed an adapter.

Pro's- Staff very accomodating.  Location was quiet yet very walkable to Thamel District- perfect place to relax outside by the pool after a busy day in Kathmandu or after coming off a trek. Food-Breakfast offered up a lot of variety as did restaurant dinner meals (also this was reasonably priced). Breakfast area was bright and welcoming. Spa was somewhat expensive considering where we were but to be expected.  Con's- communication via email was seriously lacking, requested a place to keep my bags prior to check-in, had to send two messages before getting a response and by the time the response came at the very last minute, I had made other arrangements.  Dinner location was uninspiring, downstairs, low ceilings, no natural light, bar area was dark, small cramp space.  Rooms with double beds were small where as the rooms with king beds seemed much more spacious.  That said, I would return, if for no other reason than the pool area was great place to relax and have a drink, so quiet and peaceful and the staff at the hotel were incredibly kind and helpful.

I booked this hotel 3rd  time in a year.  First time was okay but this time was terrible.  I reported to reception but noice comes whole night.  In the morning too - I made a complain about 6, still worker were working.  Even I told them on my checkout time staff member are not listening at all.  

Its waste of money.  I mention it on the time to checkout I'm not happy and going to write on TripAdvisor they didn't bother at all.

What a shame ??

What will give you a feel that you are staying in a star category hotel ??? this hotel will give you a zero feeling that you are staying in a star hotel. Enter hotel looking for a reception a tiny reception counter with 50 years old outdated billing system will welcome you and looking for a lobby get a microscope to look for the lobby. Enter room this hotel calls itself a star hotel where is a mini bar a iron board a mini safe and a good television set to watch and just outdated phone set besides your bed and an air conditioner that hardly runs as that keeps on turning off due to power outage.  Enter bathroom will welcome you with filthy smell and it is so narrow feels like going into cave with no bathroom amenities at all and fracture your body or injure yourself when taking a shower very uncomfortable and towels inside bathroom is like a toilet paper. Food good for local cuisine and just edible and forget other cuisine you will certainly curse that your ordered that. Just total nightmare and Disgusting.

This cave reminds me of another similar and special place of Uttarakhand, India - the Patal Bhuvaneswar. Unlike there, this is comparatively smaller and easy going cave. This cave is moisty as the Sweti river flow inside it. Protect your camera, you don't want to damage your precious gear for those one or two shots in dark.
You must be able to walk up and down stairs...pretty place but not a must see. It was part of our tour and it was fine for a few minutes.
Though I am Nepali but it was my first time to visit Boudhanath. Me n my mother feel relaxed there.We spend a couple of hours n get relaxed.It is a very very good destination for visit Nepal 2020.

Take the time to visit this site. Circle around the site like locals do. The site is beautiful during the day and mesmerizing at night. The local stores and markets that surround the site offer beautiful traditional art and crafts from Nepal. Local music complements the spiritual atmosphere of the place.

I’ve seen a view of these, and this was just a really big one, surrounded by tourist restaurants and shops. 
All completely rebuild after the quake.  
I sincerely hope the city will extend the rebuilding of this part to the rest of the city.

...but combined with Davis Falls, it’s something to do.  Really not much to say.  The way down into the cave is a bit ornate; inside it was really a letdown.  There’s nothing in it.   One small shrine.   No photos and wet feet by the way.   After walking down to caves, there were shoes at the entrance (no signs) so I took mine off too.  Walked into something called the Cow Shed and the man sitting kept saying “can wear shoes.”  No one else was so I wouldn’t anyway.  I got past the shrine and the path got to rocky to walk so I turned back.

I liked the hotel ambience, even though the interiors were quite old.. This has a nice lawn and a beautiful garden area to walk around.. If you are looking for a quiet holiday, then this is a nice place. If you want to visit places, then this will not be the right hotel, as attractions are quite far away from the hotel. The traffic during working hours is horrible, so please do not venture out during working hours.. Its also far away from the shopping areas... The food at the hotel is quite nice.. Lounge is too small, can accommodate only 3 groups.. If more than 3 groups, sitting place will not be available..
Devi's fall is normally added to sight seeing iternery by travel agents, but surely can be avoided.The water fall is very normal and nothing much to offer
Its refreshing to visit devi's fall. The sound of water gives you power. Do visit this place and feel the power of nature. Its among the best place to visit in Pokhara valley.

The waterfall is a little outside the city, opposite of the cave. When you do some hiking you see probably more beautiful falls, but the fall is still nice to see. But it is pretty crowded especially with school-classes. It’s not something you have to see, but it’s ok and i would recommend this over the cave.

Its very deep and you need to walk down hundreds of stairs to reach the bottom, but once there the view is splendid. The Shiva Temple is amazingly divine. Going further down under is extremely rewarding. The waterfall there is an unbelievable sight.

MUST VISIT!!!

Absolutely wonderful - excellent staff, great service, beautiful decor/details, excellent location!

Barahi Pokarah is locally owned by the same people as Barahi Jungle Lodge and   Barahi Kathmandu - we stayed at all three locations and our trip through Nepal was amazing because of the staff and management.   We highly recommend staying at all of their locations.  

Bikash at Barahi Jungle Lodge coordinated our arrival and stay at Pokarah.  We highly recommend talking to Bikash at Barahi Jungle Lodge or Sabina at Barahi Kathmandu if you need anything.

Yes. I was little bit shocked after visiting this place as there was very limited attraction. But thinking in depth, you can realize what is natural beauty. Probably this fall created in between two mountains with naturally flowing water from hill top. Amazing part is the sound of the running water. It can make u puzzled and after visiting Gupteshowr Mahadevs Cave, anyone can understand it is nothing but continuation of Davi's Fall. I would say it's worth watching. You should not miss it by seeing negative reviews here. Go and just enjoy it.
IT WAS AN AMAZING PLACE TO VISIT IN KATHMANDU WHERE YOU  Can experience  buddism peace and harmony, I spend a whole day visit around other monasteries neqr by the main one,
Had really good romantic moments here was such a lovely place . Really a very nice place must visit for all

Compliment to Ragisha n Britney at the Restaurant, they are good staff, attentive with warm smile in there face make me so comfort enjoying my meal n drinks, they should be reward for their hardworking job. The room are so comfort n clean, the location also very nice near the city centre so easy for me to explore. All staff are good from the entrance to the lobby, cleaner also do their job well.

a green clean break out in a noisy and polluted city from nowhere. u need to buy a ticket to get in and has a restaurant within. located at the entry point of Thamel and opposite to SAARC office. food is good but expensive.

This was our second stay in Kathmandu.  The Shanker's an old hotel, dark, dank rooms not decorated for years.  The Bathroom was aweful, with a huge 'blob' of something stuck in the bathtub - no idea what it was but we stayed well away!  Our room was next to a road and, having stayed on a Friday night, the music was loud and went on until 1am (not great when we had a flight back home the following day).  The restaurant food was poor, breakfast average.  Location was good but the only saving grace.  Objectively, this would be 2 star by international standards
The Devi's fall would simply fill your heart with thrill. But it's nice to be visited during June when the monsoon has just started and the water is in plenty.
Had a great stay at The Soaltee, Kathmandu. The room was comfortable and clean. The staff are courteous and helpful. Would highly recommend to my family and friends.

Beautiful property, all amenities above average. A lot of facilities , ATM, taxis, sightseeing, casino, etc. i found their pool is great.
Food is something to remember!
Worth every penny.
Excellent for both business and pleasure.
Staff and service is also very good
We expected fantastic place for sightseeing but when we reached there we dint find anything rather then rude shopkeeper outside.

I would like to compliment Sajja and Bibita for an amazing service they r the best. They made my stay so much better.
I would also mention Yubak for taking care of us during his evening shift he is very kind and amazing service from all the staff. 
I visit this property often and their service is amazing.
A  hyped  attraction . If the weather is good, One can enjoy some time in the Sun. A Small Garden . Charges to visit are  a bit high .

Let me begin my review with the positives -
1. Very warm and friendly staff
2. Rooms are spacious and are maintained neat & tidy
3. Bathrooms are very clean
4. There are 4 restaurants in this property and all of them are good! Especially in the one which serves buffet breakfast, you tell the staff your food preferences on day 1 and they will remember it during your entire stay duration and no need to repeat it :)
5. Room service is really quick and efficient

On the flip side -
1. After a couple of hours delay in landing at Kathmandu [not blaming the hotel for this ;) ], the courteous hotel staff with your name board calls the driver and your approx. 45 min. to 1 hour journey to the hotel begins! Within a few minutes, you realize that on a hot, sunny, smoky (due to vehicle pollution) afternoon, the taxi AC's won't be switch ON as hotel as instructed their drivers so. Even after insisting that it is getting really nauseating, the driver still not turn it ON and then you call up the hotel and literally explain it a few times (coz they will keep transferring the call, for reasons better known to them) then the driver would obey their command! I haven't faced it in any other part of the world. May be it is a norm in Kathmandu and people who frequently travel to Kathmandu are accustomed to this. But, I wasn't :(. Hotel was kind enough to waive off the airport pick-up bill and also upgraded me to a next higher level room type.
2. As if my tryst with the cab wasn't enough, in the upgraded room allotted to me on the club floor, within half an hour of check-in water started dripping near the wardrobe and I had to get myself changed to another room. Later on I learnt it was due to some issue with the air conditioner that the water was dripping. Isn't it the hotels responsibility to look after these aspects before allotting rooms to guests?
3. On the last nights of my 3N stay at about 4:30 AM some strange nose (as if someone is hammering or driving a screw) started and it was growing louder and louder to disturb the sleep. After I switched ON the lights and started searching for the source of the noise it gradually stopped. After the initial fantastic experiences, I didn't even bother to report this to the hotel staff.

To sum up it was a one-off experience . . .!

General Information:
Due to the after effects of the earthquake many places in Kathmandu are still undergoing redevelopment works and this hotel is also in such a phase. I saw that the pool wasn't yet available for use and some construction work happening almost round the clock.

Fantastic Service, amazing staff and fine food.

The hotel stands up to its name of the original hotel in kathmandu. The functional level were awesome, courteous. Never without a smile and happy faces.

The managerial staff especially Sanil left no stone unturned in making out stay warm And comfortable... look forward to staying with you all some time... again

We stayed at this hotel for a few nights in March on our visit to Kathmandu. The standard rooms are very dated and the sinks and bathtub are not very clean( stained). 

However when we upgraded for 1 night to the suite , they we very clean and well appointed.

Beware of the Elevators , as we had a VERY bad experience getting stuck in between floors. When we called for help they sent some of the employees to try to open the doors and have us climb out. I requested them to call emergency services but they told me they can't. We were horrified as they partially opened the doors and then shut it back and my wife is clusterfobic.

However, the WiFi was extremely unreliable and the breakfast spread was limited and average.  The room was clean although it could use some upgrading, eg, the tv looked like a 20" lcd computer monitor.

Being so overpriced there very less options  in buffet breakfast and dinner!!!! No snacks no option for beverage!!

I m writing this  by staying here in my first day

This guy had said that since it was a small amount of money they could'nt refund it. As I was ringing from another city he was'nt too bothered. I then contacted a manager of some sort (Yogender) but all he did was to get the crook Guru to ring me back.
If you want a hassle free holiday stay away from this hotel.
Breathtaking. The atmosphere, the People, the sounds and the lack of car sounds wich you can hear in the city. A place to rest.

As I said before Shanker hotel is at best a 3 star hotel going by the available facilities. However to be fair to the hotel it was going through renovations at the time of my visit. 
Firstly I must start by saying that this hotel is not for the claustrophobic as most of their rooms don't have a window worth its name and thereby no view to speak of . In fact the rooms without the windows had a stale , musty smell which made me go and request for a room change. To their credit my request was considered and my room was changed to another one with a tiny window. I was told that in Kathmandu all 4 star hotels have casinos but this one didn't. The Hotel did in fact have the heritage look however it needs urgent attention and preservation.  It also needs a more professional management if I might say so.
Now there are a lot of plusses also. The hotel gives a feeling of safety and in spite of being located in a very busy area was reasonably quiet. It was situated at a walking distance from Thamel and had good power back up systems considering the amount of power cuts that take place in Ktm. The breakfast service was quite elaborate and catered for all tastes. The garden was excellent and the favourite place for my Son who was quite put off by the dark and dingy room (it also had a bath tub masquerading as a swimming pool _pun intended).The hotel staff were courteous and special thanks to Mr.Ramesh at the desk who agreed to change my room without any problems. 
My suggestions to the hotel management is to put the correct rating for the Hotel and also urgently look into the cleanliness and restoration of this heritage hotel which has great potential but flatters to deceive.

A peaceful break from walking around Thamel.  I came early, as it opened, and enjoyed the quiet with a few others. As two hours went by, it became busier, but there is enough space for everyone to spread out 

I found a quiet bench in the shade and enjoyed the calm.

A soothing place for a sensitive traveler to pause and breathe.
Though you can not take bath but seeing itself is amazing.Don't cross the iron Bars area.The water flow is so fast.Also don't forget to take picture near the Nepal map.

Good hotel. Super awesome staff. Very polite and well trained. I had a wonderful stay experience. Would recommend it for families. 

Great Indian food served at the restaurant. 

Very clean hygienic and well maintained  place that is great value

The locatins is absolutely wonderful, the view amazing, perfect. But the rooms are in a poor condition for the price we paid. The furniture is old and in bad condition and the bathroom was really basic, no electric dryer, no bath gel, no carpet... for 200 dollars a night, we expected a lot more.

This stupa is quite the presence, and is worth visiting for is grandeur.    I’d recommend going to a nearby restaurant to a higher floor level to get what I think are better views of the stupa itself.
one of the best Buddhist religious sites in Nepal. When i visited there i found peace and enlightenment with the lamas and gurus. Best place to visit.

It is a ancient Buddhist stupa

Well maintained world heritage sight identified by unesco but located in very conjusted area

Just opposite of Devi's fall on a busy road. Be prepared though there's quite some stairs to descend, and of course climb back up. Nothing great to see. Though it takes entry fees which is just a waste of money and time also. A small temple in cave and slight view of Devi's falls. If you're in shortage of time and money please avoid.

20 years after our first visit to Kathmandu this was the only 'major' site we wanted to return to. It was still a great visit but the coffee was much better. The rest of our time was wandering the backstreets and loving it.
Best place in Kathmandu valley. You get eternal peace and self heal if you hear the mantra chanted. So nice to visit. Love the place.

Sudib’s service was exceptional.
He paid attention to details and made us feel very welcome and comfortable.
The food was very good .
We enjoyed ourselves and will be coming back.
We also enjoyed the live music so much .
Thank you Sudib, I recommend that he gets a promotion or a raise as a reward for his hardwork.

Gupteshwar cave sounds interesting.......
Gupteshwar Cave is regarded as sacred and inviolable by the local people. The cave is divided into two absolutely different parts. One carries the great Lord Shiva temple where a shivlinga, phallic symbol of Lord Shiva is preserved and it is believed that the linga is preserved the way it was originally discovered. The second part is comprised of the snaky caves that widen and narrow down to amuse the tourists. This cave is 3 Km long. At few places, you even have to crawl down to the dust to pass through it. 

From the extreme end, ona can even have a bird's view of nearby Devi's falls. If visiting temple alone, you need to pay Rs 30/-. But if adding caves as well, you need to pay an extra Rs 70/-.

I was surprised to see that this restaurant in a so called 4 star hotel is a tourist trap!! At the Barahi hotel /Pokhara Flavors restaurant, they double charged us on all the alcoholic beverages we had! The manager reply was: "Sir, when you asked for a glass of Rhum, I thought you wanted a double!" Even though the glasses he brought were not doubles, he charged us as if they were double! - not a great review for a high end Hotel / Restaurant!! I liked though the ethnic cultural dance show they had (this is why my rating is 2 over 5 and not 1 over 5)

Though very simple in its design and decoration, I’d still say this is one of the most affecting religious sites I have ever visited. Watching and listening to the prayer flags fluttering over the dome of the eyed-stupa is really very relaxing and peaceful. We loved it.

Fantastic place out of the city. Lovely view 360 deg. Better way to perfect holiday with family. This place made me feel I was very close to nature. Thier Hospitality is amazing across the resort. Hope to be back again.
I went there because of so many reviews from here and there but eventually found it ordinary. Who knows you might like it. So there's no point missing. Go enjoy your time.

Nice hotel. Great ancient building with garden and pool. Rooms are so so. They spent a lot to repaint etc. but chose to install cheap shaky handles for the room and bathroom doors. Didn't have any view from our room. Perhaps there are others. 

Why they supply red towels is beyond me. It's nauseating. What's wrong with white? 

We were there one day when the cleaning staff came to do the room and one man's b/o was so offensive that my wife ran out.....

But other than that we had a fine time. Would stay there again. Staff at reception were marvelous. Good short walk to Thamel.

I went to seek blessings of Lord Shiva. Its a beautiful place. Go downstairs and you reach a small cave then you have to go downstairs again. The you reach the temple. Its all dark inside so lamps are installed everywhere.

We visited this Stupa as part of a one day whistle stop tour of Kathmandu. It is very impressive and can be admired by walking around (clockwise!), popping into smaller temples on the periphery, then taking to one of the several roof top cafes to relax in the sun and enjoy the view and some people watching.

This is a cave temple that leads down to the water from the Devils falls across the road. There is a temple inside the cave - no photo's ensured by the presence of security.
It is wet and slippery so not ideal for all but it is worth a visit alongside the Devils Falls.
Hotel is great ! Service is excellent and food is tasty. Really enjoyed the pool and the bar. I recommend it, and will happily come back

Well, if you want to eat good food, this is not the place. Secondly the money you pay for room is just not the value you get... room amenities are so pathetic. so is the quality of room. Service is 3/5.... so make sure before you make your bookings.
This place is easily accessible for tourists and getting there is hassle-free. I enjoyed the people and the culture immensely, but I would advise caution around the faithful who circle the monument.

Maybe I'm too long travelling but you could miss this place without any problem. Probably more important to the Hindus as it's different from other temples but as a westerner, even with an interest in Hinduism, this is still average

This is a palace that has been converted into a hotel. This hotel could have been epic if not for a few odd staff behavioural issues. The hotel facade is pretty badly damaged due to the earthquake but they are doing their best to get it up and running. The pick up was on time and what i loved was the fact that the room was exactly as per what i like. To all the americans and Europeans ,please do not compare the room to your standards however for kathmandu standards the rooms were big and spacious with absolutely no view though. 
It was also heartening to see that the hotel was a part of charity activities as i did see specially abled children using the hotel pools probably as a good will gesture. The food ranged from excellent to average depending on what you ordered.
The beds offered were nice and cosy although the bathrooms could do with an upgrade although not as filthy as some reviewers have complained about in their previous reviews.
What spoiled it for me though was the behaviour of the check out staff. It was absured that their own room boy offered to open the room for me and then dissappeared with the key. Since i had a spare i did not bother. Unfortunately due to having an infant with us ,we misplaced the room key which is no big deal really..however we were made to pay 600 rs around us dollars 10 for the 2 keys which i found ridiculous. Furthermore the receptionist decided to blame us for losing a tv remote that wasn't there in the room in the first place ! I have no idea what i would do with a hotel tv remote !. All in all a good hotel with lovely staff minus a few rotten eggs. 
Ps the breakfast was pretty decent with a wide variety of food choices !

Crammed with people milling about, camera flashes and cheap tacky stuff from China, the cave in itself is quite interesting if you are not claustrophobic. Its worth it to go right to the end to watch the Devis fall at the back of the cave.

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites in a cave, there are none.  It looks very interesting from the outside and even when going down the spiral staircase.  But once inside, it is just a low ceilinged tunnel, dark, and dripping water.

One of the best place in Kathmandu  City.
I will would like to recommend to all of you  , who like Buddhism and peaceful place

I visited it in the month of March. It was disappointing as there wasn't enough water gushing through. One had to make effort to watch the stream. Also the height of fall isn't too good at all. Kakori is the best restaurant!  Had the best meal and a super time! Janak in particular deserves a special mention for being very hospitable and so warm. I’d highly recommend coming here for dinner if you’re in Kathmandu! You’re guaranteed an amazing meal. :)

Nice and friendly staff. 
Good services and food. 
Some disturbance due to wedding guests staying at some floor. Ill suggest Hotel to accommodate wedding guests and other staying people to place in separate floors.
Well managed place and good ambiance.
An interesting and surprising place to visit in the middle of Pokhara. The river dives under the town through a cave the exits a little further on

Nice place to learn more about Buddhism in Nepal. I loved the central place where people were singing the traditional prayers. Still a pity that the earthquake has left its marks. Also too bad that you need gas masks in the traffic to get there.

Tibet will provide you with many more interesting stupas, but this is an average one, if you have not seen any before. It is surrounded by shops and restaurants with rooftop views. It is touristy. Outside of the circle, that part of town is not the best.

being a Nepali, and staying 20 mins far from Boudha Stupa was and is still amazing.. If in stress, low esteem, or any sad/negative word you can take, you'll always come back home with a fresh mind, happy ( if you ignore the road esp in rainy season) .

Boudha Stupa has always been a place for me. there is many continental/authentic restaurants, cafe, etc if you wish to hangout with your friends, beloved ones and family as well. many tourists visit here and they get their ZEN as well.

#recommended site visit.
Most visit place if you are in Nepal. I must say  it one of the largest spherical stupas in the world
Great experience,water was released on from the lake the day i visit. Outstanding experience to see and also to realize the power of water. Nature seen.

It has a great historic and cultural significance. However, It seemed a bit crowded and the management needs to pay attention to resolve this issue.

Gupteshwar caves is right across the Davis Falls. Walking into the caves is slightly musty and you need to be careful as the steps get wet.

Once inside you walk up and down to view the various statues. 
Right to the end is a sorry excuse of limestone deposits. But what is good about the end is that the caves splits into 2 with the Davis Falls seen from the split.

A beautiful natural creature in the middle of a busy town.

Devi's Falls is a waterfall located at Pokhara, Nepal.

A surprising thing is that the water disappears in a tunnel after reaching the ground, its 500 meter in length and about 100 meters in depth.

As per the info shared there, the best time to visit is June to September.

Also, FYI when you visit this place;after this visit "Gupteshwar Mahadev Cave" which is almost on the opposite side of the Devi's Fall entrance gate.

This is a Buddhist icon and as such is held in high regard. However it is completely surrounded by hawkers and shops and millions of pigeons.  It is certainly not difficult to collect all the tourist articles you may wish to buy in this area but beware of  high-pressure sales people in the various specialist shops

I have seen the Boudhanath Stupa many times in documentaries and photographs and after seeing it over and over i honestly wasn't expecting to be blown away by it the way i was when i entered. Little place where it can see this singular (and very little) fall (very very preatty).
