My stay at Hotel Shanker was spectacular. I loved the service and staff is very friendly and helpful.

Pros:
You get a proper breakfast with all types of diets, starting from fruits, salads, juices, types of bakery items, proteins and many more.

Cleanliness is their utmost priority. Rooms and all the premises is very neat and clean.

Staff is very friendly and helpful.

You get a full proper bar with all sorts of drinks.

You get a full feel of having a stay like a king in his or her own palace.

Cons:

Restaurant rates could have been a bit more reasonable looks a bit pricy.

Hotel taxi for pickup, drop and tour is not available.

Small but beautiful cave to visit.
Tourist pay extra for the cave, the fall is very small but nice to visit.
May stalls nearby for souvenir, much cheaper than the ones at lakeside or Hathmandu especially if you are nice to them and can negotiate.

All of the things is very good
Swimming pool was nice
Room service was very good(including Housekeeping, In room dining)
Housekeeping lady(Sushma), Front desk(Dhan,Ram,Laxmi)
Front desk service was very good
For the things need to be fix is:
Firstly swimming pool light and also need to clean up the pool once a month
Second is need to have finness room for the guest as is five star hotel
I went here with my girl and was good to visit with some religious place where we can find the romantic environment in evening

I am sure that visiting these falls in the rainy period June-August must be impressive but visiting in November is dull as there is almost not water and all you see is a dry creviss and the sound of a waterfall.

I think I did not expect the place to be right by the road side, with shops and other businesses across it. Nevertheless it's an easy activity, and definitely a spot you don't want to miss while sightseeing in Pokhara. 
Right across the street from it is the Mahadev cave, where the waterfall from the Devi's fall descend into the cave. 
 Entrance fee is at Rs30, and there's lots of stalls selling souvenirs and crafts you can check out.

stayed at this hotel for 3 nights to attend a conference...compared to other crowne plaza properties such as beijing, manila, london and chicago, i would say that it is not quite up to par... but considering that this hotel is in nepal, i would say this is a much safer choice for business and leisure.. it is not a city center type hotel , but given the condition, or situation , i figured it was secure to stay in.. rooms are functional, limited lcd tv channels, bathroom and toilet leaves much to be desired, and i wont elaborate..  coffeeshop serves adequate buffet asian offerings with little western consideration, it has an outdoor pool, internet a little pricey, ballroom where we attended the conference was good, biggest advantage of this hotel is the staff , where it seems they are sincere , friendly and honest...

Beautiful heritage hotel in Kathmandu. Large spacious rooms. The lobby is very grand. The restaurant decor is full of wooden sculptures and paintings reminding you of rustic Nepal. The restaurant staff too was very helpful. Both breakfast and dinner were excellent. We being vegetarian Indians had enough choice both times. Thanks also for arranging the covid test within the hotel.
One improvement suggestion is to have a bucket and plastic chair in the room. My mother who had her leg operated struggled to get one after talking multiple times with reception and housekeeping staff.

Located on a busy and dusty street. Entrance fee NPR 100. There is a stupa. One can climb upon its plinth. Around the stupa is a walkway and many small restaurents, hotels and souvenir shops. Thats it!
Waste of time and $4. Pointless - barely anything to see and you’re done within 3 minutes - not worth the entry fee, rip off.

Lovely hotel in a very colonial style. Friendly helpful staff. An oasis of peace amidst the mayhem of Ksthmandu. Beautiful gardens and a nice swimming pool with small eating area beside it. Nice breakfasts but the dinners were slightly disappointing.
In Kathmandu it is hard to enjoy any garden in downtown area.  It is too noisy and polluted.  It is so much better to go outside the city and to climb a hill or small mountain.

it is classical seen.water fall makes a tunnel.which is about 500 feet long. it is named as in 1961 a swiss couple Davi went for swimming but woman drowned and recovered after 3 days in river phusre. her father wished to named it as DAVIS FALL .before it has nepali name patale chango which means..under world water fall..after exiting tunnel water passses through a cave GUPTESHWOR MAHADEV or cave beneath the ground

We often return to this hotel with its charming castle building. Peaceful location with a nice garden and a wonderful pool area. Close to the center and Thamel. Nice rooms, very good breakfast. In the Kailash restaurant you eat well, lots to choose from. A visit to the bar is not a bad thing. Excellent service and very nice and helpful staff. Good help with trips and excursions.
Majvor o Kaj Alvén.

we have stayed for 4 night with group of 12 people, rooms are OK nothing special 
greet swimming pool are, good food expensive, WIFI chargeable for 5 star hotel :)

they should make it free, very slow access any how even if you buy it
i would not stay again unless they make it free :)
expensive compared to other 5 star hotels

It was an amazing experience staying in hotel barahi, we stayed for 10 nights and gained amazing hospitality from staffs. Rooms were super clean, 24 hours hot water,food service is bit slower as what i expected.i don't recommend buffet if you're into spicy food.would love to definitely visit once i'm around pokhara.

Also known as Patale Chhango, this waterfall marks the point where the Pardi Khola stream vanishes underground. When the stream is at full bore after monsoon rains, the sound of the water plunging over the falls is deafening.

According to one of the many local legends, the name is a corruption of David’s Falls, a reference to a Swiss visitor who tumbled into the sinkhole and drowned, taking his girlfriend with him. The falls are about 2km southwest of the airport on the road to Butwal, just before the Tashi Ling Tibetan camp.

I was surprised at how many people were in the Garden of Dreams. It is a small corner lot in the large city but it offers a nice step away onto green grass, ponds, and beautiful flowers. Don't expect it to be quiet, but it's nice for a cup of coffee or two.
Great hospitality by warmth and friendly staff. A good recommendation ideal hotel to stay while in Nepal. Staff are equipped with good knowledge and beyond expectations.

stayed here for 2 nights on a trip with friends. I guess its the best hotel in Pokhara. Rooms were of good standard. Mountain view rooms are good as u can see the annapoorna mountain range. very close the the main Market Street & Phewa Lake. Only place in Pokhara with a 24 hrs restaurant & bar. Breakfast & food was quite decent. Swimming Pool also clean & tidy. Avoid the spa.

The falls themselves are impressive but it is nigh impossible to see much of them. There is a tall thick fence around them that block you getting a good photo. I know it’s a safety fence but it’s a bit much in a small area like this. The rest of the gardens are nice short walk and worth the small entrance price.
Wonderful and supportive staff, clean atmosphere and room, homely. Lovely food, great and big and healthy breakfast. You should try once.

Hotel Sanker doesn’t quite live up to the grandeur of its history. The outside is much better than the interior both for looks and amenities! The best part of this hotel is the pool area. It’s a small pool but relaxing and quiet, a welcome relief from the hustle outside the gates!
Inside the rooms are quite cramped although the beds are very comfy. I think the bathrooms have been remodelled but have a death trap step up / down into the room that can catch you out!
The restaurant ala carts service is very slow but the curries are very tasty. It’s much better than the buffet which is limited. However the breakfast buffet is extremely good - huge amount of options and tasty food. 
A small hotel bar but quite cosy.

The cave is fairly interesting. It's one of the more interesting temples I've visited. It is surprising to descend so far and then see light from the long vertical crack in the earth at the end. 

One recent reviewer expressed concern about safety given the weights of buildings constructed near the cave. The reviewer did not cite any credentials, such as an engineering or geology background. If someone has an informed opinion on this, please elaborate.

The reason for supporting this hotel is that it was badly affected by the earthquake last year, particularly the front. It is in a quiet location within walking distance of the centre. It has nice gardens and pool. The breakfast was very good as was the service. The problem is the rooms. Many do not seem to have a view. We paid extra for a deluxe room but despite numerous requests we ended up with a very pokey room which they insisted was deluxe but we could see very little difference from the standard. It was not just the waste in paying the extra 35 dollars, it was the unhelpful, disdainful and almost sneering attitude of the management that hurt.

Came across this by accident after walking sown from peace pagoda. Also right next to tishling tibetian camp (worth a visit ). Interesting entrance with statues. Damp n warm inside. Steps slippery. Nice shrine inside. Was worth 100rs ticket price.

great historical hotel - newly joined marriott group

we picked that hotel to stay 3 nights coming back from pokhara and before flying back home.
we were very happy to stay there.
they introduced us the history of the hotel. (it was the first 5 star hotel in nepal. they hosted many head of state and celebrities).
as a platinium member, we got all the perks you can wish (upgrade, late check out, lounge acces. special thanks to hari from the lounge and his colleagues. thanks to them for the recommendation on what to visit).
as we were celebrating our wedding anniversary, we got some special surprise. they went far beyond our expectations.

the breakfast was very good with a large choice. our son likes very much the local yogurt juju dhau). the local food was great. and my wife liked a lot the massala tea.

we tried one restaurant and it was great.

even the room service was great. they check on us regularly to make sure everything was ok with the room.

the overall setting of the hotel is nice in a peaceful coumpound.
the city center (thamel) is just a short taxi ride away. we were very glad to have stay here for 3 days
in the end point of the cave you can see davi's water fall and in the middle of the cave there is a Hindu temple of load shiva

The Garden of Dreams is a beautiful place to get away from the noice and the dirtiness of Kathmandu. But it is overcrowded inside the garden and even thethe restaurant inside is overpriced and overcrowded. The worst thing for me is that smoking is allowed inside the garden!
Shame it was all sectioned off hard to see and felt like it was a bit of a tourist scam ..the fencing was hard to see the full effect off the waterfalls
It cost us 1000 rupees to get in the garden. It is very nice and it is well taken of but it is very expensive for its size and compared with other attractions in nepal

The hotel facade & the structure is like a palace. Inside too the old times feel was good. We had booked a suite which was more like an extended L shaped room. The bathroom was quite big with a tub & well equipped. The housekeeping people were very courteous and helpful.
We were welcomed with a fruit basket and a flower basket. 
The only draw back was the view from our room, which was nothing....just some rooftops & Hotel Radisson  :( 
They don't have any Garden facing rooms which was very disappointing as they have a lovely garden with the pool.
They give a litre of mineral water per person everyday which is a plus as compared to other hotels which are very stringy about water.
The in house restaurant Kosy Kailash was a disaster. Dinner was the worst of the whole trip. No veg. food, extremely slow service. The menu was limited & buffet was also meagre. There was almost nothing for the Indian pallete. We satisfied our hunger with chocolate icecream.
The buffet breakfast was much better with continental as well as Indian spread.
It may be good for the foreigners with its palace like ambience but failed to impress us (Indians) who have visited real palaces in Rajasthan.
On the whole it was an average experience.

Beautiful place with mind blowing architect and history. This is has very interesting history with massive structure. 

There are many rooftop restaurant which offer delicious local food with the view of Boudhanath stupa. i highly suggest people try to visit this place around afternoon. You can see religious people doing Kora (circling boudhanath stupa) and evening view with lights on Boudhnath is magnificent. 

Beware of thugs who ask for money around stupa showing their fake small baby, sometime they follow you for some distance. You have to strongly say No for them.

The Cave is a popular tourist destination and attracts a large number of visitors every year. The cave is about 200 meters long and has several chambers with various stalactites and stalagmites formations.

Lovely hotel in the centre of Kathmandu. Room was great with comfortable suite and plenty of space for our clothes. Food was excellent, staff were very helpful and friendly. Would stay here again. Good location for your stay. Roads nearby are a challenge if walking, so rely on local taxis, make sure you download the local taxi app ‘Pathao’ which is a must. Taxis are very cheap.
This cave is a sacred and natural cave; there is temple of Load Shiva.Cave famous for it's religious importance located in the southern end of the city, Chorepatan.
Far more spectacular than I was expecting.  There is a story to the place too. Very easy to reach by taxi from Pokhara.

As the story goes, Ms. Davis slipped into the falls in 1961 and the attraction was named after her. The entire place is now fenced off to prevent such a tragedy from happening again. The location also has a garden where visitors can pose for photographs with various Nepali dress and a Buddha.

If you have enough time in Kathmandu it’s worth the visit. 
If you are in a hurry, there are more Beautiful things to visit in Kathmandu.

Location is great.  Rooms were nice enough but a bit damp and worn out .  At $170/night during the high season it is overpriced.  Our AC did not work.  Neither did the TV, though who cares when you can look at the Himalayas.  There is also no internet access to speak of.  Our beef was with the service though.  The desk staff was unattentive and unprofessional; we saw them laughing at a guest after he had left, though his request seemed quite reasonable to us.  The last nail in the coffin is that when we arrived at the airport for our 10 AM flight we learned that we had been bumped to the EARLIER flight and that the hotel staff who confirmed the ticket had been told that. . . they just failed to inform us.  Small problem given that we had an international flight to catch from Kathmandu later that afternoon!

Great location for accessing the Thamil market area but the service was average at best and the food could certainly be better.

Used the guide service at the hotel for a half day of sight seeing which was great value and covered the key sites in Kathmandu but be sure to book your flight to Everest before you arrive, so you only need a car to take you to and from the airport.

If you are in the area, the Garden of Dreams is a lovely place to relax for an hour or two.  It is clean and quiet, with beautiful walkways and meticulously groomed gardens.  It is a nice place to visit, though I wouldn’t include it on a list of must-see Kathmandu attractions.

Although it is a former palace, I would not come back. it is uncleaned, smelly carpet, arrogant reception, and very bad food. Room has No view, only a small window with a view of AC compressors. Small bathroom and bad ventilation. I hate the ceiling and made me itchy. There is nothing I enjoy staying at this hotel. It is not a chained hotel therefore they don’t seem to have a quality control. People are attracted because it is a former palace. It may be good for conference as it has conference room.

Always a great stay! Friendly and attentive staff. Excellent facilities. The restaurant is very good, a nice variety of food. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. The grounds are very well maintained. The spa is wonderful. This was my fourth stay at the Hotel Shanker.

Connecting to our self past/life which one often is not aware.I made a round around the Stupa and start feeling the vibration emanating from the latter.A place to visit and stay for some time in order to feel the positive vibration and be yourself and also cut off from the hectic current life.

Despite of the many load shedding that occurred in the hotel, our stay was a pleasant one. We loved the warm hospitality and the staffs were friendly. However, the lights in our room were really dim that made the room really dark n depressing. And another major let down was the 2 ladies in the reception who started taking their own sweet time while we were checking out. There was no “Thank you” or “Hope you had a nice stay. See you again”!! We ended up with a sour note. May be you should train the front desk staffs to be a little more professional and friendly.

We a group of 7 , were on vacation in Kathmandu for 10 days . we stayed at  this hotel for 5 nights   and  balance 2 nights in Nagarkot and  another 2 nights in pokhara.. The booking of the hotel was done by our travel agent from New Delhi , India..  The hotel rates charged by  our tour agent was double from the the rates, if we booked online hotel bookings . I was convinced that a  tour package was the total responsibility of the tour agent providing ground arrangement plus hotel bookings. If we had did the online hotel booking  the wifi is free . When we checked into the hotel , the hotel refused to provide free wifi service ,stating that only online hotel bookings were provided free wifi .. We were cut out from communicating with the loved ones at home because of the said hotel policy; while all the westerns were given free wifi service compared to Asian. It really shows a double standard.in hotel management.After some complaining to our tour agent we were given free wifi  on our 3 day of stay for 4 pax for the 4 rooms we stayed  there before we moved to Nagarkot and Pokhara where free wifi was given as we checked into the hotel..The food and beverage prices were very expensive for this hotel.. Other then that the hotel service was excellent , very spacious garden with swimming pool and near to main shopping center. I would like advice future travelers  who have booked to stay in this hotel to make sure that you are provided the service as per advertise  online  by the hotel. Finally if I were to come back to Nepal again ,I will definitely not stay in  this hotel..

We visited twice. 
The second time was great. It was busy, people and sounds everywhere. 
Enjoyed the walk and the coffee we had at Himalaya Cafe.

Located close to Devi’s Falls the main cave contains two chambers with several shrines located throughout.  The largest of these shrines is dedicated to Shiva. After walking through the roadside archway, before entering the cave, there are many souvenir stalls.  Before the ticket counter is a round concrete balcony which allows a close look at the cave entrance and the statues leading up to it.  After the ticket counter, enter down the large spiral staircase.  Here there are many modern statues and plaster works depicting semi-clad ladies to bearded men similar to some of the Kathmandu Valley's erotic carvings.
As you enter the cave you'll discover how dark it is inside.  The lighting is a series of small light bulbs so a torch comes in handy.  As you descend a little, you will see a small tunnel like cow shed.  About 40 meters further down is the main Shiva temple.  No photography is allowed here.
The lingam is enclosed in heavy iron grills.

Fishtail Lodge is a nice, charming hotel though a little old and run-down now. It is currently being renovated shifting the restaurant to a makeshift location. It can get quite crowded during mealtimes.

Our experience was exceptional and we would rank the hotel 5*! I went with my old parents and <10 yr old daughter and stayed 3 nights. The rooms and bathrooms were spotless (7th floor), the beds were super comfy, AC worked very well, the hotel truly felt like a palace with its exceptional decor. The room had all the amenities you expect from a 5* hotel. The breakfast and la carte menu dinner were excellent too. The staff was super helpful for anything you would need. The free airport transfer was helpful. The swimming pool and area was also very clean and welcoming. The location was excellent as well. I would definitely stay here again!

A very deep place beneath the earth surface where you can enjoy the amazing environment. You can see the downward devi's fall from the cave. The place is slippery due to continuous small drops of water and hence it's better to use shoes with spikes. Since the cave is quite deep, it might not be suitable for elderly persons.

A must visit place in Kathmandu. Taxi ride from the main city to stupa might be quiet a ride filled with chaotic traffic but at  vibe over there. The smell of incense stick, the lamas in their robes and the unbothered crowd gives you a sense of peace over there. Plenty of good eating options over there.

I traveled there during monsoon with my parents . We really enjoyed the greenery  and rush of water .   Although it's not very big , it has a charm of it's own .But the littering by tourists should be stooped immediately .
a must visit for all able bodied travellers. seniors may avoid due to dark and steep stairs. nice cave walk though anti climax as river at the end is not very prominent. but good experience.

I had a wonderful experience at this hotel, thanks in large part to the exceptional staff. From the moment I arrived.

"Aashish"and the staff were incredibly friendly and always ready to help. Their great service truly made the stay even better!

Hotel is amazing..! I visist this place quite often and the staff never fails to provide an excellent experience.. The buffet service is also amazing.. Today the stewardess SHRIYA was very professional and pro active.. thankyou for an amazing experience. Cheers !!

Do not miss this spectacular stupa, a UNESCO heritage site and the largest stupa in Nepal.  We visited around 9:00 am, so the crowds were still low.  The circular grounds are lined with vendors selling prayer beads, jewelry, and all kinds of food. There is an entrance to a side temple that you can enter and climb several flights up for a wonderful view of the entire property.  Take your time, soak it in, and enjoy!

The only nice thing about this place, given the high price for accommodations, is the facade and gardens. Bed is comfortable but rooms are very small as well as windows, where you can see people cleaning the facade just as you get out of shower. There are way better hotels near Thamel at one quarter of what you pay to stay here. Breakfast is pretty basic. Would never stay here at this price again.

This is the place where you can actually realise the power of mother nature. The water forms an underground tunnel when it reaches the bottom. We were informed by our tourist guide that the name was given by a Swiss couple in 1961. The wife Davi had gone for a swim and drowned due to the water overflow. Her body was recovered 3 days later. Her husband named it "Davi's falls" in her memory. Its Nepali name is Patale Chango, which means "underworld waterfall".

Natural cave under the ground, many floors.
Pure bliss to have visited such divine place. Very good experience, must visit site once in Pokhara.

We went there in monsoon, was a kind of scary when huge amount of water going down and drops of water coming up after hitting the rock below, more enough to wet you up.. view of rainbow formed by those drops is really incredible.... it may be dissapointing to those who visit there in dry seasons (even I was dissapointed)  as there's no much water enough to show all the great effects..

Seems to be a classic hotel about 10 minute (tough) walk to downtown Thamel. It's nice to get away from the chaos of downtown for a night but for a "4 star"hotel I expect better beds, better food, and more upscale accommodation. I would pay no more than $50 for this when there plentiful numbers of hostels and cheap hotels downtown.  Suggest the Hyatt or another chain.  If you are a westerner you will be disappointed - but for the area this is definitely on the nicer side... But still hard to justify 4 stars when you're used to marriotts, etc.  I will say that the service was impeccable. Every request I had was completed within <5 minutes.
A beautiful garden to spend an hour or two and get some lovely pictures.  There is a small entry fee.  Don’t miss it during your trip to Kathmandu.

The Garden of Dreams स्वप्न बगैँचा is a very small garden, but if you are looking for a respite from the Katmandu traffic and hustle and bustle this can be recommended.
It also is a nice place to eat or drink at the cafe or restaurant in it.
Be careful when you pay to count your change as the woman shorted me 200 rupee. Admission is 400 rupees ($3 USD) or 200 rupees for seniors.

We checked into this beautiful hotel recently. Lovely ambience on the natural lake Fewa taal. No complaints with the property overall however if the management paid attention to smaller details, this holiday of ours would have left an everlasting impression on us. 

First and foremost, we booked 2 dbls and one single well in advance. Yet upon check in we were told that sorry we only have 3 twins available!! Now this is the basic. Why werewe not told in advance? Next was the welcome drink. We finished our check in formalities and yet the welcome drinks were nt ready. They were asking us to wait for the drinks!! That too after a five and a half hour road journey! Definitely not done. Lastly after we entered our rooms we found that there was no room service menu? I think even the smallest lodges have this basic item placed in the rooms and definitely not expected from this fine hotel. 

Now we come to the breakfast. Extremely well laid out. However the refills of the items took forever to come. And ofcourse the staff forgot that they need to serve tea/coffee to the guests at breakfast table. It seemed as if they were too tired catering to an 80%occupancy. 

Looking into such small details would enhance the overall image of the property. Hope the management looks into this and we do hope to have a better experience the next time.
Beautiful waterfall and worth visiting the cave under the waterfall too! Be prepared that it is wet and slippery in the cave and you have to watch where you tread.
A beautiful  walled  garden - an unexpected joy in busy Kathmandu.  Lovely lay out, beautiful buildings and a quiet place to relax and recharge. Has a restaurant. Note that there is an entrance fee.

Also known as Patale Chhango, this waterfall marks the point where the Pardi Khola stream vanishes underground. this place is perfect for recreational activities and enjoyment. it is perfect to visit during the rainy season where the waterfalls is in full "bloom". there is also a luck or wish pond constructed there and you can try it by throwing and placing the coin on the statue of a god. but there is this eerie feeling when you get near the falls. it got its name from a Swedish tourist who fell unto the falls while taking a bath.

The ambience, food, and services were excellent. We loved the engaging and supporting staff. On top of the best food we received, friendly, cheerful and supporting hospitality of staff (specially, Saroj ji, Akash ji, Hari sir and master chef Sagar) were praiseworthy. Never forget to try Rawadi in your dessert.
If you are planning to visit pokhara,you most go to this place to get more entertainment.it is really good place where you can chill out with your family as well as wit your love one

Stupa is beautiful, but the real star is how cool the architecture around it is. It’s completely encircled by gorgeous buildings full of shops and restaurants, and it’s just so stunning and interesting. There is a temple you can enter without shoes and observe different rituals or ceremonies taking place. Monks inside chant mantras from parchment and perform rites and other religious services. So cool! 

Beware that you should not walk from Thamel area to this site- it’s too long, roads are congested and dangerous to pedestrians, it is also unbelievably dusty to the point visibility is really limited at times. Bring a face shield for the ride over- but it’s clean and lovely in the Stupa courtyard itself.

We visited this in the afternoon—around 5 pm. This is a very peaceful place. We visited the cafe and had some tea. This place had wifi, which was nice.

We walked around the garden after tea. Really nice place.

Amazing hôtel, I loved the room, the bad, 
And also the food I went to the lunch buffet it was delicious, I want to thank also the staf for the amazing service .

It was a nice experience to see the hidden waterfall and the cave. 
Although renovation was underway, we could enjoy the place.

If you aren't spiritually attracted to the place, this will have limited attraction for you. Yes, an iconic tourist place, good to take few steps, some shopping. A guide is better choice, if you don't have any connect. 1-2 hours max required, you may combine with lunch in surrounding. Can be hot during summers hence check temperatures before visiting and prepare accordingly.

I think the best time to see the fall would be after the monsoon. The market at the entrance looked interesting unfortunately the earthquake prevented me looking at it. Never mind I loved Nepal and will certainly go back and finish my touring.
Amazing! We had a great time driving around with Indra! Very funny and answered all our questions we had. Best driver EVER!!!!!

Had some fabulous Mughali dishes at Kakori. The paneer skewers, grilled chicken and mutton nihari were the best of the bunch. Gajar halwa was fantastic. Narattom and Janak took great care of us. Thumbs up and a must visit if you are in Kathmandu.

This Stupa is absolutely incredible. I had a friend tell me, “every time you look at the Stupa, it looks different” and it’s so true. If you’re not able to do Kora (walking mediation) around the Stupa, definitely sit down on a nearby bench and take in the angles. I would really suggest going a little before sunset, grabbing dinner while you watch it go from sunset to night. It’s truly spectacular.

I stayed around Bouddhanath Stupa during my stay at Kathmandu. I used to visit this place on a daily basis. This place was amazing. I got chance to learn soo much about ancient Buddhist teaching. Aroma of incense and sage surrounded the place and it gave different feeling. It was really liberating experience.

Excellent Customer service, felt home! Special thanks to Mr Ramesh he managed us so well! The food, spa, hospitality is beyond words! Also special thanks to Ms. Sandhya , she did amazing spa! Would want to come back again and again and experience this wonderful property and services
great customer service, very good hotel, great food and very friendly staff and with good manners, i love it , I recommend this hotel to others
caves are well but going inside too deep is risky as lot of water and too slippery, If they are charging for seeing these caves they must manage them properly as well.

I was in the Soaltee for 4 days and had a great experience. The staff were very sweet and helpful. They made sure I was not at all in any stress or discomfort throughout my stay. They location is very lovely and tasteful, the gym was excellent as well with a multitude of equipment for both cardio and weightlifting (no barbell tho). The food throughout the location was fantastic. We went to the garden terrace restaurant a multitude of times throughout our stay and were always greeted and taken care of extensively. Mr Dharmendra is the manager of the restaurant and made our visit to their restaurant all the more better with excellent and personal service sandwiched with amazing recommendations for us to try. The food was finger licking and I would highly recommend it. Will definitely be making a second trip sometime soon

Amazing atmosphere here. Open and light. Just walking around, having coffee just watching the locals is really nice.  I think paying entrence fees are importante and I hope the money goes where it is supposed. Think i so far paid three visits.

Stayed at this hotel from 8-13 Sept 2018. Hotel is located approximately 20mins drive from Kathmandu international airport and 12 mins stroll to Thamel. There’s some local eateries on the main road and a well stocked supermarket about 5mims walk. 

The hotel was previously a palace for the royals. Hence the old world charm design of the building. I was given room 616 with a king size bed. Room size was good enough for single occupancy. Some of the amenities available were fridge, electric kettle, hairdryer, individual control AC, basic toiletries, indoor slippers, electric safe and 2 bottles of water provided daily. 

Breakfast starts at 630am and serves relatively good range with some local delights. Love the vade! There’s a Swimming pool with pool side cafe which I didn’t use. gym and spa are available. 

Everything were good for the price. The down side of this hotel are: 
- Water has slight yellowish tint from tap. 
- There’s a small flight of steps before going up to the elevator. Hence one have to carry their luggage up before getting to the it. 
- Rooms were not 100% sound proof. One may hear people walking outside. 
- No peep hole on the room door. 
- Front desk staff were found sleeping on the couch at 5am every morning. However there was security guide at the main entrance. 
- Dinner at the restaurant was almost double the prize for the quality you can get from Thamel.

Boudhanath, also known as Boudha, is one of the most significant Buddhist sites in Kathmandu, Nepal, and indeed, one of the largest stupas in the world. This ancient monument stands as a symbol of peace, harmony, and enlightenment, encapsulating the essence of Buddhist philosophy and practice.

The origins of Boudhanath date back to the 5th century AD, although its precise founding remains shrouded in legend and myth. According to tradition, the site was established by the Lichhavi King Manadeva after a dream in which the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara instructed him to build a stupa at the location. Over the centuries, Boudhanath has undergone several renovations and expansions, becoming the impressive structure that it is today.

At the heart of Boudhanath is its magnificent stupa, a massive hemispherical dome adorned with intricate carvings, prayer flags, and colorful prayer wheels. The stupa is surrounded by a circular path known as the kora, where pilgrims and visitors alike walk clockwise, spinning prayer wheels and reciting mantras as they circumambulate the sacred monument.

The significance of Boudhanath extends beyond its architectural grandeur. It serves as a focal point for Buddhist practitioners from around the world, attracting devotees, monks, and scholars who come to pay homage, meditate, and engage in religious rituals. The bustling streets surrounding the stupa are lined with monasteries, temples, and shops selling religious artifacts, creating a vibrant atmosphere of spiritual devotion.

One of the most striking features of Boudhanath is the piercing gaze of the all-seeing eyes painted on the four sides of the stupa's tower. These eyes, known as the "eyes of the Buddha," are believed to symbolize wisdom, compassion, and the ability to see beyond the material world.

Boudhanath also plays a significant role in the cultural and social fabric of Nepal. It serves as a gathering place for festivals, ceremonies, and cultural events, bringing together people of diverse backgrounds in celebration of their shared heritage and beliefs.

In 2015, Boudhanath suffered extensive damage during a devastating earthquake that struck Nepal. However, through the collective efforts of local communities, international organizations, and government agencies, the stupa was meticulously restored to its former glory, reaffirming its status as a beacon of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.

In conclusion, Boudhanath stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Buddhism and the power of sacred architecture to inspire and uplift the human spirit. Its majestic presence continues to draw pilgrims and seekers alike, offering a sanctuary of peace and enlightenment in an ever-changing world.

Pokhara is famous for mountain views and lakes but underground there is a hidden secret - the spectacular Gupteswar cave. The cave is well worth a visit for those interested in geology as the cave is linked to the Devi Falls across the road, and to the lake and to the mountains.  You might think the entrance to cave is set in a rural landscape, but it is easy to miss unless you know what you are looking for. The entrance is through an archway almost hidden in busy shops along a busy road. Walk through the entrance arch and along a few metres through market stalls to the ticket office - the entrance fee is very small for tourists.  Also time your visit to the cave for days other than the local Saturday holiday or any other public holiday otherwise you will be surprised to find hundreds of locals visiting the cave making it very crowded. The entrance is quite amazing as in the middle of the shops and market stalls you walk down a deep staircase into the dark cave which is only lit by lightbulbs strung along the roof. Highly recommended you take a torchlight. Then follow the stairs as fair as you can go first through the main cave and then deeper underground to a huge cavern - the view is spectacular as you can see daylight shining through an opening in the rocks where the Devi waterfall across the road pours into. During the monsoon season this deeper cave may be closed due to the amount of water pouring in. The Gupteswar Cave is said to be one of the longest and deepest in south east Asia, and you can only marvel at the size and depth of the cave and its link to the river and the lake and up to the mountains. Allow about 2 hours for the visit. It is not suitable for people who do not like enclosed spaces as you need to walk through a very narrow tunnel to reach the big cave and the path is wet and slippery - but there is plenty of fresh air in the cave coming from the opening where the waterfall comes into the cave. And when you come out of the cave and look across the road to the Devi Falls, you can only wonder how the cave has manage to survive as above it are roads, traffic, shops and cafes and busy city life!  Well worth a visit.

But later my bank statement shows the hotel has made 3 swipes and withdrawn 3 times the bill amt without my authorization. This happened on 31st May 2017 and till date they have neither replied my emails nor returned my money

The falls themselves would be beautiful if it weren’t for the 6 foot tall iron gates that surround the falls on all sides.  Unless you want to feel like you’re looking at the falls from a prison cell, it’s not a great view.  Check it out if you’re in the area, but I wouldn’t make a special trip just for this.

We wanted to eat or lunch here and that wasn't aloud. So we had to eat our lunch in the dust of the street. We don't understand why it isn't allowed if you keep everything clean. So don't buy lunch and try to eat here.

We went on a Saturday, which was probably the busiest day of the week. The garden itself is very small. There were lots of teenage couples, which made us feel out of place. The restaurant serves great food.

Nothing worth watching 
Small little fall 
Can avoid 
There r more other places to be visited in an around Pokhara  if u want can rent a bike n take a stroll Round d town

Great people as everywhere in Nepal. very friendly and helpful. This Hotel Shanker has been so well photo-shopped on the website and in the general advertising. Best part of the hotel are the gardens which are amazing and the Jasmin is heavenly. The old world charm is wearing thin, our room was dated to say the least. Barking dogs kept us awake every night until we checked out three days early. There are beeter hotels in Kathmandu in this price range. Needs a facelift!

The stupa was a very interesting place to visit. We walked around the outside, which is completely lined by multiple-storey shops and cafes. It was interesting to sit in one of these cafés and people watch. The place definitely had a peaceful vibe about it.
Ok for short  VISIT . Taking a local  US to this spot is difficult.  Easy is taxi but taxi want to charge a lot .

Very friendly staff from check in to the Cafe. Waiter Mr Bigyan was  exceptional in his job.  Room was clean . Cafe breakfast selection were plenty from Vegs, Dosa &Puri Keep up the good job. Do support this hotel & staff. Will come back again for sure.
This is Lord Shiva's cave which is approximately 2.5 - 3km long. A nice place to visit. It's opposite to Davis falls.
Been there with friends, can see the upper part of the waterfall with the sound of water falling, but can't see where water falls,

Wonderful staff, great food in the restaurant for breakfast and dinner. Helpful at the front desk and Travel desk both. 

Our room could have done with a thorough clean though. Sheets and bed clean, but the floor and bathroom a bit grubby. A real shame, as otherwise an excellent stay. I would stay again.
It was a great experience staying in Soaltee kathmandu. Being Marriott Bonvoy member we were taken care really good by all staff. Thank You Soaltee Kathmandu. We will visit again.
I’m not sure how this is a garden area listed as somo not to be missed. Small area and not very child friendly. Disappointed.

Boudhanath Stupa in Kathmandu is a serene and awe-inspiring UNESCO World Heritage Site, with stunning architecture and intricate carvings that showcase Nepal's rich cultural heritage. Witnessing the daily rituals and prayers of the locals adds to the peaceful atmosphere, and nearby monasteries offer an opportunity to learn about the Buddhist faith. It's a must-visit for culture, history, and religion enthusiasts.

My experience at The Soaltee Kathmandu was absolutely wonderful! The hotel itself is set within stunningly beautiful and expansive gardens, creating a truly peaceful and luxurious oasis away from the city buzz.
What really made the stay special was the incredible staff – everyone was so genuinely warm, welcoming, and attentive. Their hospitality was outstanding! The amenities are top-notch; the large swimming pool was fantastic for relaxing, and the spa facilities looked superb.
Our room was very comfortable, clean, and well-appointed. We also thoroughly enjoyed the dining options, especially the extensive and delicious breakfast buffet each morning.
For a truly comfortable, luxurious, and memorable stay in Kathmandu with exceptional service, I highly recommend The Soaltee!
If you visit the stupa a night it is beautiful building to see and the atmosphere with the surrounding shops, cafes and things to look at are very interesting too

This is a comfortable, nicely laid out, clean and well located hotel in Pokhara. It is not a luxury hotel and is very basic, even though it is one of the only hotels with a pool in this area. The gardens are really lovely, mature trees, very green and lovely pool. Friendly hotel staff, but to be honest they were very basically trained and customer service is not great. Our room was clean, very basic, we did have hot water (had to run the tap for 10mins when we arrived!!) but the bathroom was very simple. Breakfast is a buffet and is also not great BUT you are in a developing country and its just not possible to get freshly squeezed juice, brown toast and poached eggs in a basic hotel like this! As long as you keep your expectations to a minimum you will not be disappointed.

Our tourist group visited those lakes, and as a nature lover, they looked mesmerizing because they showed true force of water against hard rock. I was sad because very high prison bar fence was erected, because it obstructs view on this magnificent water power. 

Yes, waterfall isn't tall or specially fotogenic, so you cannot take great shots to show at home. But, from all 20 minutes that we stayed there I stared into raw force of nature, with respect that it deserves. In the belly of waterfall, where water enters the cave, there was pretty rainbow. Everything looked magical. If I could have whole our at site, I would have stayed there.

Would never go there again. Very over priced and extremely bad service from the hotel manager. No interest in us. Wifi is additional and very expensive. Beds were so hard we didn't sleep all night. Rest of the staff seems to be ok and friendly.

its unique must see......
though it is a small falls it is attractive can't explain....
its on the way of may attractions hardly takes 5 minutes just give it a try if you like you may want to stay there for longer

Behind a bustling street of businesses, restaurants and vendors on a busy street in Pokhara, is garden like area that includes the beautiful Devi's Waterfalls. Upon entering the site, I immediately heard the sound of the powerful water rushing along the rocks. However, before venturing down to get a closer look at the waterfalls, I enjoyed the lush landscape around the site. There is a tribute to the Hindu god Shiva as represented by statutes of bulls and the phallus that I saw in shrines around Nepal. There was also a fountain where visitors are encouraged to toss in coins for good luck. There are always young entrepreneurs at Nepali sites with fountains who are eager to sell coins to visitors!

The various steps leading down to the viewing of the waterfalls are uneven in stops, but well worth the short walk. While a relatively small waterfalls, it is very scenic and the sounds quite soothing.

The only reason we chose this hotel  was for the pool. We stayed in a different hotel the first time in Nepal and had regrets about not having a pool. It’s a rat run to get to some of the rooms but they are nice and The breakfast is good. Ate lunch a few teams here but it’s expensive and you can get an awesome falafel for a third of the price in Thamel.

Big Stupa was destroyed by earthquake but already rebuilt. This is amazing place with a lot of restaurants. We took a clockwise round and then had delicious lunch in Vietnam restaurant. Service was quick. Portions big. View - stunning.
Such a nice waterfall and such a scenic view it is which is indeed very romantic one feels out of the world here
Amazing stay, very spacious and comfortable rooms with a lot of amenities, and the staff is very kind and always smiling.

Found it like an elderly duchess who's memories of finer days are fading but the facade is still there. Relatively peaceful and that is a rare spot in Kathmandu but hasn't been well maintained for flora nor the water features or statues. Sad.

The staff is very friendly pay attention to detail. The anticipation of the staff is another level my heart has been so welcoming since they picked us from the airport till the drop off to the airport! The live show, the restaurant dining special thanks to sudip who took great care of us :)

These waterfalls are amazing because they are hidden in a fairly busy area and you would never believe that these amazing falls wait behind these gates only a short walk away. Make sure to stop at several points along the way to admire the viewpoints as the falls change as you move along to the farthest viewing point. As you get closer you get to enjoy the mist. We visited during monsoon season, so the falls were full and very powerful, quite the sight! Make sure to include this in your visit to Pokhara!

I loved this place, gushing water, misty air, a nice stop on a hot day. I'll be back!
Trinket stalls abound so I'm sure you will find something special to take home with you

The building is sumptuous and the grounds are well kept. From outside its gorgeous. Stay outside. 
Sadly the interior is much outdated. A shame that the palace interiors have been ripped out and transformed into small cookie-cutter rooms. The staff was not overly friendly are rather procedural - was expecting an actual experience but the hotel failed to do so. The room was comfortable - bed too soft to my liking. Not much light as the windows are small. Bathroom was somewhat clean with odors emanating from bath tub and sink. But the worst thing was the odor of the room - a moldy and horribly humid smell. Had to buy some incense and that only covered the smell. Nice to have some chocolates and bananas sent on arrival. Was also pleased to get the International New York Times. Breakfast is served in a monstrously big hall with food spread out miles apart. Pool looked lovely but it was raining sadly. All in all, a massive renovation would do the Shanker well. For the time being find another place to stay.
Very clean and well maintained hotel. The staff is super friendly and always available to help you. Overall an amazing stay.

The service was as excellent. Sambhav was really good at his duties. He had good education regarding the menu. Gave us suggestions and helped us in every way possible. The food was amazing. Loved how the chef came to us for the feedback.  Enjoyed the dinner with soothing music.

nice cave, temple inside the cave. most interesting part is just before we went inside the cave we had been to Davi's fall and we saw the falls but not the button, but when we went inside the cave we saw the same falls and its button. it was good.

The place is right next to thamel and has an entry fee to just go into the garden. You can spend some time there just chilling but beyond that there isn't much. There is a Kaiser cafe which is highly rated but we had already has food by the time we got there and so just got a coffee and a milkshake which was good.

During monsoon, there is a lot of water. In March, it is a small waterfall. Go over to the right side and see the depth of the gorge and that is impressive. The story of why it is named is a nice story.

Our small group tour had made a quick stop at the Devil's Falls in Pokhara - a small tourist attraction area.  There is not much here other than to see a small waterfall in a small gorge area - OK to see what it looks like, but in my opinion it was not very impressive.

We would like to extend our heartfelt thanks to the entire team for making our stay and events truly memorable. A special note of appreciation goes to Housekeeping Executive, Mr. Jeevan Rai, whose support and dedication were exceptional. He went above and beyond in assisting with our guests during the events and ensured that our stay was comfortable and well-coordinated.

Despite the ongoing curfew in Nepal, Mr. Jeevan Rai and Anil sir Front office, the hotel management arranged transportation and provided all necessary facilities in a timely and efficient manner. His efforts made a significant difference and ensured everything ran smoothly.

The food, especially during the event buffet, was excellent and received great feedback from our Chinese colleagues . All the staff members were courteous, professional, and attentive, contributing to a wonderful overall experience.

We are truly thankful for the warm hospitality and seamless management. Highly recommended for anyone looking for quality service, safe and a memorable stay.
I had a wonderful day attending a festival at Boudnath. The stupa is awe inspiring, it takes your breath away at first sight.

Did not meet at airport as requested. Avoid buffet, a la carte better. "Travel desk" very very poor, I booked a flight with avia club microlites, told would see "fishtail" ie two peaks on a 1/2 hour, not so - needed an hour, also not told that there was a small plane which (for same amount)goes further/higher.
All seats in gardens/outside rooms were slatted wooden, no cushions, uncomfortable - but by pontoon, staff seats had padding!!!!
However, wonderful setting

The cave can be seen going down a series of steps and in many places you have to walk through very narrow and very low - roofed areas. Once you reach the bottom level one can see the awesome seti gandaki

Does not give the feeling of a hazardous adventure as does the Mawsmai caves in Meghalaya, India - but is still well worth a visit. Especially for a family, it's a wonderous experience for kids to be seeing a real cave from the inside!

It may be the best hotel to stay in terms of comfort and cuisine. We were initially disappointed during our check-in because the executive did not properly handle it, and we were allocated an old corner room in their old wing. Things were alright once we met the property's GM, Mr.Avinash Deshmukh. Thanks to him. Even Mr.Krishna Baniya allocated rooms in their new wing (Heritage / Classic room) and took care of us well until Check/out. We are also Thankful to everyone in the restaurant who served us with care . There is a variety in the Breakfast / Dinner buffet spread and they are delicious. especially "Bhara" was very tasty.  We highly recommend this property for the one's who loves Luxury and hospitality . Anyhow Renovation is highly required for the rooms in old wing .

It amazes me the way Hindus and Buddhist can have a legend for almost anything in this country and to make a temple around it!  In the cave is a stalagmite that has been made into a temple to worship as a Shiva lingam which is for fertility.  No photos are allowed of this area.  There are many stairs and at the bottom of the cave you can look through a small opening and see Devi Falls.
This beautiful Rana architecture garden is a great retreat in the heart of the city. With a restaurant and bar and plenty of space to explore

Fascinating to see how popular this cave has become amongst Nepali tourists. There is an impressive spiral staircase down into the depths and you can join people in there tens as they move down to genuflect to the Shiva linga and to look up from the bottom of Devi's Fall. 
I'd suggest missing out on the Cowshed Entrance which is congested with the faithful seeking blessings from a small statue of a cow.

Sorry to say, its beautiful but totally overrated. Its nothing "real" about the place. To go relax somewhere and unwind from the craziness of the city ... you might as well hide in a quiet local cafe, restaurant or the new (awesome!) mall in Thamel.
Amazing place with great spiritual vibe. Lot of small shops and nice restaurants around. Loved it...

The good:  Hotel is clean with good spa service.  My massage was very good and much needed after a long flight and carrying luggage.  The restaurant staff understood that I had a food allergy and directed me to non-offending items that were safe for me to eat.  Breakfast was an immense spread where everyone should find plenty to eat.  There is a mini fridge in the room to keep cold drinks.

The bad:  Rooms are small with poor lighting.  The electricity kept going off, not for long but so many times that it was annoying.  You'd be in the middle of a shower and then it would be completely dark for about a minute before the power came back.  We told the front desk and they seemed surprised and sent maintenance who looked befuddled, did nothing other than listen to our complaint, and then left.  We changed rooms, same thing happened.
I was hoping for more of a botanical garden. Seemed to be more of a place where teenagers went on dates. My friend and I did enjoy photo bombing some people.

This resort/hotel is classified as "5 Star" hotel.  Defiantly not a 5 Star Place.  I would classify it as "3 Star".  Room was average.  Old "Cabin" like rooms.  Shower does not have a door.  When you take a shower, water spills everywhere in the bath room.  Power kept flickering.  Happened at least 4 to 5 times a day. Had Breakfast and Dinner for 2 days.   Limited Breakfast selection.  Dinner food was poor.  Food did not have a taste - very bland.  Food was way over priced.  Service was average.  Hotel grounds were good.  Lots of greenery - Trees and plants.  You need to take a small Canoe from main road to the hotel/resort - across the lake -  short distance - like 100 yards or so.  This is cute and romantic 1st time when you do it.  After that it gets old and annoying.  There is no bridge or walkway from hotel to main road.  If you just want to get out and walk to main road, you need to ring a bell and wait for the Canoe to show up.  Bottom line, for the money, it's not worth it to stay here.  There are other hotels near this one that are better and for less money....
They charge 500 NPR/person for this small garden like arrangement. it took only 10-15 min to cover the garden on foot :).
Food at the bar was great! Attendant Sajja was excellent! She should be promoted anytime soon! Good customer service and genuine smile.
Although the water level was low the falls were still worth the visit.  The walk down to various vantage points gave you a different view each time.
It's hard for one to try remember all the names, which the tour guide was persistent to get us repeating them.
You must visit Devi's Fall if you go to Pokhara. The water fall is really strong, it is surrounded by some shops. It is an attraction for tourists.

my big humanitarian team and I had arrived almost sunset after a week from huge earthquake of April 2015, a lot of people crowded front of reception, but Nepali real smile was attended at the faces of all of the receptionists under all pressers, i think 4 weeks of stay under a pressers can gives you a good justice estimating for all around in hotel, but i don't like to explained all ! old building, nice helpful staff, delicious food, green view (eastern one), but the lobby was far from the entrance,Despite everything, they did not give us a competitive price with we booked almost 12 rooms for a month ( the only most advantage was that it was next to the Humanitarian Operation Center of the earthquake "Nepal Red Cross")..  rooms level and hotel in general status comparing with the price and other 5 stars hotels was over for an old hotel inside of an old public area !..
Fantastic place. Excellent service. Great staff and hospitality. Very good spread of food. Well stocked bar and location. Surendra. Sunita. Tej. Are excellent

The walk down the cave can get slippery but with good footwear and slowly trudging along,it is quite fun. There is a small Mahadev temple and many steps down, can see light through the side of the cave which connects with David fall.
The cave is slippery and risky to go down during the rainy season..Nice cave to see..The temple is poorly maintained but charges quite a lot..

The Garden of Dreams is quite small, and as others have said it doesn't really offer much that you can't find in towns all over the world.

However, I found it a nice break from the business of Kathmandu, especially nearby Thamel.

I thought it was just about worth the entrance fee for a 30 minute visit.
Such a great place to shop tighten art and handicrafts and all! One of the best World Heritage sites of Nepal 🙏🙏

We stayed for one night and found the hotel a nice place to be. The room we had was alrge and the bathroom was clean and had a hairdryer as a bonus. 
It has obviously seen better days, but that seems to add to the charm.
Breakfast was ok (we had early start so not full breakfast available). Staff were friendly.
The only thing that put me off were cockroaches in the bedroom!
Bit of a walk into Thamel area and you take your life in your hands crossing the roads. But embrace the challenge....

Not worth the time and entrance fee to get in. It’s just a waterfall, nothing magnificent and you can complete this in just 10mins.
Place is not properly maintained, there’s plastic waste along the side walk or at the base of the waterfall ...

Stay was very comfortable...Food was amazing...There was availability of variety of food...
Ambience and housekeeping was amazing...
All the services were available whenever needed...Staff is cordial..
Rooms are clean and hygienic

I stayed at the Shanker for a wedding in Decemeber for 2 nights was less than impressed. Although I got a special rate for thr wedding I still found the value to be lacking and could not imagine paying full price.  I stayed at Hotel Tibet prior to moving to the Shaker and preferred that hotel over the Shanker.   I was on the 7th floor (Room 720) and the housekeeping staff would start talking outside my room befinning at 7am each morning and would continue all day long until I called reception to ask them to quiet down. The first day I heard a lot of noise outside my room so I opened the door and saw dog poop outside my room.  I showed housekeeping who was standing outside by door chatting and they apologized at cleaned it up.  But that put a horrible taste in my mouth.  When I asked for room service or an Iron and the staff would come in my room and just start blatenly staring around and had to be ushered out the door. 

I am sure the hotel was once lovely but it has seen better days and needs a refurb.  My bathroom shower leaked and there was a weird smell everywhere.

Stayed for a few days while visiting Nepal.  The hotel grounds are nice.  Staff are great.  They are very helpful and courteous.  The rooms are a good size.

The meals were very good indeed (other than the breakfast).  

Price wise it was not good value,  The rooms are expensive, the drinks were more than double the price of those in the city centre and the internet access is exorbitant.

If you are looking for a quiet place to stay that looks like every other hotel chain in the world then this is a good choice.  There are other places in the city that may be better if you want to experience Kathmandu.
I had really good romantic moments at the Garden of Dreams.  It was such a lovely place which is very close to Thamel. Really a very nice place must-visit for all
it is an average place. water is falling in a gorge. a park is built around the place. greenery is a positive point. it has a big market outside

Beautiful but if u want to sit peacefully, quite difficult.lack.of benches and sitting possibilities.  Crowded with lot of tourists celebrating their selfie mania. Don't just sit in front if one of the kissing couples if u re solo traveller,can be quite depressive.*Joking* Cafe looks fancy,exclusive, didn't made me feel like going there  .at least some sweet squirrels to see.

Very comfortable stay. Very courteous staff. Excellent hospitality. Very beautiful garden with a nice swimming pool. Breakfast has so many items fresh and delicious. Centrally Located. Everything is  nearby like airport markets. Heritage building felt like staying in a palace.
I have been there with my friends.it was good place to visit there because there is an other place to visit & it is on the way to world peace pagoda.

Had a nice day out at Davis fall. Have been there few treats back. Back then the water fall was quite big and when we stand next to the fall we get soaked with water drizzle. But this time the fall is very small. Maybe it’s not the season. Looks dried up. Anyway as is one of the touristic place so had to visit. Was ok nothing special.
Stay in Barahi is amazing and everything is great. Staff are so hospitable friendly. Durga Saha and entire staff are smart and great service
Situated in the Pokhra city , it's a fall situated right opposite to Gupteshwar caves . Not much to see there and the fall is not that big . However one can go just to take a look
Exciting to look at and walk upon. I’m not Buddhist but this is impressive. Saw them painting it for real after watching it on tv.
It’s not in a great place, a bit hard to get there and the roads are pretty bad. But definitely worth a visit! It’s got a lot of so-so restaurants around it. Best at full moon days!

The entrance to this cave is across from the street to Devi's Fall. Devi's Fall empties into this cave and it is an interesting view of watching the water fall from the waterfall above into the bottom of the cave through a narrow crack in the mountain/hill structure.

There is a separate entrance fee to this cave. The authorities have tried to make it like a temple, with a newly built concrete staircase, which leads into the cave. The cave itself has some steps, a cowshed, a deity's altar, a further rough stone path and a flight of iron stairs to the end of the cave. All the stairs, steps and rough paths are wet and dank. Even in the peak of winter, it is quite humid inside the cave. The lighting is poor, but considering it's a cave, it's quite understandable. Do watch your step and tread slowly. 

Right at the end of the cave is a very limited amount of space (about 10 people max) to stand and view the falling water through the gap between the rocks. The cave walls just before the iron stairs have some sort of white mineral deposit of them, which was interesting to see.

visited there with my friends and the casino was huge and mind blowing....... the crowd was not that great but the games were nice.... we all enjoyed the free food and drinks............ the cover charges were 2000 rs..........

Was in town for little over 24 hours. Was greeted at the door by the duty manager upon getting of the hotel car.

The service was OK, but they manage to forget my wake up call. Luckily i had a back up alarm clock. The breakfast was very average but there is definitely room for improvement in this aspect. 

I had tried the Indian restaurant for dinner and the service and food was good. 

Not sure if i would stay here on my next trip around as there are other hotels that i would also like to try.
We visited just after the monsoon season and the water was pretty high.  It's crazy to see it just disappear into the cave system.  Well worth a visit and was included on our Day tour.
The place is extremely clean despite all the tourists around. The staff takes care of the place really well. You feel calm and peaceful.

A huge stupa surrounded by Tibetan monasteries and Thanka school - take your time to visit these as well.  There are many roof-top restaurants to enjoy a coffee or meal and take in the spirituality of the place.

Severely damaged during the earthquake of 2015 but still worth a visit.
It will probably be more impressive when renovations are done.

Hotel Shanker is a well-made choice for location, rooms. and staff-  But isn't equipped with SPA, internet-point (only free wifi)
international call nit possible in room, restaurant poor Menu)

In the heart of the tourist district of Pokhara, the Bahari offers a relaxing haven with splendid rooms, an excellent pool, a host of leisure activities and a decent view of part of the Annapurna range if it's not cloudy. The staff at the front desk were very helpful in dealing with my many requests. The breakfast buffet, though, is only average and acceptable provided you do not arrive with a tour group. You are then subject to endless queuing for eggs - only one chef handling everyone's order - and the toaster machine. Perhaps it was a result of these delays that I left my favourite cashmere scarf in the hotel when I departed after an early breakfast for the airport. Of course, that was my fault, but every attempt to contact the hotel since then has failed. Anxious to get it back at whatever cost, I have twice sent emails via their website - absolutely no reply depsite their promise to reply promptly. I have tried many times to send faxes to their fax number - they do not go through. I have even called several times. The phone is answered, but they can not hear my voice! It is all incredibly frustrating and leaves a rather sour taste after what had been an enjoyable visit.

Nothing special in this average hotel.  Was a fine hotel in past perhaps but generally run down now.  Renovated rooms are nice.  Rooms not renovated are really outdated and in need of repair.  Staff are generally cold, with some nice exceptions.  Food buffet for breakfast is very good and meals otherwise are good also.  Entrance cracked during earthquake taking forever to repair.  Construction on back restaurant veranda where could be very pleasant makes too noisy to use.  Location not great as nothing around.  Gym in basement is minimal and needs updating.  Functions like weddings and receptions seem to keep this place alive and hard to deal with taxis and move around these events when happen.
my stay was very nice, i have a good rest, good breakfast & dinner. thankyou !❤️❤️ excellent service by ms. bhintuna & her friend . recommended🌟🌟🌟🌟

This may be one of the oddest stops I've ever made. It's one they all tell you to go see so since we were out in a cab over that way we went. It's about a poor western woman named Davis that was swept away while bathing in the sixties. Very odd. They say the water was higher at other times. I guess you could go but don't break your back to get there !

Sakshi moktan from reception is a superb host 
Silan is a very helpful boy.  Thankyou for everything, enjoyed my stay throughout

So fresh and clean hotel, delicious breakfast and friendly staff - always ready to help you.
During our time we hade the best driver aand guide ever - many thanks to Indra!

Two nights in this hotel with a tour group. Good breakfast, good location and wonderful views of the mountains at dawn, but oh dear, the bed! The mattress lacked any padding, and there wasn't even an underblanket between the sheet and the rather dirty mattress ticking. The hardest bed we've ever slept (?) on, anywhere. We must have been in the cheapest rooms.

The positive frequency you get by just putting a first step inside makes you feel light on the inside, prayer flags flowing with air can make your pray express from the inside. A must visit pilgrimage place with smiling faces thus closing there eyes, mumbling prayers and chants deep inside feels you are somewhere loved. It's just makes you smile big.

Great location! Avoid the restaurant though. My wife and I had a banana lassi and both got sick afterwards and although we hadn’t left the hotel premises at all that day, hotel staff insisted that it was not their fault (we suspect that the fridge is not powered by a generator which is asking for problems in a country with scheduled power blackouts)

Huge overwhelming structure.Just walked around it.Its surrounded by quaint little shops selling woollens,artefacts,gifts,jewellery,etc. Plenty of cafes aroundwith lovely rooftop seating serving international & nepalese cuisine.Full of tourists & Buddhist monks.

It was a family trip during Xmas time and my daughter was excited with the heritage look of the palace hotel. When read about history, I was overwhelmed to learn that this hotel has been in operation since 1964 by converting then palace, pioneer promoter !!
Upon arrival, we been greeted by the hotel staffs. What a hospitality! 
We been given 2 rooms. Unfortunately the bathroom of one of room was bit congested. Upon request, hotel management arranged the alternative room next day, which was spacious & on top floor with garden view - top score.
My daughter, even got the recently renovated room, lucky her!
Due to family events, we didn't make lunch/dinner at hotel, but we enjoyed the variety of breakfast and unique tastes were exciting. 
I must say great location. it's a very quite place within core city.
It will be unfair, if I forget to mention about the beautiful gardens, well maintained.
The hotel stay nice, I personally grabbed the opportunity to congratulate  owner in person for all the services and excellent management. 
Best value for money, and above all great memory !
Love to stay again !!
a part of pokhara sight seen place (Devi's Fall).nice to see water is going to be down to down.from near by cave(gupteshor madave gufa) nice to see inside cave to view of fall.
magnificent and definitely worth the visit.  we then ate a one of the numerous restaurants around.  great day with perfect view

I would like to thank Ms. Bim Kumari for her prompt assistance with my request to change room. 
She was friend and very helpful. 
Thank you, Bim!

I loved my Stay here!! The property is amazing and hospitality is on point. We had a great experience with Mr. Sudip. He was really kind and sweet to us.

I will highly recommend you all to stay at Soaltee if you are here in Kathmandu. You can never go wrong with your stay at Soaltee Kathmandu.

While I agree the location of this lodge is a bit unique, there is nothing special this place has to offer.

-Good location
-Friendly/helpful staff

Cons:

-Terrible internet connection throughout the hotel.  Nearly dial-up speed in the guestrooms. I stayed at the Barahi for a total of three nights, before and after a trek.  I negotiated a rate more in line with hotels in the area - their rates otherwise are rather high.  
Breakfast was good, rooms were spacious and had balconies.  Cleaning service was good.
A few issues:
1. in my first room the armoir reeked of of mildew.  I brought this to a staff member's attention but the only thing he could do was provide an air freshener, which of course does nothing to solve the problem.
2. I found my single interaction with the concierge desk to be quite unhelpful. I sought a taxi to the World Peace Stupa, a 30 minute taxi ride, at about 5:00 PM.  I was clear that my friend and I wished to go immediately.  The person at the desk informed me of his price (2x the going rate on the street right outside) and failed to inform me that the World Peace Stupa accepts its last visitor at 5:30 PM!  This is the sort of thing you don't expect from a hotel with a concierge desk.
3. Service for lunch is painfully slow unless you order a sandwich.
4. In room internet incurs an extra fee, and on the last day I visited all internet was out most of the day.

THIS place is a peaceful oasis from the noisy bustle and crazy traffic which is Kathmandu.
The gardens are well laid out with several water features, colourful planting, graceful trees and a chance to relax in a little cafe area.
All that said, I still felt I was being discretely drained of as much money as the site could get out of me.
Entry cost R400 or about £2.40. This is not a lot of money but it is still a great deal by local standards for what might politely be called a "compact" garden.
The cafe then adds to the cost. Yes, you can ignore it, but a cool drink on a hot day is difficult to resist and that was another R170 or just over £1.
I didn't begrudge the money but I'm bound to say others sat round me grumbled at the cost which was a pity as I had spent a pleasant half hour walking round the gardens and enjoying a break from the busy merry-go-round of sightseeing in Kathmandu.
Overall I would say that a visit to the Garden of Dreams is worthwhile without being outstanding.
