The room size is decent but the bathrooms are in poor condition with significant stains in the bathtub and sink. The room rate included breakfast. the breakfast is a buffet with choice of cereals, fruits, juices, eggs to order, an Indian vegetarian hot option, breads as well as a small selection of cold cuts and cheese.
The garden and pool at the front of the property are the standouts. the hotel is located close to the popular tourist hangout - Thamel. There are a couple of bars and restaurants just outside the hotel property as well as an ATM.If requesting the hotel to book a taxi to the airport, please insist on a metered taxi to avoid any confusion with the taxi drivers.

Came here thinking you could walk around the place for a while but realized pretty quickly that the garden is very small. The garden itself if very nice and lots of people were there relaxing, reading a book, etc. There is a little building that has pictures of the history of the garden if that's your thing.
Very interestingly built. A massif stupa, many monks make rounds chanting om mane padhme hum and hang praying flags.

The brochures claim this to be a must visit but I would say avoid. There are better caves in India. It's an underground temple but it was wet and dark and you have to pay more if you want to go all the way to Devi falls which was also a disappointment. Save your time and go see the International Mountain Museum instead.

The cave has two sector. The first part did not really have much to see. the second part costs a little more but takes you to the bottom of Devi falls. Very slippery inside. Good experience of a natural cave.
Very easy to get to and is very accessible for tourists. Loved the people and the culture but stay clear of the faithful circling the monument..

It is by far the best attraction at Pokhara barring Lake and Adventure activities..Natural Cave .. One should be normally fit to go through it.. Worth Visiting this place  because it gives you different feel.

When visting the falls, don't be frustrated. There is not much to see, just the water flown away into the grounds. But when leaving this place walk opposite and visit the cave. When going inside the cave to the far end you see the waterfall again from inside. A great view!

The breakfast was amazing and there are many selections. The service was great and Durga got me any food I needed. The hotel was clean and very nice in the inside. The pool was fun and clean. The property is very spacious overall I would give a 4 star because the bathroom door was broken😭

This is a beautiful little gem of an hotel set on the lakeside at Pokhara in Central Nepal.
You get there accross the lake on a little hand pulled ferry which is a cool way to arrive.

The roundhouse restaurant is excellent and serves really good food, a rarity in Pokhara City where I got a bad dose of Salmomella on a previous visit. The views over the lake are beautiful (see my photographs attached).

Staff are friendly and efficient - they are all, I was told, long termers and know how to treat guests.

There are two types of rooms, Heritage and Main Block. I would normally recommend the roundhouse Heritage rooms, where England's Prince Charles apparently stayed once but they are very "tired" and not very large. Its difficult to operate in the bathroom - very small. Also, the Heritage rooms have people walking past day and night so are not very private. I suggest you rather stay in the Main Block rooms which are up to 4 star standard in every way, being well equipped, clean and roomy.

Its quite simply the best place to stay in Pokhara city - I'll go back again.

This waterfall is a bit unique.It has a strong flow, as a result the water has cut through stone and made a channel underground, so the water just disappears, unlike other waterfalls !!
We went in July amidst rains, and the flow was ferocious.
There is a park, some food-stalls and a nice market for souvenirs & handicrafts in front of the fall/

The hotel's location was perfect . It was conveniently situated in the heart of the city, within walking distance of many attractions, restaurants, and shops. This made exploring the area a breeze. I was thoroughly impressed.
A small waterfall you come across as you enter Pokhara by road, quite crowded with tourists during peak time, really not worth the effort though.
Sweet little garden away from the hustle and butle of Kathmandu. I was hoping for a little garden shop/cafe but didnt find any. 400,00 NPR for tourist. Short walking distance from Thamel
Very very nice place to visit with family and friends tour at Boudhanath kathmandu is one of the largest stupa on world.
Blueish water flowing from Fewa Lake in Pokhara falls in cave like place creating an elusive atmosphere. Must visit place in Pokhara!!!
I loved the buddhist culture growing in this place peaceful and breathtaking. I enjoyed shopping in the mini shops got some beautiful beads and thanka arts.

Amazing staff 
Speciallly Staff name Bharat and Sakshi  very nice positive attitude towards customers and well behaved 
Loved to stay here 
Thank you so much for being amazing

The hotel is actually has 3-4 buildings - one of them is newly constructed. The others are old. The rooms are pretty small and the furnishing is old. Even the washrooms are not the same level which you would expect from a 5 star property. The moment you enter the room you would actually feel a little underwhelmed. The only saving grace is the food - the breakfast buffet is good and so is the dinner buffet. The restaurants also have outdoor seating.
For Rs200 entry fee it was just ok. It's a big garden, that's all. In and out in 10 minutes.. not really worth a visit.
I like saying this place patalay chango then devis falls. This time I'm little bit sad about its careless. All the bars are made random and also seeing view is not as before.

Our family group looked forward to staying at Fishtail but it fell short of our expectations. The staff on duty at breakfast and during the day, didn't appear to care and adopted an indifferent attitude. The service was slow, but we first had to find a member of staff which wasn't always easy.

In contrast the service in the evenings was better.

The food was average at best.

I would certainly not recommend this hotel.
Very nature place waterfall surrounded by green. Take more time to go inside the cave, its amazing. Some small shop nearby are interesting, can find some good hand-made things.

The renovated garden is a rather strange park- half green with plants, a couple of European inspired buildings, a restaurant and a small museum; the other half abandoned and in dire need of repair. Not really much to see and I went in as I was in the Thamel area and thought it might be a quiet place with the high walls and all. Unfortunately, inside was noisy and busy as it was full of of locals and tourists- I was there on a Saturday. You pay 200rupees/2$ to enter and will need about 15-20 minutes (maybe less) to get the lay of the land.
After the earthquake the statue is not any longer in place, however you can go around shopping and take some pictures of the images in the bottom of the monument

I have stayed in hotel Shankar last week. I have booked 3 rooms via booking.com and at the time of check in payed tarrif vide 3 cards.
At the time of checkout they told that they are unable to provide 3 bills at that moment and will send the same thru email. But we never got he same and after 3 days when we reached again to the hotel we were surprised that hotel staff was unable to provide the bill again. This is a truly unprofessional and B grade hotel, food is also ordinary. Please avoid.

It is not just the building but the immediate surroundings. The Stupa is a magnificent building and one I am glas I decided to visit, even though we had a limited time in the area. The area surrounding the Stupa is also a very pleasant experience. There are monasteries, shops galore trying to sell artefacts related to the Stupa but not pushy, many prayer wheels and pilgrims using them, lots of people both tourists and residents, and I have never seen so many feral pigeons in one place. An essential visit.

eventhough there many stupas in Kathmandu but each stupa still has its beauty and special part.
strong energy
Love Devis - we went there 10-12 years ago and this time with the kids I did enjoy it ! Watch for the upside down rain ...

Been here a few times already, have my own goal to do kora the second time n was invited to a close friend’s tibetan wedding. June is awfully hot, avoid circulating the stupa between 1030~1500, and there is afternoon thunder rains.

Online photos are deceiving.  Rooms are tiny.  No views. Wifi is lousy in the rooms, nonexistent by the pool.  Pool is nice but poolside restaurant service is pathetic.  Seems like staff are on holiday.  Food....meh...nothing to write home about except expensive for what you get.  Hallways are very dark.  All in all, extremely disappointing as I was hoping for a pleasant 3 day rest after spending several months in the area. My room is so small I'm claustrophobic and can't imagine spending any more time than necessary here.  And I've seen 3 rooms - first one was really dark and didn't smell too good, second was better but didn't have a bathtub.  Only local tv channels it seems.  Going to be a very long 3 days.  I'm not even mentioning the renovations due to the earthquake because that can't be helped and was expected.  Too bad.  I spent a fraction of the cost at a guesthouse in Boudha for a large, airy apartment with kitchen and really friendly staff.  Beds here are better and the AC and pool are nice...but I'm paying about 5 times more with a 50% discount due to renovations.
No need to visit this Garden, it shattered my Dreams, very small Garden and Entry  fee is 250 INR very high, there r many big gardens in India n USA are free

I love visiting Boudhanath Stupa for its grandeur and spiritual energy. The colorful prayer flags and intricate murals are mesmerizing, and the nearby cafes provide a great spot to relax and enjoy the view. It's a must-visit destination in Kathmandu!

I had an excellent stay at Fish tail Lodge. The peaceful lakeside setting is beautiful, and the rooms are clean and comfortable. What made the experience truly memorable was the outstanding hospitality from Prakash, Hasta, and Pradeep. They were kind, attentive, and always ready to help, which made me feel very welcome. I would gladly come back again and highly recommend this place to anyone visiting Pokhara.

The Garden of Dreams Its beauty is unmatched, offering a serene escape from the hustle and bustle of urban life.  it's a convenient retreat for anyone seeking solace amidst nature's splendor. The tranquil ambiance, coupled with its fascinating historic background, adds depth to the experience, making it not just a garden but a journey through time. this garden caters to all. Highly recommended for couples, families, and solo travelers . Don't miss
You will be amazed to see the force of water flowing. There are plenty of stalls selling semi precious stones at reasonable price.

We stayed there with my son for a couple of nights. The food was nice, we both ate with a good appetite.  Another plus is  the swimming pool area. It was quite refreshing to be there. 

But the the rooms I did not like at all, dark and rather small.

Have recently stayed at The Shanker Hotel in March, booked based on TA reviews. As mentioned in previous reviews the outdoor pool/garden area is pleasant to relax away from the Thamel chaos.
The staff are friendly and service overall I would rate as good. However, the breakfast buffet is poor, we walked to the Radission Hotel nearby one morning to avoid eating at the hotel. Room Service dinner one evening was half eaten due to poor quality and a casear salad ordered poolside one lunch left alot to be desired. The rooms are below acceptable - musty, damp smell in the bathroom 24/7; airconditioner does not work properly, beds are the worst I have ever slept on - lumpy & old spring mattresses; our mattress actually sloped on one side. Wardrobe doors didn't slide at all, no minibar, poor lighting, curtains old and didn't close properly - fine if you wished to wake up early.The supposed free wifi - was free it just didn't work 80% of the time. The character and charm of the building ; the warmness of the staff unfortunately is not enough to warrant a repeat visit. Location is good, walk into main Thamel area easily - although no street lights at night - not recommended for solo travellers. The Shanker Hotel does not live up to its potential.
A small town waterfall. Nothing special. Only the story of its name gives some identity to the place.

The staff in the hotel are all very nice. I suggest having a massage from the spa, it is worth your money. I also would like to commend Shriya from the restaurant for being so attentive and friendly. The food can be better, but overall experience is really good. I highly recommend this hotel!

This amazing gorge has been carved in-around-and-under the rock over the millennia. The river plunges into the gorge and disappears into the Gupteshwar Mahadev cave system. Unfortunately both of these awe-inspiring natural phenomenon have been trashed by irresponsible tourists. The “Devi” in Devi’s Falls is actually a corruption of the name of Mrs.Davis, who lost her life when she was swept over the falls and into the caves.

I visited this place as part of a pre-departure cultural tour around Kathmandu; of the three destinations this place has to be the least interesting. The entrance fee is NRP 250 which allows you to take a walk around the stupa etc. The place is surrounded with shops and places to eat so it is good for a bit of a break! If you want to see Buddhist stupa visit India or Sri Lanka where it is much more of a pleasant experience.

Do note: be mindful of the surroundings as there are plenty of scams especially picking pockets; also the local dogs can be violent (as they attacked a person - could be a one off).
Good photo opportunity.The overground version of the river which goes underground in the caves just across the road.

This waterfall goes straight into an underground cave and no one is really sure where the water comes out at. Some locals call in "David's Fall" due to an unconfirmed story about a traveler named David who fell in and was taken away underground by the insane current.

The place clearly is of significance culturally and religiously to Tibetan Buddhists.  It is iconic but has resulted in the entire place becoming overly touristy and commercial.  Then there was the opportunistic gouging of tourists - there was a man seated in the small building just by the entrance to the stupa where there were two giant prayer wheels... he was demanding ‘donations’ in an aggressive from foreigners... asking for Rp.1000 per pax but somehow also ok with Rp.100 when people walked away.  It’s utterly disgraceful that this is allowed to persist in a holy site and where foreigners already paid a hefty legit entry fee.  Feels sad that much of the religiosity and cultural significance is drowned out by tourist kitsch and greed.

Rooms are comfortable and clean, we had no problems with the hot water. Located just off the main road. Staff was friendly and competent. It's a large hotel with little original atmosphere, but the garden is a lovely peaceful place to hang out. Breakfast was great. It's a safe bet if you're staying in Pokhara for a few nights.

The indian restaurant provides nice and authentic food, very delicious.
All the waiters are very friendly and welcoming especially Sambhav is very good and he keeps looking after his guests.
I really recommend this restaurant.
Good job.
The pic u always see of Gupteswar?  The pretty one with sunlight streaming in? You won't get that coa the inner part of the cave is closed. So skip it til it opens. All u see is this. Bummer.

The setting in the lake is beautiful. The approach to it on a punt - atmospheric. Views from the Lodge of the Fish Tail Peak - superb.

Check-in was courteous and efficient - BUT - it was raining and there were no umbrellas in the Reception area (nor indeed in the room).

The room itself - comfortable - BUT:- there was no tea or coffee making equipment (no jug or kettle) available in the room - tea/coffee has to be ordered from room service. Wifi in the bar/lounge area only, was patchy at best.

The room was comfortable but - it smelled strongly of furniture polish or linseed oil. 
During our two night stay we were provided with just one bottle of drinking water (sure, it's readily available for purchase everywhere - BUT!) There is no hairdryer in the room (normal kit in any 4* establishment). Toilet paper was not replaced when the room was serviced - call housekeeping - but it should be routine to check the supply when servicing the room!

Food and service in the Dining Room were quite good. Checkout - OK.

As it was when we were there - a good 3* Resort - but with some 'tuning up' it could be a lovely 4* Resort.

first time  in nepal and what experience at this Hotel. 
1. Could not find reservation with AGODA
2.  I was charged for 3 guests extra even thought the reservation was made for 
2 rooms and 2 guests in each room. Just to begin we arrived on Wednesday. According to reviews 4 stars and I usually stay in 5 stars but I could find on available in Pogkara Nepal.
The city is stunning with friendliness and even at the airport no one attacked you like in Kathmandu. Here everything is slow. You hail for a taxi and it's inexpensive. Arriving at the hotel what a surprise. First they didn't have my reservation and they charged me extra for 3 guests even so the AGODA cleary said 2 guest in each room. Rooms dilapidated and old.
Beds hard as a rock is in bad shape for new matresses. Beds are small and old too. 
Air Conditioner didn't work. 
Moscitos in the rooms. Old bathrooms. Basically the hotel is in need of new management and renovation of the total lodge. View is magnificent...........just spectular.

I will forever remember the hair dryers in this hotel!

I don't know what the options are in Katmandu, but this facility is nice, but not outstanding.  We were here as part of a tour package.  It is located in a large compound and has on site shopping (and the vendors we dealt with were very kind individuals).  Hard to assess the foodservice-had a Chinese style dinner one evening that I didn't much care for, and the breakfasts were good but not great.  Staff really tried hard to accommodate but were either very jaded, and "couldn't be bothered" or on the other hand, really challenged to communicate in English.  The room was medium sized, showed signs of wear, and moderately clean.  And, that hair dryer! It was attached a drawer in the bathroom with a very small amount of cord, so that I had to sit down, and tilt my head over to one side to be able to use it.  It was obvious that someone was trying to please but had no idea how to do it, which pretty much sums up the experience here.

After a couple of days trekking and lodging at night, I hoped a to have a nice retreat in Hotel Barahi. At arrival, the appearance of the hotel was nice. Beautiful garden and even a swimming pool were very promising to have a relaxing time. 
Reception staff was friendly and easy going. 
The rooms have a good size and are clean. Unfortunately, the beds are even too tiny for a 1.73cm European man. I barely fit straight in the bed and the mattress felt like brick. No chance for a relaxing good night sleep. The breakfast was ok, but definitely not worth paying the extra money compared to guest houses.
WiFi should be available, but I had to reconnect and type in user name and password nearly every 20 min.
I booked paragliding with the agent in the hotel. Prices are all fixed in Pokhara for paragliding among all operators so no need or concerns to bargain or to be ripped of. 

bottom line, nice hotel, but not worth spending extra money. I stayed better and cheaper in guest houses around town.

Having stayed in 4 hotels now in Kathmandu, crown plaza is definitely the best. 

However, the best Kathmandu has to offer.  

I could not fault the staff, the breakfast nor the excellent Chinese and Indian restaurants. 

The biggest problem I have is with the rooms. They are clean and functional but all hotels in Kathmandu are very dated and it feels like no investment has taken place for decades. 

However, when I return to Kathmandu which I do about every 2 months, I will definitely go back and stay here. 

You will definitely receive a warm welcome from the second you arrive and staff are well trained to take care of guests from start to finish.

Hotel Shanker is an historic19th-century palace that was once the royal residence of the rulers of Nepal from 1894 until 1964, when it was converted into a luxury hotel (by Nepal standards). The façade of the hotel is stunning (a little earthquake damaged as of this writing), but the interiors are old  and tired. The corridors are actually quite dark! The rooms are hit and miss. We stayed twice, one night on arrival in Kathmandu and another night as we existed. The first night we had an enormous room that in the States would have been a suite. The second time we stayed in a tiny room, barely big enough for two people to move around and not be constantly in each other's way. That said, the hotel did us a great service by letting us check-in at 9am without additional charge. My husband was sick and wanted to lay down in striking distance of a bathroom and they accommodated us immediately. That small room may have been all that was available that early and believe me, we were grateful. That said, if space is important to you, ask that you not be put in the small room (same price as the big ones).

As  I am not such a great follower of Buddhism, so it was okay kind of experience for me. After all it is just another stupa in a large size. But its okay for a visit & I, would suggest 10-15 min stay would be sufficient if you are not Buddhism follower.

I am from Nepal but I must say, I traveled only ones to this place and it was really beautiful but dangerous at the same time. Not much rain so the river wasn't that strong, I am not 100% sure but it didn't feel like it was super strong.

Food and the compound is good as it is 5 stars hotel. Elevator, rooms and amenities are as 2 stars hotel. AC is hard to control. Internet is good. Very friendly helpful staff. Not bad for business travelers.

Its very good experience in Hotel Barahi.
Loved it a lot. We enjoyed a lot. Thank You for this good experience............

Very good property and food. excellent staff and service. Got good discounts with Club Mahindra membership. They even gave us free cake on our last day. Live music at night was a great experience. Old property but very well maintained. Live music at night was a beautiful experience in great weather.

Everytime I visit Pokhara, I do visit Gupteshwor Mahadev, also known as 'A cave beneath the ground.' 
A must visit for Hindus, & not only Hindus, also for those who believes in equality in every religion. Here you can find and feel a sense of relief, & a sense of peace in your inner soul, through Lord Shiva's Blessings.
A must must visit place in Pokhara.
There is nothing to see in this place. The cave is small and crowded. It was as well under construction! It is a waste of time.

The hotel is so famous and I think it’s amongst one of the most expensive accommodations by Phewa Lake, but really don’t think too much of it.
It is interesting to get to the hotel by raft of by boat, the garden is well maintained, the staffs are nice and responsive, but the room is old, and when we got in the room we killed 6 or 7 mosquitoes in 5 minutes. We told the reception on our way out and they took care of it, so we only got to kill another 2 in the evening. Bed is old and squeaky, worst of all is, the hot water supply. It suddenly turned extremely hot Sheila in shower, almost got burnt. Anyway, won’t recommend to my friend or anyone plans to go to Pokhara.

Devi's Fall is a unique look at the local geology with a beautiful little water fall and a really cool cave experience, right in the center of Pokhara. It is really good if you don't have alot of time in country to make it to the larger, more distant sites.

Great experience overall. The service was wonderful. Everyone from the FOH to the concierge to the guards to the bell boys. I was in a wheelchair because of an injury and everyone was more than willing to help out. Thank you Sakar for assisting with getting my food and making sure I could partake in the buffet despite my mobility. I appreciate that.

Gupteswor Gupha (Gupteswor is Hidden & Gupha is Cave in Nepalese) this Hidden Cave were found around 1997 Since than i been able to Explore the cave several times This Is a Famous Sight Seeing spot in recent days , as the cave is Just beside the Devis Falls this is Rather far Better to see the Water falls than from the Devis falls i love walking inside & See All the natural stones too A Most Visit while in Pokhara

Busy square with lots of people. We had a guide who explained some of the detail. Small entrance fee for foreigners (400Npr). Lots of bars and restaurants with a view where you can sit and take in everything
Devi's fall is a must go place in pokhara. Next to it is a huge cave, although if crowded there is a bit of breathing problem in the cave but still one should try to go inside the cave.
Though it is a heritage site but nothing worth to visit except a colony of budhists.  It is located in the citys congested area with road jams, so make sure the time to be consumed for visiting it.
Great ambiance good food with excellent service at fishtail lodge thank you so much fishtail family for your attention and thanks to staff mr krishna lamichhane zenisha sunita bidur and ganga

I really wanted to like this hotel but in current state it’s hard be impressed. The building seems getting a big impact from the last earthquake. There are major works to renovate the main entrance. This is the source of complaint about noise. To be fair, it has to be done. There were some constraints on the dining space as well.

We got the small room that has seen the better days. The bathroom has unpleasant smell. I guess this is because of the ventilation is not proper. The room really needs some refreshing. And overall, with or without impact from earthquake, the hotel could use some refurbishment.

The staff were great. They were also courteous all the time. We took the half board option so we also had dinner there. The food was not bad but not special either. Same applied to breakfast.

I will not recommend this hotel at current state. Things might get better when the renovation works completed.

First realize the hotel is old and is need of some refurbishment.  Some of staff is very personal, while most of staff is cold and distant.  
Pool is not operational,which I can understand this time of year.  Room is in bad state, furniture needs to be replaced along with some of the bathroom facilities, cabinets don't open and door locks don't lock. 
Restaurant for breakfast was horrible and while sitting in my chair it broke and I fell on the ground, the staff saw it happen but nothing was said.  
Chinese restaurant for dinner completely different staff and was optimal in service.   

They brought us snacks in room each night but since they had ants crawling all over we decided to pass on it . Maybe a local hotel delicacy. 

I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

It was a rare  and interesting religious site, located in the midst of shopping area. Though I was extremely tired with pain in my legs, yet I could not resist the temptation of visiting this cave. It was a mix of divine & adventurous experience.
I visited Devis fall.it was an amazing water fall all water going to down step to step.passing though under to Gupteshor cave.

It is a lovely property with  nice sized rooms, mattress that were actually comfortable, a lot of staff to help with anything and a nice little ferry to take you back and forth to mainland which is just across a river. in the morning you get the incredible views of the Annapurnas.

That being said it is priced exponentially higher then any property in town and I don't know that it is worth it.  The restaurant and spa also charge western/high prices for everything.

To get away with being so much more expensive then anything else in town they need to actually offer much better quality then they have to justify it.

It is nice for a treat for 1 night after a trek  to relax and take a good hit shower which is hard to come by in Nepal - but not for anything more then that.
I recommend going to the Garden of Dreams although it is not a must. There are pretty plants and flowers. The food is very good although super expensive. Go if you have time.

I stayed there for a week. it was pleasant, the service was excellent, however i found it pricy.
The room was clean with a nice view over the garden and the pool. The power goes off from time to time however it very normal in Nepal. Internet speed was average.
This is one of the ‘must see’ sights in Pokhara - it only cost 30rupees amd if you happen to be passing by then pop in for 5mins but I guarantee you won’t spend much longer than that!

The cave is more of a gorge with steps taking you deep into the earth. The place is really wet and damp not really suited if you are claustrophobic. Its also not the kind of cave where you can go exploring. Its more of a walk into the earth to a temple and a walk back out.
Amazing UNESCO world heritage site.  Foreigners pay about $4 to get in, a huge bargain for a quality sight.  Friendly shopkeepers and lots of restaurants and coffee shops with views around.

We have visited Gupteswar Gupha on our way up to Peace Pagoda stupa and it is probably worth stopping if you are heading up there but don't expect too much - you won't see much for the money you pay but it is still worth giving a go.
Great hotel with peaceful environment and good service. Very friendly and good staff. There's Korean restaurant inside where delicious food is served. Hotel plus restaurant service.

This is a cave.start with cow temple..then another temple. You need to go down only.its really slippery.all the time water are dropping so floor are weight. You need to more careful specially with kids.my 6 years son was very excited to go he went with me but my wife and another 12 years boy didn't find interest to go down and climb back again. It's better to avoid if you are not fully physically fit and aged people not to go there. After going down we found river end and sun light .It was really nice view.
The service was excellent. Our room was very comfortable and had a great view. The food in the restaurant is excellent. We enjoyed our stay and would return.

A garden in the middle of Kathmandu, It's a nice place to escape the busy and noisy streets. A European style garden with an expensive cafe. Not a must see site but a nice place to chill, entry fee at the door.
Small but lovely garden near Thamel.  Many varieties of blooming flowers and trees.  The gardener was very happy to speak with us about the plants.  Many nice spots for photos.

Brilliant piece of work done by nature. Series of tunnel will lead you towards the bottom of devi's fall. you can experience a presence of different world in there as the landscape inside the cave are totally stunning. 
The only problem is you can't access this gufa in rainy season because of risk of flood. Anytime in summer or no rainy season will do the trick which would make your visit unforgettable.

View is awesome. There are tales abt it. Patalechhango is another view to it.

Its the another point in the beautiful lake city.

Just amazing and exciting majestic view with it. 

Loved it. Loved Nepal and Pokhara...
Beautiful ambience and food quality is good and also the hotel staff is very cooperative..I have visited many times work related reasons, every time I feel very comfortable staying here..

Great food and great ambiance 
Staffs are also very welcoming specially
Krishna lamichhane 
Prakash 
Sunita 
Ganga & sukhad were so friendly ❤️❤️

This huge hotel is one of the oldest in town, but I did not have close a 5 star hotel experience there. The staff are slow and not always helpful, the rooms are old and not so clean, the food is average at best. Plus, the hotel is a drive from the center and with the Kathmandu traffic, moving around can be very stressful. You can get much better quality for the same rate or lower.

The falls in itself are not much to write home about. But they make a wonderfully surreal silhouette at the point where they fall into the Gupteshwar Gupha. Clearly, one of the most memorable places to be, when in Pokhara.

Just completed a three nights stay at this hotel as a delegate to a conference held at the hotel.

The journey from airport to hotel was about half hour, the journey from hotel to airport...on a Sunday morning...took over an hour; through chaotic streets.

The hotel is over a large area. Several well maintained greens. Furniture indicated it was probably constructed in the 80s when heavy wood and brass were much used just hotel furnishings. That's absolutely fine, but very disappointed with housekeeping:
1. My minibar fridge had moulds growing!
2. Cigarette ash and crumbs of food under my bed, very easily visible from the sofa.
3. One of the towels had brown stains.
4. Bed post and table tops were not dusted properly.
5. Don't think top of sofa back had ever been dusted!!
6. Sachets of tea/coffee/sugar in the room were kept in haphazard manner.

I mainly had room service food. Food quality was ok; not much sign of quality, but I got the impression they tried their best with the limited supply of quality ingredients or imported goods.

Boudhanath Stupa is a must-see when visiting Kathmandu. It's one of the largest stupas in the world, and the spiritual energy here is truly mesmerizing. As you walk around the stupa, you can see pilgrims spinning prayer wheels, monks chanting, and people from all over the world taking in the peaceful atmosphere.

The stupa itself is beautiful, with its iconic white dome, eyes of Buddha, and colorful prayer flags fluttering in the wind. I recommend visiting early in the morning or around sunset when the atmosphere is calm, and the stupa is beautifully lit. It’s a great place to meditate, reflect, or simply enjoy the moment.

There are also several rooftop cafes around the area, offering a great view of the stupa while you sip on a cup of tea. You can easily spend a few hours here, soaking in the serenity and exploring the small shops that sell Tibetan artifacts, prayer flags, and souvenirs.

Entrance fee is 400 rupees for foreigners. A magnificent stupa, which is one of the largest spherical stupas in Nepal. There’s lots of restaurants, cafe and shops around the huge stupas. One can spend a good 1-2 hours.

The first time I visited Devi's falls it was right at the height of monsoon (indeed it was raining when we went) and I was amazed!  This MASSIVE flow of water rushing straight at us, and then... POOF!  it disappeared down a big hole.  my friends and I spent some time wandering around for different view points to see where the water went.

The second time I had talked it up so much to some friends they were all buzzed, and then quite disappointed.  We came in May, at the end of the long dry season, and there was barely a trickle of water coming down the canyon (although now I could see the canyon itself, which was also interesting, geologically) and then going down a big black hole.  Interesting, but hardly mind-blowing.  the lack of water also revealed a lot of trash hung up on the rocks and plants surrounding the cave, which definitely took away from the mystique.  For a dry-season cave experience I recommend the Bat cave as my favorite natural attraction near Pokhara (some of the caves are closed during monsoon because of the water levels).

I give Devi's Falls 3 stars as an average for the two visits (excellent in monsoon, average in the dry season).  Bottom line, if you happen to be in Pokhara during Monsoon (June - September) it is worth a visit.

This was our second trip to this incredible stupa. It is the area's number one religious attraction. The stupa complex is one of Nepal's UNESCO designated treasures. The place exudes magnetic magic. Majority of visitors enter for free, but we used the official entrance where the tickets are issued. That seems appropriate for the foreign visitors.
It is fascinating to watch the crowds of devotees, mixed crowd of tourists, locals, monks, everyone walking in the clockwise direction, most in prayerful concentration.
It is recommended to spend some time here. Smell the incense. Observe the customs and people. Enjoy the unique atmosphere. There are many interesting stores and boutiques in the immediate area and four monasteries. Truly a lot to see.
We ate a late lunch in a restaurant with the great view of the stupa.

Was there for a 2 day stay. Tis nice, calm, quiet, safe place with good boundary wall securing the place and hotel zone. Staff are very good and try to help in every way possible. The hotels in the place are well equipped and clean. I could see many marriage functions happening in their hall..so it must be a well trusted place as well here eh ?

Ok now,,they have to fix the walls a bit. I could hear my next door neighbour coughing, meaning he could possible hear me watching tv as well i guess or my alarm ringing. That must have been a convenience. Also the furniture is really old.

They had some shops at the ground floor. Nice, but slightly expensive than outside the hotel. But i guess that is normal of sorts in such place. Has a bar right in front, but i wouldnt know anything cos i wasnt drinking from the place.

Anyways..nice place. Would surely stay there again, possibly when i come to visit with my wife.

Hotel is a bit rundown, but very nice for Kathmandu standards. The pool was great to soak in at the end of a long (dirty) day. It's definitely a historic hotel, so it was nice to have some culture. They front desk staff were relatively friendly. 

If we'd do it again, we'd probably stay in a hotel in the middle of Thamel. They all looked equally as nice and we loved that area. This hotel is close to Thamel, but not in the middle of the madness.

After a very bad experience for my first 5 days in Nepal this hotel turned a bad experience to a good one for me. 
The staff were so friendly, hotel beautiful, bed comfortable, so clean. I only ate in the hotel and the food was amazing. 
If it was not for this hotel I would potentially never return to Nepal. 
Thank you Hotel Shanker for making the last 2 days of my trip in Nepal a great experience.

It was muddy all over the cave and I didn't like this cave. It could be a natural cave but it didn't appear like that.

It was a disappointment as I have been to Batu Caves in Kuala Lumpur.

We have visited a number of Buddhist Stupas including the largest in Yangon, Myanmar. 
Unfortunately this one doesn’t hold a very good second place. Not well kept, very commercial. It comes across as a monument not a religious place. The whole ring around it is full of cheap souvenir shops. It needs cleaning.

We (3 Couples) went to Nepal for a leisurely experience for 5days and 4 Nights. We stayed at Soaltee for 3 Nights, and 1 Night at Nagarkot. Coming back to the Crown Plaza,

1) Check - In : 
It was smooth, but despite informing them beforehand to arrange for better rooms (mountain facing), they gave us back facing rooms on 2nd Floor which had views of a pathetic terrace with generators. 
2) Welcome Drink : 
Pathetic. Which 5* property in this age serve you Lemon and Orange Squashes for welcome drink? At least have some courtesy to serve Juices instead of Squashes after paying 7K INR a night.
3) Rooms : 
As I mentioned earlier, we were given the worst kind of rooms on 2nd floor. Rooms weren't clean. There were hairs all around on the Bed linen and on Washroom floor. Bed was comfortable though. Television wasn't working in one of the rooms which they repaired after complaining. I think they are on a cost cutting spree, as if you want to get the linen changed, you need to leave a placard on the bed. There weren't any Tooth Brushes / Shaving Kits nothing inside on the wash basin. On the next day, after a lot of fight with their duty managers, they changed our rooms to 3rd floor and 5th floor, which had better views and were nicely maintained.
4) Food : 
- Breakfast - Excellent. Had a wide spread from Indian, Continental etc.
- Dinner - Had Dinner at Garden Terrace. Both Food and Service were pathetic. Food, especially the Paneer dishes were stale (which we complained to the chef also). Service was pretty slow.
- Room Service - Was fast, but again the quality of food was bad, looking at the price.
5) Swimming Pool :
It wasn't operational. The reason they cited was maintenance, but after confirming with some other people, it was actually a marriage which forced the shut down of the pool. A engagement ceremony took place besides the pool. The management was actually fooling the people residing to accommodate this function. Frankly speaking, we choose this Hotel because of its Pool, but we really felt bad at the attitude of management at the hotel.
6) Gym / Sauna / Steam Bath :
Excellent. All 3 facilities were nice and properly maintained. The staff at the male Sauna section were great and friendly, but the ladies complained about the behavior of some staff at the Female section.
7) Service / Attitude :
This was the biggest problem with this hotel. Since, its a big property, no single person is responsible for the maintenance. I would especially like to mention the name of their Duty Manager, Mr Deepak, to whom we complained about everything. Instead of helping us, he didn't listen to us, rather was rude and unaccommodating. He didn't even let us meet the senior management, rather said that he's the senior most guy available. 
The service Manager of Garden terrace was good though. 
8) Check Out :
Check was fast and quick.
9) Casino :
Nice and excellent. People present there really helped us understand the games, and kick start.

Overall, its a big property with lots of people staying in their Hotel. Its basically a business hotel, booked mainly by Travel agents. I would highly recommend to converse with them about the rooms, recreational facilities etc before checking in. Our stay at the property was pretty average looking at the price we paid.

Decent and clean but for the money there are better options in Pokhara. The service was good and the bedding and room size adequate, facilities lacking and showers and fixtures very old fashioned, the main issue is the hotel due to the fact that it is all stone floors and old doors is incredibly noisey and residents have a habit of chatting between rooms and banging doors all night as I think the hotel caters to a lot of domestic tourist groups.  It's well located in the middle of town and has free WiFi.

We stayed here for 5 nights and the accommodation is definitely not equivalent to what you would pay for in other countries. Rooms are dated. Wifi is expensive. Breakfast is okay. Staff service is average. I would recommend the Hyatt, which is in the same price range, over Crowne Plaza.
Beautiful waterfall but can't really see it. It is surrounded with tall metal gate for safety measure.
We went on a rainy day. The flow had increased and the fall was in its element. No camera or video can capture the beautiful reality.

I recently had the privilege of visiting The Soaltee Kathmandu with our Hotel Management students, and the experience was truly outstanding. From warm hospitality and friendly staff to top-notch service and delicious food – everything was flawless.
Heartfelt thanks to Mr. Rupesh Shrestha for his dynamic training session. what a phenomenal trainer! His motivation, mentorship, and deep industry insight left a lasting impact on our students. His session helped our students see the true image of the hospitality industry, understand their potential, and inspired them to become future leaders.
As a lecturer, I highly recommend The Soaltee Kathmandu as an ideal learning platform for hospitality students. The visit was not just informative but truly inspiring.

This is the biggest Stupa in Kathmandu and can be considered an entire town by my standards. I went there hoping to experience Buddha though I am a non-believer as in my country there is nothing close to this. 

Indeed this is probably the best-maintained stupa. However, if you do not believe in paying the entrance fee (because it often does not lead to maintenance), walk around to the area where all the public buses congregate (towards Ratna which is the closest public stop to Thamel as Thamel itself is a tourist district and controlled differently)  outside, the locals have a way to enter and exit freely without a gantry. Just follow the locals.

Inside, there are tonnes of restaurants, but most are rated poorly on TA. We went to a decent cafe and indeed, it was overpriced and underwhelming. Inside the Stupa, it is just a place for monks to meditate. Everything is extremely dusty and covered in webs, the only thing that sparkled is probably the gold statues which cannot tarnish. 

If you go there to pray you may get what you ask for, but as a tourist, a few pictures from the outside sufficed. (no photos permitted inside anyway)

Fish Tail Lodge by Annapurna Hotel offers a truly memorable stay in Pokhara. The location is unbeatable—nestled on a peninsula in Phewa Lake, accessible only by a hand-pulled boat, which adds a special charm to the experience.

Rooms are clean, cozy, and thoughtfully designed, with many offering stunning views of the lake and surrounding mountains. Waking up to the sight of the Annapurna range reflected in the water is magical.

The food is excellent—fresh, well-prepared, and with a good variety of local and international options. Whether it's breakfast by the water or dinner under the stars, the dining experience is delightful.

The staff are warm, attentive, and always ready to help with a smile. Their hospitality enhances the overall experience, making you feel genuinely welcome.

Views from the property are breathtaking—especially during sunrise and sunset. The peaceful setting, surrounded by nature, makes it perfect for relaxation or a romantic getaway.

Overall, Fish Tail Lodge combines natural beauty, warm service, and comfort to create a truly special stay. Highly recommended for those seeking tranquility and scenic charm in pokhara.

Good:
*The service was always extremely attentive and polite.

*Bottomless high-quality coffee in the breakfast hall every morning.

Not so good:
*Breakfast buffet was all fairly tasteless even with many options available.
*Standard size room is a bit too small to be really comfortable.
*Somewhat difficult walk to get to where the action is in Thamel.

Overall, a fine place to stay if you are looking for a hotel with some history as well as decent amenities in central Kathmandu.

The Boudhanath Stupa is the largest stupa in Nepal taking up a whole city block and serving as the central drawing card to Boudhanath Durbar Square.  It is a huge edifice festooned with the eyes of Buddha, covered with sprinkled saffron water and draped with Buddhist prayer flags strung together with five colors representing sky (wind), air, water, fire and earth.

While there is a monastery located on the Square, whose monks tend to the Stupa, the real draw is the large array of shops and restaurants located on the outer fringes of the square (it's really a circle). This is a great area for shopping.

If you want to escape the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu for a few minutes The Garden of Dreams is worth a visit. It is not massive or spectacular but it is nonetheless quite charming. There is a cafe / restaurant in which we had tea and coffee and for us the service was pretty good. The garden it self is neat and tidy and there were several water features. The garden buildings are being restored and there are a couple of areas off limits.  Not much of a gardener so I can’t tell you if there are any super rare plants or not but what was there looked good to me.

I booked a 3 night stay at this hotel as a treat following a 12 day trek in the mountains. I ended up only staying 2 nights due to a slight change in travel plans, but 2 nights was fine enough for me. 
My positives:
*the pool area is lovely to hang out at after dealing with the chaos of Thamel. The bar makes awesome mojitos and the Dragon Chicken is delish
*I was upgraded to a suite which was huge. The king bed was comfy, the sheets were clean and crisp, and the a/c plus 24 hour room service was great!
*much of the staff, especially the doormen, bellhops and waiters, were very friendly
My negatives:
*I found the a lot of the staff stood around and waited for tips, even when it was obvious I was not intending to tip. (the guy who brought the fruit and chocolates to my room was the worst. This is a welcome gift and to expect a tip for bringing it was ridiculous) I stay in beautiful hotels all over the world and rarely run into this behavior anymore. I'm a generous tipper, but it's the service that dictates the tip, not the fact that you showed up for work! I found this rather tedious during my stay. Plus, what's that 10% "service charge" I paid for on every single bill??

*After dealing with super friendly people for the 3 weeks prior, I have to say that most of the Front Desk staff was borderline rude. I'm sure they deal with jerks all day long but I wasn't one of them and was very surprised when my friendliness was not reciprocated. 

I stayed in 3 mid-range hotels in Thamel and honestly, I preferred those to the Shanker. I would only recommend the Shanker a) if you really don't want to stay in Thamel, and b) for the sheer lazy pleasure of hanging out by the pool.

It looks like it's made on the top floor of someone's mansion. Cheap dance happening at the backdrop. And not even the kind of cheap that gets you excited! Really sleazy.
Casino was okay, but because of the sleazy dance, my experience got ruined.

during my stay was shocked to receive such a treatment from the front office staff, and the food and beverage department is just awful. ordered for goan fish curry and found the fish was not fresh, was really disappointed with my experience.

This is one of the world's largest spherical stupas. Walked around in a clockwork direction and take in the atmosphere created by the burning incense, chanting and fluttering Buddhist flags. Don't forget to spin the prayer wheels.

Sadly that's no longer the case. But wait, there's more....

The hotel indeed has charm and the makings of its former glory. I suspect it needs a manager that has experience in western hotels to bring it back. The staff try, and some even try hard but like most things in this part of the world... They miss the mark.

That all being said, we enjoyed our stay here. It's far away from the Hustle and bustle of the street. That's a positive and a negative. If you decide you don't want to eat at the hotel restaurant, you'll have a 5-10 minute walk minimum to an alternative. The hotel restaurants food was surprisingly amazing. Well the Indian fare at least. Food prices were reasonable for Nepalese rupee. Service could be better, but they try.

The second issue - clean the chandelier above the restaurant entrance. It's disugstingly dusty. Fishtail Lodge markets itself as a top range hotel/resort offering the best views of the lake and Annapurna range in Pokhara. Three standard rooms are marked as having special views and are sold at a premium - we stayed in one of these (Room 16) on our honeymoon. The room normally has two single beds and although the offer was made to push the beds together, we said that we would prefer not take the room. The hotel then promised to put in a double bed for us as we were staying for four nights. We booked on that basis. On arrival, the room had two single beds pushed together. We asked for the double bed to be put in but this didn't happen.

The room promised unobstructed views. In reality, there is a grass area in front of the rooms that is open to all hotel guests with chairs and hammocks. We found our views were often of other guests  relaxing or taking photographs of the view or each other. Some guests seemed to enjoy peering in our windows too - when they weren't climbing through the flowerbeds to get better camera angles. The area in front of our rooms also seemed to be a social club for hotel staff to come and chat (shout to one another) or have conversations on their mobile phones. This also spoilt the tranquility somewhat. 

The restaurant served very expensive food that was really pretty grotty. Mostly bland international fare - even the Nepali dishes were bad. One, for example, turned out to be fish and chips despite an exotic description. The breakfast buffet was exorbitant, especially when the only food taken were a couple of slices of bread and some undercooked potatoes. There is no atmosphere in the restaurant either, with the only diners seeming to be large tour parties on corporate rates. This is a missed opportunity as the views from the restaurant were great. But better to eat in town.

Oh, and the wonderful view was mostly obscured by clouds - don't bank on being able to see the mountains. 

All in all, this is probably the best hotel in a town where most offerings are loud and garish. But it is still not quite hitting the spot, despite charging top dollar Western prices.

Stayed for 3 nights in early Nov 2011.

Location: About 20-25 mins away from Durbar Sq etc., but not too bad. Easy to get to/from to tour.

Hotel: Gorgeous hotel and grounds. Well kept, clean and fantastic staff. Very friendly and helpful. 

Room: Clean, comfortable and large. Great for business and leisure travellers. 

Breakfast: Great breakfast. Great selection and quality of food. 

Internet: I didn't try it, because it was incredibly expensive. It worked out to about $12 CAD for 1 hour. Crazy! 

There were only 2 negatives during my stay:

Cockroach: Last day at breakfast (buffet held in the China garden Restaurant), there was a cockroach on the wall by the ceiling. I understand that the environment/city is prone, so that wasn't the biggest issue (but was a little gross in a restaurant). The waiter swatted it very dramatically off the wall with a towel to the ground and just left it there. It was on it's back still wiggling it's legs. I totally lost my appetite at that point. I waited to catch a waiter's eye to mention the roach was still alive, but before I could - another staff member scooped it up and threw it out in a napkin. 
I appreciate the attempted killing of the cockroach, but I thought leaving it still alive (or dead for that matter) on the floor was incredibly poor.

Indian Restaurant: We ate at the Indian restaurant our first night. The food was good and well priced - so no issue with the food. It was the wait-staff that I found fault with. I appreciate attentive wait staff, but not staff who hover while you eat the entire meal. For every bite I took, the waiter would step in and try and fill the void on my plate. I appreciate the service they are going for - but it was a bit too much. We could barely have a conversation without someone approaching the table and doing something. They also would start clearing the table while others were still eating, which was annoying. 
The bigger issue was the service charge. I am used to this, and I think it's a great way to build in a tip so people don't short-change the staff. However, when we paid the bill, it included the service charge of 10%. When we paid, the waiter showed it to another waiter (who gave us a dissaproving look) and then to the head waiter, who also gave us a look of displeasure. I thought at that point, that the service charge meant something else in Nepal so we asked and the staff said that no, it was NOT the tip or service charge...that it was a 'tax'. We tipped 15%. 
Out of curiosity the next morning, we asked at the front desk if the service charge was infact the tip/service charge (and showed them the bill) - and they said yes, most definitely!!! They said there was no way we should have been told it was a tax. Basically, the wait staff took advantage of 'new forigners' and ended up with a 25% tip. Not impressed at all.

I would go back to the hotel, as it was fantastic, but I would not eat at their Indian Restaurant again.

This hotel has been my home for the last 2 months, and it's a toss up between the fantastic staff and the great buffet (breakfast and dinner) as to its best asset (and I don't even usually like buffets). The wide selection of Indian and Nepali food was fantastic. For a while I loved the pool, but earthquake damage put this out of action for most of my time there which was too bad because it was beautiful and clean. Whilst there were many aftershocks in Kathmandu the hotel appeared to 'stand up' to these without adverse effects. 

On the downside, the hotel only has one non smoking floor and doesn't seem to be able to stop people smoking even on this floor. Current building works start at 6.00 am(!!!). And it's not the best location/proximity to Thamel and Patan areas. However taxis are cheap and plentiful (best to walk to the street outside for cheaper rates.) Spa is good in terms of service, but just functional in terms of decor/atmosphere (i also felt a bit nervous being on the basement during a period of many aftershocks).

When we were asked by people at Kathmandu where we were going to stay for two nights at
Pokhara and we replied that it would be at The Fishtail Lodge, they said that we'll be staying at
a very fine property and one of the best in pokhara. Once featured in the book 1000 places to
visit before you die, this picturesque resort managed by the Annapurna hotel was once the prime
vacation spot for famous people including Prince Charles. Thus with high hopes we proceed to
FTL.
Getting to the resort is actually fun and gets you into the mood of staying with nature. You
require a boat or a raft to get from the roadside to the resort as we have to cross a part of the
gorgeous phewa lake. The staff manning the rafts were very friendly people. The raft service is
available 24×7 as that is the only way to reach the resort.
The only downside to this setup is that during the rains there is a good chance that some of your
luggage may get slightly wet as was our case. But the staff were really careful.
The resort itself is breathtaking and beautiful. Since it is literally in the lake, you get a
wonderful view of the Himalayas beyond it. However since we visited during the monsoon season
we could only see some distant hills due to the low clouds. Nonetheless, it was still beautiful.
It's quite, secluded and peaceful. The resort is laid out in the form of many cottages with each
cottage having a couple of rooms. The main building had the lobby and the restaurant called The
Circle which also has a bar. The lobby had a board with pictures of all the celebrity who have
stayed here. We were checked in quickly and taken to our two rooms which were attached.
This is where the resort started disappointing us. The rooms at one glance were clean enough
and in good shape although a bit small. But the lack of maintenance supervision showed as we
started using the rooms. To say the least, they were in a very bad state. To start with, one
bulb in each of the rooms weren't working. This room had severe lack of lighting when it's the
evening and the handful of warm bulbs don't actually brighten up the room much. Add to that
broken bulbs, then it was almost hard to read books. There were no table lamps or bedside lamps
either which, to be honest, is very poor for a resort that is said to be the best at Pokhara. The
windows couldn't lock properly as the locks were bent and deformed. The TV reception was poor
and seeing the TV properly was almost impossible. The cables and even the receiver were just
hanging out of the TV with no support. The numbers on the keypad on the phone were almost
completely wiped out and barely visible. It shows that the phone is very old and hasn't been
properly maintained. The coasters for the cup were very filthy and stained. The cups were also
dirty and we had to clean one ourselves. The slippers provided in the room in our cupboard was
used as there was sand on it. These may be small things but they show how badly kept this place
is. No wonder the amount of celebrities visiting this place lately has been less. The photos have
been attached below.
After keeping our bags in the room, we went to the restaurant to have some snacks as we
hadn't eaten anything since morning at it was about 4. Since it was rainy they provided umbrellas
for us to walk to the restaurant. The restaurant was cozy and warm with a fire place at the
centre. There was also a large screen showing the cricket world cup matches. It also has a bar.
The main dining area is further down with views of the beautiful phewa lake. Outdoor seating
is also available. Our server showed us to our table and presented the high tea menu and the all
day dining limited menu. We ordered a plate of veg pakoras, grilled veg sandwich, grilled cheese
sandwich and some hot and sour soup. The food was excellent. Really good quality and tasty with
a sizeable quantity.

We left for our rooms and after refreshing ourselves and resting for a while we went to have
dinner back to the restaurant. Again, we were shown to our seats and given the dinner menu.
We had some Indian dinner which was also great. The one slight complaint that I felt was that
the restaurant staff, although they were extremely friendly, weren't polished.
Breakfast the next day, was in the form of a buffet having various Indian, Chinese and
Continental options. Everything was great except the sambhar which didn't even taste like
sambhar. Otherwise the spread was big and really good.
After breakfast we went for the city tour of Pokhara and came back before dinner. We had light
dinner of various snacks as we were full from the late and heavy lunch. Again, the food was
good.
The next morning we explored a bit around the resort as the rains had stopped. The resort
as I mentioned above was beautiful and it also has a pool. We went for breakfast but was
disappointed that there was no buffet due to the lack of customers there. Instead we could
order food in an à la carte format. The selection was huge and maybe even more than the buffet.
We had a little of everything in the Indian selection and some noodles. All of it was good, except
the sambhar. We ordered a bottle of water to drink because we don't prefer the normal water.
As we were about to leave the restaurant we were presented with a bill. I was confused because
the breakfast was complimentary. When I checked the bill, I found out that they charged me
for the water bottle! Usually at buffet breakfasts bottled water is complimentary. Never have
I been charged extra for mineral water for a buffet anywhere where I've stayed across the
world. I don't mind paying for it, and I did because that may be the policy here (but I'd argue that
it is a very weird one). They could've atleast told us that it was chargeable when we ordered it
instead of surprising us with a bill in the end! That was very unprofessional.
We went back to our rooms to pack as we were checking out that morning. Before we went we
called the manager and showed him all the problems in the room. He took it well and accepted it
as positive criticism. He said he was sorry and that it was unacceptable that the rooms were
in this state. He was very friendly. I appreciate the time he took to hear me out and to accept
their mistakes. I've had many instances at other places where such criticism wasn't taken well,
but the manager was extremely professional.
Upon departure, the hotel staff presented us with some souvenir. They gave the women a
handmade pouch with some jewellery and the they gave the men the traditional hat.
The only reason I gave this place 2 stars is mainly because of the friendly staff and the good
food. The rooms were horrible.
I also stayed at the Annapurna Hotel at Kathmandu and I found that this lodge had identical
problems. The rooms were poor but the staff and food were excellent. So is this because of a
lack of supervision by the officials at the Annapurna group? Maybe. But whatever is the case the
renovation and maintenance of the rooms are well overdue.
I do not recommend staying here from my experience.

Known as Nepal’s most famous cave, it is located just across the street from Devi’s Falls. Said to be discovered in the 16th century, it may be the longest cave in Nepal at 9600 feet (2950 m). The cave is venerated for its huge stalagmite worshipped as a Shiva lingam. To enter the cave, you’ll pass through a shopping arcade and then down a spiral staircase lined with carvings and statues. Things go downhill (literally) after that. The inside of the cave is damp from the continual dripping of water. The floor is wet and slippery; thankfully there are handrails down the steps. While the cave has lighting, have you own light handy just in case. You’ll need to watch your head in several tight places. If you’re claustrophobic, this is not for you. Eventually you’ll find yourself in a damp cavern. A sliver in the rocks provides a view of Devi’s Falls (5 stars)! Overall, the experience didn’t feel safe and I was anxious to get out of the cave (1 star). The water from the falls forms an underground tunnel, under (or around) and though the cave. During monsoon season this part of the cave may be closed.
