Not up to the promise. They forced me to buy tickets for the program on 31st December. We the entire family did not enjoy the program because that was not of our type. Though they charges NRS 3500 per ticket, the drinks were very expensive.

The caves are located around 30-40 metres underground. There is a Mahadev temple once you get down around 50 steps. The caves are moist and damp and not well lit. You need to carry a small torch to see things and click pictures. The end of the cave is where the water from Devi's Fall is seen. The Cave gives you a feeling from Movie " Journey to the Centre of the Earth". Not bad. But it will fatigue if you are not used to physical activity.

There are not many things to do in Pokhara, but Gupteswar Gupha is one place you have to see in Pokhara. The cave is not very far from the lake/ city. It is just past the airport. There is a small temple in the cave and a long winding wet and moist staircase takes you to the narrow crack from where the water from Devi's falls empties into the cave.

My second time here. You get treated really well from when you arrive to when you check out. The staff are very nice and always greet you whenever you walk by them which says a lot about their great hospitality. Rooms are pretty big with a comfy king size bed.

Food at The Patio restaurant had great ambience and the staff were so attentive and polite (Ms Sajja and Mr Sujal who served me for lunch) and they packed my leftover pizza and Belgian Fries for room service because I was stuffed. 

Overall great experience.
It was a good place to visit but not that great a fall. I heard that it's a great to see this fall in rainy season. You can spend at max 10 15 mins here.

Had visited this waterfall in Pokhara a long back ago. This waterfall is visited by locals as well as foreign tourists and is a popular tourist attraction.

This extraordinary waterfall was named after a Swiss tourist, Davi who drowned in this waterfall in 1961. It is known by the locals as 'Patale Chhango' or underworld waterfall. It is one of the most visited places in Nepal. Before entering the waterfall, there is a garden having a replica of the Himalayan mountain ranges, a wishing pool, a small Buddha statue, a replica of Nepali huts etc. The source of this waterfall comes from the Phewa lake dam. It was nice to see the gushing waterfall. There are railings to protect children from falling into the falls. Outside the complex, there are shops selling handicrafts, clothes etc. The entry fee is a small fee. One can visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave located close by.

This waterfall is an ideal place for families, couples as well as friends. It is s must visit place and should not be missed while in Pokhara.

We were here at an important religious time and saw Monks performing a ceremony. It was worth a visit, but I don't think it stands out on its own so try to make it part of a day's worth of activities...

If you went trekking and saw a waterfall up close, please, don't pay for this, and don't even bother wasting time and money travelling to this attraction. This must be the biggest rip-off waterfall I have visited in my life.

If you have a day not knowing what to do, better to visit for the cultural and heritage experience than sitting in the hotel. same for the cave across the road.

Our stay in hotel brahi Pokhara will be unforgettable, the hotel is unique, exceptional in location, staff, food, services, cleanliness, and the overall atmosphere, we really enjoyed every moment spent in the hotel.
The cheerful, friendly, helpful  staff in every corner of the hotel    is the common  feature all the time.

Whilst visiting the shrines and seeing the cave was very special, the presence of litter remains a huge disappointment. I understand that the waterfal may deliver washed up litter but can't people be employed to remove it.
Why are there no litter bins along the passage ways and why must people drop their wrappings, water bottles and tissues!
This is a place of beauty and spirituality, respect it please.

You get an opportunity to see the wonder of nature. The water falls down at great speed in good quantity. Once it falls, it disappears into the ground (underground natural tunnel). Walk through the cave to have the real picture of vanishing water after fall.

No matter weather you are a Buddhist or not, this worldly known place must not be missed from your list of sightseeing! 
It is an icon of Nepal, n a great sacred place for Buddhists! 
There are restaurants, shops, coffee place, surround it! People pray and walk around the stupa in chatting! 
This is first recovery landmark after the great quake, which also signify its importance of being!

We walked here from Thamel on our first morning on the way to Durbhar Square.  Yes you have to pay 400 NPR pp but it is quiet,  calm and full of interesting architecture water features and planting. 
Disappointing that the Kaiser cafe was out of business,  just a jumble of chairs. 
Kathmandu needs more spaces like this, we have found little garden cafes to help get away from the noise/air pollution of the roads.

The hotel,  has great amenities. 
Staff is always there for you and your help . 
Cleaning is one of their priority. 
You have the opportunity to try local and international dishes.

In Nepalese language "Patale Chhango" means underground waterfall. It is aptly called so because its water mysteriously vanishes underground. It reportedly goes in the Gupteshwar Mahadeo cave which is also quite deep down under nearby.
The waterfall has three levels and the tourism department of Nepal has constructed good steps, galleries and bridges to view its glory. The wate to this fall comes from Phewa lake overflow.
We visited the fall in April and hence the fall was thinner. But it must be great view just after the monsoon.
I also spotted a pair bird called Blue whistling thrush near the waterfall.

You can just walk here from Pokhara city central. There are some shops nearby and you can enjoy some street food too.

The fall is beautiful. There are platforms where you can stand and enjoy the view. The tickets cost 20 Rupees i think.

Manish was very helpful and patient with us great service and very friendly with us i would definitely recommend to go back to the restaurant due to the good service 
Always good to have nice people taking care of you we were group of friends and he took our order without any mistake keep up the good work 🙏
Well run, clean and just beautiful to behold. Don't forget to cross the road and see where the falls end up
Unique adventure, bit of a steep, slippery walk. But worth the trip for seeing once. Pretty dark. Advisable to carry a torch. Older people need to be careful. Hold hands of children below 10.
This is one of the largest and most impressive stupas in kathmandu and whilst i was there colour was being added to the dome so it was quite spectacular.

We went to this cave as we supposed to see Devi's fall from the side (as some photos shows) but we were so disappointed that the part was closed for security reasons (as is monsoon season I suppose). No notice about closure. What's the point of visiting if the main attraction is closed? Ticket wasted... Don't go!

It starts of just as any other cave of tourist interest. And at that moment you would feel its not any great especially if you have seen other caves like the ones in Jagdalpur, chattisgarh , and Araku, Andra Pradesh - Both in India. 

Do get the tickets done till the end of the cave. There are two kind of tickets: one costs 30rs and allows you to go till a temple inside the cave, and on the way you see a cow cave which is actually artificially built. But, till this temple its pretty boring, and you should definitely get the 100rs Ticket for the entire tour of the cave where at the end of the (destined pathway) you get to see the gushing waters from Davi's falls going regally underground.

Its a lovely property with sprawling greenery around it. Fabulous entrance and serene sitting area just before the main lobby. Lovely to just unwind. Superb Chinese restaurant, China Garden, with excellent staff, great food. Went out of their way to cater to our special requests and suggest variations. Kakori, Indian restaurant was good too. Breakfast spread could be better. As for the hotel service, unfortunately disappointed. The front office staff needs to be more receptive and warm. They could just not handle the crowd and appeared lost. And most disappointing was we actually had someone try to enter our room at night. Room service and housekeeping disappointing, could not cater to the  needs. Paid WiFi that was not great at all. For IHG standards, disappointing service levels.

Mr.Samridha and Mr. Rujal service from patio were beyond the expectation. Their service made me feel very pleasant and comfortable. And chef kesav gaire prepared me a very delicious food which was really amazing. Also the ambience of the restaurant was peaceful. Due to that reason I would like to visit this restaurant again and again in the future. 
At last I would like to thank all staff for such a memorable experience.

Small water fall coming down from zig zag path and converging to one channel. Nice place to see and spend some time. In this period of time, water was not more. May be during rainy season, fall would be in full swing.

Good condition American brand hotel in this town. The day of our visit,  they have international investment conference or attendees of that conference staying at this hotel. Tents are also added in the garden for a wedding or banquet. There are three restaurants on site: Indian, Chinese and a American buffet type casual dining. I think it is perhaps one of the better venues in town for parties.
The most Beautiful places in Kathmandu!! Mighty stupa is Surroundings by shops, hotels, cafes & business. Very rich for spiritual energy ❤️❤️

Located 4 kms from Pokhara city and opposite to Gupteshwar Mahadev cave. A vary beautiful water body situated here. After death of swiss couple, Patale Chango named devis fall. This is a must see place for tourist.

a nice experiance, a shiva temple in the cave... However, this looks as if there has been a lot of human intervension that has taken away the natural beauty & originality of the cave temple. However, good to visit looking at it's religious significance.
Davis fall is not so big water fall but science you are in pokhara this is one of the best fall where I recommend to visit 😈😈😈
The entrance was only 250 npr. What is cheap if you compare to other temples. But for me, it wasn't really special. It is just a nice stupa

Incredible place to spend a few hours. Once you’ve had a walk round just grab a seat and watch the world pass by. Or, try a bit of retail therapy. You can buy almost anything at the hundreds of small shops that circle the Stupa. Visit the temple or just find a rooftop for coffee or something stronger. Well worth a visit.
This is a lovely little spot. It is best seen with a guide. My guide explained the history of the falls very interesting,

As a member of its Signature Card Program, my recent experience at the Soaltee Hotel was a symphony of a perfect human touch and modern luxury. Each moment unfolded like a well-composed melody: I found a quiet charm of architecture, the soft hum of hospitality, and the thoughtful touch of refinement in every moment!
Starting from the information I got from Mr. Shreejan Sharma, the gentleman leading The Signature Card program, I had a feeling more like an invitation into a world of balance and beauty, leading to the soothing calm of the spa, and the serene expanse of the pool, and the Chocolate Cake along with every experience from rooms to the restaurants carry The Soaltee’s timeless promise of care and excellence.
To those who seek a space where elegance meets authenticity, this is where the heart feels at home. I await the day when the Heritage Club members will meet at a networking event, when conversations flow like music among those who share an appreciation for legacy, luxury, and connection. Keep shining, Soaltee!

-Dr. Kashiraj Pandey, Kathmandu
This was an alright place to visit. There is not much to see here so you can do it in a fairly quick visit.

Entrance into the cave is 100 rupees.  The outside is interesting with a winding staircase.

Once you get inside, you walk less than 10 minutes and you will see the bottom of Devi Falls.  Some of the areas in the cave is wet.

This was an ok attraction.  Nothing really special.  The max you will spend here is 30 minutes.
We were here in December, which means there is not a lot of water, so not much of a waterfall. The environment is uninspiring.

Very pleasant stay, lovely service and helpful staff. Excellent restaurants with a very good selection of food. Highly recommend the spa. Also the bar with the exceptional service, high praises to Sashika and the rest of the staff. Thanks for a great experience.
ok if you like history otherwise it's good time enjoying my overall visit for it was a honey moon so we both enjoyed there where ever we went we like it

I don't normally write reviews, but I have to say I was offended by this hotel.  We arrived from Kathmandu after an 8 hour bus journey, expecting to be picked up at the bus stop.  When no one from the hotel appeared, and after standing around in the hot sun, we took a cab to the hotel.  The reception was less than apologetic, explaining simply that they had car problems.  Huh?  They had our cell phone and could not have organized a taxi to pick us up.

The rooms in this hotel have not been upgraded for a long time, and are dingey.  The bathrooms in particular show their age.  We had no towels and waited 4 hours to receive them.  The breakfast buffet was chaotic and the waiters seemed poorly trained.  

For the price, this hotel was a major disappointment.  We looked around and found the Temple Tree, a newer hotel with far better service, food, and much much nicer rooms for a slightly higher price.   The Bahari is well located in Pokhara and seems to be depending on this for a brisk business.   Location was not matched by service or quality.

I stayed here as part of Friendly Planet's Taj Mahal Express tour with Nepal extension. This hotel has a good location and beautiful grounds, but inside was outdated. From the hotel, we were able to walk to some local shops safely without a problem. The row of shops inside the gate to the property, but outside of the actual hotel had wonderful deals and helpful shopkeepers. Even after I spent the very last of my Nepalese Rupees (having negotiated a deal where I agreed to pay him all that I had to just get rid of the currency) he returned a bill to me as a souvenir and proudly showed me his currency collection under glass at the counter and proceeded to also give me a singing bowl demonstration without pressuring me to buy one. There is also a casino on site. It was definitely not "hopping" with people, but we just played at our own table and had the opportunity to talk to the locals working there. It was a nice way to spend a low key evening on a hectic sightseeing vacation. The rooms were dark and dreary and prone to power outages. Also, it looks like there had at one time been a fridge or minibar in the room that was removed, and not carefully. There are several dining options in the hotel, and the food was decent, but several items on the menu were not available. Breakfast was a nice spread and the morning we did the Everest flight we would have missed breakfast but our guide called ahead and the hotel kept it open for us which was a nice touch. The pool area is lovely and was a nice place to spend the morning before the flight home. This hotel has the potential if it updated its interior, but our tour guide did mention that Friendly Planet was no longer going to use this hotel as either a Hyatt or a Hilton had recently been updated.

Big rooms - with small height. Still have a palace like feeling. But in evening - they don't put on the out side lights; else could be a better view.

Average food - 

I should mention an incident - the gatekeeper was greeting and saluting only WHITE people - not Indians.
Not a very good trip but probably worth popping your head in. View of the falls are limited and ruined by the large green bars infront of the falls.

The property itself is 125 years old.  However the toilets are soooo small. The Wash basin hardly has enough space for a person to fit. The size of the rooms (414 and  417)  is too small for the price charged. Non of the toilet doors were working. It is difficult to turn the knob to open or close them.

Worth a visit to give an insight into the religious culture of the city. Colourful and noisy. Obviously a huge favourite with the Nepalese as well. Many shops surrounding this stupa for quick souvenirs. 

There was no harassment to speak of. Lovely visit.

Imagine parking in front of a retail store in downtown Kathmandu and finding out you are at Devi Falls.  A passageway through lots of vendors leads to an overbuilt concrete plaza with more tacky shops.  Nothing natural to be seen.  Everyone heads to the right where you can see a small falls, but the heavy fencing keeps you from getting any view of the "hole in the earth" that it falls into.  Cannot see anything.  Crowded and not worth the visit.  AND you pay for this too.  Skip it.

The fall's ain't that high but i disovered the formations that have taken place due to the direction and force of the water flow. There was a baby dam and beautiful creases created by the water flow for years. It sure was an interesting experience
The service was very nice. I had a good sleep in my comfortable bed. Even the facilities has fulfill my satisfaction. The food all delicious -Dilkumari over it was good  in the hotel
Go to the monkey temple instead. Monks are visible but inaccessible. Not worth the money. Only good thing is Pashupatinath gnats are close by.
Devi fall is highly over hyped up but can go if you have time. There is a wishing pot where u can wish. I would avoid completely.

the price was very expensive.... not a star standard at all!!! there were so many cockroaches on the floor!!!! lost my cloth from the room and tried to find out but couldnt get any liable response!!!! not a customer focused hotel!!! Just money oriented!!!!breakfast was absolutely crap!!! will never ever go there again because i really had a very bad experience in terms of getting service at its best !!!!

The caves primary are a point of attraction from importance for Hindu religion. It is a temple for Lord Shiv. However, that is only a part of it. The caves themselves present awesome glimpse into nature and its power. You go deep into the caves amidst low roofed tunnels and arching slopes. It is no less than a hike, And at the end of it you get to see marvelous view of the Devi falls in backdrop through cracks among the rocks.

Interesting to see hindu shrines in a cave. The view of the falls is very limited. The lack of safety in the cave is scary particularly if you are not steady on your feet, tall or a little wider than average. A torch or a cell phone with light will help. Not sure how to score this cave between average and poor. Shops outside are a little more interesting.

I have booked Hotel Barahi through Agoda. I had a terrible stay there. Staffs are always confused. I mentioned in agoda to provide me high floor with swimming pool view. They provided me a room where AC was not working so we had to move out to a corner room with no view. We mainly booked this hotel for swimming pool but could not use it because lack knowledge of the staffs. When I asked at the reception about the swimming costume they said they do no rent or sell any costume and I have to wear polyster material . At noon when I wanted to use pool with costume I have. The staff over there suddenly said I can not use pool with costume I am wearing though I was wearing polyster. In reception they could not reply anything when I asked about it. A lady at the reception utterly useless who does not know anything other than saying manager knows. It was utterly disrespectful that I was all wet had to stand there and they were not helping us. After 30 mins they said they have costumes which I have to buy which was outrageous because I already bought my costume. Hence I could not use pool. Then again next morning when we had to go for breakfast my husband asked the reception that we were supposed to get breakfast coupon which we did not get. They as usual clueless and said they will let us know but it was almost 30 mins but did not inform. Then my husband went to the reception and had to sort it out. At the breakfast buffet they behaved like they pity on us by allowing us for breakfast and they were not attentive to us whereas all they cared for Indian guests. It was disgusting stay over where as after that we decided not to extend our stay and we went Dahlia Boutique Hotel where we were very much satisfied to stay. Since being a hotelier I understand there are pressure but there is no place to justify the carelessness towards any guest. We were utterly disappointing.

Nice fall. Can be combined with the Peace Temple if taking the road. I wouldn't go specially if not combined "on the way" to something else. Especially if you came from trekking and saw many waterfalls that are far more impressive.

I can't remember how much I paid to get in at the entrance but I think it is worth it. The stupa is big and there are a lot of shops and restaurants/cafes within the area. That being said, you can just walk in through one of the many other entrances. I would advise the first time you go to pay, because you are supporting the location and maintenance but then if you go other times just walk in through the other entrances. Especially since there are a lot of restaurants inside, and if that is all you want to go to then there is no point in paying every single time at the entrance. You can spend 1-2hrs here exploring and looking into the shops. If you are lucky you might see a procession of some sort, of which a lot of them start at the stupa.

Location of this hotel is great, just a quick taxi ride from many restaurants and sights away. Staff is mostly nice. But: as a former colonial grand hotel, there is not a lot left of the old glamour or even service mentality. The reception looks like a bad kept chaotic office, if you are looking for staff in the morning you might find them at the breakfast buffet instead at their stations, the water has a "healthy" beige colour, and if you order a Taxi from the reception the driver will charge you 3 times the normal price. When asking staff why they support ripp off taxis for their guests they just laughed. 
The pool and garden is nice but it doesnt make up for the rest as the price paid does not reflect the value.

I didn't think this was so special. Having paid US$ 40 for a family of 4 I was a little disappointed in the value. We walked around the Stupa 4 times just to use up time, browse the shops a little and then left. It is a very polluted area, as with most of Kathmandu. Lots of pigeons flying around and dogs.

This is a holy site for the Buddhist people. Around the temple are prayer wheels and people walk around the whole temple spinning the wheels as forms of prayers (Advice: if you are walking on the smooth pathway next tot he temple, walk around the temple counter-clockwise out of respect).  

Surrounding the temple is a huge ring of stores, souvenirs, cafes, craftsmen, paper shops, painting stores, and massage stores (for back, head and foot massages).

It is worth walking around it twice as it is easy to miss the unique stores or to miss the monks and children as they take breaks from their temple duties and schooling as monks.  The area is colorful with buddhist flags and a lot of support for Tibet.

If you are buying souvenirs, just be aware of the souvenirs that hav etc buddhist eyes on them...unless that is what you want.

There is an entrance fee to the shopping area around the temple (About 500 Rupees per person)

The cave is good enough to go and see. There is a hindu priest who sell marbles and you insert that marble into the whole and the cow will give you the holy milk. This is a unique technique to earn some money for the good cause of the cave. Overall I had a fun and had a nice time at this cave.

The water flows under the ground and passes through the cave called Gupteshwor Cave.  The natural scenery is beautiful although the surrounding area is not maintained as there are many trash, be sure to keep tab on where you are walking.
A most place to visit in Kathmandu when you are around in Kathmandu, thank you Budget Adventure Treks and Expeditions for making our sightseeing so wonderful.

We ended our trip in Kathmandu in this very special place, an old palace with a mix of colonial and local setting.
Very well located in the busy area but with a nice garden and pool that really made us feel like an oasis.
Room well appointed, top breakfast with Nepali specialites.
Very proffessional service by senior staff, very efficient!
Stay was very nice! From initial welcome up to our departure, all the staff were very helpful and pleasant. Kudos to Sandhika, and Rajendra.

quite small, but nicely set in a garden;
In the ground there is a big hole which the small stream falls into. 
In summer apparently the water level is higher, but also in Nov it was nice to view.
Accross the road is a cave in which you can see the hole from down under to complement your visit.
Very nice stay. Good and friendly staff.  Binay, Khusi  and Bhintuna.   Good environment  and casino walking distance. Overall good.
Wonderful stay. Staff was so friendly and attentive. Morning breakfast -thosai was excellent. Thank you for a lovely stay.
It’s a very beautiful garden. The problem is the guy in the booth to get our entrance money. He is rather RUDE. If you are a senior citizen like me than you can get a reduced entrance fee.
Best place to be for peace and meditation in early morning without much hassle and disturbance.  Please do visit and spread the word around
This is a need for me. This place is so special to me. Doing Kora or not . I really enjoy just being there. Having a coffee or lunch at Roadhouse cafe with view on the Stupa! Even

great feeling when you go down the cave in to the depth awesome feeling when you get a glimpse of the water fall.water dripping from the roof was nice to watch
what i didn`t like was no security personal in the caves to help the visitors as the caves are in at a vey depth if some accident happens

Beautiful serene place in the middle of hustle and bustle. This palace has been refurbished in hotel has all the grandeur of its age. Apparently from research it’s the birthplace of Queen Aishwaria.
Staff are wonderful and make the stay memorable.
We stayed here for 2 nights when we first arrived Nepal from Australia. Seeing how well this place hosts guests we again booked room for 2 nights on departure. Best decision ever.
Rooms are immaculate as desired by travellers with all ammenities provided. Housekeeping keep everything refreshed and well stocked, we never had to ask cos they know and understand our needs well.
Kitch is very well organised and sanitary services. They serve excellent coffee too.
I know I will definitely come back and will stay in this palace.

We stayed here twice whilst travelling with Kathmandu and Bhutan. The first stay was on the 20/21st of May. This time the room was fine with a temperamental AC and bathroom that was adequate. We went and saw the manager with our various problems and he was most helpful and the next time we arrived we were given a lovely room and lovely welcome. However, the hotel needs refurbishing. A great and well used pool. 
The Staff were great.
Great place , great atmosphere, take time to explore spend time here . Eat and drink or do a yoga retreat or look into Tibetan medicine ,
The place to visit once if you are around the Kathmandu valley . The main point of the buddhist temple called Boudha stupa .
Go underground and down many steps to reach the point from where Devi's Falls are visible.

There is an impressive volume of water, but the waterfall itself is disappointing and difficult to see from the position of the viewing platform. There are some nice, small garden areas and fun photo opportunities with body cut outs(!) so maybe it is worth the 50 Rupee entry.

One of the main tourist sites of Kathmandu and it’s pretty obvious with all the visitors and tourist shops around the site. 

It’s worth the visit and I recommend getting a guide to let you know the different parts of the site. However, have to admit it was a bit underwhelming.
Awesome place.  We can see Lots of handmade art and crafts and a big bouddha statue. One of the best place to hangout.

Kathmandu is a very poor and dirty city.  It is though well worth seeing.  The best way to experience the sights, smells and sounds is to stroll along the many streets.  Hotel Shanker is very conveniently situated close to many interesting sights and street markets. The hotel is a clear throw-back to the colonial past, with interesting architecture, interior and a very nice swimming pool. The waiting staff try their best.  The Kailash Restaurant has a varied menu, but the curries are the best. The hotel is only 20 minutes from the airport. If you are in Nepal to trek or climb, the Shanker will keep some of your luggae while your away. All in all a great place to stay in Kathmandu.
Its a big water fall.The water comming from the fewa lake follows there.very natural beauty.good sightseeing spot.many tibetan shops there.you get a bit hassel.

The Boudhanath Stupa is a top attraction in Kathmandu Nepal.  This "Stupa" is big in size and stunning to look at and a very important monument to Nepal which is one of the many reasons why this is a UNESCO site as well.  There are shops that are situated all around the the Stupa, as well as a traditional Buddhist Monastary.  
A very worthwhile stop to see this Stupa and to walk all around the base of this monument as well as to walk around the upper level.
The staff is extremely nice and very professional. The room is great and the whole place where the hotel is located is beautiful

The soaltee Kathmandu is the best place to stay in Nepal.
Ambience and staff are very warm and friendly 
We had fun at the hotel and staff was there for us even at the odd timings like 3 am to serve us 
Kudos to Dil Kumari for her professionalism and warm nature.

A sacred place for Hindus. The temple of Mahadev. An ancient temple dated back 5000 year ago. A shivlinga in the cave. As you enter into cave a warm hot air feels you.caves are slippery in some part & some passage are so small that one has to crawl. There is a entry fee of 100NPR. just close to gupha is Devi's fall.
its beautiful to see in raining season when you see rainbow in front of you.in the down of the fall there is a cave its called gupteshowr cave

The review before this puts it well and I agree, I am also not quite sure to rate it. I suspect if you are Hindu this is a 5 star event. My Guide encouraged us to pay the 10 rupees to  " milk the cow " which did not work so I would probably skip that! Yes, the actual bit by the falls was really scary and I did not go onto the very rickety steps to see them and the light as there was a nasty drop with no safety railing. I would not personally take small children anywhere near this yet the pilgrims all had them with them so I imagine it is a blessing for them.( Just hope the managers start to think a little bit more about safety issues.)
The shops in the lead up to it were excellent with some of the best prices in Pokhara for tourist things like bags etc.

Booked 2 rooms for 3 nights. Like previous reviewer mentioned some rooms are renovated and we got them but with broken doors & handles. The window would not lock and the safety locker is not bolted so did not feel safe to keep our valuables! Rooms are clean but not sound proof. The grounds are beautifully kept with lots of flowers, trees and walk paths. Sitting in the open front lobby in the entrance was pleasant. 
The food can vary. Breakfast had plenty of choices but still not appealing. One night out of 3 they had buffet which was very good choice and delicious. After that they had Punjabi dhabba style buffet which was waste of time. Staff serving did not have a clue what food they were serving and it was tasteless food anyway. Veg and non-veg were displayed next to each other in a very dim lighting which we did mention in our feedback. The only way to tell the difference was they had actual goats head on display which put us all off eating our dinner and it was not cheap. Your best bet would be to order sandwiches but no guarantee in that too. On our arrival night we ordered sandwiches and veg burger which was freshly made as it should be but same food on the 3rd night was dry and hard! 
Swimming pool was out of order and their spa felt like entering a hospital bathroom. (on ladies side) Over all if you just want a clean room to sleep then this hotel will do!

Resort has such unique entrance, the view from their dining area is mesmerising. Service and staff are very kind and friendly. The overall outlook of resort is heaven like. Ms. Kiran was very helpful and well coordinated for our stay services. She has excellent managerial skills.

Very nice staff 
We had two rooms, double bed room was very nice but the room with two single beds was very small and dark and not spacious at all. Staff very nice , lovely gardens and pool. The food and breakfast was delicious and we had a good choice. Staff was very helpful and friendly

Starting from lackadaisical staff at check in to no wi-fi service in the room, staff was not bothered about keeping the room clean or providing basic amenities like towels in the room. Even the staff at the restaurant for breakfast was non-responsive at all the occasions when approached.

And was damn expensive for this kind of service and environment.

If you ever wonder about where does the water of the Davis Falls go, then the 2950 meters long cave is answer, which is completely stunning! The way to enter is via spiral staircases and the inside view is mesmerizing with chilling temperature!

A popular attraction for one and all, a deep cave with Sacred Siva Linga at the base, one has to walk deep into the place and pay respects, there is an entrance ticket and steps are a bit slippery. Gushing waters from nearby Davis falls pass through underground.

I stayed here for 3 nights. Beautiful hotel, gardens are well maintained & most staff are helpful. Rooms are small with no balcony.

Security staff were excellent & friendly. Thank you

Been here on Sept and missed the breakfast before went back to my country. But i manage to had a lunch and it was an amazing experience with the staff. The water fall is nice but during the dry season there is not much water.I heard during monsoon there is huge water from the fewa lake.There is nice park & little nepali house.we could see many young boys &girls were taking pictures.

one of the place you can enjoy the waterfall. there is a large fence in the front and that stands for the safety and its really peaceful to have a waterfall and enjoy the place, seem simple with elegance.
A large stupa. Walked around to see the entire stupa. Shops all around, plus rooftop restaurants to enjoy the view. Another place to visit in Kathmandu.

Whilst the location and hotel rooms are pretty and surrounded by well kept gardens, I was disappointed to see the swimming pool empty, have two towels when there were three of us and feel like we were secondary importance to the Chinese tour group. Let me start off by saying that I believe that on another occasion in another part of this big hotel, things might have been a lot better. 

We met with a large group of friends (500 of us) arriving at the hotel mainly over a period of 2 days. Reception was clearly not prepared and did a really lousy job at trying to get everybody checked in as fast as possible. Personally I had 3 people staying in line before me, which should not have been so bad, especially taking into account that everybody was pre-registered and that all dues were paid in advance. Novertheless, I had to wait 25 minutes. 

3 counters, 4 hotel employees who could actually check you in, and at least 6 trainees that tried to make copies of passports and were getting in the each others way. After checking your payment, we were transferred to another person who checked your passport, then off to a person who was supposed to block an amount on your creditcard but actually charged it, to finally get the the person who gave you your key card. What a mess!

My room was situated on the ground floor. The water in the toilet reached 2 cm under the toilet seat. I called reception who sent a plumber right away. He showed me a trick to get the water to a normal level. It consisted in having to flush 3 times, each time you would use the toilet. Afraid every single time everything might just overspill during the process... 

I had to wait 3 hours and call reception twice to get my Wifi connection going.

The AC worked perfectly well. 

The closet doors didn't fit in the wall perfectly and were very difficult to open or close. 

The room had a good view on the front lawn of the hotel.

Second night I woke up to set foot on a completely wet carpet. Water sipped from under my door (no idea where it came from, but it was a very rainy night). Again, service arrived quickly, and used tens of towels to try dry everything. Eventually, the next night, everything got back to normal, except for a bad stench in the room, that lingered on until I left. At no time did anybody suggest I should get another room.

When I wanted to extend my stay for one more night, I was offered a price that was 40 dollars more expensive then a reservation I was able to make through Booking.com on the same day. Only after seriously complaining and asking for the manager, did they agree to do something for me.

As we were in a group, some meals were included, others were not. We had badges, and each time we went to a restaurant that was not in charge of serving us our included meals, we were stopped. The wake-up service worked fine. 

The conference rooms were well equipped but the AC took time to kick in.

Unique Cave Experience in Pokhara — Worth a Quick Visit

We visited Gupteshwar Gupha, one of Pokhara’s well-known cave temples. The entrance is small, and you’ll need to walk down a narrow staircase to enter the cave. Inside, it’s a bit dark, slippery, and humid — so good footwear is a must.

The natural rock formations are interesting, and you’ll find a Shiva Lingam temple inside, which adds to the spiritual feel of the place. As you walk deeper, you can also see a glimpse of Devi’s Falls from inside the cave, which is a unique viewpoint.

It’s a short visit — around 20-30 minutes — and worth seeing if you enjoy caves or spiritual sites. However, those uncomfortable with narrow, damp, and uneven paths might want to skip it.

Overall, a decent and different experience in Pokhara for a quick stop.

This was our second stay at Soaltee, the first one being 8 years ago. The hotel is supposed to be one of the best in Nepal. The property is great in itself with lush, well landscaped gardens and a really good swimming pool as well. The rooms were also spacious and well furnished. However, the rooms had a very strong mouldy humid smell which was almost nauseating. We changed rooms but did not help. In fact, we had booked 2 rooms for 5 of us and the all the rooms had the same problem. The carpeting and sofas in the room were not well maintained and even the bathroom fittings were clearly in a bad shape with the shower not functioning properly. The plus points were definitely a very courteous staff and the outdoors in the hotel. If not maintained properly in the future, this great property will only deteriorate further.

Nice place. We enjoyed.

While it is a given that a 5 star hotel in Nepal will not possibly match up to what constitutes a 5 star in developed countries, this hotel sure does charge like one. And when you have paid more than what you would pay for a real 5 star even in India, of course you dont want to put up with what can at best be described as a 3 star. 
We had booked a club room (most expensive apparently) and the size of the room was smaller than even rooms in 2 star hotels and the bathroom absolutely tiny. My husband (at 6 feet) had trouble even moving around the bathroom properly to shave or shower.
Then comes the topic of the view from the room. We had to change rooms THRICE (for a 2 day stay). The first 2 times they gave us rooms facing the back of the hotel with the grand view being the hotel generators the sound of which was astounding. We insisted for a change and the room assigned yet again did not have a working AC!!!!!!
Absolutely fed up we asked to another change after waiting hours for a AC repairman and then were given a satisfactory room.
All rooms featured a CEMENT SLAB for a bed and it really was the worst bed I have slept in a hotel anywhere with any star. I had a fully body ache when I woke up both nights and it is strange why the hotel does not realize this!!
Another major problem with the hotel is its offbeat location, far away (7km to Thamel) so if you dont have a dedicated 24hr car its a hassle.
The much hailed breakfast buffet wouldnt even be called 'adequate' by international standards and the coffee served was absolutely below standard. The very expensive Italian restuarant (Al Fresco) can be described 'passable' at best. The swimming pool (scenic enough) was quite small.
The lobby washrooms were stinking and not even clean thus any claims to this hotel being a '5 star' could not be further from the truth.
The only pro to this hotel were the staff- always smiling and patient and ready to accomodate. Not a least irritated coping with a almost full hotel. They were the only pleasant part to the otherwise major disappointment the stay here was.

Hi,

A few point to note on this hotel:

1) The front staff are friendly but more fake and business like. This is not typical Nepal culture. Other staffs were overly greeting and clearly expecting tips. Made us quite uncomfortable. 
2) Our room had plumbing problems for two days. Was quite irritating. We were finally upgraded after continuous complaining. However, I have to give credit to the head house keeping lady (a bit elderly, don't know her name but had red hair). She really was apologetic and tried her best to get it solved. She even arranged a temp room for us while they tried to repair. Even the next day, she kept asking if our new room was ok.
3) The hotel is actually a gorgeous palace. Beautiful garden. Some painting will do it good.
4) The breakfast is not as spectacular as other reviewers said. I travelled extensively in Asia and this is the lowest basic fare for a star hotel. No quality items e.g. the jam, cereal, butter,, bread etc were all real cheap stuffs. There were fresh fruits and juices which I would love to take but I usually would avoid as I don't know how it has been cleaned or handled.
5) We also ordered room service. That was pretty ok and price was reasonable too.
6) The complimentary mineral water was sealed but still leaking. So, we dared not drink it. This was a general problem in Nepal where we could not be sure of getting clean water.
7) Bed was ok. Comfortable enough to sleep.
8) Room is spacious
9) Bath also spacious but not that clean. Toilets n tub pretty stained. Would be nice if they had new toilets
10) walking distance to Thamel, but was of no interest to us.
11) Narayanhiti palace is just next door. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
12) If your room does not come with wifi package, it can be quite expensive for wifi charges. Go down the street to the sports shop whereby there's cafe along side it. There is free wifi there with good signal and decent coffee. In the next street, there is Barista coffee. Nice coffee and free wifi too.
13) There is swimming pool but quite small..

I stayed in this hotel for my business trip, I had excellent experiment while staying here. The facility in the hotel is everything. I love the food in all the restaurants that hotel provides.

Last month I have been in Davis' Fall, located just opposite the Mahadev cave. The fall is named after a Swiss lady Davis. On 31 July 1961, a Swiss couple Davi went swimming but the woman drowned in a pit because of the overflow. Her body was recovered 3 days later in river Phusre with great effort. Her father wished to name it "Davi's falls" after her.

Its entrance fee is Rs 30/person. The fall is surrounded by metal fences for safety purposes. The fall is small with heavy flow of water. It may be better to visit in the rainy season when the fall is full of water. There is a little wishing pond next to the fall and the Nepalese like to throw the coin into that pond to pray for luck.

We popped into the Garden of Dreams as it was just along the road from our hotel. We were expecting a much larger space and was expecting to be able to walk around the gardens and see the local flora and fauna. The entrance fee was only about $2 but still not really worth paying to go inside. We had walked around in about 5 minutes and whilst it was quite peaceful and relaxing it just wasn't that interesting.

Nice experience overall!

Excellent property amidst nature . We went there to attend a close friends wedding. All the arrangements were spectacular. Staff was very courteous and helpful . Well maintained rooms . Food was also good especially the breakfast spread with a special mention of masala chai . Terrace garden staff was very good especially Sabita in the morning breakfast with a beautiful smile and warm hospitality. Full marks to this property

one of the famous place in kathmandu Boudhanath Stupa,meany Buddhist making round at the stupa at the evening,its  looks beautiful, when there full moon  is best  time to hang-around  at night time just love it ... i visit cant count always happy

Great stupa and surroundings, best place in Nepal, visit during Kathmandu stay, close to the airport, 24 hours open. many monks and spiritual place.
Enjoyed every moment at devis fall....had capture lots of amazing picture infront of water fall.... enjoyed alot there

Our group went here at the end of our trek for some sightseeing in Pokhara. I wouldn't recommend the cave for someone with unsure footing, poor balace, fear of enclosed spaces or of the dark. 

We went there during Dasain, so there were crowds of people packed into the narrow cave's walkways. The view wasn't as impressive as the bat cave, but the walk down the spiral staircase with the carved, colourful depictions of Hindu Gods and Goddesses was interesting. 

Otherwise, it wa damp, slippery, humid, dark and crowded with other people.

The hotel is old, yes, but that's not the main reason for a negative review (although a renovation is long overdue). The main reason for a negative review is that I simply dislike having to listen to the strong bass of the music of the weddings, every day (repeat: every day!) that are taking place in the hotel. I realise that is your money-maker, but you should also realise it drives guests away.

Silent, serene and peaceful; there are the words that would be best to describe this place. IN my previous trips to Nepal, Garden of Dreams was my my go to place to just refresh myself from the hustle and bustle of the city, all the activities and just find a quiet time for myself. Returning here after Covid, I am glad to say that not much has changed and it still offers a peaceful place  like it used to before.

a.       Modern hotel with modern amenities.

This place is an underground temple and is linked at the end to another waterfall - Davis fall. Bit risky but adventouros

The place is a living reminder of the Heritage. The river,by its constant flow has eroded the soft underlying soil and made the GORGE. It's indeed a well thought out idea to make an easily accessible pathway for tourists to go and watch.

Was quite surprised that this was considered a highlight of Pokhara in our guide book, the waterfall was neither impressive nor accessible to view clearly. The entry was only Rs30, only come if you are already nearby (world peace pagoda for example).

A completely acceptable 3-star hotel. It doesn't pretend to be anything it isn't - you get what you pay for, which is clean and comfortble rooms with cable TV, and a great location within easy walking distance of the Lakeside shops and restaurants. 
The staff were friendly and polite, and willing to help out with my queries. BIDUR, Sunita and Hasta Pradeep Nepali were awesome with there service..So kind and helpful verry beautiful property .we will Caine again in this hotel. We injoy a lot .

Beautiful place in thamel Kathmandu..don't forget this place in thamel. I requement all of you this place

Can't see much good stuff here, but since it is located not so far from town, and on the way, if you go to world peace temple, it's still okay to see. The entrance fee is 30 Npr which is also cheap. But the parking fee is 100npr, so I recommend not to bring vehicle here.

I’ve been visiting The Soaltee Kathmandu from very long time back. The Soaltee Kathmandu has been my go to destination for any business occasion and specially for my students hotel visit. Mr. Roopesh Shrestha (L&D Director) is an amazing personality who had a great session of motivation and soft skill mentorship for my students. 

The food were mind-blowing as always. The sales team were very friendly during the entire business. 

Hope to come back again and again. 

Thank you!!!

The stupa and surrounding shops are fun to visit.  It only takes an hour to include a short stop at a cafe.  I went during Diwali holiday so it was a festive atmosphere. I enjoyed the walk around and onto the lower level of the stupa.

We have been to several touristy palaces in Nepal and made so many Napali friends. Other than the fact that there is not much to see, the entrance security is the rudist I've ever met. We got our pass tickets and entered. On the way out, our tour guide, Nepali, and I decided to pass by the toilets. They had works going on, so we had to exit and re-enter from the main entrance.  The guy at the door attacks towards me asking that I buy another ticket although the toilets are even from behind the ticket check. After successfully passing Heimdall, on the way out he didn't let us exit the same way and asked us to walk all around to the tour exit (And we were dead after a day of trekking). I do not recommend the place especially that their attitude is insulting to local people such as our nice guide.

Really amazing stay.good food here

This hotel perhaps used to be a luxury hotel back in the day, but it has shown signs of wear and tear. It is not 5-star, and I would be pressed to say 4-star. My friend and I had two twin beds and it was a bit small. I must admit I loved the hallways and artwork and the architecture definitely felt like an old colonial hotel. The buffet breakfast was quite good. The hotel grounds seems to be a popular spot for weddings, since 2 out of 4 nights at this hotel had large, loud weddings (they did get quiet late at night). There was what seemed to be a nice, clean pool (not heated). It was good that the hotel had its own grounds and were a bit removed from the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu. I'm still surprised that people rave about this hotel. Maybe they had upgrades and better rooms, but ours seemed pretty standard.
It was a very good experience and photo opportunities inside the cave. The river flows into a cave and disappears.

The Hotel says there are a 5 star hotel, but i guess they need to have a relook..not worth more than a 3 star status.

For starters, the moment you land, there are no porters, on enquiry they say they have gone for a cuppa tea. so you wait until they come or better take the bags yourself to your room

Rooms stink.... looks like nobody stays here, so rooms are locked for weeks... They cud do better by airing the rooms before checking guests in

The hotel lobby staff have a look on the face that reminds you of having seen a horror. Guys pls smile. These guys get more defensive when you give them feedback of the room, services rather than offer a solution

Their sightseeing tours are lousy, not sure why they tie up with lousy travel desks who dont know how to take care of the guests.

All in all, a lousy and an irritable experience...doesnt deserve more than a 3 star status.
Just apposite devis fall. A temple and a cave where you can see waterfall which is connected from devis fall. 100 rupees is per person enterance fee. Not worth it because it is very ordinary.

Stayed for 2 nights and though there was an initial hiccup regarding check in as room was paid from a day prior yet kept waiting for 20 mts to have key which was a dampener...

Food quality and variety simply of top notch standards ...

If one is looking for an initial stay in Kathmandu,  soaltee is definitely the best option
Cave was overcrowded and air was very stuffy, it’s a cave obviously it’s gonna be tight and have low ceilings and drips at points. Lots of trash, low visibility and mediocre views nothing memorable.

I with my wife visited and stayed in Hotel Barahi Pokhra from 24th May for 2 nights. This hotel can not run AC on Generators. Electricity in Nepal seems to be regular problem. Imagine a room without AC and No fan :(. The hotel has 4 levels Ground , 1st, 2nd and 3rd and NO lift. On welcome, they provide luggage carrying service but on check out..... you have to carry it yourself. Food, I experienced only breakfast was half cooked. Chef said...this is what we provide for breakfast. I think this hotel does not deserve to get any star rating.

Located in the busy market place just opposite Devi's Fall this is a nice place to visit. The priest at the temple was from Assam in India and he helped us to perform aarathi.There is an entry ticket of NPR 30 to visit the temple.

Beautiful cave.
say about 150 metres below the ground.
They are beautifying the place currently so im guessing it should be even better in a few months.

It is a really wonderful Budhist temple,not that very big, but then,as they say,"small is beautiful".
Very busy indeed, with many people circling around the temple and the atmosphere is fantastic.
Good cafes and restaurants around and not that expensive, try the Nepalese Tea which is very soothing and tasteful

the waterfalls which you have seen worldwide are quite amazing,but this waterfall have its own specialty of water being coming back in reverse direction,you can just feel the drizzle sprinkling when water passes through a cave,you can just have look of the speed of flow of water
It's a huge fall, the gush of water frightened me. The fencing was very small earlier but now it's very huge. The waterfall is very huge. I got little scared  when I visited it.

Yes when you travel around Kathmandu the hotel looks impressive compared with the surroundings, however when the room is cooking in December and the solution by the engineer is turn off the AC and wait 30 mins you know that you are imposing first world complaints on a third world situation. Relax and sweat. 
Other than that. Bed is not great and I think I should have tried elsewhere.

This cave is 50m away from the Devi's Fall and suggest to visit this cave when visited Devi's Fall.

The entrance fee for foreigners is NP100 per person, with considerable steps to go down and up from for access. 

They believed this cave to be 5000 years old and one of the wonderful and largest cave in south asia.

Once enter deep inside the cave, you may find an Idol of Lord Shiva and drop of water continuously dripping from the ceiling if the cave.

Once you have passed through a tunnel, you will find yourself in a huge open space which is really a huge cavern inside and full of enormous rocks (currently some restoration works on going, and open to public).

The climate of this tour, after few yards of scrambling througt the darkness, you may find yourself on the edge of crystal clean pond and awe inspiring patale chhango falling right to the top.
Excellent service nice property lobby area nice. Sakshi from Guest relation was very helpful, and other staffs are also very courteous. Loved and enjoyed the stay

Since this was my first visit to Kathmandu I can't compare this hotel with any others, but I would be surprised if there aren't better top-end hotels in town. This place isn't bad, but it doesn't have the level of perfection that you expect from a top-end establishment. The swimming pool was only open 9-5, making it inaccessible to business travellers. The gym is small, dark and badly equipped. My room faced the back of the hotel, where there are two house-sized generators providing electricity for when there are power cuts (which is often in Kathmandu), and they made a terrific amount of noise, even at night. If you are staying, here, make sure you ask for a room which faces the front gardens. The choice of TV channels was quite good, and the wireless internet worked fine. I tried the Italian restaurant (Al Fresco) and it makes a decent pizza. 
If I come back to Kathmandu I think I'll try the Hyatt instead.
For me personally I didn't find anything special about this place. Yeah it was nice and maintained inside but it's packed with tourists and it's rather pricey. Entry fee is also 200 rupees.

It was a good hotel, clean rooms, etc. but I was not impressed by a single restaurant of the hotel. The food was really not that good. The room service was not that effective. I was definately expecting more from this hotel especially since I have stayed at other Crowne Plaza properties in the United States. This Crowne Plaza was definately not up to the mark compared to the International ones.

Great room and comfortable bed and pillows. Nice and polite and friendly staff. I enjoyed dinner at the restaurant, tried traditional food, momos, it was delicious. The waiter Dhiraj was very attentive, polite and overall provided great service.

I visited many places around Kathmandu but I liked boudhnath because of its clean and full of peace. Where you can have deep knowledge about Buddhism.
Lovely place and interesting.

It's a beautiful garden with greenery all around with nice beautiful flowers but bit of expensive in ticket they are charging which is not necessary no restaurant inside for tea , coffee or any drink which looks not good even not bottle of water no self service freezes it's necessary . definitely we back again thank for your service.

I have visited pokhara and booked 6 rooms for 2 days. Initial process itself was terrible. Visited this attraction and was very impressed by the natural beauty of the place.  It was such a shame to see so much litter, especially plastic bottles all around.

Pretty powerful and impressive waterfall in pokhara. Short drive from lakeside or you can hike down to here from the stupa.

The most striking feature of the Hotel is the large grounds in which it is set. There is a big open, lobby which also serves as a bar in the evening. There is a general air of spaciousness in this Hotel which is located reasonably close to the City centre. They have a choice of restaurants including a nice Indian restaurant serving kebabs. The food is good although service is slightly below par. They have a business centre, internet in the rooms and wi-fi -- although at nearly $15/day internet access is ok for the busineess traveller and not really cheap for the casual user. They have a shopping arcade, swimming pool etc. The buffett breakfast is very good with lots of choice. Check your room .. ours had a view of large plastic water tanks. Overall a nice, if slightly predictable hotel which could be anywhere in the World. If you want a feel of Kathmandu this hotel is not for you.

Very good hospitality.....a royal splendour for family in vacation. Good staff and service. It was worth spending quality time here. The space around made stay pleasant and very approachable to nearby must visit tourist points. Hotel gives us the royal feel from its historic architecture.
The Gupteshwar Gupha is quite an adventure as you keep on going down till you reach the largest cave.  Surreal and magnificent.

Views of falls are severely restricted by huge thick blue fencing bars. Unnecessarily large and obtrusive, and far enough from the edge that it’s impossible to get a view down the falls even if you hold a camera through the railings.

come to see the monkeys as they are very entertaining. the view is outstanding over the city. the stairs to the top very dramatic 200rps for foreigners to enter although you can get in for free if you come the back way. bit of a building site at the top due to earthquake. usual collection of tat stores and overpriced cafes but worth the walk from thamel as a nice half day trip.

There was water dripping down the ceiling of the cave, we were wet & also sweating since it was the beginning of June, it was very hot inside. Best place in Nepal to visit. Air have different type of aroma and ambience was great. located in birth place of load Buddha. i love the people enjoying from different religion and society which is its best part for us..

At one session of the store / temple circle, there were a lot of pigeons.  People sell pigeon food to attract the tourists.  I do think that it is rahter unhygienic walking among hundreds of pigeons.

I had travel In Pokhara April 2015, Devi's fall was best water fall in to very deep.there was clean water and the source of falls from Phewa Lake.If, any one travel In Popkhara don't forget it to look around at the falls.

Our reservation at another location was cancelled at the last mopment and we were dropped at this hotel. I beleive the deluxe rooms are nice. However, we were given a "standard" room. Only good thing about this area is all the souvenir stalls as you walk to the cave entrance, so only visit if you are a shopaholic.

My first buddhist temple I have ever visited - made a huge impression on me. Surrounded by small motels, gorgeous restaurants and small souvenirs shops... accompanied by cute monkeys I felt the a spirit of Nepal, it's people and small piece of religion...

Boudha is lovely, surrounded by shops and cafes in the middle of a town . . It was buzzing with people walking around and a great place to shop, take pics and grab a roioftop coffee. .  highly recommended

Interesting but filthy - they need to clean this place up! The monkey temple was better! There is one nice temple that is very old and different. Also there are a few monasteries nearby. The road next to this place is a disaster. Everyone wears a pollution mask!

The Hotel Barahi is close to the lake and used by tour groups, amongst others, so it must be pretty good.  The rooms are clean if a little dark, and the lack of a lift can mean some steady stair climbing to get to your room.  There's free, no quibble wifi in the restaurant and breakfast area, and a smallish pool (perfectly adequate), as well as a small shop. Good breakfasts - an omelette station and buffet and you can sit outside (although seating is a bit limited).  All in all a good standard tourist hotel i.e. clean, safe, convenient - what more do you want?

Would much prefer visiting the Monkey Temple (Swayambu) as it has better views, more to see, and is far easier to reach from the touristy part of Kathmandu (Thamel).  Not much to see here other than a large Stupa.
Being slightly claustrophobic I passed on the opportunity to enter the cave. It was dark and very poorly lit.

Save yourself the time and trouble do not visit it is not worth it. It is dank, dark, slippery and has a dark vibe to it. It does however have inmportance for Hindus we just really disliked it.

Stayed a total of 3 nights in 2 different rooms. This hotel is not remotely up to par for a 5-star Crowne Plaza.
Location: Away from noisy street, nice gardens.
Rooms: Very cold (the housekeeping staff leaves the A/C on with the thermostat set at 15°C), no heat even though the outside temperature drops to 14°C at night (I was told it doesn't get turned on until the end of November). Very old furniture. Light switches difficult to find. Comfortable bed. Room amenities include coffee maker and laptop-size safe. There is an iron but its plug is not compatible with any of the electrical outlets in the room. One of the rooms had an unpleasant smell of cigarette smoke, apparently coming from the ventilation system.
Bathroom: The shower in one of the two rooms (on the 5th floor) had very low water pressure, the other one (3rd floor) was good. Toiletries half empty and not replenished. No hair dryer.
Staff: Housekeeping leaves some to be desired (coffee and toiletries not replenished).
Gym: Open 0600-2100 (did not use).
Breakfast: Ok, but not great.
Internet: WiFi charges (about $5 for one hour or $15 for 24 hours) are exorbitant by Nepalese standards. WiFi was once down for 15 minutes.

Stayed at the Shanker for three days for business and based on the reviews I was expecting more. Service is very good, this is certain. Restaurant is also quite nice, and spa offers excellent treatments of very high quality and professionalism. However, rooms are really small, with no light, stuffy, and have a feel of being dirty and dusty. I changed three rooms, something that had never happened to me before. In the first one, on the first floor, air quality was just awful and it had no natural light at all; in the second one the mattress was broken so that once you lay on it you go 30 cm down; and in the third one the bathroom was in a very bad shape. Wifi is poor to nonexistent. Noise isolation is also not at all provided, you can hear your neighbours very clearly. Given the price, I'd rather pay some 30 USD more and get a much better hotel.

Unique cultural (and religious) experience. Powerful to observe pilgrims visiting their sacred place. If timing works out, one may also observe other festivities. Went after 4pm and able to see views of day and night. Rooftop cafe/restaurants are recommended after walking around the stupa.

All over hotel has large area but walking all over it can be most tiring thing. Excellent casino but it takes effort to walk from hotel to there. The hotel should get some kind of shuttle from casino to hotel.
Free wifi is also a needed facility.

If you go to Pokhara, it's a must to visit. Nice fall.
When the sun is up, don't forget to wear sunglasses & cap/hat.
You can do a little bit of shopping in the stores around it. But do bargain.
The most famous temple in Kathmandu also it has largest stupa. Compare to other temples, this temple is more organized and has many shops also restaurants.
Not far out of Pokhara (lake side) and worth spending a hour at the falls and around the small market .
Went here with my wife and friends. Enjoyed a lot there. Some statues are made there so you have to fix your head and it gives an impression that you are wearing different attires of Nepali culture.
