This is a great place to spend some time watching the gushing water! The noise of the water really calms you down and feels good to watch natures power.

The hospitality Mr. Sudip offer me tonight at the bar was absolutely perfect. He was very friendly and professional. I would like to thank him very much. Also I loved the sisha that he recommended me. The vibe of the bar is ver nice too. I will definately visit again. Thank you!

Our stay there for 3 nights was fairly ok, probably because we had booked the suite. Apart from the old, sour smell on the corridors, everything else was fine. Oh, there was also the time when the guys at the bar made it pretty bluntly clear that they are tired and would like us to get out (around 11:30) so we apologized took our drinks and went to the garden. The breakfast was nothing fancy, but at least it was a buffet, so we could choose. Don't get me wrong, i enjoyed my newary meal in a neighborhood restaurant, but i review a 4 star hotel here. 
Things went wrong at the end of our stay. We had invited a couple of friends to join us in Shanker and booked a room for them. I asked about rate and availability at the reception, all they had was a standard room. I got the rate and it sounded decent (for those unaware, remember to ad the 23% service and whatever other taxes there might be, they never mention it unless asked for it), only to find out the next morning, at check out that my friends were supposed to pay a higher rate. It was useless of me going there and ask to talk to the person who initially gave me the price. All they did was shuffle a bill in our face and say this is what you have to pay. They did offer to deduct the extra money from the next bill when they heard that my friends intended to return to Kathmandu. That was under the excuse that they have made a mistake but since the bill is already written (a lousy piece of paper written by hand) they can't change it .... So my friends paid and decided not to return.
All in all, just make sure you clarify the money issues with them in advance.

We were in awe with the gushing water and briefly understood how the name came about. There's a cave just opposite the road can visit both but during my visit unfortunately it was closed due to heavy rainfall.

I would have given this hotel a poor for its dirt and grime, but it does have a tv, nice shower, and a POOL!!! The pool is so nice on a hot day. I am so grateful that we chose this hotel just because of the pool. Definitely recommend this hotel when it is very hot and humid.

Visited in December 2022. We went to this place as part of a full day sightseeing tour. It is located right opposite to Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave. You need to traverse a market before reaching the ticket counter. There are few small picture taking spots before you walk few steps to the falls. There is only one spot for taking a good picture of the falls and there is quite a crowd for that coveted spot. There are washrooms. Didn't use though.
The Garden of Dreams is a lovely peaceful garden in the middle of bustling Kathmandu. Entry Nrs 200 pp. Well worth visiting on the way to Thamel.

We went before the monsoon so the water was not at its max but a nice falls nevertheless. You can’t approach the falls or touch the water but only view it. Heard it’s awesome at its peak after July with rainbows above it!
A pity about the plastic junk that people throw around it.

We spent 4 nights in this beautiful location.
The staff were very friendly and attentive and went out their way to make our visit special.
The views of the mountains over the lake were stunning and the gardens were beautiful.
It had a very peaceful atmosphere and a perfect place to relax.
The food was delicious and the waiters always ready to help. There was an indian flute and tabla recital one evening which was a real treat.
We hope to return.

It was a wonderful experience at Hotel Shanker—a calm and quiet place. Markets are within walking distance. It was a pleasant stay at the hotel. The food and accommodation facilities are the best in Kathmandu. The staff is very humble and polite.

Most unsafe property, lost 600 USD there outside our room. And the management is totally uncooperative, didnt even let see the CCTV footage. GM Mr Kushal singh and DM Mr krishna Thapa, kept on defending their staff instead. 

Most unsafe for Indians atleast

This cave is a delight after the disappointing visit to the Seti river gorge.
This cave has an entrance to a cow shed and from there low ceilings, winding alleyways and all that a cave must have.
At the fag end of it, there is a tiny crack in the cave through which you can see a white waterfall.
amazing experience.

You must visit this place!

We had a comfortable stay at hotel shankar. Nice room, decent room service and a nice pool however our experience was spoiled by an obnoxious manager in the breakfast hall. We were traveling with our four year old and often pack a sandwich and a banana to go. In all our years traveling with a child no one has ever objected to this, when my husband asked for a box he was rudely told that he can only pack for the child and not for us! This is before he had even given us the box. The next day upon asking for the same he  rolled eyes proceeded to stare and mutter with waiters, I would have given him a piece of my mind on the spot but i this review should suffice. Completely uncalled for bad behaviour. Someone needs to fire him or send him back to hospitality school. I am writing a piece on Nepal for a travel magazine and will exclude  hotel Shanker based on our experience with this individual.

Really an average spot to visit. Just opposite side of the road to Devi's fall. There is a water fall at the end of the cave. I feel suffocated inside of the cave due it's hot & humid weather. Will never visit again.
Visited Bouddhanath temple this month. It is one of the nice place to hangout with partner in the evening. Highly recommended place in Kathmandu to visit.
One of the best hotel and my top favourite hotel. The room is amazing, the breakfast, overall 100% will stay here if i come for vacation.

friendly and attentive staff, cleanliness, well-maintained rooms, and delicious food luxury experience, comparing it to high-standard hotels. Surendra and sunita and other  staff treat you with service you with smile face.

We stayed for 3 nights at the end of December, and I was deeply annoyed by the poor quality of service, in a hotel where we (2 people, 1 double room) spent more than 120 USD per day. The rooms were nice, even if they were 3 times smaller than I expected, and we found them very clean.
But when it comes to the front building (Front desk, Restaurant), it's a chaos. The staff at the front desk is unable to process a check-in normally, and I found them very cold with non-Nepali customers. We had to fight every morning to eat breakfast, as the room was completely full, with children and people shouting all together.
Every time I asked something to someone I felt like I was disturbing them, which is a bit frustrating.
There are no ameities such as Sauna, Gym etc... 
I've been coming to Pokhara every year for more than four years, and this experience was the worst ever. You can't charge the same price as Hyatt Regency if you offer a cheap Holliday Inn service.
The entrance free is only thirty rupees but there is nothing so interesting to see just a simple fall

The staff and cleanliness is on par with international standards. Laxmi at reception was more than accommodating with us. Excellent service. The food menu could do with a more multi cultural update. However everything we had was great. Thank you for having us
I was expecting the biggest stupa in the world to be... impressive. Unfortunately, it wasn't, but I still believe it's a must-see in Kathmandu.
I am sorry but for me was the most interesting restaurant Pho around... We had to pay as foreigner but if we choose some side street it will not necessary. our guide it didnt know...
Many people at falls, completely gated off. Nothing terribly special about it. Also visited cave across the street.
Such an experience actually being here after seeing it on televison. Tranquil, peaceful, beautiful setting with an excellent shopping area surrounding the stupa.

I had a very pleasant stay. As soon as i arrived we are welcome with a very polite and friendly staff. They even offer to help me to carry my luggage. Once i enter the room it was very beautiful and comfortable. I took a shower and i love how the shampoo and conditioner makes my hair shiny and soft. Room service was great. Food was amazing. Thank you for the hospitality.
Nothing special if you have visited caves earlier. Crowded and not that well maintained yet although some reconstruction is on
Just view it from outside. No point going underground and have to pay for a fee and get all dirty and wet walking down the tunnel/cave. The view from outside is much more pleasant and nice.
This is amazing cave, You can see Lord Shiva temple inside here. The water which flows from Davis fall can be viewed from here. The place is really amazing.
Room are so cozy, breakfast are so nice, staff are so helpful and courtesy. Thank you for your hospitality! Recommended 💯

I guess just come since it's just next to the fall. It's a short 10 minute walk into the cave. It's slippery and dark so not for the physically challenged. You basically are inside he cave where the falls end. Cheesy deco in the way into the cave.
The food was delicious and the staff were amazing. I really enjoyed my stay here and will definitely come back again. Thank you so much.

The best place we have been in asia .
Surendra ganga and  tej kumar from.the hotel are the greatest hospitality manners ever. 
We will gladly return.

Known as "paataalo chaango" locally this amazing waterfall known as Davis Fall is one of its kind and a must visit place in Pokhara Nepal for its awesome view and varied sounds of waterfall.. although reminded me of bhedaghat in India at Jabalpur Madhya Pradesh.
A garden in the mid of busy city..Nice to viist..You can sit or walk around for a while..But theres entrance fee to be paid..

There is an interesting entrance with beautiful sculptures depicting the rich culture of the place. However, the walk down was wet and slippery. Tourists need to watch their steps and their heads as there are some parts that requires you to bend low. As the place was very dark and there seem to be no control of the number of people going into the cave, it was rather claustrophobia inducing for me personally.When I reached the little waterfall, there was not enough time to focus the camera to capture a proper picture as there were many people waiting behind me. And the vantage point was a little too low and too slippery for me. And there was only one narrow stretch on some slippery rocky steps in the dark to reach the vantage point within the cave. I find it was quite dangerous, and was glad when I finally reached the better ventilated outer half of the cave. I would advise those who are thinking of doing this as an adventure would probably enjoy it better on a less crowded day.

The garden was close to our hotel and the images online looked great. However I've it was a little sad, the head not so green and not many flowers. Walking around took all of 5 minutes.

Although the architecture is stunning and it could be a nice place to sit, meditate and read (with the little chipmunks by your students), the obscene amount of crows making a lot of noise ruined any serenity.

Devi's falls is about 30 minutes walk from Pokhara market. I would suggest to walk to the place instead of taking the local transport. Local buses are crowded and can take long since they wait till the bus is full to move. Walking down to the falls, helps you better acclimatize with the locals and the roads.
Loved the Devi Falls. It was so serene and beautiful. Easy access to see everything. Loved the wishing well.

It was a very comfortable stay at Soaltee. The property is beautiful. All the staff specially Ragisha and Sabita Thapa at Garden Terrace restaurant who were very kind and attentive to all our needs. Our kudos to them! Thank you for your service.

Was in Kathmandu for business rather than for trekking and wanted to have a hotel that offers internet/wlan, office facility in the room and good enough restaurants to survive after hectic long meetings. 
Booked the hotel because of the reviews on another webpage.
Unfortunately not impressed.
- rooms are tiny, not very clean
- bathroom is so tiny that one can only enter backwards to sit on the toilet as no turn around possible ( i am not fat)
- internet is not reliable and very very slow
- breakfast was disorganized with dirty tables and disgusting food
- after seeing the breakfast i avoided eating anything else in this hotel
Summary - will not recommend or book again

I need to preface this review by telling you that we had just come off a 17 day trek, a trek that we weren't ready for ending- we wanted to keep going but you dont know that when you make your original plans and we had planned to finish our trek in Jomsom and fly to Pokhara. So, my review is possibly not as enthusiastic as it might have been if we had been ready for it.
Anyway, arrived early morning after a flight from Jomsom. To the hotel's credit early check in was not an issue. 
The room was high floor and facing into the hotel grounds. The porter assured us that next time we could get a lake view- it hadnt occurred to me to even request one, so if you want a lake view pre-request. We were happy with our view of the gardens.
The room was big, light and had a great little balcony.
Furnishings, bedding and walls need a spruce up- they are looking dated. Same with the bathroom.
Bed was comfortable, sheets nice and clean and the a/c was useful in quickly cooling the room down. Quiet nights sleeps, we didnt hear noise for other rooms at all. The bathroom was very functional, deep bath, hot water (luxury) and enough amenities provided.
Used the restaurant for breakfast only. It was always busy but we managed a seat inside. Outside  diners seemed to be having problems with flys. Breakfast food was fine- fruit, porridge, cereal and some hot Nepali and international dishes. Bakery items were plentiful. The wait staff did a great job at keeping your cup of tea/coffee refilled and they were very pleasant. WIFI available here.
There is a coffee shop with wifi too, big range of baked goods and a very nice cup of coffee (first one for weeks).
Big pool- lots of people enjoying it and it looked lovely.
Location works- close to restaurants and the main shopping strip.
Checkout efficient.
In conclusion, it was fine. Would I stay there again- no, I didnt "fit" the hotel. I'd go smaller and more personal.
Disliked it ....Not worth the visit ...Only if you are too much religious then only you should visit ...Its not a touristic spot ....dangerous to walk in wet cave

Go here in the rainy season to see the falls. Its experience not to miss. Then do go the the cave and see the waterfall from the bottom its truly amazing to go down the caves and see how the water made its way deep down to an abyss.

On my this trip, first bad impression was from front officers. No any charming face, no any welcoming words. All face were so dull & so serious. So, that was bad feeling.

Front officers need to change there attitude or it’s problem with management.

This resort style hotel my Marriott Autograph Collection was a wonderful experience with awards winning Restaurant and Hotel with dedicated staff that are passionate about serving guests and attentive service!
Management and Hospitality are excellent, guest rooms are very clean and well equipped with all the amenities that come with the service you expect!
Restaurant staff are very professional and friendly always make sure you have the best food and beverage’s you want.
Food selection is wonderful and tasty, continental food and Asian cuisine is also great, with an excellent selection.
Thank you for a wonderful experience and excellent service!
Beautiful place but the management should replace the impolite, rude security guard at the entrance.

Came back to try a different food choice at Kakori restaurant. Special mentions Ashmit, Manoj and Janat as usual went beyond expectations. Both of them care so much for their guests and I believe someday soon become managers in their respective Hotel/Restaurants. I wish them all the very best for their future. They are very hard working and genuine. 
I REQUEST THE MANAGER READING THIS TO APPRECIATE THEM WITH PROMOTION OR A SALARY HIKE. 
My stay was from 13th Mar to 14th Mar, 2024
This cave is beautiful to look into it.  Going down through stairs one need to go deep to visit the cave. This cave is linked with Devis fall beneath the street.
If you have a spare half day Devis Fall'is well worth a visit.  Easy to get to it can be combined with visit to the Hindu Temple and cave across the road.

•Entrance fee is Rs 30/ person 
•It is located just opposite the Mahadev cave. You can see the part of  falls from the mahadev cave too
• Inside it there’s a wish pond. Some People throw coins and make wish
•The fall is surrounded by metal fences for safety purposes 
•The fall is small with heavy flow of water and due to metal fences you couldn’t enjoy the proper view. 
•Its only the story behind the falls that touches me.

The circular stairs leading to the cave is nice but the cave itself is not so big or deep and did not have a lot of natural formations to marvel at. It was also slippery from the dripping water and not well-lit. There is an area with nice rock sculptures (stacked rocks) and that's it. You may find it interesting for religious reasons. Otherwise, if you have been to big, beautiful caves before, you may want to skip this.

Whilst I am not disappointed that I visited the Garden of Dreams, I feel it has so much potential to be a more amazing tourist destination. It is clearly a place of respite amongst the busy streets of Kathmandu, but felt it was in need of some maintenance. A little disappointed there were no monkeys visible.
very unusual water fall. Must visit. If you are lucky, you may see security soldiers practising to go go down to meet any eventuality

Devi's fall or Davis fall is named after a swiss couple, the wide had drowned and her body got stuck. For the locals it became difficult to rescue her body. The waterfall is named after the wife Davi's Fall. 
The fall is beautiful but it will only give you a view from the above, you will get the real view from Gupteshwar caves, hence i would recommend visiting the caves as well which is 100m walk from the waterfall.

We visited on New Years Day and arrived by taxi. It's a very busy spot but still very peaceful. The entry fee (for foreigners)  is 400 rupee (around $5 AUD)  per person. There are lots of market stalls, shops and restaurants around the stupa so plenty going on.  We left the crowds and headed up to a second floor cafe which gave us a great view and a nice break from the busyness. It's a good place to visit but expect lots of crowds and to pay more for food/drinks than in downtown. Overall, a great place to see and worth the entrance fee.

Cockroaches in bathroom, terrible service, poor upkeep, steep prices. Not worth a stay! This hotel has fallen drastically since the last time I stayed here. Quiet a disappointment. Probably the worst Crowne Plaza I have stayed in. This is certainly not a deserving of its IHG affiliation. The staff attitudes are equally undeserving of a guest stay.
Visited on a day tour in Pokhara, including with some other places. The Falls and Gupteshwar caves together makes it a special attraction.
You will see the biggest stupas and some Buddhist monks, you will also find lots of souvenirs for your friends and family.

We have four days in pokhara, so we went and checked it out . If I had less time I wouldn't mind missing it. Entry cost was 100 rupees which I thought was fair . Steps are wet and slippery so watch your step !
Cave is deep and slippery, temple inside is good cave go beyond the temple you can explore for more fun. Tickets are quite costly as per location.

One of the best hotel I have stayed so far.  The food, services and safety is good. Staff is very co-operative. Great value for money. I would love to stay again in this hotel on my next trip whenever I visit Nepal and would recommend others as well.

A place for young lovers to hang out. Garden is not spectacular. A place to get out of the hustle and bustle of the city - but there are otters places in Thamel region that is free an quiet to eat and hang out. The restaurant is resonantly good - like the Nepali Dhal Bhat. Entrance fee charge to contribute to restoration.
Neat surroundings. Worth a visit, easily accessible. good shops around. clean Public Toilets available. serene ambiance.

yes,any hindu tourist will think it is devi's place because devi is goddess durga. but it is not.after purchasing a ticket you will go inside and and find a stream coming through a hole and thus making a gushing sound and waterfall looking great.a swedish lady was drowned here while taking bath .her name was davis so the name of this waterfall is devi's fall.and there is awishes well....here you throw coins and if it rests on the head of the idol your wishes will be fulfilled
This is the biggest stupa in the world and to experience the Tibetan Buddhist culture this is the place to visit.
Too many tourists, and stupa just surrounded by souvenirs shops and bad quality restaurants for tourists.... place to avoid... there are lot of more interesting sites in Kathmandu....

This temple is beautiful and easily accessible.  
the shops around it offer a great variety of goods,  It is amazing to watch the preservation work thatis continually happening.
Not worth it in winter, flowers not in bloom and grass dead. Cafe nice but expensive. Don't bother at this time of year.

This is a very impressive Stupa. Obviously by the number of worshipers walking round ringing the bells its an important place for them. There are loads of shops selling local gifts as well as the usual hawkers but they don't seem pushy.
It is an interesting place to visit. Elderly people can avoid it as they my find it bit suffocating.
it is small but fantastic David falls bottom observation. Temple and naturally art inside. marvelous and amazing day tours around pokhara

Hotel is general is great! Amazing service and delicious food :)  at the beggining we though room was small and a little old to be a 5 start hotel, but later we got used to it and they told us they are just staring renovations so I’m pretty sure it will soon be new and a lot better :)
It's a standard tourist location. Nothing to write home about. But, I did hear that someone fell over the rail and they never found the body. So, be careful. lol!

Fantastic food, very good ambience and lovely and friendly staff. Especially remarkable staff  like Mr Narottam, Mr Madan & Mr Anjal have done wonderful service. 
Good DDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDFFDDDDDDDDDDDD………………………….,,,,…

The location is amaaaaazing and I am sure that when it was constructed that hotel must have blowed your mind. But not now. The service was poor, we had to continous ask for champus and water because the cleaning service will forget to do this kind of things. There is no fitness studio, no sauna, etc, which was really a pity as we had three days of raining when we stayed there. 
The massage "spa" place is ridiculous and the massagist does no even know what is a muscle (no real training for massage). She did not speak well English either, so it was like talking to a wall. 
On the last day, we asked for breakfast to take away as we were leaving the hotel quite soon and instead of giving us breakfast for two, they did for one person only. Not even that they could manage... So, great great great location but bad service.

My husband and I went along today with our books and relaxed for a few hours and then wandered around. 
The Garden was stunning and the staff were lovely. Lots of people taking pictures of themselves 😂. 
It was a wonderful experience and we'll be good back again before we leave to experience it in the evening as suggested in other reviews.

Work on the Stupa is still ongoing, and so, currently, there is not much to see apart from a lot of tourist stands, souvenirs and restaurants. 

Still good to have gone, also a good spot for some people watching.

Today we had family dinner at Soaltee, whole ambience and peaceful atmosphere was very amazing. It was a very warm welcome. Foods were fantastic and the service is great. We were served by amazing staffs, Janak and Subharaj. We really appreciate their dedication towards their work and service. We felt really welcome and we really enjoyed the whole experience. Thank you Soaltee and thank you Kakori Soaltee staffs.

The property is very good. The service is average, even to the nepali standards. Good spread for breakfast. No views worth mentioning. Stayed there for 2 days and I was happy that I didn't have to stay inside the hotel.
Good place make sure to visit. Also make it a point to visit nearby cave. Difficult steps and a little lighting but the view at the bottom is verified good.

A rather strange smelling gorge in the middle of Pokhara city, this (natural ? ) Miniscule water fall could be on your itinerary while you are in Pokhara if only you have nothing else to do.
A bright spark has made a commercial enterprise out of the water flow by immersing an idol in a small pond and taking the gullible tourist for a ride by asking them to throw overpriced coins on the toy.
Having said that, the manicured small lawn has a few clean benches for the weary traveller to relax and contemplate the meaning of life.
Another tourist focussed venture in Pokhara.
Not recommended.
Interesting stupa if you like that sort of thing. Lots of pleasant eateries in the area. Not impressed that tourists are charged more to visit these places

If you go early in the morning on a weekend there are lots of mass prayers and it’s a very calm, enjoyable day. The coffee shops near by are a great place to sit and watch everyone and watch the world go by.

Across the road from the Davis Falls, lies this cave. As you enter and exit, you'll encounter a lot of shops selling handicrafts, souvenirs and local stuff. Be sure to haggle!

There is a fee to enter this cave, You need to walk down some roundabout steps before entering the actual caves. The caves also lead down into the ground to some extent. Many of the places in the cave were under repair and there was water dripping. The ground can be slippery. Thankfully, these caves have lighting inside. There is also the customary Hindu shrine in the cave.

At the end of the caves, you can see the Davis Falls from a distance. Since there was not much water, there was nothing much to see.

I guess it is worth a visit but don't expect a major cave system.

Unlike the Monkey Temple where Entrance is FREE, here visitors are required to pay to gain entrance. Fee for foreign visitors  is 250 NPR, cheaper for locals.

The Stupa is similar to those of the Monkey Temple. There are no steps to climb here. Along the way are shops and restaurants. Very commercialized areas for my taste!

One of the famous attraction in Kathmandu is Boudhanath stupa and that’s why it is very crowded. The stupa is huge and visible even from the flight. The entire stupa is surrounded by various shops and restaurants. You will see devotees, monks, caretakers, shopkeepers and also beggars. Good place to visit during your visit to Kathmandu.
We went to see Devi's Fall with lot of expectations in mind but sorry to say we were greatly disappointed to see the size and view
A nice way to spend an afternoon after the trek. It’s only a short taxi drive from Thamel but couldn’t be more different. Have a drink on one of the rooftop cafes
It is a small place to visit. take 15-20 min to complete the visit. Good architectural religious place.

I just love the way staffs were treating us and outsiders. Lovely gesture professional staffs. They even help in celebrating my parents 25th anniversary. Very cooperative. I will visit again whenever I visit Nepal. Thank you hotel shankar for amazing experience.

Stayed here for work in July 2016 for three weeks. The hotel is situated in a rather isolated location although only about a 15 min taxi ride from Thamel provided reasonable traffic. The hotel sits on a huge property with its neatly presented landscaped gardens. A very refreshing experience given the dustiness of Kathmandu proper.

Rooms:
Aged rooms but very generous in size. Newly refurbished bathrooms with good lighting. Large windows, sofa and a desk all within the room. Slightly weird that the sofa is located in the opposite direction of the TV and the desk is also facing away from the TV. 

Internet
Poor wifi signal in my room which made it very difficult to have Skype calls back home or for work. Wifi seemed to work fine in the lobby with a strong signal.

Gym:
Probably one of the WORST gyms I have frequented at all IHG hotels. It's small, poorly equipped, no ventilation, poorly lit and worst of all, wooden floor which makes equipment such as bench slide. Quite dangerous really. Please please improve the gym given how pricey the hotel rates are. There's also a sauna and outdoor pool I believe but didn't test it out

Location
Not much around but then again, it wasn't that far by taxi to anywhere in Kathmandu unless there's traffic. Dining option outside of the hotel is very limited and mainly just local Nepali food.

Breakfast
Limited choice but the staff working at the restaurant was so nice and efficient. Really appreciate the morning coffee as well as the take away coffee that was generous prepared for me every morning.

Overall, a suitable hotel for a long business trip. However rating downgraded due to the extremely poor gym facility - hugely disappointing. Fantastic staff though who were always willing to help.

The garden of dreams is a walled in botanical area in a more European style. It is a nice quiet retreat from the overcrowded and loud streets surrounding it, but if visitors are willing to pay the 400 rupees admission, they should be aware that the garden if dreams is not very big and in my opinion nothing special. I did not visit the cafe, which I heard is nice.

The room are so small and cramp.  The ceilings have characters because it is painted with designs.  The lobby is being renovated when we were there.  I was hoping for little more space to move around.  The bathrooms are even smaller for a top rated hotel.  The location is good because it is walking distance to town.  The set up of the room and bathroom are very awkward.

Ticket is overpriced for foreigners. There’s nothing special in it. I found local teenagers come here for dating. Its nothing but nicely organized small park. If you have enough time to pass a lazy evening in KTM then you can come here otherwise skip the place.

Devil`s Fall (together with that Cave next to it) is a fine place to visit if you have a couple of days to spend here and have nothing much to do. 
Don`t expect to see a great waterfall as it doesn`t look that impressive. Same about the cave. But the price is silly (less than 1 euro or something) so if you want to get out of your hotel or are tired of shopping, just come and take a look. The secret is -  don`t expect much and you will probably be satisfied :)

Standard rooms are small. Bathroom is too small. Bath tub and toilet seat somehow make between the two walls. . Breakfast is ok but no fresh fruits. hard bed and very poor wifi reception which often goes off and front desk can;t do anything about it during night. Overall, an overpriced hotel. Don;t call taxi thru the hotel front desk. There would be a good markup. You may get much better price if you reach the road and walk left for 50 yards. Avoid taxis near the

Going down to cave was little thrilling . Semidarkness and wet stairs always remind to be careful. One or two electric bulb gives you the glimpse of the surrounding . Half of the there is Shiva Lingam..The cave is 150 meter deep . At the we saw a water fall though the opening of the rock .May be the same flow of Devis Fall.On the surface like all other attractions of Nepal there are souvenir shops.

I'm still blown away by Sajina and Abhaya's incredible customer service., they went out of their way to help me find a solution. Their patience and kindness really made a difference. The food are amazing, the ambiance is great. Go go go go be GREAT always!

Special thanks to Aryaman, Rohan & Saroj  for there superb service. We recently visited patio restaurant which has welcoming atmosphere with great food ( pizza n spaghetti was best)  and charming outdoor dining experience with lovely songs.

I am staying in this Hotel at now actually. There is a nice small garden, but there is not a refrigerator in the rooms  and regard  to  traditional door lock ,it is not comfort  to realize the safety and security. Staffs are polite and cooperative.

Excellent service and friendly staff  highly recommended. Nice and delicious food with lots of of options. Very clean and neat and fantastic views around. Highly recommended 
 .🙏❤️❤️

Just opp to Devi`s falls is the entrance to this wonderful cave temple, I went there on 28th August, when I entered into the cave it was thrilling with water droplets falling in our head , after going in, squatting in some places I saw a cow,

When we go deep into the cave we can see a absolutely blissful naturally formed Shivling, it was so unique and Blissful !!!

We have to pay a small entrance fees to enter the cave, and phography is not allowed inside the cave.

When we sit in silence after doing all the formalities, we will be absolutely peaceful and feeling relaxed.

Thanks a lot for everything,
Loving you so much,
Peacefully yours.
S M Bega Raaj.
Happy travelling...
💘 ❤ 💘

When we visited this place no sufficient water was flowing at that time. However, it was very beautiful place and there was also story behind this. Entrance fee is very cheaper.Surroundings are very appealing with greenery.

Had a very good view of water gushing in to the hole- the flow was good due to monsoon. I loved the misty atmosphere around the fall- did not understand the reason of the concrete walkways and grill railings painted blue though.
I'm running a taxi in Pokhara city and you may call up this cab anytime from any place of Pokhara city 🙏

The falls are nice but nothing to rave about. I did expect it to be a lot bigger and more beautiful than it was. 
I walked there from lakeside and then got a taxi back. 
Didn’t stay for long. There were a few sections which showed lovely photos of the falls but most of it was fenced off (for obvious reasons) but it was then difficult to see.

I loved my stay at the Soaltee. Perfect location - easy to get to the centre of Kathmandu to see the sights, yet situated in its own gardens so it’s a lovely breath of fresh air when you get back.

There are always taxis at the hotel that you can take to see the sights. I never had to wait more than a couple of minutes for one. They were happy to take me places, wait for me while I looked round, then pick me up again. Easier than trying to find a taxi when I was ready to leave somewhere.

The front desk of the hotel was able to exchange money to Nepalese rupees at the same rate to what I saw elsewhere. I took GBP which was easy to exchange.

My room had international/ universal  as well as local plug sockets.

All the staff were so friendly and helpful. I would love to come back.

Amazing service from two ladies( Kunchhen and  Sajina) at rodi Bar who constantly made sure I was comfortable .
Overall the greenery and ambience is relaxing , full of positive vibes plus relaxing music.
Clean and neat place  at Rodi bar and  kunchhen has an amazing and cheer full smile .
.
This is a beautiful stupa surrounded by shops and places to eat with a Tibetan feel. If you are visiting Kathmandu this World Heritage sight is a must to visit.

The caves ahead are beautiful. Good to explore how the falls were lost and went further ahead into the caves which is a different story all together. Still sort of an undiscovered place, it still has the making of being a place for dumping every waste material known to man. Like I have seen here in India. Hope they can keep the place beautiful. And well, clean.

Had a wonderful dining experience at the restaurant in Soaltee Hotel. The food was delicious, The ambiance was relaxing and perfect for an enjoyable meal. The service was excellent as well, with the staff being attentive and friendly. A special mention to Sajja, who went above and beyond to ensure we had a great time. Highly recommended!

I walked from Thamel to reach this Stupa, probably in not more than 1.5 hours.

I expected the entrance fee to be Rs. 200 but the sign indicated Rs. 400.  Feeling not very pleased, I decided to experiment the “evil” idea I had had for some time. I walked casually past the staff sitting at the entrance, with eye fixated at my phone. Not too surprisingly, I was not challenged and I have avoided the entrance fee ! Which was the most exhilarating element in this Bodhnath visit :-)
 
I was allowed to climb up the first level of the stupa and walk around. I also climbed the opposite Guru Lhakhang Gompa and took a couple more pictures. After a long lunch in one of the restaurants ("Chengdu") circling the stupa, I left and walked the 6-7 km back to Thamel.

First of all, I didn't expect something like that in heart of city life. But when I faced it, I was stuck with the beauty of it. You know some beauty brings with danger too. And you may feel this while enjoying the view. How forcefully the water comes and falls in so deep is really stunning to watch. But thanks to the management, they've provided safety railing around the fall, still be safe to visit there especially at the time of rain. 

My overall experience is Awesome. Visit there if you go to Pokhara, I bet you'll say the same.

This is the third time i am staying in a "palace" in south asia and each time it has been the same story. First if you decide to anyways stay at this hotel please avoid the restaurant. In a place which looks like Miss Havisham's home from Great expectations...the restaurant is even more Havishamish(for a lack of a better word). The rooms are small, very basic, the food terrible and the staff not very much in the Know. I would stay in this hotel if the price is about USD 30 not the kind of money they charge. They dont have a spa on premise(they advertise for a spa in the city). The breakfast spread is very basic. Again as i said its habitable like a basic hotel would be but if you are looking for luxury and size and are willing to pay for it please avoid.
For the first time we saw such a huge Cave Temple below the ground. The cave at the bottom connects to the Davis Waterfall.

Honestly speaking, there is not much to see. It is a garden. Definitely unusual for Kathmandu, but there are thousands and thousands of those across Europe. I don't want to diminish his beauty, but I think people overdo it. Everyone is talking about some peace and quiet, and in the garden itself, noise is heard from the street and from the construction sites surrounding it.
It's worth seeing, but don't expect too much
went by, saw it. took some pictures. but i didn't find it to have that "wow" factor. Obviously if you're in town, its one of the main must see attractions. so go see it.

I'd read the reviews for Fishtail before leaving, so I kind of knew what to expect, but it doesn't stop you still being a bit disappointed by the whole experience. 
The management and staff at Fishtail seem to live of this air that it's an exclusive resort that we are all lucky to be staying at with the (yawn) heritage of all their famous guests. Well look carefully people, when was the last time you had anyone rich, famous or powerful staying there?? According to your own proud posters, about 25 years ago (if you exclude Betty Boothroyd's visit in 1994). So yes, about 25 years ago, which to my reckoning, should be when the place was refurbished and cleaned up, cos it certainly hasn't been since then!!!
To be fair though, there was some refurbishment work going on in the two story building when we were there.
Out two night stay there was part of our honeymoon. We actually spoke to reception and mentioned it was our honeymoon and could we upgrade to one of the lake view rooms. By the way, we hadn't asked for a free upgrade, if it was reasonable we might have considered it. The guy on reception didn't even acknowledge anything we had just told him, and just gave us this long spiel about how these were the rooms that the dignitaries stayed in (yes we know, yawn) and therefore bound to be at least twice the rate we were paying. To be honest, we didn't even pursue it after that, this guy was so far up his own ****side we couldn't be bothered!
 I have to be honest, overall this is the most unwelcoming and unfriendly reception I have ever come across.
We were shown to our room, where all the doors and windows were wide open, we walked in and it stank of damp. The smell seemed to go when we put the a/c on but as there were so many power cuts it was a constant battle. 
Apart from that, and the obvious need for a refurb, it was ok. We had neighbours on both sides and didn't hear them so I guess it was well insulated! 
The hotel restaurant buffet and a la carte menus were pretty basic and the food quality was mediocre. We had much better, cheaper and more authentic food when we ventured out over the road / lake. Didn't try the spa, but my husband used the pool a couple of times to cool off and said it was nice. 
The grounds of the hotel and its location are really the best and only things going for Fishtail Lodge. I guess, because of that they don't have a lot of competition. But really, up your game Fishtail, you could be such an amazing place to stay.

If you're into waterfalls go there. The water falls into a gorge (a dark pit) and due to pressure water oozes out upwards from down below. From above visitors hear the water hit the bottom, but can't see how deep the gorge is.

Also has a nice garden with shades to cool off.
Best stupa in Nepal 🇳🇵to understand Buddhist culture and monk. I like that huge stupa with beautiful Buddha eyes.
Good place but little bet hard to reach there BCS of the way ,I didn't got any thing to special ,,,,

Every time I visit Pokhara, I do visit Devi's Fall too. Nepal, being rich in it's season, every time you visit you will see different view of Devi's Fall due to the season change. In summer, or in rainy season there'll be abundance amount of water while in winter or off season water'll be in it's lowest (March). 
Devi's Fall is also known as 'Patale Jhango' in Nepali.
A must visit place. From here you can also visit Gupteshwor Mahadev (Cave beneath the ground). This is the lowest part of Devi's Fall. You can view the end part of Devi's fall flowing beneath this ground, from Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave.

Had a great stay at Hotel Shanker - the room was very cosy and comfortable. We ate dinner and breakfast at the hotel, and all the food was great, with lots of options. The staff are super friendly, and we could exchange currency at the front desk easily, which was very handy.

I also arranged for the hotel to pick me up from the airport, and this went very smoothly. Would recommend.

These are the caves that take you quite a way underground which opens out to see the waterfall at the end.Under construction as I said but well worth the time to visit.Looking forward to seeing the completed stairs to enter the cave.It will be amazing
Interesting and worth a look but wouldn’t make a special trip to see this. Could be difficult walking for elderly and those with a disability

We had clue about this cave...but when we went,it was impressively large cave and there was a lord shiva ling...the place was well lit..was impressed! there is anew temple being constructed out side so probably due to that the place was little untidy.but a must visit.
It is one of the adventure place in Pokhara. It is nearer to Gupteshwore Cave and on the way to Peace Pagoda. You can see the amazing flow that gets disappeared in the earth.

A public bus from Lakeside costs 20 nepali rupees and takes less than 10 min, ask the conductor if the bus is going to Devi´s fall because some of them go to other part of the city. If you go to damside road near Lakeside road every bus passing at this road goes to Devi´s fall. Entrance fee is 30 rupees for locals and foreigners, so a round trip visit to this place from your hotel in Lakeside is no more than 100 rupees or U$ 1,00 but take the chance and visit also Gupteshwor cave in right front of it, entrance fee 100 rupees wich willm make your tour U$ 2,00, will you save it in your AC hotel room ?

nice and quite place to explore 
Morning time is the best i like morning sun coming  over Stupa. 
Prayer flags and monestery are the top.

Entrance is inexpensive, but it's such a meh attraction why bother to visit? You see the fall from a distance behind metal bars. Also on the grounds are a lame mini Annapurna range, a shack with cropped out national costumes that you can take picture with and a tiny buddha placed in a bird cage structure (presumably to protect it). Give it a miss please and save your time for a cafe!

We stayed here for two nights whilst in Pokhara. The rooms are dated but adequate, but what was frustrating was the lack of wifi. We only had a free voucher for one device in the room, and the signal was patchy at best. This lack of connectability has not been an issue in any other hotel or restaurant in Pokhara so it seemed odd to pay this much money and be so limited.

Breakfast was adequate but ruined by badly behaved children rampaging loudly around the restaurant; their parents didn't seem to believe in discipline and good manners.

The staff were very friendly and were the highlight of the stay, along with the attractive grounds. 
Expensive for the experience.

Loved the hotel, the room and the grounds.  Was looking forward to 4 days of rest and relaxation. Unfortunately, we experienced a strike by the hotel staff that cut our stay short. Very disappointing that we couldn't stay longer, but most disappointing was the assistance we received in making new reservations. Hotel staff made reservations for us at what they told us would be a suitable replacement hotel. Sadly, it was far below standard and unacceptable. I understood their difficulty of dealing with the strike, but was most disappointed in their assistance to help us continue to have a good family trip.

You will have the feeling of ancient cave as you descend and there are a number of people going so nothing to be scared of. You can have some really good pics of the place and the small opening you see has a beautiful view of the waterfall inside the cave.

We visited this place as part of an organised tour. However, if you are going on your own, I would not bother. There is a minimal entry fee but this is not the problem. The falls themselves are nothing special but are made worse by high steel bars as fencing that completely block whatever view is available and take away any natural beauty of the place.  On any trek around Pokhara you will see much nicer waterfalls. In my view, there are much better things to do with your time in Pokhara.

Okay, so this is a Crowne Plaza and a hotel with a history in Kathmandu, but compared to a boutique cheapy I stayed in afterward, I wasn't very impressed. The meeting facilities were adequate and the food is good, but there ware a couple of things that really disappointed for the price.
The in-room wifi was okay, when it worked. It frequently didn't work. It would drop out and not come back on for hours, or it would drop in and out making work impossible and browsing a frustrating experience.
The other thing was the noise. I was just unlucky with the room, I guess, but considering I was one of the first at the conference to book in, they should have given me a better room and left mine empty or at least the last assigned. It was right above the diesel generator and since the power frequently went out it would start and stop often. It was uncomfortably loud.
To be fair I was approached by hotel staff each morning at breakfast and asked how everything was. When I complained about the noise they suggested I could go to reception and asked for a different room. I had already unpacked for a week stay and didn't want to be bothered re-packing to relocate. I regretted that more and more as the week progressed.
Finally, this hotel is a fair way from anything. It is a big compound that has a few shops, but no convenience store. So it was quite a walk to go to the shop for snacks or anything.
On the plus side, my room was one that has been renovated recently and the bathroom was good. Great shower actually. The room was not large, but big enough. The bed was comfortable.

Devi's Falls was not only crowded but certainly not worth the time it took us to walk there. The river runs from Phewa Lake and disappears into a tunnel after reaching the site. There are a series of stairs that lead down into the tunnel and you can see the underground cave, complete with stalagmites. The day we were there, the line up of visitors was so long that it took 45 minutes to complete the tour. We were very disappointed in the hype of this attraction and the reality of it!

I’ve arrived at the hotel late at night, it is a beautiful hotel, nice courtyard, nice classical interior decorations etc., I was told it was once a palace. I had a good night rest. Their MoMo (steam dumplings and milk tea was good), because I’ve to depart very early, the hotel kitchen has prepare breakfast takeaway (sandwiches, fruits, drink and boiled eggs) for me. But lights went off two times for a few minutes during my short stay there. Overall it was an okay experience. Check in check out process was fast.

We stayed five nights at hotel Shanker. It's a very beautiful hotel. We arrived earlier than the check-in time and got our room right away. The common areas were clean and calm and the staff very friendly. Our room was also clean, but had mold. The bathroom was otherwise fine but had a really terrible smell at times. It smelled usually when it hadn't been used for a while, for example every morning when we woke up and in the evening when we came back after spending the whole day out. 

Breakfast wasn't included but we bought breakfast one morning for 14 US dollars per person, which we think is quite expensive. The breakfast buffet was good.

The location is really good and it's close to Thamel. Good and reliable WiFi which also works in the pool area. Taxis were available all the time in front of the hotel. There were weddings in the hotel almost every evening, but it didn't bother us. We didn't hear any noise from the parties to our room.

The hotel is one of the better hotels in Kathmandu. The rooms are adequate but somewhat cramped. The staff are friendly and the loby unfortunately is overcrowded with day visitors at sunset coming for drinks. The disappointing experience was that we had arranged an early breakfast but the dining room was not open.
The staff is amazing! So helpful! They help me and they are very attentive to customer needs thank you so much! Im looking forward coming back

The time was when for two days it was raining and somehow god gave us chance to move out and we happen to visit here. Water flow was high and one could feel the pressure or force with which the water was entering the falls. Worth a visit when in Pokhara....even when in non-rainy season, it would be amazing.
Nothing special. Standard maintained park with some flower sighting. Not worth the entry fee, you can find such thing anywhere.
David's fall aka Patale Chhango , marks the point where the Pardi Khola stream vanishes underground.
A terrific piece of architecture in a run-down part of town...once you've paid to get in, there's enough to keep you occupied around the stupa for an hour or so.

This stupa is surprising in that from the street it seems like a regular street, but once you walk in the area is quite charming. It is large and essentially you may just walk around and take pictures. It is surprisingly peaceful and serene compared to what is happening around it.
We visited the Stupa as part of a Kathmandu day tour. Of all the locations, I found this place to be the most welcoming and full of smiling faces.

I was there around the last week of November during a day tour and i loved the place. The perfect place for meditations and to hang out as well.The surrounding was amazing too. I recommend to visit the place atleast once!!
Peace environment can visit for away from your stressful life but getting more crowded then before good for sunset view from rooftops restaurants
buddha natha is for praying and enjoy with family peoples are so nice and good market to buy thanka!!
There is a cover charge of rs200 per person and is beautiful garden owned by the king. Main attraction is kaiser cafe Resturant. Worth trying the peanut starter and momos.

Nice, clean rooms, very good breakfast buffet, attentive staff. Request receipts for everything you charge to your room. Their accounting is not accurate to put it mildly. Wifi is on and off. Music by the pool a bit too loud.

I stay here for a few days and I am very impresioned about the hotel staff and the old architecture of this hotel. A quiet place with good food and big court with a nice swiming pool, exact you need to recreate in KTM.

I stayed at this hotel with my wife for two nights either side of a trekking trip. The rooms were grubby (though not full on filthy) and the beds were appalling - hard with not so fresh looking linen and blankets. At this price, this place should be offering a much higher standard of service. Hotel prices are going up rapidly in Nepal and there is obviously an attitude that they can get away with charging for poor quality accommodation. 

Nice pool though.
Great stupa with a circular street of shops, coffee houses, restaurants and lodging. Very clean and enchanting. Great place to spend a half day

The place is beautiful with a huge water fall in Monsoon. During dry season, the water fall is ok. You have to go down by the Gupteshwor Cave to take some glimpse of the water of the water fall. The are has good souvenir shops. 
Once is enough to visit this place.

Hotel Shanker is located centrally in Lazimpat, ideal for visiting the different places around Kathmandu. It’s an old palace converted to a hotel and has the natural old world charm. There’s a lovely garden in the front with a swimming pool for enjoyment during the hot days. Lots of good amenities, restaurant and bar and also a spa. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Highly recommend.

We stayed several days in several different rooms due to in and out for hikes around the country. Consistently exceptional was the staff, helpful, professional, friendly, no areas for improvement, very top notch. Breakfast consistently exceptional. Area that desperately needs improvement is the WiFi reception. While in the cheap small 4th floor (main floor close to lobby) WiFi was great. Upgrading to a pricier suite when all the family was assembled had no WiFi. Usually this wouldn’t be an issue for me but with a 5 week absence from work I had committed to answering emails every few days. WiFi is now a staple, not a Luxury. Even cheap hostels in Thailand have super fast WiFi, so a high end place in Kat should be able to manage this. For this reason they get a 3 star.

The place is nothing out of the ordinary. Dried grass dirty pond. 
I went with my friends to take some pictures with y DSRL. Since my camera looked a bit better than a normal mobile camera I was harassed by a guard not to take pictures. 
It was very uncomfortable trying to have fun with my friends taking picture while a guard was all the time there making sure I didn't take "commercial photos". 

Again. The garden is nothing out of the ordinary. I've seen better public gardens in other places. 

Bad idea to go there.
The Stupa is surrounded by shops and therefore, is quite a touristy place. Many visitors are taking selfies of themselves rather than of the Stupa.
This is a must see if you are in Kathmandu... So you can tell your friends: I have been there! We didn’t go in - we just walked outside.

The website for this hotel is misleading.  The place suffered significant damage in the earthquake of 2015, and it is still under repair.  The grounds and facade are still being repaired, and the interior is damp.  Our room had such moisture problems that even our room service menu pages were stuck together with dampness.
In spite of this, our stay was reasonable, and their travel desk agent was exceptionally helpful in helping organize our week in Nepal - in Kathmandu, Pokhara, and Chitwan.

We didn't have a great experience at this hotel, we had to ask to change rooms twice (smoking rooms with 3 kids?? when there were plenty of floors with non-smoking rooms available) and the second rooms offered had overwhelming paint fumes (triggered breathing issues for 2/5 of the family) due to being put on the "Undergoing Renovations" floor.  Third time lucky - the rooms were average at best. The staff were mildly responsive to our requests to find a decent room (actually 2 rooms, as we were a family of 5) but they didn't go out of their way and let us know we were being difficult. This hotel is in a good location, and the grounds were pleasant, but it's not one we'd come back to in Kathmandu. Check out took over 20 minutes.

beautiful architecture! the stairs down to the cave are really impressive. loved how everything was overgrown. the cave itself is less impressive, you need to walk barefeet some more wet stairs down to find a hindu temple down there. photos or videos are not allowed. sadly the 2nd part was due to too much water closed. entry fee is 50rps, which is absolutely worth it.

Lots of slippery steps, down down into a cave. The lower part is closed due to flooding. It is right across from the waterfall and we combined it with out taxi trip up to rhe World Peace Stupa. It’s right in the middle of a strip mall. Good for a quick stop but would be ok to miss unless it has religious meaning to you.

I've been there several times in  past yrs. Interesting in that the falls dissapear into a cavern. Across the road you can descend into a cavernous tunnel & see where the falls enter. Note: you can't enter the cavern during the monsoon rains, even tho they still sell tickets!

Hotel Shanker is located in an old colonial building about 10-15 minutes walk from Thamel. While situated nicely - away from the noise of Thamel, it is let down by the service.

- The Hotel in a guarded and gated compound so safety is pretty good. However, when walking back from Thamel at night, you will need to stay alert as you need to cross two busy roads.

- Service was a let down at the hotel. Check in staff were unhelpful and unfriendly.

- The rooms were large and clean but nothing exceptional. USB ports and universal power sockets were available which was a plus. Otherwise, the furniture and decor were functional but tired looking. 

- Wifi was available in the room. Speed was slow during peak times - breakfast and night.

- Breakfast was available each morning in a large dining hall. An egg station was available but was not particularly interesting. The highlight however were the different curries served each morning. 

- An outdoor pool is available - but unheated. Though perfectly fine after a day of walking the streets and temples.

- Typically, I don't go to the hotel restaurant for dinner. However, rather than crossing the busy roads at night, we stayed for dinner for one night. Food was good, though it was more Indian than Nepalese. The room service menu was different and significantly cheaper than the restaurant. If the weather is good, recommend having the room service meal delivered to you by the poolside.

Overall, the hotel is basic (by Western standards) and provides some sanctuary after a day of walking around the city. If the service improved, it would be even better.

It is a nice place with a unique background story . It was on July 31, 1961, when a Swiss couple Mr and Mrs Davis made their visit to this enchanting place. Little did they know that their adventure was about to take a dark turn. While bathing in its water, the overflow pushed the woman in a sinkhole where she drowned. Her body was recovered after three days. It was at her father's request that the fall was named Davis Fall.
every day i go see the stupa, always impressive, very good ambiance, people making koras (walking in circle, clockwise, around the stupa)

They were very helpful with everything the service was excellent they even brought me a heater when I told them I’m feeling cold they are amazing the hotel cleanliness the gym spa and also the breakfast was also excellent the hotel crew lounge was also very good we have got drinks thank you
This a cave .There are steps to go down.It is well lit.You have a excellent view of Davis fall from the bottom of this cave which is unique
Stupa is brilliant & strikingly beautiful too. A sense of calm while walking around clockwise. Quaint architecture of nearby shops & houses with typical Nepali style.

Ive got a very good customer service experience with staff name BIGYAN. He is just awesome with his superb service, he is very attentive, very helpful, and he is always with his smile. BIGYAN is an asset to Soaltee. 

Hotel environment is peaceful, soothing and clean. But the room has too many wood element that make the room old and stuffy.

great water fall. it's not that big but very interesting!
not bad for one time. there were lots of people....
It is a good to visit place not must visit. please check the opening hours before your visit. It is always crowded. If you are looking for photographing this place try to get there as early possible.

Nice hotel, good staff but on this occasion the pool was not very inviting having turned a not very nice green colour .... apparently due to recent rains ?! A shame since we'd booked the hotel for the pool.   Otherwise room was comfortable and clean with good ac and breakfast buffet was great.

The 2nd largest stupa in the world, a sacred place for Tibetan Buddhist, beautiful and interesting. Surrounded by decorated 3 storages houses, shops and restaurants. It’s peaceful to walk around clock wise, spin the prayers wheel and immerse on the Buddhist tradition.

Went here as it's a must when in Kathmandu. Like most places it's beautiful but your never to far away from someone trying to sell you something and large crowds of annoying people. The spiritual side of this stupa is in my opinion lost to the tourism industry and the large crowds of people trying to take selfies.
this is a very interesting place,you cannot miss it i think that this i s a very important and nice stupa,a very impressive place

Given that this is listed as a significant tourist attraction, I was disappointed at how unattractive this cave was. It is not very big and has none of the natural decorations that one expects in a cave. There is a long flight of concrete stairs, a short tunnel, and a viewpoint where one can catch a glimpse of a small waterfall inside the cave. There was no aesthetic appeal and I got out as soon as I could. There are various stores around the entrance selling the usual tourist trinkets. There is also a small shrine in the cave but it did not offer any particular appeal. I would give this "attraction" a pass unless you are interested in killing some time.

The garden charges half price for children, suggesting they are welcome, but they are not. Our kids were just playing, not particularly noisy or annoying anyone, just kids being kids. But a security guard came and brusquely and angrily said that kids are not allowed to play in the garden. My kids were so intimidated by this rude and imposing guard that they wanted to leave immediately. So while not physically kicked out, the end result was pretty much that. We hardly spent any time there as it happened very soon after entering. As for my experience going alone without kids and thus not shood off the property, the garden is a decent place to hangout in the middle of the polluted Thamel area, but you cannot bring your own food and the restaurant was not great - being a resident of Thamel I've tried many of the restaurants in the area and can confidently say that Thamel has many better options, including those at a much more reasonable price.

I wouldn't go to far out of my way to see this. I'm not sure if it has some spiritual significance but it appeared popular with local school groups. It's a fall that goes underground so not particularly spectacular as a sight.

This place is more like a decent garden cafe anywhere else, but I guess is a very nice refuge from the immediate chaos right outside the gates.  However I don't know why you would come here unless you plan on having some coffee or a light meal.  Decent gardens, but could use more native varieties.

I stayed at this hotel last December. The first 3 nights were through a tour and the last night was a direct booking so during check in I informed the front desk asking for an upgraded room (as I had spire elite status) so that I didn't have to change rooms. They assured me that this was going to be the case. I checked into my room which was old, filthy and had a terrible smell. 2 nights later I looked up on my direct reservation and it said it was supposed to be a mountain view room which I wasn't given. I was extremely annoyed so I talked to the manager. He offered me to transfer me to a room but I didn't care to pack up and move again as I had to clean the room using anti-bacterial wipes. I simply didn't care to go through the process again. As I told the manager, knowing this could happen, I specifically asked to be given the right (upgraded) room during my initial check-in to avoid the unnecessary inconvenience of moving again yet this hotel failed. I am therefore hugely disappointed by this hotel and the management. I did provide feedback as soon as I returned and received a useless apology email.  IHG needs to seriously reconsider their licensing agreement with this sub-standard hotel.
lot of water everywhere as the place is under construction.... no clear directions and no guides available
Its a really small but nice waterfall. Its all guarded by railings so safe with kids. If you have free time, its good to go and see this falls.

When I first saw the falls - it just amazed me. Such a beauty! It is huge and you will hear its roar from a distance. You actually can not drown yourself in the falls - as there is a boundary. There should be as its dangerous as well. True, all most beautiful things in the world are dangerous as well. You need a ticket of RS 20 only. ITs worth it. also you will enjoy the surrounded view - gardens etc. I think the falls is one of the most beautiful thing I have seen in Nepal-Pokhara. Worth visiting. But make sure - when you go, there should be enough water in the falls.

this has to be one of the most stunning Buddhist temples ever. Surrounded by a Bazaar housing so many souvenir shops n Tibetan restaurants this place is so lively,  must visit when in Kathmandu, and do remember to take loads of pictures of this stunning Buddhist temple

water is gudhing thru the tunnel underneth the busy streets and vanishes into tunnel,
view from top and the garden on top is nice for photo in local dress dols.
located in busy place in city.

We had originally been booked into another hotel and quickly relocated to Hotel Barahi. From start to finish our experience was wonderful. The staff are amazing, so helpful and kind. The service and amenities are second to none and the view of the Annapurna mountains from our room was breathtaking.

It is said that Devi fell in the gorge and so it was called Devi's Fall.

If you prefer, follow these:

1. Take a short stroll along the lake side road (towards Basundhara Park) and go to Dam Side Park (ask locals how you can walk there) (15-20 mins walk). Cost: a coffee or cigarette for yourself.

2. Once you're done at the Dam Side Park, get out of the park, cross the road and wave at the next bus. Ask if the bus goes to Devi's Fall (some people also call it David Fall)

3. Get in the bus and ask the bus conductor to stop you near Devi's Fall. (Cost: NPR 30).

4. Once off the bus, look for the "Welcome to Devi's Fall" sign across the road. Go through little alley (entry cost: NPR 20 for Nepalese citizens, NPR 30 for all others).

5. Once you exit Devi's Fall and you're back on the road, cross the road and go to your right (say around 100yards/meters) and you will see the entrance to Mahendra Cave and Guptshwar Mahadev. Follow the signs: they are in English too (entry cost: NPR 10 for Nepalese citizens, NPR 30 for all others. If you see Kamadhenu cow as well, it is optional, it will cost additional NPR 10)

6. Once you're out on the road, go towards your left for about 250yards/meters where you can catch buses to the World Peace Pagoda (costs up to NPR 100). Ask the locals if you can't find the bus stand (there are no signs). No, don't walk to the Stupa unless you're in a big group. Walk is scenic but QUIET (less travelled) and steep. You never know what kind of people you may encounter on the way. Be safe than sorry!

7. Once out of the Stupa, catch a cab (costs NPR 800; 1000 max) to Lake side!

Voila!

Devi’s Falls are where the huge Phewa Lake in Pokhara disappears down a narrow but deep waterfall at the dam end of the lake. You might think the waterfalls are set in a large open area set in hillsides, but alas you will need to get a taxi or bus there and you will need to look for the entrance gate along the busy street filled with shops and people. Walk inside and buy a ticket for a few rupees, and make your way along the paths and right at the end you will be surprised to see a very narrow but very deep waterfall which they say in the monsoon season is powerful with a big water spray. The area is very popular with local Nepali people so perhaps visit there on any day but a Saturday, which is the weekend holiday in Nepal, otherwise wander along with the crowds to view the falls through a high metal fence. There is a bit of a mystery about the naming of the falls involving some foreigners who were swept into the Falls so they are now known as Devi’s Falls. After visiting the Falls, make sure you cross the road to visit the spectacular Gupteswar Mahadev cave as deep down underground in the cave can see an opening in the rocks where the Devi’s Falls pour underground. A fascinating area to visit to see how the mountains, lake, rivers and caves are connected, especially if you are interested in geology.

Boudhanath Stupa is a UNESCO World Heritage, Nepal's biggest stupa, known as Jhyarung Khashyor, Khasa Chaitya, at Boudha-Jorpati Road, 4.5 km north of Kathmandu airport. The stupa covers 6756 sq km of land, 141 ft tall, 100 ft in diameter, and 3-tiered plinths in yantra form raised over 12 crossed rectangles. Five Dhyani Buddhas set Vairochana at the centre, Ratnasambhava in the south, Amitabha in the west, Amoghasiddhi in the north, and Aksobhya in the east direction. The dom tied 108 small niches with icons of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and female deities of conjoint figures in erotic poses. The floor base has countless praying wheels with carving mantras, Om Mani Padme Hum.

This is where the water goes from Devi’s Falls. When it plunges into the earth, this cave takes you to the bottom of those falls where it runs for a short distance before it again plunges into the earth. To get to it you have to work your way deep down through a series of caves along variable access tunnels for a distance of some 800 metres or so. 

Your journey starts pleasant enough down an ornate stairway but then it gets grim. The cave itself looks a more like a mine than a visitor attraction and frankly is dangerous in places. Scaffold erected without thought for the visitor, inadequate handrails, uneven and wet ground and low claustrophobic tunnels. It is a health and safety nightmare and would be shut down in most other countries. There is virtually no supervision and it gets very, very crowded so the narrow tunnels lead to long queues as no-one will give way. 

The whole place looks filthy and is hot and dank. There are no geological features, just black walls. When you get to the end, you can just about see the falls through the gloom but you cannot get close and some of the handrails are dangerous. There are a lot of steps and your return journey will be arduous, very arduous and people with only minor walking impairment should not even attempt it in my view. As caves go, this is a shambles and not worth the effort.

It a short walk 100 meters to the falls.  The path is OK but lots of steps without hand railings.   Only 30 rps enterence to the falls.  Great photo place.  Bring coins to throw into the wishing well.  Keep an eye on your children!  Management should put more fences up.

We covered it as part of our day’s tour in pokhara.

It is an open area with long rounded steps from ticket window leading to the main cave.

As we enter the cave , Kamdhenu mukh (Holy Cow) is there. Then we moved ahead within the cave and found the main temple of Shivling within the cave.

We then moved ahead and slowly there was mist flowing all along. Water was trickling down on us as we crossed multiple labrynthine areas of narrowed passages within the cave. I was fearing if the roof of the cave would fall on us. We were getting wet with the water from the fall pouring on us. Though their was light in the cave but the pits and floor and the unknown end along with the interiors of cave was a bit frightening. I wanted to go back but with the thought to resolve the mystery of underground Davis Fall kept me courageous. With little kids, it was not a wise decision unless one is extra careful with kids.

We reached the end of cave and saw slit like opening between the two mountains with Devis fall on the other end. It was a wonderful experience and we all were superexcited to reach here. We clicked a few snaps but mist was right there on our cameras as well.

We rested for a while and started on our way back. It was a little tiring to climb up the steps in the end but the effort was worth the scenic memorable view of this cave. There were iron stairs to reach the end of caves. They were a bit dicey and we had to carefully step down with kids.

I would recommend all to visit this cave if staying in Pokhara but be extra cautious with kids.
