I stayed in April 2017 and was under the impression that the renovations would be finished but the whole of the front of the hotel was blocked off as they were still working on the front rooms, hence no garden view rooms available, and the one we were in had a terrible view of inside, not sure, as it's all a quirky shape? So we had to keep our curtains closed and felt like staying in a cave. The hotel was a palace and so is a very quirky layout, took us days to find our room with confidence, lot of walking and stairs. The room itself was fine with everything we needed although no fan in the bathroom so it got very steamed up but there is a 'proper' toilet. Maid service excellent. Breakfast buffet beautiful with everything you could ever want, and restaurant in the evening serving gorgeous food at reasonable prices. Pool area nice to relax with attentive waiters although the water was freezing so didn't swim. Taxi outside to take you wherever but you can walk to thamel, which is great for shopping if you can put up with the traffic, noise, pollution, and madness of the city!

Devi's fall is a small fountain which is in pokhara opposite gupteshwars cave...
The water forms an underground tunnel after reaching the bottom. This tunnel is approximately 500 feet (150 m) long and runs 100 feet below ground level. On 31 July 1961, a Swiss couple Davi went swimming but the woman drowned in a pit because of the overflow. Her body was recovered 3 days later in river Phusre with great effort. Her father wished to name it "Davi's falls" after her. Its Nepali name is Patale Chango, which means "underworld waterfall".

Its an old hotel, we had veg food which was tasty. Wi-fi was slow and connection not so good at times. The washroom was without any exhaust fan so it was stinking at times. We have another Hotel called Ambassador right in front of this one, which was more decent and new.

Hotel is nice looking from outside but not very convinient for staying. all rooms and internal spaces are very small and narrow, stairs are very steep. Windows in rooms are small and located near the floor level. there was a smell in a room. it is 10min of walk to Thamel, and it is unpleasant walk through trafic, noise and polution. In Thamel we found better place to stay for 1/3 of price. overall the Shanker hotel is too overpriced. the breakfast was good though.

The room was huge, lots of amenities and the bed was big as well. 

I had dinner at the restaurant or patio with live band. Love the ambiance. Food was great, price was good and there was a promo for the drinks. 

The staff/cashier was very accommodating. He helped me out with recommendations on what food and drinks to try. 

Sajja was the one attending to me during my dinner. She was very nice, friendly and had a very sweet voice. Very accommodating, quick and always checking onto me if I ever need anything. Thank you for the amazing customer service. I'm very happy with my time with Soaltee.

Gupteswar Gupha is a sacred cave, lies 2 km from Pokhara airport on the Siddhartha Highway leading southwest from the city. The entrance is right across from Devi's Fall and the cave is almost 3 km long. It has some big hall-size rooms and some passages where you have to crawl on all fours. This cave holds special value for Hindus since a phallic symbol of Lord Shiva is preserved here in the condition it was discovered. An entrance fee of Rs. 5 is charged and taking pictures inside the cave is prohibited.

Crowne Plaza chain of hotels is considered to be good business hotels. I was however very much dissatisfied during my stay in the hotel. The furniture in the room has been very old and table drawers are not working. It requires replacement/repairs. Very limited power sockets provided in the room for charging of electronic devices. Restaurant food is not upto the desired international standard. Insect shown to the restaurant staff in the dry fruits container during buffet breakfast. Hotel does not have any gym/health club facilities. When asked about such a facility, the hotel staff recommended that I can go to the nearby hotel and use their gym facility which is not practical.

We walked into clouds of incense smoke that choked . The crowds walk clockwise and it's considered an insult to walk counter clockwise. There are many roof top cafes and restaurants to take advantage of the views over the Stupa

From the moment we arrived, everything was perfect. The food was absolutely amazing fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The service was top-notch; every staff member was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Breakfast was the highlight of our stay, they literally had 50 different items to choose from! I’ve never seen such variety and quality in one spread.

If you’re looking for a place with outstanding food, exceptional service, and true hospitality, this is the spot. Can’t wait to come back!

The casino at soltee are a total cheat.
They say no entry fee.
Once you go they will force you to buy entry ticket worth INR 2500. Which is not mandatory. If you are playing you need not be buying entry ticket. Do Insist on not paying entry they will eventually let you enter.

This biggest Budhist stupa is stunning. 
With the praying flags at the top make it very nice to see.

Suggest to go there in the late afternoon. You can explore the place first then enjoying the sunset from the terrace cafe. 
The stupa itself is very large and you can walk around its dome (clockwise of course!)
I can find few monks walking and touching  the praying wheel. The atmosphere is really peaceful and beautiful
But....still find garbage in some spots which is not nice

Nice, clean hotel, in good location, with great pool (although it was rather cold when we went!) and garden area. Nice clean bathroom, with great shower, but fan wasn't working. Twin room was good size, with balcony. TV in room. Reception staff spoke English to varying degrees. Most staff very polite and helpful, and very well presented, some staff just said 'yes' to any requests, but then did nothing (i guess they were very busy or did not understand us).  Ate at the restaurant on 1st night and was dissapointed. Very slow service (?think they forgot about us), perhaps because we didn't have the buffet meal that most guests chose. I enjoyed a lentil curry, but my partners mutton curry was luke-warm and had hardly any meat in it, and lots of bone splinters. Traditional dance show on most nights in restaurant.  Buffet breakfast mixed quality - some items were brought out from the kitchen cold.  Best bet was the bread goods, and the eggs, which were cooked to order. Very odd noise in our room  intermittently thought the day and night - sounded like a lift or aircon unit. Bit noisy in room next to stairwell (slamming doors and people banging up and down at all hours), but couldn't hear traffic noise. Spa treatments pricey (we had massages from local place, which was cheap, but probably not as good a quality as i imagine the hotel spa would be, & local massages tend to be done by men)
Very good place for just relaxaning and cup of coffee. Entry fee is NPR 200 and donot know the reason for this high charges as it also relates to higher beverages cost.
Its nice monument with history, but nothing much to see there, only view of surrounding from the first floor

We enjoyed the setting as a respite from hectic Katmandu and upon the recommendation of a Canadian couple chose to eat lunch here. Great looking menu and reassurances from the waiter that they took great care with food safety, not wishing customers to suffer ill effects. So we had fine results on first visit and day 2 suggested to the rest of our travel companions that we have our final meal there prior to departure. Three of 11 travelers required medical treatment at airline clinics receiving IV fluids, etc and all but one were able to board second leg of flight. Our sickest companion got on a later flight. The rest of us experienced some form of intestinal distress making a very long flight home most uncomfortable. We highly discourage you from eating here. Pay the 2 rupee fee and enjoy the garden only.

The cave is easily accessible although you need to watch your steps and head as well. At some points you need to really bend and get down which those not used to might find quite challenging. If you want to experience a cave environment this is a good place to do that.
Interesting little climb down to a fall in Pohkara. If you like stairs and interesting and beautiful falls that dissapear into a cave then check this little gem out.

The hotel is centrally located about one block in from the main street next to the lake. There are many restaurants, bars, and stores without walking distance of the hotel.

I stayed in a "standard" room in the main building with the reception area for 3 days. The "standard" rooms were very basic and run down for the price (though I paid more than the hotel list price). The room was on par with what you would find in a hostel, not a hotel. The room was dark and worn. The carpet had large hairballs. The bathroom had old fixtures and was not the cleanest. The whole bathroom was basically the shower since there was no walls or curtain and it was next to the toilet. There was soap but no shampoo. The beds were fine. The tv had good channels. The AC worked well. There was also no complimentary water. 

The breakfast was fine and there was a guy making omelettes. The wi-fi was not free in the rooms but was free in the restaurant.

wasn't really sure what this was or how big it was so set aside a couple of hours to visit, we only spent 40-50mins inside. It was very nice and well maintained, the highlight was really the friendly little squirrels. It was pleasant and quiet, you could walk around it all in about 10-15 minutes. The history of the gardens was interesting and the old photos showed how it had fallen into disrepair before being restored. had a coffee and lassi at the café, it was not the best. Overall a little disappointing, maybe we were there in the wrong season as nothing was in flower.
Great experience with facilities and service. The people who work there are fantastic especially the room service attendants. Food was amazing too.

One has to go down a flight of stairs to reach the mouth of the cave, before you descend even lower. Please note that it will be muggy, slippery, wet, sometimes mildly smelly and ofcourse, very dark inside the cave. If you are even slightly claustrophobic, avoid it. But if you're not, carry on till the very end for stunning views of the sunlight peeking through a small ridge-like gap and reflecting on the water gushing down here from the adjacent Devi's Falls.

Ofcourse, there is a Shiva temple on the way with a pretty massive Lingam that is worshipped by a lot of people on the way down. Our guide said that in the monsoons, one cannot go beyond that temple, and if that is the case, it would be massively disappointing. The true thrill of the cave is beyond that temple when you have to bend, watch your head, watch you feet, traverse through narrow openings and eventually reach the point from where the view is truly spectacular.
if you like caves with a little mythology than this would be nice. some enterprising person has set up an ice cream parlour near the exit

Another highlight during the visit to Kathmandu.  The stupa is beautiful and visitors are able to climb up to an upper level for better view of the surrounding.

There are many souvenir shops, cafes surrounding the stupa.

Suitable for all (some steps required), the entrance fee is NP30 per head. 

Small area, you may finish ur tour in 10 to 15 minutes. Just a strong water stream.. this place is favoured because of the history, when Mrs Davi fall slipped and fall down when she and her husband go for shower.. due to many efforts took to take her body out, the place is then knows as Davi's Fall
The room is excellent, spacious and comfortable.Thanks to Sandhika for making our stay more special and going above and beyond to ensure our comfort.
There was nothing interesting here. It was a cave that was dark, dank and wet. There was more confusion by the tourists  trying to get out than anything worth noting.

Hotel located around 30 min drive from airport.
Staff is nice and friendly and always ready to help.
Wi-fi for as was complimentary and works very well.
Rooms are quite good but needs to be refurnished - looks used.
But in general not bad hotel.
Service was excellent from the start to end. Silence, view and scenery was adorable. We also enjoyed breakfast, thanks to service team, Prakash, Hasta, Pradeep.  Thank you,
Ooh, I got this confused with Seti Gorge earlier.  Yes, enjoyed the walk up and the view from the top.

The Indian restaurant at the Soaltee hotel is an absolute delight. Great food and service. And the price is very affordable for the food quality. The ambiance is also well maintained with light and music. I always dine here when In kathmandu and I will always come back. Thanks to the staff and specially to Sambhav.
This Buddhist pilgrim spot to be visited when you are in Kathmandu. Quiet near from the airport and easily accessible.

this cave is connected to the devi's fall. it is actually a holy place, you will first see hindu temple and u walk down the stairs.. and along the way downstairs..you could enjoy lots and lots beautiful statues..beautifully curved.. at the temple area..we were not allowed to snap any pics.. but we walk further down..u can already start snaping pics..u might need to go through narrow walkway..but its beautiful and safe. during our visit to this place.. it was raining...but the walk way are not that slippery and still safe to walk. as u walk the cave..u could see the continuation of the devi's falls...beutiful and cozy inside.. a lil bit wet everyday couse it was raining..otherswise it lovely...enjoyed listening to the running water..its lil bit dark in there..the waterfall is lil bit difficult to be captured with a normal camera phone.:) be careful if u are bringing ur parents..coz its nice to walk down and enjoy the view...but its a lil bithard to climb up back for those who are not fit like me:) we took a few pitstop to catch our breath:)))
don't consider must go and  see. there is outside shopping, you guys its feel small but its bigger history so go and know about it
The solution to the mystery behind where did davis flow down with the water was solved years after his death. The Gupteshwar cave is a bit scary with the rocks and the darkness.

Many of the hotels in Kathmandu are a little tired and the same has to be said of the Crowne Plaza Soaltee   

The rooms are large but old fashioned.  The shower over the bath with discoloured grouting and plastic shower curtain finishes off the outdated look.  The club lounge was also only open from 6pm to 7.30pm

The staff were very very good, the food was also good.

The location was also good given that taxi's were easy to get and unless you stayed in the very centre of Thamel  you have to get used to the congestion and the enormous pot holes. 

If I were to go to Kathmandu again, I would recommend Dwarika Hotel but it is significantly more expensive in all areas.

We had an excellent experience in Kakori Indian restaurant..Rajlaxmi served us very well and she was extremely courteous & friendly. ..the chef Basant Nayak also was excellent..highly recommend this place for family outing and dinner….

we were very pleased with our stay as a whole. the reception and hotel staff were very hospitable.
i was disappointed to find small beds  to accommodate 2 adult and a kid comfortably. The basement floor rooms are very stuffy. The breakfast buffet has very limited Indian options. The food through room services are good. its away from city and do not expect to take a walk around the place. The airport pick up comes with a sub-standard car.
despite all these issues, people in the Hotel make you feel nice....
I have been to Devi's Falls twice and always enjoy. A nice place to visit while in Pokhara and the caves are adjacent. There is a lot of walking and stairs/steps particularly in the caves.

I have visited many bigger caves before. It is not a big cave and it just took about 15 minutes to visit gupteswar cave, may be it is a big cave but it was not possible to visit the other parts so it was not something special.
Lots of small tea houses and shops around the stupa so its a one stop shop for Souvenir's and paintings.
The most beautiful Stupa in Kathmandu. It gives peaceful vibes. I loved the colours here. The views of Kathmandu city are fantastic!
Best place to spend the evening for a sunset view and much happening. I have spent the whole evening viewing this stupa. Such an amazing place in Kathmandu.

The hotel is amazing! Spa is very relaxing, food is delicious, 24 hours room service. Our family loved it. We travel a lot, but this one was one of the best experiences we had! The premises are beautiful too, they have a pool and we enjoyed ice cream at the bar every day.

If you’ve got time and you’re in the area go for a peek. Not too much here but it’s a nice change from just shops. The waterfall itself is pretty small if you’re from the US/Canada/Australia or the tropics, but I noticed in Japan they also are impressed by a trickle of water.

apart from busy traffic outside, just being here is a different atmosphere.
surrounded with big trees , different design of the buildings make us feel so comfortable, just sit and reading book or doing meditation
Will return again and again to the stupa and flow with the circumambulators in the clockwise direction within this special place for Buddhists.

A very nice and peace place to be 
If you are in kathmandu city :) 
I bet mroning time is the best time to be here.
This place is totally the number one of all places you must see in Kathmandu. Huge stupa and hundreds of monks walking around with their prayers. It's a lifetime experience.

VisitorsVisitors pay a small fee, then enter the park. It is a short walk to the attraction.  If you have no experience seeing running water across rocks, it may be worthwhile to pay a visit.  If you are in this area of the city and have nothing else to do, it may be worthwhile to pay a visit.  Otherwise, I would not add this to any itinerary or go out of my way to visit this.
Ambient atmosphere with cozy rooms and polite and kind hospitality. Located 100 m from the fewa lake at the prime location of lakeside, peaceful and quiet with a neat environment.

It's one of the bucket list in Katmandu, it's quite interesting and have infrastructure, number of cafes/restaurant around stupa. We made it our launch stopover. The stupa(temple) is really huge, having installed lucky drums over perimeter - it's not easy job to all turn them and quite dirty. There are benches to rest, nice small temple to make clicks from high. Look fotos attached. 

Of course it's not free, in Nepal you pay in many temples. I guess it's a pivotal landmark because it's on the covers of foto books all over. I didn't figure out but it's nothing inside - there no entrance and no indoor to see. But there a lot if temples mentioned on the map which I attach and fares.
Not the best, but not the worst stupa here to spend time for.

Packed with people because of the last day of the Dashain Harvest festtival.   Families upon Families here. 30 Nepalese Rupee entrance fee. You'll be met by a model of the Himalayas as seen from Pokhara.  We squeezed ourself to the many viewing spot of the Devi Fams.  Fun to rub elbows with strangers. Got bit by two big mosquitoes.  It's nice to see!  Take care not to slip!
Well worth the visit. Very interesting mandela workshop. Good range of coffee shops! (very important!)
This was a complete waste of time. Hardly any water flow currently made this attractive nor worthwhile. It was hard to believe that they are still charging an admission fee to see nothing.
Peaceful place to go for a walk and the long stairs are totally worth it once you get to see the view from the top
The cave is big. And you could see the water that go to the devis fall. But they renovated during my visit. Inside the cave you could see the Siva statue.
Recomend the visit 500 rps per person to get in. Nice quiet get away from the busy streets of Thamel. We expected more botanical plants but, it was still an nice educational get away.

Nice hotel with nice staff but it's not four star. We got a great rate and half board and it was good value. But if you are expecting the Savoy or Raffles......its musty, under renovation, and the pool is average. The car they sent to pick us up was late and older than the hotel, and not in a good way.

The hotel is fine.  Old, but perfectly clean and pleasant with an extremely professional and friendly staff.  But with the entire city being torn up from road construction, I can't really recommend the location.  You can walk to Thamel for shopping and eating, but it's so treacherous to cross the roads, I think it might be better to stay in one of the hotels a bit out of the way and just get a cheap taxi to take you into Thamel when and if you want to go there.  So I would choose a different hotel next time, based solely on location and because of the current rebuilding situation all over the city.  I think I would prefer to be near the Paten district next time.

Great property, easily the best in Kathmandu, tastefully decorated rooms, fabulous breakfast spread, significantly large property to drown out the chaos outside, definitely coming back here when I'm back in Nepal, that's for sure. Been to many hotels in Nepal, this one is definitely the top one.

Our stay at Fish Tale Lodge was everything we expected and so much more. Thanks to the amazing team we enjoyed our stay to the fullest. The location is perfect for exploring Pokhara and it's surroundings. Directly from the hotel you can do a boat trip on Phewa Lake and enjoy sunrise and sunset over Annapurna Mountains. The area of the Lodge is well maintained - there are plants everywhere and you feel instantly relaxed. The rooms are great - spacious, modern, big plus: hot water immediately (not everywhere in Nepal the case), great room service (really attentive -> they check on you if you need something in the evening). There is everything you need: a fridge, a safe, hangers, a TV, a comfortable bed and lots more. 

The service in the restaurant is awesome - they take really great care of you - always making sure you have everything you need. The food is delicious - thanks to chef Govinda Khanal and thanks to the team of the head of the whole restaurant Surendra you always feel taken care of. Especially Sunita was really attentive during the service of our table.

All in all I can definitely recommend to stay there during your trip. I will definitely come back next time I'm in Nepal.

I with friends 5 couples 4 kids visited pokhara nepal in march with lot of hopes. Hotel barahi was shown very good .. Our agent also told barahi hotel is good. But what we found was horrible. We were first checked in to a old building.rooms were like govt hospitals. Old tv boxes.local bathroom fittings. We all decided to leave hotel as we had family.... then we were shifted to another block after so much of arguement.
Poor bathrooms. Old build . Beds were not comfortable.Pathetic breakfast.hotel manager was rude with us on the very first 15 mins while we reached. They dint allowed girls to swim as it was compulsory to wear costume which our tradition dint allowed us.  All fooding was too costly with Zero taste. Hotel Travel manager was good Mr.Dilip pant. Coz of him we experienced Ultra light flight n sarangkot. 
Overall its a 2 Star hotel . I dont recomend anyone to go Barahi Hotel in Pokhra. There are many other hotels in lesser price with more comfort.

We stayed on two separate occasions, the first time for one night in a Palm Court Room, which is the highest category room. It was very dated and smelt foisty and the bathroom was small and dingy although the shower was hot. Bed and pillows uncomfortable and towels well past their best.  For our return stay for 2 nights after our Annapurna trek we asked to be moved to a standard room. This category of room is made up of small bungalows situated in the garden. Again a very dated room, but we felt it was marginally better than the Palm Court rooms. The overall impression we got of both room categories is that they are greatly in need of total refurbishment.

The lodge is in the middle of Fewa Lake and you are either rowed across in a boat or hauled across on a pontoon - a very unique way to arrive. The grounds of the hotel are very pleasant and on a clear day the views from the restaurant terrace across the lake to the snow-capped mountains are wonderful. The restaurant looked as though it had been refurbished and breakfast and dinner were both buffet style and adequate.  Although we'd booked dinner as part of our package we only ate one night at the lodge as we were not keen on the choice of dishes. Eating out in Pokhara was our preferred choice as there are many reasonably priced restaurants with a real buzz and a more authentic feel - delicious food too. 

Some of the staff were very pleasant, others not so. On check-out there was no 'hope you've enjoyed your stay', more a concern that you were settling your bill. Also worth bearing in mind that large tour groups use the hotel so it can get noisy. Would we stay again - definitely not - on reflection we would have preferred to stay in a smaller boutique hotel along the lines of the Temple Tree House which knocks spots off the Fishtail Lodge. To our mind the lodge is resting on its past reputation and unique location and is more in the market for quantity rather than quality.

One of the best hotels I have stayed at. The staff was very kind and helpful. The breakfast had many options in Nepali and Indian food as well as western cuisine. The breakfast had very good options, as well as the dinner. The pool was big and very beautiful. The hotel offers all amenities such as spa and casino.The only downside is that is not so close to the center.
Good place to visit but when we visited there the cave is extremely slippery due to reconstruction work. Keep your eyes on the roof and path because some times it’s become very narrow.

Very divine feeling once you go inside. 
The view at the end of Cave is awesome. 
Need more lightings on the way while going down or up.

No Dislikes.
Just a tiny fall with grill boundary. No much enjoyable. But anyone can take a photo  through jooming lens.

I have been visiting Soaltee for a long time since we live nearby, but the property has changed a lot and has lost its authenticity and it feels charmless these days. The staffs are mostly new, and their smiles seem forced as there's a noticeable lack of warmth. After our meal, I received the bill without any discount, despite being a regular customer, and was asked to provide feedback on the hotel and food. It was surprising that a staff member who hadn't checked on us for the entire hour suddenly approached us with the intension of getting a positive review and wanted her name mentioned, which I chose not to do. The food itself was bland. As I was heading home, I realized how Soaltee used to embody a sense of legacy and richness that seems to have faded. While writing my review, I looked at other reviews of Soaltee and found myself unconvinced by them.
Stopped by here on a recommendation.   During this time, the rainy season, the falls were raging. I am told that there is a cave you can walk through during the dry season. It's a short stop.

I can't believe I took shower in mold all over shower, I did not expect this dirty and filthy hotel for 4 star hotel . Also they promised for female Sanitary products and when we called they said they don't provide that!!!
Must visit place in Kathmandu. Situated in neighborhood of Boudha, its a calm soothing place amid hustle and bustle of busy k-town life.

Devi's fall is nice and peaceful and there is also a temple which is on the other side of the falls. Its a long way walk down into caves and you would see the falls from the inside. The steps are steep and wet. Not for claustrophobic ones. Elderly people may also find it really difficult to walk down and then again walking up the same distance to come out. But worth the walk for those who can.

Theres a little waterfall with some rocks, but you cant even see it because of the fence.
Not worth at all

Just to give an idea of size of the garden, you can walk across the whole garden in 5-6 minutes. Within this area there are some nicely maintained flowers and plants. But this is no good reason to spend NPR 200 and few more on taxi. Comparing to any other garden in India or around the world, it is miniscule.
It is an amazing spiritual site in Kathmandu. Excellent work of arts and crafts. People are really cool. Not very far from the valley. Must visit places indeed!!
Very good . Loved my stay here. Sakai and Sandhika from the reception were very helpful. Enjoyed my stay thoroughly and I wish to come here again and I recommend my friends to visit here.

I stayed in this hotel for the first time and found to have made a mistake by choosing Soaltee Crowne Plaza. I booked this hotel through a travel agent who probably did his business not not really worthwhile.

The airport pickup was promised but nobody turned up at the airport to receive me. However, I could locate somebody from the Hotel who did not have any idea of my pickup. He had come to pickup someother guest and refused to let me in. This was totally unacceptable. I knew from the begginning of this trip itself that from hereon it is not going to be a fruitful visit.

I then took a taxi whom I paid a ridiculous amount of money from the airport till the Hotel, the local people from the airport did not allow me to take a cab of my choice either.

I reached the Hotel with full stress and check in at the reception. The person at the reception was so unattentive that she was busy on the phone while a new guest has arrived, she didn't even bother to look at me for 10 minutes. Finally, the second person came in front and gave me my room key.

Upon entering the room it seemed to me that I had infact choosen a 2-star Hotel. The room was in a pathetic state, bedcovers not clean, stains on pillow covers and no room slipper. 

I tried calling up home but the lines were not yet opened for long distance calls. I literally had to request for an outgoing call thru the operator.

Breakfast however was nice and the restaurant was neat. The fitness center was far below my expectation. Gardens were well maintained and was perfect for an outdoor drink.

The next day I was waiting for a guest to arrive to the Hotel to meet me, therefore had left a message at the reception. This meeting for me was rather the main reason for visiting this beautiful country. I was waiting for the guest in my room for 2-hours but did not receive any message of arrival. Upon contacting him he mentioned that he had to wait for an hour at the reception but no body informed. This was most unacceptable and I had to loose my temper. 

I then went to the guest services desk to make a complaint, and she first even refused to give me a comment sheet. I then asked her to connect me to the General Manager, she replied that I will have to first meet the duty manager and refused to connect me to GM's extension number.

I made my point to write all my bitter experiences to the General Manager while leaving the Hotel but have not yet received any reply from Soaltee Crowne Plaza. I would not recommend this Hotel to travellers and please do not just listen to the travel agent while making your selection but do not forget to check out reviews in websites like Tripadvisor choosing your accommodation.

Soaltee Crown Plaza has lost its image and the name and will have to go a long way to overcome its detoriating standards.

If I ever come to Nepal, I will make sure that I do not stay in this pathetic hotel.

I think most of the staff feeling very proud of because they working in good hotel. I never found good response about rate inquiry and booking. hope all service are good but it is better to make quick response service. I seems that there was email & internet problem. Management should have to make well equip office.

The Barahi is among the best hotels in Pokhara. It's independently run and the staff are unfailingly pleasant. The rooms are pretty well appointed, though the view of the mountains in not as unobscured as I had been led to believe. But what lets the Barahi down is inattention to detail. It was very chilly when I was there - early January - but the heating was weak, and there seemed to be either no heating in the restaurant, or they left all the doors open so the place was windswept. There is wifi, and it's free, but getting into it was difficult, and I had to choose between sitting in the marginally warm breakfast room or the freezing cold restaurant, where the signal was stronger. I wish I could be more positive, but once the sun went down I froze - dress warmly, kid!
Completely fenced near the fall. Keep wondering where the water is actually going. In and around small market as you enter the place. Nothing much inside.

This is actually called as Davis' fall as it is named after the couple who died on their honey moon. They have grilled the place to avoid accidents. Good place to see. There is a wishing well and statues where national dresses of nepal from different Provences are shown.
Its quite crowded and the place were not that well maintained as garbages is all over the places though there is near cave that you could visit.

My 24-year-old son and I (50s) found this tiny but lush garden a welcome break amid the dusty streets of Kathmandu. Be sure to explore the house that explains the '6 seasons' in Nepal - which then explains why this was originally called 'the 6 season garden'. There is a small fee to enter: worth it. A nice restaurant is on site - and accessible from the street. 30 mins is enough.

We spent 2 nights at this hotel.  We booked the room direct with the hotel and it cost £30 per night.  This price included breakfast.  

The hotel has its own swimming pool plus a nice garden.  It is situated in a convenient location with the lake and the various shops and restaurants along Lakeside just over a 5 minute walk away.  There was some noise at night from the street but not to bad.

The breakfast was a buffet with both hot and cold food available.  I thought overall the breakfast was very good.  There is a restaurant in the hotel but we didn't try it.

Our room was a decent size and also had a balcony overlooking the pool and garden.  The room wasn't cleaned during our stay which was a bit disappointing.  Another problem we encountered was the toilet!! Basically we had to shut off the water supply to it otherwise the water overflowed onto the floor once it filled after flushing.  This was a bit annoying to say the least.  Also the shower didn't have its own cubicle which meant everytime the shower was used the entire bathroom floor got very wet.

The hotel has Wi-fi but we found it to be intermittent and a bit erratic.  We couldn't get it to work in our room while in the reception area it worked but was very slow.

The staff were generally friendly and helpful.  Indeed they booked us seats on the bus to Kathmandu.

Overall at £30 per night one can't complain to much about the hotel though of all the hotels we stayed in while in Nepal this was probably our least favourite
The staff here are giving me a Very good service and being so kind. The staff here all are always with smiling face and very helpful. It is very comfortable being here.

This could have been so much better if the area surrounding the falls was cleaned up and crowd control implemented. Very little to see and the plant growth needs some serious attention. People pushing and jostling didn’t help.
It's was fantastic day for us  it is beautiful palace. And clean palace. All facilities are available here. Highly recommend this one

This was a interesting place to visit on our day tour of Pokhara.  Our guide parked on the street in the main part of the town and then walked through a small market area to an entrance with spiral stairs. We walked down the stairs which are very slippery due to the constant water dripping from above. The first attraction is the small temple dedicated to Shiva which is very hard to see as the lighting is non existence we did no stop to view really as had to remove your shoes and that was not happening as everything is so wet.  

You continue walking down the very steep stairs with my dreadful knees it was difficult especially as it is quite low so you also have to bed down in a number places.

Keep walking as once you reach the end you see the Davis Falls entering the underground cave.  I then walked down the metal steps to take some photos of the falls.
Even though the walk is hard is was worth it and I would recommend going to the cave

If you are not interested in religions and discovery I don't recommend this place. You have to walk down a very deep walk using old and wet stairs to see nothing. It's an experience and curiosity to explore. This underground location includes very old hindu temple.
Amazing place to go and needs to be seen. Very different from temples visits and totally peaceful and relaxing too.

Incredible feeling of seeing Devi's fall. The view of the Devi's fall which was opposite to Gupteswor cave was inexpressible. The view of Devi's fall seen down from the Gupteswor Mahadev cave was superb

The best thing about this hotel is the tranquillity. It's set back from the road with security and a (for us) short walk from Thamel, about 15 mins. The room was large, clean with a modern bathroom. It exhibits "old world charm" with all the modern conveniences. Staff were super friendly and helpful. The pool area is also discreetly sheltered from the hotel building itself within a nice garden area.

worst experience in this hotel this hotel not for Indian citizen actually y i said that because we stay in this hotel 31st dec  2016  they charge us rs 11000 per with and rs 5000 per person for dinner but room is not that quality which i paid there is not thing in the room regarding food there is not thing for indian food only nan is there when i complain regarding food there management told that we have lot of tourist form other part of the world but i saw there is 70% guest is indian  when i told management about this they are not responding i went other place for food after paying rs 5000 per person for food and service is very worst after that next morning 9.30 am house keeping came and told me we have lot of room to clean so pls check out early because they have to go home early i told that we checkout before 12: oo noon housekeeping request that they have other guest in this room after that i angry and told what is your check out time then they told me that the check out time is 12:00 noon ...... now you people think you want to stay in is lodge or not i never stay i this lodge actually this is lodge ... never stay this hotel sorry lodge..............

This is simple a very very poor Hotel, and not worth the trip.Im surprised Crowne would let this hold its brand.   Rooms are old and Urgently need a Revamp.
Internet is very slow.

Food quality in Restaurant is simply terrible. The Staff are NOT well trained, and this is expensive Hotel for what it is. US$4.00 for a coke at the Bar, in Nepal is Criminal.
TV is Limited channels. Nepalese are wonderful people, and what a shame this Hotel, could not invest in a real make over. Forget the restaurant - You may as well out side on the road.

The entrance free is only thirty rupees, which is not expensive in my opinion, but that was the main reason I was disappointed. I was not expecting Devi's falls to be an enclosed, pay to get in, type of experience. I've see some beautiful waterfalls for free in nature, without having fences to block my view. I understand that maybe they are trying to preserve the area, and don't want people getting injured, but this was not what I expected. There is a huge market outside the area. If you pay to get in you can use the toilets, which I guess is nice.

The fall was very small due to it being winter. If you go after monsoon season it will be better.
30 rupees to enter. Many shops around.

We reached Kathmandu for a one night stay and decided to stay here. First of all the location is far off from Airport and the hotel itself is not great as per the looks. We checked into our room and it was stuffy with bad air and the windows pane were not functional. The moment we sat down on the bed, we felt insects and mosquito bites. Soon, we found there were bed bugs around and it was surely not a pleasant site. I called the Duty Manager and she sent a bell-boy with an anti-insect spray. 
When i demanded that she comes to see the place, she turned up 30 mins late and then gave lame excuses on how the bed bugs have come there. Then she moved us into a separate room which was smaller than the one which i had booked and also did not had complete amenities. But we managed to stay there overnight and left first thing in the morning. I would suggest you book Hyatt or some other 5 star hotel and give this one a miss.

The location as mentioned in previous review is great, away from the hustle and bustle of the city. It is a beautiful grand old building with lovely decor and character. The grounds around the hotels are beautiful and the breakfast was good, The gardens of dreams and thamel are all very close.   The other main sites are a taxi ride away ( £2)
As an old building it does creak a bit in some places, first night moved rooms as some motor or pump kept kicking in every minute , it was no issue to move, The second room was nicer , with the odd noise.It is a nice place to stay, it is ok for a short stay.

Fish Tail Lodge is an absolutely stunning property.  Their location and the romantic raft you must take to and from the property make for a truly special experience.  And while some of the service is outstanding, attentive and warm, some is slow, apathetic and ambivalent.  Despite having some of the poorer service in the poorly air conditioned restaurant, we enjoyed our stay till the final minutes.  When the Lodge had erred and failed to charge us for laundry services after we had paid and were already at the airport, they called us repeatedly even though I offered to email the payment as soon as I returned home.  They even sent someone to the airport despite the fact that I had told them I didn't have enough local currency to pay - which was why I paid my bill by credit card - and would have happily paid the laundry bill too *if* they had included it on my bill.  When their representative came to the airport, my spouse returned through security to meet this person, and offered him all the CAD cash we had with us which was CAD $7 short of the total.  He wouldn't take this money because it was short of the total.  Long story, less long, it was a ridiculous reaction to a mistake THEY made.  It's easy to provide excellent service when things are going smoothly - but we all learn what a business' true service protocol is when things go awry.  Go there and enjoy the uniqueness of the location and raft ride, but be very VERY careful to make sure there are no mistakes or things won't be fun anymore.

The hotel Lobby looks wonderful.  The rooms could be fixed to look better.  The lamp shades are falling apart, the mini bar did not work and they wouldn't fix it even after reporting it responding that 'most rooms do not have a mini bar.

This hotel is clean and the people are helpful.  You can bargain with the guy at the shop.  I did not know that and paid full price for the things I bought.  While some of my friends received good bargains! You learn every day, and some experiences make you pay!

We had problems with the Chinese Restaurant at the hotel.  The service was horrendous!

When you have a bit of time left over, this could be an attraction to visit. The small park has a few statues and  things to see, and then the small waterfall. The story behind it is interesting. A bit far from Pokhara city.
Within the city, nice market around, nicely maintained, good structure, entry cost is also nominal, good that taking pics is allowed

Stayed here on several occasions for business as well as for pleasure. The quality of service has gradually declined over the years. The reason I stayed here time and again was because of the proximity to the lake, the service and their room rate as compared to other nearby hotels. Now it seems that their room rate as compared to other high end resorts (much much better than theirs) has also increased! Time to retrain your reception staff on meeting the demands of guests (be it Nepalese or otherwise) and re-think your corporate as well as usual rates. But for me, Barahi- NEVER AGAIN!!
Select a roof top cafe for excellent views.  Camera will need an extra wide angle lens to cpture the site in one frame.

The garden terrace restaurant staffs so friendly, courteous and professional especially Sakar who treated us professionally. He is so knowledgeable and helpful. He introduced us Nepalese breakfast and we tried them out. Very delicious.

Thoroughly recommend a visit to here. Beautiful structure with many locals carrying out their religious rituals. Vibrant area. Surrounding it are many many shops and restaurants. One of our  favourite sites in Kathmandu.

Me and my family have been to Nepal to visit Pasupati Nath temple and we chose Shanker Hotel for our stay. We were on a package for Indian nationals for 3 nights and 4 days. After going through various hotels on Trip advisor, we finally took chance to stay in Shanker Hotel. Everything was ok while our stay but we didn't like much because of so much commission taken on every service given by tour operators and reception staff. For example: We booked Everest Experience for 6000 INR per person with hotel tour service whereas original rate is 5200 INR per person including airport taxes and transfers. Whereas we were charged 6000 INR as I said previously including transfers and taxes. Same was the case for room service, there is charge on every thing you order (tea sachets, sugar etc.) and food is costly also. No style and options of breakfast. cold stuff lying for breakfast and staff is also lazy and back biting in Nepali language whenever a customer is around. Always searching for tips and money wherever possible. Overall, we didn't like our stay there but its good for people who are not interested in room service and people around.

Checked in on 4th may 2017, service of the hotel was very ordinary, specially the in-charge of the restaurant was over smart & ill behaved, the keys of our rooms (6) became in-operative several times during the stay of 2 days, the food was pathetic & non edible, thank God we carried snacks from India.

I have always wanted to visit a Buddhist Stupa. And when I finally had the opportunity to fulfill my wish, I was not disappointed. From the moment I stepped forward to the spread-out vastness of whitewashed stupas, the place's grandeur took me aback. 

Many other travelers around me paused to take in the beauty of this immense representation of spiritual devotion. Many locals milling around the stupa were devoutly bowing down to pay their respects.
A must-visit site if you are in Kathmandu, Nepal. I love going here when I can, early morning especially. Walk around the stupa clockwise!

We were a group of boys and had our first bad experience with the front desk which was very uncooperative towards Indians and super friendly with foreigners. We stayed there twice on entering and leaving Kathmandu and both times our requests were not entertained. 

Wifi is chargeable and rooms have become outdated. The feel is very palatial and breakfast room is pretty but breakfast was very bland. 

The service was not upto the mark and could improve. Location was little off Durbar Marg and Thamel where all the night life is but taxis are readily available outside the gate. 

The swimming pool and lawn are around the pool are beautiful and fun. 

Overall, an average stay with average service with worth a try if cheaper than other options.

This hotel is old and needs badly to be renovated in order to justify the price. The pix is deceiving. The grounds are surrounded by cement walls and gated but not so nice looking. My airport pick up was scattered with no one there at the airport when I arrived at night. Other taxi drivers found my driver by phone but he was too busy to pick me up so he pawned me off to another driver. This driver told me that the junk car he drove belongs to the hotel. But it appears the taxi driver had access to it like it was his. 
The room was musty smelling and the bathroom smelled like mothballs. That was disappointing b/c I just came from Myanmar where the cheaper hotel I took in Yangon was so sickening full of mothball odor i had to check out of that hotel. For this reason I chose to pay more and get a better hotel in Nepal ~ but Boooo, same issue, but not as bad. Still for the price in Nepal this is not worth it. Plus taxis over charged from this hotel. 
So what if it was once a palace. Now it's a broke down big musty place. The staff was mostly OK but some had attitudes and not so many smiles. One waiter was very rude.

Try to stay a little bit longer in outside after visiting the inner parts, while sipping a coffee from a small cafe. Morning time is the best time for photo or slow motion video when the birds suddenly swing.
Mind blowing peaceful place, very beautiful and culture place to be. A lot of shops around it for shopping an restaurants as well
Interesting experience to see limestone's. You need to climb down a lot to get underground..Worth a visit
Unfortunately this visit was part of our tour. Absolutely hated it. Really sad to see so much rubbish here. No photos to share ‘cos I didn’t take any

Nice comfortable rooms as would be expected of a hotel of this standard but the communal areas could and should have been cleaner.  The public toilets are grim and the bar area had dirt and dust in places that made it apparent it hadn't been cleaned properly in a long time.  When hotels charge international prices for accommodation, restaurants and bar prices they should deliver international standards.

The spiral entrance staircase is tackily over-decorated with concrete carvings of Hindu deities and the cave is often crowded with Hindu pilgrims lining up to see the holy model cow in the steamy, smelly, artificial "cave within a cave" that's labelled as a "cow shed", but if you follow the dark, dank tunnel you emerge in a wonderful cavern with a view to the Devi's Falls waterfall, which plummets from a surface stream above into this chasm then flows off as an underground river. Amazing geological feature!

My friend and I stayed there for 2 nights before embarking on a 12 day trek. The location is very convenient, close to Thamel, but yet removed from the street noise. The ATM just outside the hotel is also convenient. The building and gardens look very nice, but the rooms and inside common areas are quite run-down. Maybe we were given a particularly bad room due to the cheap online rate we snagged on the hotel's website? The room was dark, very noisy (we could hear people walking by all night long and hear the bellhop's phone ringing very loudly without anyone picking up), and tired looking, with lots of wear and stains in the bathroom and on the furniture. The breakfast selection is very large, but many of the hot dishes were actually only lukewarm. On our second night, there was a wedding in the gardens and we were kept awake by the loud music until midnight. On the plus side, there was hot water whenever we needed it and reliable electricity. All in all, this could be a great place, but it is in dire need of renovations.

HOTEL BARAHI .. Pokhara.. Nepal 

On arrival we firstly encountered a nice small reception area with friendly staff, outside was a nice swimming pool area and all appeared to be going well, however that's where it ended,
On entering our very tatty and dated room (room No 212) the first thing you noticed Is there are no complimentary bottled water, no in room safe, no mini bar or fridge and the furniture is tatty and dirty. Power point next to mirror never worked.
The air conditioning unit was barely  working and it took an age to cool the room, that is when it was working, each and every time the electricity flicked the air con turned itself off, not too much of an issue whilst you're awake but during the night the heat woke us up on several occasions.
Our room looked absolutely nothing like the photos on the Barahi's website.
Bathroom,,, oh my goodness here we had a mish mash of units, white sink and WC, pink bath and toilet seat and a blue litter bin, the bath was a disgrace, on first looking at it I thought that it was just filthy and had not been cleaned, but on closer inspection it was apparent that it was actually the fibreglass or material that the bath was made from was so old and worn out it had a shattered cracked look to it.
The bed was relatively comfortable but the pillows felt as hard as a rolled up blanket, I ended up utilising the spare quilt as a pillow.
This hotel is well overpriced.  Had I paid around the 45 usd I would not complain but I paid three times that.  Their website leads you to believe the in room wifi is included but there is a fee if you want to use in room, folks walking past and having a glass of water downstairs can use it free.
There are many hotels as good as this one for a lot less money.  Do not let it's expensive room prices trick you into believing you are getting more than you really are. Also be aware that this hotel prices by per person and not per room .. Ill never stay. Here again. Contact me for photos, you'll not stay here

First this is a world heritage site and for a good reason based on its history. It's an iconic site. But, for me, this place is smaller than expected. What an amazing place restored to its former beauty following the 2015 earthquake. Take a moment to sit and absorb the  ambience. The atmosphere is so calm and serene around the Stupa. An array of sights and sounds in a most beautiful surrounding. Words cannot describe the peace you feel here. There are shops selling traditional Nepali goods and lots of cafes and restaurants. One visit is never enough - it captures part of your heart.

Locally known as Patale Chhango which means underground falls
Devi's waterfall is a must-visit when in Nepal. Witness the grandeur of nature as you see this colossal fall struggling with rocks to set itself free.
Davis Fall in Pokhara is an extraordinary waterfall which creates a 500 feet long underground tunnel as it reaches its bottom..
underground waterfall." Fed by Phewa Lake Dam, the waterfall is surrounded by abundant flora. A landmark of Pokhara..

We stayed here for a couple of nights. the rooms are small for the rates being charged. they had a decent breakfast buffet but otherwise I don't think the hotel is that good or well located for that matter. Everything was just average in my opinion.
Though the driver told us that water wont be available, we still went for it and were thoroughly disappointed.
good place to visit. but covid has its own restrictions. so the fun is gone. once the restrictions are lifted, it is really a heavenly beauty for every tourist.

I'm sure the stupa is lovely.  But we went in the midday sun and the steps was being whitewashed which detracted a lot from its charm. Not sure how's it's one of the largest stupas either: we've seen much bigger in Myanmar and Indonesia.

A large, artistic and beautiful place to visit. I spent 2 hours here walking around the giant stupa including taking a late lunch at one roof top restaurant, visiting the shops to buy souvenirs, taking pics and of course climbing up the stupa. 

Many local people and some tourists. A very nice and holy place in Nepal.

Rooms quite large, all rooms on ground floor and set in nice garden area.  I was there in June so quite quiet.  Although not amazing, having stayed in other smaller hotels in Nepal this one was reasonably clean the food was amazing. I had a hot shower in my walk in shower room, I had a large twin room for myself.  The only problem with this hotel, it was quite a walk out of town and you have to cross the river, which is ok if you're in a group but when you're alone and there are no street lights it can feel a little isolated.

Check in took more than half an our as they had confusion on type of room I booked through Expedia. Eventually room was allotted and was taken to room only to find room is not ready. Hence House Keeping Staff was called to prepare the room which again took almost half hour till the time we were made to wait outside the room.

In case you look for Smiling and Happy Faces, certainly FishTail Lodge is not the place to stay, staff never smiles and  aren't warm.

Untrained waiters in Restaurant is something you have to live with. They will not assist you in ordering food, will keep food basket in your plate, wont serve food in your plates. You will keep looking for them for service and reordering, so please don't mind your food getting cold while you look for waiters. Food taste isn't great but very expensive. Dinning here may be perfect recipe for spoiling your dinner or lunch. Better option can be... take a stroll and you will find plenty of places who serve better food and at 1/4th of price. 

And at last, please carry your own umbrella, don't expect hotel staff to offer umbrella if it rains rather have trust on your feet and run. 

Don't expect evening/ turn around service. Room dining plates wont get cleared after waiting for half an hour so putting them out of room may be better idea. Bellboy will not show up at check out time.

At the time of booking never thought will have this kind of experience for bomb kind of money (compared to most of the places in Pokhara) I spent.

We are at the hotel Barahi in  Pokara following Diwali and our experience was of the charts managers make sure we were taken care of from the moment we entered the property with white glove service, and at every interaction including the staff walking a five-year-old around the property by hand giving them tours. Level of service here only reminds me of the four seasons and the Ritz Carlton invented the snuggle of Service. It’s a beautiful property with a nice pool and spa and protected parking, but the service you experience makes this a can’t miss property anyway visiting the city or any of the other locations they have.  As a tech executive who has experienced all levels around the world, kudos  to the management/staff/ownership  on their tireless obsession to put  the customer above all!

This place can be visited any time. View of  white stupa in the day light with Buddhist chant and observe the devout passerby brings peace in itself. It has sepctacular view at night when adorned with butter lamps and light focusing stupa.

Its a nice place to just sit and talk/read/surf internet on a hot afternoon. Small but a well-maintained garden. They also provide you with a pillow and mattress to lay down on the grass. Full place is covered with Wi-Fi. Entry fee is 200NPR and It will cost you 50 NPR per hour for the internet.  There is also has a nice restaurant inside the garden.
The Garden of Dreams is pretty small and underwhelming (at least in January), but only costs around $0.20 so for the money is worth a visit, but will only take up a few minutes of your trip.
It was really hard to find what we went there to see, full of shops and eateries but at 2nd / 3rd floor without lifts.

Most rude, arrogant, antagonistic desk staff I have ever dealt with. I experienced three arguments with staff. The first regarding extending my stay an extra day. I checked with four different staff members over a period of three days to make sure arrangements had been made. I was told no problem. Not one of them actually did anything. I was called the last day and asked why I was still there, and told I would be charged a higher rate for that day because I had not made arrangements. The second involved the plumber. The toilet in my room would flood to the top, but not flush. He told me that the handle needed to be pushed again when it reached flood stage and then it would work. All the toilets were like that, he said, and acted like I was crazy. I started using the toilet in the lobby, which ironically did not flood. The third involved my last meal; I was part of a group that had arranged for our meals to be provided. I went to the lunch room with other group members. The waiter tried to charge me without telling me, because they considered me no longer part of the group since I stayed an extra day. No need to tell me that, no apologies for misunderstandings. Instead, they yell at me in the lobby "What part of English do you not understand?" A fourth incident involved an unusually high credit card charge I received later for a phone call I had made, but they simply chose not to respond to any of my communications asking for clarification.

On arrival we were greeted. However once we were given the keys we were not shown where to go and from this started a dismal stay. Once we entered the room we were thrown off by a terrible smell and noticed the smoke alarm had been covered. Upon finding this we went down to resolve this issue. But after returning from dinner had found nothing had been done, except them closing the curtains. Went to use a bottle of complimentary water for brushing our teeth to find the bottle not sealed and the glass beside it filthy. If I could get negative stars I would.

One of the places to visit whilst in Kathmandu but I found it hard to get the photo I wanted - even from the viewpoints upstairs - as there were just so many people in your shots.
Nice place but perhaps too tourist driven now what with it being encircled with souvenir shops and cafes....

Hi,

We went to hotel shankar just last week on 13th Aug 2011 for 3 days. And Actually i was very excited coz as per the hotel site.. I was very much convinced for this hotel. But when we reach.. first room given to us was not proper.. Mattress of the bed some separate.. We asked staff person to do the changes but first they simply said that we dont have any other room..
