In room, food menu was not proper. When we called house keeping they said this is the actual menu. We order something n when waiter came to deliver the same we asked him that there is no such option in the menu. He check the menu lying on the table of our room and said this is not actual menu. I will get the other one so it means person of house keeping doesn't bother to know which menu we have.

Main course food quality is good but snacks quality need to improve. We order grilled chicken n it was horrible.

One thing which i like to mentioned for sure that staff is very polite n helpful.. staff at reception also is good.

 There is no such options in breakfast buffet.

Like many of the other reviewers, I stayed here at the beginning and end of my trekking holiday (a total of two nights only due to flight delays at Lukla on the return leg to Kathmandu).  
As a place to 'get you in' & 'get you out again', the Shanker does its duty but the whole place feels dated and to be trading on its quaint-ness.  However, having said that, it does deliver what is expected of it: a bed for the night before you head up-country and a level of comfort having come down from the hills after the trek.  (Never under-estimate the degree of luxury imparted by a hot shower with seemingly unlimited hot water).  
The rooms are basic but adequate and the bathrooms, although small, are functional.  
The extensive buffet breakfast is great and the 'egg station' will cook you an egg just about any way imaginable - my scrambled eggs were outstanding!
However, you do need to be quick to ensure that the tea/coffee waiter is flagged down fast enough to give you a 'hot' coffee rather than just warm.  
If I came back to Kathmandu, I probably would stay at the Shanker again since it's convenient for the shopping district and is comfortable enough although hopefully I'd get a larger room and one with a better view than the top of the atrium... but then I'd probably hope to stay for more than a couple of overnights.
One of the largest spherical stupas in the world. Boudhanath also called Boudha is a stupa in Kathmandu, Nepal There is a popular myth associated with the place.

Nice breakfast selection. Love the poori and masala dosa. The staff also very friendly especially mr Sakar. Always come and ask for order. Very helpful. Keep up a good work. Love to seat outside the restaurant. Can enjoy the morning chill weather.
Very nice waterfall and surrounding area.  This isn't a main draw but it is something to do in Pokhara if you run out of other things to do.

going inside this cave is an amazing experience. it will give you this strange feeling of excitement, worry and relief! this place is not good for claustrophobic persons. it's a little bit confined and a little bit dark and dimmed. it's also a bit wet and slippery inside so don't forget to wear proper clothes and sturdy shoes. there is a small fee to get inside. the place closes at around 6pm so come as early as possible. there is a little Hindu shrine inside where you can offer prayers. there is also a souvenir shop outside that sells quality items.

The hotel is currently under repair and renovation, which is good as, other than the damage sustained in the earthquake, it really needs a revamp. It is old and musty and a bit too overpriced for the quality of accommodation provided. I was unimpressed with the buffet breakfast. The quality of the food at breakfast was average.  However, the location is good, the staff were helpful and the dinner in the evening from the a la carte menu was good. Nice grounds and pool. So, the hotel has potential.

A lovely garden in the center of Kathmandu.  Not exceptionally crowded on the day I was there (9March 2020).  And the sunset casted a golden glow on the garden. Loved the flowering plants found in the garden and saw few squirrels scurrying about which I had found it to be so delightful.

Had coffee and cakes in Kaiser Cafe and I must say the price is not cheap.  Service was good (thank you Santosh - I hope I got the name correct).

Amazing place. Nepal's one of the best place that everyone must visit. People are very humble and greatful and takes their job very seriously. Only the thing is they should move those small shops to somewhere else. Recommend for everyone. Thank-you  Nepal.
A series narrow canyon, that goes underground and through  caves. Not much attraction to view. May be due low season.
I have visited the falls several times and must recommend that the falls are more fulfilling during the rainy season.  Watch you step and enjoy
The water fall and its thunderous sound can be heard from far..

Fall is not that great like Victoria or Niagara but combination of shoping complex ,gardening and fall itself added to the beauty .Its a small fall of gradual slope . There is a balcony from where one can watch. After that going to the bank of fall is possible by walking.

Hotel Shanker was intended to be a relief after a long hike in Langtang having nice facilities and a large garden with a big swimming pool in the middle of a smog and dusty Kathmandu. However the hotel staff could barely speak English and had little interest in trying to do more than the bare minimum one would expect from a standard hotel and the food was disappointing as well, making us to wonder how it could be that the small tea houses in Langtang actually had better service and more interest in accommodating its guests so the second day we escaped to the neighboring Radisson Hotel for much better food and service

Wonderful place in Kathmandu. My recommendation don’t take a taxi.
Walk there slowly from Kathmandu centre.

A must in Kathmandu if you are there and have time.  It was a 30 minute walk from our hotel.   Street are poor (there are no sidewalks) lots of cars to be careful of.  Area around temple is surround with some garbage and beggars the stairs leading up to  temple are lined with people selling you something and once at the top again people selling you stuff.    it was a beautiful temple - lots of monkey

The rooms are very old. The air conditioning is not working effectively. The bathrooms are not at all good. The water pressure is very slow. Over all the rooms are not as per 5 star standards. Not worth for the price paid. Breakfast is very good and tasty. Tried ala carte lunch it was also good. Front office and restaurant staff are courteous and friendly.

This fall is located next to main road and can be access by walk from downtown Pokhara. Entrance fees is NPR 30 for foreigners. Nothing can be done except photo for memories. For safety purpose there will be fence around.

THIS place has been hailed as probably the longest and most attractive cave in South Asia, but it wasn't a pleasant experience.
For a start, it is cramped and claustrophobic with frequent places where two people cannot pass each other. Another unwelcome feature was the pushing and shoving of fellow visitors keen to see something or just to get out.
Add to that poor visibility, treacherously wet and uneven footing, slippery steps and a very low ceiling in places where I hit my head and it is definitely not a memorable experience. Not disabled friendly.
Visitors also end up wet because there is a constant drip of water which can't be avoided.
At the lowest gallery people can experience the rushing entry of the river with glimpses of the falls but it is hardly memorable.
A lot needs to be done to make this cave deserve any sort of recognition as a place everyone should visit. A good start would be better lighting so people can see where they're going.
Definitely an average experience.
we both have good time enjoying every moment out of this world experience for my wife we like to visit again if it possible

Kathmandu's pollution has apparently reached a stage to turn bathwater yellow (and this hotel has inadequate water-filtering), so shower--at least the water then runs off you quickly rather than soaking into you, as in a tub.  And the menu is unimaginative (the veg lasagna is sour and the grilled fish can send you to the pharmacy) , so you want to try a restaurant, but the hotel location is bad--neither in Thamel nor on Durbar marg.  And the breakfast, while ok, is not enough to keep us here just because it used to be a palace.  On the good side:  the front desk staff are outstanding, willing to help and knowing the city.

I stayed here for two nights.  The staff are helpful and friendly and helped me book flights before I arrived.  The rooms are a bit disappointing especially the bathroom's which have dirty bathtubs and are in need of refurbishment.  The buffet breakfast was to a good standard.  So all in all a little disappointing.....but I suppose in Kathmandhu the standard is acceptable.
Very good experience of walk through water caves. You can see the ridges and water mark as you go down the place.

The cave is actually connected to the Davi's Fall. So you can see the water streaming to the outside part of the Davi's Fall. It is dark and humid as water is falling from the cave. Be careful of slippery. No photos are allowed to be taken here. But it is good to see the caving from inside.

this place is best to stay in an average budget, plus they have an casino attached, just make sure while having your deal with hotel you clarify everything in detail like they will offer you dinner buffet included but when u go u,ll see that it is in the casino area a very below average food, for sight seeing dey'll give you a matadore type van. so dont get duped with the price hv your deal in detail n in written!

There is a ticket booth at the entrance to the square where this huge temple is located. The admission fee is 400 rupees for foreigners and only Nepalese money is accepted. It was interesting to walk around the temple to see all sides of it and also watch the devotees as they walked around the outside and spun the prayer wheels. You can walk inside the temple a small distance and see some prayer bells. If you want to climb the stairs to walk around the upper level of the temple, you must then remove your shoes. This temple is located in an area of Kathmandu known as “Little Tibet”, and there are lots of shops and restaurants located on all sides of the temple.
For us from India, the place has a lot of historical and religious significance.  Construction work in and around the place was slightly upsetting.
Good place to visit and know the ancient culture.  Explore the caves and see water seeping inside the caves.  Good to take pics there.  Place for worship too.  The place is being maintained.

We were advised that the entrance fee was NPR 400/- for non-SAARC national however when we enter the place it seems like we were the only one who paid the entrance fee as there is no way to check it. The surrounding of the temple was full of souvenir shops, hotel and coffee shops that make the area crowded, busy and noisy. The solemnity of the place was gone due to it become more of a market than of a temple for praise. We only stayed for 5-15 minutes as there is nothing to see except for the stupa itself.
We had a great time in this stupa our guide explained very well about this monastery surrounded by both small and giant prayer wheels.
I am not into these crowds place... but at the evening it was quite windy... the place was nice but the road was very it was good to visit one time place

We stayed here a few days before our trekking. The hotel is fairly good, but the rooms our small group got were very different: some of them good sized and with mountain view, some other smaller, dark and quite old. Breakfast was ok, service very slow (like elsewhere in Nepal), cleanliness just average. The location is central but the surroundings quite noisy a times.

The grand stupa has a magnificent appearance and is worth visiting. There is an entrance thqt charges you 400 NPR but there are some others that doesn't have a ticket booth, meaning you can enter for free. 
There are buses from Jamal that take you to Boudhanath. I recommend visiting Pashupatinath on your way to Boudhanath, which is on the way from central Kathmandu.

One needs to walk down many steps to see the main attraction and it's worth that. 
The view at the end is absolutely mesmerizing. 
However, for claustrophobic people it might get a bit problematic because it is after all an underground cave, so that should be kept in mind.

But if stairs and closed spaces are not a problem for you them you must visit this place.

Was supposed to stay at the Crowne Plaza for three nights but left after one due to number of issues.

I need internet access to get my work done. The hotels DNS was misconfigured at some point and the connection worked so-so after designated Google's open ones.

I had DND hanging on the door and was disturbed twice.

Was upgraded to an Executive floor based on the Spire Elite status with IHG. Not sure what the "executive" was.

Did like the fruit, nuts, chocolates and cookies left.

This is not up to Crowne Plaza standards. It is at best a Holiday Inn. Fair assessment would be three stars and I deducted one for the issues I had.
This is a nice place to go but a lot of people pass at once you need to go very ground where there is less oxygen, they can bring oxygen from upwards and the passage are very narrow and irregular
Small caves with waterfalls at the end of the caves. Not really a must see but it is OK for a short walk and some shopping outside the caves.
Boudhanath Stupa is one of the most beautiful places to visit in Kathmandu valley. A great stupa in the center of city. If you are traveling to Kathmandu, please do visit and spread the word around
Unimpressive tourist spot. The waterfall was but a trickle. Even the story behind the site was ho-hum. Suggest you spend your time elsewhere.

We were a group of nine family members, including a five-year-old child. A young waitress at the pool area went out of her way to give several tours to our little one — such exceptional service! We’ll definitely be choosing this hotel again while traveling to pokhara.

Not with the money nor the time.  There's really nothing special about the gardens and absolutely nothing warranting the 400 rupee charge for foreigners.  If you're visiting on a hot day good luck finding a seat in the shade with all the local couples.  I've been in Nepal for 3 weeks and this is the first place I've been truly disappointed in.
Wonderful garden with both Nepalese and western culture. Definitely a must visit for the people who come to Kathmandu.

We had a very nice stay in this hotel. Large clean rooms, the staff are attentive and professional. Excellent spa on-site with a long menu of treatments. We ate in the main restaurant and the more expensive Chinese restaurant - the food in both were very good. There are 3 ATMs on site. Would stay here again.

I found this cave a really amazing. It think it is the oldest and biggest cave in south Asia. It is related to Hinduism,somehow. Inside you can see  various types of statue of god and goddesses. You can see the waterfall from this cave which is so amazing.If you have planning to visit pokhara then please don't forget visit this cave in Pokhara.

The whole stupa was under big renovation when we visited . 
Seems the place is great as there were lots of tourists around but not worth the travel from the city as it was too crowded and lot of construction going on !

we went to see what is supposed to be a great fall. You are unable to see the falls fully. To see the falls closer i had a very bad fall due to the poor state of the steps. no guard rail. I was luck I only fell 12 feet into the ravine. I was told later that there are about 12 bad accidents with a fa tasty each year.
Beautil historical place. You can feel the positive energy. It if safe and offers tons of entertainment and shopping. Beautiful views and the luxury of seeing devotees praying for love and kindness.
Our family had a vibrant stay at the Fishtail Lodge by the fewa lake. The atmosphere is calm and peaceful. Staff were very professional, A la carte menu were delicious.
Overall stay was good, room is spacious and clean. Anyway, found a tiny bug on the pillow, immediately called for assistance and their recovery action is good. Dinner buffet could be more delicious
Great stupa, major buddhist temple in nepal. It is a lovely places with some very beautiful shops. Must visit place in kathmandu.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I’m so glad we chose to stay at Hotel Barahi in Pokhara. Everything about this place felt five-star and first class, from the warm welcome at check-in to the attentive service at breakfast and dinner. Even the driver who took me to the airport was incredibly professional and kind.

Now that I’m staying at another five-star in Kathmandu, I can really see the difference… Barahi stands out for its service, attention to detail, and genuine hospitality. Highly recommend Barahi Resorts, you’ll be happy you stayed here!
Maybe it's not spectacular any time of year but definitely not worth it in dry season. At least 30 rupees isn't much to lose!

Yes, it's a waterfall.. Yes it's located very convenient. Yes,there is a cave. But it is very disappointing due to the lack of proper maintenance, the insanely ugly fence that blocks any decent view, the dangerous and uncontrolled access to the cave... Don't make time to go see it. If you have a spare hour in Pokhara, and you're tired if the mountain scenery (how can you) you might want to check it out

In this time of year the waterfall does not produce that many water as in monsoon. Still good place to stop by and combine it with a visit to the cave. The fall has a small garden around it and its cheap to visit.

This was my first visit to boudhanath and that too after the earthquake...the reconstruction has ended and the stupa is very beautiful...the area around the stupa was sort of clean but it was very crowed.. it was quite a difficulty to reach the boudhanath stupa...the roads are in a very bad condition..on top of that rain adds up a lot...We had our private car but the problem was no parking space...however few meters ahead from the stupa we found a parking space... 
In the end we decided to eat sth... one of my friends recommended to eat "laphing "... it's a soupy,spicy noodle dish...I didn't understand the dish much... but it tasted good...
Hospitality and the ambience was excellent in very economic tarrif.  We extended our stay only be coz of its hospitality.

Glad to give it five minutes!
But to find this in the center of town was unexpected!
Would recommend for a quick stop in...

We spent three nights in the Crowne Plaza Hotel while touring the area of Kathmandu with a group of NU Alumni.  This hotel was a survivor of the chaos of Nepal's civil war, and there were very few hotels to do so.  Thus, this is the best hotel in the area, but that said, it is in need of refurbishing.  Although the grounds, the lobby and dining areas are bright and clean, the rooms baths, and hallways need lots of work done to bring them back to a 4 or 5 star level.  And new elevators are sorely needed.  With the exception of the doormen, and one waiter, the staff seems unfriendly to the point of acting resentful if asked a question.  The breakfasts in the main dining room,  and the dinner served in the Chinese Restaurant on lobby level were very disappointing.  However, there is no where else to stay when touring the Valley of Kathmandu.

The experience was very good. Liked everything. Staffs are the best. Special thanks to recipiention staff. Oshin and Bijita.
Thanks to Housekeeping Mr.Dil.
Would recommend to everyone.
Lots of shops surrounding the stupa, some earthquake damage to the stupa itself, area seemed toutty, personally i could have given it a miss.

WOW!  My husband and I have traveled ALL OVER the world...and we have never seen a hotel this dirty.  Our room had several stains on the sheets, brown towels to conceal dirt, mold and mildew covering the entire bathroom, including the mirror and shower curtain, dust and dirt on the floor, a non-working refrigerator,  and a tired air conditioner.  The bathtub/shower floor was peeling off the bottom of the tub, leaving disgusting residue everywhere.  
Yes, it is true that the water is discolored brownish, yellow!  
The room curtains were too small to close, thus the light shown in.
Our tour guide went to the front desk to request clean linens, etc.  We were later told our room "had been sanitized" by the manager at the front desk...only to find NOTHING had been done in our room (same stains, same dirt, mold, and grime).  A real disappointment and a shame.  Unhealthful!
The only redeeming factor for this hotel was the dining room service.  The evening wait staff was excellent and tried to accommodate our needs in a friendly manner.  The food was tasty.  The breakfast selection was less than average.

This dated hotel is stretched in many ways, the building facilites and the staff!
we had rented the seminar room for 2 weeks and we were told to clear out by 5 pm sharp because there was another function in the same room. Our group of 40 had to collect all their belongings and just move!
The staff is stretched because there are so many guests. they are willing to help but are raced off their feet. rudeness has been experienced as well!
Finally the hotel rooms need refurbishment badly, seems to be overdue
Recommend another 5 star hotel in town!
Big Stupa and beautiful place with pleasure energy. Not fees. I recommend you will like go around the Stupa.

We had a lovley lunch on a rooftop restaurant over looking the Stupa before we went around it. 
One of the most amazing places we've ever been too. 
Amazing to see so many worshippers and visitors. 
A must see when visiting Kathmandu.

While I went to this place it was closed and was being repaired after earthquake. Didnt see what was inside but loved the atmosphere around this place , the market, the bells on the boundary of the stupa...

This British inspired garden is a welcome refuge from the frantic pace of the streets of Kathmandu. The garden is exceptionally well maintained and is a peaceful place to relax for an hour or two. There is a cafe where you can get something to eat or drink or you can just sit in the garden and admire the view. There are squirrels which live in the garden and it’s a good place to come if you are into photography. There is an entry fee which for foreigners is 200 rupees per person. You can also purchase wifi here.

It is beautiful, especially if you walk until the last corner and observe that crack which links up to the Davi's fall.  It is kind of magical somehow.  If you have time and there are not so many tourists, spare a few minutes to mediate there will be good.  Just beware the floor is quite slippery.

There were cockroaches in the room, there was a building site next to our room and the managers were rude and liers. We had negotiated one rate then they denied telling us this and then changed their mind on departure. They originally offered is then a free dinner to compensate and then again denied having offered us it.  We also use no hot water and again the customer service was awful. Overall I would not recommend this over priced hotel.

Not sure they can call this a Luxury hotel. It is a historic hotel. 
It has great bones and could be an amazing hotel if they spent some money updating the hotel.  They need to bring in an Interior Designer who understand old world charm. Wifi did not work in all rooms. Buffet breakfast was adequate.

Went with On The Go Tours!  This was for 2 days including Christmas day.  We had our 17 yr old daughter with us and had requested a room with 3 beds. What we got was a camp bed where the mattress was holy and flea bitten. Asked for the bed to be changed and the hotel receptionist was extremely rude. It took several attempts even with our tour guide to get any joy and eventually to be told theyes reluctantly had to take another single bed from another room. From then on and for the next day, the staff at reception were either rude or just ignored us. We would never stay there again!

We had an amazing experience at this beautiful hotel in Pokhara. From the moment we arrived, the staff made us feel genuinely welcome — always attentive, kind, and eager to help with anything we needed. Their warmth and hospitality truly made our stay special.

The hotel itself is stunning, with spacious, clean, and comfortable rooms. But what really sets it apart are the incredible views — waking up to the Himalayas and serene lakeside scenery felt absolutely magical. Whether enjoying breakfast or simply relaxing, the panorama is unforgettable.

Everything was seamless, from the check-in to the service throughout our stay. We left feeling refreshed, cared for, and already wishing we could return.

Highly recommended to anyone visiting Pokhara — this is the perfect place to relax, enjoy nature, and experience true Nepali hospitality.

its underneath a highway just outside pokhara. its just opposite to devis falls. if we climb down 3 storey downwards, we can have darshan of swaymbu shiva(gupteshwar), lord ganesha.we can see water trickling from devi falls and falling water between rocks at a distance. best time to visit is post monsson when water gushes in devis falls.

from evening til late night - basically the place felt like a large, very large wedding venue with an attached hotel.  Call me old-fashioned if you like, but I think that next to a comfy clean bed and good temperature - which the Shanker does provide - the main task of a hotel is to let one sleep.  That is not the case here, and I wasn't even accommodated on the side of the hotel facing the party halls.  And this was the case *every night*!  Trying to catch up on sleep later in the morning or during a siesta?  No way José, because - at least most of the days - the renovation/reconstruction crew will relentlessly hammer away as if performing some 1920s industrial symphony.  I do understand the problem of the earthquake damage, but I am afraid that I also really like to sleep, especially during a business trip.  

The hotel as such, as has been mentioned, is very nice, a converted former (aristocratic, *not* Royal) palace, even if the interior is partially 1970s Yugoslavian style (furniture!), and the damage means that reception and pathways are in the very low-ceilinged ground floor and that walking from A to be inside the hotel is something of a maze run.  Gardens and pool are nice for hanging out.

The rooms are partially nice, the towels etc. are good, but the WiFi is very weak and often fails altogether - and no, this is not (only or mainly) the Nepal-as-such problem, but a lack of a good repeater or other e-infrastructure.  If you're here on business, you need a Nepali SIM card (Ncell recommended).  Empty refrigerator that might deep-freeze what's in it; lots of drinking water supplied.  Good water boiler etc.

Staff is basically nice, but certainly not as nice as often described here.  I had some laundry to be done (and by the way, it was done well and very cheaply, so this is recommended!) and took the bag down to the reception because I was leaving for some event.  The concierge: "Now you can take it right up back to the room!"  What...?  Turns out that by regulation someone needs to count the items in front of you (ugh...), but I had to firmly state that I would not do that. - I used the spa once for a massage, and it was quite good - expensive for the context, but very convenient to have it in-house.  The cleaning staff and the porters very helpful and friendly.

I am at a loss why the breakfast buffet receives such raving accolades as here.  This is not my experience at all.  Items are okay, not more; the egg station fries eggs so daintily that the egg-white is still transparent, the coffee for all guests comes from one automatic machine hovered over by three waiters which creates a bottleneck.  My main problem however was the milk - stuff swimming in it including what appeared to me mold the first day and, alas, the second day as well. - I also once ordered room service, and it wasn't very good. 

I think that altogether, the price for this property is much too high for what they deliver.  Even calculating in the general and specific context, I did not have an adequate stay.  It was certainly not catastrophic and had the mentioned good and even excellent aspects, but the noise (and the breakfast and the connectivity) really does not allow for a better rating from my own personal perspective.

The Gupteshwar cave is  a must  see in Pokhara . It  is  not far  away  from the city . The cave entrance  is  beautifully  decorated by  statues and you will not  feel as if you  have  come  to  visit some  cave  seeing  the  entrance .  But  as  you  proceed and  enter the  cave  you  will be  pleased  to  see  a natural  cave  inside  the  mountain . The Cave  is  well lighted by CFLs  and  natural stairs  made  by cutting  and  rubbing  the  ground . The  cave  is  quite  long  and  at the  end  of  the  cave  you  can   see  the   Devi's fall from  the  slit  between  the  rocks   . It  is  a  natural  wonder.
Gorgeous falls.  Very affordable fun quick outing. I enjoyed visiting and recommend to friends and family.

The hotel and grounds are beautiful in for a period hotel.  You can see the elegance from years past.  The staff were especially helpful and pleasant.  Especially the door man since I was coming in and out all the time :-).  Everyone from check-in to housekeeping was great.  The rooms are dated but clean and comfortable, plus the grounds are great for sitting outside, by the pool where you can get drinks and food!  I would recommend the club sandwich, you will not be disappointed.  I'd like to give a special thank you to my pool bar favorite who keep my glass full of ice and we had many chats while he tried to teach me some of the basic language.  Saandesl lama Stanton thank you!
The area around this place is very chaotic and dusty.Entrace fees is 400NPR for foreigners.If you are Buddhist then this is a must.There are lots of shops and restaurants around the stupa.
Excellent momos at the poolside bar! Beautiful space and friendly service. Great location just a few minutes from the lake.

Beautiful place. Seeing this place in tv doesn’t do it justice. I just wish more people wore masks (don’t hate me for it). Surprisingly there are some hotels on a few buildings right opposite side of the outer courtyard of the temple.

When you arrive after a minute you get the idea of how to see this place. Walk around on the ground the Stupa on one side all the shops on the other. Then you can go up top and walk on the Stupa. After that you can go to the giant prayer wheel where the monks are and go upstairs for a better view. A interesting place with the eyes of Buddah looking down from atop the Stupa.

The hotel is in a superb location, however the facilities are very old and needs a major upgrade.
The setup can be upgraded to be really superb.
The food is relatively good.
In Pokhara though it is probably he best hotel

I expected this hotel to be first class, ~after all most of the reviews claim that this "charming" and beautifully located lodge situated on an island that can only be reached by a raft...Well I was in for a huge let down.  The rooms were mildewy, the carpets dirty, and I came down with a miserable asthma attack which foced us to leave the place ahead of schedule. Despite the fact that large tour groups come in day after day (from Estonia, Germany, you name it) and that it's "the best" that Pokhara has to offer", I will never ever go back.  I'd take Hotel Nirvana at $20 a night over the $150 rip off any day of the week!

Amazing service at the restaurant by mr hari and shriya 
Food/ambience/politiness of the staff.
The overall property too is beautiful and again I must say the staff is makes this hotel so nice and peaceful.
Just brilliant..
Thankyou for the same and I look forward to come again soon.

The room given to me was stinking......I had to change 3 rooms to get normal room. Even the room i got was old. The room staff is stupid and not understand english. In room dining staff is also very slow and took me 10 minutes to make them understand my order. Only good person was at the bar.

The location is also very far from main areas.
Not a great sightseeing but interesting sorrounding. Actually the caves in front are much better. Just cross the road and you will see the entrance
Quiet, beautiful gardens with excellent restaurants with magical views. Take your cameras and go at sunset the play of lights as the sun goes down is amazing.

This garden is nice. It’s a quite area away from the huddle of Kathmandu street. 

There is a cafe in side. 

Enjoy a sit down and rest your legs

Some people call it Davi's falls others Devi's fall.  Story is that a Swiss couple went swimming and the woman drowned.  Her father named it Davi's fall.  The water passes through a cave beneath the ground.
The place is good bariquettes are placed in such a manner the real scene cannot be watched and charges to enter seems to be high as compared to things and facility poorly maintained

The cave is in the middle of the market in the city. It is accessed through a flight of steps in a well. The first level houses a shiva temple, which is considered sacred by the locals. You can go further into the cave through a narrow small passage. The cave is very humid here with water dripping from the top. At the end of the cave, you can see the Devis waterfalls through a narrow crevice or opening. An interesting place to visit.
The best hotel which I have ever experienced in my life. Food items, service systems, well environment, all the personnel of Barahi Pokhara are friendly and speak politely with customers.
Interesting waterfall with truly sad story. There is also a fountain on the site where you can throw coins and it is said to fulfill wishes.

We walked from Pokhara to Devi's Falls with 2 children. It was a great experience walking through the tiny villages that live at the base of the mountain. 

30 NPR each entry (children were 2 for 1 - 15 NPR)

So much force / power in these rapids / falls. Imagine the electricity that could be produced here with that force!
Not sure why this place us a highlight. Not worth the taxi or entrance fee. Waterfall is tiny. Was in and out in 2 min.

Nice hotel away from the hustle and dust of Kathmandu. Bathroom cleanliness is on par with 3rd country -lots if mould, etc, had to ask for tea bags to be replaced 3 times in one day as they did not replace when the room was serviced. Didn't  replace any of the standard toiletries once used.
Staff friendly. Pool was nice but surprisingly cool (not in control of hotel but observation) no sun umbrella over sun lounges which is disappointing due to risk of sun burn.
Didn't eat at hotel so can't comment.
Hotel not in great location to Thamel as it is not a great walk from hotel to a huge selection restaurants or shopping.
On the first night the mattress was so squeaky and I didn't sleep commented to reception and they replaced it that day and slept so much better next night. The did not supply top sheet after asking reception for next sheet twice as doona was too hot.
I might stay on our next visit as the grounds were nice and it was quiet!
Was it worth about $90US a night - not sure!

saw it only from the outside. Our group wasn't offered a visit to the inside (unfortunately) as I can see from photos posted by others. the stupa is immense and walked pretty much around it. Lots of little shops surround it that are quite interesting.
the eyes make it look almost kind of spooky.

Once the best property in Kathmandu, the room size is good, but tired  with smelly carpets, passages and musty rooms. The furniture is timeworn and the bathrooms show age as well. Maybe we got their old rooms, but it was not very pleasant once inside the rooms. Also, there was ongoing construction noises during the day and the place was full of tour groups bound for Himalayas. Not the perfect peaceful stay for us.
 
Having said, the grounds are immaculate, the restaurants fantastic (we tried Chinese & Indian), the service is really good (as across Nepal) and the pool area is lovely. Breakfast spread also very good.

If the rooms were nicer, I would highly recommend this property. But we did not enjoy the smelly indoors and shifted to the Hyatt for the latter half of our stay.

We initially booked two night stay at the hotel and we had such a great experience that we extended our stay to three nights. The staff were  amazing and the hospitality was incredible. I will definitely be coming back. Great location and the pool area is beautiful, although it would've been brilliant if the pool was open little later than 8pm. Also big shoutout to Durga for her great service and making our experience even better:)
It is a nice place to visit. I recommend everyone to visit this wonderful place. If you visit Nepal , Boudhanath is the most place to go.

We spent 4 days in Pokhara and stayed the entire time here. Assuming the lower levels were being renovated most guests were put up on Level 6(not sure why or how the ground floor is labeled 3rd floor). Nice size modern hotel with full amenities including a swimming pool and a spa. But the noise from the other guests slamming doors, talking outside the doors and the cigarette smoke(we had the top most floor corner room with a window just outside the door where continuously people would stand there puffing away). Good central location as once you get out to Lakeside left and right are shops and money changers.
Breakfast spread was good and they say the menu changes everyday. Very attentive staff who always smiles and delivers.
Biggest drawback was poor WiFi reception. We were told the entire Lakeside WiFi was down but when we went to a nearby restaurant there was no issue. WiFi was restored the next day and even then I had to stand out the balcony to get a connection, nothing in the room. Yet every morning I spend an hour just trying to get 2 to 3 emails done but it was frustrating as the internet just disconnect on poor signal.

With a background in boutique travel planning, I was very excited to spend a night at the recommended Shanker Hotel. Upon arrival onto their gorgeous grounds, the excitement was still there...checkin was a breeze and the staff was very accommodating and helpful. We were upgraded to a larger suite and shown to our room. The first thing that was a turn off were the dark dreary hallways. First, the hotel web site was the very thing that convinced me to book at the Shanker. Also, my travel agent in KTM agreed that it's a fine place. Second, I would not stay in the Shanker again.

After a 6-day trek I wished for my son (age16) and I to stay in a nice place out of the center of the noise and chaos. Well, the Shanker delivered on the 2nd wish only. 

The hotel is a rip off - not worth the price you pay and not worth the nickels and dimes they charge for Wi-Fi and Internet in the grimy business center.

They charged us full rate for 2 nights even though we arrived 7pm Friday and checked out 10pm Saturday - no rated discount.

The small room itself had very hard beds (not a surprise) the bathroom had plenty of hot water but the grime and dirt everywhere was a real turn off. I did not see other rooms but may be, just may be they gave us a crappy room because we went through a local agent. 

The hallway carpets, furniture, doors, mirrors and walls were filthy. The lobby bathrooms are a disgrace. 

The restaurants are all in the "basement" of the hotel so they're dark and cavernous. 

The food was ok, they messed my steak order 2 times until I finally gave in a just ate it. The buffet breakfast is fine. A decent assortment of foods and the coffee was drinkable. 

The staff are moderately helpful - not terse - not unfriendly...just ok.

In my opinion the entire hotel needs to be gutted, scrubbed, re-furbished and re-fitted, then the image they promote will actually match the hotel value. 

And put a cafe or something in the gardens - why they're in the "basement" is beyond me. I asked about that and the concierge said that they're not in the basement they're on the ground floor. Well, technically that may be true but architecturally, they're in the basement.

It is well located - 15 minutes to the Int'l airport and a 20-minute walk to Thamel - if that is your scene.

The Shanker likely saw better days 50 years ago when it was first converted from a 19th Century Maharajah Palace but it seems that nothing has been done to it since that time.

Be careful if you are considering the Shanker. If that style is your thing, look elsewhere or try the new KTM Radisson down the road.

Patale Chhango ("underworld waterfall") is also known as Devi’s Falls, named after a couple that drowned here. The Pardi Khola stream, with water sourced from the Phewa Lake dam, spills through a narrow gorge and disappears before your eyes. What really happens is the water forms an underground tunnel that is about 500 feet (150 m) long and runs 100 feet (30 m) below ground level. After exiting the tunnel, the water passes through a cave called Gupteshwor Mahadev or "cave beneath the ground". We were somewhat underwhelmed by the waterfalls, but I can imagine it’s a sight to see when the stream is at full power after monsoon rains. The area is protected by railings to prevent accidents. Admission is only 30 NRs per person and it’s a quick visit.

Many landmarks in Kathmandu demand attention, but for me, none resonate quite like Boudhanath Stupa. More than just a magnificent piece of architecture, Boudha is a profound sanctuary—a place where the chaotic energy of city life dissipates, replaced by an overwhelming sense of peace. It is, without a doubt, my favourite spot in the entire city.
The moment you pass through the gates and the vast, white dome (the mandala) comes into view, the world seems to quieten. The Stupa itself is breathtaking. Its massive structure, adorned with the watchful eyes of the Buddha painting on the gilded tower, seems to absorb the worries of all who circle it. It is the heart of Tibetan Buddhism in Nepal, and that heritage infuses every corner of the plaza.
The core of the experience is the kora—the ritual walk around the Stupa. As you join the continuous flow of pilgrims, the air is thick with the scent of juniper incense and the soft, rhythmic sound of chanting. The colossal prayer wheels, spinning with countless inscribed mantras, are a hypnotic presence. It’s impossible not to feel grounded as you move, your footsteps marking time with the low hum of "Om Mani Padme Hum."
While the vibrant market and rooftop restaurants surrounding the plaza offer beautiful views and lively interactions, the truest peace is found when you focus inward. The white dome beneath the spire seems to be a vessel for quiet contemplation. Whether sitting on the steps, watching the sun catch the prayer flags, or simply following the circuit, Boudha offers a powerful meditative space. It's a reminder that even in the midst of a bustling city, profound stillness is always accessible.
Boudhanath Stupa isn't just a sight to see; it’s an experience for the soul. It is the place I go when I need to reconnect, find balance, and immerse myself in the timeless, tranquil energy of devotion and community.
I recommend visiting in the morning to see the local devotees praying and doing cora, or in the evening for the lighting decoration and a peaceful walk around the stupa.

The good:
My $.02, this place should be redecorated and renamed to the Shanker Palace or something.  It has a lot of potential.  Yes, this is a fomer palace.  The hotel and the grounds are palatial.  The decor in the lobby and the walkways are exotic woodwork.  You won't get this anywhere else in Kathmandu. The location is nice and is located away from the road construction and noise and the dust.  The hotel management was really good with emails and we made all the reservations through emails. They offered a better deal if you booked directly through them with airport transfers etc.

The breakfast spread was the biggest I've ever seen.  The menu is different everyday and the food quality was good.  The best upma and chole bhature in town.  Even the Nepali version of quesadillas were great (parathas with cheese).  The hotel even packs a boxed breakfast if you have an early flight.  The hotel staff makes you feel royal.  From the person who opens the door for you to the room service folks, everyone greets you when they see you.  

No issue with power cuts, heat or A/C.  The hotel always had power and went to backup generator when you lost power.  The hotel is safe - we had 4 bags in their 'cloak room' for 4 days and had no issues.

The bad:
We arrived at 8am after an international red-eye flight with small kids.  We were shocked that the room was not ready for us after an overnight flight.  The front desk guy 'Ramesh' with the Nepali hat would not give us the room saying checkin time is noon!  I tried to convince him multiple times and even offered to pay extra for an early checkin.  You could see that he was lying that rooms were overbooked.  Such poor customer service -- such folks should be fired (if he is not part of the family run business).  Leaves a bad taste in your mouth.  Our family of four were sleeping on the lobby couches before we were given the room.

The rooms were small and we upgraded to the 'suite' for almost $40 more. The welcome drinks and gifts were a nice touch. The rooms have seen better days and in need for an overhaul. The rooms were dusty with musty odor (no vent in the bathrooms).  We asked the room service to clean and mop the room.  

Bottomline:
Kathmandu has a myriad of hotel options (from $8 rooms to $500 rooms).  Personally, we didn't stay in Thamel thinking it would be dirty/dusty.  Thamel turned out to be surprisingly nice and bustling part of Kathmandu.  I would pick up a nice hotel in Thamel the next time I'm in Kathmandu.  For $100/night, I don't think Shanker was worth it.

We arrived around midday and were happy to be given a room a little early - however as we had just a basic room I wasn’t hugely impressed – it was rather small (by European standards) and looked onto concrete – perhaps because we’d paid a low internet rate but just beware they aren’t much like the pictures – so no duplex rooms on our floor. We didn’t try to change the room so perhaps others were better though the fire plan suggested our floor (2nd) were all the same. The bathroom was particularly small (think toilet between the bath and wall with no space at all between the two), however the water was hot. Internet was provided and free.

Breakfast was tasty enough, including an egg chef – in a large hall with light, however the evening before we tried to eat in the hotel’s restaurant which was a terrible idea; the food wasn’t great quality, was reasonably expensive and for some reason used a different room which was more like a bunker (no natural light). In addition there were only large tables there (for 6-20 people) and just as we, a couple, were finishing a (slightly) romantic meal they placed two other people right next to us… very surprising especially when we saw how much space they have elsewhere if they weren't just trying to crowd us in. There was a buffet option offered and though pricey for local standards it did appeal to the tour groups staying there.

So overall not a great experience but the building itself was rather lovely and we also had a welcome basket of fruit which was nice. Strangely I might consider returning as the hotel was a bit of an oasis in Kathmandu and a good location for our exploring (and looking to be outside Thamel), but would be a lot more careful of the room being chosen and would not eat there.

I just came back from staying for 2 nights at Fishtail Lodge. Our flight from Kathmandu was delayed one hour (apparently not unusual) and Fishtail Lodge had our flight number, however no-one was there to pick us up. A quick call from the tourist desk at the airport and the Fishtail shuttle turned up 4 minutes later.

You get dropped off on one side of a lake inlet and you have to take a rope-pull ferry over to the Lodge (it takes about 3 minutes to cross). It is cute and there are plenty of porters to help with the baggage. Reception was busy but the staff were attentive. We were given room number 18 (16, 17 and 18 have the best views of the lake and mountains) so I was happy as I didn't really want to pay what I considered exorbitant price given Nepal's cost of living. I booked what I thought would be the nicest hotel in Pokhara as we were traveling with our 2 year old daughter and didn't want to be slumming it. However, my excitement was dampened in getting to the room. We had twin beds rather than a king/queen as requested. Reception said that they were full and couldn't change rooms for us (plus we would definitely be downgrading views so I didn't complain too much). The room was small, outdated, terrible lighting, tiny bathroom with just a curtain across part of the bathroom for a shower. Nowhere to put toiletries. TV was tiny, mounted on the wall and didn't work (luckily we weren't there to watch TV anyway). It is what I would expect from a 2 or 3 star hotel, not for somewhere in a developing country and paying $150 per night excluding breakfast (which by the way, isn't worth paying for, take the ferry and 2 minute walk into town and eat elsewhere).

That being said, the location has to be the best in Pokhara, fabulous views of the lake and mountains. I found the staff to be very attentive and friendly. The gardens are gorgeous with hammocks around the property, and each of the cabins has a nice front porch/patio with adirondack chairs and table. It is a very short walk into Pokhara.

I'd stay there again but not for the price. You'd be better off finding somewhere better value and then head over to the Fishtail for a drink where you can sit and enjoy the views and the gardens.
Often go there in the evening , spend my time having coffee and few rounds of stupa  and sit for while .

This is a 5 star property in kathmandu. Also it's a chain of crowne plaza hotels so, I thought this hotel would be very high class hotel but it was completely opposite.

Pros:

Check in: They were able to provide me early check in and they also changed our room from rear side view to garden view room.

Room view: They have a nice garden and swimming pool view room if u take last even number rooms.

Garden: There is a big garden in the hotel.

Cons:

They have more respect for people who come in large number in a group of 30-50 people, delegates but no respect for the families and speciallt Indians.

Bed: Extra bed for 3rd person was very uncomfortable.

Bathroom : There is something wrong with their tubs. There was a water logging problem in the bathrooms. Size of the bathroom is not large. There was also something wrong with the showers.

Room Service: Room service is damn pathetic and if u want something then u have to remind them 2-3 times then also there is no surity whether they provide the thing u asked them or not. Also even if they get it they might take 2-3 hours or may be they don't provide u anything. They don't have talcum powder, oil, swing kit, etc. Don't depend for basic things as in which u expect in 5 star hotel.

Food: I had a 3night/4days stay (in the 1st week of june) in hotel with breakfast  in Garden terrace restaurant everyday. In all 3 days there was something wrong with the food. Food quality in the restaurant is very poor. They don't change the menu for vegetarians and may be for non-vegetarians also sometimes. The food is very unhygienic and stale. Juices are not chilled.

Linen: They don't change the linen themselves until u put a change my linen card.

Maintenance: Maintenance people are always reaching but they will never reach u. So,  dont expect anything from them.

Locker: They don't have fixed locker in the room. So don't keep ur valuable items in the lockers as can be moved from one place to another easily.

Wifi: You have to pay 500 nepali rupees for an hour. Wifi is not complimentary.

Location: It is far away from the main city and for 1 non AC Taxi u have to pay 300nepali rupee for 3 km.

Check out: They won't pick your luggage from the hotel. So please take ur luggage yourself. Don't depend on them. You might miss ur flight if u do so.

No Activities for kids: They don't have any activities for small kids.

Conclusion: It doesn't seems to be a 5 star property. It's just a 3 star hotel according to me.

We stayed one night on our arrival in Kathmandu, prior to arriving we thought we might return at the end of our  trip and use the Shanker as a base with a nice relaxing garden and pool.

We found the building quite interesting and quirky, our room was basic.... Although it was just a standard room which was without much natural light (because of the half 'style' windows where the palace was turned into a hotel).

It's a shame about the earthquake damage which remains under repair as it means guests at not able to see the hotel at its best as it was once a grand (albeit pretty faded) old place! 

Although we weren't expecting much from the dining room for dinner, we didn't want to go far as we arrived late and decided to give it a try. The waiting staff were nice and we enjoyed our meal, it was good value and busy with other guests. 

Breakfast was served in the large dining room the following morning, the buffet was just ok.... The experience was a little like stepping back in time! Again the staff were friendly. 

We took a walk around the garden, which was in a pre monsoon state - dry, but cared for by the friendly female gardeners. The pool and seating area didn't look like it saw much use to us, but we could be wrong. It didn't look particularly ready or comfortable!! 

We had read such good reviews about the hotel, so we were anticipating really helpful and friendly reception staff - but they were indifferent with us. This made us feel we would be unlikely return at a later stage of our trip... And we didn't. 

All said, we like unique and different experiences. We are pleased we tried the Shanker, it is clearly popular with others. Perhaps if we had stayed longer than 18 hours it would have grown on us too!!
